comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
REGRESSION IN THIS BEAD'S TEST, and the cause is a misapplication of a rule I wrote. The bead's substance holds; one assertion is brittle.

src/content/provenance/receipt.test.ts is 83 pass, 1 fail at HEAD eeceda3e:

    647 | assert.equal(typos.length, 6, "ap-17-891 carries six typographical records");
    AssertionError: 7 !== 6

The seventh record is err-typo-p908-1, printed page 908, live, recorded by
agent:LilacValley under am-src-ledger-relativity-sby. pane29 found a real
typographical error while transcribing page 908 and recorded it properly, with
an attribution and a bead reference. That is the project working. Finding typos
in a 1905 printing is what a critical edition DOES.

## The defect: a hard-coded count over a deliberately growing population

The receipt's typographicalErrors list grows every time a transcriber finds an
error, and pane29 is currently at page 911 of 31 with twenty more to read. So
this assertion is guaranteed to fail repeatedly, and each failure will look like
a regression while being a success.

## The subtlety, which is worth more than the fix

The test comment directly above the assertion reads:

    // Denominator named: six records on this receipt, three of them retracted

That is the author following the repo law I added to AGENTS.md - "a count used
as evidence is anchored, and names its denominator". The law was written for
REPORTS: a number in a commit message or a finding must say what it counted, so
a reader can re-derive it. Naming a denominator makes a MEASUREMENT auditable.
Freezing one into an equality assertion makes a TEST brittle. Those are opposite
effects and the same sentence produced both.

So the law needs a boundary: anchor a count when you REPORT it; derive a count
when you ASSERT it. A test over a growing population asserts the PROPERTY, not
the census.

## A second consequence, already seen once today

The count assertion is at line 647 and the retraction checks are below it, so
the failure ABORTS the test above the part that actually matters. Right now
nothing is verifying that retracted records stay distinguishable from live ones
- the property this bead exists for - because a stale census number fails first.
That is the same shape as the manifest test earlier in the session where
assert.equal(units.length, 87) aborted above the assertion I was reasoning
about.

The property itself is intact, checked by hand: 7 records, 3 retracted
(typo-h-for-y-axis-p899, err-typo-p899-1, err-typo-p902-1), 4 live, and every
retracted one still carries a reason and an author.

## Fix

Assert the property, not the census. Retracted records are excluded from
liveTypographicalErrors; every retracted record has a reason and an author;
live + retracted equals the total. All three hold at any size. If a count is
genuinely wanted, derive it from the parsed receipt rather than pinning it.

NOT reopening this bead: the retraction mechanism works and the planted negative
that proved it is untouched. This is a brittle assertion in its test, routed to
pane29, which wrote it and found the seventh record.

title: verify-content audited 1 of 24 readings owners and 1 of 38 instruments, with the restriction unrecorded and unenforced
description:
Filed by pane31 on TanElk's ruling while working am-unwired-audits-uwot. Fixed in the same change;
this record exists because the defect was real and should not be invisible in history.

## The defect

`scripts/verify-content.ts` is a registry step and it calls four audits. Two of them were called
with a filter that restricted them to a single item:

    readings      loadLiveReadingsAuditInput(root, { ownerBeadIds: ["am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly"] })
                  1 of 24 owner files in content/editorial/readings-owners/
    instruments   loadLiveInstrumentRows(root, { ids: ["bm-01"] })
                  1 of 38 catalogue ids

Both loaders default to the full population when no filter is passed (`options?.ids ?? CATALOGUE_IDS`;
the readings loader iterates every owner file unless `ownerBeadIds` is given), so the restriction was
deliberate at the call site rather than a limitation of the loaders.

The ruling: this is a defect even if the staging was deliberate, because nothing recorded the
restriction as intentional and nothing failed when the population grew. A twenty-fifth owner file or
a newly built instrument would simply not be audited, and every summary would still say the audit
ran and passed.

That is the same family as am-izth and the am-niyd licence table: no false sentence anywhere, and a
reader concludes the corpus was audited when one item was.

## Measured before the fix

    readings      scoped: 0 errors.  Full population: 23 errors across 3 of 24 owners.
    instruments   scoped: 1 row, ok.  Full catalogue: 38 rows, 83 findings across 34 of 38 ids.
                  Only bm-01, bm-05, sr-02 and me-02 are clean, consistent with AGENTS.md
                  recording that thirty of the thirty-three instruments are unbuilt.

So full population is red for both, and simply widening would have been a red-on-arrival change.

## The fix

Both audits now run over the whole population. Items that cannot pass yet are recorded in a keyed
map with a reason, and the entry expires: if a recorded item stops producing findings, the audit
raises `stale-audit-exemption` naming it, so the entry must be deleted rather than left behind as
stale prose. Same shape as `EXPECTED_UNREACHABLE` in `src/testing/scriptReachability.test.ts`.

Recorded exemptions: 3 readings owners, 34 instruments. 106 findings are now visible as flags that
were previously not computed at all, and audit errors remain 0.

## Planted negatives, both directions

    A. population audited    removed the am-sr-07-field-equations-xxes entry
                             -> ERROR: r3-citation-missing: sr-07 ... and r2-length: sr-07
                             -> audit errors 0 -> 2
    B. reason goes stale     added an entry for bm-01, one of the four clean instruments
                             -> ERROR: stale-audit-exemption: bm-01 is recorded as not yet
                                auditable, but the instruments audit now reports nothing against it
                             -> audit errors 0 -> 1

Both reverted; `shasum -a 256 -c` OK both times; baseline back to 0 audit errors.

## Not changed, deliberately

`shelf` and `misconceptions` still receive empty inputs. `content/historical-premises/` and
`content/misconceptions/` do not exist, so empty is honest there and inventing data would be worse.
Per the same ruling, they were left alone.

## Steps to Reproduce

Before the fix, at any commit where scripts/verify-content.ts passed a filter to either audit:

1. Note the call sites:

       grep -n 'ownerBeadIds: \["am-bm-01' scripts/verify-content.ts
       grep -n 'ids: \["bm-01"\]' scripts/verify-content.ts

2. Count the populations those filters exclude:

       find content/editorial/readings-owners -name '*.yaml' | wc -l     # 24
       # catalogue ids: loadLiveInstrumentRows(root) with no options returns 38 rows

3. Run `bun scripts/verify-content.ts`. The readings and instruments audits report on one item
   each and contribute 0 errors, while 23 readings errors and 83 instrument findings exist in the
   population and are never computed.

4. Add a new owner file or build a new instrument. Nothing changes and nothing fails, because the
   filter names the items to audit rather than the items to skip. That is the defect: the
   restriction is invisible and does not expire.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both audits run over the full population rather than one item.
- [x] Every restriction is recorded with a reason, in a keyed map.
- [x] A recorded reason expires: a listed item that stops failing raises an error naming it.
- [x] Planted negative in both directions, each confirmed red and reverted byte-identically.
- [ ] The 34 instrument exemptions shrink as instruments land. Each entry names its finding count
      at 2026-09-19, so a reviewer can see which are nearly clean.
- [ ] The 3 readings exemptions are resolved by their owning beads.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
NUMBERS RE-DERIVED, WITH THE RULE THAT PRODUCED EACH. The bead's own point is that an unstated
denominator hides what was counted, so every figure below carries its population rule.

RULE A - readings owners. The population is the files matching
content/editorial/readings-owners/*.yaml. Measured two ways because `ls | wc -l` on this machine
is aliased to lsd and counts . and .. - it reported 26:
    ls -1 content/editorial/readings-owners/*.yaml | wc -l   ->  24
    git ls-files 'content/editorial/readings-owners/*.yaml'  ->  24
  The bead's 24 stands.

RULE B - instruments. The population is CATALOGUE_IDS, which is Object.keys(CATALOGUE_STATUS)
in src/experiments/catalogue.ts:95.
    CATALOGUE_IDS.length                          ->  38
    loadLiveInstrumentRows(root), no filter       ->  38 rows
  The bead's 38 stands.

RULE C - instrument findings. auditInstruments(loadLiveInstrumentRows(root)), counting
report.findings and the distinct recordIds among them:
    findings                                      ->  82      (the bead says 83)
    distinct ids with at least one finding        ->  34 of 38
    clean ids                                     ->  bm-01, bm-05, sr-02, me-02
  34 of 38 and the four clean ids stand. The finding count has drifted 83 -> 82 since the bead
  was written. One finding has gone; I have not chased which, and I am reporting the drift rather
  than repeating 83.

RULE D - the readings figure has changed SHAPE, not just value. The bead recorded "23 errors
across 3 of 24 owners". verify-content now prints, from its own run this tick:
    readings audit: 21 of 24 records judged against the full rule, 3 recorded as not yet auditable.
    instruments audit: 4 of 38 records judged against the full rule, 34 recorded as not yet auditable.
  The three owners and the thirty-four instruments are no longer counted as errors; they are
  recorded exemptions with reasons. So "23 errors across 3 owners" and "3 recorded as not yet
  auditable" are the same three owners in two different accounting shapes, and quoting the old
  number today would overstate the open work.

THE FIX IS COMPLETE ON THIS BEAD'S OWN TERMS, and I checked the mechanism rather than the call
sites alone. verify-content.ts:429 and :453 now pass no filter. applyAuditExemptions does three
things that answer the defect as filed:
  - every exemption carries a reason (ReadonlyMap<string, string>), so the restriction is recorded;
  - a finding against an exempted key is DOWNGRADED to flag and its message gains
    "[recorded as not yet auditable: <reason>]" - it is not removed, so it stays visible;
  - an exemption whose key produces no finding becomes a stale-audit-exemption ERROR, so an
    exemption cannot outlive its defect. That is the half that usually gets skipped.
  The population total is printed with the comment "Reported so '0 errors' cannot be read as
  'all of them'", which is the sentence this bead exists to make true.

ONE RESIDUAL, measured not read. summarize() returns ok = (errorCount === 0) regardless of
population, so an audit over an EMPTY population passes. Executed:
    summarize("readings", [], { total: 0, judged: 0, notYetAuditable: 0 })
      populationLine -> "readings audit: no records to judge."
      report.ok      -> true
  The prose is honest - it says plainly that nothing was judged - and only the boolean is
  unguarded. That is the am-wdqy shape exactly: the sentence a human reads cannot lie, the verdict
  a script branches on can. It is reachable if content/editorial/readings-owners/ is renamed or
  moved, because loadLiveReadingsAuditInput guards with existsSync and yields an empty input.
  Nothing is escaping today: both populations are non-zero and stated. Say if you want it filed;
  by my own bias rule I am recording it here rather than opening a bead for a latent boolean.

| `suspicious/noArrayIndexKey` | 5 | **1** |
| `a11y/noNoninteractiveTabindex` | 20 | **20** |
| singletons (`noAssignInExpressions`, `noImplicitAnyLet`, `useHtmlLang`, `useAriaPropsSupportedByRole`, `noStaticElementInteractions`, `useExhaustiveDependencies`) | 6 | **0** |

Commits: d373e025, 74c965cf, 4274a603, 4999a1c7, 8aaf634c, d2adc327, f51d9e9f, 840f284a, f2872076, 7e18a7d4, f9ce1e26, 93a9d2ec. No rule disabled, no `biome-ignore` added, the fifteen formatter-excluded files never opened.

=== A CORRECTION TO WHAT I TOLD THE ORCHESTRATOR TWICE ===
I reported that the 20 `noNoninteractiveTabindex` errors sit in a **contradiction between two gates**, biome against this repository's `src/testing/a11y/scrollableRegions.test.ts`. **I tested that claim instead of re-asserting it, and it is wrong.** I removed `tabIndex` from `DatasetTable.tsx` and ran the ratchet: **3 pass, 0 fail.** None of the fifteen files carrying these errors is in that ratchet's BASELINE, so the gate does not govern any of them. I restored the file immediately.

The action does not change, and the reason it does not change is the point. All twenty sit on four classes - `.table-scroll`, `.formula`, `.encounter-table`, `.me-table` - and **every one of those genuinely sets `overflow-x: auto` or `overflow: auto`**. They really scroll, so `tabIndex={0}` is what makes them reachable by keyboard under WCAG 2.1.1 and axe `scrollable-region-focusable`. Removing it would be a real regression **that no gate in this repository would catch** - which makes it more dangerous than the contradiction I described, not less. Gate silence is not permission.

Five candidate markups were probed - `<section>`, `role="group"`, `role="application"`, `<output>`, `role="figure"`, each with `tabIndex={0}` and `overflow:auto` - and all five were rejected. The rule accepts tabIndex only on genuinely interactive roles, and giving a data-table container `role="button"` would lie to assistive technology.

=== THE 21 ===
- **20 `noNoninteractiveTabindex`**, above. Needs a `biome.json` decision, or browser measurement at 320px and 1280px to prove individual regions never overflow and may honestly lose the attribute. The repo's own escape hatch, `RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING`, already demands exactly those measurements.
- **1 `noArrayIndexKey`**, the token glyphs in one SVG. A token has no identity beyond its position; the composite key was tried and rejected by the rule.

=== WHAT I GOT WRONG TONIGHT, SINCE IT IS A PATTERN WORTH NAMING ===
Three times I declared something unfixable and was wrong, and each correction came from running an experiment rather than reading a document: the AS 241 coefficients (the surplus digits never reached a calculation, so the rewrite is provably bit-identical - 48 coefficients, 0 differences); the term trigger (only one of the two broken tests was real, and it was the one pinning the workaround); and the gate contradiction above. The one that still stands, the scrollable regions, is the one I probed five ways before saying so.

CI STEP 3, biome lint, from pane29. MEASURED, NOT FIXED, and I need one ruling before anything lands. No commit.

THE MEASUREMENT, current tree, `biome lint --reporter=json .`: 21 error-severity findings across 15 files (the dispatch said 11 files; peers have been landing a11y fixes all evening, so the count moves). 484 warnings and 48 infos are not what fails the step.

  20  lint/a11y/noNoninteractiveTabindex   in 15 files
   1  lint/suspicious/noArrayIndexKey      LightQuantaFirstEncounter.tsx:154

THE FIFTEEN FORMATTER-EXCLUDED FILES: zero lint errors, one warning. Nothing to do there, and I reformatted none of them.

WHAT THE 20 ACTUALLY ARE. Every one is a content region deliberately made keyboard-focusable: 16 wrap a <table> (`table-scroll`, `encounter-table`, `me-table`, `missing-step-table`, DatasetTable), 3 are formula or math blocks, 2 are gloss sentences. Not one is a stray tabIndex on decoration. `.table-scroll` is `max-width:100%; overflow-x:auto` (globals.css:506), so the tabIndex is what lets a keyboard-only reader scroll the table at all - WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1.

EVERY HONEST CODE FIX, PROBED ON A REAL SITE RATHER THAN REASONED ABOUT (RodSimultaneityLab.tsx, error counts by rule):

  baseline <section tabIndex aria-label>   noNoninteractiveTabindex 2
  + role="region"                          noNoninteractiveTabindex 2      (no effect)
  + role="group"                           noNoninteractiveTabindex 2  + useSemanticElements 1
  + role="grid"                            noNoninteractiveTabindex 1  + useSemanticElements 1 + noNoninteractiveElementToInteractiveRole 1
  <div tabIndex aria-label>                noNoninteractiveTabindex 2  + useAriaPropsSupportedByRole 1
  remove tabIndex                          0 errors, and keyboard access to an overflow-x:auto region is gone

So there is no role, element or attribute arrangement that clears the rule. The only code change that clears it removes the accessibility the rule exists to protect.

THE REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY DECIDED THIS, 10 TIMES. `biome-ignore lint/a11y/noNoninteractiveTabindex` appears at 10 sites in 6 files - SplitTabs, FacsimileFace, kitchen/page (2), DerivationStepComponent (2), ComparisonPanel (2), ShowTheCode (2) - with three wordings, the fullest being "a scrollable region must be keyboard focusable so keyboard-only readers can scroll it (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1)". The rule is not configured off anywhere; biome.json has no a11y rule config at all, so this is the recommended default and the ignores are the accepted exception.

THE RULING I NEED, and why I did not just do it: the instruction was "never suppress a rule". Applied literally that forbids the one resolution this codebase has already adopted for this exact rule, and the alternative is stripping keyboard scrolling from 20 regions to make a linter quiet - the same trade I refused on the voice rule earlier tonight, where the fix was the matcher and not the text. I am not extending a suppression pattern to 20 new sites on my own authority, and I am not regressing accessibility. One line from the owner settles it:
  (a) extend the existing precedent - a per-site biome-ignore citing WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1, one per site, no blanket disable. I can land this in minutes, commit by filename, and it leaves the rule enforced everywhere else.
  (b) rule the whole pattern wrong and remove the tabIndex, which is an accessibility decision with an owner of its own.
  (c) something else.

THE 21st, noArrayIndexKey at LightQuantaFirstEncounter.tsx:154, is a separate case and also not mechanical. The element is a token in a static arrangement diagram: `row.parts.map((part, token) => ...)`, where `part` is which part the token sits in and several tokens share a part, so the ordinal is the only identity a token has. A comment already in the file says a composite key was tried and still flagged; I verified that independently at biome 2.5.8 - `key={`token-${token}-part-${part}`}` still reports noArrayIndexKey, because the index appears in the expression. A peer fixed the neighbouring list properly in 93a9d2ec by keying on the part name, which worked there because those boxes DO have identity. These tokens do not.

Nothing committed. The measurement above is the deliverable; the decision is not mine.

comments.text:
CI STEP 3, biome lint: THE DOCUMENTED REFUSAL, per your ruling. No suppressions added, no code changed, nothing committed. From pane29.

THE PRINCIPLE YOU ASKED ME TO PUT HERE, in your words and mine: a list whose items have genuine identity gets keyed on it; a list whose items do not must not be given a fake key to silence the rule. That is the difference between fixing the code and rewriting the rule's mind. 93a9d2ec was the former - the arrangement boxes really do have a part name. The same test decides every case below: does the code have the property the rule is asking for, or is the rule asking the wrong question of this code?

MEASURED AT THIS TREE (b5d2b968): 21 error-severity findings, 15 files. Unchanged from my previous count; the "11 files" in the dispatch is from an earlier snapshot. 484 warnings and 48 infos do not fail the step.

CLASSIFICATION, every one of the 21 checked individually against the CSS or the inline style of the element it sits on:

A. EIGHTEEN are tabIndex on a region that genuinely scrolls. The rule says "this element is non-interactive, do not make it focusable". The element is focusable precisely so a keyboard-only reader can scroll it, which is WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1. Evidence per class:
     .table-scroll         overflow-x: auto   globals.css:508           9 sites
     .encounter-table      overflow-x: auto   countingEntrance.css:29   2 sites
     .me-table             overflow-x: auto   massEnergyEntrance.css:43 1 site
     .missing-step-math    overflow-x: auto   missingStep.css:41-44     1 site
     .missing-step-table   overflow-x: auto   missingStep.css:41-44     1 site
     .formula              overflow: auto     globals.css:292           2 sites
     DatasetTable.tsx      style={{ overflowX: "auto" }} inline         1 site
     (BrownianFirstEncounter contributes 1 table-scroll and 2 .formula)
   THE REFUSAL: the rule should not apply to these eighteen. Removing the tabIndex is the only code change that clears it, and it removes keyboard access to a scrollable region. I probed every alternative on a real site and none works: role="region" no effect; role="group" trades it for useSemanticElements; role="grid" trades one error for two; <div> instead of <section> adds useAriaPropsSupportedByRole. There is no arrangement of role, element or attribute that satisfies the rule and keeps the affordance.

B. TWO are tabIndex on something that does NOT scroll, and they are a different case: GlossSentence.tsx:95 and :127. `.gloss-sentence` has no overflow property. These are focusable so a reader can land on a sentence, which is a design choice belonging to the gloss face rather than to a lint sweep, so I have not touched them - but I found a real inconsistency inside them and it is a genuine defect rather than a rule disagreement:
     :127 is a <section class="gloss-sentence"> with tabIndex={0} AND aria-labelledby naming its header.
     :95  is a <div class="gloss-sentence gloss-sentence-missing"> with tabIndex={0} and NO accessible name at all.
   A focus stop that announces nothing is the thing the rule is gesturing at even though its specific complaint is wrong. The fix is a name, not the removal of the tabIndex, and it belongs to whoever owns the gloss face; I did not guess at the intended announcement. Flagging it here so it is not lost inside a refusal.

C. ONE is noArrayIndexKey at LightQuantaFirstEncounter.tsx:154, and by the principle above it is a refusal, not a fix. `row.parts.map((part, token) => ...)`: `part` says which part a token sits in and several tokens share a part, so a token's ordinal is the only identity it has. The list is a static diagram of one arrangement and is never reordered. A composite key would be a fake identity built out of the index, which is what you just ruled against; I verified at biome 2.5.8 that `key={`token-${token}-part-${part}`}` is still flagged anyway, so it would buy nothing even as a silencing move. The in-file comment already says this; I confirmed it independently rather than trusting it.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, and why: I did not add a biome-ignore to any site. Ten such ignores for this exact rule already exist in six files - SplitTabs, FacsimileFace, kitchen/page, DerivationStepComponent, ComparisonPanel, ShowTheCode - the fullest citing WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1, so the precedent for silencing exists and you have ruled against extending it. I did not remove a tabIndex, because that regresses the accessibility the rule exists to protect. Those were the only two ways to make the step green, so the step stays red and this comment is the reason.

CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than implied: CI step 3 will keep failing on these 21 until either the a11y rules are configured for the scrollable-region pattern (an owner decision about the gate, not a code fix) or the pattern itself is ruled wrong (an owner decision about accessibility). Both are above my authority. Everything else in the sweep is clean: the fifteen formatter-excluded files carry zero lint errors and I reformatted none of them.

ORCHESTRATOR RULING on the last lint sites (TanElk). These are judgement calls, not mechanical debt, which is why the count stalled at 3 files for two ticks.

REFUSED, by me, with the reason on the record:

  scripts/e2e/controlledComparison.mjs:41 and :53
  lint/suspicious/noApproximativeNumericConstant

  Both lines are assert.equal(await ratio(...), 0.70711). That value is 1/sqrt(2) rounded to
  five significant figures, and it is an EXPECTED VALUE in an equality assertion, not a constant
  being used in a computation. Biome's suggested Math.SQRT1_2 is 0.7071067811865476, so taking
  the fix would silently change what the test asserts - from "equals the value we rounded to and
  recorded" to "equals a full-precision float" - and the assertion would then fail for a reason
  that has nothing to do with the physics. The rule is correct in general and wrong here.

  This is a refusal, not a suppression: the rule stays on for the rest of the repository, the
  reason is recorded here, and anyone who later wants the rule satisfied has to change the test's
  meaning deliberately rather than by accident.

LEFT TO pane29 TO JUDGE, with my reasoning offered rather than imposed:

  src/workers/protocol/conformance.ts, lint/suspicious/noExplicitAny at six sites
  A protocol conformance checker exists to inspect shapes it has not been told about, so `any`
  may be honest there in a way it is not elsewhere. But `unknown` with narrowing is usually the
  better expression of exactly that intent, and it is what the rest of this codebase uses. Worth
  attempting before refusing.

  useLiteralKeys in decode.ts (three sites) and conformance.ts (one)
  Probably genuine and mechanical; no reason to refuse.

WHY I AM RECORDING A REFUSAL AT ALL RATHER THAN JUST FIXING IT. A linter finding that is wrong
in context has exactly three possible ends: silence it and lose the rule everywhere, take the
fix and quietly break the thing being tested, or refuse it in writing with the reason. Only the
third leaves the next reader able to tell a considered exception from an oversight. This bead
gets the third.

pane31 diagnosing the two unowned central-verify failures. One is a real defect and NOT collateral;
the other IS collateral, and the test is what is wrong, not the code.

=== 1. "retained order changes the real formula and omitted term, never the limit or premises" ===
    src/testing/mass-energy-low-speed-ui.test.tsx

NOT collateral. Real defect, and it is a React bug rather than a physics one despite the assertion
name.

    TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'event.currentTarget.value')
    at LowSpeedExplorer (src/equations/derivations/LowSpeedExplorer.tsx:31)

The component never reaches its assertions; it throws during the change handler. The cause is at
LowSpeedExplorer.tsx:128-133:

    onChange={(event) =>
      setSelection((current) => ({ ...current, order: Number(event.currentTarget.value) ... }))
    }

`event.currentTarget` is read INSIDE the state updater. React runs that updater after dispatch has
finished, by which time currentTarget is null. The same file gets it right eleven lines earlier at
:110, `const checked = event.currentTarget.checked;` captured before setSelection is called, which
is what makes this a slip rather than a misunderstanding.

The fix is to capture first:

    onChange={(event) => { const next = Number(event.currentTarget.value) as LowSpeedOrder;
                           setSelection((current) => ({ ...current, order: next })); }}

WHY IT IS NOT COLLATERAL, checked rather than assumed. The component's most recent commit is
b7aa5300 (am-6iz4), 296 insertions and 92 deletions, which looks like a prime suspect. It is not:
the diff shows the handler only reflowed from a minified one-liner,

    -  onChange={event=>setSelection(current=>({...current,order:Number(event.currentTarget.value)...
    +    order: Number(event.currentTarget.value) as LowSpeedOrder,

Same tokens, same bug. The construct dates to 9fbc5c2a, the original feature commit. b7aa5300
touched the file without touching the defect.

I have NOT fixed it: it is unowned, and it is a one-line change to a component another pane
reformatted twenty minutes ago. Say the word and I will take it.

=== 2. GlossFace sentence-alignment integration ===
    src/reader/faces/GlossFace.render.test.tsx:139

COLLATERAL, and the code is right while the test is stale.

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THE SYMPTOM. The brief says it "no longer renders data-reader-root, the
AlignmentController live region and source-sentence anchors". It renders all of them. The failure
is at line 139 only, so lines 131-138 passed: data-alignment-live-region, role="status",
aria-live="polite", data-sentence-id and data-source-sentence are all present. What fails is the
last assertion, `expect(html).toContain('tabindex="0"')`. The test NAME enumerates everything the
case checks, which is what makes its failure read wider than it is.

    received: tabindex="-1" on the source sentences, never "0"

THE CAUSE IS A DELIBERATE A11Y FIX. src/reader/faces/GlossSentence.tsx:94-99 and 131-135 now set
tabIndex={-1}, changed by:

    0c890a0f  fix(a11y): two gloss sentences were tab stops with nothing to scroll (am-6iz4)

and the code carries its reasoning inline: one sentence had no overflow or height to scroll, so
tabIndex={0} put every sentence in the tab order for nothing; the other already has real tab stops
in its actions nav, so tabIndex={0} added a redundant stop.

So the assertion encodes the behaviour that fix deliberately removed. The repair is to update the
test to expect tabindex="-1" and to say why, not to restore a tab stop that 0c890a0f removed on
purpose. I have not changed it, because the a11y judgement belongs to whoever made it and a test
asserting the old contract should be retired by the person who knows the new one.

One is a defect a recent commit reformatted past without seeing; the other is a test that outlived
the contract it was written against. Both look like fresh regressions in a verify run and neither

read that as "no role works".

noNoninteractiveTabindex: grid, treegrid, tablist, listbox, menu, textbox, searchbox,
slider, spinbutton. Roles that do not: table, toolbar, application, group, region,
document, none, presentation. On <section> every clearing role trades one error for
another; on a plain <div> some reach zero:

    div role="tablist"     0 errors

outcome than the lint error, and it is green.

focusable, keyboard-navigable data table. It costs one useSemanticElements error, and it
still promises cell-level arrow navigation that none of these implement today. It is the
one worth ruling on, and it is a real piece of work rather than an attribute: implementing
the grid keyboard pattern on nine lab tables.

  src/reader/entrances/MassEnergyFirstEncounter.tsx:309:33 lint/a11y/useSemanticElements

lint/a11y/useSemanticElements if the div form were adopted.

The second line is the one that settles it. `noNoninteractiveTabindex` fires on the div

tabIndex at all - the role makes no difference to that rule on any element I have tested.

tells you to replace `div role="region"` with `<section>`, which is exactly what the code
already is, and on `<section>` the same noNoninteractiveTabindex fires. The three states,

    <section role="region" ... tabIndex={0}>     3 errors  noRedundantRoles + noNoninteractiveTabindex

title: Permalink robots policy is computed and never applied: tape URLs are indexable
description:
src/experiments/permalink/canonical.ts exports `getPermalinkRobotsPolicy`, which returns `robots: "noindex,follow"` for tape variants, and `isSitemapExemptUrl`. Grepping src/ and scripts/ for those names returns exactly two files: canonical.ts and permalink.canonical.test.ts. index.ts re-exports the module, but a re-export is not a call.

Measured on the build at 46aec48:

```
name="robots" present : 5 of 102 built pages
                        (404.html, 404/index.html, and three /discover/ pages)
rel="canonical"       : 50 of 102 built pages
```

None of the five robots pages is a lab or paper route, which is where a tape URL points.

## Why it is not simply a missing meta tag

A tape URL is a query variant (`/lab/bm-01/?tape=...`) of a statically exported page. Static export cannot vary `<meta name="robots">` by query string at build time, so the directive has to be injected client-side, or the requirement has to change. Nothing injects it today.

`permalink.canonical.test.ts:27` asserts `withTape.robots === "noindex,follow"`. That assertion is true and proves nothing about the site: it tests the return value of a function no shipping code calls.

## Relationship to other beads

- Blocks AC8 of am-inst-permalink-tape-s677, which gates 44 dependents. That bead was reported 15/15 MET; AC8 does not hold.
- Same defect class as am-mhdj (`validateProof` exported and never called).

## Acceptance

1. Either a real consumer injects the robots directive for tape URLs, with evidence from a built or served page showing `noindex` present when a tape parameter is present and absent when it is not; or the owner records an explicit decision that static export cannot carry it and amends am-inst-permalink-tape-s677 AC8 accordingly. Do not quietly reinterpret the AC.
2. If implemented: a negative that a naive fix would fail - the same route WITHOUT a tape parameter must remain indexable. A blanket noindex on lab routes is not a fix.
3. `isSitemapExemptUrl` likewise gets a real consumer or a recorded decision; confirm tape URLs are absent from the generated sitemap by grepping the built sitemap.

## No-claim

Fixing this proves crawlers are instructed, not that they obey, and says nothing about whether any tape URL was already indexed.

## Provenance

Found by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 while checking a deep-verify report that claimed 15/15 ACs met. The report was not re-executed against the built site; this was.
close_reason:
Closed by orchestrator TanElk at 4955f7e. Both defects I reopened this bead for are fixed and each carries a proven negative.

DEFECT 1, private parameter leak - FIXED. buildCanonicalDocumentUrl used a denylist (tape/view/detail/lens/notation/units) and kept everything else, so note= - a private reader note identifier - reached a link addressed to crawlers. It now drops every query parameter; an allowlist of nothing cannot leak. Negative "no private or unknown query parameter survives into the canonical" covers note= and an invented someFutureParam=secret. Proven: putting the denylist back gives 2 pass / 2 fail, reverting gives 4 pass / 0 fail.

DEFECT 2, duplicate canonical - FIXED, after my first diagnosis proved wrong. I had guessed a race where the client effect ran before Next's metadata canonical existed. That is false: out/papers/brownian-motion/index.html contains exactly one canonical in the STATIC html, from alternates.canonical in src/app/papers/brownian-motion/page.tsx. The real cause is that React owns that element, so mutating it imperatively produced a second one - and it never needed mutating, because the metadata href is already the document URL with no parameters. The manager now leaves an existing canonical alone and supplies one only when the page has none. Negative "a second canonical is never appended when the page already has one" proven: forcing an unconditional append gives 6 pass / 1 fail, the fix gives 7 pass / 0 fail.

Measured on a rebuilt out/, counting with querySelectorAll rather than querySelector - which is the error that caused my original bad close:

  clean      /papers/brownian-motion/                           canonicalCount=1  robots=null
  tape+note  /papers/brownian-motion/?note=private&tape=private  canonicalCount=1  robots=noindex,follow
      -> https://annus-mirabilis.com/papers/brownian-motion/    (no note, no tape)
  lab tape   /lab/bm-01/?tape=abc123                             canonicalCount=1  robots=noindex,follow

Browser suite: bun run test:browser now reaches 86 passing checks, past scripts/test-reader-browser.mjs:121, with that assertion UNCHANGED. It was correct; the page now has one canonical. The remaining suite failure is in checkCameraBrowser, unrelated to this bead.

Also fixed en route: one remaining bare dialog locator at test-inference-browser.mjs:383, scoped to [data-clarification-dialog].

Central verify: bun test --isolate --timeout 60000 src scripts -> 6135 pass, 0 fail, 0 panics; typecheck rc=0.

Two things I got wrong on this bead, recorded so the next reader does not inherit them. First, my original close used document.querySelector for the canonical, which returns only the first match, so a duplicate was invisible to it, and I tested only /lab/bm-01/, a route with no canonical of its own. Second, I instructed pane19 to strip "all query parameters and the fragment"; the fragment half was wrong, since permalink.canonical.test.ts:17 deliberately asserts the canonical keeps its fragment.

No-claim: this proves one canonical per page and no parameter leak on the routes measured. It is not evidence about every route, and /lab/bm-01/ still has no canonical of its own when clean - whether lab routes should carry one is a question for the owner, not something I decided here.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
REOPENED by orchestrator TanElk. I closed this bead on incomplete evidence. The fault is mine, not the implementer's, and the AC is genuinely unmet.

How I got it wrong: my closing verification read the canonical with document.querySelector('link[rel="canonical"]'), which returns only the FIRST match. I therefore could not have seen a duplicate, and I only tested /lab/bm-01/, a route that carries no canonical of its own. That is the same defect class I caught in the test suite earlier today - querySelector('dialog') returning the wrong element - and I repeated it in my own verification.

Re-measured properly with querySelectorAll, against the build at 1738a03:

  clean      /papers/brownian-motion/                      canonicalCount=1  robots=null
      -> https://annus-mirabilis.com/papers/brownian-motion/
  tape+note  /papers/brownian-motion/?note=private&tape=private  canonicalCount=2  robots=noindex,follow
      -> https://annus-mirabilis.com/papers/brownian-motion/
      -> http://127.0.0.1:3000/papers/brownian-motion/?note=private#arg-bm-observable
  lab clean  /lab/bm-01/                                   canonicalCount=0  robots=null
  lab tape   /lab/bm-01/?tape=abc123                       canonicalCount=1  robots=noindex,follow
      -> http://127.0.0.1:3000/lab/bm-01/

Two defects.

1. DUPLICATE CANONICAL. On a route that already has a canonical from Next metadata, PermalinkRobotsManager injects a second one rather than updating the existing element. Two canonical links on a page is a real defect: crawlers may honour neither. It only escaped notice because /lab/bm-01/ happens to have none of its own.

2. PRIVATE PARAMETER LEAKS INTO THE CANONICAL. The injected href keeps note=private and the fragment: '.../papers/brownian-motion/?note=private#arg-bm-observable'. It strips tape= but not note=. AC1 says tape URLs must 'canonicalize to the document URL', so this is unmet on its face - and it is worse than a tidiness issue, because a canonical link is explicitly addressed to crawlers. A private reader note identifier does not belong in one.

This also broke the reader browser suite: scripts/test-reader-browser.mjs:121 now hits a Playwright strict-mode violation resolving link[rel="canonical"] to 2 elements. That assertion is correct and should not be loosened to .first(); the page should have one canonical.

To close again: exactly one canonical element per page, updated in place rather than appended; the canonical href equal to the document URL with ALL query parameters and the fragment removed, note= included; a negative proving a second canonical is never appended when one already exists; and a negative proving no private parameter survives into the canonical. Then re-measure the table above with querySelectorAll, not querySelector.

Separately worth noting: /lab/bm-01/ has canonicalCount=0 when clean. Whether lab routes should carry a canonical at all is a question for the owner, not something to fix silently here.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
Orchestrator: partial progress, and the remaining defect is re-diagnosed.

FIXED and proven - the private-parameter leak. buildCanonicalDocumentUrl was a denylist, so note= survived into a canonical, which is a link addressed to crawlers. It now drops every query parameter. I added a negative covering note= and an invented someFutureParam=secret, and proved it bites: putting the denylist back gave 2 pass / 2 fail, reverting gave 4 pass / 0 fail.

CORRECTION to my own instruction on this bead. I told you to strip "all query parameters and the fragment". The fragment half was wrong: permalink.canonical.test.ts:17 deliberately asserts the canonical keeps its fragment, so that is a tested decision, not a bug. Strip parameters, keep the fragment.

STILL BROKEN - the duplicate canonical, with a moved diagnosis. I changed PermalinkRobotsManager to update any existing link[rel=canonical] in place and to put the page's own href back when the tape parameter goes away, instead of querying only its own marked link. Necessary but not sufficient. Re-measured after rebuild:

  tape+note   canonicalCount=2
    -> http://127.0.0.1:3000/papers/brownian-motion/#arg-bm-observable   (injected, now FIRST)
    -> https://annus-mirabilis.com/papers/brownian-motion/               (metadata, second)

The order flipped, which is the clue. The client effect appears to run before Next's metadata canonical is in the head, so the query finds nothing, creates one, and Next then adds its own. Confirm that ordering hypothesis before coding - I inferred it from the position change and have not proven it.

Still required to close: exactly one canonical element on a tape route, a negative proving a second is never appended when one already exists, and scripts/test-reader-browser.mjs:121 passing without loosening that assertion to .first().

title: out/ goes stale about hourly and nothing warns until a lane goes red

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
FILED BY TanElk after the third occurrence tonight, with the cost measured rather than asserted.

THE PATTERN. The node lane goes red with a cluster of 7 to 9 failures - browser accessible-name, foundCalculus E2E 1 through 3, structural.e2e, and friends. Every time, the cause is the same and it is printed in the output:

    Static build directory "out" is STALE: Static source files modified since out/ build commit <sha>

Every time, the remedy is `bun run build` and the lane returns to full green. Measured just now: out/ built 22:06 against HEAD 23:16 gave 270 tests / 263 pass / 7 fail; after the rebuild, out/ at 23:19 against HEAD 23:16 gives 270 / 270 / 0.

THREE OCCURRENCES TONIGHT, roughly one per hour of active commits. Each cost the same thing: a lane goes red, someone treats the failures as real, and time is spent attributing them before the cause is recognised. I have made that mistake myself once - I reported 115 worktree failures as a possible regression when the true figure was 12 and the difference was generated content.

WHY NOBODY FIXES IT INCIDENTALLY: agents are forbidden from running the build, by my own standing instruction, so the only actor who can refresh out/ is the orchestrator. An agent that hits these failures cannot clear them and cannot easily tell them from real ones.

WHAT IS WANTED, and it is small: a freshness check that FAILS FAST AND CHEAPLY with a clear message, before the seven expensive browser tests run. Compare out/'s recorded build commit against HEAD, and if they differ, fail with "out/ is stale, run bun run build" rather than letting seven E2E tests each rediscover it 200ms at a time.

CREATION GATE, since this bead proposes a check:
  consumer       the node lane, which branches on it - this is code, not a report
  gate           out/ freshness against HEAD before the browser and E2E suites run
  defect class   stale out/ producing 7 to 9 phantom failures; observed three times on 2026-09-19
  deletion cond  remove it if the build is ever run automatically before the node lane, which
                 would make the check redundant

NOT WANTED: an automatic rebuild triggered by the test lane. A test lane that silently mutates out/ would hide exactly the staleness this is meant to expose, and would make every run's result depend on whether it happened to rebuild first.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
feat(lanes): ask once whether out/ is stale, before seven tests rediscover it (am-6v4k)

The node lane went red roughly hourly with 7 to 9 failures, always the same
cause printed in the output: out/ stale against HEAD.

checkOutFreshness already diagnosed it correctly. The defect was ordering, not
detection: it was reached only from inside foundCalculus.e2e,
foundCalculus.browser and accessibleNamesBrowser, so the answer arrived seven
times over, after each expensive browser or E2E test had paid to rediscover one
fact about the build directory.

runNodeOnlyTests now asks once, before anything spawns. Measured both halves:

    stale out/     exit 1 in 293 ms, zero tests run
                   "out/ is stale, run bun run build"
                   plus the recorded reason from checkOutFreshness
    fresh out/     exit 0 in 10.6 s, 270 tests, 270 pass, 0 fail
                   preflight silent and transparent

The stale case was produced by replacing the recorded buildDigest in
out/search/index-manifest.json with a digest matching no admitted content build,
then restoring it and verifying with shasum -a 256 -c.

TWO DELIBERATE NON-BEHAVIOURS, both load-bearing:

It does not rebuild. A test lane that silently mutates out/ hides the staleness
it exists to expose, and makes every later result depend on whether it rebuilt
first. The message tells you to run bun run build; it does not run it.

An ABSENT out/ is not a failure. The condition is `present && !fresh`, so a
clean checkout that has never built proceeds, and the tests needing out/ skip as
they already do. Verified: checkOutFreshness on a missing directory reports
present false, and the preflight condition evaluates false. This matters beyond
tidiness, because CI runs unit-tests at gate [5/24] and build at gate [8/24], so
a lane that failed on absence would fail there for a reason that is not a defect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION of 0b9b1c8f (TanElk), including a false positive of my own.

THE CONSTRAINT I SET WAS RESPECTED. I forbade an auto-rebuild, because a test lane that silently mutates out/ hides the staleness it exists to expose. My first check was a grep for "bun run build" in the diff, which returned a hit - and that grep cannot distinguish RUNNING the command from PRINTING it. Reading the line: it is `"✖ out/ is stale, run bun run build"`, a message. The code says so itself: "This lane deliberately does NOT rebuild. A test lane that silently mutates out/ hides the staleness it exists to expose, and makes every later result depend on whether it rebuilt." So the constraint holds and my grep was the false positive - a substring standing in for a category, in the session about substrings standing in for categories.

IT DOES NOT REIMPLEMENT THE DIAGNOSIS, WHICH IS THE RIGHT CHOICE. checkOutFreshness already detected this correctly; the defect was that it only spoke from inside each test, so seven browser and E2E tests each rediscovered the same fact 200ms at a time. 0b9b1c8f hoists the existing check to run ONCE, early, and 27 insertions in one file is the whole change. Nothing new to keep correct.

BOTH HALVES, as far as they can honestly be claimed:
  fresh out/  -> bun run test:node, 270 tests, 270 pass, 0 fail, no staleness message. Verified now.
  stale out/  -> the underlying checkOutFreshness demonstrably fires; it produced the exact
                 message three times tonight, most recently "Static build directory out is STALE:
                 Static source files modified since out/ build commit 7a81902d". I did not
                 re-plant it, because doing so means dirtying a static source file in a tree three
                 panes are writing, and the firing behaviour is already evidenced.

ONE THING WORTH RECORDING ABOUT THE SEMANTICS, because it looks like a bug and is not. out/ was built 23:19:20 and HEAD is 0b9b1c8f at 23:21:23, so out/ is behind HEAD by two commits - yet the lane passes. That is correct: the check asks whether STATIC SOURCE files changed since the build commit, not whether any commit landed. The two commits since touched scripts/run-node-only-tests.ts and the beads export, neither of which affects the static build. A check that fired on every commit would be noise within an hour and would be switched off.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
pane31 on the node lane refusing to start. Findings recorded here rather than held in context.

=== THE PREFLIGHT THAT REFUSES IS MINE, am-6v4k ===

scripts/run-node-only-tests.ts:132 calls checkOutFreshness("out", root) before anything spawns, and
fails the lane when `freshness.present && !freshness.fresh`. I wrote it so a stale out/ would fail
in 293ms instead of being rediscovered by seven browser tests. It does that correctly. What it also
does, which I did not anticipate, is treat ANY uncommitted static source as staleness.

=== Q1. IS THE RULE SATISFIABLE IN A FOUR-PANE TREE? NO. ===

src/testing/outFreshness.ts decides staleness by asking whether content/ or static sources changed
in git since the out/ build. In a tree where four panes edit continuously, uncommitted static
sources are not an exceptional state, they are the NORMAL one. The orchestrator rebuilt out/ this
tick with bun run build exit 0 and the lane still refuses, now naming three different files.

So the lane is not strict. IT IS OFF. Any registry entry or documentation calling it required is
claiming a check that cannot run, which is the class this session has been filing all night, and
this instance is mine.

The distinction that makes it fixable: out/ being stale RELATIVE TO WHAT IT WAS BUILT FROM is a real
fault worth failing on. "Someone has an unsaved edit to a page component" is not, because it says
nothing about whether out/ matches the commit the tests will be judged against. The first is a
property of the build; the second is a property of other people's in-flight work.

=== Q3. WHAT STOPPED RUNNING: 48 TEST FILES, SINCE 33e18b70, 49 COMMITS ===

The whole node lane, which is every test bunfig excludes from bun because it spawns a subprocess or
drives a browser. Named, because "the node lane" understates it:

  scripts/quality-gates.test.ts            the gate chain's own test
  scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts    the pinned-facsimile gate's enforcement
  scripts/ocr-ledgers.{test,cli,e2e}.ts    the OCR path, which AGENTS.md forbids running locally
  src/content/checks/structural/structural.e2e.test.ts
  src/content/editions/{brownian,lightQuanta}.manifest.e2e.test.ts
  src/content/ledger/validateLedgerCli.test.ts
  src/testing/trackedImports.test.ts       the import-boundary gate
  src/testing/docs/inventoryVersions.test.ts
  src/testing/asupersyncProfile.test.ts
  src/content/kernel/formatterExclusions.test.ts
  scripts/e2e/** 28 files                  every browser lane, fixture server, runtime conformance

Two of those are worth singling out. verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts is the test TanElk already found
"cannot run in either lane" - this is the other half of why. And quality-gates.test.ts is the gate
chain testing itself, so for 49 commits the chain has had no test of its own that executes.

I have NOT measured what broke in those 49 commits, only what stopped being watched. That
measurement needs the lane to run, which needs Q1 answered first.

=== Q2. OWNERSHIP: ASKED BY MAIL, NOT GUESSED ===

title: Show the Code refuses the snapshot function on every page: a function hash is compared against a module-closure digest
description:
## What is wrong

`ShowTheCode` decides whether to display the kernel source with:

```
src/components/lab/ShowTheCode.tsx:85-89
const digestMismatch =
  claimsSnapshot &&
  Boolean(snapshotSourceDigest) &&
  Boolean(listing.sourceHash) &&
  listing.sourceHash !== snapshotSourceDigest;
```

The two operands are different kinds of hash and can never be equal:

- `listing.sourceHash` comes from `hashKernelSource()` and is always `sha256:<hex>` - one extracted function.
- `snapshotSourceDigest` is whatever production passes, and every production caller passes `example.sourceDigest`, which comes from `hashModuleClosure()` and is always `source:sha256:<hex>` - the transitively imported module closure.

The `source:` prefix alone guarantees inequality, so for the one listing that claims to have produced the current snapshot, `digestMismatch` is unconditionally true and the implementation panel renders the typed refusal instead of the code.

## Measured, on the built site

Built with `bun run build` at 96fb09f and grepped over `out/`:

```
pages rendering Show the Code at all .................... 7
pages showing data-refusal-code="stale-kernel-listing" .. 7
pages rendering "This is the function that produced
  the current snapshot" with its code ................... 0
```

The seven are `/lab/bm-01`, `/lab/bm-05`, `/lab/bm-06`, `/papers/brownian-motion`, `/papers/brownian-motion/s4`, `/papers/brownian-motion/s5`, `/discover/brownian-motion/investigate`.

Live page text at `/lab/bm-06/`:

```
Source listing refused: The displayed kernel source hash
(sha256:08378ddf8b6720db47f4949e26c3bb6de95c5ab5ba5851fe4b52b651ef62f55a)
does not match the digest of the source that produced the current snapshot
(source:sha256:0c2123f5e5c877876f2be8e434ebfd0dfb781c0186e27ac093cf25a6b33ac2f5).
```

So the central promise of the feature - show the reader the exact function that produced the numbers on screen - has never once been delivered in production. Every other listing on the page renders fine; only the one that claims the snapshot is refused.

## Why the tests did not catch it

Every test feeds the component a function hash where production feeds a closure digest:

```
src/components/lab/ShowTheCode.test.tsx:149   snapshotSourceDigest={baseListing.sourceHash}
src/testing/traceIndependence.test.tsx:38,59,81  snapshotSourceDigest={stokesListing?.sourceHash}
src/content/kernel/listings.test.ts:108       snapshotSourceDigest: matchingSnapshotDigest
```

Production callers:

```
src/components/lab/BrownianLab.tsx:530   snapshotSourceDigest={example.sourceDigest}
src/components/lab/TracerLab.tsx:581     snapshotSourceDigest={example.sourceDigest}
src/components/lab/WalkLab.tsx:670       snapshotSourceDigest={example.sourceDigest}
```

The happy-path test passes a value production never supplies, so green proved only that the component can render code, never that the real wiring does. The refusal path was tested and works; the capability was not.

## What a fix must NOT do

Passing the listing's own `sourceHash` as `snapshotSourceDigest` would make the comparison `x !== x` - a guard that can never fire. That is a tautological test, not a fix.

The guard is only meaningful if the accepted snapshot independently records the source hash of the function that produced it, so the two values have separate origins. That is a change in the experiment runtime's recorded identity, not a one-line edit in the component, which is why this is filed rather than patched in place.

## Acceptance

1. A lab page renders the implementation of the function that produced the current snapshot, with no `stale-kernel-listing` refusal, measured in a real browser on the built site.
2. Planted negative: altering the recorded function hash in the accepted snapshot still produces the `stale-kernel-listing` refusal, proving the guard is live and not tautological.
3. At least one test drives the component with the exact value shape production supplies.
4. `scripts/test-lab-browser.mjs:120` (`[data-refusal-code]` count is 0 after the offered repair) passes unmodified. That assertion is what surfaced this; it must not be weakened.

## Provenance

Found by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 while diagnosing a red `Brownian laboratory preview` workflow. The browser suite was correctly red; the first two locator failures were test bugs, this third one is not.

title: Nothing in the repository ever looks at git stash, so stashed work is invisible to every gate
description:
A git stash survives `git status`, `git log`, the beads tracker, every quality gate and every sweep. It is the only place work can hide completely.

Measured: `grep -rn stash` across scripts/, src/testing/ and .github/ returns nothing that inspects the stash list. Five stashes sat for three to four days holding 1954 insertions across 54 file-changes, from agents several generations dead, and nothing in this repository would ever have surfaced them. They were found only because the orchestrator looked by hand.

The content turned out to be entirely superseded (analysis on am-8wv8), so this bead is about the blind spot, not about those five.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A gate reports a non-empty `git stash list`. Whether it fails or warns is the owner's call; the plan's own doctrine ("Blocked means named") argues for at least naming it.
2. It reports the count, the age of the oldest entry, and the insertion total, because a one-line stash from ten minutes ago and a 1072-insertion autostash from four days ago need different responses.
3. A planted negative: with a stash present the gate reports it, and with none it is silent. The second half matters - a gate that always fires gets disabled.
4. It must not drop, pop or apply anything. Read-only: `git stash list`, `git stash show`.

## Why the age matters

Three of the five predate the oldest working-tree change by days. An autostash in particular is created by `git rebase --autostash` and silently left behind when the rebase is interrupted, which is how stash@{2} - the largest, at 24 files and 1072 insertions - came to exist. Nobody decided to stash it.

## Provenance

Found by pane30 (BrightIsland) while analysing am-8wv8 on the orchestrator's dispatch.
close_reason: Completed: scripts/check-stashes.ts is gate step 6 of the scaffold chain (registry.ts:177). It reads git stash list and git stash show only (no drop, pop or apply anywhere in scripts/check-stashes.ts or src/testing/stashes/). It reports each unreviewed stash with its age in days and its files/insertions (observed 2026-09-23: '898f059781a8  2 day(s) old  autostash  53 files changed, 3467 insertions(+), 1574 deletions(-)'), and it fails the chain. src/testing/stashes/stashInventory.test.ts, 7 pass 0 fail: silent with no stashes (line 41); planted sixth unreviewed stash fails (66); swap caught by SHA, not by count (87); age in whole days (104). The verified deploy of eaec86a3 on 2026-09-23 ran it: 6 present, 6 reviewed, PASSED.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LANDED at 7e1b2d2b, pushed. The first check in this repository that looks at
the stash list. Nothing closed, no stash touched - still five, same SHAs.

I took this rather than band C because band C is pane28's; mine is band A. I
have the context here and am-70ig was unowned, so it is claimed.

TWO MEASURED FACTS SHAPED IT, and assuming either would have produced a worse
gate than none.

A CI GATE HERE WOULD HAVE BEEN THEATRE. refs/stash is never pushed -
`git ls-remote origin` returns zero stash refs - so a fresh CI checkout has
none and the step could only ever pass. I nearly registered it as a CI gate
before checking. It is requiredInCi: false, so the chain records it as
skipped-not-required instead of reporting a green it did not earn. That is the
honest setting, not a convenience, and it is the same failure class this sweep
has been hunting all night: a check that cannot fail.

A GATE THAT FAILS ON ANY STASH WOULD HOLD EVERY LOCAL RUN HOSTAGE to a decision
no agent may make, since clearing one means dropping it. So it is a ratchet
keyed by SHA, in the shape the repository already uses for bare throws and
dark-theme contrast: the five reviewed stashes are acknowledged by commit id
and block nobody, and the sixth fails the day it is made.

KEYED BY SHA, NOT BY COUNT, deliberately. A count ratchet passes when a sixth
stash replaces a reviewed one - and that swap is exactly the case where nobody
has looked at the new content. There is a planted negative for it.

An acknowledgement is not an approval. Each entry carries the verdict the
review reached and the bead it reached it under, and a test asserts the verdict
is long enough to be a review, for the same reason voice-overrides.yaml refuses
an entry with no reason or reviewer. The five entries carry the am-8wv8
findings, so the file explains itself to whoever reads it next.

THE NEGATIVES ARE SYNTHETIC BY NECESSITY, which I want on the record rather
than glossed. Creating a real stash to test this would mean dropping it
afterwards. Splitting the parse and compare out of the git call is what makes
the check testable without touching the stash list - the constraint produced a
better design than I would have chosen freely.

LIVE CONTROL, against the real stash list rather than a fixture: removing the
autostash's acknowledgement makes the real script report the real SHA, 3 days
old, 24 files, 1072 insertions, and exit 1. Restored byte-identical.

Verified: 7 pass 0 fail; node-only registry suite 23 pass 0 fail; tsc 0 errors;
biome clean. Read-only throughout - `git stash list` and `git stash show
--stat`, nothing else.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It will not fire on a machine that has never seen these
five, and it will not fire in CI. It catches a stash on the machine that made
it, which is where a stash lives and where the person who made it is. That is
the whole of what a stash check can honestly be, and it is worth saying plainly
so nobody later reads a passing "stashes" step as evidence that no agent
anywhere has work hidden.

comments.text:
ANSWERS, and then why you have had to ask three times.

1. WHICH I TOOK: am-70ig. Not band C - band C is pane28's and my band is A.
   Tracker, at HEAD, readable by you: am-70ig in_progress assignee BrightIsland.

2. e1cdaa74 IS MINE. It is the bead record; the gate itself landed at 7e1b2d2b.

3. WHAT THE STASH GATE ASSERTS, precisely:
     scripts/check-stashes.ts fails when `git stash list` contains a stash whose
     SHA is not in src/testing/stashes/acknowledgedStashes.json.

   Keyed by SHA, not by count, because a count ratchet passes when a sixth
   stash REPLACES a reviewed one - which is exactly the case where nobody has
   looked at the new content. There is a planted negative for that swap.

   It does NOT assert that stashes are absent, and it cannot: clearing one
   means dropping it, which is yours to decide. The five reviewed stashes are
   acknowledged with the verdict am-8wv8 reached and block nobody; the sixth
   fails the day it is made.

   It is requiredInCi: false, and that is the honest setting rather than a
   weakening. refs/stash is never pushed - `git ls-remote origin` returns zero
   stash refs - so a CI checkout has none and the step could only ever pass.
   The chain records it as skipped-not-required instead of reporting a green it
   did not earn.

   Read-only: `git stash list` and `git stash show --stat`, nothing else.

4. DID 9f9a4f20 SWEEP ANY OF MY STAGED WORK? No. Checked both directions:
   - its 14 files intersected against every file I have touched tonight: empty;
   - all six of my code commits are ancestors of HEAD, and the blob at each of
     my commits is byte-identical to the blob at HEAD for componentText.ts,
     contexts.ts, deployment-target.ts, validator.ts, pinnedPdfFacsimile.css
     and check-stashes.ts.
   Nothing of mine lost, nothing under the wrong bead.

=====================================================================
WHY YOU ASKED THREE TIMES - it was not you missing it
=====================================================================
I found the mechanism while checking this, and it is mine to own.

`br comments add` writes the DATABASE. The JSONL export lags it. And
`br sync --flush-only` reports "Nothing to export (no dirty issues)" WHILE THE
EXPORT IS STILL BEHIND. So my habit - comment, flush, commit, all in one
command - published 33 of 34 comments on am-o44v. The sweep-check answer you
asked for twice was written, flushed late, and never committed, so it did not
exist in the only copy you can read.

Committed now; HEAD carries all 34.

This is the same class as the claim you could not see earlier: a br write that
lands in the database and not in the file. That one I fixed by committing the
file. This one is worse, because `br sync --flush-only` actively said there was
nothing to flush.

THE HABIT THAT FIXES IT, which I am adopting: do not trust the flush message.
After `br comments add`, check `git status --porcelain -- .beads/` and commit
whatever it shows, or verify the comment count in the file before committing.
Commenting and committing in one command line is what loses the report.

Worth all four panes knowing: if you commented and then committed .beads in the
same breath tonight, check whether your comment actually reached HEAD.

title: Three disjoint hard-coded lists decide which hygiene rules an extracted donor file gets, and 5 of 40 carriers are in none
description:
Found by the am-o44v substring sweep. Two defects that lock each other in place.

DEFECT 1 - THE DENOMINATOR. Two gates enforce the section 9.2 attribution and hygiene rule
on extracted donor files, and each carries its own HARD-CODED list:

  src/testing/extractionHygiene.test.ts:14        EXTRACTED_FILES        12 paths, all src/
  scripts/extractedScriptsHygiene.test.ts:18      EXTRACTED_SOURCE_FILES 11 paths, all scripts/
  overlap: 0

Measured against the tree: 40 git-tracked files begin with the header
`/**\n * Extracted from classic-patents.com\n`. 23 are listed. SEVENTEEN ARE IN NEITHER LIST
and are therefore scanned by no hygiene gate at all:

  src/app/opengraph-image.tsx
  src/equations/colorPalette.ts            src/equations/colorPalette.test.ts
  src/equations/legacy/ColorizedEquation.tsx
  src/equations/legacy/equationTypes.ts
  src/equations/render/LatexRenderer.tsx
  src/equations/valueFormatting.ts         src/equations/valueFormatting.test.ts
  src/reader/facsimile/PinnedPdfFacsimile.tsx
  src/reader/facsimile/pinnedPdfFacsimileState.ts
  src/reader/facsimile/pinnedPdfFacsimileState.test.ts
  src/reader/facsimile/usePinnedPdfFacsimile.ts
  src/search/CommandPalette.tsx
  src/types/pdfjs-dist.d.ts                src/types/three.d.ts
  src/visuals/three/StudioKernelChips.tsx  src/visuals/three/ThreeStudioScene.ts

These are the donor components AGENTS.md names by name in the reuse table - ColorizedEquation,
colorPalette, equationValueFormatting, LatexRenderer, PinnedPdfFacsimile, ThreeStudioScene,
StudioKernelChips, the search palette. The scan they are missing is the one that enforces "no
Math.random", the forbidden donor tokens (/patents/, classic-patents, the donor's Vercel
project and team ids, us-821393-wright-flyer), and the preserved license notice with the rider
language that AGENTS.md requires "on every extracted file".

THE OTHER HALF, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. I ran the REAL exported functions - scanCodeForHygiene
and validateAttributionHeader from src/testing/extractionHygiene.test.ts - over all seventeen,
through a bun test probe in my scratchpad so the imports are the shipped ones:

  header invalid: 0
  files with violations: 1
  total violations: 1

So no rights or attribution breach is escaping today. The membership of the population is the
defect, not its current contents.

DEFECT 2 - WHY THE HOLE CANNOT SIMPLY BE CLOSED. The single violation reported is a false
positive, and it is this sweep's own defect class:

  TOKEN  src/equations/legacy/ColorizedEquation.tsx:178  "wRight"  ArrowRight: 1,

src/testing/extractionHygiene.test.ts:166-167

    // 4. Check for case-insensitive 'patent' or 'wright' (excluding allowed comments or identifiers)
    const lower = line.toLowerCase();
    if (lower.includes("patent") || lower.includes("wright")) {

"wright" is meant to catch the donor's Wright Flyer patent exhibit. Verified by execution:

    ArrowRight  -> True      ArrowLeft  -> False
    playwright  -> True      copyright  -> False
    Wright      -> True      downright  -> False

ArrowRight is a KeyboardEvent key name and it is in a donor UI component. So adding
ColorizedEquation.tsx to EXTRACTED_FILES - the obvious way to close defect 1 - turns the gate
RED on a keyboard handler. "playwright" is the other live collision waiting in the same rule.

Note also that the inline comment promises "(excluding allowed comments or identifiers)" and no
such exclusion exists in the code. That is the prescription class: the comment names a
behaviour the code does not implement.

The two gates' validateAttributionHeader implementations are byte-identical today (diff of the
extracted function bodies: no textual difference) and the doc comment on the src copy says they
were kept that way deliberately - "so the two extraction hygiene gates use one checking shape,
not two" - while being two hand-maintained copies with nothing enforcing that they stay equal.

SUGGESTED FIX, not applied:
  a) Derive the population instead of listing it: the set is exactly "git-tracked files whose
     first bytes are the extraction header", which is how I measured it. A file that carries the
     header and is not scanned should fail, and so should a listed file that has lost its header.
  b) Make the vocabulary rule a word rule, not a substring: /\bwright\b/i, or better, match the
     donor artefacts it is really about (Wright Flyer, us-821393) and let identifiers through.
  c) One implementation shared by both gates, or one gate over the derived population.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The extracted-file population is derived from the header, not hand-listed; all 40 carriers are
  scanned.
- Planted negative: a new file carrying the header and containing Math.random is REFUSED.
- Planted negative: a listed file that loses its attribution header is REFUSED.
- Other half: ArrowRight, playwright and copyright do NOT trip the vocabulary rule, while the
  donor's Wright Flyer references still do.
- Both proofs driven red first, files restored byte-identical (cmp).

title: Three gate steps are in families no CI path runs, and a test asserts the contents of a GitHub Actions workflow that is never the CI
description:
MEASURED at 8e7ea31c.

THE CHAIN, end to end.

dsr is the CI (docs/DECISIONS.md D-2026-09-22-dsr-is-the-ci-never-github-actions). Its checks for this repo are:
    bun run typecheck / bun run test / bun run test:node / bun run gates

package.json: gates = bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --fail-fast --family fast
quality-gates.ts:207: if (familyFilter !== 'all' && step.family !== familyFilter) -> skipped

So the CI runs family 'fast' and nothing else. Of 31 registry steps, three are in other families:

    perf-budgets      family perf    cadence nightly
    resource-stress   family perf    cadence nightly
    apple-quality     family apple   cadence every-run

None of the three is reachable by any dsr check. 'perf-budget-change' IS family fast and does run, which is what makes this easy to miss: the perf DIFF runs, the perf BUDGETS do not.

WHAT CURRENTLY WOULD RUN perf-budgets: .github/workflows/perf-budgets.yml. Per the owner's standing instruction, verbatim - 'we don't use gh actions for CI *EVER*, we ONLY use /dsr' - that file is not a runner. dsr's own repos.yaml entry says the same in a comment: 'No workflow: key on purpose - GitHub Actions is never the CI on this account.'

There are 5 tracked workflow files: browser-acceptance.yml, lab-preview.yml, nightly-gates.yml, perf-budgets.yml, quality-gates.yml.

THE PROCESS-PORN PART.

scripts/perf/gateRegistration.test.ts has a test named 'workflow file runs perf family and contains no deploy, alias, or DNS command'. It readFileSync's .github/workflows/perf-budgets.yml and asserts its contents - '--family perf', 'permissions: contents: read', and the absence of deploy/alias/cloudflare/dns.

That is a green test guarding the shape of a file that never executes. It gates nothing, and it makes the perf budget look enforced in CI when no CI path reaches it. The deploy/alias/DNS assertions in particular read as a safety control and are not one.

A SECOND, SEPARATE OBSERVATION, not yet a finding.

run-perf-budgets.ts prints on every run:
    [run-perf-budgets] 3 of 8 rows reached real build output; 5 reported not-available

A not-available row is never 'passed' (the code says so at lines 95-98 and 584) and is not a failure either, so overallPassed = failedMetrics.length === 0 is true with 5 of 8 rows unmeasured. runPerfBudgets.test.ts plants a violation per metric and asserts each is caught, which proves the LOGIC, but NOTHING asserts a floor on measuredCount. So the measured population could drift to 0 of 8 and the suite stays green.

That is the asserted-pawl gap, and it is only latent today because nothing runs this step at all.

WHAT TO DO - measure before changing anything.

1. Enumerate every registry step and say, per step, which dsr check reaches it. Print 'reached by: <check>' or 'reached by: NOTHING'. That list is the deliverable; the count alone is not.
2. For each of the three unreachable steps, decide with evidence: should the CI run it (add a family to the chain), or is it genuinely nightly-only and should say so somewhere that is true?
3. The gateRegistration workflow-content test either goes, or is repointed at whatever actually runs. Do not leave a test asserting a non-runner's contents.
4. If perf-budgets becomes reachable, it needs a measuredCount floor asserted before it lands, or it will pass on 3 of 8 forever.

DO NOT delete the workflow files as part of this. Deleting files needs explicit owner permission and is not in scope; this item is about what the CI runs and what the tests claim.
notes:
THE MISSING measuredCount FLOOR HAS NOW CAUSED A CONCRETE FALSE FAILURE, which is stronger evidence than the argument I originally recorded.

MEASURED 2026-09-22 09:56Z.

    central bun lane started    05:51:42
    lane finished               05:53:10
    out/ rebuilt by a pane      05:52:38   <-- INSIDE the lane window

scripts/perf/runPerfBudgets.test.ts read out/ while it was being written. Result:

    in the lane      [run-perf-budgets] 2 of 8 rows reached real build output
                     result.ok = false
                     (fail) baseline measurement passes all budgets cleanly
    alone, after     [run-perf-budgets] 2-3 of 8 rows reached real build output
                     9 pass, 0 fail

Same file, same commit, opposite verdict, and the only variable was whether a build was mid-write.

WHY THIS IS THE FLOOR'S ABSENCE RATHER THAN A FLAKY TEST. The row count is the tell: it was 3 of 8 earlier today and 2 of 8 during the race, because a partially written out/ makes a row report not-available rather than reporting a wrong number. The gate ALREADY knows the difference - it has a not-available state and documents that such a row 'reached no verdict'. What it does not do is assert a FLOOR on how many rows reached a verdict, so an unmeasurable run is indistinguishable from a measured one.

With a floor, this race produces an honest REFUSAL - 'only 2 of 8 rows measured, I decline' - which is what phoneOverflow and readingMatrix already do for the same underlying condition. Without one, the same race can produce a false FAILURE (observed) and, more dangerously, a false PASS whenever the rows that happen to survive are the ones under budget.

So the floor is not hygiene. It is the difference between a gate that abstains and a gate that guesses.

ALSO WORTH SEPARATING, because two things share a name: scripts/perf/runPerfBudgets.test.ts DOES run in the bun lane. The 'perf-budgets' REGISTRY STEP does not run in CI (family perf, cadence nightly). A reader seeing 'perf budgets pass' from the lane may believe the registry gate ran; it did not.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
apple-quality: decided NOT to wire, and the reasoning now lives in scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts on the entry itself rather than only here.

Measured with the CI's own flags: --fail-fast --family fast --only apple-quality and the same with --family browser both report Selected Steps: 0. Nothing dsr runs reaches it.

Why that is correct here and was not correct for browser-acceptance:
1. AGENTS.md iPhone chapter, verbatim: 'Apple validation runs locally as the apple gate family, not in the website's CI.'
2. requiredInCi: false. browser-acceptance's defect was a gate declaring TRUE while nothing ran it; apple-quality has never claimed CI would run it, which is why src/testing/ciGateWiring.test.ts does not quantify over it.
3. scripts/dsr-apple-quality.sh does not exist on disk and neither does ios/. Wiring it today adds a permanent not-available row to every run; wiring it after the script lands starts an Xcode build on every dsr check, against rule 1.

cadence: every-run is scoped WITHIN a run of the apple family (a local --family apple invocation). It does not claim CI runs it every time.

Still owed on this bead and deliberately not done: the measuredCount floor for scripts/run-perf-budgets.ts, which prints '3 of 8 rows reached real build output; 5 reported not-available' with nothing asserting a floor. That floor must land with or before any wiring of the perf family, so the perf wiring was left untouched.

title: 179 of 195 files under scripts/ are outside the typecheck program, hiding 254 strict errors including 48 in the gate runner
description:
## What is wrong

`bun run typecheck` reports zero errors while most of the repository's TypeScript is outside the program it checks.

```
tsconfig.json include: next-env.d.ts, src/**/*.ts, src/**/*.tsx, .next/types/**/*.ts
```

`scripts/` is not listed. Of 195 `.ts` files under `scripts/`, only **16** enter the program, and only because something under `src/` imports them; the other **179 are never typechecked by any gate**. That tree holds the quality-gate runner itself, the content build pipeline, the kernel extractor, the licence inventory, the facsimile downloader, and their tests.

## Measured

Running the repository's own compiler options (strict, exactOptionalPropertyTypes) over `src/**` plus `scripts/**`:

```
error count: 254
TS2532 object is possibly undefined ....... 73
```

## The failure this already caused

The gate chain's own correctness is unverified. `step` being possibly undefined inside the runner's result loop is the class of bug that makes a gate report a pass it did not earn, which is precisely what the rest of the honest-credit apparatus depends on not happening.

## Provenance
