title: The Brownian DoD gate asserts the facsimile is absent at a path the project never used, while it is pinned at the canonical one
description:
Shape 1 (am-o44v): a property asserted in one place and contradicted in another, where the
assertion can never notice because it names a path the project never used.

src/testing/dodBrownian.test.ts:46

    const facsimileExists = fs.existsSync(path.join(process.cwd(), "public/ap-17-549.pdf"));
    assert.equal(
      facsimileExists,
      false,
      "Facsimile scan ap-17-549.pdf must be absent at this milestone",
    );

MEASURED:

    public/ap-17-549.pdf                exists=false
    public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf    exists=true   sha256 c42f9ac278283bda...
    bun test src/testing/dodBrownian.test.ts  ->  9 pass, 0 fail

The SHA-256 prefix matches the one AGENTS.md records for the pinned Brownian facsimile, and
AGENTS.md's own naming convention is `public/papers/pdfs/<key>.pdf`. So the facsimile has been
pinned since 2026-09-17, with a provenance receipt at docs/provenance/ap-17-549.md, and this gate
still records it as absent - because it is looking somewhere else.

EVERY OTHER REFERENCE IN THE REPO USES THE CANONICAL PATH. Greped, eight of them:

    src/content/editions/brownianInventory.ts:165        "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"
    src/content/editions/brownian.facsimile.test.ts:352  "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"
    src/content/editions/brownian.inventory.test.ts:171  "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"
    src/content/editions/editions.refusals.test.ts:52    "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"
    src/content/editions/editions.refusals.test.ts:394   "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"
    src/content/provenance/receipt.test.ts:412           "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"
    src/content/provenance/receipt.test.ts:467           "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"
    src/testing/fixtures/provenance/ap-17-549.md:69      "public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf"

dodBrownian.test.ts:46 is the ONLY occurrence of the `public/ap-17-549.pdf` spelling anywhere in
src/, scripts/ or docs/. receipt.test.ts:478 even comments "Live pass: auditPinnedAssets succeeds
on real pinned assets because public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf exists" - the same repo, the same
file, opposite recorded facts.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TYPO. A definition-of-done gate exists to make a milestone
observable: when the facsimile lands, the "must be absent" assertion is supposed to go RED and
force someone to advance the DoD record. Pointed at a path the project never uses, it cannot
go red for any amount of work, so the milestone can never advance and the gate's green is not
evidence about the milestone at all.

SCOPE - ONE LINE OF FIVE, and I checked the rest rather than sweeping them in. The same file
asserts four content directories are absent:
    content/misconceptions/brownian-motion   content/results/brownian-motion
    content/shelf/brownian-motion            content/margin/brownian-motion
None of those four exists under content/ today (the directory holds aliases, arguments,
bibliography, datasets, editorial, equations, experiments, foundations, notation, papers,
quantities, reasoning, scenarios, source-blocks), so those four assertions are correct and
current. Only the facsimile line names a path that was never the convention.

SUGGESTED FIX, not applied: point line 46 at public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf. That turns the
assertion RED, which is the correct outcome - the facsimile IS pinned - so the DoD record for
item 2 needs updating in the same change rather than the assertion being relaxed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The DoD gate reads the canonical path public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf.
- The milestone record for Brownian DoD item 2 reflects that the facsimile is pinned, with the
  receipt at docs/provenance/ap-17-549.md cited.
- Planted negative: the assertion as written today is confirmed to go RED once the path is
  corrected, BEFORE the DoD record is updated, so the sequence is observed and not assumed.
- Other half: the four content-directory assertions still pass, and a future authored
  misconceptions ledger still turns its assertion red.

title: A ledger's first line says REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION even when nothing has been reviewed
description:
Raised while producing the first real ledger, ap-18-639 (am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z),
2026-09-20, LilacValley. Raising rather than fixing, because the marker grammar belongs to
am-edn-ledger-validator-edv and changing it would invalidate every fixture in the tree.

THE PROBLEM, in one line: the first line of every ledger is

    --- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---

and the file is named `<key>-reviewed.txt`, but under the owner's am-1hv0 decision-1 ruling a
ledger can now legitimately be a MACHINE DRAFT WITH HAND CORRECTION that no human has read. The
grammar token and the filename both say "reviewed" and the artefact is not.

Today's mitigation, which is real but indirect: the ledger file carries no header by design, so
the status lives in the receipt (`transcription.ledgerStatus`, one of not-started, in-progress,
corrected, corrected-second-read, reviewed), and docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md now says in prose
what the artefact is, who drafted it, under what authority, and that it satisfies no criterion
requiring human review. That is the right home for provenance.

But a reader who opens the .txt sees the word REVIEWED and nothing else. A reader who greps the
repository for "reviewed" finds the filename. Neither reaches the receipt. The single most
load-bearing editorial distinction in this project - reviewed versus not - is carried only by a
file the reader has to know to go and find.

This is not urgent and nothing is currently mislabelled: ledgerStatus is in-progress, editors is
empty, and open-german-source-mass-energy is unfilled in docs/OWNERS.md. It becomes urgent the
first time someone cites a ledger as reviewed because its first line says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The format owner decides and records one of: the marker grammar becomes status-neutral (for
   example `--- TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---`) with a migration for every fixture and the one
   real ledger; or the grammar stays and the mismatch is documented at the top of
   LEDGER_FORMAT.md and in AGENTS.md's ledger paragraph, so the word is known to be a token
   rather than a claim.
2. If the grammar stays, `validate-ledger` prints the receipt's ledgerStatus in its summary line,
   so the tool that reads the ledger always states what the ledger is.
3. Whichever is chosen, a test asserts that a ledger whose receipt says in-progress cannot be
   reported anywhere as reviewed, with a planted negative confirmed RED.
close_reason: Resolved by the same change as am-wisq and folded into commit ea3923a8, which names both beads. This bead's defect - a ledger's first line says REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION even when nothing has been reviewed - is exactly what the receipt gate now prevents: declaring REVIEWED requires transcription.ledgerStatus reviewed in the receipt, refused as declared-review-unearned. Before it, validateLedger.ts:600 carried a comment saying 'what makes REVIEWED a claim rather than a synonym is the receipt gate below' and there was no receipt gate below; declaredStatus was read and compared only against other page markers, never against the receipt, so any transcript could open REVIEWED and the validator agreed. Same evidence as am-wisq: two plants, the second showing a symmetric gate reddens only the explicit asymmetry assertion. All four real transcripts open MACHINE DRAFT against in-progress receipts, so the gate fires on none of them. Closed by the orchestrator, not by the pane that wrote it.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
DUPLICATE of am-wisq (P1, TanElk's), which describes the same defect and states the mechanism better. Recommend closing this one in favour of am-wisq; the detail that was only here - the receipt mitigation, the filename half of the defect, suggested acceptance criteria, and the am-j92v ordering constraint - is now ported into a comment on am-wisq, so nothing is lost by closing this.

Not closing it myself; closure is orchestrator-only. LilacValley.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
FOLDED INTO ea3923a8 (am-wisq), and criterion 2 is MOOT rather than skipped - saying so explicitly as instructed.

This bead asked the format owner to choose between (a) a status-neutral grammar with a migration, or (b) keeping the grammar and documenting the mismatch. The owner chose NEITHER: the grammar became status-BEARING - MACHINE DRAFT TRANSCRIPTION and REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION are both legal tokens and the transcript states its own status in its own first line. Criterion 2 ('if the grammar stays, validate-ledger prints the receipt's ledgerStatus in its summary') is conditional on branch (b), which was not taken, so it is not implemented and should not be.

Criterion 1 is satisfied: the decision is made and recorded, all four transcripts and eight fixtures carry the status-bearing token, and the filename is <key>-machine-draft.txt rather than -reviewed.txt.

Criterion 3 is the test in that commit. 'Cannot be reported ANYWHERE as reviewed' was checked rather than assumed: the only other places in src or scripts that ever claimed review are two COMMENTS recording that coverageReport's 'Reviewed ledger on disk.' was removed on 2026-09-20 (coverageReport.ts:85, sourceFaceNotice.ts:14). No live reporter claims review for a draft. The planted negative is confirmed RED - reverting the gate reddens exactly that test.

The concern this bead opened with - 'it becomes urgent the first time someone cites a ledger as reviewed because its first line says so' - is now structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely: a first line saying REVIEWED is refused unless the receipt records it.

title: segment-ledger --update writes no unified diff before overwriting
description:

out of am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1 during Unit 1 scoping (2026-09-20) as a real deferral rather

title: The client import boundary watches three directories while its better-built sibling watches every .tsx; 37 of 126 client files are outside it
description:
Found by the am-o44v sweep, shape 2: a population no gate's denominator includes. Two sibling
gates guard the same surface with very different denominators, and the narrower one cites the
wider one in its own comments.

THE RULE. AGENTS.md: "Never create a giant aggregate module (an allEinsteinContent.ts) imported
into client components." src/testing/clientImportBoundary.test.ts:37 enforces it.

THE POPULATION IT USES:

    const appFiles       = await walkDir(resolve(root, "src/app"));
    const visualFiles    = await walkDir(resolve(root, "src/visuals"));
    const componentFiles = await walkDir(resolve(root, "src/components"));
    const scannedFiles = [...appFiles, ...visualFiles, ...componentFiles];

MEASURED, over every git-tracked .ts/.tsx/.mts under src/, using the gate's own definition of
"client" (`"use client"` or `'use client'` in the file, or "/visuals/" in the path):

    client-marked files anywhere under src/                  126
      inside the gate's three roots                           89
      OUTSIDE them, invisible to the gate                      37

The 37 are not marginal. They include the whole reader shell and equation layer:
    src/reader/ReaderController.tsx
    src/reader/actions/PassageActions.tsx
    src/reader/faces/AlignmentController.tsx, FacsimileViewer.tsx, GlossReasoningToggle.tsx
    src/reader/entrances/{Brownian,Clock,LightQuanta,MassEnergy}FirstEncounter.tsx
    src/reader/detail/DetailControl.tsx
    src/equations/SemanticEquation.tsx, EquationScope.tsx
    src/equations/accessibility/TermExplorer.tsx
    src/equations/derivations/LinearProofExplorer.tsx, LowSpeedExplorer.tsx
    src/equations/legacy/ColorizedEquation.tsx, src/equations/render/LatexRenderer.tsx
    src/a11y/readingSettings/ReadingOnlyView.tsx, ReadingSettingsPanel.tsx
    src/discovery/MassEnergyArgumentWorkbench.tsx
    src/platform/storage/DataPanel.tsx
    src/experiments/permalink/ShareControl.tsx ... and 17 more

OTHER HALF, MEASURED. I ran the gate's own forbidden-import regexes over all 126:

    forbidden imports INSIDE the gate's roots  : 0
    forbidden imports OUTSIDE them             : 0

Nothing is escaping. The defect is that 29% of the client surface is not in the denominator, so
a regression there would not be caught.

THE SIBLING THAT GETS IT RIGHT, and this is what makes it actionable rather than a matter of
taste. src/testing/noPhysicsInComponents.test.ts guards the neighbouring rule over the same
surface and does two things better:

    export function isWatchedPath(repoRelativePath: string): boolean {
      return repoRelativePath.endsWith(".tsx") ||
        WATCHED_DIRECTORY_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => repoRelativePath.startsWith(prefix));
    }

  - Population: EVERY .tsx anywhere, plus .ts under four named prefixes. No directory list to
    fall behind the tree.
  - Import extraction: the real TypeScript parser, with the comment "never a string-literal grep
    (JSX prose mentioning a path is not an import)". clientImportBoundary uses two line regexes.

clientImportBoundary already knows this sibling: its scanned-nothing guard at :46-51 carries the
comment "Sibling gate noPhysicsInComponents.test.ts:123 already asserts this; this one did not."
So the file borrowed one lesson from its neighbour and not the two that decide what it can see.

SUGGESTED FIX, not applied: reuse isWatchedPath, or the same shape - every .tsx plus named .ts
prefixes - and extract specifiers with extractImportSpecifiers rather than the two line regexes.
Both already exist and are exported.

A SEPARATE ONE-LINER, noted not filed. src/testing/viewImportGuard.test.ts:10-15 lists forbidden
prefixes, three with a trailing slash and three without:
    { prefix: "src/content/datasets/statistics", ... }
    { prefix: "src/physics/reference/diffusion/statistics", ... }
    { prefix: "src/testing/stats", ... }
matched at :68 with `resolved.startsWith(forbidden.prefix)`. The three without a slash are
unanchored, so src/testing/statsomething.ts matches src/testing/stats. This one fails CLOSED -
it forbids more than intended - so it is a consistency point, not a hole.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The client import boundary's population covers every client-marked file under src/, not three
  directories.
- Import specifiers come from the TypeScript parser, not line regexes.
- Planted negative: a client component under src/reader/ importing src/content/compiler is
  REFUSED. It passes today.
- Other half: the tree as shipped stays green, and the scanned-nothing guard still fails when a
  root is renamed.
- Both proofs driven red first, files restored byte-identical (cmp).
close_reason:
Fixed at ac30b9e2 by pane31; closed by orchestrator TanElk on re-executed evidence.

THE DEFECT. The client import boundary gate scanned only files under three declared roots - src/app, src/visuals, src/components - while 37 of the 126 client-marked files under src/ sat outside all of them. 29% of the surface the gate exists to guard was invisible to it, and the gate reported zero violations over the part it could see, which reads identically to zero violations overall. That is the populations-no-denominator-includes shape: not a wrong answer, an unasked question.

VERIFIED BY PLANT, against the real staleness case rather than a synthetic one. I renamed one entry in ROOTS_THAT_MUST_STILL_BE_REPRESENTED to simulate a directory being renamed out from under the root list - which is how the gate came to miss 37 files in the first place - and got src/testing/clientImportBoundary.test.ts 1 pass 2 fail: the main boundary assertion plus 'a root that contributes nothing is reported'. Restored byte-identical, confirmed with shasum -c. Baseline 3 pass 0 fail, 13 expect() calls.

THE PAWL IS THE FIX, not the widened scan. unrepresentedRoots() asserts that every declared root still contributes files, so the gate can no longer quietly stop covering a directory. Without it, widening the scan today would drift shut again the next time a directory is renamed, which is the failure this bead documents.

SHARED CODE EXTRACTED RATHER THAN DUPLICATED. src/testing/clientSurface.ts now holds walkTypeScriptFiles, hasUseClientDirective, isClientSurfaceFile, extractImportSpecifiers and unrepresentedRoots. pane31's own diagnosis of the root cause - 'two gates drifting over one surface is what produced this bead' - is the am-xgf9 shape, and the extraction is what stops it recurring between these two.

LEFT UNDONE AND CORRECTLY SO: noPhysicsInComponents.test.ts should also point at clientSurface.ts, and pane31 did not change it because this bead does not own that file. Recorded here so the next person does not rediscover it.

title: OWNER DECISION: should quality-gates.yml cancel in-progress runs, or queue them?
description:
# OWNER DECISION: cancel-in-progress, or queue?

`.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml` sets `concurrency: { group: workflow-ref, cancel-in-progress: true }` on push to `main`. am-h0nb asserted this makes the workflow "essentially never complete". **It does not**, and the decision should be made on its own merits rather than as a bug fix. I am not picking; both readings are below with the numbers each rests on.

## What the measurement settles, so it is not re-argued

    gh run list --workflow=quality-gates.yml --limit 1000
    811 runs, all push, 2026-09-16T05:56:53Z -> 2026-09-22T02:22:34Z

    cancelled 517 (63.7%)   failure 288 (35.5%)   success 5 (0.6%)

293 runs completed. Even with cancellation removed entirely, 288 of those 293 would still have failed, on one step, for an artefact reason recorded in am-h0nb. **Cancellation is not what keeps this workflow red.** Whatever is decided here, the workflow stays red until the artefact gap is closed.

## The numbers the decision actually turns on

    arrival rate, whole window        5.8 runs/hour
    mean run duration                 195s  ->  capacity 18.4 runs/hour at concurrency 1
    utilisation if nothing cancelled  31.4%
    busiest rolling hour observed     90 pushes  =  489% of one runner-hour
    push-to-push interval             median 97s, p25 31s, 38% under 60s

The averages and the peak disagree, which is why this is a judgement rather than an arithmetic problem.

## Reading A: keep cancelling

- The tip of `main` gets a verdict fastest, always. With a median 97s between pushes, feedback on a superseded commit is of little value to a swarm that has already moved on.
- Bounded cost. 63.7% of runs are cancelled early; the runner-minutes they would otherwise consume are not spent.
- The peak supports it: in the busiest observed hour a queue would need 4.9 runner-hours to serve one wall-clock hour, so a burst leaves the queue hours behind and the newest commit waits longest - the opposite of what CI is for.

## Reading B: stop cancelling, let the queue drain

- Every commit gets a verdict, so a regression can be attributed to a commit rather than to a range. In a swarm where several panes commit per minute, "which commit broke it" is currently unanswerable from CI.
- Average utilisation is 31.4%, so the queue drains comfortably outside bursts. "The queue never drains" is not supported by the whole-window rate.
- The 0.6% success rate means cancellation is currently hiding very little: there is almost no completed-and-green signal being protected.

## What would make either safe

- Reading A is improved by a scheduled or nightly unconditional run, so at least one full verdict per day exists that no push can cancel. `nightly-gates.yml` exists and should be checked against this before deciding.
- Reading B is improved by capping concurrency above 1, or by cancelling only runs older than N minutes, which keeps burst behaviour bounded without discarding every intermediate verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The owner records the choice and the reason, in this bead.
- Whichever is chosen, the workflow states in a comment WHY, with the arrival rate and utilisation that justified it, so the next person does not re-derive it.
- If reading A is kept, the existence of an uncancellable scheduled run is verified rather than assumed.
- This bead does not close the artefact gap; am-h0nb owns that and is independent of this choice.

title: Two theme radios render zero pixels wide in WebKit while Chromium draws them 13x13
description:
Two of the four theme radios render zero pixels wide in WebKit. Measured while running
the two-engine browser acceptance for am-ahyb, against the production build at 1280x800,
with the same page and the same code in both engines:

    label              WebKit          Chromium
    Annalen            0 x 12          13 x 13
    Kramgasse Night    38 x 12         51 x 13
    Slate              0 x 12          13 x 13
    Follow system      45 x 12         58 x 13

Computed styles are identical and unremarkable in both: display block, visibility
visible, opacity 1, appearance auto. The CSS in src/app/theme/themes.css does not hide
the input; `.theme-toggle label` is an inline-flex with a border and a gap, and the
radio is a child of it.

Note the pattern, because it is the lead for whoever fixes this: the two with zero width
are exactly the two with SHORT labels. The inputs appear to be taking their width from
the label's content box in WebKit, and collapsing when there is nothing to take.

## The feature still works, and that is why this is not a P1

Playwright refuses to click a zero-area element, which is how this was found: driving the
input directly fails in WebKit and succeeds in Chromium. Clicking the LABEL - the
bordered word, which is what a reader actually clicks - switches the theme in BOTH
engines. Verified. So no reader is blocked today.

## Why it is still worth fixing

A zero-width radio is a pointer target of zero area. It is reachable by keyboard and by
the label, but anyone aiming at the control itself in Safari has nothing to hit, and
WCAG 2.2 target-size reasoning applies to the control. It also means any future test or
assistive-technology path that addresses the input rather than the label behaves
differently in Safari than in Chrome, silently.

## Provenance

Found by pane28 while writing scripts/e2e/uiExtraction.e2e.test.ts (am-ahyb). First
misdiagnosed by me as a WebKit failure of the theme toggle; it is not, and the test now
drives the label and says why. Reported in am-ahyb comments and filed here so it does
not live only in a commit message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The four theme radios have a nonzero, comparable rendered box in WebKit and Chromium,
  measured at 1280x800 and at 320px, and the numbers are recorded in the fix.
- Planted negative that goes RED: a rule that collapses the input again is caught. The
  fixture is the current markup, so confirm the zero-width state is reachable before
  trusting the guard - it is reachable today, which is what this bead records.
- Control: clicking the label still switches the theme in both engines, and the
  scrollable-regions and contrast gates are unchanged by the fix.
- No change to the accessible name, the radio semantics, or the keyboard order.
close_reason: Superseded: the theme radios no longer exist. D-2026-09-22-one-sun-moon-theme-toggle replaced them with one button.theme-toggle. SapphireCastle measured live b73d967a: 0 theme radios and 1 theme button on each of /, /papers/, /papers/light-quanta/, /papers/special-relativity/, /lab/bm-01/ and /notebook/. As a positive control, the 11 radios that remain on each page are reading preferences. They are 1x1 in both engines, with 44 px label targets in WebKit and Chromium. No WebKit/Chromium divergence remains.

title: A required CI gate reports 158 of 158 source units REVIEWED from a hardcoded literal, having read no inputs
description:
scripts/coverage-report.ts:166-174 constructs its LedgerContext from literals:

    const sourceManifestsMap = new Map([
      ["brownian-motion", { paper: "brownian-motion", totalUnits: 158,
                             byStatus: { reviewed: 158 } }],
    ]);

and the variable beside it is named `sampleNodes`. The whole context is demo data. The
emitted report then prints, verbatim, today:

    - **Inputs:** None
    ## 1. Source Status
    Total source units: 158
    - reviewed: 158
    - not-reviewed: 1

The gate tells the truth in one line ('Inputs: None') and contradicts it in the next. It is
also internally inconsistent: 158 reviewed plus 1 not-reviewed is 159 against a declared
total of 158.

## Why this is P0 and not a tidy-up

  requiredInCi: true, cadence every-run, family fast (quality-gates/registry.ts:284-290).
  It runs on every CI run and is required to pass.

This project is a critical edition. Its credibility rests on the claim that source units
have been reviewed by named people. Right now docs/OWNERS.md holds ONE human plus nine
'open: recruiting' slots, every human-review gate in the repository correctly refuses
everything for want of a reviewer, and pane29 established this same hour that no reviewed
ledger exists for any paper anywhere in the tree. Against that, a required gate emits a
document asserting 158 fully reviewed source units. That is not a gate failing to catch
something - it is a certificate asserting scholarly review that did not happen.

## A NEW SHAPE, distinct from the empty-set class and worse

pane31 found it and named the distinction precisely: "A floor wouldn't fix this one: the
population isn't empty, it's INVENTED, so length > 0 passes." Every shape-4 fix so far -
licence inventory, release checklist, edition contract check 8 - works by refusing when the
population is empty. None of them would touch this, because the population is populated,
with fiction. Call it the fabricated-population shape. The detector is different too: not
'what does it print on empty input' but 'where did this number come from, and can the run
name its source'.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The report derives source status from the real content tree, or reports not-available
   and STOPS emitting coverage numbers. Those are the only two honest outcomes.

title: The one-LaTeX-tokenizer gate checks four spellings, and a 168-line second tokenizer sits inside the directory it guards
description:
Found by the am-o44v substring sweep, in the category-word band of the 415 gating sites.

src/equations/latex/tokenize.test.ts:143-165. The assertion message states the rule:

    `tokenizeLatex must be the only LaTeX tokenizer in src/. Found duplicate in: ...`

The code that decides it:

    if (filePath.includes("src/equations/latex/tokenize.ts") ||
        filePath.includes("tokenize.test.ts")) { continue; }
    const content = readFileSync(filePath, "utf8");
    if (content.includes("function tokenizeLatex") ||
        content.includes("class LatexTokenizer") ||
        content.includes("export function tokenizeTeX") ||
        content.includes("class TeXTokenizer")) { suspiciousFiles.push(filePath); }

Four literal spellings standing in for the category "this file declares a LaTeX tokenizer".
It is a denylist where an allowlist is one directory away, and everything about the rule -
single owner, no second implementation - is exactly what an allowlist expresses.

THE ESCAPE IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. src/equations/latex/parens.property.test.ts:204 declares

    function tokenizeTestLatex(input: string): Token[] {

It spans lines 204-371 - 168 lines - and it recognises \approx \cos \exp \frac \langle \left
\ln \pi \rangle \right \sin \sqrt. It is a LaTeX tokenizer, it lives in the very directory the
rule names, and the gate scans it. Measured, both members greped:

    content.includes("function tokenizeLatex")     -> False
    content.includes("class LatexTokenizer")       -> False
    content.includes("export function tokenizeTeX")-> False
    content.includes("class TeXTokenizer")         -> False
    path skip "src/equations/latex/tokenize.ts"    -> False
    path skip "tokenize.test.ts"                   -> False

A property test may legitimately want an independent second implementation to differential-test
against. That is the point: the gate is where such an exemption should be recorded and argued.
Instead it passes on a spelling, so nobody had to justify it and the gate's green cannot
distinguish a deliberate differential-test oracle from an accidental duplicate.

THE OTHER HALF, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. src/equations/tree/parse.ts:598
`function tokenize(src: string): Token[]` is NOT a violation: it tokenises this project's own
expression-tree DSL (`@name` op annotations, `~=`, `:=`, `->`), not LaTeX. The repo-wide search
for tokenizer-shaped declarations outside the owner returns it, tokenizeTestLatex,
src/discovery/exercises/grammar.ts:42 (exercise grammar), src/content/kernel/highlight.ts:55
(kernel source highlighting) and src/content/editions/tokenizeGerman.ts:47 (German text).
Only tokenizeTestLatex tokenises LaTeX.

Trivial further escapes the four spellings also miss, for whoever fixes this:
  export const tokenizeLatex = (s: string) => ...   (arrow, not `function`)
  function tokenizeLaTeX(...)                        (capital T-e-X)
  class MathTokenizer / class KatexLexer / function lexLatex
and a false positive in the other direction: any file whose prose comment contains the words
"function tokenizeLatex" is flagged as a duplicate implementation.

SUGGESTED FIX, not applied: decide by category, not spelling. Either (a) an allowlist of the
paths permitted to declare a LaTeX tokenizer, with a reason field per entry as
scripts/app-router-architecture.ts already does, or (b) an AST pass for a function or class
whose body matches on LaTeX control-sequence literals, which is the actual property. Record
tokenizeTestLatex explicitly if it is wanted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gate decides by category or by an allowlist with reasons, not by four literal spellings.
- Planted negative: a second tokenizer spelled `export const tokenizeLatex = (s) => ...` is
  REFUSED. It passes today.
- Other half: the shipped tree is GREEN once tokenizeTestLatex is recorded with its reason, and
  removing that record turns it RED.
- Both proofs driven red first, files restored byte-identical (cmp).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
pane28: DONE in 8c7e4431, one file, src/equations/latex/tokenize.test.ts. Reporting, not closing.

RE-DERIVED FIRST, as you asked. `function tokenizeTestLatex` opens at parens.property.test.ts:204 and its matching brace closes at :371. Inclusive that is 168 lines. The bead's number is right this time. I also measured the body rather than eyeballing it: 12 distinct LaTeX control words.

AND IT IS A LEGITIMATE SECOND IMPLEMENTATION, which turned out to be the interesting part. parseTestLatex uses it to re-parse the renderer's OWN OUTPUT and check that precedence survived rendering. If it shared the owner's tokenizer the comparison would be vacuous - a defect present in both would agree with itself. So the right outcome was never "delete the duplicate"; it was "make someone say why it exists". The old gate could not tell a deliberate differential oracle from an accidental duplicate, and that is a sharper statement of the defect than "it misses a second tokenizer".

THE FIX, both halves of the bead's suggestion because they need each other. Category detection: a declaration whose name is tokenizer-shaped BY SEGMENT and which either names TeX or carries LaTeX control-sequence literals in its brace-matched body. Allowlist with reasons for what that finds. Across src/ it finds exactly four, all recorded: the owner, the owner's error type, this gate's own detector, and the oracle.

THREE THINGS I HIT WHILE BUILDING IT, all the same disease one level down, all measured not guessed:
  - `lexer` occurs inside `globa|lExer|ciseCheckerLogger`. An unanchored name test flagged it. Fixed by segment membership, which is the am-o44v repair.
  - a first attempt keyed on `token` as a segment flagged every design token in src/app/theme. Narrowed to tokenize/tokenizer/lex/lexer.
  - the detector flagged its OWN source, because the four spellings the old gate searched for appear in this file as string literals. Fixed by requiring a declaration to begin a line, and by blanking string contents for brace matching only - the LaTeX evidence lives inside string literals, so blanking them for the evidence scan would have blinded it. My first blanker paired quotes across newlines and silently ate real declarations; this file is full of regex literals containing quote characters. Bounded to a line.

PLANTS, each restored byte-identically and verified with cmp:
  1. `export const tokenizeLatexFast = (s: string) => s.split("\\")` appended to tokenize.ts: RED, naming path and declaration.
  2. THE CONTROL THAT SEPARATES A FIX FROM A REWRITE, and the one I would want to see from anyone else: the SAME plant against the OLD gate, 8 pass 0 fail. Invisible to all four spellings.
  3. The tokenizeTestLatex record removed: RED. The allowlist is load-bearing, not decoration.
  4. A stale record fails, and a reason under 40 characters fails.

Two permanent tests carry the rest: the detector catches the arrow form, tokenizeLaTeX, class MathTokenizer, class KatexLexer and lexLatex - none of which matched the four spellings - and it stays a CODE gate rather than a prose matcher, so a comment naming tokenizeLatex, a string warning against writing a second one, tokenizeGerman and the expression-tree `tokenize` are all unflagged. That second test is the am-jb4c lesson applied here: widening a spelling gate carelessly is worse than the hole.

ALSO REMOVED: the path skips. `filePath.includes("tokenize.test.ts")` excused an entire file by spelling, in a gate whose bug was deciding by spelling. Nothing is skipped by path now; everything found is recorded with a reason or it fails.

ONE THING I DID NOT DO. The detector is regex over line-anchored declarations, not an AST pass. It will not see a tokenizer declared as a class METHOD (`class Reader { tokenizeLatex() {...} }`) or one built by a factory. I considered that out of scope for a test-file gate and I am naming it rather than leaving it implied. If you want it airtight it wants the TypeScript parser, which is a different bead.

EVIDENCE. bun test src/equations/latex/tokenize.test.ts: 10 pass 0 fail, up from 8 - two new tests. bunx tsc --noEmit exit 0. biome clean. parens.property.test.ts is untouched; the oracle stays independent, which is the whole reason it is allowed to exist.

title: resolveVoiceContext matches substrings of a field path: argument recaps lint as progress copy, and 'variant' contains 'aria'
description:
`resolveVoiceContext` (src/content/checks/voice/contexts.ts) decides which
severity every rule applies to every scanned string. It tests `fieldPath.
toLowerCase().includes(<substring>)` with no regard to the record kind and no
word boundary. Two consequences are measured below, and the function has NO
TEST FILE of any kind.

## 1. LIVE: an argument's scholarly recap is linted as progress copy

contexts.ts:41 maps any field path containing "recap" to `reader-progress`,
which is the only context besides task-feedback and ui-label where the theater
rule is an error rather than a flag. `grep -n reader-progress
content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml` returns exactly two lines: the context
declaration and `theater: reader-progress: error`. So this classification has
one practical effect in the whole rule set - it applies gamification strictness.

Measured: every `recap` field in the corpus belongs to a record of kind
`argument`. 42 of them. `Counter({'argument': 42})`, and zero `recap:` keys in
any YAML record. They read like this:

  "Independent centred steps add mean squares; the root therefore grows as the
   square root of time."
  "For an unbounded point source, the Gaussian has mean square 2Dt and
   coordinate RMS sqrt(2Dt)."

That is the argument's one-sentence summary, sitting beside question,
conclusion, premises and limitations - not a progress readout.

WHY THE MAPPING EXISTS, because this is not simply a typo. am-read-notebook-tde
adds the `recap` field to ArgumentNode and displays it in the interrupted
reader's recap card. So the field was mapped by where its text is SHOWN (a
progress surface) rather than by what the text IS (authored argument prose).
That reading has it backwards: the gamification risk in a recap card lives in
the card's own chrome ("You are 40% through"), not in the scientific sentence
the card quotes. And the card's own strings are .tsx, which componentText.ts
hands to the linter as context "prose" regardless - so the strictness is applied
to the one text in that surface that does not need it, and not applied to the
text that does.

Blast radius, measured across all 42 recaps under both contexts:
  recaps producing any finding            5
  errors as reader-progress               1  (am-xsue's)
  errors as prose                         0

## 2. LATENT: "variant" contains "aria", so relativity vocabulary reads as a label

`"variant".includes("aria")` is true - v-ARIA-nt. So does `variants`,
`invariant`, `invariants`, `covariant` and `variance`. Every field path
containing one of those words is classified `ui-label`, where theater is an
error, because contexts.ts:84 tests for "aria".

Measured today: 199 strings, all `glyph.variant` enum values in the notation
concordance ("plain"), which trigger no rule. CURRENT HARM IS ZERO and I am not
claiming otherwise.

It stops being latent the moment an author fills a field the schema already
declares: src/content/schemas/experiment.ts:1707 declares
`invariants?: { expression: string; description: string }[]` on Experiment.
That `description` is prose. No experiment record populates it yet (measured: 0
files with an `invariants:` block under content/experiments/), and the plan
requires expected invariants, so this will be filled.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A branch matches a WORD of the field path, not an arbitrary substring. Words
   come from splitting on ".", "[n]", "-", "_" and camelCase humps. Measured
   delta of this change alone: 208 of 13980 scanned strings change context, of
   which 199 are the glyph.variant correction and the remaining 9 are inside
   content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml, which the linter scans as content because
   it is a YAML file under content/.
2. An `argument` record's `recap` resolves to `prose`. A `recap` on any other
   record kind still resolves to `reader-progress`, so the branch keeps working
   for the notebook surface it was written for.
3. contexts.ts gets its first test file.
4. PLANTED NEGATIVES, each driven red against its own failure mode:
   a. THE PLANT THIS BEAD IS FOR: a real scholarly recap, taken verbatim from
      content/arguments/, goes through checkVoice and is NOT judged as progress
      copy. It goes back to being judged that way if the kind check is removed.
   b. A genuine progress recap on a non-argument record STILL resolves to
      reader-progress and still errors on gamification vocabulary. Without this
      the fix is indistinguishable from deleting the branch.
   c. A field path containing "invariant" or "variant" resolves to prose, and
      an `aria-label` still resolves to ui-label. Without the second half, the
      word-matching change would be indistinguishable from deleting the aria
      branch.

title: Build the action-contract framework so every scientific action has a nonvisual equivalent
description:
# Build the action-contract framework so every scientific action has a nonvisual equivalent

**Epic:** `am-ep-accessibility-wrk` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.8, §7.2, §10.4, §10.5, §12.6, §16.2, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

Every core instrument exposes an **action contract**: an action names its inputs, the question it changes, the accepted result, and **the equivalent operation without dragging, color discrimination, sound, or a visual canvas**. The plan's families:

| Instrument family | Visual action | Equivalent scientific action |
|---|---|---|
| Probability and diffusion | Drag a selected histogram interval | Enter lower and upper limits, inspect interval probability, compare two named intervals |
| Clock and event geometry | Select points on a diagram | Choose named events from a table and ask which frame regards them as simultaneous |
| Radiation entropy | Resize the constrained-state volume | Enter a ratio or choose half, same, or double, with fixed energy and band stated |
| Fields and boosts | Rotate an arrow or move an observer | Select an axis or component and signed magnitude, then inspect transformed components at the same event |
| Energy accounting | Drag a boundary around objects | Select the objects included in the system and inspect energy crossing that boundary |
| Derivations | Highlight and transform part of an equation | Select a named subexpression, read its role, and advance a justified step |

"A long prose description alone is not equivalent to being able to investigate. Conversely, no screen-reader user is forced through every particle coordinate." For first encounters, the visual action, keyboard action, and screen-reader action manipulate the same entries and expose the same totals; a nonvisual reader never receives a weaker question. In the innovation sequence this is **P0**, expanded only after readers can perform the comparison, not merely hear a description of it.

## Scope

In scope: the action-contract fields in experiment manifests (an additive extension of the `ActionContract` shape owned by `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`); a command builder guaranteeing that visual and equivalent affordances produce identical runtime commands; the equivalent-action component of the interval family (probability and diffusion), built and proven before the Brownian slice freeze; the framework (schema, command builder, equivalence harness, audit rule) that the other five families' equivalents register with when `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` builds them after the slice freeze; audit integration; equivalence tests with fixture instruments on the real runtime.

Out of scope: visual interaction primitives and the interval selector (`am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`); the event, partition, coefficient, channel, and expression families with their equivalent components (`am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`, built after `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` against their first real consumers); parameter controls (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`); command-class semantics (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`); instrument-specific contracts (instrument beads); the audit script itself (`am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`, which registers this bead's rule).

## Requirements

- **Schema** (one shape, no parallel names): the manifest's `actionContract` keeps the fields defined in `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` (`family`; `actions[]` with `id`, `visualAction`, `equivalentAction`, `inputs`, `result`) and adds, as a reviewed additive change in that schema module, `question` (what this action changes, in plain language), `commandClass` (`setup-change`, `physical-intervention`, `observer-change`, `measurement-change`, `estimator-change`, or `presentation-change`), and `announcement` (a template for the committed result). `inputs` reference parameter ids, event ids, object ids, or subexpression ids; `result` lists output quantity ids and their permitted typed statuses.
- **Single command path**: both affordances call the same command builder, so identical intent from the same starting state yields an identical command (class and canonical payload, compared by hash) and therefore identical accepted outputs and the same increment of `snapshotVersion`. Instance ids differ across instances by design and are excluded from the comparison.
- **Equivalent components, split by the slice freeze.** This bead builds the interval family's equivalent before the slice freeze: interval entry with lower and upper limits, the interval probability, and comparison of two named intervals, proven on BM-06 with `IntervalSelector`. The other five families' equivalents are specified here as the contract `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` implements after the freeze: event table selection with a simultaneity question per frame; ratio entry and half, same, or double choices with fixed energy and band stated; axis or component selection with signed magnitude and transformed-component readout at the same event; object inclusion checklist with boundary-crossing energy readout; subexpression list with role reading and justified step advance. The schema, command builder, equivalence harness, and audit accept each of those family kinds without a framework change.
- **Operability**: every equivalent control has a visible label contained in its accessible name (for voice control), works with keyboard and touch assistive technology, meets the 24×24 target rule, and announces the committed result through the baseline announcement utility once per commit.
- **Scale of the question**: equivalents offer summaries and selectable comparisons first, with optional detailed data; never force traversal of every particle coordinate.
- **Visible to everyone**: equivalent panels are ordinary visible controls, not screen-reader-only markup.
- **Audit**: every interactive action of every core instrument declares a contract; a missing contract, a contract whose `equivalentAction` requires dragging, color, sound, or a canvas, or a contract whose `result` differs from the visual action's result fails the instrument audit in `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`.

## Technical Approach

- `src/a11y/actions/commandBuilder.ts`, `src/a11y/actions/equivalence.ts` (command hashing and comparison), the interval family's component under `src/a11y/actions/families/interval/` (later families add sibling directories in `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`); schema additions land in `src/content/schemas/experiment.ts` with the schema owner's review.
- The interval fixture instrument is registered with the e2e harness's fixture application bundler (`scripts/e2e/fixtures/fixtureApps.ts`, owned by `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`) and runs on the real runtime (snapshot store, command classes, worker path), not on a mocked framework; nothing adds a fixture build, flag, route, or conditional import to the application. Five planted contract fixtures, one per later family kind, exercise the schema, command builder, and audit without visual components.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The schema additions and command builder exist; the interval family component is implemented against its fixture instrument before the slice freeze; the planted contract fixtures for the five later family kinds validate, hash, and pass the audit without framework changes.
- [ ] For the interval family (and, through the same equivalence harness, for each later family when `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` lands it), performing the visual action and the equivalent action with the same intent from the same starting state yields identical command hashes, identical accepted outputs, and the same `snapshotVersion` increment.
- [ ] Keyboard-only and accessibility-tree checks complete the interval family's question; labels are contained in accessible names; each commit produces exactly one announcement.
- [ ] A fixture instrument missing a contract, or with a drag-only equivalent, fails the audit.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `commandBuilder.test.ts`: identical command hashes from both affordances per family; different intents produce different hashes; command class matches the contract.
- `families/interval.test.tsx`: component behavior, labels in names, announcements, bounds and typed-status display; `contractKinds.test.ts`: the planted contract fixtures for the five later family kinds validate, hash deterministically, and pass or fail the audit as specified.
- `equivalence.integration.test.ts`: with the real runtime, visual and equivalent paths produce matching accepted outputs for the interval fixture; the harness is exported so `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` runs the same comparison for each later family.
- `contractAudit.test.ts`: the audit rule rejects missing, drag-only, and result-mismatched contracts.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (instrument state read from `data-instance-id`, `data-snapshot-version`, and `data-accepted-input-revision`): for the interval family fixture, run the visual path and the equivalent path in separate instances from the same seeded starting state and compare output hashes; keyboard-only lane; accessibility-tree checks; touch emulation lane; 320 px; WebKit.

### Structured logging

JSONL through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp` to `artifacts/test-logs/a11y-actions/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `actionId`, `family`, `path` (`visual`, `equivalent`), `commandClass`, `commandHash`, `snapshotVersion`, `outputsHash`, `equal`, `announcements`, `browser`, `viewport`, `outcome`, `message`; failures retain screenshots, traces, and accessibility-tree snapshots.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- An equivalent that asks an easier question is a failure even if it is accessible.
- Keep equivalent panels usable by everyone, not hidden behind screen-reader-only markup; many sighted readers prefer typed entry.
- Two different field names for the same contract (for example a separate `visualAffordance`) would split the manifest contract; extend the existing schema instead.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (instruments whose actions are contracted); `am-rt-command-classes-dzp` (the command classes each contract names); `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (the equivalence lanes and the fixture application bundler this bead's fixture instrument registers with).

Unblocks: `am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy` (visual primitives must pair with these equivalents; through it `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`, which builds the other five families on this framework); `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly` and `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl` (their nonvisual action contracts).

title: WASM manifest asserts a wasm-pack Rust build that never happened; 154-byte stub declares capabilities it does not export
description:
## Background

Found by the orchestrator (TanElk) at HEAD 195326f on 2026-09-17 and verified directly, not taken from an agent report.

## Evidence (reproduce exactly)

1. The only .wasm artifact is 154 bytes:
   `ls -la public/wasm/fs-annus-diffusion/105d7ffc15414de5/fs_annus_diffusion_bg.wasm` -> 154 bytes.
2. Its entire export list, read from the binary, is: `memory`, `touch_wasm`, `__wbindgen_malloc`, `__wbindgen_free`, `__wbindgen_realloc`. It does NOT export `brownian_frames`, `philox_normals`, or `diffusion1d_frames`.
3. `public/wasm/manifest.json` nevertheless declares three capabilities - `diffusion.brownian-frames` (browserExport `brownian_frames`), `diffusion.philox-normals` (`philox_normals`), `diffusion.ftcs-1d` (`diffusion1d_frames`) - each with `acceptanceState: "owner-decided"`.
4. `public/wasm/manifest.json` asserts build provenance that did not occur:
   `"command": "wasm-pack build --release --target web -- --locked"`, `"toolchain": "nightly-2026-07-06"`, `"wasmPackVersion": "0.13.1"`, `"wasmBindgenVersion": "0.2"`, plus pinned frankensim/asupersync git revisions.
5. That command never ran. `scripts/build-wasm-artifacts.ts:184` writes the wasm-pack string as a literal, while `scripts/build-wasm-artifacts.ts:73` produces the bytes by calling `buildWasmBinary()` from `scripts/wasm-artifacts/wasmArtifactGenerator.ts:35`, which hand-assembles the module byte-by-byte in TypeScript.
6. There is no Rust source and no Cargo.toml in this repository (the only .rs files are an archived copy of frankensim under `artifacts/frankensim-archive/`).
7. The real numeric kernels (Philox, brownian frames, FTCS) are hand-written JavaScript in `public/wasm/fs-annus-diffusion/105d7ffc15414de5/fs_annus_diffusion.js`, shaped to look like wasm-bindgen glue.

## Why this is a defect and not a style question

AGENTS.md, "FrankenSim Binding and Honesty": execution labels are earned per snapshot and "A loaded WASM file does not earn the FrankenSim label." AGENTS.md swarm rules name this pattern RH-2, proof-class inflation: presenting a fixture as live proof. A manifest that names a toolchain, a wasm-pack version and upstream git revisions is a provenance claim; here it is false, and the digest-verification machinery built around it lends it credibility it has not earned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `public/wasm/manifest.json` no longer asserts any build step, toolchain, wasm-pack version or wasm-bindgen version that did not actually execute. Either the fields are removed, or they are replaced by fields that truthfully describe the generator (`scripts/wasm-artifacts/wasmArtifactGenerator.ts`) and label the artifact as a generated placeholder, not a compiled Rust build.
- [ ] The manifest does not declare a capability whose `browserExport` is absent from the artifacts export list. A test reads the actual .wasm export section and fails if any declared `browserExport` is missing. Prove the test works by planting a bogus capability, observing the failure, then reverting the plant.
- [ ] `acceptanceState: "owner-decided"` is removed or re-typed for capabilities that no owner has actually accepted.
- [ ] Any reader-facing execution label that would read "computed with FrankenSim" for these capabilities instead reads the honest label for a host calculation or an unavailable experiment. Check `src/content/coverage/coverageManifest.ts` (`RuntimeProvenance` = WASM | TS_FALLBACK | HONEST_PLACEHOLDER) and prove no instrument reports WASM provenance off this artifact.
- [ ] `src/physics/wasmArtifacts.test.ts` passes for the right reason, not by relaxing a check. It is currently failing at HEAD on `manifest-digests-and-validation` because commit c43ae07 reformatted the generated JS without regenerating the manifest digest.

## Explicitly forbidden

Do not fix this by deleting the test, widening a tolerance, regenerating the digest to match reformatted bytes without addressing the false provenance, or by writing a stub that exits 0. Removing a false claim is a valid fix; making the false claim harder to detect is not.
