title: The scrollable-regions staleness check credits an accessible name by bare substring, so a record may name a different element entirely
description:
src/testing/a11y/scrollableRegions.test.ts, staleReason(), added in b0239862:

    if (record.ariaLabel !== undefined && !src.includes(record.ariaLabel)) {

The accessible name is the discriminator that lets one file hold two recorded
elements of the same class. It is verified by asking whether the string occurs
ANYWHERE in the source file - not whether an element of that className carries
it as its accessible name.

## Demonstrated, not argued

Orchestrator TanElk, by plant. Baseline 11 pass 0 fail. Changed the
RodSimultaneityLab record's ariaLabel from 'Accepted laboratory telemetry
snapshot table' (the real label of the table-scroll at :750) to 'Predict before
calculating' - a REAL aria-label in the same file, at :220, belonging to a
button that is not a table-scroll and not a scroll region at all. Result:
11 pass 0 fail. The gate accepted a record naming a different element of a
different kind. Restored byte-identical.

## This is the sweep's own defect class, inside the sweep's own gate

am-o44v exists because a substring test stood in for a category test. This is a
substring test standing in for a structural test, introduced by a fix for that
sweep. It is the THIRD such gap found in this one file: the dead escape
(bc70d571), the measurements documented as 'parsed and checked' that nothing
parsed (0da563a9), and now this.

## Not a reproach to b0239862, which is an improvement

file-plus-class could not separate two elements at all, and pane28 shipped the
key that can, disclosed the residual limit in its own commit message
('the gate is static and never measures, so it can verify that a named element
exists and cannot verify which element a measurement came from'), and proved
that limit with a plant it reported as GREEN rather than hiding. This bead is
one step past what it disclosed: the name need not belong to an element of that
class at all.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The check verifies that an element carrying `className` also carries that
   accessible name - a structural relation, not co-occurrence in a file.
2. Planted negative that goes RED: a record naming a real accessible name from a
   DIFFERENT element in the same file is refused. Confirm the fixture reaches
   that state - the plant above is the exact fixture, and it currently passes.
3. Control: the four existing single-element records, which carry no ariaLabel,
   keep their current keys and still pass unchanged.
4. What this bead does NOT claim to fix, so nobody closes it saying so: whether
   a recorded MEASUREMENT came from the named element. pane28 is right that only
   a runtime measurement settles that, and it is a separate, larger bead.
close_reason:
Fixed at b785daa7 by pane28; closed by orchestrator TanElk on re-executed evidence.

THE FIX. staleReason no longer asks whether the FILE contains the accessible name. A JSX walker (elementsWithClasses) yields every opening tag carrying a className with its attribute text, and the check requires an element of that className to carry that accessible name - a structural relation. Verified by reverting the fix rather than by reading it: changing names.includes(record.ariaLabel) back to src.includes(record.ariaLabel) gives src/testing/a11y/scrollableRegions.test.ts 12 pass 1 fail, failing test named 'am-afam: a name belonging to a DIFFERENT element in the same file is refused'. Restored byte-identical, 13 pass 0 fail. The check is therefore non-vacuous - it catches the exact historical defect.

THE PLANT BECAME A FIXTURE, which is better than what the bead asked for. Criterion 3 asked for a planted negative; pane28 kept my one-off plant as a standing test with the provenance in a comment ('The fixture is TanElk's plant, kept as a fixture instead of a one-off run'), so 'Predict before calculating' - the real aria-label of a button at :220 that is neither a table-scroll nor a scroll region - is now permanently asserted to be refused rather than checked once and forgotten. A one-off plant proves a moment; a fixture proves it every run.

title: Rewrite AGENTS.md 'Project Status' from measurements: 8 of its clauses are false
description:
## Background

AGENTS.md "Project Status: Read This First" is where every pane reads the state of the project at session start. It warns it goes stale.

## What is wrong (measured 2026-09-24)

8 clauses are false or stale, including:
- "This repository is at the planning stage";
- "`ios/` does not exist" (5,894 lines of Swift exist);
- "The application above is not deployed" (live since 2026-09-21, 429 pages);
- "`vercel.json` keeps git deployment disabled", which may still be true; verify;
- the instrument, German-face and facsimile figures, which have moved.

Panes act on this text.

## What to do

- Rewrite the section clause by clause from commands run the same day. Each clause names its command.
- Keep the honest gaps prominent: no reviewed ledger, no English translation, no FrankenSim result reaching a reader, 1 named human reviewer.
- Remove nothing else from AGENTS.md.
- De-slopify; no em dashes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every factual clause in the section is followed by the command that produced it, and re-running each command reproduces it.
- The orchestrator reviews the diff before commit.
- Committed alone.

## Tests and logging

- Each clause's command re-run by the orchestrator before commit, with its output quoted in the commit message.

Structured logs: each suite writes JSON lines to artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>.jsonl with the AGENTS.md fields that apply (timestamp, suite, logRunId, testId, beadId, paper, anchor, instrumentId, expected, actual, outcome, browser, viewport, jsEnabled, message). A failing browser test keeps a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot and console log.
close_reason: Rewritten in the commit above: every factual clause carries its command, re-run by TanElk before commit. Self-reviewed by the orchestrator, not independently.

title: Browser acceptance for the extracted chrome, palette, error boundaries and OG route in Chromium and WebKit
description:
`am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31` has one acceptance criterion nobody has been able to claim
across four passes at the bead: "The theme toggle, command palette shell, error boundaries, and Open
Graph route work on the empty site in Chromium and WebKit."

Every other criterion on c31 is met and verified. This one needs a built site and the browser lanes,
which is the e2e harness's business and not the extraction's, so it is split out rather than left as
the single open box on a P0 whose code work is finished.

The checks, from c31's own test plan:

- the theme toggle switches and persists across reload;
- Cmd-K or Ctrl-K opens the palette and Escape closes it with focus restored to the opener;
- a nonexistent route shows the not-found page with HTTP status 404;
- the Open Graph image route returns an image with the expected content type;
- the network log of the home page contains no request to another origin.

The last one has a source-level and built-output equivalent already passing
(src/testing/thirdPartyRequests.test.ts, 8 tests, scans src/, public/ and out/), so the browser
version tests what the other two cannot: what the browser actually requests at run time, including
anything a framework or font pipeline adds after the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The five checks run in Chromium and in WebKit through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, against a
  production build, not a dev server.
- On failure the harness retains a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console log and network log
  under `artifacts/test-logs/ui-extraction/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.
- Structured JSONL per the logging standard, with `suite: "ui-extraction"`, `browser`, `viewport`
  and `jsEnabled`.
- A planted negative per check, each failing for its own reason: a remote script tag added to the
  built page fails the network check and not the others; a removed Escape handler fails the palette
  check only.
- If a lane cannot run on this host, it reports not-available with the reason rather than passing.

I own that ratchet's last two repairs (am-uj6w, am-bc6s, am-afam) and I did not find this in any of them, because every element I was looking at happened to carry a string-literal class. comments.text:

WHAT THE LAB CLAIMS vs WHAT I DROVE.

  CLAIM "The default worked example and all its numbers are readable without JavaScript."
  DROVE it with javaScriptEnabled false, not emulated. All 17 declared quantities are in the static HTML, every one numeric rather than a placeholder, and the no-script notice is shown. HOLDS in both engines.

  CLAIM "One accepted, instance-scoped snapshot supplies every displayed quantity" and "Changing only beta changes the observer, not the emitted pulse."
  DROVE it where it can fail: beta 0.6 -> 0.2, then required that the nine source-frame readings and both invariant masses hold still ACROSS ALL THREE TABLES while the six moving-frame readings follow. HOLDS in both engines. The test asserts those readings exist first, or "nothing moved" would be true of a page displaying nothing.
  NOT ASSERTED: quantumRatioMoving. The page says E'/(hv') equals E/(hv) "apart from numerical rounding", so an assertion either way would be an assertion about rounding.

  CLAIM the typed refusal - "these are this instrument's admission bounds".
  DROVE it with beta = 2. IN BOTH ENGINES THE BROWSER'S CONTROL VALIDATION ANSWERED, NOT THE PAGE: "Value must be less than or equal to 0.999999". The page's own refusal wording never reaches a reader who uses the control, because the input carries max and the submit never runs. Well unit-tested, unreachable through the interface. The claim that matters either way does hold: the last accepted worked example stays on screen, unchanged, byte for byte.

  CLAIM the execution label "Ideal model, host calculation".
  PRESENT in the markup; I did not verify it against what actually computed, which is the session's business.

WHAT I DID NOT EXERCISE, so nobody reads this lane as complete: the physics itself, the bookmark and popstate restore, the predict-mode disclosure, and the print stylesheet.

THE tableWrap MEASUREMENTS, reported and not asserted because pane30 owns that item:

  all three regions, both engines, both viewports: 254/254 at 320px and 1150/1150 at 1280px. NOTHING OVERFLOWS. tabIndex is -1 everywhere EXCEPT chromium at 320px, where all three report 0 - Chromium's keyboard-focusable-scrollers heuristic disagreeing with its own scrollWidth. So the honest status of this route's scroll regions is "does not currently overflow at either tested width", which is the same evidence shape the RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING map takes.

THREE FINDINGS.

1. title: Make native and edition surfaces work with VoiceOver, Voice Control, Switch Control, Dynamic Type, and a hardware keyboard
description:
# Make native and edition surfaces work with VoiceOver, Voice Control, Switch Control, Dynamic Type, and a hardware keyboard

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** a11y · **Plan sections:** App plan §10 (traceability only)

## Background

The master plan's accessibility target is the ability to reason: a reader can compare event times, choose a displacement statistic, change a parameter, inspect a conservation balance, and explain an equation step with their own assistive technology. The website verifies that on real assistive-technology combinations (`am-a11y-baseline-1cg5`), including VoiceOver with Safari on iOS, and records the equation announcement pattern (`am-eq-math-announcement-at-matrix-0al6`). Inside the app, VoiceOver moves between native chrome and a WKWebView, Dynamic Type comes from the system, and iPad readers may use a keyboard. This bead makes those transitions work and tests them.

## Scope

In scope: accessibility of native surfaces; focus handoff into and out of the edition; Dynamic Type layouts through the accessibility sizes; Voice Control and Switch Control reachability; hardware keyboard shortcuts on iPad; automated audits; additions to the manual assistive-technology protocol for the app.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the edition's own accessibility (the website's beads); sessions with disabled readers (`am-app-at-sessions-n6vj`).

## Requirements

1. **VoiceOver.** Native screens have labels, traits, and a logical order; opening an edition route moves focus to the edition's main heading at the requested anchor; the edition's landmarks and headings work with the rotor; leaving the edition returns focus to the native control that opened it.
2. **Equations.** Inside the app, the equation announcement pattern the website chose reads correctly with VoiceOver (MathML plus authored spoken forms, no duplicate announcements), verified on a real device.
3. **Dynamic Type.** Native layouts reflow at every size through the largest accessibility size without truncating essential labels or requiring horizontal scrolling; the edition's type size follows the mapping from `am-app-settings-prepaint-tydj`.
4. **Voice Control** labels match visible text; **Switch Control** reaches every native action; no native action depends on a gesture alone.
5. **Keyboard on iPad.** Command-K opens search, Command-F opens find in page, and Tab and arrow keys move focus through native controls; shortcuts appear in the system shortcut overlay.
6. **Motion.** Reduced motion follows the system; native transitions respect it; reading-only mode is available from native settings.
7. **Automated audits.** `XCUIApplication().performAccessibilityAudit()` runs on every native screen in UI tests, with any suppression recorded with a reason.
8. **Manual protocol.** Add an app section to `docs/accessibility/manual-protocol.md` (VoiceOver, Voice Control, Switch Control, largest text size, keyboard on iPad) with the reasoning actions to perform.

## Technical Approach

Accessibility identifiers for tests follow a stable naming scheme per screen; audits run in a dedicated UI test lane; focus handoff uses `UIAccessibility.post(notification: .screenChanged, argument:)` targeted at the web view after the edition's readiness signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Accessibility audits pass on every native screen, with any suppression recorded.
- [ ] VoiceOver focus lands on the requested anchor's heading after navigation and returns to the originating control after closing.
- [ ] At the largest accessibility text size, the library, outlines, catalogues, settings, and data panel remain usable without truncation of essential labels.
- [ ] Keyboard shortcuts work on iPad and appear in the shortcut overlay.
- [ ] The manual protocol has the app section, and a real-device VoiceOver check of an equation is recorded.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `AccessibilityLabelTests`: labels and traits for generated catalogue rows and states.

### End-to-end tests
- `AccessibilityUITests`: audits per screen; focus handoff; largest text size lane; iPad keyboard lane.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/app-a11y/<logRunId>.jsonl` with `screen`, `audit` (`passed`, `issues`), `issueTypes`, `textSize`, `device`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Automated audits are a supplement; the manual protocol and disabled readers decide acceptance.
- Do not duplicate edition content in native accessibility labels; let the edition speak for itself.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-settings-prepaint-tydj`, `am-app-navigation-shell-61d9`, `am-a11y-baseline-1cg5`, `am-eq-math-announcement-at-matrix-0al6`.

Unblocks: `am-app-at-sessions-n6vj`, `am-app-testflight-preview-w1if`.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Audit by GreenOx (pane %50), dispatch 117 item 1. Commits a1252da8 (product changes), 068e0273 (AccessibilityUITests and the manual protocol). Not a close request.

REQ 7, automated audits: DONE for every native screen. AccessibilityUITests 4 of 4 pass; 18 screen audits, 0 failing issues.
- AccessibilityUITests runs performAccessibilityAudit(for: .all) on 8 native screens at the default size (light) and at AccessibilityXXXL (dark): reading, menu, Contents papers, outline, Discover, a route, instruments, and Your data. The route's button is audited again once in view.
- A native issue fails the test. Every issue passed over is attached to each run with its reason:
  - DEBUG probes;
  - bar buttons (Done, Back, the segmented control), which report Dynamic Type "partially unsupported" because the system stops them growing and offers the Large Content Viewer;
  - the edition's own web content on the reading screen.
- What the audit found and what fixed it (a1252da8):
  - SwiftUI .secondary text failed contrast (secondaryLabel composites to #8a8a8e on white, about 3.4:1). It is now the site's muted ink, MutedInk.colorset generated from THEME_TOKENS, with a 4.5:1 test on every list background.
  - List section headers nearly passed; now muted ink.
  - The Contents tab bar's glass lay over the ends of long lists, and the text under it failed contrast. It is now a segmented control.
  - `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` inside a tinted button resolved to the tint, so rows were red. They now use explicit ink.
  - Sheets ignored the reader's dark theme, since preferredColorScheme does not cross a presentation. They now follow it.
  - "Open the route" (the Discover route's button) is the one element the audit keeps flagging as Dynamic Type "partially unsupported" and "may be clipped". Five forms were tried and all were flagged alike: plain Text, .font(.body), Label, an explicit colour, and no accessibility identifier. The AX5 screenshot shows the label wrapped onto two lines, whole. Those two findings are passed over for that element only, with the reason recorded. testOpenTheRouteGrowsWithTheReadersTextSize measures it instead: the text at AX5 must be more than twice its default height and inside its button. Measured: 20.3 pt tall at the default size, 125.3 pt at AX5, inside its button. A fixed 17 pt font planted in a scratch worktree turns the test red ("20.33 is not greater than 40.67").

REQ 3, Dynamic Type: the audits run at AX5 on every native screen, including the textClipped audit. The page's type size follows the mapping from am-app-settings-prepaint-tydj (15520867).

REQ 1, VoiceOver:
- A new page posts .screenChanged with the web view while VoiceOver runs.
- The page's title and §4 heading are in the accessibility tree (testThePagesHeadingsAreInTheAccessibilityTree).
- NOT verified: that focus lands on the anchor's heading, that it returns to the originating control, and that the rotor lists the headings as headings. XCUITest cannot run VoiceOver; each is a device task in the manual protocol.

REQ 6, motion: the native chrome adds no animation of its own (no withAnimation or transition in native code), so its sheets and menus are the system's, which follow Reduce Motion. No native reading-only setting exists.

REQ 8, manual protocol: docs/accessibility/manual-protocol.md section 8 (the app), with 7 device tasks. None has been performed.

NOT DONE:
- Req 2: equations checked with VoiceOver on a device.
- Req 4: Voice Control and Switch Control checked on a device.
- Req 5: iPad keyboard shortcuts (Command-K, Command-F) and the shortcut overlay.
- Req 7's structured artifacts/test-logs/app-a11y log.

SITE FINDINGS, reported to TanElk: on the reading page, the face tabs, the eyebrow and the skip link fail Apple's hit-area audit. They are recorded as web content, not failed.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SapphireCastle (p46), 2026-09-24, dispatch 125. The reading screen's web-content audit issue 'Hit area is too small' on the four face tabs is NOT fixable by CSS. Measured in the simulator, not inferred.
METHOD: two copies of the built products (DerivedData/AnnusMirabilis-am, xctestrun 26.1-arm64) went to my scratchpad; the shared build was not touched. Run: xcodebuild test-without-building -only-testing:AnnusMirabilisUITests/AccessibilityUITests/testEveryNativeScreenAtTheDefaultSize on AM iPhone 17 (iOS 26.1). Both runs passed (182.7s, 186.7s).
- A, control (edition CSS unchanged: .face-tabs>a{display:inline-flex;min-height:44px}, a 44px box): reading-default reports Explanation (16,645,75,18), Results (106,645,47,18), German source (168,645,97,18), Facsimile (280,645,60,18). This reproduces xcresult 20260924T110259Z-5f6260ad.
- B, the same app with .face-tabs>a{min-height:0;padding-block:0;line-height:44px}, re-signed ad hoc: the same four at 75x18, 47x18, 97x18, 60x18, y 646. The screenshot shows the tab row 2pt taller, so the CSS loaded.
CONCLUSION: iOS gives a web link the frame of its text's glyphs, not its CSS box and not its line box. For these tabs that is 18pt at the fine size. The tappable box in WKWebView is 44 tall and 45 to 97 wide; the audit measures something CSS does not control. It records web content without failing, which is right for this finding. Making the audit's number reach 44 would need 32px text or turning navigation links into buttons, and I recommend neither. No commit. Evidence: the two xcresult bundles and screenshots are under my session scratchpad in xcexp/{A,B}.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: UPDATE (GreenOx, 2026-09-24): the accessibility audit on the iPad. AccessibilityUITests on AM iPad first failed on every native sheet: grey system sheet backgrounds lowered muted ink to 4.19:1, and a small form sheet left rows over the dimmed page. Fixed in fcfca6aa (the edition's paper, 5.98:1 in both themes) and 0a04445a (page-sized sheets on iPad). Run 20260924T174509Z-8c313d9f: every named issue is gone. Three issues without an element remain, all on the Instruments screen (1 contrast at default size, 2 Dynamic Type at the largest). The audit names only a SwiftUI.AccessibilityNode, so they cannot be attributed; they are recorded here, not passed over. The gate audits on the iPhone, where every screen passes (7/7 with these changes).

title: Add the verified iPhone app chapter to AGENTS.md and README with commands and rules
description:
# Add the verified iPhone app chapter to AGENTS.md and README with commands and rules

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** App plan §3.3, §4, §14 (traceability only)

## Background

FrankenPatents' AGENTS.md had no iOS section at all, so agents learned its native rules from comments in `project.yml` and from bead text. Annus Mirabilis's AGENTS.md gained a short planning-stage iPhone app section when the plan was written. Once the Apple gate and the release script exist, that section must become a verified chapter: real commands that were run, the rules that protect the doctrine, and the pitfalls the donor paid for.

## Scope

In scope: expanding the AGENTS.md iPhone app section into a chapter and adding an iPhone app section to README.md, with every command verified.

Out of scope: changing any rule of the master plan.

## Requirements

1. **Rules:** Swift never computes a displayed physical quantity or authors reader-facing scientific text; the reader never loads remote content; the edition is built from the same commit and bound to the website's `releaseId`; generated models, tokens, route tables, and editions are never hand-edited; no third-party Swift packages without a recorded reason; uploads only through the verified app release script with authorization; Apple accounts, external testing, and submission are human-gated; never delete or erase simulators or reader data; Apple validation is local.
2. **Commands,** each run and verified before writing it down: regenerate the project, create the named simulators, run the Apple gate, export and bundle the edition, run edition parity, run the in-app journeys, and a release dry run.
3. **Map:** the `ios/` and `scripts/app/` layout from App plan §4.
4. **Pitfalls:** stale generated projects, simulator attachment, screenshot orientation, DerivedData disk use, user script sandboxing, universal link caching, and the bridge's security rules.
5. **README:** a short iPhone app section with the build commands and a link to the app plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every command in the chapter was executed on a clean checkout, and its output matched the description.
- [ ] README and AGENTS.md command names match the package scripts and files.
- [ ] The chapter's rules match App plan §3.3 and the epic's rules.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- The existing check that README and AGENTS.md command names match package scripts covers the new commands.

### End-to-end tests
- A fresh-clone walkthrough of the chapter's commands, with its log retained.

### Structured logging
- The walkthrough logs each command, exit code, and duration to `artifacts/test-logs/app-docs/<logRunId>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never document a command that does not exist yet; mark planned steps as planned.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-apple-quality-gate-q6gs`, `am-app-verified-release-1jbu`.

Unblocks: none.

title: Set up the Apple Developer team, App ID capabilities, App Store Connect record, and upload key with explicit authorization
description:
# Set up the Apple Developer team, App ID capabilities, App Store Connect record, and upload key with explicit authorization

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P2 · **Labels:** human-gate · **Plan sections:** App plan §14.1, §14.3 (traceability only)

## Background

Uploading a build needs an Apple Developer Program membership for the chosen team, an App ID with the capabilities the app uses, an App Store Connect app record, and an App Store Connect API key for command-line uploads. These steps involve accounts, legal agreements, and credentials. An agent never creates accounts, accepts agreements, or handles credentials; the user performs those steps, and the agent records what exists without recording secrets. The planning machine had no App Store Connect key on 2026-09-14.

## Scope

In scope: a checklist the user completes; verification that the configuration matches the identity decision; recording non-secret identifiers and the key's storage location; repository guards against committed credentials.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the identity decision (`am-app-decision-identity-wago`); the release script (`am-app-verified-release-1jbu`).

## Requirements

1. **Membership and agreements:** the user confirms active membership for the chosen team and accepted agreements in App Store Connect.
2. **App ID:** the bundle identifier from the identity decision with Associated Domains enabled (App Groups only if the later widget is built).
3. **App Store Connect record:** created by the user with the decided name, bundle identifier, SKU, and primary language (English), which cannot be changed later.
4. **API key:** created by the user with the least role that can upload builds, downloaded once and stored outside the repository (for example `~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_<keyId>.p8` with owner-only permissions); the key id and issuer id recorded in a local, untracked configuration file outside the repository or in documented environment variable names.
5. **Signing:** automatic signing with the team; no certificates, profiles, or keys in the repository.
6. **Guards:** confirm `.gitignore` covers `*.p8`, `*.p12`, `*.cer`, `*.mobileprovision`, and `*.ipa`; add a repository scan in the Apple gate that fails if such a file is tracked.
7. **Record:** `docs/app/APPLE_ACCOUNT.md` with the team name and id, bundle identifier, App ID capabilities, the App Store Connect app id, the key's role, the key id's last four characters, the storage location, and dates, with no secret values.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The App ID, capabilities, and App Store Connect record match the identity decision.
- [ ] An API key exists outside the repository with owner-only permissions, and its non-secret identifiers are recorded.
- [ ] The Apple gate's tracked-credential scan passes and fails on a seeded tracked `.p8` file.
- [ ] `docs/app/APPLE_ACCOUNT.md` contains no secret.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/app/credential-scan.test.ts`: tracked credential file detection and permission checks on the key path (reported, never printed).

### End-to-end tests
- A dry run of `am-app-verified-release-1jbu` reaches the upload step's authentication check without uploading.

### Structured logging
- The credential scan logs file patterns checked and outcome, never paths to or contents of keys, to `artifacts/test-logs/app-credentials/<logRunId>.jsonl`.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** the user, who owns the Apple accounts.
- **Evidence to record:** `docs/app/APPLE_ACCOUNT.md` and a `br comments add` with the date and the user's confirmation.
- **Agents may prepare:** the checklist and the scan. Agents never create accounts, accept agreements, enter credentials, or close this bead on their own judgment.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A downloaded API key cannot be downloaded again; losing it means creating a new one.
- Never paste key contents into a conversation, log, or commit.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-decision-identity-wago`.

Unblocks: `am-app-verified-release-1jbu`.

title: Build the local Apple gate and register it as the apple family in the quality-gate registry
description:
# Build the local Apple gate and register it as the apple family in the quality-gate registry

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** App plan §2.2, §2.4, §13.3, §14.2 (traceability only)

## Background

FrankenPatents validated its app with one local script: disk check, XcodeGen regenerate-and-diff, parity check, plist lint, simulator build, unit tests, UI tests into `.xcresult`, all with isolated DerivedData. That script caught real regressions, but it wrote no structured logs and was not part of the donor's gate registry. Annus Mirabilis already has a typed gate registry and runner (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`) and a shared JSONL logger (`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`). This bead adapts the donor script into that system as the `apple` family, local by default, required by the app release profiles, and not required by the website's CI.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/app/apple-quality.ts` and its pure planning and parsing modules; `scripts/app/simulators.ts`; `scripts/app/toolchain.test.ts`; registry entries; package scripts; tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the individual checks' subjects (for example edition parity in `am-app-edition-parity-bwa5` and journeys in `am-app-e2e-journeys-vm0t`, which register their steps here when they land); the release script (`am-app-verified-release-1jbu`).

## Requirements

1. **Steps, in order,** each a registry `GateStep` with `family: "apple"`, `requiredInCi: false`, and the app release profiles in `requiredInProfiles`:
   - `apple-disk` (at least the recorded free space, via `sbh` when present, otherwise `df`);
   - `apple-toolchain` (installed versions equal the `apple-toolchain` decision block);
   - `apple-project-fresh` (`xcodegen generate` then `git diff --exit-code -- ios/AnnusMirabilis.xcodeproj`);
   - `apple-plist-lint` (`plutil -lint` on `Info.plist`, `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, entitlements);
   - `apple-swiftlint` and `apple-swift-format`;
   - `apple-generated-fresh` (generated Swift models, tokens, and route tables match their generators; registered by those beads);
   - `apple-edition-fresh` (the bundled edition's manifest matches `HEAD`; registered by `am-app-edition-bundling-xzm1`);
   - `apple-build` (simulator build with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` into `ios/build/DerivedData`);
   - `apple-unit-tests` and `apple-ui-tests` (named simulators, `.xcresult` bundles under `ios/build/results/<logRunId>/`, UI tests with parallel testing disabled unless proven safe).
2. **Outcomes** use the registry's vocabulary: `passed`, `failed`, `not-available`, `skipped` with a reason, `refused`.
3. **Simulators:** `scripts/app/simulators.ts` creates the named simulators from the toolchain decision if absent, reuses them if present, prints their UDIDs as JSON, and never deletes or erases any simulator.
4. **Result parsing:** read test counts and failures from `.xcresult` with `xcrun xcresulttool`, not from console text.
5. **Logs:** one JSONL file per run through the shared logger at `artifacts/test-logs/app-apple-gate/<logRunId>.jsonl`, with the standard fields plus `step`, `xcode`, `simulatorName`, `simulatorUdid`, `osVersion`, `xcresultPath`, `durationMs`, and `outcome`.
6. **Package scripts:** `bun run gates:apple` runs the family fail-fast; `bun run gates:apple --all` runs every step and summarizes.
7. **Environment isolation:** `TMPDIR` and DerivedData under `ios/build/`, overridable by `AM_APPLE_BUILD_ROOT`, never the user's global DerivedData.

## Technical Approach

Keep step planning, version comparison, and `.xcresult` summary parsing as pure functions with fixtures, and a thin CLI that calls `xcodebuild`, `xcodegen`, `plutil`, `swiftlint`, and `xcrun`. Register steps in the existing registry rather than creating a second runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bun run gates:apple` passes on a clean tree after the scaffold lands.
- [ ] Seeded failures fail for the intended reason with a repair message: a hand-edited project file, a malformed privacy manifest, a failing unit test, and a toolchain version mismatch.
- [ ] A missing tool yields `not-available` (or `refused` under a release profile) rather than a crash.
- [ ] No step deletes or erases a simulator, and DerivedData stays under `ios/build/`.
- [ ] The website's CI configuration does not run or require the `apple` family.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/app/apple-quality.test.ts`: step planning per mode and profile; outcome mapping; `.xcresult` summary parsing from recorded fixtures (passing, failing, crashed test runner).
- `scripts/app/toolchain.test.ts`: decision block parsing and version comparison, including a mismatched Xcode build.
- `scripts/app/simulators.test.ts`: the creation plan from `simctl list --json` fixtures reuses existing names and never plans a deletion.

### End-to-end tests
- A full local run on the scaffold with logs retained, and a seeded-failure run whose log and `.xcresult` path are asserted.

### Structured logging
- As in Requirement 5; a failing step records the command, exit code, the last 200 lines of output, and the `.xcresult` path.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- `XCUIScreen.main` and default destinations can resolve to another booted simulator; always pass `-destination id=<udid>`.
- DerivedData can fill a disk quickly; the disk step runs first.
- Xcode's user script sandboxing blocks undeclared file access in build phases; declare inputs and outputs rather than disabling sandboxing silently.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-xcodegen-scaffold-z228`, `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`, `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`.

Unblocks: `am-app-test-harness-da6e`, `am-app-verified-release-1jbu`, `am-app-agents-chapter-egpg`.

title: Run assistive-technology sessions with disabled readers on the app's Brownian reference slice
description:
# Run assistive-technology sessions with disabled readers on the app's Brownian reference slice

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** human-gate · **Plan sections:** App plan §10, §17 (traceability only)

## Background

Automated audits prove that controls have labels; they cannot prove that a blind reader can compare signed and squared displacements, or that a switch user can change viscosity and read the result. The website runs these sessions with disabled readers using their own tools. The app changes the tools (VoiceOver on iOS with a WKWebView inside native chrome, Voice Control, Switch Control, very large text), so the app needs its own sessions before it reaches external testers.

## Scope

In scope: recruiting through the existing comprehension protocol, running sessions on the app's Brownian slice, recording findings as beads, and recording evidence.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the consent materials and rubric (`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`); fixing findings (new beads filed from this one).

## Requirements

1. **Participants.** At least three readers who use, respectively, VoiceOver, Switch Control or Voice Control, and very large text or zoom, each on their own iPhone or iPad where feasible, recruited and compensated under the comprehension protocol's consent terms.
2. **Build.** A development or TestFlight internal build of the Brownian slice, installed with the participant's consent.
3. **Tasks.** The slice's reasoning actions: explain why the signed average can vanish while the squared spread grows; predict how a more viscous liquid changes spread at the same time and check it with typed input; open the derivation step for the square-root time dependence and return to the source passage; identify which scene is simulated.
4. **Recording.** For each task: completion, the precise stumbling point with the route and action id, and the assistive technology and settings used. No diagnosis or personal history is collected.
5. **Findings** become beads labeled `app-ios` and `a11y` with evidence, linked to this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Sessions with at least three participants covering the three assistive-technology groups are recorded.
- [ ] Every stumbling point has a filed bead or a recorded decision.
- [ ] Evidence names reviewers or anonymized participant ids per consent, and dates.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- None; human sessions.

### End-to-end tests
- The journeys in `am-app-e2e-journeys-vm0t` must pass before a session, so participants never meet a known bug.

### Structured logging
- Session records use the comprehension protocol's format; any app telemetry during sessions is limited to the test build's local logs, never uploaded.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** disabled readers using their own assistive setups, and a session facilitator following the protocol.
- **Evidence to record:** a `br comments add` on this bead with dates, participant ids or names per consent, completed tasks, and the location of session notes.
- **Agents may prepare:** the build, the task script, and the recording template. Agents never close this bead on their own judgment.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A participant's own settings (speech rate, verbosity, switch scanning mode) matter; do not reset them.
- Findings about the edition itself also go to the website's accessibility beads, since the same edition serves both.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-accessibility-4h2o`, `am-app-e2e-journeys-vm0t`, `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`.

Unblocks: `am-app-slice-exit-nzvs`.

title: Define the versioned native-edition bridge with an allowlisted, schema-validated message protocol and capability detection
description:
# Define the versioned native-edition bridge with an allowlisted, schema-validated message protocol and capability detection

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** App plan §7.1 to §7.3, §12 (traceability only)

## Background

A few things only native code can do well for the edition: keep reader data safely on the device, advertise the current passage for Handoff and "Continue reading," hand a canonical link to the share sheet, open an external link outside the reader, download a pinned facsimile, and print a chapter. The bridge is the only channel for those requests. It is also the most security-sensitive seam in the app, because it connects web content to native capabilities. It must be narrow, versioned, validated on both sides, restricted to the edition's main frame, and invisible to browsers, so the same web build runs unchanged on the website.

## Scope

In scope: the TypeScript side under `src/platform/app-bridge/`; the Swift side under `ios/AnnusMirabilis/Edition/Bridge/`; the message schemas; the fixed document-start user scripts; capability detection; validation, limits, and origin checks; contract fixtures shared by both sides; tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the storage backend (`am-app-storage-backend-7at7`), settings (`am-app-settings-prepaint-tydj`), share, Handoff, and print (`am-app-handoff-share-print-9iqs`), facsimile downloads (`am-app-facsimile-downloads-72nz`), and lifecycle events (`am-app-lifecycle-resilience-4dhu`); each implements its handlers against this protocol.

## Requirements

1. **Capability detection.** A fixed document-start user script defines a frozen `window.__AM_APP__` with `bridgeVersion`, `capabilities` (an array of strings), and a synchronous frozen `settings` snapshot. Web code checks for it and, when absent (every browser), behaves exactly as today. No web build flag, no second bundle.
2. **Messages in version 1** (edition to native, with replies through `WKScriptMessageHandlerWithReply` where a reply is needed): `hello`; `storage.read`, `storage.write`, `storage.list`, `storage.clear`, `storage.export`; `settings.changed`; `route.changed` (route, anchor, title); `share.request` (canonical URL, optional tape permalink); `external.open` (https URL); `facsimile.status`, `facsimile.request`; `print.request`; and, in DEBUG and test builds only, `test.log` and `test.snapshot`.
3. **Native to edition events** through one fixed function the user script defines, `window.__AM_APP__.dispatch(eventName, payload)`, restricted to the enumerated events `settings.changed`, `lifecycle.memoryWarning`, `lifecycle.thermalState`, `lifecycle.visibility`, and `facsimile.updated`. Native code never evaluates any other JavaScript.
4. **Validation.** Both sides validate against schemas generated from one source (zod on the web side; Swift types generated by the model generator from `am-app-native-payloads-bued`). Reject unknown types, unknown versions, unknown fields, wrong types, and bodies over 256 KiB; rate-limit each type (for example 50 per second) and log rejections in test builds.
5. **Origin.** Accept a message only when `frameInfo.isMainFrame` is true and `frameInfo.securityOrigin` equals the edition origin.
6. **URL rules.** `share.request` accepts only canonical `https://annus-mirabilis.com/` URLs whose path exists in the route table and whose tape parameter passes the edition's own bounds; `external.open` accepts only `https` URLs with a host and never `javascript:`, `data:`, or `file:`.
7. **Results, never exceptions.** Replies use result shapes (`ok`, `missing`, `unavailable`, `corrupt`, `quota`, `rejected`) so no bridge failure throws into rendering code.
8. **Script integrity.** The user scripts are compiled from `src/platform/app-bridge/userScripts.ts` at export time; their SHA-256 values are written to the edition manifest, and the app refuses to inject a script whose digest differs.
9. **Contract fixtures.** Golden message fixtures (valid and invalid) generated from the TypeScript schemas are decoded by both sides with identical verdicts.

## Technical Approach

TypeScript: `src/platform/app-bridge/{capabilities,schemas,client,userScripts}.ts` with no dependency on DOM APIs beyond the message handler. Swift: `BridgeRouter` decodes and dispatches to registered handlers by message type; handlers are actors or main-actor types as appropriate. Rejections return `rejected` with a reason code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The website build runs in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with no behavioral change and no bridge errors.
- [ ] In the app, `hello` returns the bridge version and capabilities, and every v1 message round-trips with fixtures.
- [ ] Contract fixtures produce identical verdicts in TypeScript and Swift.
- [ ] Messages from a subframe, a foreign origin, an unknown type, an oversized body, or a flood beyond the rate limit are rejected and logged in test builds.
- [ ] Release builds contain no `test.log` or `test.snapshot` handling.
- [ ] A user script with a modified digest is not injected.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `src/platform/app-bridge/schemas.test.ts` and `client.test.ts`: validation, capability absence in browsers, result shapes, URL rules.
- `BridgeRouterTests` (Swift): fixtures, origin checks, limits, rate limiting, reply shapes.
- `BridgeWebKitTests` (hosted `WKWebView`): end-to-end round trips, subframe rejection, dispatch of each native event.

### End-to-end tests
- `BridgeUITests.testRouteChangedUpdatesContinueReading` once the shell exists (owned by `am-app-navigation-shell-61d9`, listed here for traceability).

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/app-bridge/<logRunId>.jsonl` with `messageType`, `direction`, `bytes`, `outcome`, and `reason`; storage contents never logged.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- `evaluateJavaScript` with string concatenation is an injection risk; dispatch serializes the payload with a JSON encoder into a fixed call template, and event names come only from an enum.
- Keep the capability surface small; every new message type is a security review item.
- A future bridge version must keep answering `hello` from older editions correctly, or the app must refuse the edition with a plain message that names the mismatch.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-edition-webview-ju3v`, `am-app-native-payloads-bued`.

Unblocks: `am-app-storage-backend-7at7`, `am-app-settings-prepaint-tydj`, `am-app-handoff-share-print-9iqs`, `am-app-facsimile-downloads-72nz`, `am-app-lifecycle-resilience-4dhu`.

comments.text: UPDATE (GreenOx, 2026-09-24): criterion 5, 'Release builds contain no test.log or test.snapshot handling', is now MET by inspection, not only by construction (9c3128b6). The Apple gate step apple-release-absence builds the Release configuration and searches its executables for the DEBUG-only markers: the properties the test.log and test.snapshot handling calls (onTestLog, onTestSnapshot) and TestEvidence's type name and literals. Run 20260924T122458Z-531f5cba: all 6 found in the DEBUG build (positive control), none in Release. Release showed both control names every build carries (onStorageWrite, EditionSchemeHandler). The short literals "test.log" and "test.snapshot" are not searched for: an optimized build may pack a string of 15 bytes or fewer into its instructions, so their absence would prove nothing. title: Decide the app's name, bundle identifier, Apple team, devices, category, and minimum iOS
description:
# Decide the app's name, bundle identifier, Apple team, devices, category, and minimum iOS

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** human-gate · **Plan sections:** App plan §1.4, §3.4, §8.1, §14.4, §18 (traceability only)

## Background

Store identity reaches almost everything downstream: the Xcode project, entitlements, the Apple App Site Association file the website serves, the App Store Connect record, screenshots, and the listing. Some of it is permanent: an App Store record's bundle identifier and primary language cannot be changed after creation. These are the owner's decisions, not an agent's.

FrankenPatents, the donor app, used the bundle identifier `com.frankenpatents.FrankenPatents`, iPhone and iPad plus Mac Catalyst, iOS 17.0, and the Reference category. The app plan proposes iPhone and iPad without Mac Catalyst, because the website already serves the Mac.

## Scope

In scope: preparing options with evidence, obtaining the user's decision, and recording it in `docs/DECISIONS.md` with a machine-readable block that later beads validate against.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: creating the App ID and App Store Connect record (`am-app-apple-account-setup-9xi1`); the Apple toolchain (`am-app-decision-toolchain-qs6d`); the final minimum iOS evidence (`am-app-webkit-probe-8hj1` records which WebKit features each iOS version supports).

## Decision

**Question:** under which identity does the app ship, on which devices, and in which store category?

**Items to decide:**
- **App Store name** (at most 30 characters) and **subtitle**, with availability checked by the user in App Store Connect. Prepare alternatives, for example "Annus Mirabilis," "Annus Mirabilis 1905," and "Annus Mirabilis: The 1905 Papers."
- **Bundle identifier** (permanent once an App Store record exists) and **SKU**.
- **Apple Developer team** (the FrankenPatents team or another), recorded by team name and team id. Team ids are not secrets; keys and certificates never enter the repository.
- **Devices:** iPhone and iPad (proposed). Mac Catalyst excluded in version 1. Decide explicitly whether the iPad build is offered on Apple silicon Macs.
- **Minimum iOS:** proposed 17.0, provisional until the WebKit probe records feature support.
- **Category:** Education primary and Reference secondary (proposed); **price:** free; **availability:** worldwide; **age rating:** answered through Apple's questionnaire (expected 4+).
- **URLs on annus-mirabilis.com:** marketing, support, and privacy policy locations (the pages themselves are built by `am-app-store-listing-ovhw`).
- **Copyright line** for the listing.

**Options and default:** the plan's proposals above. An agent never chooses among them.

**Recording:** `## D-<date>-app-identity` in `docs/DECISIONS.md` with question, options, choice, reason, decider (the user), date, and the user's verbatim words, followed by a fenced YAML block labeled `app-identity` with `appName`, `subtitle`, `bundleId`, `sku`, `teamName`, `teamId`, `devices`, `macDesignedForIPad`, `minimumIOS` (with `provisional: true` until the probe confirms), `primaryCategory`, `secondaryCategory`, and the three URLs.

## Requirements

1. Prepare a short options memo in the session scratch directory (never the repository root) with the FrankenPatents precedent and App Store search evidence for each candidate name. Web requests use the user agent "OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0".
2. Present the options to the user and record the answer verbatim with its timestamp.
3. List the implications in the decision entry: the associated-domains entitlement, the association file's `appID` (`<teamId>.<bundleId>`), and an App Group identifier only if the later widget is built.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/DECISIONS.md` contains the app identity entry with every item, the user as decider, the date, and the verbatim quote.
- [ ] The `app-identity` YAML block parses and includes every listed key.
- [ ] `minimumIOS` stays marked provisional until the probe's decision entry references it.
- [ ] No name, bundle identifier, or team was chosen on an agent's own judgment.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- The block is validated by `scripts/app/identity.test.ts`, which `am-app-xcodegen-scaffold-z228` creates: it parses the entry's YAML and asserts that `ios/project.yml` and the generated association file agree with it.

### End-to-end tests
- None; this is a human decision.

### Structured logging
- None.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** the user.
- **Evidence to record:** the decision entry and a `br comments add` on this bead with the quote and timestamp.
- **Agents may prepare:** the options memo and the entry skeleton. Agents never close this bead without the user's decision.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The store requires unique names; a close existing name may push the choice toward a subtitle.
- The owner decided on 2026-09-14 that public-domain photographs of Einstein are welcome, including the frontispiece. The icon uses the page-count mark from the placeholder site.
- Do not create the App Store Connect record here; creating it fixes the bundle identifier.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: none.

Unblocks: `am-app-xcodegen-scaffold-z228`, `am-app-universal-links-re8v`, `am-app-apple-account-setup-9xi1`, `am-app-store-listing-ovhw`.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Decided under the owner's 2026-09-23 delegation (dispatch 101 for %50), recorded as agent:GreenOx, overrulable: docs/DECISIONS.md D-2026-09-23-app-identity, commit fc879215. YAML block app-identity parses (18 keys). Team id is the named placeholder OWNER_SUPPLIES_APPLE_TEAM_ID, which the signing gate refuses; the owner supplies it. App Store search (iTunes Search API, us, software + iPadSoftware) for 'annus mirabilis': 0 apps. minimumIOS 17.0 stays provisional. This bead carries human-gate: the owner can overrule any field before the App Store Connect record fixes the bundle id.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
AUDIT (GreenOx, 2026-09-23). This bead carries human-gate.
1. Entry with every item, the USER as decider, and a verbatim quote: NOT MET, by design of the delegation. D-2026-09-23-app-identity (fc879215) has every item, but the decider is agent:GreenOx under the owner's delegation. The Apple team is the named placeholder OWNER_SUPPLIES_APPLE_TEAM_ID.
2. app-identity YAML parses with every key: MET. scripts/app/identity.test.ts parses it (5 pass). Keys: appName, subtitle, bundleId, sku, teamName, teamId, devices, macDesignedForIPad, minimumIOS{version,provisional}, primaryCategory, secondaryCategory, urls{marketing,support,privacyPolicy}.
3. minimumIOS provisional until the probe entry references it: MET. provisional: true; D-2026-09-23-app-edition-hosting says the probe justifies nothing below iOS 26.1.
4. No name, bundle id or team chosen on an agent's own judgment: NOT MET for name and bundle id (agent-chosen under delegation); MET for the team (not chosen).

title: Lock the Apple toolchain, Swift language mode, project generator, linters, test frameworks, simulators, and the local Apple gate policy
description:
# Lock the Apple toolchain, Swift language mode, project generator, linters, test frameworks, simulators, and the local Apple gate policy

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** App plan §2.2, §4, §13.3, §14.1, §14.2 (traceability only)

## Background

The Xcode project must be reproducible from `ios/project.yml` on any machine the project uses, and every Apple gate result must name the tools that produced it. On 2026-09-14 the planning machine had Xcode 26.1.1 (build 17B100), Swift 6.2.1, the iOS 26.1 simulator runtime with iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, and iPhone 16e devices, and SwiftLint. XcodeGen, fastlane, and an App Store Connect API key were absent.

FrankenPatents used XcodeGen, Swift 5.10, iOS 17.0, and a local gate script; it added a GitHub Actions Apple workflow and removed it the same day, keeping Apple validation local by policy. Its history also records DerivedData filling the boot disk until builds were isolated, and UI tests attaching to the wrong booted simulator.

## Scope

In scope: choosing and recording versions and policies for the Apple toolchain, and a machine-readable block that `am-app-apple-quality-gate-q6gs` checks.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: web stack versions (`am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`); the minimum iOS evidence (`am-app-webkit-probe-8hj1`); signing and App Store Connect (`am-app-apple-account-setup-9xi1`).

## Decision

**Question:** which exact tools and policies build, lint, and test the app?

**Items to decide:**
- **Xcode** version and build, and the iOS SDK. Policy: a new Xcode major or iOS major reruns the WebKit probe before adoption.
- **Swift language mode:** Swift 6 with complete strict concurrency checking (proposed), or Swift 5 mode with a recorded reason.
- **Project generation:** XcodeGen (proposed, the donor's precedent), its exact version, and the install method (a pinned Homebrew formula or Mint), so `xcodegen --version` can be checked.
- **Lint and format:** SwiftLint at a pinned version; `swift format` from the Swift toolchain (proposed) rather than a second formatter.
- **Test frameworks:** Swift Testing for unit and integration tests; XCTest and XCUITest for UI tests and `XCTMetric` performance tests.
- **Simulators:** dedicated, named simulators created idempotently by a script, for example `AM iPhone 17`, `AM iPhone 16e` (the smallest current screen), and `AM iPad`, on the pinned runtime; whether to install the runtime of the minimum iOS version for a compatibility lane.
- **Where Apple validation runs:** locally (proposed). No GitHub macOS runners unless the user decides otherwise. The `apple` gate family is not required in the website's CI.
- **Isolation:** DerivedData, result bundles, and logs under the gitignored `ios/build/`; a disk guard of at least 20 GB free before building, using `sbh` when present and `df` otherwise.
- **Dependencies:** no third-party Swift packages in version 1.
- **Upload tooling:** `xcodebuild -exportArchive` with App Store Connect API key authentication (proposed); no fastlane, which would add a Ruby toolchain.
- **App icon format:** the icon format the pinned Xcode expects (for example an Icon Composer file on Xcode 26), recorded so `am-app-design-tokens-3iup` produces the right artifact.

**Recording:** `## D-<date>-apple-toolchain` in `docs/DECISIONS.md` with the shared fields, plus a fenced YAML block labeled `apple-toolchain` with `xcode`, `xcodeBuild`, `iosSdk`, `swiftLanguageMode`, `xcodegen`, `swiftlint`, `swiftFormat`, `simulators` (name, device type, runtime), `diskFreeGigabytesMinimum`, and `uploadMethod`.

## Requirements

1. Record each tool's installed version with the exact command that printed it (`xcodebuild -version`, `swift --version`, `xcrun simctl list runtimes`, `xcodegen --version`, `swiftlint version`).
2. Install missing tools only with the user's approval, and record how they were installed.
3. State the upgrade policy: tool upgrades are deliberate changes that rerun the Apple gate and, for Xcode or iOS majors, the WebKit probe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/DECISIONS.md` contains the Apple toolchain entry with every item, its reason, and the recorded version evidence.
- [ ] The `apple-toolchain` YAML block parses and lists every key.
- [ ] The simulator names and device types are recorded, so tests never rely on "whatever is booted".
- [ ] The decision states that Apple validation is local and not required in the website's CI, or records the user's different choice.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `am-app-apple-quality-gate-q6gs` owns `scripts/app/toolchain.test.ts`, which parses the block and compares it with the installed tools, failing with the mismatched tool and the install command.

### End-to-end tests
- None beyond the gate's first run.

### Structured logging
- None here; the gate logs the toolchain it ran with on every run.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Xcode and simulator runtimes are large; check disk space before installing a runtime.
- Swift 6 strict concurrency catches data races in the scheme handler and bridge early, which matters because WebKit calls handlers off the main thread.
- Never delete a user's existing simulators; create the named ones beside them.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax` (the web stack and Bun versions the export scripts use).

Unblocks: `am-app-webkit-probe-8hj1`, `am-app-xcodegen-scaffold-z228`.

title: Generate native design tokens and fonts from the web theme, and make the icon, launch screen, and frontispiece asset
description:
# Generate native design tokens and fonts from the web theme, and make the icon, launch screen, and frontispiece asset

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** App plan §2.4, §8.1, §9 (traceability only)

## Background

FrankenPatents re-typed its palette by hand in `Theme.swift`, so its native colors could drift from the website's. Annus Mirabilis generates native tokens from the web theme tokens (`am-design-themes-typography-288q`), bundles the same self-hosted font subsets, and reuses the identity the placeholder site established: the Annalen paper color, Newsreader typography, the page-count mark of four bars in the proportions 17, 12, 31, and 3, and Lucien Chavan's public-domain portrait of Einstein at the Bern patent office (ETH-Bibliothek Zürich, Bildarchiv, Portr_05937), which the owner chose to feature front and center.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/app/generate-design-tokens.ts`; generated Swift tokens; bundled fonts and their licenses; a native contrast test; the procedural app icon in the format the toolchain decision names; the launch screen color; the frontispiece image asset with its credit; the `apple-generated-fresh` registration for tokens.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the web theme itself; screens that use tokens (`am-app-navigation-shell-61d9`); App Store screenshots (`am-app-e2e-journeys-vm0t`).

## Requirements

1. **Tokens.** Generate `ios/AnnusMirabilis/Design/Generated/Tokens.swift` from `src/app/theme/tokens.ts` exports: colors per theme (Annalen, Kramgasse Night, Slate) with semantic names, spacing, rule weights, radii, and the type scale, deterministic, with a "generated, do not edit" header.
2. **Fonts.** Copy the web's Newsreader, Plus Jakarta Sans, and JetBrains Mono subsets into the app, register them with `UIAppFonts`, and include the OFL license texts in the About screen's licenses.
3. **Contrast.** A test computes WCAG contrast for every native text and background pair declared in the tokens and fails below 4.5:1 for normal text (3:1 for large text and non-text boundaries).
4. **App icon.** A deterministic renderer draws the four-bar page-count mark on the Annalen paper color at the sizes and appearances (including dark and tinted variants where the pinned Xcode supports them) required by the recorded icon format.
5. **Launch screen** uses the Annalen paper color with no text.
6. **Frontispiece asset.** Derived crops of the ETH-Bibliothek scan (the same 4:5 crop the placeholder site uses) in `@1x`, `@2x`, and `@3x` sizes, with the credit string "Albert Einstein at the Swiss patent office in Bern, about 1905. Photograph by Lucien Chavan; ETH-Bibliothek Zürich, Bildarchiv. Public domain." recorded beside it for the library screen and the About screen.

## Technical Approach

The generator reads the token module through Bun and writes Swift with a stable ordering; the icon renderer draws vector shapes and rasterizes with the pinned tools so bytes are reproducible on the same machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Generated tokens compile and match the web tokens; regeneration without changes produces no diff.
- [ ] A seeded web token change without regeneration fails `apple-generated-fresh`.
- [ ] The contrast test passes and fails on a seeded low-contrast pair.
- [ ] The fonts render German diacritics in a native label test, and their licenses appear in About.
- [ ] The icon passes the pinned Xcode's asset validation, and the frontispiece renders with its credit.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/app/generate-design-tokens.test.ts`: golden Swift output for fixture tokens.
- `TokenContrastTests` (Swift): every declared pair.
- `FontRegistrationTests`: each family loads; a label with "Über die … Flüssigkeiten" renders without fallback glyphs.

### End-to-end tests
- `LibraryUITests.testFrontispieceAndCredit` (owned by `am-app-navigation-shell-61d9`, listed here for traceability).

### Structured logging
- The generator logs token counts and output digests to `artifacts/test-logs/app-design-tokens/<logRunId>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Native chrome should still feel like iOS; use the tokens for color and type, not to imitate web widgets.
- Do not use a remote font loader or system font substitution for German diacritics.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-xcodegen-scaffold-z228`, `am-design-themes-typography-288q`.

Unblocks: `am-app-navigation-shell-61d9`.

title: Write continuous in-app journeys per paper with offline, relaunch, iPad, large-text, and no-WASM lanes, and App Store screenshots from real content
description:
# Write continuous in-app journeys per paper with offline, relaunch, iPad, large-text, and no-WASM lanes, and App Store screenshots from real content

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** App plan §13.1, §13.2, §17 (traceability only)

## Background

The website proves each paper with one continuous browser journey (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, first used by `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`): enter through a deep source passage, switch face, open a foundation, return to the exact argument, operate an instrument, select a linked term, and return to the source. The app must prove the same journey in the real app, on the real origin, with the real bridge, under the conditions phones add. FrankenPatents' UI tests also produced its App Store screenshots from real records, which kept store art honest; this bead does the same.

## Scope

In scope: XCUITest journeys per paper, driven by the website's journey contracts; lanes; screenshot production; evidence retention through the harness.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the harness (`am-app-test-harness-da6e`); edition parity in WebKit (`am-app-edition-parity-bwa5`); performance (`am-app-perf-budgets-q2ku`); sessions with people (`am-app-at-sessions-n6vj`).

## Requirements

1. **Journeys from contracts.** Read the website's journey contract data (anchors, faces, foundation, instrument, typed value, term, return target) and execute the same steps in the app, starting with the Brownian slice and adding each paper when its web journey exists.
2. **Steps.** Enter through a universal link (or the DEBUG `-AMOpenURL` lane) to a deep source passage; switch face; open a foundation; return to the exact argument; operate an instrument with typed numeric entry; confirm the execution label matches the accepted snapshot reported through `test.log`; select a linked term; return to the source; share the passage and reopen it.
3. **Lanes.** Default iPhone; `offline` (network disabled for the app, all steps pass except facsimile downloads, which show their honest state); `relaunch` (terminate and relaunch mid-journey, resume at the anchor); `ipad` (split view); `largest-text` (largest accessibility size); `voiceover-identifiers` (every step reachable by accessibility identifiers); `no-wasm` (the edition's WebAssembly capability disabled through a DEBUG test flag, so instruments show host calculation or unavailable labels, never the FrankenSim label).
4. **Screenshots.** A screenshot lane captures store images from real content at the device sizes App Store Connect requires at submission time, in the Annalen theme, with honest in-preparation states for the profile being submitted; orientation is verified.
5. **Evidence.** Failures retain the `.xcresult`, screenshots, console events, DOM snapshot, and log excerpt through the harness.

## Technical Approach

A journey runner in the UI test target reads contract JSON bundled with the test fixtures, performs steps through accessibility identifiers and the edition's readiness signals, and records each step through `AMTestLog`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Brownian slice journey passes in every lane on the named simulators.
- [ ] Each later paper's journey passes when its web journey exists, with no journey code copied per paper.
- [ ] In the `no-wasm` lane, no step shows the FrankenSim label.
- [ ] Screenshots are produced from real content for the submission profile, with verified orientation.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `JourneyContractTests`: contract parsing and step planning against the web contract fixtures.

### End-to-end tests
- `PaperJourneyUITests` with one test per paper and lane parameterization.
- `StoreScreenshotUITests`.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/app-journeys/<logRunId>.jsonl` with the full shared field set, including `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, run identities, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `lane`, `device`, and `outcome` per step.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Airplane mode cannot be toggled from XCUITest on the simulator; the `offline` lane uses a DEBUG network-denial flag in the app plus a host-level check that no request left the app.
- Readiness comes from edition signals, never sleeps.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-test-harness-da6e`, `am-app-navigation-shell-61d9`, `am-app-universal-links-re8v`, `am-app-lifecycle-resilience-4dhu`, `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`, `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`.

Unblocks: `am-app-at-sessions-n6vj`, `am-app-perf-budgets-q2ku`, `am-app-slice-exit-nzvs`, `am-app-store-listing-ovhw`.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Blocked, named (GreenOx, 2026-09-24): requirement 1 says to read the website's journey contract data and execute it in the app, with no journey code copied per paper. No such data exists. am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu (the web Brownian journey) is open. The one journey in the repository is a shape fixture in scripts/e2e/paper-e2e-contract.test.ts, with selectors such as [data-foundation-open="true"] and [data-instrument-status="accepted"] that no one has checked against the built pages. Writing the app journey now would mean authoring the web contract here, or copying steps per paper; both are what the bead forbids. The pieces that exist to build on: LifecycleUITests (relaunch and web-process recovery), UniversalLinkUITests (-AMOpenSiteURL entry to a deep passage), DynamicTypeUITests and AccessibilityUITests (the largest-text lane), and ContentsUITests (native navigation to a section, a route and an instrument). Taking am-app-test-harness-da6e first, which this bead is also blocked by.

title: Bundle the verified edition into the app with a size budget and no unlisted files
description:
# Bundle the verified edition into the app with a size budget and no unlisted files

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** App plan §2.4, §5.3, §5.4 (traceability only)

## Background

FrankenPatents copied its assets with a post-build `rsync` of every non-PDF file under `public/patents` (about 306 MB) with no budget, and had to learn to clear extended attributes on the whole app wrapper. Annus Mirabilis ships exactly what the edition manifest lists, verifies it at build time, and enforces a size budget, so the bundle can neither drift nor bloat silently.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/app/bundle-edition.ts`; the Xcode build phase that calls it; freshness rules for Debug and Release; the size budget; the `apple-edition-fresh` gate step; tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: producing the edition (`am-app-edition-export-kwpu`); serving it (`am-app-scheme-handler-ghuu`); facsimile downloads (`am-app-facsimile-downloads-72nz`).

## Requirements

1. **Copy exactly the manifest.** Copy every listed file into the app's resources under `Edition/` and nothing else; verify each copied file's SHA-256; fail on a missing, extra, or mismatched file.
2. **Freshness.** Release builds refuse an edition whose `siteCommit` is not `HEAD` or whose profile differs from the build's configured profile, printing the export command to run. Debug builds may use a stale edition only with a visible in-app banner, "Development edition from <commit>", shown by the shell.
3. **Build phase.** A run-script phase in `ios/project.yml` with declared input files (the edition manifest) and output files (a stamp file), compatible with user script sandboxing; it locates Bun through the toolchain decision's recorded path and fails with a clear message when Bun is missing.
4. **Budget.** The app bundle's edition directory must not exceed the recorded budget (provisional 80 MB); the archive step in `am-app-verified-release-1jbu` also checks the App Store download size (provisional 150 MB). Over budget prints the 20 largest files.
5. **Hygiene.** Clear extended attributes on the app wrapper after copying; set no executable bits on edition files.
6. **Gate step.** Register `apple-edition-fresh` in the `apple` family: it verifies the bundled edition's manifest against `HEAD` and the configured profile without building.

## Technical Approach

Keep manifest verification and budget computation as pure functions over the manifest and file listings, tested with fixtures; the build phase calls the CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Release simulator build bundles exactly the manifest's files with verified hashes.
- [ ] A seeded extra file, a seeded modified file, and a seeded missing file each fail the build with the file named.
- [ ] A Release build with a stale edition fails; a Debug build succeeds and the banner is visible.
- [ ] Over budget fails with the largest-files report.
- [ ] Incremental builds skip the copy when the manifest is unchanged.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/app/bundle-edition.test.ts`: plan and verify against fixture manifests (clean, extra, missing, modified, over budget).
- `EditionBundleTests` (Swift): the bundled manifest decodes, and every listed file exists in the built app's resources.

### End-to-end tests
- `DevelopmentEditionUITests.testStaleEditionBannerInDebug`.

### Structured logging
- The script logs file counts, bytes, budget, freshness verdict, and outcome to `artifacts/test-logs/app-edition-bundling/<logRunId>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Xcode build phases run with a minimal `PATH`; resolve tools explicitly.
- Do not use folder references that silently include new files; copying from the manifest is the point.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-xcodegen-scaffold-z228`, `am-app-edition-export-kwpu`.

Unblocks: `am-app-scheme-handler-ghuu`, `am-app-verified-release-1jbu`.

title: Export the app edition from the same commit and release profile as the web build, with an edition manifest
description:
# Export the app edition from the same commit and release profile as the web build, with an edition manifest

**Epic:** `am-ep-app-m247` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** App plan §2.3, §3.3, §5.1, §5.2, §5.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor app's worst failures were drift: its committed native catalogue fell out of step with the website again and again, and nothing bound a native build to a web release. Annus Mirabilis avoids that by construction. The app does not own a copy of the content; it bundles the edition the website build produces, from the same commit, content, and release profile, identified by the release manifest's `releaseId` and `determinismDigest` (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`).

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/app/export-edition.ts`; the edition manifest schema and writer; route enumeration; declared exclusions; size accounting; determinism; tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: copying into the app bundle (`am-app-edition-bundling-xzm1`); serving files (`am-app-scheme-handler-ghuu`); native payload snapshots (`am-app-native-payloads-bued`); proving parity with a deployed web release (`am-app-edition-parity-bwa5`).

## Requirements

1. **CLI:** `bun scripts/app/export-edition.ts --profile <scaffold|preview|launch> [--out generated/app-edition] [--corpus <dir>]`.
2. **Same build:** run (or reuse, when fresh for `HEAD` and the profile) the website build with `AM_RELEASE_PROFILE` set, using the build mode the WebKit probe's decision selected (static export or a crawl of the production build). Refuse when the release manifest's `site.commit` is not `HEAD`, the tree is dirty in a Release export, or the profile differs.
3. **Routes:** enumerate every static route from the build's route manifest and the compiler's route index (`generated/content/index.json`); include every file those routes need (HTML, route payloads, scripts, styles, fonts, KaTeX assets, WASM artifacts listed in `public/wasm/manifest.json`, figures, the search index, `release-manifest.json`). Fail with a list when a route needs a server at request time.
4. **Exclusions:** share-card image routes, `robots`, `sitemap`, the offline-chapter export action's endpoint, the clarity-signal endpoint, and source maps, each written to the manifest with its reason. Any other omission fails the export.
5. **No HTML rewriting.** HTML and payload bytes equal the web build's bytes; the bridge's scripts are injected natively at document start, never written into files.
6. **Edition manifest** (`generated/app-edition/edition-manifest.json`, zod schema in `scripts/app/editionManifest.ts`, `schemaVersion` 1): `releaseId`, `profile`, `determinismDigest`, `siteCommit`, `contentSchemaVersion`, `buildMode`, `files[]` (`path`, `sha256`, `size`, `contentType`, `routeClass`), `exclusions[]` (`path` or pattern, `reason`), `headersPolicy` (the security-header rules per route class, generated from the same policy source as the website's headers), `totalBytes`, and `budgetBytes`.
7. **Determinism:** exporting the same commit and profile twice produces byte-identical files and manifests (sorted keys, sorted file lists, no timestamps other than those copied from the release manifest).
8. **Budget:** fail when `totalBytes` exceeds the recorded budget (provisional 80 MB), listing the 20 largest files.
9. **Logs:** JSONL through the shared logger at `artifacts/test-logs/app-edition-export/<logRunId>.jsonl` with route counts, exclusions, bytes, and outcome.

## Technical Approach

Pure functions for route enumeration, file classification, content-type mapping, and manifest construction, fed by parsed build artifacts; a thin CLI for the filesystem. Content types come from one table shared with the scheme handler's test vectors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fixture corpus exports with every route present and the manifest valid.
- [ ] Two exports of the same commit and profile are byte-identical.
- [ ] A seeded server-only route, a seeded unlisted omission, and a seeded commit mismatch each fail with a specific message.
- [ ] Every exclusion carries a reason, and no reader-facing route is excluded.
- [ ] The export fails over budget with the largest-files report.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/app/export-edition.test.ts`: route enumeration from manifest fixtures, content-type table, exclusion rules, determinism of manifest construction, budget failure.
- `scripts/app/editionManifest.test.ts`: schema acceptance and rejection cases.

### End-to-end tests
- Export the fixture corpus from a real build and compare the HTML and payload bytes with the web build output for the same routes.

### Structured logging
- As in Requirement 9.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A static export can name client payload files differently from a server build; the parity bead declares any such difference rather than hiding it.
- WASM files must keep their content-addressed paths so the loader's digest checks still match.
- Never include `.env` files, local-only source pins, or anything under the root `sources/` directory.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-app-webkit-probe-8hj1`, `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`, `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`, `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`.

Unblocks: `am-app-edition-bundling-xzm1`, `am-app-native-payloads-bued`, `am-app-edition-parity-bwa5`.

comments.text:
