title: Findings: editorial notes have two incompatible shapes, and verify-content's misconceptions audit examines nothing
description:
# Findings: editorial notes have two incompatible shapes, and verify-content's misconceptions audit examines nothing

Recorded by NavyKite for TanElk's dispatch 169, as findings with evidence. **No redesign is proposed here.** Both came out of wiring mass-energy's misconceptions and margin notes onto /papers/mass-energy/ (261d17d4, 2c1e027f).

## Finding 1: one record kind, two shapes, and neither side sees the other

**Shape A, the schema.** `EditorialNote` in `src/content/schemas/source.ts:1480`, validated by `validateEditorialNote` (`:1497`):
- `kind` is the note kind: `historian-margin`, `correction`, `typographical`, `dispute` or `side-note`;
- `author` is an authorship entry with an `id`;
- there is no `paper` field.

This shape is what renders. It is used by `src/reader/faces/EditorialNoteMarker.tsx`, the translation, parallel and gloss faces, and the page loader `src/reader/marginRecords.ts`. The six mass-energy notes in `content/editorial-notes/mass-energy/` have this shape.

**Shape B, the checks.** It has `kind: "editorial-note"`, a separate `noteKind`, a `paper` field, and an author with a `name`. It is read by:
- `src/content/checks/structural/structural.ts:498`, affected ids;
- `structural.ts:888`, dangling citations;
- `structural.ts:1396`;
- `src/content/checks/epistemic/run.ts:616`, `:621` (`noteKind === "influence"`) and `:660`.

Their tests author shape B:
- `src/content/checks/structural/structural.test.ts`, "rejects citation pais-1982 referenced by an editorial note but undefined";
- `src/content/checks/epistemic/epistemic.test.ts`, the end-to-end compiler run with `editorial-notes/brownian-motion/ed-note-clean.json`.

**Measured on 2026-09-24.** The probe is `findings-probe.ts` in NavyKite's scratchpad. It ran `compileContent` on the real corpus plus one note with a nonexistent citation `cit-does-not-exist` and a nonexistent affected id `s0-no-such-block`:

| note | validateEditorialNote | compileContent | diagnostics naming the note |
|---|---|---|---|
| shape A (schema) | valid | ok | **none** |
| shape B (checks) | **refused**: `Invalid note kind "editorial-note"` | not ok | `missing-source-block`, `dangling-citation` |

So a note that can render is never checked for dangling citations or unknown blocks. A note the checks can see can never render.

**Why the compilers do not decide it.** While writing 261d17d4 I first validated notes with the schema in both compilers. That turned the two tests above red. So both compilers now admit a note as they find it; the reason is in `src/content/compiler/marginRecords.ts`. The only check a rendered note gets is the page loader's: schema, inline math, and every cited id must exist in `content/bibliography`. That check runs at build and render, not in the content lanes.

## Finding 2: verify-content's misconceptions audit examines nothing

`scripts/verify-content.ts:333-342` calls `auditMisconceptions` with `papers: []` and empty sets for known anchors, instruments, results and sources.

**Measured on 2026-09-24, same probe.** Called exactly that way it returns `{"audit":"audit-misconceptions","ok":true,"errorCount":0,"flagCount":0,"findings":[]}`, while the corpus holds **8** misconception files in `content/misconceptions/mass-energy/`. It passes on an empty population: none of its anchor, instrument, result or source resolution runs on a real record.

**What still covers misconceptions:**
- The five-entry minimum runs in `compileContent`'s epistemic checks (`epistemic/run.ts`, `misconception-minimum`), and `src/content/compiler/marginRecords.compile.test.ts` holds that it fires on one entry and not on five.
- Each record is validated against its schema, with path identity, in both compilers (261d17d4).
- The page loader refuses unregistered instruments.

Nothing checks that a misconception's `anchors` resolve.

This audit belongs to `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`, which is open.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. With `loadReadingFiles()` for the real corpus, add one file `editorial-notes/mass-energy/<id>.json` holding a shape-A note, one whose `kind` is `historian-margin`. Give it `sourceSupport: [{ citationId: "cit-does-not-exist" }]` and `affectedIds: ["s0-no-such-block"]`.
2. Run `compileContent`. It is ok, and no diagnostic names the note.
3. Repeat with the same note in shape B (`kind: "editorial-note"`). The compiler reports `missing-source-block` and `dangling-citation`, and `validateEditorialNote` refuses it with `invalid-kind`.
4. Call `auditMisconceptions` with exactly the input in `scripts/verify-content.ts:333-342`. It returns `ok: true` with 0 findings. Meanwhile `loadReadingFiles()` returns 8 files under `misconceptions/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One editorial-note shape is chosen, by a recorded decision, and both the schema and the structural and epistemic checks read it.
- [ ] A schema-valid note citing a nonexistent source fails the content lane with `dangling-citation`, proven by a test that goes red on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] `verify-content`'s misconceptions audit is fed the real records.
- [ ] It asserts that it examined more than zero.
- [ ] A planted unresolvable anchor makes it fail.

title: License policy version ranges fall back to startsWith, so a bare range '1.1' would admit 1.10 through 1.19
description:
scripts/license-inventory/evaluatePolicy.ts:28 handles '*', an exact match, a caret range and a tilde range, then falls back to:

    return version.startsWith(range);

Prefix matching is not version matching. Measured:

    version 1.10.0  vs range 1.1  -> accepted
    version 2.15.3  vs range 2.1  -> accepted

A policy intending 1.1.x would silently admit the whole 1.10 to 1.19 line. Fail-open on a licence policy gate.

LATENT, NOT LIVE, and I am saying so rather than inflating it: docs/license-policy.yaml contains only '^2.0.0' and '*' today, and both are handled by earlier branches, so nothing currently reaches the fallback. It becomes live the first time someone writes a bare range.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The fallback compares version components, not string prefixes.
2. BOTH HALVES: a bare range '1.1' rejects 1.10.0 and accepts 1.1.4; and the existing '^2.0.0' and '*' entries in docs/license-policy.yaml still evaluate exactly as they do now, so the change refuses nothing the policy currently admits.

## Provenance

Found by pane30 (BrightIsland) completing band B of am-o44v - specifically in the 47 non-literal startsWith/endsWith sites that the first band B pass missed because it examined only .includes().
close_reason: Fixed at 160adba7 by pane28; closed by orchestrator TanElk on re-executed evidence. evaluatePolicy.ts now compares dotted segments: range split on '.', every segment must equal the version's segment at that index, a range with more segments than the version refused outright. Verified by planting the actual historical defect, not a synthetic fixture: restoring 'return version.startsWith(range);' gives scripts/license-inventory.test.ts 33 pass 1 fail, failing test named 'version ranges match by dotted segment, not by characters (am-avyr) > a bare 1.1 rejects 1.10.0 and accepts 1.1.4'. Restored byte-identical to HEAD, 34 pass 0 fail, 192 expect() calls. BOTH HALVES present as the bead required: the fix (1.1 rejects 1.10.0, accepts 1.1.4; 2.1 rejects 2.15.3, accepts 2.1.9) and the control (every range docs/license-policy.yaml actually carries evaluates unchanged - * still admits 1.0.30001/1.10.0/2.15.3/unknown/0.0.0-next, ^2.0.0 still admits 2.0.0/2.0.1/2.13.0/2.15.3 and still refuses 1.9.9/3.0.0). Remains latent not live and the code says so: the policy file has only ^2.0.0 and *, both handled above the fallback.

title: HEAD does not typecheck: a commit imports a file that was never committed
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator TanElk: 90dbf40e tracks pageMapReconciliation.ts; typecheck in a detached worktree at clean HEAD 8c2e4e73 exits 0, was exit 2 with TS2307 at c8250fd5.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
FOUND BY CENTRAL VERIFY (TanElk) at HEAD c8250fd5.

  bun run typecheck -> exit 2
  src/content/editions/editionContract.ts(48,8): error TS2307:
    Cannot find module './pageMapReconciliation.ts' or its corresponding type declarations.

WHAT HAPPENED. Commit 120c67e7 (fix(editions): contract check 4 reconciles the page map instead of reading a flag, am-06x1) added an import of ./pageMapReconciliation.ts to editionContract.ts. src/content/editions/pageMapReconciliation.ts is 147 lines on disk and is in NO commit - git ls-files --error-unmatch returns nothing for it. The importer shipped; the imported file did not.

WHY NOBODY SAW IT, and this is the part that matters. In our working tree the file is present on disk, so tsc resolves it and the repo typechecks clean. Running typecheck in the main tree returns zero matches for this error. The break is only visible in a checkout that lacks untracked files - which is every fresh clone, every CI run, and every worktree. I found it only because I run central verify in a detached worktree at HEAD, and a worktree does not carry untracked files.

That property has cut both ways this session. It costs me false failures when a gitignored generated artifact is missing from the worktree (I had two such this session, keysInjection and runPerfBudgets, both of which pass in the main repo). Here it is the only reason a genuinely broken HEAD was caught at all. The rule that reconciles both: a worktree failure is a CANDIDATE, re-checked in the main repo; a worktree failure that the main repo cannot reproduce because the main repo has an UNTRACKED file is a real break, not a false positive. The discriminator is whether the missing file is gitignored (build artifact, benign) or merely untracked (uncommitted source, broken HEAD).

CROSS-PANE CAUSE. pane30 authored pageMapReconciliation.ts and did not commit it. pane29 committed code importing it. Neither pane could see the problem from its own side: pane30's file works locally, and pane29's import resolves locally. Only a third party looking at committed state can see it.

NOT RH-1 and not dishonesty. It is a coordination gap, and the shared dirty tree is what conceals it.

CHEAP PERMANENT GUARD worth having: a check that every module imported by a tracked source file is itself tracked. That is a pure git + import-graph question, needs no build, and would have failed this commit at authoring time.

Assigned to pane31 to commit the file and verify with a detached worktree at the new HEAD.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
VERIFIED FIXED (TanElk). Closing.

90dbf40e tracks src/content/editions/pageMapReconciliation.ts. Verified the way the break was found, not in our working tree: a detached worktree at HEAD 8c2e4e73, which carries no untracked files, now returns bun run typecheck exit 0. It was exit 2 with TS2307 at c8250fd5.

The discriminator this bead established is the durable part, and it resolves a tension I had been handling by instinct. Verifying in a worktree produces two kinds of failure that look identical and mean opposite things:

  - the missing file is GITIGNORED -> a build artifact absent from the worktree -> false failure, re-check in the main repo. Two this session, keysInjection.integration.test.ts and runPerfBudgets.test.ts, both green in the main repo.
  - the missing file is merely UNTRACKED -> uncommitted source -> HEAD is genuinely broken and the main repo is the thing that is lying.

So "re-check worktree failures in the main repo" is right for the first and exactly wrong for the second. Check git check-ignore before deciding which one you have.

The cheap permanent guard is still unbuilt and still worth building: assert that every module imported by a tracked source file is itself tracked. Pure git plus import-graph, no build required, and it would have failed 120c67e7 at authoring time rather than leaving HEAD broken for roughly thirty minutes. Not filing that as a separate bead here to avoid scope-splitting; it belongs to whoever next touches the boundary gates in scripts/rsc-client-boundary.ts, which already walks imports.

title: Ten scrollable regions are unreachable by keyboard (axe scrollable-region-focusable)

A region with `overflow-x: auto` whose content fits does not violate anything, and adding `tabIndex={0}` to it would add a useless tab stop and make the page worse for keyboard users. ```tsx

  aria-label={`...`}

Green here does not prove the regions are usable, only that they can be focused. Nothing here is evidence about screen-reader announcement order.

title: permalink.fuzz 5ms wall-clock bound fails under parallel load but passes in isolation
description:
src/experiments/permalink/permalink.fuzz.test.ts:85 asserts `duration < 5.0` per fuzz input, where duration is wall-clock `performance.now()` around a decode.

Measured at 52f0b5e:

```
bun test --isolate --timeout 60000 src scripts   -> 6102 pass, 2 fail
   (fail) permalink.fuzz: fixed corpus decodes safely within 5ms per input ...

bun test --isolate --timeout 60000 src/experiments/permalink/permalink.fuzz.test.ts
   run 1: 1 pass 0 fail
   run 2: 1 pass 0 fail
   run 3: 1 pass 0 fail
```

Three isolated runs pass; the same test fails inside the 851-file parallel suite. The decoder did not get slower - the machine got busier. The assertion is measuring contention, not the code under test.

## Why this needs fixing rather than ignoring

1. It will intermittently redden central verify and CI for reasons unrelated to any change, which trains people to re-run until green.
2. It is bait for exactly the wrong repair. The obvious "fix" is to raise 5ms to some larger number until it stops failing, which destroys the bound as a check. Do not do that.
3. The underlying acceptance criterion is legitimate: am-inst-permalink-tape-s677 requires decoder fuzzing to stay within a declared bound. Bounded decode cost is worth guarding - wall-clock in a parallel suite is just the wrong instrument.

## Honest note on prior evidence

I cited this test as evidence for that bead AC9 on 2026-09-17. The isolated run I observed did pass and the bound is genuinely enforced in the code, but I did not then know it is load-sensitive. Treat that citation as evidence of the assertion existing and passing serially, not as evidence of a reliable gate.

## Acceptance

1. The bound is enforced by something that does not depend on machine load. Options to weigh and record: measure against a same-run calibration baseline (time a known fixed workload, express the budget as a ratio), assert on operation or allocation counts rather than milliseconds, or move this one test to a serial lane (bunfig pathIgnorePatterns routes to the node-only runner, which runs serially).
2. Whatever is chosen, a planted negative proves the bound still bites: an artificially slowed or quadratic decode path must fail the test.
3. 20 consecutive full `bun test --isolate src scripts` runs with zero failures from this test. Record the count; do not report "seems stable".
4. The literal 5ms number is not raised to make the failure go away. If the budget genuinely needs to change, state the measurement that justifies the new figure.

## No-claim

Fixing the instrument does not prove the decoder is fast enough for any particular device. Nothing here is a benchmark on real hardware profiles.

## Provenance

Found by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 during central batch verify, by re-running the failing test in isolation instead of accepting the suite result.

Line 141: effectiveBoundMs = NOMINAL_PER_INPUT_BOUND_MS * loadFactor. This is option 1 from the bead - express the budget as a ratio against a known fixed workload - not a raised constant.

AC4, the 5ms literal was NOT raised: line 14 still reads const NOMINAL_PER_INPUT_BOUND_MS = 5.0, carrying the comment 'Must NOT be raised to silence contention failures.' The failure message at line 175 reports the measured duration, the effective bound, the nominal bound AND the loadFactor, so a future reader can tell contention from a real regression.

AC2, planted negative proves the bound still bites: line 199, 'planted negative proves execution bound bites on artificially slowed decode path', deliberately burns CPU for 2.5x the effective bound and asserts durationMs >= effectiveBoundMs with a message naming both figures. A quadratic or heavy decode path fails it. Re-executed: 2 pass, 0 fail.

AC3, twenty consecutive full-suite runs with zero failures from this test: performed, not estimated.
  runs 1-6    fuzz-ok  (6/6)
  runs 7-13   fuzz-ok  (7/7)
  runs 14-20  fuzz-ok  (7/7), and these seven also had suiteFail=0 overall

The bead said 'Record the count; do not report seems stable.' The count is 20 of 20. I reported 6 and then 13 in earlier ticks rather than rounding up, and only claimed 20 once 20 had run.

Prior state for contrast: before this fix the same test failed inside the 851-file parallel suite while passing 3/3 in isolation.

title: Bind every brownian-motion source paragraph to its explanation and every printed display equation to an equation record
description:
## Background

- Plan §3.2: the source manifest determines completeness, and "a block cannot be covered by linking to a whole paper".
- Plan §17.7 item 3: every paragraph is explained, and every displayed equation has an Equation record.
- The mission: a reader moves between the German passage, the translation, the explanation and the instrument for the same place.

## Measured (2026-09-24)

- The explanation layer has 42 argument passages, and 0 paragraph anchors exist on live.
- 0 of the 38 manifest argumentObligations resolve to an argument record.
- 0 of the 200 printed display equations are bound to any of the 106 equation records, which are all modern teaching equations.

Nothing ties the explanation to the text it explains, so no reader can go from a German paragraph to its explanation, and completeness cannot be measured.

## What to do for brownian-motion (177 units in content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/manifest.yaml)

1. Binding records under content/, following the explanation-grain decision (am-decision-explanation-grain-8exq):
   - each source paragraph maps to one or more argument passages;
   - each printed display equation maps to an Equation record (existing or new), or to an explicit declared status such as "printed only, explained in passage X";
   - every argumentObligation in the manifest resolves.
2. Every paragraph gets its own R0 overview, one or two sentences, if the decision chooses (a).
3. The compiler rejects:
   - a paragraph with no binding;
   - a binding to a nonexistent passage;
   - a printed display with neither a record nor a declared status.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The compiler reports "brownian-motion: N of N paragraphs bound, M of M printed displays bound or declared, K of K obligations resolved", with the denominators from the manifest.
- Planted negative: remove one binding; the build fails, naming the paragraph.
- On live, each German-face paragraph of brownian-motion links to its explanation passage (no JS needed), and back.

## Tests and logging

- A compiler test: paragraph, display and obligation coverage for this paper, with denominators.
- Planted missing binding and planted binding to a nonexistent passage, each red.
- Browser (no JS): German-face paragraph to explanation and back, where a German face exists.

Structured logs: each suite writes JSON lines to artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>.jsonl with the AGENTS.md fields that apply (timestamp, suite, logRunId, testId, beadId, paper, anchor, instrumentId, expected, actual, outcome, browser, viewport, jsEnabled, message). A failing browser test keeps a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot and console log.

title: Build BM-01 tracer ensemble and observable selection
description:
# Build BM-01 tracer ensemble and observable selection

**Epic:** `am-ep-brownian-slice-6m2` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Type:** feature · **Plan sections:** §7.6, §8.2, §9.3, §10.1–10.7, §12.4–12.11, §13.3, §13.5, §19.2 (traceability only)

## Background

BM-01 is the opening instrument of the Brownian paper and of the reference slice. It puts the reader in front of a calibrated microscope field of suspended tracers and asks three questions a careful observer should settle before anyone hands over a law:

- Is there a net drift?
- Does a longer observation produce proportionally more displacement?
- Which statistic stays stable when individual paths do not?

The first discovery is that signed displacements average to about zero while their squares reveal a growing spread. The reader chooses an observable before being given $\langle x^2\rangle = 2Dt$.

The same instrument hosts the **velocity trap**, the mistake behind Exner's 1900 measurements. The apparent speed $\lambda_x/\tau$ grows as $\tau^{-1/2}$ when you look more often, so it cannot be a property of the particle.

BM-01 is also the slice's proof of the architecture. One accepted snapshot drives a microscope trace view, a displacement-distribution view, a statistics plot, a table, the linked equations, and an accessibility summary, and no component recomputes physics. A FrankenSim export owns a seeded stochastic experiment honestly. The Batch B exit demonstration uses BM-01 for three of its points: the reader predicts the effect of changing viscosity and then sees the admitted comparison; the trace and the distribution show the same accepted state; the page stays intelligible without the simulation.

Other beads address this instrument by id, so the manifest registers ids rather than describing behavior in prose: the Brownian misconception ledger (`am-bm-misconceptions-2hk1`) cites three presets, the fifteen-minute Brownian tour (`am-tour-15min-brownian-z034`) cites a predict prompt, and the later underdamped deep dive (`am-later-deep-underdamped-ide4`) adds a declared mode. Every one of those ids is registered here.

## Scope

In scope:
- the manifest and owner binding;
- the replay grid, stream allocation, and work budget;
- all views: the microscope trace, the displacement distribution, the log-log statistics plot, the table, and the summary;
- statistics through the ensemble-statistics owner functions, and the velocity-trap mode;
- the Einstein preset and its teaching tape;
- the two registered predict prompts (observation interval and viscosity) with their candidate ids;
- the three registered presets the Brownian misconception ledger cites;
- the action contract and permalink;
- the R0–R3 caption readings of this instrument and its readings-owners file;
- declarations consumed by other beads: weave predicates together with the worker-side band outputs they read, the real-rate declaration, and show-the-code kernel and identifier lists;
- tests.

Out of scope:
- histogram interval probability, radial laws, and FTCS (`am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`);
- step-distribution experiments (`am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`);
- inference of $N$, censoring models, and measurement error (`am-bm-07-infer-molecular-number-frf9`, `am-bm-08-measurement-bias-h1ye`);
- the licensed real observation sequence (`am-later-real-brownian-sequence-o6l3`);
- the true-rate playback toggle itself (`am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez`, which wires BM-01's declaration);
- the show-the-code disclosure and pinned hashes (retrofitted by `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`);
- the `/lab/bm-01` and `/embed/lab/bm-01` pages (`am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`, `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`);
- paragraph readings of §§4–5 (`am-bm-readings-s4-s5-uqbb`) and displayed-equation readings (`am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81`);
- evaluating predicates and lighting sentences, which `am-read-result-weave-jex` does and `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` asserts;
- the normal and chi-square quantile functions themselves (the diffusion owner's statistics submodule; see Ownership);
- the underdamped model, its views, and its fixtures (`am-later-deep-underdamped-ide4`, which declares its own mode in this manifest; see "A later mode arrives in this manifest");
- the misconception ledger's entries and their text (`am-bm-misconceptions-2hk1`, which cites the presets registered here).

## Requirements

### Explanatory question and source links

"When individual tracers wander unpredictably, which statistic of their displacements stays stable and grows lawfully with the observation interval?"

Linked source passages (ids from `am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg`):
- §4: the mean vanishes while the mean square grows;
- §5: $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$, printed as "$\lambda_x = 8\times10^{-5}$ cm = 0,8 Mikron" for 1 s and "ca. 6 Mikron" for 1 min (verify the exact printed forms on the facsimile);
- the introduction: Einstein's stated uncertainty that these motions are the reported Brownian motion.

Argument ids come from `am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81` (Chains A and C).

### Controls

Each control declares dimension, display unit, model domain, numerical domain, visual range, default, mapping, independent or derived status, and command class.

| Control | Unit | Model domain | Teaching range and default | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seed | none (u64 decimal string) | $0$ to $2^{64}-1$ | recorded; "same seed" and "new trial" explicit | setup-change |
| Constant set | none | `einstein-1905-brownian-printed` or `modern-si-2019` | default `einstein-1905-brownian-printed` for the Einstein preset; labeled everywhere | setup-change |
| Temperature $T$ | K | $T > 0$ | 273–330 K; default 290.15 K | setup-change |
| Viscosity $\eta$ | mPa·s (typed Pa·s accepted with explicit conversion) | $\eta > 0$, Newtonian liquid | 0.5–20 mPa·s typed or dragged; default 1.35 (Einstein's printed water value); temperature never silently changes $\eta$ | setup-change |
| Radius $a$ | μm | dilute spheres, $a > 0$ | 0.1–5 μm; default 0.5 | setup-change |
| Ensemble size $M$ | count | integer ≥ 1 | 1–10 000; default 400 | setup-change |
| Time resolution $h$ (settings drawer) | s | $h > 0$ | provisional default 0.02 s | setup-change |
| Recording length $H$ (settings drawer) | s | $H \ge h$, integer multiple of $h$ | provisional default 60 s; up to 600 s within the work budget | setup-change |
| Observation interval $\Delta t$ | s | positive integer multiple of $h$, at most $H$ | 0.02–60 s at the defaults (0.01–600 s with other grids), logarithmic, with steps on the replay grid; default 1 s | measurement-change |
| Statistic | none | signed mean, mean absolute (radius for 2D and 3D), mean square, RMS, apparent speed | default: signed mean and mean square side by side | estimator-change |
| Dimension | none | 1D marginal, 2D projection, 3D (statistics only) | default 1D | measurement-change |

- Typed entry is always available.
- Out-of-domain input is explained with an admissible boundary; it is never silently clamped while the label shows the requested value.
- A gas card is refused with the typed request refusal `stokes-gas-medium` (domain kind `model`, from the shared registry of `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`), built from the owner's `outside-domain` result: Stokes drag without the Cunningham slip correction is invalid when the mean free path is comparable to the radius.
- An observation interval off the grid (for example 0.015 s when $h = 0.02$ s) is refused with the typed request refusal `off-replay-grid` (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`). Its ranked repairs list the nearest admissible intervals and offer a grid change (a new run), and the last accepted snapshot is kept. The path is never silently resampled.

### Replay grid, latent streams, and work budget

- **One declared replay grid per run.** Positions exist at times $k h$ for $0 \le k \le H/h$. Observation cadence, plots, and the selected $\Delta t$ subsample this fixed path and consume no draws (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`).
- **Three-axis latent path.** Every tracer has independent $x$, $y$, and $z$ coordinates, so changing Dimension is a measurement change that never consumes new draws. The owner call uses `brownian_frames` with kernel 3 (Gaussian with the exact $D$) on $3M$ series with the documented allocation `bm-01.latent.v1`, `tile = 3·i + axis`: tracer $i$, axis 0 for $x$, 1 for $y$, 2 for $z$. This allocation is registered in `docs/STREAM_ALLOCATION.md` and `src/experiments/streams/allocation.ts` by `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`. The export's prefix stability then preserves tracer identities when $M$ grows.
- **Chunked accumulation.**
  - The worker generates tracers in bounded chunks and yields between them.
  - For every chunk it accumulates the sums needed at the declared plot intervals (the 1-2-5 sequence of grid multiples up to $H$) and at the selected $\Delta t$, plus histogram counts at the selected $\Delta t$.
  - It retains full trajectories only for the drawn microscope subset: at most 200 tracers, $x$ and $y$, at a display cadence of 25 samples per simulated second, which is every second grid point at the defaults.
  - Large buffers never enter React state.
- **Work budget.** Each request declares its work in deterministic units: $3M(H/h)$ Gaussian steps plus retained bytes. Provisional per-run limits are $2\times10^{7}$ steps on the desktop tier and $5\times10^{6}$ on the mobile tier, with 8 MiB retained. The defaults ($M = 400$, $h = 0.02$ s, $H = 60$ s) use $3.6\times10^{6}$ steps and about 4.8 MB. Final limits come from `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` measurements and are recorded in the manifest.
- **Over-budget requests.** Exceeding the budget produces the typed execution outcome `budget-exhausted` with repairs (fewer tracers, a shorter recording, a coarser grid). It is never a physical refusal and never a silently reduced ensemble.

### Derived outputs (typed statuses)

**Model values:**
- $D = k_BT/(6\pi\eta a)$ in μm²/s (`value`), with the historical form $\frac{RT}{N}\frac{1}{6\pi kP}$ under the historical constant set.
- $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2D\Delta t}$ and the total second moment $2dD\Delta t$ for $d$ coordinates (`value`).
- The model $\lambda_x$ at the two printed intervals, 1 s and 60 s, for the accepted $D$ (`value`; two outputs bound to `rmsDisplacement1d`, computed by `rmsDisplacement` whatever $\Delta t$ and $H$ are). `bm01-s5-printed-numbers` reads them.

**Sample statistics of the ensemble at $\Delta t$:**
- the signed mean per axis (`value`), shown with its sampling band $\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{2D\Delta t/M}$;
- the mean square per axis and the total, beside the model $2dD\Delta t$ (`value`), each axis shown with its sampling band $\left[2D\Delta t\,\chi^2_{M,\alpha/2}/M,\ 2D\Delta t\,\chi^2_{M,1-\alpha/2}/M\right]$;
- the RMS (`value`);
- for $d = 1$, the mean absolute displacement beside $\sqrt{4D\Delta t/\pi}$; for $d = 2$ and $d = 3$, the mean radius beside $\sqrt{\pi D\Delta t}$ and $4\sqrt{D\Delta t/\pi}$ (`value`);
- the Kolmogorov distance between the selected axis's sampled displacements and the model Gaussian $\mathcal N(0, 2D\Delta t)$ (`value`), which `bm01-s5-distribution-agreement` reads.

**Sampling bands published for the weave.** For every measured axis and for $\alpha = 10^{-3}$ and $\alpha = 10^{-4}$, the worker publishes the signed-mean band and the mean-square band above as outputs (`value`), so the weave's `owner-band` conditions read bounds rather than compute them. Two-sided normal quantiles are $z = 3.290527$ ($\alpha = 10^{-3}$) and $3.890592$ ($10^{-4}$). The bands come from the model variance $2D\Delta t$, never from the sample, and the table labels them "sampling band under the model," never as an uncertainty of the model itself.

**Apparent speed:** $\lambda_x/\Delta t$, labeled "apparent speed over this interval," never "velocity" (`value`), with its $\Delta t^{-1/2}$ scaling shown on log-log axes.

**Displacement distribution at $\Delta t$ for the selected axis:**
- histogram counts in 40 bins of width $\lambda_x/4$ centered on 0, plus two overflow counts, so the counts always total $M$;
- the model's bin probabilities over the same edges, from `intervalProbability`, and density values from `gaussianPropagator`.

**The census** (tracers inside and outside the microscope viewport) is a presentation count computed by the view kit's trajectory layer. Both groups remain in the ensemble.

**Non-numeric and special states:**
- At elapsed time 0 the spread is an `analytic-limit` point distribution.
- With $M = 1$ the statistics are one realization, labeled as such.
- A workload over budget is an execution outcome, never a physical refusal.

### Ownership and execution labels

- **Trajectories:** the FrankenSim `brownian_frames` export (kernel 3) in the slim artifact, running in the dedicated worker. The TypeScript fallback is `brownianFrames` in `src/physics/reference/diffusion.ts` on the Philox port.
- **Closed-form model values:** `stokesEinsteinD`, `rmsDisplacement`, `apparentSpeed`, `intervalProbability`, and `gaussianPropagator` in `diffusion.ts`, with the constant set passed explicitly.
- **Sample statistics** are host reductions of the accepted positions by the ensemble-statistics functions in `diffusion.ts`: `ensembleMoments` and `displacementHistogram`, plus `kolmogorovDistanceToGaussian` for the weave predicate. `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` owns them. They run in the worker, never in a component.

BM-01 never implements a quantile, and the weave never computes one. If the owner does not yet list `ensembleMomentBands` or the quantile functions when this bead is built, they are added there with the fixtures below before the manifest declares `bm01-s4-cancellation`, and the addition is recorded with `br comments add am-ref-diffusion-lr3`.

  - Positions produced by the fallback show "Ideal model, host calculation" (`data-execution-label="host"`), even if the WASM module is loaded.
- A running experiment never switches engines without a new identified run.
- Demonstration trajectories are labeled synthetic in the microscope caption and in the model note.

### Model assumptions and domain

- Dilute, approximately spherical tracers in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid; low Reynolds number; free, unbounded, isotropic diffusion without drift; independent tracers.
- Observation intervals long compared with the momentum relaxation time $m/(6\pi\eta a)$, about $1.1\times10^{-7}$ s for a 1 μm-diameter sphere of density 2000 kg/m³ in water of viscosity 1.0 mPa·s.
- Without fluid, particle, and time-scale data, the instrument says the regime is **assumed**, not checked.

### Views (SVG and Canvas; no Three.js)

- **Microscope trace view (Canvas).**
  - A calibrated scale bar (1 μm) and the drawn subset's $x$–$y$ paths.
  - Tracers start from a deterministic lattice of initial positions. The lattice is presentation layout, excluded from scientific digests; displacements come from the owner.
  - The boundary is a camera viewport, not a reflecting wall. Paths leaving it stay in the ensemble: never wrapped, reflected, replaced, or dropped, and an off-screen count is shown.
  - Polylines are a rendering convention and never supply an instantaneous velocity.
- **Displacement-distribution view (SVG).** The histogram for the selected axis at $\Delta t$, with the model Gaussian overlay. A toggle switches between bin probability and density, with the bin width and normalization stated. The overlay is a theoretical curve, visually distinct from the sampled bars.
- **Statistics plot (SVG, log-log).** The chosen statistics against $\Delta t$, with model lines: mean square slope 1, RMS slope 1/2, apparent speed slope −1/2.
- **Table and summary.** A table of the same numbers, including each statistic's sampling band, and a plain-language summary.
- **Harness DOM contract.** Every view reads the one accepted snapshot and exposes `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, and `data-snapshot-version`. The instrument root `[data-instrument-id="bm-01"]` carries the full contract of `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, `data-snapshot-version`, `data-input-revision`, `data-accepted-input-revision`, `data-pending`, and `data-execution-label`; the primary result (the tracer positions) carries `data-result-status`; a refusal message carries `data-refusal-code`.
- No 3D scene. The 3D option changes statistics only.

### Rendering must not change the experiment

- Render cadence, zoom, and the number of particles drawn never change the ensemble behind the statistics.
- Observation cadence subsamples one fixed logical path and never consumes different random draws.
- A mobile tier may draw fewer particles; it never computes statistics from fewer.

### Action contract (probability and diffusion family)

The manifest's action contract uses the `probability-diffusion` family. Nonvisual users can do everything the visual interface allows:
- choose a statistic from a list and type an interval, then read the table;
- compare two named intervals ("1 s" and "4 s");
- run the viscosity comparison (type a viscosity, read $D$ and the RMS before and after);
- read the census and the summary.

Screen-reader summaries are announced on committed changes, never as a live 60 Hz stream.

### `notModeled`

- molecular collisions (no collision bath owns the displacement);
- the ballistic short-time regime and inertia;
- hydrodynamic interactions;
- walls and near-wall corrections;
- sedimentation;
- non-Newtonian or active fluids;
- rotation;
- polydispersity;
- a temperature law for viscosity;
- localization error and motion blur (BM-08);
- gas-phase slip.

  - **`bm-01-predict-observation-interval`** (control: the observation interval $\Delta t$). "If you watch four times as long, the typical distance from the start becomes 4 times as large, 2 times as large, or unchanged?" The candidates are curves of slope 1, 1/2, and 0 on empty log-log axes; sketching is the alternative.
    - `bm-01-predict-observation-interval-four-times`, "four times as large": distance grows in proportion to time (slope 1);
    - `bm-01-predict-observation-interval-twice`, "two times as large": distance grows as the square root of time (slope 1/2; the model's answer);
    - `bm-01-predict-observation-interval-unchanged`, "it stays the same": the typical distance is a property of the particle, not of the watching time (slope 0).

  - `bm01-s5-printed-numbers` lights for the Einstein preset and stays unlit under `modern-si-2019` and under `scenario-modern-water-17c` ($\lambda_x(1\text{ s}) = 0.8871979$ μm).
- **Stream allocation:**
  - regenerating tracer 17's three axes alone reproduces the ensemble's values bitwise;
  - tracer identities match between $M = 18$ and $M = 400$;
  - changing $\Delta t$, the statistic, or the dimension leaves positions bitwise identical, with the latent digest and draw counter unchanged;
  - the seed `9007199254740993` survives a URL round trip;
  - the manifest's allocation id is `bm-01.latent.v1` and matches the registry entry.
- **Common random numbers:** same seed with $\eta$ going from 1.35 to 2.70 mPa·s scales every position by $1/\sqrt2$ within $\max(10^{-12}\,\mu\text{m},\ 10^{-10}|x|)$; a new seed does not.
- **Replay grid:** $\Delta t = 0.015$ s on $h = 0.02$ s is refused with `off-replay-grid`, whose ranked repairs list 0.02 s and a grid change; $\Delta t = 0.04$ s is accepted with zero new draws.
- **Budget:** $M = 10\,000$ with $h = 0.02$ s and $H = 60$ s ($9\times10^{7}$ steps) returns `budget-exhausted` with the three repairs, the request echo keeps $M = 10\,000$, and no partial snapshot is published as complete.
- **Labels:** WASM positions with host statistics show the FrankenSim label and a model note that lists the host reductions; fallback positions with WASM loaded show host calculation.
- **WASM versus fallback on one seed:** integer Philox output bitwise equal; positions within the tolerance recorded by `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`; the comparison kind is logged.
- **Status cases:** elapsed time 0 gives `analytic-limit`; $M = 1$ is labeled a single realization; the gas card is refused with `stokes-gas-medium` and the Cunningham explanation.
- **Constant-set labels:** the Einstein preset's displays name `einstein-1905-brownian-printed`; a display of "6.1 μm" under that set fails; a caption or model-note fixture calling $R$ "printed" fails the claims check.
- **Captions:** `audit-readings.ts` over BM-01's caption ids finds all four readings with contract fields, and a fixture caption target missing from the readings-owners file reports `owner-unassigned`.
- **Guard:** the view-import guard fails if any BM-01 view module imports `diffusion.ts` or computes a statistic.

### End-to-end tests

BM-01's own lanes run on the §5 passage's companion and on the harness fixture host page; the `/lab/bm-01` lanes belong to `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`.
- Predict with the interval prompt, then change $\Delta t$ from 1 s to 4 s by typed entry and read the table. The model RMS doubles and the overlay shows prediction and result; the recorded `prediction` tape event carries `bm-01-predict-observation-interval` and the chosen `candidateId`.
- Predict with the viscosity prompt, type 2.70 mPa·s, and confirm $D$ halves and the model note shows the common-random-numbers statement.
- Load each of the three registered presets by id and confirm its displayed pair: `bm-01-velocity-trap` (1.589567 μm/s at 0.25 s against 0.7947833 μm/s at 1 s), `bm-01-radius-probe` and `bm-01-viscosity-comparison` (both 0.5619966 μm at 1 s).
- Toggle the velocity trap and confirm the −1/2 slope label and that the apparent speed at 0.25 s is twice that at 1 s.
- Type an off-grid interval and confirm `data-refusal-code="off-replay-grid"`, the repair list, and an unchanged `data-snapshot-version`.
- Enable reduced motion and confirm the walk pauses with statistics visible.
- Block WASM and confirm `data-execution-label="host"` and statistics equal within tolerance.
- Reload a permalink and confirm identical snapshot identities.
- Drive tracers out of the viewport and confirm the census total stays $M$ and the statistics are unchanged.
- Run at 320 px and keyboard-only. With JavaScript disabled, confirm the static worked example with the printed numbers, their constant set, and the synthetic label.

### Structured logging

- JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/bm-01/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`. Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId: bm-01`, `scenarioId`, `presetId`, `modeId`, `tapeId`, `promptId`, `candidateId`, `predictionForm`, `constantSetId`, `instanceId`, `runId` (the experiment realization), `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `seed` (decimal string), `streamVersion`, `allocationId`, `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `refusalCode`, `statistic`, `M`, `gridStep`, `recordingLength`, `workUnits`, `predicateId`, `axis`, `boundFamily`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `alpha`, `lowerBound`, `upperBound`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `message`.
- Failures retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console log, and the snapshot JSON.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never estimate a "Brownian speed" from a fine polyline, and never use one to gate Stokes drag.
- Demonstration trajectories are synthetic and labeled so until a licensed real sequence exists.
- The plan's fixture table lists 6.1 μm at 60 s. That is the modern-$k_B$ value (6.146687 μm) at two figures; the constants Einstein used give 6.156365 μm, which is 6.2 μm at two figures. Declare the constant set in every scenario and tape, and label every displayed number with its set.
- $R$ is an editorial input in this fixture: paper 2 §5 appears not to print it, and paper 1 §2 appears not to print it either. The scenario declares it rather than presenting it as a transcription, and no text calls it printed in either paper unless a facsimile shows it.
- The weave's bands come from the model variance, not from the sample. An ensemble whose statistics wander from the model leaves the sentence unlit; it never lights a sentence against its own data.
- Equal seeds do not give pathwise-consistent paths across different grids; a grid change is a new run.
- Doubling $\eta$ and doubling $a$ give identical displacements because $D \propto 1/(\eta a)$; say so rather than presenting them as independent evidence. That is why `bm-01-radius-probe` and `bm-01-viscosity-comparison` display the same number, and the ledger entries that cite them say which claim each one settles.
- An off-grid interval cannot be evaluated on the recorded path, so it is a request refusal that keeps the last accepted state, not an output status on a new snapshot.
- An id is a contract with another bead: the tour resolves a prompt id, the ledger resolves a preset id, and the deep dive declares a mode id. Renaming one here without changing the citing bead breaks a build, so a rename goes through both beads in one change.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`: Stokes–Einstein, moments, the ensemble-statistics functions, the sampling bands, and the host fallback.
- `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`: the pinned `brownian_frames` export.
- `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`: the viewport, histogram, log-log plot, and table primitives.
- `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`: schema-generated controls and domain explanations.
- `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`: labels earned per accepted snapshot.
- `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`: worker stepping, chunking, coalescing, and stale rejection.
- `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`: three-layer descriptions and the live-region policy.
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`: the "Einstein's 0.8 micron" teaching tape.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: per-control predict prompts, their id grammar, and the prediction tape events.
- `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`: the shared action-contract framework.
- `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: bounded `?tape=` permalinks.
- `am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg`: the source-passage ids this manifest links and the sentence ids its weave predicates target.
- `am-read-result-weave-jex`: the weave data contract and compiler pass that the manifest's `weavePredicates[]` must validate against.
- `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`: `audit-readings.ts` and `audit-misconceptions`, which the acceptance criteria and the manifest-registration test run over this instrument's caption ids and preset ids.

The stream allocation registry (`am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`), command classes, the refusal registry, the constant sets, and the quantity registry arrive transitively.

Unblocks: `am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias`, `am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`, `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`, `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv` (retrofit), `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3` (lab lanes), `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez` (true-rate wiring), `am-ver-adversarial-audit-1ef` and `am-ver-fixture-table-audit-nh5` (browser checks), `am-tour-15min-brownian-z034`, `am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i`, `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu`, `am-later-real-brownian-sequence-o6l3`.

`am-bm-misconceptions-2hk1` cites the three preset ids registered here, and `am-later-deep-underdamped-ide4` declares `bm-01:underdamped` in this manifest. Neither has a direct edge to this bead, and neither needs one: both already depend on it transitively, the ledger through `am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp` and the slice retrospective and exit demonstration, the deep dive through `am-dod-brownian-2k4y` and `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`. title: Build BM-02 osmotic partition
description:
# Build BM-02 osmotic partition

**Epic:** `am-ep-brownian-complete-6xe` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Type:** feature · **Plan sections:** §3.4 §1, §5.4, §8.2 Route A, §9.3, §10.2, §10.3, §13.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Einstein's §1 makes a daring equivalence. A visible particle suspended in water should exert an osmotic pressure by the same law as a dissolved molecule, because van 't Hoff's law has no term that knows how big the molecule is.

§1 also states the rival fairly. In classical thermodynamics, the free energy of a system with suspended bodies appears to depend only on total masses and qualities, pressure, and temperature, not on where the partition and the bodies sit. So no force on the partition would be expected. Einstein sets gravity aside, and he sets aside the energy and entropy of the interfaces (capillary forces) on the assumption that the contact surfaces do not change. On the molecular-kinetic view, a dissolved molecule differs from a suspended body only in size, and there is no reason a number of suspended bodies should not produce the same osmotic pressure as the same number of dissolved molecules.

Physicians learn osmotic pressure in medical school; almost no one is shown that the same law applies to a micron-sized sphere. BM-02 lets the reader do three things:

- hold number density fixed while changing particle size, and see that the ideal dilute pressure does not change;
- connect the number-density pressure to its mechanical meaning as a force per area on a partition;
- compare the molecular-kinetic expectation with the classical one without pretending this instrument decides between them.

A visible suspension pushes with micropascals, while a centimolar sugar solution pushes with tens of kilopascals, under the same law. That contrast teaches that the count per volume matters and the size does not. BM-02 opens Route A in Journey II.

## Scope

**In scope:**

- The full instrument contract for the osmotic partition.
- The owner functions for force, head, volume fraction, the dilute-domain check, and the classical-expectation model (added to the diffusion owner if absent).
- The labeled comparison of the two models.
- The scenario files.
- The caption R0–R3 readings, owned here under the readings ownership ruling, and this bead's readings-owners file.

**Out of scope:**

- The osmotic pressure law itself (`osmoticPressure` in `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`).
- The volume-factor derivation (`am-bm-03-configuration-integral-e84v`).
- Drag and the force balance (`am-bm-04-drift-diffusion-balance-fpow`).
- The equation records and their readings (`am-bm-equations-s1-s3-u6j7`).
- The paragraph readings that reference this caption (`am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp`).

## Requirements

### Explanatory question and source links

"Why should visible suspended particles obey the same osmotic law as dissolved molecules, and what would classical thermodynamics have expected instead?"

Linked to:

- §1: $pV^* = RTz$ for a dissolved substance, the classical expectation, the molecular-kinetic view, and $p = \frac{RT}{N}\nu$;
- the introduction's conditional claim and decisive-test statement;
- the §1 law record and Chain E in `am-bm-equations-s1-s3-u6j7`.

### Controls

Every control declares dimension, display unit, model domain, numerical domain, default, mapping, and whether it is independent or derived.

| Control | Unit | Model domain | Teaching range, default | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Particle count $N_p$ | count | integer ≥ 0 | 0–100 000 typed; slider 0–20 000; default 1 000 | setup-change |
| Accessible volume $V$ | μm³ | $> 0$ | $10^3$–$10^9$, logarithmic; default $10^6$ | setup-change |
| Temperature $T$ | K | $> 0$ | 273–330; default 293.15 | setup-change |
| Particle radius $a$ | nm to μm | $> 0$ | 0.5 nm (a sugar-sized molecule) to 5 μm; default 500 nm | setup-change (shown to have no effect inside the dilute domain) |
| Partition area $A$ | μm² | $> 0$ | typed; default $10^4$ | measurement-change (the area of the same partition over which the force gauge integrates; the suspension is unchanged) |
| Model | none | molecular-kinetic (Einstein §§1–2); classical-thermodynamics expectation for suspended bodies (as §1 characterizes it) | default molecular-kinetic | setup-change (a different governing model) |
| Constant set | none | modern exact SI (`modern-si-2019`); historical 1905: $N = 6\times10^{23}$ as printed in §5 (`einstein-1905-brownian-printed`) with $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, an editorial input, since paper 2 does not print $R$ and paper 1 §2 appears not to print it either | default modern, labeled everywhere | setup-change |

**Declared constants:**

- Solvent density $\rho = 998$ kg/m³ (water near 20 °C), used only for the head readout.
- Standard gravity $g = 9.80665$ m/s² (defined).

Both are shown in the model note with provenance.

**Input rules:**

- Out-of-domain input is never clamped while the label shows the requested value. It is explained with the admissible boundary.
- A non-integer particle count is refused, with the nearest admissible integers offered.

### Derived outputs (typed statuses)

- **Number density** $n = N_p/V$ (`value`). A symbol card distinguishes $n$ (printed $\nu$) from the total count $N_p$ (printed $n$ in §2, to be verified) and from Avogadro's number $N_A$ (printed $N$).
- **Osmotic pressure** $\Pi = nk_BT$ in Pa, with the historical form $\frac{RT}{N}\nu$ (`value`). In the historical constant set it is computed from $R$ and $N$, never from the modern $k_B$.
- **Mechanical interpretation**, both from the same snapshot (`value`): the force the partition must supply, $F = \Pi A$, and the equivalent head of water $h = \Pi/(\rho g)$.
- **Volume fraction** $\phi = N_p\cdot\frac43\pi a^3/V$ (`value`).
  - The admitted dilute domain is $\phi \le \phi_{\max} = 0.01$. Justification: for hard spheres $\Pi/(nk_BT) = 1 + 4\phi + O(\phi^2)$, so the ideal law is within about 4% at the boundary.
  - Above it, every pressure output is `outside-domain`. The explanation says interactions and excluded volume are not modeled, and the refusal carries the admissible boundary: the largest $N_p$ at the current $V$ and $a$, and the smallest $V$ at the current $N_p$ and $a$.
- **Zero particles.** $N_p = 0$ gives $\Pi = 0$, $F = 0$, $h = 0$ as valid `value`s.
- **Classical-expectation model.** The pressure attributed to suspended bodies is $0$ (`value` within that model). It is labeled "the expectation §1 attributes to classical thermodynamics for suspended bodies."
  - The model note states what decides between the models: Einstein's predicted displacements (§5), and later Perrin's sedimentation equilibrium (1908–1909, dated later evidence).
  - This instrument never labels the classical model refuted.
- **Same law, different count** (a named comparison computed by the same owner). A 0.01 mol/L sugar solution at 293.15 K has $n = 6.022\times10^{24}\,\text{m}^{-3}$ and $\Pi = 2.437\times10^{4}$ Pa. Its head is 2.49 m, and $\phi = 3.15\times10^{-3}$ at $a = 0.5$ nm, inside the dilute domain. The default suspension has $n = 10^{15}\,\text{m}^{-3}$ and $\Pi = 4.05\times10^{-6}$ Pa.

### Assumptions and owner

**Assumptions:**

- an ideal dilute suspension;
- a perfectly selective partition passing solvent but not particles;
- thermal equilibrium;
- no interactions;
- no gravity-driven concentration gradient in this instrument.

**Owner** (host calculation, in `src/physics/reference/diffusion.ts`):

- `osmoticPressure(n, T, set)`, which already exists from `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`.
- Added by this bead if absent:
  - `volumeFraction(Np, a, V)`;
  - `diluteDomainCheck(phi, phiMax)`, which returns the admissible boundary;
  - `partitionForce(Pi, A)`;
  - `hydrostaticHead(Pi, rho, g)`;
  - `osmoticPressureClassicalExpectation()`, which returns the typed zero with its model note.
- The additions are pure, unit-documented, and tested in `diffusion.partition.test.ts`. Record them with `br comments add am-ref-diffusion-lr3`.

A FrankenSim owner is used only if the capability audit assigns one. The execution label follows the accepted snapshot.

### Views and action contract (energy accounting and comparison families)

- **The SVG chamber** is split by a partition. Particle glyphs are drawn at a fixed seeded layout (never `Math.random`), explicitly labeled as an illustration and not a collision simulation.
- **A pressure gauge** and **a table** of $n$, $\Pi$, $F$, $h$, and $\phi$.

**Nonvisual equivalent:**

- Type $N_p$, $V$, $T$, the radius, and the area.
- Read the table.
- Compare three named settings:
  - "same $n$, radius 0.5 nm versus 500 nm";
  - "molecular-kinetic versus classical expectation";
  - "this suspension versus a 0.01 mol/L sugar solution".

Each comparison is read as a two-row table with the changed input named.

### Caption readings (owned here)

The instrument caption has R0–R3 texts owned by this bead under the readings ownership ruling, declared in `content/editorial/readings-owners/am-bm-02-osmotic-partition-n13x.yaml` and added in the same change as the first reading texts. The paragraph readings of `am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp` reference them and never duplicate them, and `audit-readings` reports them against this bead with no `owner-unassigned` or `owner-conflict`.

- **R0:** "Particles you can see push on a partition by the same law as dissolved molecules. What counts is how many there are per volume, not how big they are."
- **R1:** the number-density law, the force and head readouts, the dilute domain, and the classical expectation stated as §1 states it.
- **R2:** each readout in turn ($n = N_p/V$, $\Pi = nk_BT$, $F = \Pi A$, $h = \Pi/(\rho g)$), and why the radius drops out of the pressure inside the dilute domain.
- **R3:** Einstein's §1 contrast with classical thermodynamics, van 't Hoff's law, and Perrin's later sedimentation equilibrium as dated evidence.

### `notModeled`

Particle interactions and excluded volume; non-ideal activity coefficients; imperfect partitions; gravity and sedimentation; electrostatic effects; adsorption at the partition; the kinetics and time needed to reach osmotic equilibrium; molecular collisions with the wall (the drawn glyphs are illustrative).

### Predict mode, probes, tapes, weave, code

- **Predict:** "At the same number of particles per volume, does a 1000-times-larger particle push harder on the partition, the same, or less?"
- **Probes**, each a registered preset of this instrument:
  - the size-independence toggle `bm-02-size-independence` (a sugar-sized molecule versus a 0.5 μm sphere at equal $n$);
  - the model toggle `bm-02-classical-expectation` (molecular-kinetic versus classical expectation);
  - the sugar-solution comparison `bm-02-sugar-0p01M`.
- **Weave:** agreement between the number-density pressure and the force readout lights the §1 law sentence. The target sentence id is marked by `am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp`.
- **Show the code:** the pressure, force, head, volume-fraction, and domain-check functions, with pinned source hashes and colors matching the equation terms. Live terms bind `osmoticPressure`, `numberDensity`, and `temperature`.

### Misconceptions addressed

- "Visible particles cannot exert osmotic pressure."
- Confusing pressure with force.
- Confusing $n$, $N_p$, and $N_A$.
- "A bigger particle pushes harder."

## Technical Approach

- **Manifest.** `content/experiments/bm-02.yaml` declares:
  - every parameter's class and domains;
  - the registered preset ids above;
  - `notModeled`;
  - acceptance cases including refusals;
  - the tape model identity;
  - `embeddable: true`;
  - predict mode.
- **Registry.** An explicit dispatcher case, and an instance-scoped owner.
- **Views.** Controls and views come from the platform frozen by the slice retrospective, using `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r` primitives and `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`.
- **Scenarios** in `content/scenarios/`: `bm-02-golden-default`, `bm-02-molar-agreement`, `bm-02-size-independence`, `bm-02-dilute-boundary`, `bm-02-zero-particles`, `bm-02-sugar-0p01M`, `bm-02-classical-expectation`, `bm-02-historical-constants`.
- **Tolerances** come from `src/units/tolerance.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] $\Pi$, $F$, $h$, and $\phi$ agree from one snapshot, and changing radius at fixed $n$ leaves $\Pi$ unchanged inside the dilute domain.
- [ ] The dilute-domain check refuses above $\phi = 0.01$ with an explanation and the admissible boundary, and never clamps.
- [ ] The classical-expectation model is shown fairly as a labeled alternative, with the observations that decide it, and is never called refuted.
- [ ] The historical constant set never reads the modern $k_B$, and no text calls $R$ a printed value of either 1905 paper.
- [ ] The symbol card for $n$, $N_p$, and $N_A$ is present at every reading.
- [ ] The full instrument contract holds: execution labels, action contract, predict mode, show-the-code, tape, permalink, embed eligibility, 320 px, keyboard, reduced motion, and a JavaScript-disabled worked example.
- [ ] Caption R0–R3 exist, this bead's readings-owners file lists the caption ids, and `audit-readings` passes.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

Real owner functions and the real compiler are used; no mocks.

- **Modern golden default.** $N_p = 1000$, $V = 10^{6}\,\mu\text{m}^3$, $T = 293.15$ K, $A = 10^{4}\,\mu\text{m}^2$ give:
  - $n = 1.0\times10^{15}\,\text{m}^{-3}$;
  - $\Pi = 4.0473725\times10^{-6}$ Pa;
  - $F = 4.0473725\times10^{-14}$ N (40.47 fN);
  - $h = 4.13544\times10^{-10}$ m (0.4135 nm);
  - $\phi = 5.23599\times10^{-4}$.

  Tolerance: $10^{-9}$ relative with exact constants.
- **Molar agreement.** $n = 1.0\times10^{18}\,\text{m}^{-3}$ at 293.15 K gives $\Pi = 4.0473725\times10^{-3}$ Pa, and $\Pi = cRT$ with $c = n/N_A$ agrees within $10^{-12}$ relative.
- **Historical constants.**
  - The same $n = 10^{18}$ gives $4.0601\times10^{-3}$ Pa from $N$ as printed in §5 and $R$ as a declared editorial input, each labeled with that provenance; the two values differ by 0.32%.
  - The constant-set access log shows no read of the modern set.
  - A fixture that reads modern $k_B$ in historical mode fails, and a caption fixture calling $R$ "printed" fails the constant-provenance check.
- **Size independence.** Equal $n$ at radius 0.5 nm and 500 nm gives bitwise-identical $\Pi$.
- **Dilute boundary** at $V = 10^{6}\,\mu\text{m}^3$ and $a = 0.5\,\mu$m:
  - $N_p = 19\,098$ is accepted ($\phi = 0.0099997$);
  - $N_p = 19\,099$ is refused as `outside-domain` ($\phi = 0.0100002$), and the refusal carries boundary $N_p^{\max} = 19\,098$.
- **Zero and invalid inputs.**
  - $N_p = 0$ gives $\Pi = F = h = 0$ as `value`.
  - $V \le 0$, $T \le 0$, $a \le 0$, non-integer $N_p$, `NaN`, and infinite inputs return typed refusals with codes and readable reasons, never zero or a clamp.
- **Sugar comparison.** 0.01 mol/L at 293.15 K gives:
  - $\Pi = 2.43738\times10^{4}$ Pa;
  - $h = 2.4904$ m;
  - $\phi = 3.1532\times10^{-3}$ at $a = 0.5$ nm (accepted).
- **Classical model.**
  - The pressure is 0 as `value` under that model id.
  - Switching model is a setup change with a new `runId`.
  - Switching back restores the molecular-kinetic numbers bitwise.
- **Command classes.** Changing $A$ increments `measurementRevision`, changes $F$ only, and leaves $n$, $\Pi$, and `runId` unchanged.
- **Illustration.** The glyph layout for a given `instanceId` and $N_p$ is identical across renders and consumes no scientific randomness.
- **Adversarial.** A fixture asserting "a larger particle pushes harder at equal $n$" fails because the owner returns identical $\Pi$.
- **Caption readings.** `audit-readings` passes for the caption against this bead's owners file, a fixture removing R2 fails, and a fixture owners file claiming a §1 paragraph id fails with `owner-conflict`.

### End-to-end tests

`e2e/brownian-complete/bm-02.spec.ts`, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:

1. Open `/lab/bm-02` and the §1 passage.
2. Answer the predict prompt.
3. Type the default values and read the table.
4. Run the size-independence probe (`bm-02-size-independence`) and confirm equal $\Pi$.
5. Toggle the classical model and read its label and deciding-evidence note.
6. Type $N_p = 19\,099$ and confirm the refusal with the boundary.
7. Open the sugar comparison.
8. Reload a permalink and confirm identical snapshot identities.

**Lanes:** keyboard only at 320 px; reduced motion (the state is shown without animation); JavaScript disabled (static worked example of the default and the sugar comparison); WebKit.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/bm-02/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, written through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`.

- **Standard fields:** `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId: bm-02`, `instanceId`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `message`.
- **Bead-specific fields:** `Np`, `V`, `T`, `radius`, `area`, `volumeFraction`, `model`, `constantSetId`, `preset`, `Pi`.

Failures retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console log, and the snapshot JSON.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The drawn particles must never be presented as the owner of the pressure.
- For micron-sized particles the pressure is tiny. Say so with the numbers above, and explain why the argument still matters: the same law, applied to countable visible particles, leads to a measurable diffusion.
- Do not caricature the classical expectation; state its reason as §1 does.
- Keep the head readout labeled as an equivalent column of water, not a manometer that exists in the apparatus.

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:**

- `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`: reference evaluator module and constants.
- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: frozen instrument platform.
- `am-bm-equations-s1-s3-u6j7`: the instrument links the §1 law record and Chain E by id, and the compiler rejects dangling ids.
- `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`: the instrument contract requires a show-the-code disclosure pinned to the kernel source.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: the instrument contract requires predict mode or a recorded exemption.
- `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: the instrument contract requires bounded `?tape=` permalinks.

**Unblocks:** `am-bm-e2e-complete-gmdb`, `am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u` (Route A begins here), `am-bm-results-cards-ft8k` (card 1's probe opens `bm-02-size-independence`).
