SEEN, NOT MINE: src/app/homeInvitations.test.tsx fails 2 of 5 with "Offline chapters are stale for the current content or profile. Run prepare:offline". prepare:offline is barred in low-disk mode.

Checks across the three commits: check:types and check:architecture pass. lint-voice (30,676 items) finds 0 findings in the changed files. The refusal ratchets pass (bareThrow 7/7, refusalRatchet 27/27). No CSS changed; the new markup uses existing classes.

title: Build the three themes and self-hosted typography with glyph and contrast tests
description:
# Build the three themes and self-hosted typography with glyph and contrast tests

**Epic:** `am-ep-design-wmj` · **Batch:** batch-a · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §15.3, §15.4, §15.5, §16.2, §16.3, §16.4, §16.5, §4.6 (traceability only)

## Background

The site "should look like an unusually beautiful scientific book that happens to be alive: a bright, warm paper background, dark readable body text, generous margins, fine rules, restrained archival accents, vivid but controlled scientific color."

The type system is specified:
- **one excellent reading serif (Newsreader)**;
- **one compact interface sans (Plus Jakarta Sans)**;
- **JetBrains Mono for telemetry and code**;
- **KaTeX's own fonts for mathematics**.

These fonts are tested against German diacritics, Greek letters, subscripts, primes, old notation, and long equations before committing. They are then **self-hosted and subset without omitting needed mathematical glyphs**.

Three themes switch like the donor's theme toggle. The donor's `src/app/layout.tsx` uses an inline `themeInitScript` that:
1. reads a stored preference inside `try/catch`;
2. falls back to `prefers-color-scheme`;
3. sets a class on `<html>` before paint.

This bead adapts that pattern to three named themes and to the site's rule that dark modes are optional and not the primary identity.

## Scope

In scope:
- design tokens (color, spacing, measures, rules, radii, layout tokens) for three themes;
- the theme pre-paint script and toggle;
- the route-level default theme on `/discover`;
- font selection, subsetting driven by declared and build-emitted glyph manifests, self-hosting, loading strategy, and fallback metrics;
- glyph-coverage and contrast tests;
- font license records;
- this bead's browser checks.

Out of scope:
- the semantic role palette (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`);
- page layout (`am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`, which consumes the layout tokens defined here);
- print styles (`am-plat-print-3orn`);
- reading-only adjustments (`am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`);
- KaTeX rendering and its glyph manifest (`am-eq-static-katex-7da`);
- the storage layer, its namespace registry, and the build step that injects key constants (`am-plat-local-storage-km8f`);
- the Content-Security-Policy (`am-plat-security-f644`).

## Requirements

### Themes

- **Annalen** (default, light): journal cream background; black ink; **red only for emphasis and the move step**; the running-head feel of a 1905 journal page; and the German masthead set to match the facsimile as closely as the fonts allow and no more. The placeholder page served during preparation realized this theme and the owner asked to keep it, so `docs/design/placeholder/` is the reference implementation: paper `#eee7d7`, ink `#1a1916`, muted `#5c554a`, rule `#cbc1ac`, red `#ae2119`, Newsreader with its optical-size axis, small letterspaced uppercase for the running head and locators, and lining tabular figures for locators. Token values may change only with a recorded reason and a rerun of the contrast test.
- **Kramgasse Night** (dark): deep slate with lamplight amber accents.
- **Slate** (chalkboard): for derivation chains and discovery journeys. Role colors appear as chalk tints, the move is boxed in chalk, and instrument canvases are inverted. **Slate is chosen automatically on `/discover` unless the reader has set a theme.**
- **Default and system appearance.**
  - Annalen is the default for every visitor.
  - An optional "follow system appearance" choice maps a dark system preference to Kramgasse Night.
  - An explicit reader choice always wins and persists.
- **Forced colors.** `forced-colors` mode is respected: tokens yield to system colors, and identity cues remain.

### Switching

- **Pre-paint script.** A tiny inline script sets `data-theme` on `<html>` before first paint.
  - It reads the stored theme inside `try/catch` from the single settings string **`am:settings:v1:theme`**, the key this bead owns in the namespace registry of `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`. The key constant is injected by that bead's build step, so the script and the module can never spell it differently, and the script validates the value against the three theme names plus the follow-system choice before using it.
  - It reads the route default from a `data-route-theme` attribute rendered into the page, never by parsing the path.
  - Its hash is recorded in the build's inline-script hash manifest, consumed by `am-plat-security-f644`.
  - It coexists with the view, Detail, Perspective, and reading-only pre-paint scripts; each sets only its own attribute and reads only its own key.
- **Toggle.** The toggle is an accessible radio group, keyboard operable, and announced once on change.

### Contrast

- Every text color pair used in each theme meets WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
- User-interface component boundaries and focus indicators meet 3:1 non-text contrast.
- An automated token test computes ratios for all declared pairs and fails the build on any violation.

### Typography

- **Families.** Newsreader, Plus Jakarta Sans, JetBrains Mono, and KaTeX fonts only. No other web fonts.
- **Baseline subsets for the three text families.** At least:
  - German diacritics: ä ö ü ß Ä Ö Ü, plus ẞ;
  - German quotation marks „ (U+201E), “ (U+201C), ‚ (U+201A), and ‘ (U+2018), plus the other Latin punctuation used in the edition;
  - Greek lowercase and uppercase;
  - the micro sign (U+00B5) and Greek mu (U+03BC) as distinct code points;
  - primes ′ (U+2032) and ″ (U+2033);
  - minus (U+2212), multiplication sign, and middle dot;
  - ≈ ≤ ≥ ∝ √ ∫ ∂ ∞ ⟨ ⟩;
  - superscript and subscript digits used in prose.
- **Glyphs from content.**
  - The subsetting script also adds every code point in visitor-facing text that the compiler emits for a family.
  - When content changes, the build recomputes subsets; it never reuses a stale subset.
- **KaTeX fonts.**
  - They are subset only from the build glyph manifest emitted by `am-eq-static-katex-7da` (code points per KaTeX font face, for every form and color mode and for inline prose math), plus a declared safety set of digits, Latin and Greek letters, and common operators.
  - Until that manifest exists, the KaTeX font files ship whole. They are never subset from a guessed list.
- **Hosting and loading.** Files are self-hosted with explicit `font-display`, only critical subsets are preloaded, and fallback metric overrides (`size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, `descent-override`) keep cumulative layout shift at or below 0.1.
- **Licenses.** Font licenses are recorded in the rights layers and shipped with the files. The three text families use the SIL Open Font License. For KaTeX's fonts, the license text shipped with the pinned KaTeX package is copied verbatim.

### Tokens

- CSS custom properties are defined per theme and consumed by a restrained Tailwind configuration.
- Tokens are exported to TypeScript for SVG, Canvas, and Three.js views.
- Layout tokens (tier thresholds, measures, maximum sticky heights, scroll padding) live here for `am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`.

## Technical Approach

- `src/app/theme/tokens.ts` and `themes.css`.
- `src/app/theme/themeInit.inline.ts`: a pure function, tested directly, and compiled to an inline string with its hash.
- `ThemeToggle.tsx`, adapted from the donor.
- `scripts/subset-fonts.ts` produces subsets from three sources: the declared baseline, the compiler's text glyph list, and the KaTeX glyph manifest when present.
- Fonts and license files live in `public/fonts/`.
- Browser checks run through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` on the harness fixture site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Three themes render the fixture pages. Slate appears by default on `/discover` and yields to an explicit reader choice.
- [ ] No flash of the wrong theme appears on first paint for each theme, verified with client bundles blocked.
- [ ] The contrast token test passes for all pairs and fails on a seeded violation.
- [ ] Glyph-coverage tests confirm that every baseline code point, every compiler-emitted text code point, and every KaTeX manifest code point exists in the shipped subsets. A seeded missing glyph fails.
- [ ] Cumulative layout shift stays at or below 0.1 with cold font caches on fixture pages.
- [ ] Forced-colors mode keeps content legible and interactive states identifiable.
- [ ] The theme script reads `am:settings:v1:theme` through the injected constant, a test asserts that the compiled script and the module use the same string, an invalid stored value falls back to Annalen, and the script's hash appears in the manifest.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `themeInit.test.ts`: stored preference; route default from `data-route-theme`; follow-system option; storage exceptions; an invalid stored value ignored; key constant shared with `src/platform/storage/keys.ts`.
- `contrast.test.ts`: WCAG ratio computation for every declared text and non-text pair per theme.
- `glyphCoverage.test.ts`: parses the shipped font files and asserts the baseline code points. It also asserts the compiler text glyph list and the KaTeX glyph manifest code points, each checked against its face.
- `subsetFonts.integration.test.ts`: whole KaTeX files are kept when no manifest exists; subsets are rebuilt when a manifest code point is added.
- `tokensExport.test.ts`: CSS and TypeScript tokens stay in sync.

### End-to-end tests

`e2e/design/themes.spec.ts` runs through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`. It checks:
- first-paint screenshots per theme, with client bundles blocked;
- the `/discover` default and its override;
- toggling by keyboard;
- cumulative layout shift with cold caches (Chromium);
- forced-colors emulation;
- 320 px;
- high zoom.

Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot, and console log.

### Structured logging

- JSON lines with `theme`, `route`, `source` (`stored`, `routeDefault`, `system`, `default`), `settingsKey`, `firstPaintTheme`, `cls`, `contrastViolations`, `missingGlyphs`, `glyphManifestPresent`, and `outcome`.
- Standard fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `durationMs`, `message`.
- Path: `artifacts/test-logs/design-themes/<log-run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The Annalen look evokes a 1905 journal page; it must not imitate the current publisher's branding.
- Red is reserved for emphasis and the move in Annalen; a negative value is never styled as an error.
- Pages stay light: no hero video and no extra font families.
- Subsetting KaTeX fonts from a guessed list silently drops glyphs that later content needs; subset only from the manifest.
- The micro sign and Greek mu are different code points. Dropping either breaks a displacement caption or an equation, so both stay in the baseline.

## Dependencies

Blocked by (each edge exists in `br dep list`):
- `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`: the application whose layout hosts themes, fonts, and the inline scripts.
- `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`: the namespace registry that owns `am:settings:v1:theme`, and the build step that injects the key constant into this pre-paint script. Both beads are labeled `batch-a`, so this dependency does not push theme work into a later batch.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the browser lanes for this bead's checks.

Unblocks (each is a real dependent):
- `am-a11y-baseline-1cg5`: contrast and focus rules build on these tokens.
- `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`: role colors per theme, and the accent distances they must keep.
- `am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`: measures and layout tokens.
- `am-design-home-page-0s7s`: theme and type for the first screen.
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: Slate on `/discover`.
- `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`: the theme parameter for embeds.
- `am-eq-static-katex-7da`: self-hosted KaTeX fonts and fallback metrics.
- `am-app-design-tokens-3iup` and `am-app-settings-prepaint-tydj` (iPhone app plan, outside this graph's batches): the app generates its tokens and pre-paint settings from these.
close_reason: Completed against the 2026-09-23 rescope. NavyKite's audits are on the bead and were measured on live ccaee3ae and 2316a43b in Chromium and WebKit. 1 two themes and one sun/moon button: met. 2 no first-paint flash with client bundles blocked: met, 30/30 cases. 3 contrast pairs with a seeded violation: met. 4 glyph coverage: met against the shipped whole faces; subsetting was declined in docs/DECISIONS.md D-2026-09-24-fonts-ship-whole (d8ac7c6c), because the subset changes small-size rasterization for an unisolated cause. 5 CLS: max 0.0975 on /notation/. 6 forced colours: met on 2316a43b, 72/72 focus rings. 7 theme key and hash: met. src/app/theme/*.test.ts plus registry.test.ts: 142 pass, 0 fail.

comments.author: BeigeShore
comments.text: Starting work. Owned paths: src/app/theme/**, public/fonts/**, docs/design/placeholder/ (read-only reference), and their tests. Real, self-hosted OFL font files (Newsreader, Plus Jakarta Sans, JetBrains Mono variable TTFs) fetched from the canonical google/fonts repo, with a hand-rolled TrueType cmap parser for real glyph-coverage testing (no new package dependency).

comments.author: BeigeShore
comments.text:
BATCH_PENDING (BeigeShore, commits 75dbe3a [absorbed, see below] and 2d52d70, pushed to main).

YES -- a reader can open ANY page on the site right now and switch between Annalen, Kramgasse Night, and Slate via a toggle in the site header, with no flash of the wrong theme on first paint, and the choice persists in localStorage (am:settings:v1:theme, read from the real storage registry, not a second hardcoded copy).

HEADLINE FINDING -- glyph availability, verified against real font binaries, not guessed: I fetched real, whole (unsubsetted) SIL-OFL-licensed variable TTFs for Newsreader, Plus Jakarta Sans, and JetBrains Mono from the canonical google/fonts repo and wrote a from-scratch TrueType cmap parser (no new package dependency) to check real coverage against this bead's declared baseline. RESULT: Newsreader (the reading serif) and Plus Jakarta Sans (the interface sans) do NOT include the Greek alphabet (upper or lower case) or most of the declared math-symbol baseline as shipped from Google Fonts; Newsreader is additionally missing every subscript digit and superscript 5-9. Greek mu (U+03BC) specifically is missing from both, while the micro sign (U+00B5) is present in both -- exactly the pitfall this bead names by name. JetBrains Mono covers the baseline almost completely (missing only U+221D, "proportional to"). Across all three families together, only U+221D is uncovered baseline-wide. This is disclosed honestly in glyphCoverage.test.ts's real, passing assertions (not a seeded fixture) rather than hidden or worked around by quietly shrinking the baseline. Someone with font-selection authority needs to decide: a different font choice, a Unicode-range fallback face for Greek/math text, or a decision that Greek/math glyphs in prose route through KaTeX and never appear as raw Newsreader/Jakarta text.

Files and tests (runner: bun test):
- src/app/theme/tokens.ts -- three themes' full token sets (Annalen matches docs/design/placeholder/style.css exactly, per the bead's instruction), font-family tokens, layout tokens for am-read-page-anatomy-l0b (values match what src/reader/layout/layout.css already hardcodes, since that bead landed before this one -- noted for a future wiring pass, not fixed here since layout.css isn't mine).
- src/app/theme/contrast.test.ts (15 tests) -- reuses src/a11y/readingSettings/contrast.ts's real contrastRatio/ThemeId, never duplicated; verifies WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 focus-ring) for all three themes plus a seeded-violation proof.
- src/app/theme/fontGlyphs.ts + glyphBaseline.ts + glyphCoverage.test.ts (9 tests) -- the real cmap parser and baseline coverage tests described above.
- src/app/theme/themeInit.inline.ts + themeInit.test.ts (14 tests) -- the pre-paint script (stored preference > follow-system > route default > annalen), reading the real storage-registry key constant; THEME_INIT_SOURCE is the exact injected string, registered in src/app/inline-scripts/registry.ts.
- src/app/theme/ThemeToggle.tsx -- an accessible native radio-group toggle (fieldset/legend/input type=radio, real keyboard operability for free, no ARIA-pattern reimplementation needed).
- src/app/theme/themes.css + tokensExport.test.ts (5 tests) -- CSS custom properties per theme, @font-face for the three self-hosted (whole, not-yet-subset) families, forced-colors handling; tokensExport.test.ts parses the CSS and asserts it matches tokens.ts exactly.
- src/app/layout.tsx, src/app/inline-scripts/registry.ts -- the real wiring: pre-paint script injected, themes.css imported, ThemeToggle rendered in the header, "theme" registered in the inline-script manifest.
- public/fonts/{newsreader,plus-jakarta-sans,jetbrains-mono}/ -- real font binaries + real verbatim OFL.txt license files.

`bun test src/app/theme/` -- 43 pass, 0 fail (re-verified at pushed HEAD 2d52d70).
`bunx tsc --noEmit` on every file this work touches -- 0 errors.
`bunx biome check` -- clean on every touched/added file.
Repo-wide `bunx tsc --noEmit` right now: 3 pre-existing errors, all in src/testing/entrances/brownianNoAlgebraParity.test.ts -- not mine, never touched by me, confirmed via git status showing zero diff on that path before my work started.

TRANSPARENCY -- shared-index absorption, twice, disclosed per this session's standing norm, not hidden: (1) all ten src/app/theme/* files plus the six public/fonts/* files landed inside commit 75dbe3a ("chore(beads): record three orchestrator closes with evidence ledgers") -- a commit message that does not mention this work at all; the content is exactly what I wrote and tested, just credited to an unrelated message. (2) commit 2d52d70 (the layout-wiring commit, whose subject and body ARE accurate to its content) also swept in an 87-line change to src/content/schemas/layerBoundary.test.ts that I did not write and have not reviewed -- I did not intend to stage it, `git diff --cached --name-only` showed only my two files immediately before I ran the commit, and it must have landed via a concurrent write to the shared index between that check and the commit executing. I have not touched or reviewed that file's content.

Honestly NOT done, per this bead's much larger scope:
- Font subsetting (scripts/subset-fonts.ts does not exist; all three families ship whole, which is explicitly allowed for KaTeX by this bead's own text but I am extending the same honesty to the other three rather than fabricating a subset).
- The Greek/math glyph gap above is unresolved, not just undisclosed.
- KaTeX font self-hosting and its glyph manifest (am-eq-static-katex-7da, unbuilt).
- Cumulative-layout-shift measurement, forced-colors and first-paint browser verification, and e2e/design/themes.spec.ts -- only unit-tested so far, not verified in a real browser.
- Structured JSONL test logging per the bead's logging fields.
- Font license records in the rights layers (docs/provenance or equivalent) beyond the OFL.txt files themselves sitting in public/fonts/.

comments.author: BeigeShore
comments.text: Resuming (queue re-issued this bead). Prior commits 75dbe3a/2d52d70 already landed the theme system, real self-hosted fonts, and a hand-rolled cmap parser that DISCLOSED real Greek-alphabet/math-symbol gaps in Newsreader/Plus Jakarta Sans via passing tests. What's still missing per this message's restated trap: those tests currently encode the gaps as expected/passing, not as a BUILD FAILURE. Now building: a real scan of what content actually uses (not just the declared baseline) and a gate that fails when a used glyph is missing from its font. Owned paths unchanged: src/app/theme/**, public/fonts/**.

comments.author: BeigeShore
comments.text:
BATCH_PENDING (BeigeShore, content landed in commit da71d8a -- shared-index absorption, disclosed below).

DONE this pass: the actual build-failure gate the restated trap asked for. Prior work (75dbe3a/2d52d70) had disclosed real Greek-alphabet/math-symbol gaps in Newsreader/Plus Jakarta Sans via tests that PASSED by correctly describing the current state -- that is not the same as a build gate, since nothing there checked what content actually uses or would fail on a genuinely new problem.

src/app/theme/contentGlyphUsage.ts (new) scans the REAL content corpus (content/**/*.{json,yaml}), structurally parsed (js-yaml/JSON.parse, never a byte-regex), collecting every non-ASCII code point that appears in a value a reader could actually see. It excludes values under a key literally named "latex" (KaTeX source, exempt -- KaTeX has its own fonts) and content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml (a lint-rule config file whose "markWords" list includes the literal characters "✓"/"✗" as FORBIDDEN vocabulary, never text shown to a reader -- confirmed by reading that file, not assumed).

src/app/theme/contentGlyphCoverage.test.ts (new) is the gate: every code point the scan finds must be covered by at least one of the three self-hosted fonts, or it fails the build, naming the code point and the exact file it came from. A seeded-glyph test proves this is not vacuous.

REAL RESULT: scanning actual content found 56 distinct non-ASCII code points in use (not a declared baseline guess). 53 are covered by at least one self-hosted font (JetBrains Mono alone covers nearly all of the Greek alphabet and most math operators used in real content, which is a materially better story than the per-font gaps disclosed in the theme bead's first pass suggested). THREE are genuinely missing from all three fonts, found in real, currently-published content, not a hypothetical:
- U+2207 NABLA (∇) in an authored R3 reading (content/editorial/readings-owners/am-sr-12-charge-current-bgq0.yaml), literally quoting "∂ρ/∂t + ∇·J = 0"
- U+221D PROPORTIONAL TO (∝) in content/experiments/lq-01.yaml's labeled relations ("I ∝ r^(-1)", etc.)
- U+22A5 UP TACK (⊥) in content/notation/special-relativity.yaml's notation concordance ("a_⊥")

These three are named, dated exceptions (KNOWN_GAPS) so the gate stays green today rather than blocking every other lane's unrelated work, but the test also asserts each KNOWN_GAPS entry is STILL actually missing and STILL actually used -- a stale entry (fixed but not removed, or removed from content but not from the list) fails on its own. Fixing the underlying gap needs a fourth font or a documented per-symbol substitution, a real design decision I am not making unilaterally in this pass.

Files and tests (runner: bun test; local only -- CI has not run all day per the orchestrator's earlier report, though this tick's message says browser-acceptance is now green; quality-gates has a separate, unrelated content failure I have not investigated):
- src/app/theme/contentGlyphUsage.ts (new)
- src/app/theme/contentGlyphCoverage.test.ts (new, 5 tests)

`bun test src/app/theme/` -- 48 pass, 0 fail, re-verified at pushed HEAD da71d8a.
`bunx tsc --noEmit` -- 0 errors in both new files, locally.
`bunx biome check` -- clean on both files.

TRANSPARENCY: both new files landed inside commit da71d8a ("fix(reader): correct misconception fixtures and add gate/schema tests [am-read-misconception-callouts-a3o]"), not a commit I authored or intended -- shared-index absorption during a `git add`/concurrent-commit race in the shared working tree, same pattern disclosed earlier this session. Verified byte-identical against what I wrote (git show da71d8a:src/app/theme/contentGlyphUsage.ts diffs clean against the working-tree file). Not claiming that sha as mine; disclosing it because the content is real and already on origin/main.

Still not done: the three real gaps are unresolved (need a font-sourcing decision, not just a gate); font subsetting; KaTeX font self-hosting; browser/CLS/forced-colors verification; structured logging -- same list as the first BATCH_PENDING on this bead.

comments.author: BeigeShore
comments.text:
STATUS: landed, not closeable. Walking this bead's own seven acceptance criteria one by one, file:line evidence for each, naming what's NOT met plainly. All file:line refs are current at pushed HEAD da71d8a (my content; landed via shared-index absorption into that sha, disclosed in the prior comment, byte-verified identical).

1. "Three themes render the fixture pages. Slate appears by default on /discover unless the reader has set a theme."
   PARTIALLY MET. Three themes: src/app/theme/tokens.ts:50-75 (THEME_TOKENS, annalen/kramgasse-night/slate), src/app/theme/themes.css:8,17,26 (:root[data-theme="..."] blocks). Wired site-wide: src/app/layout.tsx:5 imports themes.css, :27 injects the pre-paint script, :43 renders <ThemeToggle/> -- every real page renders under an active theme today.

comments.text:
GLYPH COVERAGE FINDING, recorded by TanElk. The bead stays OPEN, and pane16 is right, not wrong.

pane16's glyph gate is the strongest new gate this swarm has produced. It reads the real font files
from public/fonts with readFileSync and parses their cmap (loadCmap / missingGlyphs) rather than
asserting against a hardcoded list, so the proof class is the actual shipped artifact. The typecheck
rework that landed with it (a2e489c) used explicit if-throw narrowing with zero casts, zero
@ts-expect-error and zero non-null assertions; the three assertions it appears to remove are the
same three rewritten after narrowing. Theme suites: 78 pass, 0 fail, 174 expect() across 5 files,
and tsc --noEmit is now at 0 errors repo-wide.

And it found a REAL DEFECT rather than manufacturing a green:

  Newsreader and Plus Jakarta Sans do not contain the Greek alphabet at all.
  U+00B5 MICRO SIGN is present but U+03BC GREEK SMALL LETTER MU is NOT.
  Subscript digits are absent; JetBrains Mono is missing U+221D PROPORTIONAL TO.

The test names this explicitly - "REAL GAP: the micro sign is present but Greek mu is not, exactly
the pitfall the bead names by name" - and asserts hasGlyph(0x3bc) === false. Documenting the true
state instead of asserting [] is the honest move and I am crediting it as such.

Why the bead does NOT close on this: its own text requires the fonts to be "tested against German
diacritics, Greek letters, subscripts, primes, old notation" and to be "self-hosted and subset
without omitting needed mathematical glyphs". Greek coverage is therefore an in-scope acceptance
condition, not a follow-up. Closing this bead and moving the Greek gap into a new one is exactly
RH-9 follow-up laundering, which AGENTS.md forbids by name. So it stays open and the gap stays
attached to it.

Why this needs the project owner rather than more agent work: subsetting cannot add a glyph the
upstream face never had. Newsreader and Plus Jakarta Sans ship no Greek, so this is not a subsetting
bug that can be fixed by re-running a tool. It is a decision among three real options, which pane16
already identified: (1) change one or more text faces to a family that carries Greek and subscripts,
(2) add a Unicode-range fallback face for Greek and mathematical text, or (3) decide that Greek and
math glyphs in body prose always route through KaTeX, which ships its own fonts, and never appear as
plain text. Option 3 has teeth beyond typography: AGENTS.md requires mathematics to survive with
JavaScript disabled and in print, so "route it through KaTeX" must be checked against the no-JS and
print lanes before it is chosen.

This matters concretely for THIS edition: mu carries particle mass and mobility in the Brownian
paper, nu is frequency in the light-quanta paper, and the notation concordance already binds
\kappa, \mu, \nu and \varphi to quantities. A reader hitting a tofu box where mu should be is a
prerequisite dead end, which doctrine 2 forbids.

1. Route Default Strictly Via data-route-theme Attribute (Zero Path Parsing):
- Updated src/app/theme/themeInit.inline.ts: completely eliminated location.pathname inspection.
- Route default is resolved exclusively via data-route-theme attribute on document.documentElement, container elements ([data-route-theme]), or meta tags (meta[name='data-route-theme'], meta[name='route-theme']).
- In src/app/discover/layout.tsx: metadata.other declares both 'data-route-theme': 'slate' and 'route-theme': 'slate', ensuring the pre-paint script detects the attribute before paint.
- Automated tests in src/app/theme/themeInit.test.ts verify:
  * data-route-theme on documentElement selects slate when cold.
  * data-route-theme on container element selects slate when cold.
  * meta[name='data-route-theme'] selects slate when cold.
  * Explicit stored reader preference strictly overrides data-route-theme.
  * Non-annotated pages fall back to annalen.
  * Planted negative: a simulated resolver ignoring data-route-theme fails to select slate.

2. Three Themes & Pinned Tokens (src/app/theme/tokens.ts, src/app/theme/themes.css):
- Annalen matches docs/design/placeholder exactly: paper #eee7d7, ink #1a1916, muted #5c554a, rule #cbc1ac, red #ae2119.
- Kramgasse Night: paper #1c2128, ink #adbac7, muted #768390, rule #444c56, accent #e29b38.
- Slate: paper #14181a, ink #e6e8ea, muted #8c9296, rule #2a3034, accent #d97762.

3. Pre-Paint Script (src/app/theme/themeInit.inline.ts):
- Runs inside <head> synchronously, sets data-theme on <html> before paint.
- Reads am:settings:v1:theme inside try/catch.
- Validates against known theme ids plus follow-system.
- Derived into inline script with verified hash in src/app/inline-scripts/registry.ts (tested by scripts/build/inline-script-hashes.test.ts).

4. Accessible Radio Group ThemeToggle (src/app/theme/ThemeToggle.tsx):
- Reflects active theme (including Slate route default) on initial render.
- Announced once on change via role='status' aria-live='polite'.
- Operable by keyboard; selecting a theme updates localStorage and documentElement dataset.

5. Forced-Colors Mode (src/app/theme/themes.css, src/app/theme/contrast.test.ts):
- Outline uses 2px solid CanvasText with 2px offset under @media (forced-colors: active).
- Color never carries meaning alone: structural underline (0.2em offset, 2px hover), font-weight bold on active states, cursor not-allowed on disabled controls.
- Equation color palettes verified to provide textual badgeLabel, underlineClass, and activeRing outlines, with planted negative.

6. Automated WCAG AA Contrast Suite (src/app/theme/contrast.test.ts):
- 31 pass / 0 fail (69 expect calls).
- Normal text >= 4.5:1 across all three themes (ink on paper, paper on ink, paper on accent, muted on paper).
- UI boundaries >= 3.0:1 (focusRing on paper).
- 3 Planted negatives proving failure: identical colors fail (1.0 < 4.5), white on Kramgasse amber fails (2.18 < 4.5), white on Slate coral fails (3.07 < 4.5).

7. Verification:
- bun test src/app/theme/: 82 pass / 0 fail across 5 files (207 expect calls).
- bun test scripts/build/inline-script-hashes.test.ts: 8 pass / 0 fail.
- bunx biome check on changed files: clean (0 errors, 0 warnings).
- Bead remains open awaiting project owner decision on the font half.

pane31. The U+207F constraint is RESOLVED through the gate's own contract, not by silencing it. Commit 8a1c264. Bead NOT closed.

== THE FAILURE, REPRODUCED ==
  bun test src/app/theme/contentGlyphCoverage.test.ts -> 4 pass, 1 fail
  "U+207F (ⁿ) in content/arguments/light-quanta/arg-lq-independent-configurations.json"
Three occurrences, all in PROSE strings: the recap, the overview reading, and step 3 of the steps list, each writing "fⁿ".

== WHICH OF THE TWO PERMITTED ROUTES APPLIES, ESTABLISHED BY MEASUREMENT ==
You said either the font covers it or I name and date it. I checked whether "the font covers it" was actually reachable before assuming it was not, because a missing glyph can be a subsetting artifact rather than a typeface fact. Direct cmap probe of the three shipped TTFs:

  glyph                         Newsreader   PlusJakarta   JetBrainsMono
  U+207F superscript n             false        false          false
  U+2071 superscript i             false        false          false
  superscript 0-4                  true         true           true
  superscript 5-9                  false        true           true
  U+207A superscript plus          false        true           true
  U+2080 subscript zero            false        true           true

And there is NO subsetting step in the repo - scripts/subset-fonts.ts does not exist, which the bead's own Technical Approach still lists as to-be-built. So public/fonts holds the upstream variable fonts as shipped, and U+207F is absent from the typefaces themselves. A wider subset cannot recover it. Adding a fourth font is excluded by this bead ("Newsreader, Plus Jakarta Sans, JetBrains Mono, and KaTeX fonts only. No other web fonts."). So route one was genuinely unavailable and route two is correct.

Worth noting for the record: U+207F is a superscript LETTER. The bead's declared baseline asks only for "superscript and subscript digits used in prose", so a superscript letter was never in the baseline; it entered through content. The gate did its job exactly as designed - it caught a code point the declared list never anticipated.

== WHAT I WROTE ==
Added 0x207F to KNOWN_GAPS with a named, dated entry (2026-09-19, pane31, this bead), and extended the header's gap record from three to four with the measurement above.

I also recorded something that distinguishes it from the other three gaps, because I do not think it should live there permanently: IT IS CHEAPLY RETIRABLE AND NEEDS NO FONT DECISION. The same content file already states the identical quantity in prose without the glyph - its "question" field reads "Why is the probability f to the power n, rather than just f?" while its "recap" reads "... is fⁿ". One file, one idea, two prose conventions. The exact algebra is already carried properly by that file's own formula node, latex "W=f^n", so nothing mathematical is lost by spelling it out in the three prose strings.

I did NOT make that change. Editing reader-facing argument prose belongs to the light-quanta argument bead, not to a typography bead, and you have been clear about not reaching into other people's content. Recommend dispatching it there; it retires a permanent gap for a three-string edit.

== PROOF IT IS NOT A SILENCER ==
The entry is self-retiring, and I proved it rather than asserting it. Planted: replaced all three prose occurrences of "fⁿ" with "f to the power n" in the content file, then ran the gate:
  (fail) "every entry in KNOWN_GAPS is still actually present in the real content (a stale entry hides that content changed)"  -> 4 pass, 1 fail
So the moment the content stops using the glyph, the gate fails until someone deletes my entry. It cannot rot into permanent cover. Content restored byte-identically afterwards, shasum -a 256 -c OK.
The gate's other pawls also still bind my entry: "every entry in KNOWN_GAPS is still actually missing from all three fonts" would fail if a future font covered it, and the seeded-U+1F4A9 test still proves the gate is non-vacuous. All five tests pass now.

== STATE OF THE REST OF THIS BEAD, measured just now, one test file per invocation ==
GREEN already, not my work, recording so you know what is banked:
  src/app/theme/contrast.test.ts             37 pass, 0 fail
  src/app/theme/themeInit.test.ts            33 pass, 0 fail
  src/app/theme/glyphCoverage.test.ts        18 pass, 0 fail
  src/app/theme/tokensExport.test.ts          5 pass, 0 fail
  src/app/theme/contentGlyphCoverage.test.ts  5 pass, 0 fail  (was 4/1 before this commit)
  npx tsc --noEmit exit 0; biome on my changed file exit 0
All three themes are declared in themes.css: [data-theme="annalen"], [data-theme="kramgasse-night"], [data-theme="slate"]. OFL license files ship beside all three families (public/fonts/*/OFL.txt).

STILL MISSING against the Acceptance Criteria, so this bead is nowhere near closeable:
  - scripts/subset-fonts.ts does not exist. No subsetting happens at all today; the full upstream variable fonts ship. That means the "subsets are rebuilt when content changes" and "KaTeX files ship whole until the manifest exists" criteria are untested because there is nothing to test.
  - e2e/design/themes.spec.ts does not exist, so every browser-side criterion is unmet: first-paint screenshots per theme with client bundles blocked, the /discover Slate default and its override, keyboard toggling, CLS <= 0.1 with cold caches, forced-colors, 320 px, high zoom.
  - I have not verified the pre-paint script's hash appears in the inline-script hash manifest.
No claim is made on any of those. I fixed the one live constraint you named and measured the rest.

comments.text: pane31. Increment d7f435d: the colour-never-alone rule is now PROVEN for all three themes by a corpus sweep, not by examples. And the sweep found a real defect class in the two dark themes. Bead NOT closed. == WHAT WAS THERE, AND WHY IT WAS NOT YET A PROOF == contrast.test.ts already had a "color never carries meaning alone" block. Read closely, it asserts six hand-picked selectors with `toContain` against two CSS files, and its planted negative defines a helper INSIDE the test and runs it on two literal strings. So it proves those six rules are fine and proves the helper works; it never looks at a seventh rule and never reads the corpus. Nothing stopped the next rule from encoding a distinction in hue alone. I did not remove or weaken any of it - 37 tests went to 50. == SWEEP 1: COLOUR IS NEVER THE ONLY CHANNEL == New src/app/theme/colourChannels.ts reads every rule in src/**/*.css that paints --accent and requires either a non-colour channel in the same rule or a registered reason naming where the channel actually lives. Audited all 45 accent rules: 30 carry their own channel, 8 needed a registered reason, and ZERO were genuine violations. I want to be plain about that: I went looking for a colour-only defect and the project does not have one. Each of the 8 was verified by reading the markup, not assumed: .legend-prediction PredictOverlay.tsx:110-145 gives the prediction a DASHED stroke and SQUARE marker against the result's SOLID stroke and CIRCLE marker, plus ASCII glyphs and a bold label. Four channels. It is the model of how to do this. .warning markup says "(wrong model)" in words (LightComplexLab.tsx:367,374) .badge-status markup says Status: (TermExplorer.tsx:243) .explanation-text renders the refusal's own prose (ParameterControl.tsx:433) .beyond-track renders a separate "Beyond visual track (value unit)" element (ParameterControl.tsx:421) .error always used as "notice error"; .notice supplies border-left: 3px solid, call sites add role="alert" a:not(.button), .direct-pdf-link, h1 em UA defaults: link underline, italic .a11y-btn, button:hover, ::selection, .concordance-card:target, .search-option focus outline from themes.css, figure/ground swap, a background block appearing, a box-shadow ring, aria-selected The registry is checked for staleness both ways: a registered selector that stops existing, or that gains its own inline channel, fails the test and must be deleted. SCOPE, stated because it is a judgement call you may want to overrule: the sweep polices --accent only. That is the token AGENTS.md reserves for meaning ("red only for emphasis and the move step"). --muted is de-emphasis - a reader who cannot perceive it loses no information, since the secondary prose still reads and says what it is. Holding muted to the same rule would flag every hint and caption in the project and teach people to add exemptions, which is how a gate dies. --ink/--paper are default text and background and --rule is already documented as decorative in tokens.ts. == SWEEP 2: A REAL DEFECT IN THE TWO DARK THEMES == The AC says "Every text color pair used in each theme meets WCAG AA". The existing check tests the six DECLARED TOKEN pairs per theme. Those are not the same thing, and the gap hides a whole defect class: a rule that hardcodes a pale background and sets no colour leaves its text at --ink, which is near-white in Kramgasse Night and Slate. Neither colour is a token, so no declared-pair check can see it. MEASURED: 86 hardcoded background hexes across 11 stylesheets. 50 set their own colour and are exempt - self-consistent, though not theme-aware. 36 set no colour and inherit --ink. 67 file-theme pairs fall below AA, most around 1.01:1, which is pale-on-pale and effectively invisible. The affected selectors are not decoration. Worst offenders: 1.01 .equation-inspector equations.css:68 1.02 .card-collision-alert notation.css:481 1.03 .genealogy-node-btn[data-selected="true"] genealogy.css:166 1.03 .weave-assumption-active reader.css:392 1.03 .error globals.css:402 1.05 .derivation-step[data-is-move="true"] derivation.css:74 1.06 .equation-sentence span[data-selected="true"] equations.css:35 The selected equation term, the weave's active assumption, collision alerts, and the MOVE STEP - the single marker AGENTS.md reserves red for - are unreadable in the dark themes wherever no override exists. A CORRECTION I MADE TO MY OWN NUMBER MID-MEASUREMENT: my first pass said 32 failing rules and did not account for theme-scoped overrides. I then found [data-theme="slate"] .derivation-step[data-is-move="true"] at derivation.css:116 and re-ran with overrides excluded, expecting the number to drop. It did not: there are only TWO theme-scoped override selectors in the entire project, both Slate, both the move step, so the count went to 34 distinct rules / 67 file-theme pairs. The correction went the wrong way and I am reporting the larger number. I did NOT restyle 11 stylesheets. Replacing 36 hardcoded pastels with tokens is a visual design decision across components owned by other beads, and inventing design is the one thing forbidden here from the start. Instead this lands as a per-file ratchet (src/app/theme/darkThemeContrastBaseline.json, 67 across 10 files) that may only shrink, with a no-slack pawl so a file below its number must be tightened in the same commit. Same shape as declaredClassesBaseline. The paydown is a real piece of work and wants its own dispatch and a design ruling on what the dark-theme equivalents of those pastels should be. == PROOF BOTH SWEEPS BITE, AGAINST THE REAL CORPUS == In-test planted negatives use fixtures, so I also planted in a real stylesheet: appended ".planted-hue-only-state { color: var(--accent); }" to src/app/globals.css -> caught: "src/app/globals.css:938 .planted-hue-only-state { color: var(--accent); }" appended ".planted-pale-panel { background: #f5f0e8; padding: 1rem; }" -> caught: "src/app/globals.css: 4 > baseline 2" globals.css restored byte-identically afterwards, shasum -a 256 -c OK. I also had to fix one of my OWN new assertions when it failed: the "reason names where the channel lives" test used a regex assuming every channel points at a file or a UA default, which is wrong - some channels are geometry facts like a box-shadow ring or a figure/ground swap. I broadened the vocabulary rather than padding the reasons to match a bad regex. == ALSO ADDED == Accent-vs-ink distinctness per theme: annalen 2.538, kramgasse-night 1.750, slate 2.658, floor 1.5. Explicitly labelled a PROJECT floor, not a WCAG threshold - WCAG says nothing about accent-vs-ink. The point is that where colour is the redundant second channel it should actually be perceivable; the floor sits below the observed minimum with margin so it catches a future token collapse rather than today's values. == EVIDENCE == bun test src/app/theme/contrast.test.ts -> 50 pass, 0 fail, 319 expect() calls (was 37 pass) npx tsc --noEmit -> exit 0 ; npx biome check on both changed files -> exit 0 No existing assertion weakened, removed, or skipped. == STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD == - scripts/subset-fonts.ts still does not exist; the full upstream variable fonts ship, so the subsetting ACs remain untestable. - e2e/design/themes.spec.ts still does not exist, so every browser AC is unmet: first-paint per theme with bundles blocked, the /discover Slate default and its override, keyboard toggling, CLS with cold caches, forced-colors, 320px, high zoom. - the pre-paint script's hash in the inline-script hash manifest is still unverified by me. - the 67 dark-theme contrast failures are recorded, not fixed.

pane31. Increment 9133dd1: dark-theme contrast paid down worst-first, baseline tightened in the SAME commit, and the pre-paint hash question answered. Bead NOT closed.

== BEFORE -> AFTER PER STYLESHEET (as requested) ==
  src/reader/reader.css                            22 ->  8   (-14)
  src/equations/derivations/derivation.css          9 ->  4   (-5)
  src/equations/equations.css                       6 ->  4   (-2)
  src/app/globals.css                               2 ->  0   (-2)
  src/app/notation/notation.css                    10 -> 10
  src/equations/genealogy/genealogy.css            10 -> 10

No baseline entry widened; I assert that mechanically as well as by eye. Your pawl did exactly what you said it would: my first run after the fixes failed with "the baseline has no slack: a stylesheet below its number must be tightened in the same commit", and it stayed red until I tightened it in this same change.

== THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH WAS BIGGER THAN THE HEX LIST ==
My previous sweep only looked at hardcoded hex backgrounds. Chasing the worst offenders led to the actual cause: --wash and --plot were declared once in globals.css :root and NEVER given per-theme values. themes.css themes paper/ink/muted/rule/accent/focus-ring/plot-darkfield and stops. So every "background: var(--wash)" rule painted Annalen's light beige in the dark themes too - 38 rules across 16 stylesheets, near-white --ink on #e5ded0, 1.07:1 in Kramgasse Night and 1.16:1 in Slate. My own sweep had EXEMPTED all 38 because it only matched #hex, so the reported 67 was an undercount of the real damage. --plot is fine (7.34 / 7.94); it is a dark green and light ink reads on it.

--wash is now a real exported token with per-theme values, derived rather than invented: I took Annalen's own relationships as the reference (ink 13.14, muted 5.50, wash-vs-paper 1.086) and picked values that reproduce them. Kramgasse Night #232a32 gives 11.62 / 5.50 / 1.116 - the muted figure lands on Annalen's 5.50 exactly. Slate #1b2123 gives 14.13 / 7.74 / 1.096, the closest available to Annalen's panel separation. tokensExport now asserts wash stays in sync between tokens.ts and themes.css, and auditThemeTokensContrast gained ink-on-wash and muted-on-wash so the token is actually gated; its pinned pair count went UP, 18 -> 24, which is a tightening.

Fixing --wash first also meant I could widen coverage later without widening any baseline: those 38 rules now pass, so bringing token-valued backgrounds into the sweep adds zero entries. Order mattered.

== TWO DEAD SELECTORS, THE BEST FIND IN THIS PASS ==
derivation.css carried [data-theme="kramgasse"] TWICE - for the move step and for the move box - against the real id kramgasse-night. They parse, they lint, they ship, and they never match. So Kramgasse Night silently lost the dark treatment its author had written (background #451a03, amber border) while Slate kept its own, which is exactly why the move step showed up in my failure list for Night but not Slate. That is not a design decision, it is a typo, so I fixed it rather than reporting it.

Added a sweep that fails on any [data-theme=...] in any project stylesheet naming a theme not in THEME_IDS, with its planted negative being that exact historical typo rather than an invented fixture. Audited values now in the corpus: annalen 1, kramgasse-night 2, slate 4, and zero unknowns.

== WHAT I RETHEMED, AND WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT ==
Backgrounds only, keeping every other property including the amber identity borders: four amber notice surfaces, the verbatim rights statement and the selected page-map row in reader.css; the equation inspector (its #eee7d8 was literally Annalen's paper hardcoded); the approximation and scope-change step panels; and .error, whose #f8e9df left text at 1.03:1 and which is always used as "notice error", so it now follows .notice's own var(--wash).

.facsimile-page-preview stays #ffffff and now declares its own dark ink. It depicts a scanned page, so it should be white in every theme; the bug was that it inherited a near-white --ink onto white paper.

The remaining 44 are the SEMANTIC ROLE PALETTE and I did not touch them: the four .weave-* tints (assumption-active, quantity-compared, agreement-within-bound, outside-domain), the equation selection highlights, and the genealogy and notation card tints. Those encode distinct meanings, so retheming them means choosing a dark-theme semantic palette, which is am-design-semantic-color-8vbq's decision and explicitly out of scope here. Collapsing four weave tints into one var(--wash) would have destroyed four distinctions to make a number go down. That is the paydown that needs a design ruling before anyone continues.

== ALSO FIXED ==
color-scheme was left at the global "light" for all three themes, so native form controls and scrollbars rendered light in Kramgasse Night and Slate. Both dark themes now set color-scheme: dark.

== THE PRE-PAINT HASH: VERIFIED, NOT BLOCKED ==
I said last time this was unverified by me. It verifies, and it is already well gated - I am reporting it rather than adding anything, because the coverage that exists is better than what I would have bolted on.
  artifacts/build/inline-script-hashes.json carries
    {"id":"theme","ownerBeadId":"am-design-themes-typography-288q","routes":"all",
     "sha256":"iJRgi6oyhJCQJVqFATlHoN25tZuQS1XwbzYF28TRPYI=","length":1318}
  I recomputed base64(sha256(THEME_INIT_SOURCE)) independently: identical, and the byte length matches at 1318. CSP form sha256-iJRgi6oyhJCQJVqFATlHoN25tZuQS1XwbzYF28TRPYI=.
  It cannot rot: scripts/build/inline-script-hashes.test.ts has 8 tests including byte-exactness ("an entry whose source differs from the emitted bytes by trailing whitespace fails"), an unregistered-script failure, and a stale-entry failure; and themeInit.test.ts has its own "theme script manifest registration (AC 7)" block. AC 7 is met.

== EVIDENCE ==
  bun test src/app/theme/contrast.test.ts      -> 53 pass, 0 fail (was 50)
  bun test src/app/theme/tokensExport.test.ts  ->  5 pass, 0 fail (28 assertions, wash now included)
  bun test src/app/theme/themeInit.test.ts     -> 33 pass, 0 fail
  npx tsc --noEmit -> exit 0 ; biome clean on all ten changed files
  No assertion weakened, removed or skipped; two pinned counts moved UPWARD (contrast pairs 18->24, tests 50->53).

== STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD ==
  - 44 dark-theme failures remain, all semantic-palette, blocked on am-design-semantic-color-8vbq.
  - scripts/subset-fonts.ts still does not exist; the full upstream variable fonts ship, so the subsetting ACs stay untestable.
  - e2e/design/themes.spec.ts still does not exist: first-paint per theme with bundles blocked, the /discover Slate default and its override, keyboard toggling, CLS with cold caches, forced-colors, 320px and high zoom are all unmet.
  - I have not looked at whether --plot, --line or --panel have the same never-themed problem beyond --wash; --plot I checked and it is fine, the other two resolve to themed tokens.

pane31. Increment f7a2f7b: dark-theme contrast 44 -> 22, baseline tightened in the SAME commit. Bead NOT closed.

== BEFORE -> AFTER PER STYLESHEET ==
  src/equations/genealogy/genealogy.css            10 ->  2   (-8)
  src/app/notation/notation.css                    10 ->  4   (-6)
  src/a11y/actions/families/interval/interval.css   2 ->  0   (-2)
  src/platform/print/print.css                      2 ->  0   (-2)
  src/platform/storage/dataPanel.css                2 ->  0   (-2)
  src/equations/derivations/derivation.css          4 ->  2   (-2)
  src/equations/equations.css                       4 ->  4
  src/components/lab/showTheCode.css                2 ->  2
  src/reader/reader.css                             8 ->  8
  TOTAL                                            44 -> 22   (-22)
No entry widened, asserted mechanically. Your pawl is why the baseline moved in this commit rather than the next one.

== HONEST SPLIT: 12 OF THE 22 WERE FALSE POSITIVES IN MY OWN SWEEP ==
I want this separated clearly, because "44 -> 22" would otherwise read as twice the repair it is.

REAL FIXES (10 pairs):
  .interval-number-input painted background: #ffffff with no colour, so the field stayed white in every theme while its text followed the theme - near-white on white. A text field has to state both; it now takes var(--paper) and var(--ink). This one is a genuine reading failure in a control a reader types into.
  .collision-cluster-section, .data-panel-quarantine, .genealogy-list-nav -> var(--wash); .genealogy-graph-wrapper -> var(--panel).
  The derivation move-step overrides named only [data-is-move="true"], while DerivationStepComponent.tsx:53 also puts .is-move on the same element. Both theme overrides now list both forms, so the move's dark treatment no longer depends on which of the two selectors a future render happens to keep.

FALSE POSITIVES IN MY SCANNER, removed from the sweep and NOT from the CSS (12 pairs):
  1. @media print. Print is monochrome by construction: print.css opens its block with "*, *::before, *::after { background: transparent; color: #000000 }", and notation.css's print block sets ".notation-page { color: #000; background: #fff }". A pale background inside a print block therefore inherits BLACK, not --ink. My sweep had reported notation.css's printed .concordance-card and .honesty-banner and print.css's .print-scale-facts-table th as unreadable. Had I "fixed" those I would have themed a monochrome page - I was one step from doing exactly that before I read the print reset.
  2. A state rule whose base sets its own colour. .genealogy-node-btn:hover only changes background; .genealogy-node-btn sets color: #2b2621 on the SAME element, so it is self-consistent in every theme. The scanner only saw the hover rule.
  3. Comma groups in theme overrides. My override parser matched the whole selector string, so the [data-theme=...] prefix stayed glued to every part after the first and the second half of an override was never registered. That is why .derivation-step.is-move still showed as failing after I had already extended the override to cover it.

== I WIDENED TWO EXEMPTIONS, SO I PROVED THEY ARE NARROW ==
Removing findings is the shape of gate-weakening, so neither went in unproven. Four new tests hold the print exemption to its shape: it keeps the rules either side of the block, keeps a NON-print @media block (which the sweep must still police), survives a nested @page without eating the rest, and is shown to be load-bearing against the real print.css. The state exemption was planted live rather than in a fixture: appending a :hover pale background whose base sets no colour to src/app/globals.css is still caught, "src/app/globals.css: 2 > baseline 0", and globals.css was restored byte-identically afterwards (shasum -c OK).

== WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY I STOPPED THERE ==
The 22 are eleven rules and every one is semantic: the four .weave-* tints (assumption-active, quantity-compared, agreement-within-bound, outside-domain), three selection highlights at #efe0ad, the two .card-collision-alert severities, the cross-paper pill and the subexpression highlight. Each encodes a distinct meaning, so retheming them means choosing a dark-theme semantic palette - am-design-semantic-color-8vbq's decision, not mine. Collapsing them into var(--wash) would destroy the distinctions to make a number go down.

== A REPAIR TO A BEAD I HAD CALLED COMPLETE ==
Unprompted, and worth flagging because I had told you am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2 was finished. pane30's boundary audit retired s0-p8, s0-p9 and s0-p10 as flush resumptions of s0-p7 (content/aliases/mass-energy.yaml). My concordance still scoped 18 anchors to those ids, so the entries for the generic H, E, K and the additive constant C pointed at units that no longer exist. == WHY THIS ONE WAS DIFFERENT FROM THE REST OF THE SEMANTIC SET ==
I had parked the four .weave-* tints with the rest of the semantic palette. That was too cautious, and reading the rules showed why. The weave already carries its four distinctions WITHOUT colour: border-style dotted, solid, double and dashed, one per meaning, plus a visually-hidden accessible-name prefix, and reader.css says so in its own docblock. So the hue is redundant reinforcement, not the carrier of meaning - which means the fill can be made theme-aware without touching which hue means what. That is the semantic-colour bead's decision and I did not take it.

== NO NEW HUE WAS INTRODUCED, AND THE NUMBER WAS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN ==
Each dark fill is the meaning's OWN authored border colour mixed 18 percent into that theme's own --paper. I did not pick 18 percent for looks. I measured Annalen's authored fill-vs-paper separations (1.102, 1.177, 1.184, 1.160) and searched for the single blend ratio that reproduces all four at once. 18 percent does it:
  kramgasse-night  assumption-active #232545 ink 11.8 sep 1.096 | quantity-compared #1b322c ink 10.9 sep 1.186
                   agreement #19303b ink 11.0 sep 1.177        | outside-domain #3a2723 ink 11.3 sep 1.152
  slate            assumption-active #1c1e3a ink 14.0 sep 1.103 | quantity-compared #142b20 ink 13.0 sep 1.188
                   agreement #13292f ink 13.1 sep 1.179        | outside-domain #331f17 ink 13.5 sep 1.148
Maximum drift from the authored separation is 0.012, so a lit sentence is as prominent in the dark themes as the author made it on paper, and worst --ink contrast over the new fills is 10.9 against the 4.5 minimum. Same method as --wash: reproduce Annalen's own relationships rather than invent.

== A TRANSFER I ALMOST MADE, AND DIDN'T ==
My first instinct was simply to drop the fill in dark themes and let the coloured underline carry it. I measured before doing it: the four border hues against the dark papers are 2.05/2.26 (assumption-active #4338ca), 3.23/3.56, 3.02/3.33 and 3.13/3.45. The indigo is BELOW the 3:1 non-text minimum in both dark themes. Dropping the fill would have made that one highlight nearly invisible on a dark page - trading a contrast failure for a perceptibility failure, which is the transfer you warned me about on the scroll regions. With a fill present the highlight is carried by fill and border style together, exactly as on paper, so the border is reinforcement and its 2.05 is not load-bearing. Recorded for am-design-semantic-color-8vbq rather than silently restyled: that hue is the one to revisit if they ever want the underline to stand alone.

Ten new tests read the real stylesheet, not a copy: each of the eight fills is held to AA for body copy and to the authored prominence within 0.05, the four border styles are asserted distinct with their authored hues, and the planted negative is the REAL defect rather than a fixture - the authored light fills are shown to fail on both dark papers.

comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION: the page-image renders carry no colour. "Derive the palette from the plates" was my instruction and it is unexecutable as written.

## Measured, with the repo's own decoder

src/testing/decodePng.ts, sampling on a grid inside the 8-92 percent margin box:

  artifacts/page-images/ap-17-891/page-09.png  1002x1596
      paper (p90 luminance 251)  rgb 251,251,251  #fbfbfb   R-B spread 0
      ink   (min luminance 34)   rgb  34, 34, 34  #222222

  artifacts/page-images/ap-18-639/page-1.png   1018x1576
      paper (p90 luminance 253)  rgb 253,253,253  #fdfdfd   R-B spread 0
      ink   (min luminance 0)    rgb   0,  0,  0  #000000

Then across every directory under artifacts/page-images: 25 pages sampled, ZERO
with any channel spread above 6. The renders are fully desaturated greyscale.

## What I got wrong, and how

I told pane28, in a dispatch: "Expect the measurement to surprise you. Scanned
1905 stock photographs cooler and more neutral than the cream people imagine."
It is not cooler. It carries no colour information at all, because these are
derived renders of a bitonal or greyscale scan, not colour photographs of paper.

I reasoned from what the artifacts OUGHT to contain rather than opening one.
That is the same error pane28 measured against me one tick earlier, when I
asserted that removing the slate theme would shrink the header and it proved the
toggle was 105px on both sides of that commit. Both times I stated a causal or
factual claim in an instruction without checking it, and both times a pane was
already acting on it.

## What survives, and it is not nothing

TONE, not hue. Paper at luminance 251 against ink at 34 is a real measured
relationship from the actual printing, and it is a legitimate basis for the
lightness structure of both themes.

And one measured detail worth keeping: on ap-17-891 the darkest ink is #222222,
not black. Real ink on real paper is not maximally dark, which is an argument
against a pure-black ink token, and it is evidence rather than taste.

## Revised instruction, recorded so the next person does not repeat mine

Derive the lightness structure from the plates and report the measurement. CHOOSE
the hue and argue for it in the commit. It is a choice, not a derivation, and
saying so is the difference between a design decision and a fabricated
provenance. The one thing that has not changed: #eee7d7 is the generic AI-default
warm cream and is not kept by inertia; arriving near it requires an argument.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to my palette record, raised by TanElk and verified independently.

FALSE, in commit 93440769 and in my bead comment above: 'All 100 encode as PNG
type Grayscale.' Struck in bb46dfb1.

MEASURED: the IHDR colour-type byte at offset 25 of every file. 100 of 100 are
type 2, truecolour RGB. Not one is type 0. Zero malformed headers.

THE MECHANISM, because it is reusable. I cited magick -format '%[type]', which
printed 'Grayscale'. That field is ImageMagick's classification of the PIXEL
CONTENT, not a reading of the file header, and it prints Grayscale for a type-2
RGB file whose pixels all happen to be grey. Side by side on
ap-17-549/page-02.png: IHDR byte 2, %[type] Grayscale. I read a tool's derived
attribute as a property of the file format.

THE CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED and now rests only on what was measured. Re-verified
at FULL resolution on all 100 - my earlier corpus figure was taken on 300x300
resizes as a screen, and the per-channel check had covered only two files - by
two methods sharing no code path:

    max HSL saturation      exactly 0 on 100 of 100
    max|R-G| and max|G-B|   exactly 0 on 100 of 100

Every pixel of every plate is exactly achromatic. The plates are RGB-encoded
files containing perfectly achromatic data; they were greyscaled before this
project received them; they cannot speak to hue. No token moved: paper #fbfbfb
and ink #3f3f3f stand exactly as derived.

WHY STRUCK RATHER THAN LEFT. 'The format says grey' and 'every pixel happens to
be grey' are different facts and only the second is true. A false leg propped
under a true conclusion is what gets quoted onward - which is the same failure
this palette commit was correcting, where 'Annalen reads ink 13.14' had stood
long enough for a dark theme to be built on it.
