title: Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey II (Brownian motion)
description:
# Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey II (Brownian motion)

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.1–5.3, §9.3, §3.9 (paper 2 margin), §22.1 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey II asks: how can visible wandering reveal invisible molecules? Its shelf holds what a careful reader of the literature could know by the end of 1904 about Brownian motion, kinetic theory, osmosis, drag, and diffusion. Two entries are deliberately wrong turns that become forks (Nägeli's single-impact objection and Exner's speed measurements). One entry, Sutherland, is the canonical test of the shelf rules: his January 1904 Dunedin presentation is a legitimate shelf card, while his June 1905 *Philosophical Magazine* paper appeared between Einstein's submission (received 11 May 1905) and publication (18 July 1905) and is parallel work.

Anachronism controls for this paper: do not say everyone rejected atoms (represent real disagreement and existing molecular reasoning); do not say Einstein explained observations he had studied in detail (the paper's introduction says the available reports were too imprecise for a judgment); do not present Langevin equations or Wiener-process notation (1908 and later) as Einstein's derivation.

The Brownian reference slice (`am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias`) already authors the cards that Route B and the Exner fork need, **and verifies them**: because `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j` rule 3 fails a production build that cites an unverified card, and the slice's exit demonstration runs a production build, the slice creates a verification record for every card it cites before that demonstration. This bead completes the shelf, reuses those records instead of treating the slice's cards as unverified drafts, and corrects any card the originals contradict.

## Scope

In scope: one verified HistoricalPremise record per card below, with the fields and rules of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`; permitted stages; limits; the paper's own citations where present; the Sutherland split; the primary-source verification queue; the reuse rule for the slice's verification records; the list of later items kept off the shelf.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): card rendering and rules (`am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`); the chain (`am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u`); the slice's own route and stages (`am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias`); the Perrin dataset (`am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`); paper 2 margin entries (`am-bm-margin-entries-7fa4`); timeline cards for later items (`am-disc-timeline-xzef`); the human knowledge-boundary review (`am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`).

## Requirements

Store records under `content/historical-premises/` (journey-neutral card ids in lowercase kebab case, `<first-author>-<year>-<topic>`; this bead's cards may be grouped in `content/historical-premises/brownian/`). Each record carries the standard fields of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: `sources[]` as printed, `date` (`earliest`, `latest`, `latestYear`, `precision`), the precise `proposition`, `limits`, `status`, `admittedStages[]`, `paperCitesOrAsserts` where the paper cites or asserts the item, `einsteinKnowledgeEvidence` only with its own citation, and `verification` (`verifiedBy`, `verifierKind`, `date`, `method`, `evidenceLocator`, `printedCitation`, `discrepancies[]`, `reviewRecordId`).

| Card id | Date (`latestYear`) | Proposition | Limits to state | Status | Candidate citation (verify) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `brown-1828-microscopical-observations` | observed 1827, published 1828 (1828) | Fragments from within pollen grains, and inorganic particles, suspended in water move irregularly | An observation, not a cause | available | R. Brown, Phil. Mag. (n.s.) 4 (1828) 161 |
| `gouy-1888-brownian-motion` | 1888 (1888) | The motion is intrinsic and persistent; faster for smaller particles and in warmer, less viscous liquids; not caused by light, convection, or vibration; Gouy proposed thermal molecular agitation as its cause | Qualitative; no quantitative law | available | G. Gouy, J. Phys. Théor. Appl. (2) 7 (1888) 561 |
| `naegeli-1879-single-impact-objection` | 1879 (1879) | A single molecular impact cannot give a visible particle a perceptible velocity, so molecular agitation cannot be the cause of the motion | States the claim only; the flaw is shown in Fork A, never editorialized on the card | available | C. Nägeli, Sitzungsber. math.-phys. Cl. k. b. Akad. Wiss. München 9 (1879) 389 (queue item Q1) |
| `exner-1900-particle-speeds` | 1900 (1900) | Measured particle "speeds" are far too small for kinetic theory | States what was measured; that the measured quantity depends on the observation interval is shown in Fork B | available | F. M. Exner, Ann. Phys. (4) 2 (1900) 843 |
| `maxwell-1860-equipartition` | 1860 to Boltzmann's gas-theory work (year of the latest cited source) | In thermal equilibrium the mean kinetic energy of translation is the same for every kind of particle, whatever its mass (written today as $\tfrac32 k_BT$) | Classical equipartition; the symbol $k$ as a named constant is Planck's (1900–1901) notation and the card says so | available | J. C. Maxwell, Phil. Mag. (4) 19 (1860) 19; L. Boltzmann, Wien. Ber. 58 (1868) 517 or *Vorlesungen über Gastheorie* (1896–1898) (choose and verify) |
| `vanthoff-1887-osmotic-pressure` | 1877, 1887 (1887) | Dissolved molecules exert an osmotic pressure obeying the gas law | Dilute solutions | available | W. Pfeffer, *Osmotische Untersuchungen* (1877); J. H. van 't Hoff, Z. phys. Chem. 1 (1887) 481 |
| `stokes-1851-sphere-drag` | 1851 (1851) | A sphere moving slowly through a viscous fluid feels a drag $6\pi\eta a v$ | Low Reynolds number, continuum fluid, no slip at the surface | available | G. G. Stokes, Trans. Camb. Phil. Soc. 9 (1851) 8 |
| `fick-1855-diffusion-equation` | 1855 (1855) | The diffusion equation governs how concentration changes | A macroscopic law with no molecular mechanism | available | A. Fick, Ann. Phys. (Pogg.) 94 (1855) 59 |
| `siedentopf-1903-ultramicroscope` | developed 1902, published 1903 (1903) | The ultramicroscope makes particles below ordinary microscope resolution visible | The plan's 1902 date is the demonstration; the card's date is the publication, and both are recorded (queue item Q6) | available | H. Siedentopf and R. Zsigmondy, Ann. Phys. (4) 10 (1903) 1 |
| `loschmidt-1865-molecular-number-estimates` | 1865, 1900–1901 (1901) | Estimates of molecular size and of the molecular number exist (Loschmidt's gas-kinetic estimate; Planck's value from radiation constants) | Different methods with different and large uncertainties | available | J. Loschmidt, Wien. Ber. 52 (1865) 395; M. Planck, Ann. Phys. (4) 4 (1901) 553 |
| `bachelier-1900-speculation-random-walk` | 1900 (1900) | Random-walk-to-diffusion mathematics, worked out for stock prices in a Paris thesis examined by Poincaré | Unknown to physicists at the time; no evidence that Einstein knew it | available | L. Bachelier, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (3) 17 (1900) 21 |
| `sutherland-1904-dunedin` | January 1904 (1904) | The diffusion formula for large molecules, with a slip correction, presented at the Dunedin meeting | A legitimate shelf card; record exactly what the documentary record shows was presented, and not the later published derivation (queue item Q2) | available | W. Sutherland, Australasian Association for the Advancement of Science, Dunedin meeting, January 1904 |
| `sutherland-1905-phil-mag` | proceedings with a misprint in early 1905; *Phil. Mag.* June 1905 (1905) | The published derivation of the diffusion formula with slip | Appeared between Einstein's submission and publication | parallel-work | W. Sutherland, Phil. Mag. (6) 9 (1905) 781 |

**The paper's own citations (category 3), to verify on the facsimile and record on the cards (queue item Q3):** the introduction mentions the "so-called Brownian molecular motion" and says the information available to Einstein was too imprecise to form a judgment (`brown-1828-microscopical-observations`); §3 appears to cite Kirchhoff's lectures on mechanics for the drag formula (`stokes-1851-sphere-drag`); the osmotic argument names van 't Hoff's theory (`vanthoff-1887-osmotic-pressure`). Record each only after checking the page.

**Worth proposing (queue item Q5):** earlier molecular explanations of the motion that show molecular reasoning predated Gouy, such as C. Wiener (1863) and J. Delsaulx with J. Carbonelle (from 1877). Add a card only when its original source is checked; this guards against the invented consensus that "everyone rejected atoms."

**Kept off the shelf** (timeline, margin, or world check only): Smoluchowski (1906); Einstein's second Brownian paper (1906), whose explicit discussion of why a mean velocity is not a meaningful observable belongs in the margin; Svedberg (1906) and Henri (1908) measurements (queue item Q4 settles their dates); Langevin (1908); Perrin (1908–1909) and his 1926 Nobel Prize; Cunningham's slip correction (1910); Bancelin (1911); ballistic Brownian motion measurements (Li et al. 2010; Huang et al. 2011).

### Reusing the slice's verification records

- Whichever of this bead and `am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias` lands first creates a card; the other reuses the same record and id. Neither bead duplicates a card, and neither re-authors a `verification` record that already exists.
- The slice's cards are **verified**, not drafts: its acceptance criteria run the production-profile card rules over its citations, so each of `brown-1828-microscopical-observations`, `gouy-1888-brownian-motion`, `exner-1900-particle-speeds`, `maxwell-1860-equipartition`, `fick-1855-diffusion-equation`, `stokes-1851-sphere-drag`, `siedentopf-1903-ultramicroscope`, `bachelier-1900-speculation-random-walk`, `sutherland-1904-dunedin`, and `sutherland-1905-phil-mag` arrives with a verification record naming what was checked and where.
- This bead reuses those records as they stand. When it re-checks one of them against the original, the re-check is recorded as an additional `history` review record from `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (reviewer holding `history-reviewer` in `docs/OWNERS.md`) referenced from `verification.reviewRecordId`; the existing `verification` record is not rewritten to record that the same conclusion was reached twice.
- A re-check that finds a difference is a correction: update the card, add the difference to `verification.discrepancies` with both readings, raise it with `br comments add am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias`, and leave the slice's stage text and tests to follow the corrected card.
- The three cards no slice stage cites (`naegeli-1879-single-impact-objection`, `vanthoff-1887-osmotic-pressure`, `loschmidt-1865-molecular-number-estimates`) are authored and verified here.

### The primary-source verification queue

The queue is a declared list in `content/historical-premises/brownian/verification-queue.yaml`, each entry `{ id, question, cards[], sourceToConsult, landsIn, status }` where `status` is `open`, `resolved`, or `narrowed` and `landsIn` names the exact field the answer writes. The record shape is registered as an additive schema item with `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j` (requested with `br comments add`), and each shelf bead owns its own queue file and entries. A card whose queue items are still `open` carries no `verification` record, so the publication gate keeps it out of a production build.

| Queue item | Question to settle at the original | Cards | Lands in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Nägeli's publication details: volume, pages, and the printed wording of the single-impact objection | `naegeli-1879-single-impact-objection` | `sources[]`, `proposition`, `verification.printedCitation` |
| Q2 | The documentary record of Sutherland's January 1904 Dunedin presentation: what the report of the meeting shows was presented, and its own citation | `sutherland-1904-dunedin` | `sources[]`, `proposition`, `limits`; a narrowed item says the card records only the reported title if no fuller record exists |
| Q3 | Paper 2's own citations on the facsimile: the introduction's remark on imprecise Brownian reports; the Kirchhoff lecture citation in §3 for the drag formula; van 't Hoff named in the osmotic argument | `brown-1828-microscopical-observations`, `stokes-1851-sphere-drag`, `vanthoff-1887-osmotic-pressure` | `paperCitesOrAsserts` (`{ paper, anchor, note }`) with the section anchor of the printed passage |
| Q4 | Publication dates and citations for Svedberg (1906) and Henri (1908) | no shelf card (both are later) | timeline entries owned by `am-disc-timeline-xzef`, reported with `br comments add` |
| Q5 | Whether C. Wiener (1863) and Delsaulx with Carbonelle (from 1877) can be cited from their originals, and what each actually claims | candidate new cards | new cards with full records, or the item is narrowed to "not added" with the reason |
| Q6 | The ultramicroscope's demonstration date (the plan says 1902) beside its publication, Ann. Phys. (4) 10 (1903) 1 | `siedentopf-1903-ultramicroscope` | `date.earliest` for the demonstration and `date.latest` for the publication, with the reconciliation in `limits`; already reconciled in the card text and confirmed against the scan |
| Q7 | Brown's observations of 1827 and their 1828 publication, confirmed on the printed title and text | `brown-1828-microscopical-observations` | `date.earliest` 1827, `date.latest` 1828, `latestYear` 1828; already stated in the card text and confirmed against the scan |

Resolving a queue item follows the card rules: read the scan page, never run OCR locally (AGENTS.md), record volume, pages, and dates exactly as printed, and file every difference from the plan's research queue in `verification.discrepancies` and with `br comments add`. `verifierKind: agent` is admissible with a checkable `evidenceLocator`; it never substitutes for the human knowledge-boundary review recorded in `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`.

## Technical Approach

- Read the compiled content for the cards the slice created, and reuse their ids and verification records; complete the missing cards under the same id convention. If this bead lands before the slice authors its cards, the slice reuses these records (`br comments add am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias` with the ids).
- Open the queue with all seven items and close them as the originals are consulted.
- Resolve every candidate citation, especially Nägeli's publication details and the documentary record of Sutherland's Dunedin presentation; record volume, pages, and dates exactly as printed.
- Where an original contradicts the plan's date or proposition, correct the card, record the difference in `verification.discrepancies`, and raise it with `br comments add`.
- Assign `admittedStages` from the Journey II record's stage ids (the slice allocates the first set and `am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u` extends them); until those ids exist, list the intended stages by name (the observable, Route A osmotic pressure, Route A configuration integral, Fork A, drag, Route B, Fork B, the world check, the inversion, the physician's door).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Thirteen verified records exist with every standard field; no candidate citation remains unverified; the two Sutherland cards are separate, and the 1905 card has status `parallel-work`.
- [ ] Every `available` card has `latestYear` of 1904 or earlier; the equipartition card's `latestYear` matches its latest cited source.
- [ ] No card the slice already created is duplicated, and no existing `verification` record is rewritten by a re-check that found nothing; a re-check is recorded as a `history` review record, and a re-check that found a difference updates the card and lists the difference in `discrepancies`.
- [ ] Every queue item is `resolved` or `narrowed` before the Brownian paper is published; a card with an open queue item carries no verification record, so the production-profile publication gate fails if it is cited.
- [ ] No Journey II stage cites the 1905 Sutherland card without the acknowledged parallel-work flag (compiler-enforced).
- [ ] The ultramicroscope card records the 1902 demonstration and the 1903 publication separately, and the Brown card records observation in 1827 and publication in 1828, each confirmed against the scan.
- [ ] The paper's own citations are recorded only where verified on the facsimile, each with its section anchor.
- [ ] Later items are recorded for the timeline and margin and are not attached to any shelf stage; Svedberg's and Henri's dates are reported to `am-disc-timeline-xzef`.
- [ ] The shelf audit (`audit-shelf.ts`) and the anachronism lint pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/historical-premises/brownian/brownianShelf.test.ts`, against the real schemas and validators: schema validity for every record; `latestYear` rules per status; the 1905 Sutherland card is `parallel-work`; every record has a verification record with a non-empty `evidenceLocator` and `printedCitation`; ids match `<first-author>-<year>-<topic>`; no "Langevin," "Wiener process," "photon," or "spacetime" in card text outside labeled later-lens fields; the Nägeli and Exner cards contain none of a short list of evaluative words ("wrong," "mistaken," "naive," "foolish," "error"); the equipartition card states that the named constant $k$ is Planck's later notation.
- `content/historical-premises/brownian/sliceReuse.test.ts`, over the compiled corpus: every card id the slice cites exists exactly once; each such card's `verification` record is byte-identical to the one the slice committed unless the card carries a `discrepancies` entry dated by this bead; a fixture in which this bead rewrites an unchanged verification record fails with the card id and the repair; a fixture re-check recorded as a `history` review record with a `history-reviewer` passes, and one recorded by the card's own `verifiedBy` id fails the self-review check of `am-edit-review-records-hofz`.
- `content/historical-premises/brownian/verificationQueue.test.ts`: the queue file validates; every `cards[]` entry resolves; a card with an `open` queue item and a `verification` record fails, naming the card, the queue item, and the repair; a `narrowed` item requires a non-empty explanation.
- Compiler integration with the real card rules and epistemic checks: a fixture stage citing `sutherland-1905-phil-mag` without acknowledgment is rejected, and accepted with it; a fixture stage citing a later item (for example a Perrin card) is rejected; a production-profile build citing a card without a verification record fails the publication gate and passes once the record is present.
- Duplicate check: attempting to add a second Brown card with the same citation key and proposition is rejected with the merge suggestion (card rule 8).

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-ii-shelf.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`) once `/discover/brownian-motion` renders the shelf: open the shelf; confirm date order and status labels; open both Sutherland cards and the Brown card's "What the paper itself cites or asserts" section; open a card's verification summary and read the verifier, method, and locator; follow a "Where this site uses it" backlink to a slice stage and return; repeat with JavaScript disabled, at 320 px, and in the print lane.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-ii-shelf/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `cardId`, `latestYear`, `status`, `verified`, `verifierKind`, `citation`, `reusedFromSlice`, `reviewRecordId`, `queueItem`, `queueStatus`, `discrepancyCount`, `buildProfile`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log; a failing validator run retains the offending record path and the diagnostic under `artifacts/test-logs/journey-ii-shelf/<log-run-id>/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The Nägeli and Exner cards state what they claimed, fairly. The failure is shown in the worked forks, not by editorializing on the card.
- Do not imply that Bachelier influenced Einstein; there is no evidence.
- Keep Gouy's proposal distinct from a quantitative theory.
- Keep the 1906 paper's explicit velocity discussion off the 1904 shelf.
- Re-verifying a card is not the same as re-recording it. A second identical check adds a review record; it never bumps the card and never stales the slice's tests.
- Checking a citation means looking at the scan page; never run OCR locally.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: card schema, validators, publication gate, and rendering; it also registers the verification-queue record shape.
- `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2`: card text is linted for unlabeled anachronisms.

`am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias` shares the card records, ids, and verification records with this bead without a dependency in either direction, because either bead may land first.

Unblocks:
- `am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u`: the complete Journey II chain cites these cards.
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`: the Brownian definition of done requires every shelf card dated and sourced.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the desk's premise catalogue lists every shelf card.

title: Build Journey III: the measurement procedure, both forks, the move, electrodynamics, checks, and exercises
description:
# Build Journey III: the measurement procedure, both forks, the move, electrodynamics, checks, and exercises

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-g · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §9.1, §9.4, §8.3, §5.3, §5.4, §7.2, §7.3, §14.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey III: **how could you stop assuming that everyone shares the same time?** It is the journey most exposed to hindsight. By the end of 1904 Lorentz had the transformation mathematics, and Poincaré had discussed the conventionality of simultaneity, described light-signal synchronization, and named the principle of relativity. The journey shows what was on the table, what a reader who took both postulates physically would do differently, and why the ether program is treated fairly: it reproduces the formulas and is not declared refuted by the kinematics alone. The journey covers both halves of the paper; a train animation plus a Lorentz matrix is not a complete treatment.

The journey is labeled "A route you could take." Its world checks are honest about what they can and cannot discriminate: aberration and Fizeau's coefficient were already explained within ether theories, and the later confirmations test predictions that Lorentz's completed theory and Einstein's kinematics share.

The journey record also carries the one sentence that states its move for readers with no physics background (`move.r0Summary`). The fifteen-minute relativity tour (`am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`, step 9) renders it verbatim by journey id and authors no copy of its own, so the sentence must be true at R0, describe the move this journey marks, and contain no mathematics or symbols.

## Scope

In scope: the complete Journey III record `content/arguments/journeys/special-relativity.yaml` for `/discover/special-relativity`, including the marked move and its `move.r0Summary`.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): shelf cards (`am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q`); instruments SR-01 to SR-13; shelf instruments (`am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`); datasets; the no-algebra entrance (`am-srk-first-encounter-471z`); placing the predict-perturb-explain task at the end of the reading chapter (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`, which references this record); the framework, the move-summary schema, and its guard (`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`); the `physics-math` review that makes the summary `reviewed` (a named physics reviewer, through the paper's physics review `am-sr-review-physics-omj8`).

## Requirements

**The nagging fact (SR-02 in apparatus mode).** "Nature does not care whether the magnet or the coil moves; the theory does." SR-02 shows the two classical descriptions of the same relative motion producing the same current to first order in $v/c$, one through an electric field that carries energy and one through an electromotive force with no corresponding energy.

**The first honest question.** "What if the principle of relativity is exactly true for electrodynamics too, and the speed of light is the same for every observer, and I follow both wherever they lead?"

### The chain

Preset, mode, and tape ids below are cited exactly as the instrument beads register them.

- **Two postulates and nothing else.** No ether, no electron model, no contraction hypothesis.
- **Make a measurement procedure (SR-01).** What does "at the same time" mean for two clocks a kilometer apart? Only light can carry the comparison. Adopt the convention Poincaré had discussed (1898) and described operationally with light signals (1900); the paper cites no one. Bounce a signal and assume equal travel times, $t_B - t_A = t'_A - t_B$. Keep an event ledger; distinguish an event from its reception. The no-algebra entrance (a signal leaves at 0, returns at 10, and the reflection is assigned 5, a stated convention rather than a measurement of an unknowable one-way time) is this stage in arithmetic.
- **Make the ordinary assumption explicit (SR-04's Galilean shelf step, preset `sr-04-galilean-shelf`, and the wave-equation shelf instrument `shelf-maxwell-galilean` at preset `shelf-maxwell-galilean-1904`, mode `shelf-maxwell-galilean:1904`).** Test $x' = x - vt$, $t' = t$ on slow objects (it works: an observer at 30 m/s assigns $-20$ m/s to an object at 10 m/s, and the relative deviation from the relativistic result is $3.338\times10^{-15}$) and on light, $x = \pm ct$ (it does not preserve the light speed: $0.4c$ and $1.6c$ at $v = 0.6c$). Substituting into the wave equation makes a term appear. In 1904 terms the tension is that the ether theory predicts exactly those speeds while the ether-drift experiments found none of their consequences; the conflict is between stated commitments, and the reader decides what to reconsider.
- **Watch simultaneity slip (SR-03).** Two events simultaneous in one frame are not simultaneous in another, by an amount proportional to their separation and to $v$: clocks synchronized in their own frame and separated by proper distance $L$ are out of step by $vL/c^2$ in the platform frame. Lorentz had this mathematics and did not take it physically: he kept a true time and treated the other as local. The margin cites Lorentz's own later acknowledgment (*The Theory of Electrons*, 2nd ed., 1916; verified through queue item Q8 of `am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q` and recorded by `am-sr-margin-entries-tn4l`) and presents historians' assessments of how far Poincaré's 1900 and 1904 views departed from Lorentz's, with citations, rather than asserting a verdict.
- **Fork A (after simultaneity).**
  - (a) *Lorentz 1904:* keep the ether and the true time; the transformation is a calculational device. Worked: it produces the same formulas, and the page says so. It accounts for each null result through compensating effects rather than making undetectability a principle; that is an interpretive difference, not a failed prediction. Outcome `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted`, scope note: "for the kinematic and optical predictions compared here, with the completions of Poincaré's June 1905 note (parallel work)." Proponent card `lorentz-1904-transformation`.
  - (b) No privileged frame: every frame's clocks are as real as every other's. Outcome `papers-route`.
- **The move, side door (SR-04).** Construct the map from the postulates: begin with $x' = a(v)(x - vt)$, $t' = b(v)t + d(v)x$; requiring both light directions to stay $x' = \pm ct'$ gives $b = a$ and $d = -av/c^2$; applying the inverse gives $a(v)a(-v)(1 - v^2/c^2) = 1$; isotropy gives $a(v) = a(-v)$; the positive branch connected to the identity gives $a = \gamma$. Complete the transverse step honestly instead of copying $y' = y$. Read the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\gamma & -\gamma v\\ -\gamma v/c^2 & \gamma\end{pmatrix}$: determinant 1, eigenvectors on the light lines, eigenvalues $\sqrt{(1 \mp v/c)/(1 \pm v/c)}$; rapidity appears only as a labeled later aid. Mark the construction as **the move**. Interval preservation may verify the result only as a `modern-oracle` edge, never as a premise.
- **The front door.** Einstein's §3 reaches the same map with a functional equation for $\tau$ and the synchronization condition; the reading face walks it with every step shown, in his notation ($\tau = \beta(t - vx/V^2)$, $\xi = \beta(x - vt)$, with his $\beta$ being the modern $\gamma$).
- **Read the consequences off the map (SR-03, SR-05, SR-06).** Rods, clocks, velocity composition, and nothing faster than $c$. The difference between an event separation and a rod measurement: at $v = 0.6c$, two events 10 light-seconds apart and simultaneous in the unprimed frame have $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds, which is not a rod length because the events are not simultaneous in the primed frame.
- **Fork B: now the electrodynamics.**
  - (a) Maxwell's equations hold exactly only in the ether frame and merely appear to hold elsewhere, with the magnet-and-coil case explained by two mechanisms. Worked: the predicted current agrees with observation, and the page says so. Outcome `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted`, scope note: "the same current for the magnet-and-conductor case to first order in $v/c$, the precision of the observations" (consistent with SR-02).
  - (b) The equations keep their exact form in every frame provided $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ mix under a boost (SR-07, SR-08). The asymmetry disappears. In the magnet's rest frame there is no electric field, and the moving coil's charges feel the magnetic force $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$, which is the "electromotive force"; in the coil's rest frame the same effect is an electric field, $\mathbf{E}' = \gamma\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$ for a field perpendicular to the motion (SR-08). The two descriptions predict the same current to first order in $v/c$. Outcome `papers-route`. The page states that the preference for (b) in the paper's introduction rests on removing an asymmetry "not inherent in the phenomena," not on a failed prediction of (a).
- **Transform a wave and a light complex (SR-09, SR-10, SR-11).** Doppler and aberration from the invariant phase; the energy of a light complex changes by the same factor as its frequency; the moving mirror. "File the energy result away for September" links to Journey IV's import card `einstein-1905-light-complex-energy`.
- **Charge, current, the electron (SR-12, SR-13).** A neutral current-carrying conductor is accepted. The historical force conventions are preserved: at $\beta = 0.6$ the source convention's transverse coefficient is $1.5625m$ and the laboratory one is $1.25m$, two definitions rather than two values of one mass.

### What each fork varies, and the fifth outcome

Each fork declares `varies` from the closed set of `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, and the renderer shows the value as one plain sentence above the branches.

- **Fork A declares `varies: proposed-explanation`.** Both branches keep the same transformation mathematics and the same null results, and they differ on what account to give of them: an ether with a true time beside a local time, against kinematics with no privileged frame. This fork is the framework's own example of the value. The reader's sentence: "This fork is about two accounts of the same observations, not about a disagreement over the mathematics or over what was measured."
- **Fork B declares `varies: proposed-explanation`.** Both branches predict the same current for the magnet and the conductor to first order in $v/c$, and they differ on whether Maxwell's equations hold exactly in one frame and merely appear to hold elsewhere, with two mechanisms for one observation, or keep their exact form in every frame with the fields mixing under a boost. The reader's sentence: "This fork is about two accounts of the same measured current, not about which quantity to measure."

Neither fork varies a measurement choice and neither branch uses `dead-end-on-constraint`, so `fork-measurement-choice-cannot-dead-end` has no application here. Both (a) branches keep `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted` with the scope notes already stated above, and each of those notes names the observable class within which the predictions agree, which is what a `scopeNote` must do and what "they agree here" would fail to do.

**The exhaustive case for `undecided-on-available-evidence`.** This journey's branches use `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted` and `papers-route`, and neither (a) branch is re-typed to the fifth outcome. The distinction matters more here than anywhere else on the site: both (a) branches really do make the same predictions within their stated scopes, which is a stronger claim than "the 1904 shelf cannot tell", and the later evidence this journey cites confirms predictions the two accounts share. Wherever this bead's content, branch copy or tests switch on `outcome.type`, the fifth value carries its own case rather than falling through: the per-outcome copy names it, and the record test walks all five values and ends in the framework's `const _exhaustive: never = type`, so a missing case is a typecheck failure rather than a blank branch. The case is exercised by a fixture branch carrying `insufficiency` and a `whatWouldDecide` that resolves to later evidence, never by leaving a shipped branch unworked, because the fifth outcome is not a place to hide a branch nobody worked out.

### The move's R0 summary (`move.r0Summary`)

- **Text** (authored here; editors may refine the wording through review, keeping every property below): "Instead of assuming that everyone shares one time, take two statements seriously at once, that the same laws hold for every observer in uniform motion and that light in empty space travels at one definite speed however its source moves, and then work out, from the way clocks are set with light signals, how one observer's description of where and when something happens turns into another observer's."
- **Properties that must survive any rewording:** one sentence; no mathematics and no symbols (the framework's guard); at most 100 words; both principles stated in ordinary words; the light-signal clock-setting procedure named, because it is what makes the construction possible; the result described as a change of description between observers, not as a discovery about the ether; no claim that the ether was disproved, that an experiment forced the paper, or that anything was proved; none of the later vocabulary the anachronism controls name ("spacetime," "Minkowski," "light cone," "train and embankment"); none of the fifteen-minute relativity tour's forbidden phrasings (`am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`).
- **Review state.** This bead records the summary as `reviewState: draft` and never sets `reviewed`. A named physics reviewer records a `physics-math` review record covering the journey record's revision; only then may `reviewed` be set, which the review-status check of `am-edit-review-records-hofz` verifies. Until then the production and preview builds of the fifteen-minute relativity tour fail `tour-move-summary-missing`, by design, and the draft build shows the framework's "Draft summary, not yet reviewed" marker.

### Check it against the world

- **Aberration (SR-09, computed live).** Loaded from SR-09's preset `sr-09-earth-orbit-aberration` (Earth's mean orbital speed 29.789 km/s, $\beta \approx 9.9365\times10^{-5}$), the accepted snapshot gives 20.4956 arcseconds, displayed as 20.50 arcseconds with SR-09's "modern computation" label. Bradley's own figures are read from card `bradley-1729-aberration`: his printed ratio of about 10,210 to 1 implies about 20.2022 arcseconds, computed by the owner from the transcribed ratio, never stored as a number on the card, and shown as "awaiting verification" with no number until that card carries its verification record. The difference of about 1.5 percent is presented as the difference between a 1729 measurement and a modern computation, with neither called an error. The first-order effect follows from the phase transformation, and it also followed from the ether theories; the check shows consistency, not discrimination.
- **Fizeau (SR-06, computed live).** The low-speed limit of velocity composition gives the drag coefficient $1 - 1/n^2 = 0.43722$ for water ($n = 1.333$), compared with the Fizeau 1851 dataset (an 1851 measurement on the shelf). The kinematic derivation is Laue's (1907, labeled later); Fresnel's ether theory also gave the coefficient, so again this is consistency, not discrimination.
- **Later evidence (dated, labeled later, from timeline cards and datasets):** Kaufmann's electron deflections were ambiguous in 1905–1906; Bucherer (1908) favored the Lorentz–Einstein prediction over Abraham's; Ives–Stilwell (1938), muon lifetimes (1941), flown clocks (1971, published 1972), and satellite clocks are dated on the timeline, not claimed for 1905. The page states that these confirm predictions shared by Lorentz's completed theory and Einstein's kinematics; they do not refute Fork A's branch (a).
- Without JavaScript, each computed check shows its build-time static worked example, labeled as such with its constant set.

### What Einstein actually wrote

Jumps to paper 3 §1 (simultaneity), §3 (the transformation), §6 (the field transformation and the magnet-conductor reconciliation), §7 (Doppler and aberration), and §8 (light energy), each lighting its named weave predicate from the carried instrument state, or showing the static pointer without it.

### Doors

- **Front door:** §§1–3, the synchronization definition and the functional equation.
- **Side door, linear algebra:** the SR-04 construction.
- **Side door, arithmetic:** the 0, 10, 5 signal ledger (`am-srk-first-encounter-471z`), continuing into the measurement procedure and the construction.
- All doors arrive at the same equation id, the §3 transformation, and the page says so.

### Exercises

Instrumented (four; the framework requires two to five):
1. **Verify the determinant and eigenvectors by hand** (numeric: determinant 1; at $\beta = 0.6$ eigenvalues 2 and 0.5; references from `kinematics.ts`).
2. **Two collinear boosts give a boost; say what happens for non-collinear ones** (numeric: $0.6c$ then $0.6c$ gives $15c/17 \approx 0.8824c$; numeric: successive perpendicular boosts of $0.6c$ give a speed of $0.768375c$ with a rotation of $12.6804°$; explanation part: non-collinear composition includes a rotation).
3. **Derive the desynchronization $vL/c^2$** (expression equivalence, with declared variables $v$, $L$, $c$ and the stated sign convention that the rear clock leads).
4. **The speed at which a clock loses one second per day** (numeric: $1 - \sqrt{1-\beta^2} = 1/86\,400$ gives $\beta = \sqrt{\varepsilon(2-\varepsilon)} \approx 4.811238\times10^{-3}$ with $\varepsilon = 1/86\,400$, about $1.442373\times10^{6}$ m/s; the reference uses the cancellation-free form).

Explanation item (one):
5. Explain the magnet-and-coil asymmetry in three sentences without the word ether. The constraint is part of the prompt and of the comparison criteria for the reader's own check; no code inspects the reader's text.

### The predict-perturb-explain task (`ppeTask`)

- **Prompt:** "Two transformed events have a larger spatial separation; why is that alone not a rod measurement?"
- **Predict:** the reader chooses whether the 12.5 light-second separation is the rod's length in the primed frame (yes; no; it depends on which events are chosen), stored locally and never scored.
- **Perturb:** in SR-03, change the observer speed (an `observer-change` that preserves the run and events) and then select endpoint events that are simultaneous in the primed frame, through the instrument's action contract.
- **Explain:** an explanation part with comparison criteria (a rod length needs endpoint positions recorded at the same time in the frame doing the measuring; the original events are not simultaneous in the primed frame; choosing simultaneous endpoints gives the contracted length).
- `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7` places this same record at the end of the relativity §§3–5 reading chapter.

**Added in review (relativity alignment of embedded instruments).**
- **Nagging fact.** The stage embeds SR-02 through preset `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact` (mode `sr-02:apparatus`, resolution withheld). It shows the two classical descriptions of the same relative motion; the §6 resolution caption sits in a closed native disclosure the reader may always open, so the stage never reveals the 1905 resolution by default.
- **Arithmetic side door.** The door embeds the no-algebra entrance by record id `entrance-special-relativity` from `am-srk-first-encounter-471z`, with host `returnTo` and `continueTo` targets (`continueTo` is the measurement-procedure stage). The door record keeps lens `arithmetic`, its entry and summary, and `arrivesAt` equal to the §3 transformation equation id.
- **Aberration world check.** The value comes from SR-09's accepted snapshot of `sr-09-earth-orbit-aberration`, never from a separate calculation here, so the journey and the instrument show one snapshot; Bradley's figures come from the card, in whatever verification state it is in.
- **Michelson–Morley on the shelf.** Where the journey names the 1887 null result, the printed bound is read from card `michelson-1887-null-result`, which the shelf bead transcribes; neither this record nor the shelf instrument retypes it.

## Technical Approach

- Author the journey record referencing shelf cards; SR-01 to SR-13 presets and teaching tapes (the named teaching tape `the-boost-to-0.6c`, authored by `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`); `shelf-maxwell-galilean` at `shelf-maxwell-galilean-1904` and SR-04 at `sr-04-galilean-shelf`; derivation-chain step ids with the SR-04 construction marked as the move and `isMove: true` on that step (from `am-srk-equations-30cq`); weave predicates; exercises; the predict-perturb-explain task; the door equation id; the move's `r0Summary` with `reviewState: draft`.
- The aberration and Fizeau checks bind exact quantity ids from SR-09 and SR-06 accepted snapshots and cite the dated card and dataset. No numeric literal appears in a prediction field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The nagging fact opens `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact` with the resolution withheld, the arithmetic door embeds `entrance-special-relativity` with working `returnTo` and `continueTo`, and the aberration check shows SR-09's snapshot identity beside the Bradley card's state.
- [ ] `move.r0Summary` is present, passes the framework's guard, states both principles and the light-signal procedure in ordinary words, claims no disproof of the ether and no proof, and is committed with `reviewState: draft`.
- [ ] Fork B (b) assigns the frames correctly: in the magnet's rest frame the coil's charges feel $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$ with no electric field, and in the coil's rest frame the effect is the electric field $\mathbf{E}' = \gamma\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; a copy test fails on the reversed assignment.
- [ ] The journey validates as `complete` with every skeleton element.
- [ ] Fork A (a) and Fork B (a) are labeled empirically equivalent within their stated scopes and not refuted; neither is phrased as a failure.
- [ ] Both forks declare `varies: proposed-explanation` and render the reader's plain sentence above their branches, neither (a) branch is re-typed to `undecided-on-available-evidence`, and this bead's outcome handling carries an exercised case for the fifth outcome.
- [ ] The SR-04 construction is marked as the move and includes the scale-factor and transverse steps; interval preservation appears only as a verification oracle.
- [ ] The 10 light-second event pair is presented as not a rod measurement.
- [ ] Aberration and Fizeau checks are computed live and framed as consistency checks; later evidence is dated and framed as shared by both accounts; the Bradley comparison never carries a number while its card is unverified.
- [ ] All three doors end at the same equation id; four instrumented exercises, one explanation item, and the predict-perturb-explain task work.
- [ ] Spacetime diagrams and rapidity appear only as labeled later aids; the nagging fact embeds SR-02.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/arguments/journeys/specialRelativity.test.ts`, with the real compiler, framework checks, `kinematics.ts`, `events.ts`, and `waves.ts`: validation as `complete`; outcome types and scope notes; door equation ids; exercise roles and counts; every cited preset, mode, and tape id resolves through the registry (`sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact`, `sr-04-galilean-shelf`, `shelf-maxwell-galilean-1904`, `sr-09-earth-orbit-aberration`, `the-boost-to-0.6c`); references: determinant 1; eigenvalues 2 and 0.5 at $\beta = 0.6$; $15/17 = 0.8823529$; the perpendicular composition speed $0.7683749c$ and rotation $12.68038°$; $\beta = 4.811238\times10^{-3}$ and $v = 1.442373\times10^{6}$ m/s (relative $10^{-6}$) from the cancellation-free form; the 10 light-second fixture ($\Delta t' = -7.5$ s, $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds); the SR-04 shelf step's slow case ($-20$ m/s with relative deviation $3.338\times10^{-15}$) and light rays ($0.4c$, $1.6c$).
- `moveSummary.relativity.test.ts`: the summary passes `moveSummaryGuard` (one sentence, no math delimiters, no listed characters, no Greek letter, no lone symbol letter, at most 100 words, logged); the fifteen-minute tour's `symbolScan` with the relativity notation concordance finds no symbol label (none of "c", "V", "γ", "β", "τ", "ξ", or a primed letter); it contains "uniform motion" and "light signals"; it contains none of "spacetime", "Minkowski", "light cone", "ether was disproved", "proved", "proves", "Michelson"; `reviewState` is `draft` in the committed record unless a covering `physics-math` review record exists (checked through the real review-status check of `am-edit-review-records-hofz`).
- `forkContract.relativity.test.ts`, against the real schema and this journey's record: both forks declare `varies: proposed-explanation`; a missing `varies` fails with `fork-varies-missing` naming the fork id; each `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted` branch carries a `scopeNote` that names an observable class, and a fixture note reading "they agree here" fails; a walk over all five `outcome.type` values compiles with no default arm; and a fixture branch typed `undecided-on-available-evidence` passes only with `insufficiency` and a `whatWouldDecide` resolving to a dated item after 1904, and fails with `fork-undecided-already-decidable` when it names a card already on this journey's shelf.
- `worldChecks.relativity.test.ts`: aberration 20.4956 arcseconds from preset `sr-09-earth-orbit-aberration` ($v = 29.789$ km/s, relative $10^{-4}$), displayed 20.50 and labeled a modern computation, never presented as Bradley's value; the Bradley row reads card `bradley-1729-aberration` and renders "awaiting verification" with no number for an unverified fixture card, and 20.2022 arcseconds computed from a verified fixture card's 10,210 ratio (relative $10^{-9}$), which changes when the fixture's ratio changes; Fizeau coefficient 0.43722 for $n = 1.333$; transverse coefficients $1.5625m$ and $1.25m$ at $\beta = 0.6$.
- `copy.relativity.test.ts`: no evaluative words in Fork A (a) or Fork B (a) copy; the later-evidence text contains the shared-predictions statement; the forbidden phrases of the framework's copy guard 8 are absent from every field, the move summary included.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-iii.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`): walk every stage; operate SR-02 at the nagging fact; take both branches of both forks; construct the move and read the move marker with its summary (with the draft marker in a draft build and absent in a production build); confirm that an observer change inside SR-03 does not restart its run; follow each source jump and return; enter through the arithmetic door and reach the same equation; answer exercises 1 and 3; complete the predict-perturb-explain task and reload; lanes keyboard only, 320 px, reduced motion, no WebGL, JavaScript disabled, WebKit.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-iii/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `journeyId`, `stageId`, `forkId`, `branchId`, `varies`, `outcomeType`, `doorId`, `instrumentId`, `presetId`, `modeId`, `tapeId`, `instanceId`, `snapshotVersion`, `commandClass`, `quantityId`, `cardId`, `cardVerified`, `moveSummaryReviewState`, `moveSummaryWordCount`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `constantSetId`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `buildProfile`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never frame Lorentz or Poincaré as foolish; the fork outcomes and scope notes carry the nuance.
- Michelson–Morley is on the shelf, not presented as the documented sole cause of the paper.
- Contraction is not what a camera sees; optical appearance is a separate later deep dive.
- A consistency check is not a discriminating test; say which one each check is.
- The move summary is the sentence a reader with no physics background will repeat after a fifteen-minute tour. Keeping "light signals" in it prevents the tour from sounding like a claim that the ether was disproved by an experiment.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q`: verified cards, including the Bradley and Michelson–Morley transcriptions the checks read.
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: skeleton, route, and the move-summary schema and guard.

- `am-sr-01-clock-sync-jbfn`, `am-sr-02-magnet-conductor-x1gc`, `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`, `am-sr-04-lorentz-map-px1k`, `am-sr-05-moving-clocks-2zka`, `am-sr-06-velocity-composition-7ni4`, `am-sr-07-field-equations-xxes`, `am-sr-08-field-frame-change-5ibt`, `am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd`, `am-sr-10-light-complex-kek0`, `am-sr-11-moving-mirror-wnz1`, `am-sr-12-charge-current-bgq0`, `am-sr-13-electron-dynamics-b6v7`: the stages' instruments, including SR-02 at the nagging fact.
- `am-srk-first-encounter-471z`: the arithmetic side door's entrance record.

Unblocks:
- `am-dod-relativity-105y`: the paper's definition of done requires the journey.
- `am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`: step 9 renders this record's `move.r0Summary`.
- `am-sr-review-physics-omj8`: the relativity physics review records the `physics-math` review of this record, including the move summary.
- `am-ver-no-circularity-final-i9qn`: the final circularity audit covers this journey.
- `am-disc-cross-journey-exercises-j53n`, `am-tour-evening-and-course-5kcb`, `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`.
