title: Author the word-level interlinear gloss for the whole mass-energy paper
description:
# Author the word-level interlinear gloss for the whole mass-energy paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** D · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.8, §6.9, §7.11, §11.2 (`GlossUnit`), §17.7 item 2, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

The `gloss` face renders each German sentence with a word-by-word English gloss beneath it. It serves three audiences at once:
- readers who want to read Einstein in his own language with support;
- German learners, for whom a three-page physics paper is a fine first text;
- readers whose first language is neither German nor English, for whom the gloss plus the one-breath overview (R0) is the most direct route.

The plan orders the work: paper 4 in full first, then the introductions and key sections of the other papers. The gloss face for paper 4 is a P1 delivery in the innovation sequence, and the per-paper definition of done requires "gloss units for the required sections" (the complete gloss for this paper). The same alignment infrastructure later admits reviewed editions in other languages, so glosses are keyed to stable alignable unit ids, never to positions.

This is the first gloss, so it also writes the conventions every later gloss follows. Without shared conventions, the same grammatical construction would receive different notes in different papers, and the consistency checks could not work.

The record shape is the landed `GlossUnit` of `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`. The note-class table this bead writes is a build input as well as documentation: `src/content/schemas/glossConventions.ts` reads it to decide which note classes the schema accepts, so a class that is not in the table fails the build.

## Scope

In scope:
- `GlossUnit` records in `content/glosses/mass-energy/` (`masthead.yaml`, `s0.yaml`, `closing.yaml`) for every alignable unit of the paper: every sentence of the `s0` paragraphs, and the block-level units `masthead-title`, `masthead-author`, each footnote `s0-fn<k>`, `closing-dateline`, and `closing-received`, each glossed as one unit whose `sentenceId` is its block id.
- `docs/editorial/GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md`: the shared gloss conventions, including the note-class table read at build time (owned here; later gloss beads extend it only with reviewed additions listed in its change log).
- Glossator and editor authorship entries, revisions, and review states.

Out of scope:
- the running English translation (`am-edn-translation-mass-energy-f3b`);
- the `GlossUnit` schema and the note-class table reader `src/content/schemas/glossConventions.ts` (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`);
- the tokenizer and gloss validation (`am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`);
- rendering (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`);
- the foundation lesson on reading a German physics sentence (`am-found-reading-german-u8oc`);
- glosses of other papers (`am-edn-gloss-brownian-or6t`, `am-edn-gloss-relativity-na8d`, `am-edn-gloss-light-quanta-ggj1`);
- the German source review, which includes this gloss (`am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`).

## Requirements

### Gloss conventions (`docs/editorial/GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md`)

1. **Units and tokens.**
   - A gloss unit's `sentenceId` is any alignable unit id of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`: a paragraph sentence, or a block-level unit (a heading `s<n>`, a part heading, a masthead unit, a footnote `s<n>-fn<k>`, a closing) glossed as one unit.
   - Tokens are exactly the output of `tokenizeGerman` from `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`, following the token rules in `docs/editorial/SEGMENTATION.md`.
   - Mathematics atoms, display references, footnote marks, and punctuation are never tokens and are never glossed.
   - Token indices are 0-based among word tokens.
2. **Per token** (the landed `GlossUnit` token shape):
   - `german`: the surface form as printed;
   - `english`: the contextual English sense, authored from the German and never copied from any translation; present exactly when the token does not belong to a multiword unit, because a token inside a unit carries no gloss of its own;
   - optional `lemma`;
   - optional `grammarNote`, with `noteClass` required whenever a `grammarNote` is present;
   - optional `contextual: true`, which requires a `reason` and exempts the token from the consistency rule below.
3. **Note classes.** Each class has a kebab-case name, a canonical short wording, and an example. The table in this file is the single source of accepted classes: `src/content/schemas/glossConventions.ts` reads it at build time, so the table keeps the format that reader parses, and the schema rejects a class outside it. The table starts with the twelve classes that the schema also accepts until this file exists:

   | Class | Example |
   |---|---|
   | `konjunktiv-i` | *sei* and other hypothesis or definition forms, as in "es befinde sich" |
   | `konjunktiv-ii` | |
   | `separable-verb` | |
   | `genitive-construction` | |
   | `compound` | with a decomposition, for example *Energieinhalt* = *Energie* + *Inhalt* |
   | `attributive-phrase` | a long attributive phrase before its noun |
   | `formula-phrase` | *es gilt*, *man erhält*, *setzen wir*, *wir denken uns* |
   | `archaic-spelling` | *daß* |
   | `abbreviation` | *a. a. O.*, *z. B.* |
   | `ordinal` | |
   | `unit` | |
   | `term` | a token covered by a `term` inline |

   Five further classes mark epistemic and logical force. They are part of the same single source of accepted classes, and they exist because the gloss face is the only place a reader can watch the edition's modality rule hold, with the German word and the English sense side by side:

   | Class | What it marks | German forms to verify on the edition |
   |---|---|---|
   | `hedge` | A qualified or tentative claim | *etwa*, *wohl*, *vermutlich*, *angenähert* |
   | `necessity` | A claim asserted as required | *muß* (as printed), *notwendig* |
   | `condition` | A premise being assumed | *wenn*, *falls*, *vorausgesetzt* |
   | `consequence` | A step asserted to follow | *folgt*, *ergibt sich*, *also*, *daher* |
   | `restriction` | A limit placed on a conclusion | *nur*, *soweit*, *in erster Näherung* |

   The two tables together hold seventeen classes: the twelve above and these five.

   **`modalityClasses`.** The file also carries a `modalityClasses` list naming the subset of note classes that mark epistemic and logical force: `konjunktiv-i`, `konjunktiv-ii`, `hedge`, `necessity`, `condition`, `consequence`, and `restriction`. `src/content/schemas/glossConventions.ts` parses it beside the note-class table, in the same format that reader already expects, and `am-read-gloss-face-lp2` reads the list through that reader and keeps no copy of its own. A name in `modalityClasses` that is absent from the tables fails the build, naming both the list and the table.

   The German forms in both tables are forms to look for, never a matcher. No form is assumed to be printed, and only an authored `noteClass` ever marks a token: *also* is a consequence marker in one sentence and a filler in another, so a surface-form lexicon would teach a reader that Einstein asserted a step he did not. This bead records in its verification log which of these forms the mass-energy paper actually prints and which it does not, and each later gloss bead records the same for its own paper.

   New classes are added only by a reviewed edit to this file, recorded in its change log with the editor and the date.
4. **Multiword units** gloss a separable verb, a fixed phrase, a reflexive construction, or a split verbal construction as one unit.
   - Each unit carries `tokenIndices` (at least two distinct indices in ascending order, possibly non-contiguous for a separated prefix verb), one `english` gloss, a `kind` (`separable-verb`, `fixed-phrase`, `reflexive`, `split-construction`), and an optional `grammarNote` with its `noteClass`.
   - Every index names an existing token, no token belongs to two units, and every part is marked, so the gloss face can show both halves of a separated prefix verb.
5. **Consistency.** Identical `lemma` plus identical `noteClass` receive identical `english` glosses across the corpus, unless the token sets `contextual: true` with a `reason`.
6. **Terms.** A token covered by a `term` inline is glossed in the sense of that occurrence's definition and carries `noteClass: term` with the class's canonical wording as its `grammarNote`. Every occurrence of the same term lemma receives the same gloss unless `contextual` is set with a reason.
7. **Literalness.** A gloss is word-level and literal enough to show the German structure. It is not a translation, and notes are short and grammatical, never interpretive.
8. **Metadata.** Each unit carries:
   - `revision`: a positive integer, increased on every change to the unit;
   - `lang: en` and `sourceLang: de`;
   - `attribution`: an authorship entry of `am-cm-schemas-source-1en` for the glossator, with `id` (for a human, the person's id in `docs/OWNERS.md`; for a model, the id of the agent or pipeline that ran it, never prefixed `model:`), optional `name`, `kind` (`human` or `model`), and `modelId`, required for a model;
   - `editor`: an authorship entry for the checking glossator, required once the unit is `corrected`, whose `id` differs from the glossator's;
   - `reviewState`: `machine-draft` (a model draft), `drafted` (a human draft), `corrected` (checked by the editor), or `reviewed` (only through an accepted `german-source` review record).

   `authorshipOf` maps `attribution` to `draftedBy` and `editor` to `editedBy`; the self-review check of `am-edit-review-records-hofz` compares the reviewer's id with both.

### Gloss units for this paper

- **Coverage.** Every word token of every alignable unit has an `english` gloss or belongs to a multiword unit that has one.
- **Constructions expected in this paper.** Konjunktiv I in the hypotheses ("es befinde sich", "sei"); the long attributive phrases; the compounds *Energieinhalt* and *Paralleltranslation*; the abbreviation *a. a. O.*; the archaic spelling *daß*; and the conditional *Wenn … so* in the closing remark.
- **Terms.** The glosses of *Trägheit*, *Energieinhalt*, *Lichtmenge*, and the other term tokens agree with the translation's occurrence definitions.
- **Review states.**
  - A second glossator or agent checks consistency against the conventions and the German, records itself in `editor`, and sets `corrected`.
  - `reviewed` is reachable only through an accepted `german-source` review record written by `am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`, which includes this gloss.

## Technical Approach

- Generate token skeletons from the German blocks with `tokenizeGerman`, then author glosses, notes, and multiword units in YAML in printed order.
- Write `GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md` before glossing, confirm that `glossConventions.ts` parses its note-class table, and refine the file once with the checking editor after the first pass.
- Run `bun scripts/align-editions.ts --paper mass-energy --layers gloss --report` until coverage is complete and no `gloss-stale` or consistency failure remains.
- The checking editor sets `corrected`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md` defines the unit and token sources, per-token fields, every note class with its canonical wording in the table `glossConventions.ts` parses, multiword-unit kinds, consistency and `contextual` rules, term consistency, metadata, and review states, with a change log.
- [ ] Every word token of every alignable unit (sentences, masthead units, footnotes, and closings) has a gloss or a multiword unit; mathematics atoms and footnote marks are never glossed.
- [ ] Every note class used is in the conventions table; every `grammarNote` has a `noteClass`; every `contextual` flag has a reason; recurring constructions and term tokens are glossed consistently or carry `contextual`.
- [ ] Every unit carries `revision`, `lang: en`, `sourceLang: de`, an `attribution` authorship entry (with `modelId` for a model), an `editor` entry whose `id` differs from the glossator's, and review state; every unit is `corrected`, and none is `reviewed` without a record.
- [ ] `GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md` carries the five modality classes beside the twelve, and a `modalityClasses` list of the seven classes that mark epistemic and logical force, which `glossConventions.ts` parses and which fails the build when a name in it is absent from the tables.
- [ ] The verification log records, for every German form listed in the two note-class tables, whether the mass-energy paper prints it and where, so no form is assumed to occur and no token is marked except by an authored `noteClass`.
- [ ] Gloss coverage appears in the edition coverage report.
- [ ] The paper-4 gloss face renders these units at 320 px and without JavaScript.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

`src/content/editions/massEnergy.gloss.test.ts`, against the real schema, tokenizer, and harness:
- `assertEditionContract('mass-energy', { layers: ['german', 'translation', 'gloss'] })`, with each check logged.
- Every unit validates against the real `GlossUnit` schema, and its `sentenceId` resolves to an alignable unit of the paper; the footnote and closing units are present with block ids as `sentenceId`.
- Every unit's token list equals `tokenizeGerman` of its German unit.
- `english` is present on exactly the tokens outside multiword units.
- Every multiword unit has at least two valid, distinct `tokenIndices` in ascending order, one gloss, and a defined `kind`; no token belongs to two units.
- Every `grammarNote` carries a `noteClass`, every `contextual: true` carries a non-empty `reason`, and every `noteClass` used is accepted by `glossConventions.ts` reading the committed conventions file.
- **Consistency across the paper:** identical `lemma` plus `noteClass` have identical glosses unless `contextual` with a reason.
- **Term tokens:** every token under a `term` inline has `noteClass: term`, and all occurrences of a term lemma share one gloss or carry `contextual`.
- **Modality forms actually printed:** the suite writes one line per German form listed in the two note-class tables, with `check: "modality-forms-inventory"`, the form in `german`, its class in `noteClass`, and the `sentenceId` of a printed occurrence or an explicit absent result. The inventory covers every listed form, and a form this paper does not print is recorded as absent rather than assumed either way.
- **Authorship and review states:** `attribution` and `editor` validate as authorship entries (a model entry without `modelId` fails); every unit is `corrected` with `editor.id` different from `attribution.id`; `authorshipOf(unit)` returns the glossator in `draftedBy` and the editor in `editedBy`.
- **Live-harness canaries** (run-scoped copies under `artifacts/test-tmp/gloss-mass-energy/<log-run-id>/`, never deleted):
  - a unit with one token removed fails coverage;
  - a copy of a German block with one word changed makes its gloss unit fail `gloss-stale`;
  - two occurrences of *Trägheit* with different glosses and no `contextual` flag fail consistency;
  - a token inside a multiword unit that also carries its own `english` fails the schema;
  - `noteClass: subjunctive` (not in the table) fails the schema;
  - `glossConventions.ts` parses `modalityClasses` from the committed file and returns the seven names; a fixture conventions file listing `subjunctive` in `modalityClasses` fails with both the list and the table named, and a fixture with no `modalityClasses` list at all is reported rather than silently treated as empty;
  - a unit whose `editor` repeats the glossator's `id` fails the independent-check rule.

### End-to-end tests

- `bun scripts/e2e-edition-pipeline.ts --paper mass-energy --layers german,translation,gloss` runs in the gate chain. Required stages: `ledger` through `coverage`. `static-html` may be `not-available`. Evidence is retained under `artifacts/test-logs/edition-pipeline/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.
- **Browser smoke** through the harness of `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, on the face of `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`, with JSONL logs and screenshots, traces, DOM snapshots, and console logs retained on failure. Open `?view=gloss` for this paper:
  - in the desktop and 320-pixel lanes, and in the JavaScript-disabled lane;
  - every sentence and every footnote shows its gloss row;
  - a separable-verb or reflexive unit shows both marked parts with one shared gloss;
  - no page-level horizontal overflow;
  - the three sentence actions (German, glosses, English) work by keyboard.
- The full mass–energy journey, including the gloss face, belongs to `am-me-e2e-qbbm`.

### Structured logging

JSONL goes to `artifacts/test-logs/gloss-mass-energy/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library.
- Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y"`, `paper: "mass-energy"`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled` (browser smoke), `message`.
- `extra`: `{sentenceId, tokenIndex, german, noteClass, multiwordKind, glossatorId, editorId, check, evidencePath}`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A gloss is not a translation; keep it word-level and literal enough to show the German structure.
- Do not gloss symbols or formulas; the concordance explains them.
- Keep notes short and grammatical, never interpretive.
- The conventions written here bind three later glosses, and the note-class table is read by the build; spend the care now, and change them later only through a reviewed edit.
- Field names follow the landed `GlossUnit` schema of `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`; if the schema changes a field, the conventions file changes in the same reviewed edit.
- A display name is not an identity; the self-review check compares authorship ids.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-edn-translation-mass-energy-f3b`: the aligned sentences and term decisions the gloss must agree with.
- `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`: the face the browser smoke opens.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the browser harness and evidence capture for the smoke.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-gloss-brownian-or6t`, `am-edn-gloss-relativity-na8d`, `am-edn-gloss-light-quanta-ggj1`: the conventions established here carry over.
- `am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`: the German source review includes this gloss.
- `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`: the per-paper definition of done requires the complete gloss.
- `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`: the discovery book's German-reading support needs the glosses.

title: Author the interlinear gloss for the relativity introduction and key section
description:
# Author the interlinear gloss for the relativity introduction and key section

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** E · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.8, §6.9, §7.11, §11.2 (`GlossUnit`), §17.7 item 2 (traceability only)

## Background

The `gloss` face renders each German sentence with a word-by-word English gloss beneath it. It serves three audiences at once:
- readers who want to read Einstein in his own language with support;
- German learners;
- readers whose first language is neither German nor English, for whom the gloss plus the one-breath overview (R0) is the most direct route.

The plan orders the work: paper 4 in full first, then the introductions and key sections of the other papers. The per-paper definition of done requires "gloss units for the required sections," so each paper owns its own gloss bead; a single combined bead would have tied every paper's completion to the slowest one.

This bead covers `special-relativity`, following the conventions written by `am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y` in `docs/editorial/GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md`. The recommended set is the introduction and §1 (the definition of simultaneity). These are the passages readers most want to read in German, and they carry the paper's stipulations and presuppositions, where modality matters most. The editorial owner may choose a different key section, with the reason recorded.

The German source review of this paper (`am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`, Batch G) waits for this gloss (Batch E) and covers it, so every gloss unit reaches `reviewed` through that one human gate.

## Scope

In scope:
- `docs/editorial/special-relativity-gloss-scope.md`, written before glossing: the chosen sections, the reasons, and the editorial owner's name and date.
- `GlossUnit` records in `content/glosses/special-relativity/` (`s0.yaml` and the key section's file, for example `s1.yaml`) for every alignable unit in the chosen sections: the sentences, the key section's heading (`sentenceId` `s1`, and `part-1` when §1 is chosen), and the footnotes in those sections (`sentenceId` `s<n>-fn<k>`), each block-level unit glossed as one unit.
- Glossator and editor authorship entries, revisions, and review states.
- Reviewed additions to `docs/editorial/GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md`, if a construction needs a new note class. Each addition is confirmed by the checking editor, listed in the file's change log, and accepted by `src/content/schemas/glossConventions.ts` reading the table.

Out of scope:
- the running English translation (`am-edn-translation-relativity-s0-s5-hm8`);
- the `GlossUnit` schema and the note-class table reader (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`);
- the tokenizer and gloss validation (`am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`);
- rendering (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`);
- the foundation on reading a German physics sentence (`am-found-reading-german-u8oc`);
- the other papers' glosses;
- the human review of this gloss (`am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`).

## Requirements

1. **Conventions.** Follow `docs/editorial/GLOSS_CONVENTIONS.md` and the landed `GlossUnit` schema of `am-cm-schemas-source-1en` exactly:
   - `sentenceId` is any alignable unit id (a sentence, a heading or part heading, or a footnote);
   - tokens are the output of `tokenizeGerman`;
   - mathematics atoms, display references, footnote marks, and punctuation are never glossed;
   - per-token fields are `german`, `english` (authored from the German, never copied from any translation, and present exactly when the token is outside a multiword unit), optional `lemma`, optional `grammarNote` with a required `noteClass`, and optional `contextual: true` with a required `reason`;
   - multiword units (`tokenIndices` with at least two distinct ascending indices, one `english`, `kind`, optional `grammarNote` with `noteClass`) mark every part of a separable verb, fixed phrase, reflexive, or split construction, and no token belongs to two units.
2. **Constructions expected here:**
   - Konjunktiv I in the presupposition of light propagation (*fortpflanze*) and in hypotheses;
   - stipulation verbs (*festsetzen*, *definieren*);
   - the conjecture and presupposition vocabulary (*Vermutung*, *Voraussetzung*);
   - *insofern … als*, glossed as a split construction;
   - long attributive phrases (*in gleichförmiger Translationsbewegung befindliches System*);
   - compounds (*Lichtgeschwindigkeit*, *Koordinatensystem*);
   - the archaic spelling *daß*.
3. **Consistency.** Identical `lemma` plus `noteClass` receive the same `english` gloss as in paper 4 and across this scope, unless `contextual: true` carries a reason. Term tokens (*ruhendes System*, *Lichtäther*, *Beobachter*) are glossed in the sense of their occurrence definitions, with `noteClass: term`.
4. **Metadata and review states.**
   - Each unit carries `revision`, `lang: en` with `sourceLang: de`, `attribution` (an authorship entry for the glossator: `id`, optional `name`, `kind`, and `modelId` for a model), and `reviewState`.
   - A second glossator or agent checks the gloss, records itself in `editor` (an authorship entry whose `id` differs from the glossator's), and sets `corrected`.
   - `reviewed` is reachable only through an accepted `german-source` review record written by `am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`, which covers this gloss.

## Technical Approach

- Write the scope record first.
- Generate token skeletons from the German blocks with `tokenizeGerman`, then author glosses, notes, and multiword units in YAML in printed order.
- Run `bun scripts/align-editions.ts --paper special-relativity --layers gloss --sections s0,s1 --report` (substitute the chosen key section) until coverage is complete and no `gloss-stale` or consistency failure remains.
- The checking editor sets `corrected`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/editorial/special-relativity-gloss-scope.md` lists the sections, reasons, owner, and date, and matches the gloss files.
- [ ] Every word token of every alignable unit in scope (sentences, the key section's heading and part heading, footnotes) has a gloss or a multiword unit; mathematics atoms and footnote marks are never glossed.
- [ ] Every note class used is in the conventions table; every `grammarNote` has a `noteClass` and every `contextual` flag a reason; recurring constructions and term tokens are consistent with paper 4 or carry `contextual`.
- [ ] Every unit carries `revision`, `lang` metadata, an `attribution` authorship entry (with `modelId` for a model), an `editor` entry whose `id` differs from the glossator's, and review state; every unit is `corrected`, and none is `reviewed` without a record.
- [ ] Gloss coverage for this paper appears in the edition coverage report.
- [ ] The gloss face renders these sections with gloss rows, and an unglossed section shows the coverage notice.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

`src/content/editions/relativity.gloss.test.ts`, against the real schema, tokenizer, and harness:
- `assertEditionContract('special-relativity', { layers: ['german', 'translation', 'gloss'], sections: ['s0', 's1'] })` (the chosen key section substituted), with each check logged.
- The scope record equals the sections present in `content/glosses/special-relativity/`. Every alignable unit in those sections (including the heading, `part-1` when §1 is chosen, and footnotes) has a gloss unit, and none lies outside them.
- Every unit validates against the real `GlossUnit` schema. Token lists equal `tokenizeGerman`; `english` is present on exactly the tokens outside multiword units; multiword units have at least two distinct ascending indices, one gloss, and a defined `kind`, and no token is in two units.
- **Corpus consistency:** across all existing gloss files, identical `lemma` plus `noteClass` have identical glosses unless `contextual` with a non-empty reason.
- Every `noteClass` used is accepted by `glossConventions.ts` reading the committed conventions file.
- **Authorship and review states:** every unit is `corrected` with `editor.id` different from `attribution.id`; a model entry requires `modelId`; `authorshipOf(unit)` returns the glossator in `draftedBy` and the editor in `editedBy`.
- **Live-harness canaries** (run-scoped copies under `artifacts/test-tmp/gloss-special-relativity/<log-run-id>/`, never deleted):
  - a unit missing one token fails coverage;
  - a German block with one word changed makes its gloss fail `gloss-stale`;
  - two occurrences of *ruhendes System* with different glosses and no `contextual` flag fail consistency;
  - a unit whose `editor` repeats the glossator's `id` fails the independent-check rule.

### End-to-end tests

- `bun scripts/e2e-edition-pipeline.ts --paper special-relativity --layers german,translation,gloss --sections s0,s1` runs in the gate chain. Required stages: `ledger` through `coverage`. `static-html` may be `not-available`. Evidence is retained under `artifacts/test-logs/edition-pipeline/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.
- **Browser smoke** through the harness of `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, on the face of `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`, with JSONL logs and screenshots, traces, DOM snapshots, and console logs retained on failure:
  - open `?view=gloss` at the introduction and the key section, in the desktop and 320-pixel lanes and the JavaScript-disabled lane;
  - every sentence and footnote in scope shows its gloss row, and a separable verb shows both marked parts;
  - no page-level horizontal overflow;
  - the three sentence actions work by keyboard;
  - an unglossed section (for example §6) shows the coverage notice with a link to the parallel face.

### Structured logging

JSONL goes to `artifacts/test-logs/gloss-special-relativity/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library.
- Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-edn-gloss-relativity-na8d"`, `paper: "special-relativity"`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled` (browser smoke), `message`.
- `extra`: `{sentenceId, tokenIndex, german, noteClass, multiwordKind, glossatorId, editorId, check, evidencePath}`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A gloss is not a translation; keep it word-level and literal enough to show the German structure.
- Do not gloss symbols; the notation concordance explains them. $V$, $t_A$, and $t'_A$ stay unglossed math atoms.
- Keep notes short and grammatical, not interpretive. A stipulation verb's note names the grammar, not the philosophy of simultaneity.
- A display name is not an identity; the self-review check compares authorship ids.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-edn-translation-relativity-s0-s5-hm8`: the aligned introduction and §1.
- `am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y`: the gloss conventions established on paper 4.
- `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`: the face the browser smoke opens.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the browser harness and evidence capture.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`: the German source review covers these gloss units.
- `am-dod-relativity-105y`: definition-of-done item 2 requires glosses for the required sections.
- `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`: the discovery book's German-reading support needs the glosses.

title: Inventory every source unit of the Brownian paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties
description:
# Inventory every source unit of the Brownian paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §3.4, §4.5 step 1, §6.9, §11.3, §19.1, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Before anyone writes an explanation, the paper is inventoried into stable units. The inventory is the **source manifest**: it, not a hand-maintained percentage, decides whether the edition is complete, and a unit can never be "covered" by linking to the whole paper. Freezing ids in Batch A lets transcription, translation, readings, equations, instruments, and discovery work proceed in parallel against the same anchors. It produces the Batch A exit evidence that every original source unit has a destination.

The Brownian paper (*Über die von der molekularkinetischen Theorie der Wärme geforderte Bewegung von in ruhenden Flüssigkeiten suspendierten Teilchen*, Ann. Phys. (4) 17, 549–560, bibliographic key `ap-17-549`) is the first paper built end to end. Its §§4–5 are the Batch B reference slice, so ids for §§4–5 are inventoried first and with particular care.

## Scope

In scope:
- `content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/manifest.yaml`: every source unit with id, kind, locators, labels, containment, reference occurrences, and destination, in the format owned by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`.
- `content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/manifest.ids.snapshot.txt`: the frozen id list in manifest order (the §§4–5 part first, under a `# s4-s5` section marker line).
- `content/aliases/brownian-motion.yaml`: created empty at freeze. Its format is owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`, and it is the only way ids change after freezing.
- `docs/editorial/brownian-motion-difficulties.md`: translation difficulties, notation difficulties, segmentation decisions, and verification flags.
- Refinement of the receipt's page map in `docs/provenance/ap-17-549.md`, in the format of `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: the front-matter `pageMap` entries (`sectionIds`, `displayEquations`, `footnoteMarks`, `refinedBy: am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg`) and the `## Page map` body section. `SourceAsset.pageMapping` is derived from the same front matter by `receiptToSourceAsset`, so the two cannot diverge.

Out of scope:
- diplomatic text (`am-src-ledger-brownian-8cw`) and German edition blocks (`am-edn-german-edition-brownian-phe`);
- translation (`am-edn-translation-brownian-s4-s5-jr4`, `am-edn-translation-brownian-rest-h0z`);
- concordance entries (`am-not-entries-brownian-1rq`);
- printed-constant records and fixtures (`am-ref-constants-xik`, `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`);
- readings and equation records (the Brownian epics).

## Requirements

### Units to inventory

| Unit | Id | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Title and author line | `masthead-title`, `masthead-author` | As printed |
| Section headings | `s1` … `s5` | The heading unit carries the section id |
| Paragraphs | `s<n>-p<m>` | The unnumbered introduction is `s0` |
| Sentences | `s<n>-p<m>-s<k>` | From page images, using the segmentation summary below |
| Displayed equations | `eq-<printed>`; `eq-s<n>-<printed>`; `eq-s<n>-d<j>` | See below |
| Substantive inline equations and nontrivial symbol occurrences | `s<n>-p<m>-s<k>-m<i>`; in a footnote `s<n>-fn<k>-m<i>` | `i` counts every inline math region of the sentence or footnote, 1-based, in printed order; the substantive subset has gaps |
| Footnotes | `s<n>-fn<k>` | Numbered within the section of the mark; the printed label is recorded |
| References | `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, sub-entries of the containing unit | See below |
| Date-line | `closing-dateline` | Expected "Bern, Mai 1905." |
| Journal receipt line | `closing-received` | Expected "(Eingegangen 11. Mai 1905.)"; verify both |
| Acknowledgment | none expected | Confirm on the facsimile |
| Figures | none | Record `figures: none` in the manifest header |

**Displayed equations** (the rules of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`).
- **Ids:** `eq-<printed>` when the printed label is unique within the paper, where `<printed>` is digits with at most one lowercase letter (`7`, `7a`) or the token that `normalizePrintedLabel` makes of any other printed label (parentheses dropped, a Roman numeral becomes `roman-<arabic>`, each prime becomes `p`). Every equation whose token repeats in another section takes the section-qualified `eq-s<n>-<printed>`. An unnumbered display, and each of two equations sharing a token within one section, takes the editorial `eq-s<n>-d<j>` with `editorialLabel` `ed:s<n>-d<j>`.
- **Labels:** `originalLabel` keeps the printed label exactly.
- **Granularity:** one unit per printed display.
- **Containment:** a display printed inside a paragraph or footnote records `containedIn: <that unit's id>`.

**The closing hope.** The closing hope that an experimenter will soon decide the question is expected as the final paragraph of §5. Record its actual placement; its id follows the section in which it is printed, and it is not a closing unit.

**References.** Record each printed reference occurrence (a bibliographic citation, an internal cross-reference such as "§ 3", or a reference to another paper) as a `references[]` sub-entry of the unit that contains it, in the shape of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: `{id, printedText, kind, target}`.
- `id` is the occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>` of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`: `i` counts the printed reference occurrences of that alignable unit in printed order, 1-based (`s3-p2-s1-r1` in a paragraph sentence, `s3-fn1-r1` in a footnote). The id names the occurrence, never its target.
- `printedText` is the reference exactly as printed; `kind` is `bibliographic`, `internal`, or `cross-paper`.
- `target` is `{citationId}` for a bibliographic reference, `{id}` for an internal one, and `{paper, id}` for a cross-paper one. A target record that does not exist yet (the bibliography comes later) stays unresolved; the manifest check reports it as the flag `reference-target-unresolved`, which becomes an error only when the paper is marked complete.
- Reference ids freeze with the other ids. An occurrence found after freeze takes the next unused index in its unit, so earlier ids never shift. The German edition's `reference` inline carries the same id as its `referenceId`.

**Journal furniture.** The issue article number, running heads, page numbers, and neighboring articles' text are not manifest units. The receipt's page map records them.

### Ids and freezing (canonical scheme owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`; follow it if it differs and record the difference)

- Ids are content ids, never array positions.
- At close, every id is frozen: the manifest header records `idsFrozenAt` and `frozenBy`, and the snapshot file is committed.
- Later splits, merges, and retirements are alias records in `content/aliases/brownian-motion.yaml` (with `reason`, `date`, and `editor`), and retired ids are never reused.
- **Inventory §§4–5 first** and commit a §§4–5 snapshot section as soon as it is complete, so `am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81` can start. Until the whole-paper freeze, `idsFrozenAt` is absent and the frozen-id check covers only the committed section. The whole-paper freeze follows in the same bead.

**Sentence-boundary summary.** The full rules are in `docs/editorial/SEGMENTATION.md`, owned by `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`; use that document when it exists.
- **Boundary:** a sentence ends at `.`, `?`, or `!` followed by an uppercase letter or an opening quotation mark, or at the end of the paragraph.
- **Never a boundary:**
  - a colon or semicolon;
  - inside inline mathematics;
  - after an abbreviation (`z. B.`, `d. h.`, `u. s. w.`, `vgl.`, `a. a. O.`, `S.`, `p.`, `Ann. d. Phys.`, `Sek.`);
  - after initials, after an ordinal before a month or noun, or after `§ <n>.`;
  - inside a citation string.
- **Displays:** a sentence continues through a display unless the display ends with a full stop and the next text begins with an uppercase letter.

Doubtful cases are listed in the difficulties file.

### Per-unit fields

- **`id`**, **`kind`**
- **`locators`:** an ordered list, one per page occupied, with `pdfPageIndex` (1-based, strictly increasing), `printedPage`, and optional `region` as percentages from 0 to 100.
- **Labels and containment:** `originalLabel`, `editorialLabel`, `containedIn`, `references[]`.
- **`destination`:**
  - `editionBlockId`;
  - `translationUnits: planned`;
  - `argumentObligations`: from the treatment map below;
  - `notes`.

Statuses are **derived** by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa` from records and never hand-authored; at freeze every derived status is `absent`. The vocabulary is that of `SourceBlock.reviewState` in `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: `absent`, `machine-draft`, `drafted`, `corrected`, `reviewed`. Agents stop at `corrected` after an independent second read; only the human German source review sets `reviewed`.

### The paper's treatment map (record argument obligations against these rows)

Twelve pages, five numbered sections, no figures. The statistical-mechanical foundation of §2 is not optional; both the direct route and the full derivation are provided. German section titles are expected wording; verify against the facsimile. The results column uses the plan's notation; the printed form of each result is recorded in the difficulties file.

| Original part | Reader's central question | Required treatment | Results and printed checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Introduction | Could molecular motion create visible, testable motion of suspended objects? | Einstein's conditional claim and his stated uncertainty about the observational reports, preserved faithfully | the conditional identification with so-called Brownian molecular motion (paraphrase) |
| §1 Osmotic pressure of suspended particles (*Über den suspendierten Teilchen zuzuschreibenden osmotischen Druck*) | Why should visible particles share a law with dissolved molecules? | Semipermeable partition, dilution, number density, pressure, the force/area distinction | $p = \frac{RT}{N}\nu$ |
| §2 Statistical-mechanical justification (*Der osmotische Druck vom Standpunkte der molekularkinetischen Theorie der Wärme*) | How can a vast microscopic problem yield a simple volume dependence? | Configuration counting, the volume factor $V^{N_p}$, free energy, pressure as a derivative; original notation unpacked | the free-energy argument, complete |
| §3 Diffusion of small spheres (*Theorie der Diffusion kleiner suspendierter Kugeln*) | How can drag and equilibrium determine diffusion? | Stokes mobility and the cancellation between drift and diffusion flux; limiting assumptions visible; the force drops out | $K\nu = \frac{RT}{N}\frac{\partial\nu}{\partial x}$, $K = 6\pi kPv$, $D = \frac{RT}{N}\frac{1}{6\pi kP}$ |
| §4 Irregular motion and diffusion (*Über die ungeordnete Bewegung von in einer Flüssigkeit suspendierten Teilchen und deren Beziehung zur Diffusion*) | How do random displacements produce a deterministic equation? | Transition kernel, symmetry, Taylor expansion to second order, the diffusion equation, the Gaussian solution, the RMS; the coarse-graining assumption stated | $\partial f/\partial t = D\,\partial^2 f/\partial x^2$; $D = \frac{1}{\tau}\int\frac{\Delta^2}{2}\varphi(\Delta)\,d\Delta$ |
| §5 Molecular scale from visible motion (*Formel für die mittlere Verschiebung suspendierter Teilchen. Eine neue Methode zur Bestimmung der wahren Größe der Atome*) | How could observations determine the molecular number? | Estimating diffusion from displacement, propagating uncertainty, distinguishing a synthetic exercise from historical data; the observable is a displacement | $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$; $N = \frac{t}{\lambda_x^2}\frac{RT}{3\pi kP}$; printed (expected from a comparison witness; verify): for particles of diameter 0,001 mm in water at 17° with $k = 1{,}35\cdot10^{-2}$ and $N = 6\cdot10^{23}$, "$\lambda_x = 8\cdot10^{-5}$ cm $= 0{,}8$ Mikron" in one second and "ca. 6 Mikron" in one minute |
| Closing | | The hope that an experimenter will decide the question (placement as printed); date-line and receipt line | "Bern, Mai 1905" |

**Editorial boundary.** Einstein predicts a diffusive mean displacement. No instrument on the site shows a "Brownian speed" as a physical quantity, and none estimates one from a finely rendered polyline. **Verification flag:** the plan attributes to this paper a warning that the observable is not a mean velocity and that the trajectory has no tangent at microscope resolution; check the 1905 text. Einstein's explicit apparent-velocity discussion appears in his 1906 paper "Zur Theorie der Brownschen Bewegung" (Ann. Phys. 19, 371). If the 1905 text lacks it, record that, so later layers present it as a dated later statement.

### Notation entries this inventory must flag (for `am-not-entries-brownian-1rq`)

Each entry is recorded with its printed glyph and first-use unit id (or an explicit not-found result):
- $k \to \eta$: viscosity, not Boltzmann's constant; a dangerous collision flagged in red on first use.
- $P \to a$: radius, not pressure; work function in paper 1.
- $\nu \to n$: number density, not frequency.
- $\lambda_x \to \sqrt{\langle x^2\rangle}$; $R/N \to k_B$. $N$ is Avogadro's number: a printed constant symbol, so the concordance binds it to the quantity `avogadroConstant` and the constant set supplies the printed value; only inference outputs with an uncertainty bind `avogadroNumberEstimate`. $R$ binds `molarGasConstant`.
- $\varphi(\Delta) \to$ the transition kernel; $f \to p(x,t)$.
- $\tau \to$ an observation interval (the moving-frame time in paper 3).
- $K \to$ a force (a coordinate system in paper 3, kinetic energy in paper 4).
- $D \to$ the diffusion coefficient; $p$: osmotic pressure.
- Printed symbols of §§1–3 that later layers need (expected from a comparison witness's text layer; research evidence only, verify each): $V^*$ (a partial volume) and $z$ (gram-molecules of solute) in §1; $n$ (a particle count, distinct from $\nu$); in §2 the state variables $p_1 \ldots p_l$ with rates $\varphi_\nu$, an entropy written with $2\kappa$ and "lg" of an integral, the relation $2\kappa N = R$ (so $\kappa$ is half of the modern $k_B$, a rename with a numerical factor), the configuration integral $B$ and its volume-independent factor $J$, both $\bar{E}$ and $E$, and the virtual variation $\delta$; in §3 $\mu$ as the mass of a particle and $l$ as a column length.
- Within-paper collisions to flag: $\varphi_\nu$ (§2) versus $\varphi(\Delta)$ (§4); the printed $\mu$ (mass) versus the modern mobility $\mu$ used by the explanation layers; "lg" as the natural logarithm (modern ISO "lg" means $\log_{10}$).
- Printed unit words: *Mikron* (expected in §5; modern μm) and *Sek.*; units stay as printed on the source face, and the concordance records any conversion.

### Difficulties file (`docs/editorial/brownian-motion-difficulties.md`)

Every verification flag is a list item that begins with a stable key in the form `flag:<key>` and ends with a result (`pending`, `matches`, `differs`, or `not-found`, the vocabulary of the receipt's watch list) and, when found, the first-use unit id, so tests and the German edition can read the flags without parsing prose.

1. **Translation difficulties.**
   - Modality and qualification that must survive ("suggests," "must," "under these assumptions," "to this approximation").
   - Long sentences that may need splitting; ambiguous references.
   - The introduction's conditional sentences, which must stay separate sentence units with their own ids (expected wording, verify):
     - it is possible that the motions are identical with so-called Brownian molecular motion;
     - the available reports are too imprecise for a judgment;
     - if the motion can actually be observed, classical thermodynamics can no longer be regarded as exactly valid for microscopically distinguishable spaces, and an exact determination of the true size of atoms becomes possible;
     - if the prediction proved incorrect, that would be a weighty argument against the molecular-kinetic conception of heat.
   - Period words for term annotations: *molekularkinetische Theorie der Wärme*, *Brownsche Molekularbewegung*, *osmotischer Druck*, *semipermeable Wand*, *ungeordnete Bewegung*, *mittlere Verschiebung*, and any further period terms found, each with first-use unit ids.
2. **Notation difficulties:** every scoped glyph, collision, and unit word above, with first-use unit ids and the printed form of each treatment-map result.
3. **Segmentation decisions:**
   - doubtful sentence boundaries;
   - displays before the first paragraph of a section;
   - displays printed inside a paragraph or a footnote (with their `containedIn`);
   - multi-line displays counted as one unit;
   - words, paragraphs, and footnotes crossing page breaks;
   - the placement of the closing hope.
4. **Verification flags:**
   - `flag:s5-printed-numbers`: the viscosity of water at 17° printed as $k = 1{,}35\cdot10^{-2}$; the printed particle size (a witness prints the diameter, 0,001 mm; transcribe whether the print gives diameter or radius, and its unit); $N = 6\cdot10^{23}$; the results "$\lambda_x = 8\cdot10^{-5}$ cm $= 0{,}8$ Mikron" for one second and "ca. 6 Mikron" for one minute, as printed.
   - `flag:s5-printed-units`: the printed unit words (expected *Mikron*, never the glyph μ, and *Sek.*) and the printed temperature "17°".
   - `flag:r-not-printed`: whether paper 2 prints any numerical $R$. A witness shows none, so the site's $R$ is an editorial input in the constant set `einstein-1905-brownian-printed` of `am-ref-constants-xik`, never a printed value.
   - For context only, recomputed in review (python3) with $N$ and $k$ as printed, $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg/(mol·K) as the editorial input, $T = 290.15$ K as the site's conversion of the printed 17°, and the radius $a = 5\times10^{-5}$ cm from the printed diameter: $D = 3.158\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{cm^2/s}$, $\lambda_x = 0.795$ μm at 1 s and $6.156$ μm at 60 s, printed as about 0,8 and about 6 Mikron. With $T = 290$ K they are $0.7946$ μm and $6.155$ μm (0.026% lower). These are fixtures owned by `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` and `am-ref-constants-xik`; the inventory records only what is printed.
   - `flag:intro-uncertainty`: the introduction's statement of uncertainty about the observational reports.
   - `flag:velocity-warning`: the velocity-warning attribution above.
   - `flag:s4-tau-coarse-graining`: the coarse-graining assumption on $\tau$ in §4.
   - `flag:dates`: the date-line and receipt line against the typed dates (received 11 May 1905, published 18 July 1905).

### Counts

Record totals and per-page counts of headings, paragraphs starting on each page, display equations (numbered and unnumbered), substantive inline equations, footnotes, reference occurrences, and closings. Reconcile them with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`.

## Technical Approach

- Work from page images of the pinned facsimile rendered locally at 300 dpi or more (for example `pdftoppm -r 300` into `artifacts/facsimile-renders/ap-17-549/`). **Local rendering is allowed; OCR and text-layer extraction are not.** A cloud OCR draft may help locate paragraph boundaries, but the images decide.
- Write the manifest in the format of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`, ordered by printed position. Validate it with that bead's compiler check and `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts brownian-motion`.
- Assign display ids with `normalizePrintedLabel` from `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` and reference occurrence ids by counting occurrences per alignable unit in printed order.
- Generate the snapshot from the validated manifest: the §§4–5 part as soon as it is complete, the whole paper at freeze.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every unit kind listed above has entries with valid ids, locators, labels, containment, reference occurrences, and destinations; nothing is covered by a paper-level link.
- [ ] Every row of the treatment map has at least one argument obligation recorded against the right units.
- [ ] Display ids follow the printed-label rules (normalized tokens, section-qualified ids for tokens repeated across sections, editorial ids within a section), and inline math indices follow the count-every-region rule.
- [ ] Every reference sub-entry has an occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, `printedText`, `kind`, and a target or the unresolved flag.
- [ ] Counts reconcile with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`, and both are refined with section boundaries and equation locations.
- [ ] `content/aliases/brownian-motion.yaml` exists and is empty; the manifest header declares `idsFrozenAt` and `frozenBy`; the snapshot is committed, with §§4–5 first.
- [ ] The difficulties file has all four sections, with first-use ids, every `flag:` key above with a result, and the verification values above.
- [ ] The manifest validates with zero errors, and all derived statuses are `absent`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

`src/content/editions/brownian.manifest.test.ts`, against the real manifest compiler check, id parsers, and alias resolver:
- The manifest validates: no duplicate ids, grammar-valid ids, at least one locator per unit with strictly increasing 1-based page indices, derived statuses `absent`, no authored status fields.
- Every display has a label, locators, and a `containedIn` value or a recorded standalone case.
- A computed map from `normalizePrintedLabel` over the printed labels equals the display ids: tokens repeated across sections map to section-qualified ids, and tokens repeated within a section to editorial ids.
- Inline math ids are unique per sentence or footnote, with indices of at least 1.
- Every reference sub-entry's id parses as a `ReferenceId`, its unit prefix is an alignable unit inside the containing unit, indices are unique per alignable unit, and `printedText`, `kind`, and a target or `reference-target-unresolved` are present.
- Per-page counts equal `SourceAsset.pageMapping` and the receipt page map.
- Every treatment-map row (`s0` … `s5`, `closing`) has an obligation.
- The masthead, `closing-dateline`, and `closing-received` exist.
- Footnote sections match their marks.
- The alias file is empty; the snapshot equals the manifest (the `# s4-s5` marker line ignored).
- A mutation copy under `artifacts/test-tmp/manifest-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>/` that removes an id without an alias fails, and one that renumbers a reference occurrence fails the frozen-id check.
- Paper-specific:
  - every §§4–5 unit named in the §§4–5 obligations exists;
  - the introduction's four conditional statements are separate sentence ids;
  - the closing hope's id lies in the section where it is printed;
  - the difficulties file parses into every `flag:` key listed above, each with a result from the watch-list vocabulary, and `flag:s5-printed-units` names the printed unit word.

### End-to-end tests

- `src/content/editions/brownian.manifest.e2e.test.ts` runs `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts brownian-motion` through `Bun.spawn` and asserts:
  - exit code 0;
  - no unit lacks a destination;
  - per-page counts match `SourceAsset.pageMapping`;
  - no percentage in the output.

  It then runs the content compiler's check over the corpus and asserts no rejection for this paper, and runs `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-549` (from `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`) and asserts the refined page map passes. Stdout, stderr, and report JSON are retained on failure under `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.
- `am-edn-german-edition-brownian-phe` later runs the edition pipeline, whose reconciliation stage compares this manifest with the ledger.

### Structured logging

JSONL goes to `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library.
- Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg"`, `paper: "brownian-motion"`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind` (`bitwise` for counts and id lists), `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.
- `extra`: `{unitId, kind, referenceId, flagKey, pdfPageIndex, printedPage, check}`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Decide "substantive inline equation" generously; the count-every-region index rule means adding one later never shifts an id.
- Paragraphs and footnotes that cross pages keep one id with one locator per page.
- Count reference occurrences per alignable unit, not per paragraph: a paragraph's references sit on its sentences.
- Do not transcribe or translate here, and never hand-author a status.
- A plan value in μ or with a printed $R$ is not a printed reading; the page decides, and the difficulties file says what it shows.
- §§4–5 first, but the freeze covers the whole paper before this bead closes; §§1–3 get the same granularity.
- Freezing is final: a later correction is an alias, so list doubtful boundaries now.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-facsimile-brownian-mox`: the pinned facsimile, its page images, and the page map.
- `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: the manifest format, the compiler check, and the report CLI.
- `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: JSONL logging and failure-evidence retention for the manifest tests.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-german-edition-brownian-phe`: edition blocks use these frozen ids and reference occurrence ids.
- `am-not-entries-brownian-1rq`: concordance entries are scoped to these sections and first-use ids.
- `am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81`: equation records for the reference slice bind to these equation ids.

comments.text:
TYPECHECK FIX LIST for whoever resumes (pane %15 is quota-blocked until ~06:45Z). Measured in the main working tree: bun run typecheck exits 1 with 7 errors, 6 of them in src/content/editions/brownian.manifest.test.ts. Exact lines:

  83,39  TS2339 .editionBlockId
  84,32  TS2339 .editionBlockId
  85,32  TS2339 .argumentObligations
  289,16 TS18048 'ref.printedText' is possibly undefined
  346,31 TS2339 .argumentObligations
  602,31 TS2339 .argumentObligations

TWO ROOT CAUSES, not six bugs:
(1) Five TS2339s are the same thing. 'destination' is typed as a UNION - string | { editionBlockId?, translationUnits?, argumentObligations?, notes? } - and the test reaches for a property without narrowing it first. Narrow the union (typeof d === 'string' ? ... : d.editionBlockId), do not cast.
(2) Two TS18048s are optional properties read without a guard: ref.printedText here, and unit.destination.editionBlockId at relativity.manifest.test.ts:69. Guard them; do not use the non-null assertion operator, and do not relax tsconfig - the strict flags are what surfaced this.

CROSS-CUTTING NOTE WORTH ACTING ON: this same union has now produced type errors independently in THREE panes' work - brownian (6), light-quanta (5, since fixed), relativity (1). Three agents hitting the identical shape is a signal about the schema, not about three careless authors. Rather than narrowing at every call site a fourth time, consider adding one small exported helper next to the manifest types - something like destinationBlockId(d) and destinationObligations(d) that does the narrowing once and returns a well-typed result - and use it from all three test files. That converts a recurring trap into a single tested function. Raise it as a finding if you think the schema itself should stop being a union; do not change the schema unilaterally inside an inventory commit, because that is a gate/type change riding inside feature work.

Also still outstanding from before the quota cut: commit content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/manifest.yaml together with manifest.ids.snapshot.txt (commit 8415b40 shipped the snapshot without the manifest, leaving 36 frozen ids at HEAD with 0 units and 11 tests red), and set frozenBy to am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg instead of pane15.

Independent second read against the CORRECTED renders (pane30). Pushed as b1e330f. Bead NOT closed.

Worked only from artifacts/page-images/ap-17-549-CORRECTED/parent-173.png..parent-184.png. Did not touch public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf, the facsimile config, or docs/provenance/ap-17-549.md; am-cf6m (pane29) owns that repair.

VERDICT ON THE PRIOR PANE'S 92 UNITS: built from the right paper, and largely accurate. I read all twelve pages. Confirmed against the renders: masthead (parent-173 prints article 5. and the full title); exactly three footnotes on 551, 553, 555, with s2-fn1's mark correctly on the §2 heading itself (containedIn: s2); all four printed bibliographic citations matching byte for byte, including "Ann. d. Phys. 9. p. 417. 1902", "11. p. 170. 1903" and "G. Kirchhoff, Vorlesungen ueber Mechanik, 26. Vorlesung § 4"; the label (1) printed twice and correctly section-qualified as eq-s3-1 (p.554) and eq-s4-1 (p.558); every per-page display-equation count correct on all twelve pages; the closing hope as the final §5 paragraph; "Bern, Mai 1905." and "(Eingegangen 11. Mai 1905.)"; and NO acknowledgment, which the bead asked be confirmed rather than assumed. Every §5 verification value is printed as expected: N = 6e23, water at 17 C, k = 1,35e-2, diameter 0,001 mm, lambda_x = 8e-5 cm = 0,8 Mikron, "ca. 6 Mikron" in 1 Min. Notation collisions confirmed printed in one sentence on p.555: "Kugelradius P" and "Reibungskoeffizienten k". Also printed as the bead expected: V* and z (s1-p1), n and nu (s1-p3), p1..pl with phi_nu, 2*kappa*N = R, lg as natural log, E-bar and E, B and J, delta (s2-p1), D and mu (s3-p7), phi(Delta) (s4-p4), tau as observation interval (s4-p3), K as force (s3-p1).

ONE DEFECT: five spurious paragraph units. The 1905 setting indents a new paragraph by ~55 px at this render scale; a line that merely resumes after a display is set flush to the margin. Measured left offsets on p.554: the three real starts are +55, +53, +58, while "Es werde angenommen", "Die gesuchte Gleichgewichtsbedingung" and "Die letzte Gleichung sagt aus" are +1 to +5. Spurious units: s2-p6 (553, belongs to s2-p5); s3-p3 and s3-p4 (554, belong to s3-p2); s4-p7 and s4-p8 (557, belong to s4-p6). True paragraph starts per page are 549:3 550:2 551:1 552:3 553:3 554:3 555:3 556:4 557:2 558:3 559:3 560:2. True paragraph total is 32, not 37. Not a consistent convention: s4-p6 absorbs two flush resumptions correctly, then s4-p7 splits at the next; 551, 555, 556 and 558 all fold theirs correctly. Displays, footnotes and reference occurrences are unaffected.

NOT REPAIRED, AND WHY. The five ids are frozen and the snapshot is committed, so removal is an alias operation under am-cm-id-scheme-8bn, never a renumbering - s2-p7 must keep its number and the sequence must be left with gaps. That interacts with the snapshot-equals-manifest contract asserted in brownian.manifest.test.ts, so the format owner should rule before ids move. Full recommended repair is recorded in the difficulties file: retire the five ids in content/aliases/brownian-motion.yaml pointing at their absorbing paragraph, re-point containedIn for eq-s2-d9, eq-s3-d2, eq-s3-d3, eq-s3-1, eq-s3-d4, eq-s4-d7, eq-s4-d8, and correct the three per-page numbers and the total together. Nothing downstream consumes these ids yet, so it is still cheap. I deliberately did NOT edit the expectedParagraphStartsPerPage golden: it is only wrong because the data is wrong, and regenerating it alone would be RH-3.

SECOND FINDING: that golden's comment reads "Verified paragraph start counts per page from scans" but asserts numbers the manifest already contains, so it cannot fail for this defect, and three of its twelve values (553, 554, 557) are contradicted by the corrected renders. It claims a proof class it does not have. Its neighbouring display and footnote tables I checked against the renders and they are correct.

THIRD FINDING: reference occurrence ids here are sentence-scoped (s3-p5-s1-r1, s4-p10-s5-r1, s5-p1-s1-r1) while relativity's are paragraph-scoped (s6-p2-r1). Both are in tree, and the sentence segments named do not exist as units in any manifest because the canonical format has no sentence kind.
