title: Inventory every source unit of the light-quanta paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties
description:
# Inventory every source unit of the light-quanta paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §3.3, §4.5 step 1, §6.9, §11.3, §19.1, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Before anyone writes an explanation, the paper is inventoried into stable units. The inventory is the **source manifest**: it, not a hand-maintained percentage, decides whether the edition is complete, and a unit can never be "covered" by linking to the whole paper. Freezing ids in Batch A lets transcription, translation, readings, equations, instruments, and discovery work proceed in parallel against the same anchors. It produces the Batch A exit evidence that every original source unit has a destination.

The light-quanta paper (*Über einen die Erzeugung und Verwandlung des Lichtes betreffenden heuristischen Gesichtspunkt*, Ann. Phys. (4) 17, 132–148, bibliographic key `ap-17-132`) argues from Wien's law, not Planck's, and calls its result heuristic. Its product scope is all nine sections plus the introduction and the closing.

Its printed numbers are easy to misremember, and a comparison witness already shows three places where the plan's reading differs from the print: §2 gives no numerical $R$ or light speed, its $\alpha$ may carry a misprinted exponent, and §8 makes its 4.3-volt check with the charge of a gram-equivalent rather than an electron charge. The inventory records what the page shows so no later layer repeats the plan's reading as if it were printed.

## Scope

In scope:
- `content/source-blocks/light-quanta/manifest.yaml`: every source unit with id, kind, locators, labels, containment, reference occurrences, and destination, in the format owned by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`.
- `content/source-blocks/light-quanta/manifest.ids.snapshot.txt`: the frozen id list, one id per line in manifest order.
- `content/aliases/light-quanta.yaml`: created empty at freeze. Its format is owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`, and it is the only way ids change after freezing.
- `docs/editorial/light-quanta-difficulties.md`: translation difficulties, notation difficulties, segmentation decisions, and verification flags.
- Refinement of the receipt's page map in `docs/provenance/ap-17-132.md`, in the format of `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: the front-matter `pageMap` entries (`sectionIds`, `displayEquations`, `footnoteMarks`, `refinedBy: am-edn-inventory-light-quanta-skp`) and the `## Page map` body section. `SourceAsset.pageMapping` is derived from the same front matter by `receiptToSourceAsset`, so the two cannot diverge.

Out of scope:
- diplomatic text (`am-src-ledger-light-quanta-sxi`) and German edition blocks (`am-edn-german-edition-light-quanta-eou`);
- translation (`am-edn-translation-light-quanta-s0-s4-muc`, `am-edn-translation-light-quanta-s5-s9-lgu`);
- concordance entries (`am-not-entries-light-quanta-9cb`);
- printed-constant records, typographical-error decisions, and fixtures (`am-ref-constants-xik`, `am-ref-photoelectric-q6r`, and the receipt's `typographicalErrors` written by the ledger bead);
- readings and equation records (`am-ep-light-quanta-ogy`).

## Requirements

### Units to inventory

| Unit | Id | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Title and author line | `masthead-title`, `masthead-author` | As printed |
| Section headings | `s1` … `s9` | The heading unit carries the section id |
| Paragraphs | `s<n>-p<m>` | The unnumbered introduction is `s0` |
| Sentences | `s<n>-p<m>-s<k>` | From page images, using the segmentation summary below |
| Displayed equations | `eq-<printed>`; `eq-s<n>-<printed>`; `eq-s<n>-d<j>` | See below; displays inside footnotes included |
| Substantive inline equations and nontrivial symbol occurrences | `s<n>-p<m>-s<k>-m<i>`; in a footnote `s<n>-fn<k>-m<i>` | `i` counts every inline math region of the sentence or footnote, 1-based, in printed order; the substantive subset has gaps |
| Footnotes | `s<n>-fn<k>` | Numbered within the section of the mark; the printed label (for example `1)`) is recorded |
| References | `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, sub-entries of the containing unit | See below |
| Date-line | `closing-dateline` | Expected "Bern, den 17. März 1905." |
| Journal receipt line | `closing-received` | Expected "(Eingegangen 18. März 1905.)"; verify both on the facsimile |
| Figures | none | Record `figures: none` in the manifest header |

**Displayed equations** (the rules of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`).
- **Ids:** `eq-<printed>` when the printed label is unique within the paper, where `<printed>` is digits with at most one lowercase letter or the token that `normalizePrintedLabel` makes of any other printed label (parentheses dropped, a Roman numeral becomes `roman-<arabic>`, each prime becomes `p`). Every equation whose token repeats in another section takes the section-qualified `eq-s<n>-<printed>`. An unnumbered display, and each of two equations sharing a token within one section, takes the editorial `eq-s<n>-d<j>` with `editorialLabel` `ed:s<n>-d<j>`.
- **Labels:** `originalLabel` keeps the printed label exactly: parentheses, primes, Roman numerals, letters.
- **Granularity:** one unit per printed display; a multi-line display under one brace or label is one unit.
- **Containment:** a display printed inside a paragraph or a footnote records `containedIn: <that unit's id>`. This paper prints displays inside footnotes (see the flags below), and each is a display unit contained in its footnote.

**References.** Record each printed reference occurrence (for example a citation of Planck or Lenard in a footnote, or an internal cross-reference) as a `references[]` sub-entry of the unit that contains it, in the shape of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: `{id, printedText, kind, target}`.
- `id` is the occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>` of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`: `i` counts the printed reference occurrences of that alignable unit in printed order, 1-based (`s8-p1-s2-r1` in a paragraph sentence, `s2-fn1-r1` in a footnote). The id names the occurrence, never its target.
- `printedText` is the reference exactly as printed; `kind` is `bibliographic`, `internal`, or `cross-paper`.
- `target` is `{citationId}` for a bibliographic reference, `{id}` for an internal one, and `{paper, id}` for a cross-paper one. A target record that does not exist yet stays unresolved; the manifest check reports it as the flag `reference-target-unresolved`, an error only once the paper is marked complete.
- Reference ids freeze with the other ids. An occurrence found after freeze takes the next unused index in its unit. The German edition's `reference` inline carries the same id as its `referenceId`.

**Journal furniture.** The issue article number before the title, running heads, page numbers, and neighboring articles' text are not manifest units. The receipt's page map records them with ledger-only destinations.

### Ids and freezing (canonical scheme owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`; follow it if it differs and record the difference)

- Ids are content ids, never array positions.
- When this bead closes, every id in the manifest is frozen: the manifest header records `idsFrozenAt` (date) and `frozenBy`, and the snapshot file is committed.
- Every later split, merge, or retirement is an alias record in `content/aliases/light-quanta.yaml` (with `reason`, `date`, and `editor`), and retired ids are never reused.

**Sentence-boundary summary.** The full rules are in `docs/editorial/SEGMENTATION.md`, owned by `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`; use that document when it exists.
- **Boundary:** a sentence ends at `.`, `?`, or `!` followed by an uppercase letter or an opening quotation mark, or at the end of the paragraph.
- **Never a boundary:**
  - a colon or semicolon;
  - inside inline mathematics;
  - after an abbreviation (`z. B.`, `d. h.`, `u. s. w.`, `vgl.`, `a. a. O.`, `S.`, `p.`, `Ann. d. Phys.`, `Sek.`);
  - after initials, after an ordinal before a month or noun (`17. März`), or after `§ <n>.`;
  - inside a citation string.
- **Displays:** a sentence continues through a display unless the display ends with a full stop and the next text begins with an uppercase letter.

Every boundary decided under this summary in a doubtful case is listed in the difficulties file so reconciliation against the ledger checks it first.

### Per-unit fields

- **`id`**, **`kind`**
- **`locators`:** an ordered list, one entry per page the unit occupies, with `pdfPageIndex` (1-based, strictly increasing), `printedPage`, and optional `region` as percentages from 0 to 100.
- **Labels and containment:** `originalLabel`, `editorialLabel`, `containedIn`, `references[]`.
- **`destination`:**
  - `editionBlockId`;
  - `translationUnits: planned`;
  - `argumentObligations`: planned obligations from the treatment map below;
  - `notes`.

Transcription, mathematical-transcription, translation, and review statuses are **derived** by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa` from records and never hand-authored. At freeze time no records exist, so every derived status is `absent`. The vocabulary is that of `SourceBlock.reviewState` in `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: `absent`, `machine-draft`, `drafted`, `corrected`, `reviewed`. Agents stop at `corrected` after an independent second read; only the human German source review sets `reviewed`.

### The paper's treatment map (record argument obligations against these rows)

Seventeen pages, nine numbered sections, no figures. The nine sections, not merely the photoelectric application, are the product scope. German section titles are expected wording; verify against the facsimile. The results column uses the plan's notation; the printed form of each result is recorded in the difficulties file.

| Original part | Reader's central question | Required treatment | Results and printed checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Introduction | Why might a successful wave description be incomplete? | Contrast continuous field descriptions with discrete matter without asserting that optical wave phenomena disappear; state the heuristic | The heuristic status, verbatim |
| §1 Difficulty in black-body theory (*Über eine die Theorie der „schwarzen Strahlung" betreffende Schwierigkeit*) | What goes wrong when classical energy sharing is applied to radiation? | Mode counting and energy allocation with explicit assumptions and a finite-cutoff instrument; the divergence shown as a refusal, not a clamp | $\rho_\nu = \frac{R}{N}\frac{8\pi\nu^2}{L^3}T$; $\int_0^\infty\rho_\nu\,d\nu$ has no finite value |
| §2 Planck's elementary quanta (*Über die Plancksche Bestimmung der Elementarquanta*) | What had Planck determined, and what is Einstein changing? | Historical constants and units; distinguish quantized oscillator energy from a hypothesis about radiation | $N = \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\frac{8\pi R}{L^3}$, printed $6.17\times10^{23}$ |
| §3 Radiation entropy (*Über die Entropie der Strahlung*) | How can a measured spectrum say something about entropy? | Derive $\partial\varphi/\partial\rho = 1/T$ and say what is held fixed | The thermodynamic identity, derived not assumed |
| §4 Low-density monochromatic radiation (*Grenzgesetz für die Entropie der monochromatischen Strahlung bei geringer Strahlungsdichte*) | Why does the Wien regime simplify the problem? | Invert Wien's law, fix the integration constant, integrate at fixed narrow band | $S - S_0 = \frac{E}{\beta\nu}\ln\frac{V}{V_0}$ |
| §5 Gases and dilute solutions (*Molekulartheoretische Untersuchung der Abhängigkeit der Entropie von Gasen und verdünnten Lösungen vom Volumen*) | How does counting independent possibilities produce an entropy law? | Volume probability, independence, logarithms, the gas and solution analogy; the locked-positions counterexample | $S - S_0 = \frac{R}{N}\ln W$; $W = (V/V_0)^n$ |
| §6 Interpreting radiation entropy (*Interpretation des Ausdruckes für die Abhängigkeit der Entropie der monochromatischen Strahlung vom Volumen nach dem Boltzmannschen Prinzip*) | Why does the same functional form suggest independent quanta? | Compare coefficients and infer an energy scale; mark the heuristic leap and its domain; never round $E/(\beta\nu)$ to an integer | $W = (V/V_0)^{NE/(R\beta\nu)}$; quanta of energy $R\beta\nu/N$ |
| §7 Stokes's rule (*Über die Stokessche Regel*) | What restrictions follow when light changes frequency? | Energy-budget treatment; reproduce the paper's qualifications, not a universal prohibition | emitted $\nu \le$ absorbed $\nu$ with the thermal caveat |
| §8 Photoelectric emission (*Über die Erzeugung von Kathodenstrahlen durch Belichtung fester Körper*) | What changes electron energy, and what changes electron count? | Frequency, intensity, work function, stopping potential, losses; predictions distinguished from later confirmation | $\Pi\varepsilon = \frac{R}{N}\beta\nu - P$; printed: $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ gives about 4.3 V, checked in the printed representation (expected $\Pi E = R\beta\nu - P'$ with the gram-equivalent charge $E$) |
| §9 Gas ionization (*Über die Ionisierung der Gase durch ultraviolettes Licht*) | What does the hypothesis predict about ionization energy and yield? | Threshold and upper-bound counting; separate one-quantum assumptions from real cross-sections | energy per ion $\le R\beta\nu/N$; the printed count relation (expected $j = L/(R\beta\nu)$) |
| Closing | | Date-line and receipt line preserved | "Bern, den 17. März 1905" |

**Editorial boundary.** The paper argues from Wien's law, not Planck's, and calls the result heuristic. §6 is never presented as a derivation of Planck's law or a theory of the photon; it is an inference that radiation in the Wien regime behaves thermodynamically as if made of independent energy quanta, and the extension to emission and transformation processes is a further physical hypothesis, not algebra alone.

### Notation entries this inventory must flag (for `am-not-entries-light-quanta-9cb`)

Each entry is recorded with its printed glyph as seen on the facsimile and the unit id of its first use (or an explicit not-found result):
- $R/N \to k_B$; $R\beta/N \to h$. $R$ binds the quantity `molarGasConstant` and the printed constant symbol $N$ binds `avogadroConstant`, whose value the constant set supplies.
- $\beta \to h/k_B$: Wien's constant here, unlike paper 3, where $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$ (paper 4 is expected to write the factor as an explicit radical).
- $L \to c$: the speed of light in this paper (§§1–2); in §9 $L$ is expected to be the absorbed light energy, a within-paper collision; emitted energy in paper 4; a magnetic-field component in paper 3 §6.
- $\alpha, \beta \to$ Wien's constants (editorial $A$, $B$ in the entropy workbench); in the §1 footnote $\alpha_\nu$ are expected to be phases, a within-paper collision.
- $\Pi \to$ stopping-potential magnitude; $\varepsilon \to e$.
- $E$: expected as the energy in §§4 and 6, as the charge of a gram-equivalent in §8 (9,6·10³ in electromagnetic units; the constant set records it under the quantity id `gramEquivalentCharge`), and as the energy of a system in the §5 footnote.
- $P \to$ work function $\Phi$ (radius in paper 2); $P'$ in the second §8 relation (expected a sum of two terms, per a footnote); $p$ as a pressure in the §5 footnote; verify the printed form of the escape term.
- $\rho_\nu \to u_\nu(\nu, T)$: energy per volume per frequency, not radiance.
- $\varphi$: the spectral entropy density (verify glyph and scope), with a second use expected in §5.
- $T$: the temperature, and in the §1 footnote a time interval.
- $\lambda$: a Lagrange multiplier in §3's variational displays.
- "lg": the natural logarithm throughout; modern ISO "lg" means $\log_{10}$, so the first use needs a note.
- Electromagnetic CGS units in §8: $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ read as volts (1 abvolt $= 10^{-8}$ V; 1 abcoulomb $= 10$ C), beside erg, esu, and statvolt elsewhere.
- $N$ is Avogadro's number here; the printed volume glyph in §§4–6 (verify $V$ versus $v$).

### Difficulties file (`docs/editorial/light-quanta-difficulties.md`)

Every verification flag is a list item that begins with a stable key in the form `flag:<key>` and ends with a result (`pending`, `matches`, `differs`, or `not-found`, the vocabulary of the receipt's watch list) and, when found, the first-use unit id, so tests and later beads can read the flags without parsing prose.

1. **Translation difficulties.**
   - Modality and qualification that must survive ("suggests," "must," "under these assumptions," "to this approximation"); a heuristic stays a heuristic.
   - Long sentences that may need splitting; ambiguous references.
   - Period words for term annotations: *Elementarquantum*, *Energiequant*, *Kathodenstrahlen*, *heuristischer Gesichtspunkt*, *schwarze Strahlung*, *monochromatische Strahlung*, *Boltzmannsches Prinzip*, *Stokessche Regel*, and any further period terms found, each with first-use unit ids.
2. **Notation difficulties:** every scoped glyph, collision, and unit convention above, with first-use unit ids and the printed form of each treatment-map result.
3. **Segmentation decisions:**
   - doubtful sentence boundaries decided under the summary;
   - displays printed before the first paragraph of a section;
   - displays printed inside paragraphs and inside footnotes, with their `containedIn`;
   - multi-line displays counted as one unit;
   - words and paragraphs crossing page breaks;
   - footnotes running onto the next page.
4. **Verification flags** (expected readings come from a comparison witness and are checks, never sources):
   - `flag:s2-constants`: Planck's constants as printed. Expected $\beta = 4.866\times10^{-11}$ and the printed $N = 6.17\times10^{23}$ with decimal commas as printed; a witness prints $\alpha = 6{,}1\cdot10^{-56}$, while only $6.10\times10^{-57}$ (Planck's 1901 value) reproduces the printed $N$. Recomputed in review (python3) with the editorial inputs $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg/(mol·K) and $L = 3\times10^{10}$ cm/s: $\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\frac{8\pi R}{L^3} = 6.1705\times10^{23}$ for $\alpha = 6.10\times10^{-57}$ and $6.1705\times10^{22}$ for $\alpha = 6.1\times10^{-56}$. If the facsimile shows the exponent $-56$, the ledger bead records a suspected typographical error in the receipt (original kept on the source face, corrected value marked); the inventory records the reading.
   - `flag:s2-r-and-l-not-printed`: whether §2 prints a numerical $R$ or $L$. A witness shows neither, so both are editorial inputs in `einstein-1905-light-quanta-printed` (`am-ref-constants-xik`) unless the facsimile prints them somewhere in the paper. §2 also prints the hydrogen-atom mass $1.62\times10^{-24}$ g (expected).
   - `flag:s8-printed-check`: the printed charge quantity and unit factor of the "about 4.3 V" check. A witness shows §8 printing both $\Pi\varepsilon = \frac{R}{N}\beta\nu - P$ and $\Pi E = R\beta\nu - P'$, with the check made with $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ (the charge of a gram-equivalent, electromagnetic CGS) and $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ read as volts. Recomputed (python3): $\Pi = R\beta\nu/E = 4.3385$ V (4.34 V at three figures). The esu and statvolt route (an electron charge $4.7\times10^{-10}$ esu with the printed $N$: 4.3057 V with 299.792458 V per statvolt, 4.3087 V with 300) is a modern restatement, never the printed form, and modern values are never substituted.
   - `flag:s8-result-line`: the result line's power of ten. A witness reads "$\Pi\cdot10^{7} = 4{,}3$ Volt", a suspected misprint; transcribe exactly.
   - `flag:fn-displays`: displays printed inside footnotes, each with its footnote id: §1 (a Fourier expansion with $T$ a time interval and phases $\alpha_\nu$, $dW$, and a factorization); §3 (an arbitrary-assumption footnote); §5 ($-d(E - TS) = p\,dv$ leading to $pv = R\frac{n}{N}T$); §8 ($P'$ as a sum of two terms); §9 (a negative-ion voltage five times larger).
   - `flag:s3-variational-displays`: §3's variational displays with $\lambda$ as a Lagrange multiplier.
   - `flag:s6-mean-energy`: §6's display of the mean quantum energy $3\frac{R}{N}T$.
   - `flag:s8-inequalities`: §8's partial-transfer inequality and the inverse (cathode-luminescence) inequality.
   - `flag:s9-count-relation`: §9's count relation $j = L/(R\beta\nu)$ and its printed bounds (expected $6.4\times10^{12}$ and $9.6\times10^{12}$ erg), with the printed inputs of each bound.
   - `flag:glyph-collisions`: one item per scoped collision above ($L$, $E$, $P$/$P'$/$p$, $\varphi$, $T$ and $\alpha_\nu$, $\lambda$, "lg"), each with first-use unit ids.
   - `flag:s7-thermal-caveat`: the thermal caveat in §7.
   - `flag:no-ultraviolet-catastrophe`: the phrase "ultraviolet catastrophe" does not occur (it is Ehrenfest's, 1911).
   - `flag:footnote-citations`: the citations in footnotes, recorded as reference occurrences exactly as printed.
   - `flag:dates`: the date-line and the receipt line against the typed dates in the `Paper` record (received 18 March 1905, published 9 June 1905).

### Counts

Record totals and per-page counts of headings, paragraphs starting on each page, display equations (numbered and unnumbered, including those inside footnotes), substantive inline equations, footnotes, reference occurrences, and closings. Reconcile them with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`.

## Technical Approach

- Work from page images of the pinned facsimile rendered locally at 300 dpi or more (for example `pdftoppm -r 300` into `artifacts/facsimile-renders/ap-17-132/`). **Local rendering is allowed; OCR and text-layer extraction are not.** If a cloud OCR draft exists, it may help locate paragraph boundaries, but the images decide.
- Write the manifest in the format of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`, ordered by printed position so reviews diff cleanly. Validate it with that bead's registered compiler check and its report CLI (`bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts light-quanta`).
- Assign display ids with `normalizePrintedLabel` from `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` and reference occurrence ids by counting occurrences per alignable unit in printed order.
- Generate `manifest.ids.snapshot.txt` from the validated manifest at freeze.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every unit kind listed above has entries with valid ids, locators, labels, containment, reference occurrences, and destinations; nothing is covered by a paper-level link.
- [ ] Every row of the treatment map has at least one argument obligation recorded against the right units.
- [ ] Display ids follow the printed-label rules, displays inside footnotes are contained in their footnotes, and inline math indices follow the count-every-region rule.
- [ ] Every reference sub-entry has an occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, `printedText`, `kind`, and a target or the unresolved flag.
- [ ] Counts reconcile with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`, and both are refined with section boundaries and equation locations.
- [ ] `content/aliases/light-quanta.yaml` exists and is empty; the manifest header declares `idsFrozenAt` and `frozenBy`; the snapshot is committed.
- [ ] The difficulties file has all four sections, with first-use ids, every `flag:` key above with a result, and the recomputed verification values above.
- [ ] The manifest validates with zero errors, and all derived statuses are `absent`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

`src/content/editions/lightQuanta.manifest.test.ts`, against the real manifest compiler check, id parsers, and alias resolver:
- The manifest validates: no duplicate ids, every id matches the grammar, every unit has at least one locator with strictly increasing 1-based page indices, and derived statuses are `absent` with no authored status fields.
- Every display has an `originalLabel` or `editorialLabel`, locators, and a `containedIn` value (a paragraph or a footnote) or a recorded standalone case; every display listed under `flag:fn-displays` is contained in a footnote.
- A computed map from `normalizePrintedLabel` over the printed labels equals the display ids: tokens repeated across sections map to section-qualified ids, and tokens repeated within a section to editorial ids.
- Inline math ids are unique per sentence or footnote, with indices of at least 1.
- Every reference sub-entry's id parses as a `ReferenceId`, its unit prefix is an alignable unit inside the containing unit, indices are unique per alignable unit, and `printedText`, `kind`, and a target or `reference-target-unresolved` are present.
- Per-page counts equal `SourceAsset.pageMapping` and the receipt page map.
- Every treatment-map row (`s0`, `s1` … `s9`, `closing`) has an obligation.
- The masthead, `closing-dateline`, and `closing-received` exist.
- Each footnote's section equals its mark's section.
- The alias file parses and is empty.
- The snapshot equals the manifest id list. A mutation copy under `artifacts/test-tmp/manifest-light-quanta/<log-run-id>/` that removes one id without an alias fails, and one with a split alias passes.
- Paper-specific:
  - nine numbered sections plus `s0`;
  - the difficulties file parses into every `flag:` key listed above, each with a result from the watch-list vocabulary;
  - `flag:s2-constants` records both exponents and `flag:s2-r-and-l-not-printed` a result; `flag:s8-printed-check` names the printed charge quantity; `flag:glyph-collisions` has an item for each of $L$, $E$, $P$/$P'$/$p$, $\varphi$, $T$ and $\alpha_\nu$, $\lambda$, and "lg";
  - the recomputed values in the file equal an independent computation in the test ($6.1705\times10^{23}$ and $6.1705\times10^{22}$ at relative $10^{-4}$; 4.3385 V, 4.3057 V, and 4.3087 V at $10^{-4}$ V), logged with `comparisonKind: tolerance` and the tolerance from `src/units/tolerance.ts`.

### End-to-end tests

- `src/content/editions/lightQuanta.manifest.e2e.test.ts` runs `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts light-quanta` through `Bun.spawn` and asserts:
  - exit code 0;
  - no unit lacks a destination;
  - per-page counts match `SourceAsset.pageMapping`;
  - the output contains no percentage.

  It then runs the content compiler's check over the corpus and asserts no rejection for this paper, and runs `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-132` (from `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`) and asserts the refined page map passes. Stdout, stderr, and the report JSON are retained on failure under `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-light-quanta/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.
- `am-edn-german-edition-light-quanta-eou` later runs the edition pipeline, whose reconciliation stage compares this manifest with the ledger.

### Structured logging

JSONL goes to `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-light-quanta/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library.
- Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-edn-inventory-light-quanta-skp"`, `paper: "light-quanta"`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance` (recomputed values), `comparisonKind` (`bitwise` for counts and id lists, `tolerance` for recomputed values), `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.
- `extra`: `{unitId, kind, referenceId, flagKey, pdfPageIndex, printedPage, check}`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Decide "substantive inline equation" generously: a symbol whose meaning a reader must track gets an entry. The count-every-region index rule means adding one later never shifts an id.
- Paragraphs and footnotes that cross pages keep one id with one locator per page.
- Count reference occurrences per alignable unit, not per paragraph.
- Do not transcribe or translate here, and never hand-author a status.
- The recomputations are context for the flags, not fixtures; the fixtures belong to the constants and photoelectric owners.
- The §8 photoelectric passage is famous; inventory §§1–7 and §9 with the same granularity, footnote displays included.
- Freezing is final: a later correction is an alias, so spend the care on doubtful boundaries now and list them.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-facsimile-light-quanta-t4n`: the pinned facsimile, its page images, and the page map.
- `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: the manifest format, the compiler check, and the report CLI.
- `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: JSONL logging and failure-evidence retention for the manifest tests.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-german-edition-light-quanta-eou`: edition blocks use these frozen ids and reference occurrence ids.
- `am-not-entries-light-quanta-9cb`: concordance entries are scoped to these sections and first-use ids.

NODE LANE IS RED AND IT IS A LANE-ASSIGNMENT BUG, not a test failure. For whoever resumes (pane %16 quota-blocked until ~06:45Z).

Measured in the static main working tree: bun run test:node exits 1 with
  Error [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME]: Only URLs with a scheme in: file, data, and node are supported by the default ESM loader. Received protocol 'bun:'

Chain:
- bunfig.toml [test] pathIgnorePatterns contains '**/*.e2e.test.ts'.
- scripts/run-node-only-tests.ts derives the node-only list FROM those patterns, so every *.e2e.test.ts is excluded from the bun lane and handed to Node instead. That design is deliberate and is what guarantees no test falls between the two lanes.
- src/content/editions/lightQuanta.manifest.e2e.test.ts imports from 'bun:test'. Node cannot load that scheme, so the whole node lane dies on it.

So the file is named into a lane it cannot run in. The .e2e.test.ts suffix is not a free-form label here - it is a lane selector.

CORRECT FIX: rename it out of the e2e pattern, e.g. src/content/editions/lightQuanta.manifest.integration.test.ts, so it stays in the BUN lane. That is the right lane for it: it uses Bun.spawn (which is also the source of the TS2339 'Property spawn does not exist' errors reported earlier), so it genuinely requires Bun and must not be a node-lane test.

DO NOT fix this by adding the file to pathIgnorePatterns a second time, by deleting it from the node list by hand, or by loosening run-node-only-tests.ts. Any of those would punch a hole in the both-lanes guarantee, which is a gate weakening. If you conclude the test really should run under Node, then rewrite it to node:test and node:assert/strict and drop Bun.spawn - but do not leave it importing bun:test under an e2e name.

Same check applies to brownian.manifest.e2e.test.ts, which is currently uncommitted in pane %15's working set and looks like the same shape.

pane31 resuming from pane16. LANE FIXED, but NOT by the rename in comment 726 - that rename would have broken a different gate. Evidence below.

WHY NOT THE RENAME. src/content/editions/lightQuanta.manifest.e2e.test.ts imports spawnSync from node:child_process and calls it (it spawns `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts` and `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts`; the Bun.spawn/TS2339 form named in comment 726 was already gone). scripts/quality-gates/bunfigNodeOnlyTests.ts:classifyTestFileContent flags exactly that shape as "spawns a subprocess without EBADF handling", and assertNoUnignoredSubprocessTests requires every such file to be matched by bunfig pathIgnorePatterns, i.e. to be in the NODE lane. Two live tests enforce it (subprocessE2eSplit.test.ts:70, bunfigNodeOnlyTests.test.ts:148).

Measured, against the real gate functions:
  classify(lightQuanta.manifest.e2e.test.ts) = "spawns a subprocess without EBADF handling"
  src/content/editions/lightQuanta.manifest.e2e.test.ts          ignoredByBunfig=true  -> lane=node
  src/content/editions/lightQuanta.manifest.integration.test.ts  ignoredByBunfig=false -> lane=bun

== THE ANSWER ==
Printed numbered items FOLD into the paragraph that introduces them. A run of enumerated items (1., 2., or a), b)) is not a unit of its own: the introducing sentence and the items it governs are one paragraph unit, and sentence ids run on through the items.

== I VERIFIED THE PRECEDENT RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT ==
You said brownian and relativity already do this. Neither SEGMENTATION.md nor the brownian or relativity difficulties files states the rule in words - I grepped all three - so there was nothing to read. I read it off the relativity manifest against the relativity facsimile instead.

  item 1           "1. Die Gesetze, nach denen sich die Zustaende..."
  item 2           "2. Jeder Lichtstrahl bewegt sich...", running on into the display
  display          Geschwindigkeit = Lichtweg / Zeitdauer
content/source-blocks/special-relativity/manifest.yaml records exactly ONE paragraph unit, s2-p1, before eq-s2-d1. Two separately numbered items cannot each hold a unit there, so they are already folded. Lower on the same page the operations a) and b) sit under "...ermitteln denken:" and likewise take no units of their own; they are inside s2-p2. That is decisive, so the convention is settled.

Page 145 (read at 400 dpi from the pinned ap-17-132.pdf) opens with §7's close:

title: Inventory every source unit of the mass-energy paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties
description:
# Inventory every source unit of the mass-energy paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §3.6, §4.5 step 1, §6.9, §11.3, §19.1, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Before anyone writes an explanation, the paper is inventoried into stable units. The inventory is the **source manifest**: it, not a hand-maintained percentage, decides whether the edition is complete, and a unit can never be "covered" by linking to the whole paper. Freezing ids in Batch A lets transcription, translation, readings, equations, instruments, and discovery work proceed in parallel against the same anchors. It produces the Batch A exit evidence that every original source unit has a destination.

The mass–energy paper (*Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig?*, Ann. Phys. (4) 18, 639–641, bibliographic key `ap-18-639`) is the first paper planned for completion in full (Batch D), and every unit of its three pages is in scope.

Its brevity makes a missing premise easy to hide and its printed notation easy to misremember. The plan's treatment map writes compact forms ($E'/E = \beta(\ldots)$, $H_0 - H_1 = L\beta$, $L(\beta - 1) = \ldots + \ldots$) that are editorial restatements. This inventory records what is actually printed, so no later layer imports a glyph the page does not have.

## Scope

In scope:
- `content/source-blocks/mass-energy/manifest.yaml`: every source unit with id, kind, locators, labels, containment, references, and destination, in the format owned by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`.
- `content/source-blocks/mass-energy/manifest.ids.snapshot.txt`: the frozen id list in manifest order.
- `content/aliases/mass-energy.yaml`: created empty at freeze. Its format is owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`, and it is the only way ids change after freezing.
- `docs/editorial/mass-energy-difficulties.md`: translation difficulties, notation difficulties, segmentation decisions, and verification flags.
- Refinement of the receipt's page map in `docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md`, in the format of `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: the front-matter `pageMap` entries (`sectionIds`, `displayEquations`, `footnoteMarks`, `refinedBy: am-edn-inventory-mass-energy-g2d`) and the `## Page map` body section. `SourceAsset.pageMapping` is derived from the same front matter by `receiptToSourceAsset`, so the two cannot diverge.

Out of scope:
- diplomatic text (`am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`) and German edition blocks (`am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv`);
- translation (`am-edn-translation-mass-energy-f3b`);
- concordance entries (`am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`);
- readings and equation records (`am-ep-mass-energy-siq`).

## Requirements

### Units to inventory

The paper has no sections, so every unit uses `s0` (paragraphs `s0-p<m>`, sentences `s0-p<m>-s<k>`).

| Unit | Id | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Title and author line | `masthead-title`, `masthead-author` | As printed |
| Headings | none | The paper has none |
| Paragraphs | `s0-p<m>` | See the expected paragraph list below |
| Sentences | `s0-p<m>-s<k>` | From page images, using the segmentation summary below |
| Displayed equations | `eq-<printed label>`; `eq-s0-d<j>` | See below |
| Substantive inline equations | `s0-p<m>-s<k>-m<i>` | `i` counts every inline math region of the sentence, 1-based, in printed order; gaps are expected |
| Footnotes | `s0-fn<k>` | Printed labels recorded |
| References | `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, sub-entries of the containing unit | See below |
| Date-line | `closing-dateline` | Expected "Bern, September 1905." |
| Journal receipt line | `closing-received` | Expected "(Eingegangen 27. September 1905.)"; verify both |
| Figures | none | Record `figures: none` in the manifest header |

**Paragraphs.** Every paragraph is inventoried, including the principle of relativity quoted as a separate paragraph (expected to end with "(Relativitätsprinzip)").

**Displayed equations.**
- **Ids:** `eq-<printed label>` or `eq-s0-d<j>` with `editorialLabel` `ed:s0-d<j>`.
- **Labels:** `originalLabel` exactly as printed, where a label exists.
- **Granularity:** one unit per printed display, including every intermediate line of the energy balances, the subtraction, the kinetic-energy relations, and the expansion, as printed.
- **Containment:** displays printed inside a paragraph record `containedIn`.

**Footnotes.** Expected: two footnotes on the first page, one citing the relativity paper and one remarking that the principle of the constancy of the velocity of light used there is contained in Maxwell's equations. Verify the count and wording on the facsimile.

**References.** Record each printed reference occurrence (a bibliographic citation or a reference to another paper) as a `references[]` sub-entry of the unit that contains it, in the shape of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: `{id, printedText, kind, target}`.
- `id` is the occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>` of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`: `i` counts the printed reference occurrences of that alignable unit in printed order, 1-based (`s0-p3-s2-r1` in a paragraph sentence, `s0-fn1-r1` in a footnote). The id names the occurrence, never its target.
- `printedText` is the reference exactly as printed; `kind` is `bibliographic`, `internal`, or `cross-paper`.
- `target` is `{citationId}` for a bibliographic reference, `{id}` for an internal one, and `{paper, id}` for a cross-paper one. A target record that does not exist yet stays unresolved; the manifest check reports it as the flag `reference-target-unresolved`, which becomes an error only when the paper is marked complete.
- Reference ids freeze with the other ids. An occurrence found after freeze takes the next unused index in its unit, so earlier ids never shift. The German edition's `reference` inline carries the same id as its `referenceId`.

Expected occurrences, all verified on the page images:
- the footnote's bibliographic citation of the relativity paper (`kind: bibliographic`, target the `Citation` for `ap-17-891`);
- the in-text reference to "§ 8" of that paper (`kind: cross-paper`, target the `special-relativity` exported §8 result);
- the in-text reference to its "§ 10" (the electron's kinetic energy; `kind: cross-paper`, target the `special-relativity` exported §10 unit).

The two §-references are separate occurrences with separate ids even when they sit in one sentence. The target ids come from `am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`. They may be recorded here as unresolved; `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv` resolves them.

**Journal furniture.** The issue article number, running heads, page numbers, and neighboring articles' text are not manifest units. The receipt's page map records them.

### Ids and freezing (canonical scheme owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`; follow it if it differs and record the difference)

- Ids are content ids, never array positions.
- At close, every id is frozen: the header records `idsFrozenAt` and `frozenBy`, and the snapshot is committed.
- Later changes are alias records in `content/aliases/mass-energy.yaml`, and retired ids are never reused.

**Sentence-boundary summary.** The full rules are in `docs/editorial/SEGMENTATION.md`, owned by `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`; use that document when it exists.
- **Boundary:** a sentence ends at `.`, `?`, or `!` followed by an uppercase letter or an opening quotation mark, or at the end of the paragraph.
- **Never a boundary:**
  - a colon or semicolon;
  - inside inline mathematics;
  - after an abbreviation (`z. B.`, `a. a. O.`, `d. h.`, `Ann. d. Phys.`, `p.`);
  - after initials (`A. Einstein`) or after `§ <n>.`;
  - inside a citation string (`Ann. d. Phys. 17. p. 891. 1905.`).
- **Displays:** a sentence continues through a display unless the display ends with a full stop and the next text begins with an uppercase letter.

Doubtful cases are listed in the difficulties file.

### Per-unit fields

- **`id`**, **`kind`**
- **`locators`:** an ordered list, one per page occupied, with `pdfPageIndex`, `printedPage`, and optional `region` as percentages from 0 to 100.
- **Labels and containment:** `originalLabel`, `editorialLabel`, `containedIn`, `references[]`.
- **`destination`:**
  - `editionBlockId`;
  - `translationUnits: planned`;
  - `argumentObligations`: from the treatment map below;
  - `notes`.

Statuses are **derived** by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa` and never hand-authored; at freeze every derived status is `absent`. The vocabulary is that of `SourceBlock.reviewState` in `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: `absent`, `machine-draft`, `drafted`, `corrected`, `reviewed`. Agents stop at `corrected` after an independent second read; only the human German source review sets `reviewed`.

### The paper's treatment map (record argument obligations against these rows)

Three printed pages, no section structure. The results column uses the plan's compact notation, with the expected printed form noted; the facsimile decides.

| Argument block | Required treatment | Results and checks |
|---|---|---|
| Imported result from paper 3 | Trace the radiation-energy transformation to §8 of the relativity paper; never use the desired mass–energy result as an input | plan: $E'/E = \beta(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$; expected printed: $l^* = l\,\frac{1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1 - (v/V)^2}}$ |
| Two equal opposite emissions | Explain the choice of symmetry and why the body stays at rest in its original frame | $\tfrac{1}{2}L$ each way |
| Energy balances in two frames | Track all before and after quantities with separate frame and event identifiers; the two transformed pulse energies sum to the angle-independent total for any emission angle | plan: $E_0 - E_1 = L$; $H_0 - H_1 = L\beta$ (expected printed with the explicit radical) |
| Subtraction and kinetic energy | Show the cancellation, the role of additive energy constants, and the identification of the frame-energy difference with the kinetic energy up to an additive constant $C$, which the print introduces as evident ("Es ist also klar …", expected) and the site treats as a stated premise in the explanation layers | plan: $K_0 - K_1 = L(\beta - 1)$ |
| Low-speed expansion | Derive the quadratic term and expose the approximation error | plan: $L(\beta - 1) = \tfrac{1}{2}\frac{L}{V^2}v^2 + \ldots$; the leading neglected term is $\tfrac{3}{8}\frac{L}{V^4}v^4$ (recomputed with python3: at $v/V = 0.01$, $\beta - 1 - \tfrac{1}{2}(v/V)^2 = 3.750313\times10^{-9}$ against $\tfrac{3}{8}(v/V)^4 = 3.75\times10^{-9}$); the print is expected to state the neglect of magnitudes of fourth and higher order in words rather than print an ellipsis |
| Inertia change and generalization | Separate the specific radiation argument, the broader inference, and the later modern formulation | the mass diminishes by $L/V^2$; the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content; an energy change $L$ in ergs changes the mass by $L/9\cdot10^{20}$ grams (expected printed; recomputed with python3, $(3\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm/s})^2 = 9\times10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm^2/s^2}$) |
| Empirical closing remarks | Preserve the conditional suggestion about radium salts and the conditional statement that radiation transfers inertia between emitting and absorbing bodies if the theory corresponds to the facts, without a nuclear-history digression | as printed |
| Date-line and receipt line | | "Bern, September 1905" |

**Editorial boundary.** The argument's additive constant and its reliance on the Newtonian form of kinetic energy at second order are premises (Ives 1952 called the argument circular; Stachel and Torretti 1982 answered). The formula $E = mc^2$ does not appear in the paper; the paper says the mass falls by $L/V^2$. The site neither pretends the 1905 argument is the last word nor pretends it is wrong.

### Notation entries this inventory must flag (for `am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`)

Each entry is recorded with its printed glyph and first-use unit id:
- $l$: the energy of the plane-wave system in the quoted result.
- $l^*$: that energy measured in the moving system.
- $L$: the emitted energy, $L/2$ each way; the speed of light in paper 1.
- $V$: the speed of light; $v$: the speed of the moving system.
- $\varphi$: the angle of the wave normal with the $x$-axis.
- $(x, y, z)$ and $(\xi, \eta, \zeta)$: the two systems.
- $E_0, E_1$: the body's energies before and after, in the rest system; $H_0, H_1$: the same in the moving system.
- $K$, $K_0$, $K_1$: kinetic energy; $C$: the additive constant.
- The numeral factor $9\cdot10^{20}$.
- **Whether $\beta$ occurs at all.** The print is expected to write $1/\sqrt{1 - (v/V)^2}$ explicitly. If $\beta$ is absent, record that, so the concordance and equation records treat any $\beta$ form as the site's editorial compact notation and never as a printed glyph, and so no bead flags $\beta$ as a printed collision in this paper.

### Difficulties file (`docs/editorial/mass-energy-difficulties.md`)

1. **Translation difficulties.**
   - Modality and qualification that must survive (expected wording, verify):
     - the energy principle "must" hold in both systems;
     - "Es ist also klar, daß …" introducing the additive-constant identification;
     - "offenbar unwesentlich" (evidently inessential) in the step from radiation to any form of energy;
     - "Unter Vernachlässigung von Größen vierter und höherer Ordnung";
     - "Es ist nicht ausgeschlossen, daß …" in the radium remark;
     - "Wenn die Theorie den Tatsachen entspricht, …" in the inertia-transfer sentence.
   - Long sentences that may need splitting; ambiguous references.
   - Period words for term annotations: *Trägheit*, *Energieinhalt*, *Lichtmenge*, *ebene Lichtwellen*, *Energieprinzip*, *Relativitätsprinzip*, *gleichförmige Paralleltranslation*, *Radiumsalze*, and *Lichtkomplex* only if it occurs, each with first-use unit ids.
2. **Notation difficulties:** every glyph above with its first-use unit id, and the printed form of every treatment-map result.
3. **Segmentation decisions:**
   - how the energy balances and the expansion are grouped into printed displays;
   - displays inside paragraphs;
   - the quoted principle as a paragraph;
   - doubtful sentence boundaries;
   - anything crossing the two page breaks.
4. **Verification flags:**
   - The two footnotes and their wording.
   - The cross-paper references to §8 and §10 of the relativity paper, their occurrence ids, and their target ids (from `am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`).
   - Whether an ellipsis is printed in the expansion. Transcribe exactly what is printed and never add or drop one.
   - The factor $9\cdot10^{20}$ with its stated units (erg and gram). Recomputed in review: $(3\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm/s})^2 = 9\times10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm^2/s^2}$.
   - The conditional wording of both closing remarks.
   - $E = mc^2$ is absent.
   - The date-line and receipt line against the typed dates (received 27 September 1905, published 21 November 1905).

### Counts

Record totals and per-page counts of paragraphs starting on each page, display equations, substantive inline equations, footnotes, references, and closings. Reconcile them with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`.

## Technical Approach

- Work from page images of the pinned facsimile rendered locally at 300 dpi or more (for example `pdftoppm -r 300` into `artifacts/facsimile-renders/ap-18-639/`). **Local rendering is allowed; OCR and text-layer extraction are not.** A cloud OCR draft may help locate paragraph boundaries, but the images decide.
- Write the manifest in the format of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`, ordered by printed position. Validate it with that bead's compiler check and `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts mass-energy`.
- Generate the snapshot at freeze.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every unit kind listed above has entries with valid ids, locators, labels, containment, references, and destinations; nothing is covered by a paper-level link.
- [ ] Every row of the treatment map has at least one argument obligation recorded against the right units.
- [ ] Every intermediate printed display has its own unit, and inline math indices follow the count-every-region rule.
- [ ] Every reference sub-entry has an occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, `printedText`, `kind`, and a target or the unresolved flag; the footnote citation and the §8 and §10 cross-paper references each have their own id.
- [ ] Counts reconcile with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`, and both are refined.
- [ ] `content/aliases/mass-energy.yaml` exists and is empty; the header declares `idsFrozenAt` and `frozenBy`; the snapshot is committed.
- [ ] The difficulties file has all four sections; the notation section states whether $\beta$ is printed and records the printed form of every result.
- [ ] The manifest validates with zero errors, and all derived statuses are `absent`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

`src/content/editions/massEnergy.manifest.test.ts`, against the real manifest compiler check and alias resolver:
- The manifest validates: no duplicate ids, grammar-valid ids, at least one locator per unit, derived statuses `absent`, no authored statuses.
- Every id begins with `s0`, `masthead-`, `closing-`, or `eq-`.
- Every display has a label and locators.
- Per-page counts equal `SourceAsset.pageMapping` and the receipt page map.
- Every treatment-map block has an obligation.
- The masthead, `closing-dateline`, and `closing-received` exist.
- The footnote count equals the image-verified count recorded in the difficulties file.
- Reference sub-entries of kinds `bibliographic` and `cross-paper` exist, with targets naming `ap-17-891` and the relativity paper's §8 and §10.
- Reference occurrence ids: every sub-entry id matches `<containing unit id>-r<i>` with `i` starting at 1 and contiguous within its unit, ids are unique across the manifest, and no id encodes its target. A mutation copy that renumbers an existing reference id, or that gives the §10 reference the §8 id, fails.
- The notation section of the difficulties file contains an explicit yes-or-no entry for the printed occurrence of $\beta$.
- The alias file is empty; the snapshot equals the manifest; a mutation copy removing an id without an alias fails.

### End-to-end tests

- `src/content/editions/massEnergy.manifest.e2e.test.ts` runs `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts mass-energy` through `Bun.spawn` and asserts:
  - exit code 0;
  - no unit lacks a destination;
  - per-page counts match;
  - no percentage in the output.

  It then runs the content compiler's check over the corpus, and runs `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-18-639` (from `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`) and asserts the refined page map passes. Stdout, stderr, and report JSON are retained under `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-mass-energy/<log-run-id>/evidence/` on failure, and a marked canary proves the evidence path.
- `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv` later runs the edition pipeline against this manifest and resolves the cross-paper targets.

### Structured logging

JSONL goes to `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-mass-energy/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library.
- Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-edn-inventory-mass-energy-g2d"`, `paper: "mass-energy"`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.
- `extra`: `{unitId, kind, referenceId, pdfPageIndex, printedPage, check, evidencePath}`.
- A report or render run referenced from a log event carries its id as `toolRunId`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Three pages invite coarse units; inventory every sentence and every intermediate printed display.
- The compact $\beta$ forms and "$+\ldots$" in the plan are restatements. Recording them as printed would plant a false glyph in every later layer.
- A reference id names an occurrence, not a target. Two references to the same paper in one sentence are two ids, and resolving a target later never changes an id.
- Do not transcribe or translate here, and never hand-author a status.
- Paragraphs and footnotes that cross pages keep one id with one locator per page.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-facsimile-mass-energy-cat`: the pinned facsimile, its page images, and the page map.
- `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: the manifest format, the compiler check, and the report CLI.
- `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: JSONL logging for the manifest tests.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv`: edition blocks use these frozen ids and carry these reference occurrence ids.
- `am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`: concordance entries are scoped to these first-use ids and printed glyphs.

1. **An error in the difficulties file, contradicted by the page.** It described `s0-p3` ("Die Gesetze, nach denen sich die Zustände…") as "formatted as an indented block quotation in the original print". At 300% its first line carries the ordinary paragraph indent and all four continuation lines sit flush at the normal left margin, with the normal right margin. It is an ordinary indented paragraph. Corrected in place, with the reason stated: a block quotation and an indented paragraph are told apart by the *continuation* lines, which is the same discriminator the whole segmentation rests on.
2. **Stale retired ids cited as live.** The difficulties file cited `s0-p8`, `s0-p9` and `s0-p10` as live anchors in eight places — the modality list, the period-vocabulary first-use list, two notation-collision entries, two glyph first-use entries, and two treatment-map rows. Those ids were retired by this bead's own repair. Repointed to `s0-p7`, each keeping the retired id in parentheses for traceability. The sentence-level locators inside the merged run (`s0-p9-s2` … `s0-p9-s5`) are deliberately **not** renumbered: inventing a sentence sequence for the merged paragraph would be fabrication, and no manifest can hold a sentence unit until the `am-xz2d` ruling lands. They now carry an explicit note saying to read them as locators into `s0-p7`, not as live ids.

CONVENTIONS RECORDED in `docs/editorial/mass-energy-difficulties.md`, as asked:
- The indent-versus-flush rule was already there from the earlier audit and I left it intact; I appended the measured indent steps, the full denominator, and the three confirmed retirements.
- **Item folding: stated as inapplicable rather than left silent.** All three pages print no numbered list, no lettered item and no printed equation label, so the light-quanta folding rule has no instance here. The record says so explicitly, and says that if a later reading finds one, the light-quanta rule governs it.
- Two page facts recorded so no later layer re-derives them: the stacked `H_0 - E_0 = K_0 + C,` / `H_1 - E_1 = K_1 + C,` pair on p. 641 is **one** display (`eq-s0-d5`), and the two-line `H_0 = H_1 + [...]` with its right-aligned continuation on p. 640 is **one** display (`eq-s0-d3`). Counting either as two would inflate the display census by two, which is the display-side twin of the flush-line error.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for the edition files.
- No manifest change was needed, so no new alias records. Files touched: `docs/editorial/mass-energy-difficulties.md` only.

Not closing. Relativity and brownian remain; relativity has had 31 of 31 pages at 250 percent or more and brownian 12 of 12 at 155 to 260 percent, so if you want the same 300% standard applied uniformly, brownian's seven full-page reads at 155% are the weakest link and I would redo those next.
