title: Inventory every source unit of the relativity paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties
description:
# Inventory every source unit of the relativity paper, freeze ids, and list translation and notation difficulties

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §3.5, §4.5 step 1, §6.9, §11.3, §19.1, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Before anyone writes an explanation, the paper is inventoried into stable units. The inventory is the **source manifest**: it, not a hand-maintained percentage, decides whether the edition is complete, and a unit can never be "covered" by linking to the whole paper. Freezing ids in Batch A lets transcription, translation, readings, equations, instruments, and discovery work proceed in parallel against the same anchors. It produces the Batch A exit evidence that every original source unit has a destination.

The relativity paper (*Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper*, Ann. Phys. (4) 17, 891–921, bibliographic key `ap-17-891`) is the longest. Popular accounts drop its second half; the inventory gives §§6–10 the same granularity as §§1–5. The mass–energy paper imports its §8 light-energy result and refers to its §10 electron kinetic energy, so those ids are needed early and are exported by id.

## Scope

In scope:
- `content/source-blocks/special-relativity/manifest.yaml`: every source unit with id, kind, locators, labels, containment, references, destination, and the header's `exportedResults`, in the format owned by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`.
- `content/source-blocks/special-relativity/manifest.ids.snapshot.txt`: the frozen id list in manifest order.
- `content/aliases/special-relativity.yaml`: created empty at freeze. Its format is owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`, and it is the only way ids change after freezing.
- `docs/editorial/special-relativity-difficulties.md`: translation difficulties, notation difficulties, segmentation decisions, and verification flags.
- Refinement of the receipt's page map in `docs/provenance/ap-17-891.md`, in the format of `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: the front-matter `pageMap` entries (`sectionIds`, `displayEquations`, `footnoteMarks`, `refinedBy: am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`) and the `## Page map` body section. `SourceAsset.pageMapping` is derived from the same front matter by `receiptToSourceAsset`, so the two cannot diverge.

Out of scope:
- diplomatic text (`am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`) and German edition blocks (`am-edn-german-edition-relativity-9p5`);
- translation (`am-edn-translation-relativity-s0-s5-hm8`, `am-edn-translation-relativity-s6-s10-qkn`);
- concordance entries (`am-not-entries-relativity-f6e`);
- readings and equation records (the relativity epics).

## Requirements

### Units to inventory

| Unit | Id | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Title and author line | `masthead-title`, `masthead-author` | As printed |
| Part headings | `part-1`, `part-2` | Expected *I. Kinematischer Teil* and *II. Elektrodynamischer Teil* |
| Section headings | `s1` … `s10` | Global numbering across both parts |
| Paragraphs | `s<n>-p<m>` | The unnumbered introduction is `s0` |
| Sentences | `s<n>-p<m>-s<k>` | From page images, using the segmentation summary below |
| Displayed equations | `eq-<printed label>`; `eq-s<n>-<printed>`; `eq-s<n>-d<j>` | See below |
| Substantive inline equations and nontrivial symbol occurrences | `s<n>-p<m>-s<k>-m<i>` | `i` counts every inline math region of the sentence, 1-based, in printed order; gaps are expected |
| Footnotes | `s<n>-fn<k>` | Numbered within the section of the mark; the printed label is recorded |
| References | `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, sub-entries of the containing unit | Internal cross-references only; see below |
| Acknowledgment to M. Besso | `closing-ack` | |
| Date-line | `closing-dateline` | Expected "Bern, Juni 1905." |
| Journal receipt line | `closing-received` | Expected "(Eingegangen 30. Juni 1905.)"; verify each |
| Figures | none | Record `figures: none` in the manifest header |

**Displayed equations.**
- **Ids:** `eq-<printed label>` when the printed label is unique in the paper; `eq-s<n>-<printed>` when it repeats in another section; `eq-s<n>-d<j>` for an unnumbered display, with `editorialLabel` `ed:s<n>-d<j>`.
- **Labels:** `originalLabel` keeps the printed label exactly.
- **Granularity:** one unit per printed display, so a printed group of field-component equations under one brace or label is one unit. Component-level addressing belongs to equation records, never to splitting a printed display.
- **Containment:** a display printed inside a paragraph records `containedIn`.

**Footnotes.** Inventory every footnote. The list is expected to include §1's footnote declining to discuss the inexactness in the concept of the simultaneity of two events at approximately the same place; verify the complete list on the facsimile and do not assume others. The introduction's statement that the theory rests on the kinematics of the rigid body is body text, not a footnote.

**References.** The paper cites no literature, so no `bibliographic` sub-entry is expected. Record each printed internal cross-reference (for example "§ 3" within the paper) as a `references[]` sub-entry of the unit that contains it, in the shape of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: `{id, printedText, kind, target}`.
- `id` is the occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>` of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`: `i` counts the printed reference occurrences of that alignable unit in printed order, 1-based (`s6-p2-s1-r1` in a paragraph sentence, `s1-fn1-r1` in a footnote). The id names the occurrence, never its target.
- `printedText` is the reference exactly as printed; `kind` is `internal` here (`bibliographic` and `cross-paper` are available in the shape but not expected in this paper).
- `target` is `{id}` for an internal reference. A target that cannot be resolved yet stays unresolved; the manifest check reports it as the flag `reference-target-unresolved`, which becomes an error only when the paper is marked complete.
- Reference ids freeze with the other ids. An occurrence found after freeze takes the next unused index in its unit, so earlier ids never shift. The German edition's `reference` inline carries the same id as its `referenceId`.

**Journal furniture.** The issue article number, running heads, page numbers, and neighboring articles' text are not manifest units. The receipt's page map records them.

### Exported results

The manifest header declares `exportedResults`:
- the id of the §8 display that states the energy transformation of a light complex (in the plan's notation $E'/E = \beta(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$, printed form recorded in the difficulties file);
- the id of the §10 unit that states the electron's kinetic energy (the plan's $W = mV^2(\beta - 1)$; printed symbols recorded in the difficulties file).

The mass–energy paper cites both by id, through two separate reference occurrences. `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa` rejects an import of an id not listed here.

### Ids and freezing (canonical scheme owned by `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`; follow it if it differs and record the difference)

- Ids are content ids, never array positions.
- At close, every id is frozen: the header records `idsFrozenAt` and `frozenBy`, and the snapshot is committed.
- Later changes are alias records in `content/aliases/special-relativity.yaml`, and retired ids are never reused.
- Inventory the §8 and §10 exported units first, so `am-me-equations-0mgx` and `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv` can cite them.

**Sentence-boundary summary.** The full rules are in `docs/editorial/SEGMENTATION.md`, owned by `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`; use that document when it exists.
- **Boundary:** a sentence ends at `.`, `?`, or `!` followed by an uppercase letter or an opening quotation mark, or at the end of the paragraph.
- **Never a boundary:**
  - a colon or semicolon;
  - inside inline mathematics;
  - after an abbreviation (`z. B.`, `d. h.`, `u. s. w.`, `vgl.`, `a. a. O.`, `S.`, `p.`, `Sek.`);
  - after initials (`M. Besso`), after an ordinal before a noun, or after `§ <n>.`;
  - inside a citation string.
- **Displays:** a sentence continues through a display unless the display ends with a full stop and the next text begins with an uppercase letter.

Doubtful cases are listed in the difficulties file.

### Per-unit fields

- **`id`**, **`kind`**
- **`locators`:** an ordered list, one per page occupied, with `pdfPageIndex`, `printedPage`, and optional `region` as percentages from 0 to 100.
- **Labels and containment:** `originalLabel`, `editorialLabel`, `containedIn`, `references[]`.
- **`destination`:**
  - `editionBlockId`;
  - `translationUnits: planned`;
  - `argumentObligations`: from the treatment map below;
  - `notes`.

Statuses are **derived** by `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa` and never hand-authored; at freeze every derived status is `absent`. The vocabulary is that of `SourceBlock.reviewState` in `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: `absent`, `machine-draft`, `drafted`, `corrected`, `reviewed`. Agents stop at `corrected` after an independent second read; only the human German source review sets `reviewed`.

### The paper's treatment map (record argument obligations against these rows)

Thirty-one pages, ten numbered sections in two parts, no figures, no references to literature, a closing acknowledgment to M. Besso. Both halves receive serious effort. German titles are expected wording; verify against the facsimile. The results column uses the plan's notation (compact $\beta$ forms and $m$); the printed form of each result is recorded in the difficulties file.

| Original part | Reader's central question | Required treatment | Results and printed checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Introduction | Why does moving the magnet instead of the conductor create an explanatory asymmetry? | Apparatus, frame descriptions, measurable agreement, scoped electrodynamics; failed ether-drift detections; the two postulates; the ether declared superfluous insofar as no absolutely stationary space is needed | the two postulates, verbatim |
| I. Kinematic part (*Kinematischer Teil*), §1 Simultaneity (*Definition der Gleichzeitigkeit*) | How can distant clocks acquire an operational common time? | Signal exchange, the synchronization convention, event records, event versus reception | $t_B - t_A = t'_A - t_B$ |
| §2 Lengths and times (*Über die Relativität von Längen und Zeiten*) | What do measurements of a moving rod actually compare? | Endpoint events and simultaneity; observers moving with the rod find its clocks unsynchronized | the relativity of simultaneity |
| §3 Coordinate and time transformation (*Theorie der Koordinaten- und Zeittransformation von dem ruhenden auf ein relativ zu diesem in gleichförmiger Translationsbewegung befindliches System*) | What map reconciles the postulates? | Full derivation: linearity assumptions, the remaining scale factor, reciprocity and isotropy, the inverse, the transverse step done honestly | $\tau = \beta(t - vx/V^2)$, $\xi = \beta(x - vt)$, $\eta = y$, $\zeta = z$, $\beta = (1 - v^2/V^2)^{-1/2}$ |
| §4 Physical meaning (*Physikalische Bedeutung der erhaltenen Gleichungen, bewegte starre Körper und bewegte Uhren betreffend*) | What do clocks and rods report in different frames? | Contraction, dilation, transported clocks, curved paths, the equator remark with its limit-of-model note | ellipsoid axes $R\sqrt{1 - v^2/V^2}, R, R$; a moving clock loses $1 - \sqrt{1 - v^2/V^2}$ per second, or $\tfrac{1}{2}v^2/V^2$ neglecting magnitudes of fourth and higher order (expected printed wording; recomputed with python3, $1 - \sqrt{1 - x^2} - \tfrac{1}{2}x^2 = \tfrac{1}{8}x^4 + \ldots$, at $x = 0.01$ a residual of $1.2500625\times10^{-9}$ against $\tfrac{1}{8}x^4 = 1.25\times10^{-9}$, so the printed fourth-order qualification is exact) |
| §5 Velocity addition (*Additionstheorem der Geschwindigkeiten*) | Why doesn't adding ordinary speeds preserve light speed? | Differentiate the map; transverse components; limits; the group property | $U = \frac{v + w}{1 + vw/V^2}$; two boosts give a boost |
| II. Electrodynamic part (*Elektrodynamischer Teil*), §6 Maxwell–Hertz transformation (*Transformation der Maxwell-Hertzschen Gleichungen für den leeren Raum. Über die Natur der bei Bewegung in einem Magnetfeld auftretenden elektromotorischen Kräfte*) | How do electric and magnetic descriptions change together? | Chain rule, field components, unit conventions, transformed equations component by component, the ansatz and normalization argument; the magnet/conductor reconciliation | $X' = X$, $Y' = \beta(Y - \frac{v}{V}N)$, $Z' = \beta(Z + \frac{v}{V}M)$, $L' = L$, $M' = \beta(M + \frac{v}{V}Z)$, $N' = \beta(N - \frac{v}{V}Y)$ |
| §7 Doppler and aberration (*Theorie des Doppler'schen Prinzipes und der Aberration*) | How do frequency and propagation direction transform? | Wavefront phase and linked angle and frequency treatments, not sound analogies as proof | $\nu' = \nu\beta(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$; $\cos\varphi' = \frac{\cos\varphi - v/V}{1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}$ |
| §8 Light energy and moving mirrors (*Transformation der Energie der Lichtstrahlen. Theorie des auf vollkommene Spiegel ausgeübten Strahlungsdruckes*) | Why do amplitude and enclosed volume both matter? | Transform a finite light complex (amplitude and volume factors combine); then the mirror with interception checks | $E'/E = \beta(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi) = \nu'/\nu$; mirror pressure proportional to $\frac{(\cos\varphi - v/V)^2}{1 - v^2/V^2}$ in Gaussian units |
| §9 Convection currents (*Transformation der Maxwell-Hertzschen Gleichungen mit Berücksichtigung der Konvektionsströme*) | How do charge density and moving charge fit the transformation? | Charge and current density, continuity, frame changes; neutral current-carrying cases accepted | the transformed equations with $\rho$ |
| §10 Electron dynamics (*Dynamik des (langsam beschleunigten) Elektrons*) | What force, work, energy, and deflection relations follow? | The slowly accelerated electron; historical force and mass conventions preserved and explained; the work integral; the three relations "accessible to experiment" | longitudinal mass $m\beta^3$, transverse mass $m\beta^2$ (source force convention); $W = mV^2(\beta - 1)$ |
| Closing | Who and what does the paper acknowledge? | The Besso acknowledgment, the date-line, the receipt line, the footnotes | "Bern, Juni 1905" |

**Editorial boundary.**
- **§10.** §10's transverse coefficient corresponds to $m\gamma^2$ in modern factor notation because the source combines force components in the instantaneously comoving frame with acceleration components in the original frame; Planck's 1906 convention gives $m\gamma$. The site presents §10 as printed, explains which frame's force and acceleration are compared, and offers a clearly identified modern momentum treatment beside the faithful edition. It does not repair the source.
- **Equator clock.** The equator-clock remark is shown as printed with a short limit-of-model note: on the rotating geoid, gravitational and kinematic effects approximately cancel, and that account needs later physics.

### Notation entries this inventory must flag (for `am-not-entries-relativity-f6e`)

Each entry is recorded with its printed glyph and first-use unit id:
- $V \to c$.
- $\beta \to \gamma$: the modern $\beta = v/c$ appears nowhere in this paper; a dangerous collision flagged in red on first use.
- $(\xi, \eta, \zeta, \tau) \to (x', y', z', t')$: the moving-frame time $\tau$ must not be read as the modern proper-time symbol.
- The §3 Galilean auxiliary $x' = x - vt$ is not the moving-frame coordinate. Flag every occurrence, so the modern notation form can give it a distinct glyph.
- $(X, Y, Z) \to \mathbf{E}$ and $(L, M, N) \to \mathbf{B}$ in Gaussian units. The unit conversion is a separate concordance operation. $N$ here is a magnetic-field component, not Avogadro's number, and $L$ is a magnetic-field component in §6.
- $\varphi \to$ the angle between the wave normal and the boost axis.
- "light complex" (*Lichtkomplex*) $\to$ a finite plane-wave packet.
- $K$ and $k \to$ the stationary and moving coordinate systems.
- §10: the printed symbols for the electron's mass and charge (expected $\mu$ and $\varepsilon$, while the treatment map writes $m$); verify.
- §10: whether the paper prints named symbols for the deflectability of the three relations "accessible to experiment" (the comparison witness reads $A_m$ and $A_e$) and, if so, their printed definitions. `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7` holds `magneticDeflectability` and `electricDeflectability` as reserved spellings, and `am-sre-equations-2g3h` adds records for them only if this check reports them printed; a negative result is recorded just as explicitly.

### Difficulties file (`docs/editorial/special-relativity-difficulties.md`)

1. **Translation difficulties.**
   - Modality and qualification that must survive, including (expected wording, verify):
     - the introduction's raising of a conjecture (*Vermutung*) to a presupposition (*Voraussetzung*);
     - the "only apparently incompatible" second presupposition;
     - the ether being superfluous "insofar as" no absolutely stationary space is needed;
     - §1's stipulation (*festsetzen*) of equal light times, and the constancy of $2AB/(t'_A - t_A)$ stipulated "in accordance with experience";
     - §3's linearity justified by the homogeneity "that we attribute to space and time";
     - §4's assumption that the polygonal-path result holds for continuously curved paths;
     - §4's approximation wording (expected: neglecting magnitudes of fourth and higher order, never "to first order" or "to second order").
   - Long sentences that may need splitting; ambiguous references.
   - Period words for term annotations: *ruhendes System*, *Lichtkomplex*, *Lichtäther*, *Beobachter*, *Prinzip der Relativität*, *starrer Körper*, *elektromotorische Kraft*, *Konvektionsstrom*, *vollkommener Spiegel*, *longitudinale Masse*, and *transversale Masse*, each with first-use unit ids. *Kathodenstrahlen* is not expected: a comparison witness text of this paper contains no *Kathodenstrahl*. Add it only if the facsimile shows it, and never place it in §10 from memory.
2. **Notation difficulties:** every scoped glyph and collision above, with first-use unit ids.
3. **Segmentation decisions:**
   - doubtful sentence boundaries;
   - displays before the first paragraph of a section;
   - how the §6 and §9 systems of equations are grouped into printed displays;
   - words, paragraphs, and footnotes crossing page breaks.
4. **Verification flags:**
   - For each treatment-map result, whether the print uses $\beta$ or the explicit radical $\sqrt{1 - (v/V)^2}$; in particular §§3, 4, 7, 8, and 10.
   - The §4 approximation wording (expected: neglecting magnitudes of fourth and higher order) and the equator remark's qualification (expected: under otherwise identical conditions).
   - The §10 mass and charge symbols and the printed forms of the longitudinal mass, the transverse mass, and the kinetic energy.
   - The §7 heading's printed spelling. A comparison witness reads *Doppelerschen* where the expected wording is *Doppler'schen*. If the scan confirms the misspelling, the ledger and German edition keep it as printed, and the receipt's `typographicalErrors` records it (layer `source`). Nothing silently corrects it.
   - The complete footnote list, with the §1 simultaneity footnote confirmed and nothing assumed from a secondary account. The introduction's rigid-body statement is recorded as body text.
   - The absence of references to literature, and the list of printed internal cross-references with their occurrence ids.
   - The exact location and ids of the exported §8 and §10 results.
   - The date-line and receipt line against the typed dates (received 30 June 1905, published 26 September 1905).

### Counts

Record totals and per-page counts of headings, paragraphs starting on each page, display equations (numbered and unnumbered), substantive inline equations, footnotes, internal references, and closings. Reconcile them with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`.

## Technical Approach

- Work from page images of the pinned facsimile rendered locally at 300 dpi or more (for example `pdftoppm -r 300` into `artifacts/facsimile-renders/ap-17-891/`). **Local rendering is allowed; OCR and text-layer extraction are not.** A cloud OCR draft may help locate paragraph boundaries, but the images decide.
- Write the manifest in the format of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`, ordered by printed position. Validate it with that bead's compiler check and `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts special-relativity`.
- Generate the snapshot at freeze, after the exported units are recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every unit kind listed above has entries with valid ids, locators, labels, containment, references, and destinations; nothing is covered by a paper-level link.
- [ ] Every row of the treatment map has at least one argument obligation recorded against the right units.
- [ ] `exportedResults` lists the §8 energy-transformation display and the §10 kinetic-energy unit, and both ids resolve.
- [ ] Repeated printed labels use section-qualified ids; inline math indices follow the count-every-region rule; each §6 and §9 printed display is one unit.
- [ ] Every internal reference sub-entry has an occurrence id `<alignableUnitId>-r<i>`, `printedText`, `kind: internal`, and a target or the unresolved flag; no `bibliographic` sub-entry exists.
- [ ] Counts reconcile with the receipt's page map and `SourceAsset.pageMapping`, and both are refined.
- [ ] `content/aliases/special-relativity.yaml` exists and is empty; the header declares `idsFrozenAt` and `frozenBy`; the snapshot is committed.
- [ ] The difficulties file has all four sections, with first-use ids, and its footnote flag records the verified list.
- [ ] The manifest validates with zero errors, and all derived statuses are `absent`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

`src/content/editions/relativity.manifest.test.ts`, against the real manifest compiler check and alias resolver:
- The manifest validates: no duplicate ids, grammar-valid ids, at least one locator per unit, derived statuses `absent`, no authored statuses.
- Every display has a label, locators, and containment or a recorded standalone case.
- Repeated labels match section-qualified ids; inline math ids are unique per sentence.
- Per-page counts equal `SourceAsset.pageMapping` and the receipt page map.
- Every treatment-map row (`s0` … `s10`, `closing`) has an obligation.
- `part-1` precedes `s1`, and `part-2` precedes `s6`.
- The masthead, `closing-ack`, `closing-dateline`, and `closing-received` exist.
- `exportedResults` contains exactly one `s8` display and one `s10` unit, and both resolve.
- No bibliographic reference sub-entry exists; every internal sub-entry id matches `<containing unit id>-r<i>` with `i` starting at 1 and contiguous within its unit, ids are unique across the manifest, and no id encodes its target. A mutation copy that renumbers an existing reference id fails.
- The footnote list equals the list recorded in the difficulties file, and no footnote unit lives in `s0` unless the difficulties file records one there.
- The alias file is empty; the snapshot equals the manifest; a mutation copy removing an exported id without an alias fails.

### End-to-end tests

- `src/content/editions/relativity.manifest.e2e.test.ts` runs `bun scripts/source-manifest-report.ts special-relativity` through `Bun.spawn` and asserts:
  - exit code 0;
  - no unit lacks a destination;
  - per-page counts match;
  - no percentage in the output.

  It then runs the content compiler's check over the corpus. A fixture import from the mass–energy side that names a non-exported relativity id is rejected, and one naming the exported §8 id is accepted. It also runs `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-891` (from `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`) and asserts the refined page map passes. Stdout, stderr, and report JSON are retained under `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-special-relativity/<log-run-id>/evidence/` on failure, and a marked canary proves the evidence path.
- `am-edn-german-edition-relativity-9p5` later runs the edition pipeline against this manifest.

### Structured logging

JSONL goes to `artifacts/test-logs/manifest-special-relativity/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library.
- Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9"`, `paper: "special-relativity"`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.
- `extra`: `{unitId, kind, referenceId, pdfPageIndex, printedPage, check, evidencePath}`.
- A report or render run referenced from a log event carries its id as `toolRunId`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Decide "substantive inline equation" generously; the count-every-region index rule means adding one later never shifts an id.
- Paragraphs and footnotes that cross pages keep one id with one locator per page.
- Do not transcribe or translate here, and never hand-author a status.
- The treatment map's compact $\beta$ and $m$ forms are the plan's notation; the facsimile decides the printed glyphs, and the difficulties file records them.
- Do not invent footnotes from memory; verify each on the page image. Secondary accounts describe a rigid-body caveat as a footnote, and the witness shows it as body text.
- A reference id names an occurrence, not a target. Two cross-references in one sentence are two ids.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-facsimile-relativity-kav`: the pinned facsimile, its page images, and the page map.
- `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: the manifest format, `exportedResults`, the compiler check, and the report CLI.
- `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: JSONL logging for the manifest tests.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-german-edition-relativity-9p5`: edition blocks use these frozen ids and carry these reference occurrence ids.
- `am-not-entries-relativity-f6e`: concordance entries are scoped to these sections and first-use ids.
- `am-me-equations-0mgx`: the mass–energy paper's imported §8 result cites these ids.
- `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv`: the mass–energy footnote and cross-references resolve to the exported ids.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
=== METHOD NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP (pane30, written before context reset) ===
Everything needed to repeat or extend this work. Read this before re-deriving anything.

1. THE DISCRIMINATOR: FLUSH VERSUS INDENT
A new paragraph in this 1905 setting begins with an INDENTED first line, about 55 px at the 200 dpi
renders, and the indent is present even at the very top of a page. Three things are FLUSH to the
left margin and are NOT new paragraphs:
  (a) a line resuming after a displayed equation, however much prose follows and however many
      further displays it introduces;
  (b) a line continuing across a page break - often provable independently by a word hyphenated
      across the two pages (brownian p.560/561 "addi-"/"tiven" is the clean example);
  (c) connective words set on their own line ("oder", "und", "wobei", "also").
Printed numbered or lettered items (1., 2., a), b)) ARE indented but are NOT separate paragraphs:
they fold into the sentence that introduces them. That folding rule governs relativity §1 p.894,
§2 p.895, §6 pp.909-910, §10 pp.920-921, and the sibling rules recorded for light-quanta and
brownian. Reversing it moves all four papers together.
Stacked equations LEFT-ALIGNED WITH EACH OTHER, no text between, are ONE display, not several.
That rule settled d-tau/d-y and d-tau/d-z on relativity p.899 at 280 percent, and it is the same
rule that makes the mass-energy H0-E0 / H1-E1 pair a single unit.

2. MAGNIFICATIONS: WHAT WORKED, WHAT MISLED
  130-150 percent strips: good enough to FIND candidates, NOT good enough to decide them. They
    produced three false positives in relativity (p.911, p.918, p.920 all flagged, all clean at
    250) and one false negative (p.902 read as "1 start", actually zero).
  250 percent, two vertical bands per page: the working standard. Everything in the final passes
    was decided here.
  280-330 percent: used for single disputed lines and for display grouping.
Crop recipe that works: left-margin window ~320 px wide at 250 percent, two bands per page
(y 125..795 and y 770..1470), two pages side by side. Text column x differs by parity: relativity
odd pages ~80, even ~275; brownian ~80-95; mass-energy ~120-225. GET THE COLUMN RIGHT - several
crops landed mid-text and showed nothing usable, which wastes a read and can look like evidence.

3. WHY THE AUTOMATED DETECTOR WAS DISCARDED
I wrote a numpy line-left-edge detector to find indents mechanically. It was abandoned, and the
reason matters more than the tool. It (i) crashed on some pages, and a crash printed through a
pipe read as "0 indents" - a failing tool is not an empty result; (ii) silently picked the
facing-page sliver as the text column on pages where the scan includes one, giving a wrong
baseline; (iii) was defeated by italics and descenders shifting left edges by a few px. Worst, its
failures LOOKED like clean measurements. Also note: `cmd | grep ...; echo $?` reports grep's exit
status, not the command's - that produced several bogus "exit=0" claims about the report CLI before
it was caught. Use direct invocation and check the real exit code.

4. WHY A COUNT CHECK CANNOT SEE THIS CLASS
Boundary pass = compare, per page, number of printed indented starts vs number of recorded starts.
Denominator/one-to-one pass = for EVERY unit on a page, name the printed line it begins at, and
check every display and footnote into the paragraph the print puts it in.
They catch different things. A page with one spurious unit AND one missing paragraph nets to zero
and passes the count check. Relativity's s3-p19 on p.902 was exactly this: cleared by the boundary
pass as "1 vs 1", and in fact the page carries NO indented line at all. Across relativity the
errors also partly cancelled in aggregate - 101 recorded starts vs 93 printed - so totals look
plausible while boundaries are wrong. NEVER accept a count as evidence of a clean page.

5. PER-PAPER DENOMINATORS, FINAL
  relativity  ap-17-891  31/31 pages 1:1 at 250%+. 220 units -> 211; 101 paragraphs -> 92.
              13 ids retired via alias, 4 added at section ends (s3-p20, s3-p21, s3-p22, s4-p9).
              16 defects found by the boundary pass, 1 more (s3-p19) by the denominator pass.
  brownian    ap-17-549  12/12 pages 1:1 at 250%. 92 units -> 87; 37 paragraphs -> 32. 5 retired.

title: Implement the reviewed-ledger validator for page markers, anchors, and forbidden leftovers
description:
# Implement the reviewed-ledger validator for page markers, anchors, and forbidden leftovers

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §4.3, §4.4, §17.3 (edition tests), AGENTS.md "Cloud OCR Only" (traceability only)

## Background

Each paper's reviewed ledger (`public/papers/transcripts/<key>-reviewed.txt`) is a page-marked diplomatic transcription produced by correcting cloud OCR drafts against page images. It is comparison evidence, not the visitor-facing text: the continuous German edition is built from it and must reconstruct it exactly.

The donor project learned that ledgers silently accumulate OCR leftovers unless a validator refuses them: wrap hyphens, one-word lines, glued paragraphs, ligature misreads, running heads inside paragraphs. It also learned that "reviewed" loses meaning if the page-marker contract is not enforced. This project adds mathematics: every equation is retyped LaTeX, so malformed math, stray draft placeholders, and unpaired footnotes must also fail.

Four properties of the work shape the format and the validator:
1. **Shared pages.** The 1905 *Annalen* pages are shared: an article's first page can carry the end of the preceding article, its last page the start of the next, and the journal prints an issue article number before the title and a receipt line ("Eingegangen …") after the date-line.
2. **Page-crossing text.** Footnotes are numbered per page and can run onto the next page, and words and paragraphs cross page breaks. A format that cannot express these cases forces editors to break the rules or bend the text.
3. **Skeleton-first ledgers.** A ledger is built page by page from a skeleton. The structural contract (markers, anchors, markup, mathematics) holds from the first commit; completeness (masthead, closings, no empty pages, recorded digests) is demanded once the receipt says the ledger is corrected.
4. **A slug can hold several ledgers.** The `molecular-dimensions` slug covers two printed documents with their own receipts and keys: the dissertation `ap-19-289` (a scoped ledger) and Einstein's 1911 correction `ap-34-591` (a whole short document with its own closings). Every per-ledger setting is therefore keyed by `ledgerKey`, never by slug alone.

Ledger identity, scope, status, and digests live in the provenance receipt, in the format of `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`, because the ledger text has no header.

This bead defines the ledger format precisely and implements the validator used by every `src-ledger-*` bead, the segmenter, and the edition tests.

## Scope

In scope:
- `docs/editorial/LEDGER_FORMAT.md`: the normative ledger markup, with a worked example page for every construct.
- `src/content/ledger/ledgerTokenizer.ts`: the line and markup tokenizer (reused by `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`).
- `src/content/ledger/validateLedger.ts`: the validator returning typed errors, warnings, and informational findings with ledger line and page coordinates, in structural or completeness mode.
- `src/content/ledger/ledgerMathSettings.ts`: the KaTeX parse settings used for ledger mathematics.
- `scripts/validate-ledger.ts`: a CLI with JSONL output and distinct exit codes.
- Formats for the per-paper warning allowlist (`content/source-blocks/<slug>/ledger-allowlist.yaml`) and the optional ledger configuration (`content/source-blocks/<slug>/ledger-config.yaml`), both keyed by `ledgerKey`.
- Tests with fixtures for every rule.

Out of scope:
- segmenting the ledger into blocks and sentences (`am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`);
- writing ledgers (`am-src-ledger-light-quanta-sxi`, `am-src-ledger-brownian-8cw`, `am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`, `am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`, `am-src-ledger-dissertation-ppm7`);
- the receipt format, parser, and checker (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`, whose `parseReceipt` and `receiptToSourceAsset` this bead calls);
- schema definitions (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`);
- publication rendering of mathematics (`am-eq-static-katex-7da`, which reuses `ledgerMathSettings` as the parity baseline).

## Requirements

### Ledger format (`docs/editorial/LEDGER_FORMAT.md`)

1. **Encoding.** UTF-8, Unicode NFC, LF line endings, a final newline, no tabs, no control characters. Nothing precedes the first marker: no byte-order mark, blank line, or metadata header.
2. **Page markers.** The file begins with `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---`, and markers `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE k OF N ---` follow for k = 1…N in order with no gaps or duplicates.
   - `N` is the number of in-scope PDF pages, read from the receipt:
     - the receipt's `transcription.ledgerScopePages` when present (a scoped ledger, such as the dissertation's);
     - otherwise the entries of the receipt's `pageMap` whose `contents` belong to this article, excluding pages marked `other-article`.
   - Ledger page k is the k-th in-scope page in `pdfPageIndex` order (a 1-based count). Diagnostics report both k and the mapped `pdfPageIndex`, so a PDF extract and a whole-issue scan are never confused.
3. **Printed-page anchor.**
   - `[[ANNALEN-PAGE <n>]]` sits on the line immediately after each marker.
   - Anchors are strictly increasing, lie in the printed range, and equal the `printedPage` that the receipt's `pageMap` gives for ledger page k.
   - A scoped ledger's anchors may be non-contiguous, but they are still strictly increasing.
4. **Skeleton pages.** A page may hold only its marker and anchor. Ledgers start as skeletons and fill in page by page; a skeleton page passes the structural contract.
5. **Masthead** (ledger page 1 of a full-article ledger):
   - optional `[[ARTICLE-NUMBER <as printed>]]` for the issue's article number printed before the title (issue furniture: kept in the ledger, never in the edition);
   - `[[TITLE]]…[[/TITLE]]` and `[[AUTHOR]]…[[/AUTHOR]]`;
   - separator punctuation printed between title and author line (for example a semicolon when the journal sets both on one line) stays outside the tags.
6. **Other articles on shared pages.** Text belonging to another article is not transcribed: the end of the preceding article above the title, or the start of the next article after the receipt line. An optional line `[[OTHER-ARTICLE-OMITTED]]` records where it was omitted; the receipt's `pageMap` records the boundary.
7. **Headings.**
   - `[[HEADING s<n>]] <heading as printed>`: the tag carries the editorial section id, and the text keeps the printed § number and wording.
   - Paper 3's part headings use `[[PART-HEADING part-1]] <as printed>` and `[[PART-HEADING part-2]] <as printed>`.
   - Text before the first heading belongs to `s0`; paper 4 has no headings, so all of it belongs to `s0`.
8. **Paragraphs.**
   - Paragraphs are separated by exactly one blank line and keep printed order. A paragraph may span several physical lines; soft line breaks join with one space.
   - A physical line may never end with a hyphen (U+002D or U+2010) immediately preceded by a letter. The joiner cannot know whether such a break needs a space, so the editor rejoins wrap-hyphenated words and keeps genuine compounds (for example `Maxwell-Hertzschen`) hyphenated mid-line.
   - A paragraph continuing onto the next page ends its first part with `[[CONTINUES]]` and resumes with the first body line after the next page's anchor. A word hyphenated across the page break is rejoined and written whole before `[[CONTINUES]]`. This is a declared normalization.
9. **Display equations.**
   - `$$ <LaTeX> $$`, one region per printed display. A multi-line display set under one brace or one label is one region (for example using `aligned` or `array`); lines printed as separate displays are separate regions.
   - A display belongs to the paragraph in which it is printed: no blank line separates it from the text before it or from continuing text after it. A blank line after a display starts a new paragraph only where the print starts one.
   - When a label is printed, `[[EQ-LABEL <label exactly as printed>]]` follows on the next line, keeping parentheses, primes, Roman numerals, and letters.
   - Inline mathematics is `$ … $`. Words printed inside a formula use `\text{…}` with the printed spelling.
10. **Emphasis.** `[[SPERR]]…[[/SPERR]]` for letter-spaced emphasis; `[[EM]]…[[/EM]]` for italic text that is not mathematics. Emphasis tags do not nest.
11. **Footnotes.**
    - `[[FN-MARK <label>]]` sits inline at the occurrence, including inside a heading or directly after a display where printed.
    - The footnote text follows the page's body text at the foot of the same page: `[[FN <label>]] <text>`.
    - A footnote running onto the next page ends its first part with `[[FN-CONTINUES]]` and resumes at the foot of the next page with `[[FN-CONT <label>]] <text>`.
    - Labels restart per page as printed (for example `1)`).
12. **Closings.** `[[DATELINE]] <as printed>` (for example `Bern, Mai 1905.`); `[[ACK]] <as printed>` for an acknowledgment set as closing matter (paper 3's thanks to M. Besso); `[[RECEIVED]] <as printed>` for the journal's receipt line (expected in the form `(Eingegangen … 1905.)`; verify on the facsimile).
13. **Declared normalizations only.** Rejoin line-wrap hyphenation and resolve typographic ligatures. Keep original spelling (`daß`), capitalization, punctuation, printed abbreviations with their spacing (`z. B.`, `a. a. O.`), decimal commas, units as printed (`μ`, `Sek.`, `Mikron`), and printed misspellings. A suspected typographical error stays as printed and is recorded in the receipt's `typographicalErrors`.
14. **Draft-only OCR tokens are forbidden in a ledger.** The cloud OCR instructions may emit `[[RUNNING-HEAD …]]`, `[[PAGE-NUMBER …]]`, and `[[ILLEGIBLE]]` in drafts; each is a `draft-token` error with an actionable repair:
    - running head: remove it, because running heads belong to the receipt's `pageMap`;
    - page number: remove it, because the printed page is carried by the `[[ANNALEN-PAGE]]` anchor;
    - illegible: resolve the reading against the page image rendered at 300 dpi or more and the comparison witnesses. If the page itself is damaged, record the evidence in the receipt's `watchList` and never leave the token.
15. **Forbidden anywhere.**
    - Scan and draft leftovers: running heads, bare page-number lines, draft placeholders (`[[MATH-REGION`, `unverified`, `TODO`, `???`), the replacement character U+FFFD, `[?]`, `<unk>`.
    - Machine output: confidence tokens in the format emitted by `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`.
    - Markup errors: HTML-like tags outside math regions (a `<` followed by a letter, `/`, or `!`; inside math, `<` is ordinary LaTeX); unknown `[[…]]` tags; unclosed or nested emphasis tags.

### Validation modes

- **Structural mode** is the default while the receipt's `transcription.ledgerStatus` is `not-started` or `in-progress`. Every structural rule applies, and skeleton pages pass with an informational `skeleton-page` finding.
- **Completeness mode** applies automatically when `ledgerStatus` is `corrected`, `corrected-second-read`, or `reviewed`, or when `--require-complete` is passed. Every structural rule applies, and so do the completeness rules below. Ledger tests assert completeness once the status is `corrected`.

### Validator rules

**Structural errors** (always):
- **Encoding and markers:** `encoding`; `content-before-marker`; `first-marker`; `marker-sequence` (a gap, duplicate, or disorder); `page-count-mismatch` (`N` against the receipt scope).
- **Anchors:** `anchor-missing`, `anchor-duplicate`, `anchor-order`, `anchor-range`, `anchor-mapping` (the anchor differs from the receipt's `printedPage` for that ledger page).
- **Headings:** `heading-order` (section ids not increasing, or a part heading not preceding its first section).
- **Paragraph markup:** `line-end-hyphen`; `continues-orphan` (`[[CONTINUES]]` not followed by a page break and continuing body text).
- **Mathematics:** `math-unbalanced`; `math-parse` (the region fails the KaTeX parse under `ledgerMathSettings`); `math-macro-definition` (`\def`, `\gdef`, `\edef`, `\let`, `\newcommand`, `\renewcommand`).
- **Equation labels:** `eq-label-orphan` (a label not directly after a display); `eq-label-duplicate-in-section` (the same printed label twice in one section, unless `printingAnomalies` for this ledger key lists it with the id of a receipt `typographicalErrors` entry).
- **Footnotes:** `fn-mark-orphan` (a mark without text on the same page); `fn-text-orphan`; `fn-continuation-orphan`.
- **Forbidden content:** `draft-token` (with the repair message above); `forbidden-token`; `unknown-tag`; `unclosed-tag`; `nested-emphasis`; `html-outside-math`.
- **Receipt:** `receipt-source-digest-mismatch` (the receipt's `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256` differs from the pinned scan's `scan.sha256`: the ledger was transcribed from other bytes).
- **Configuration:** `allowlist-entry-invalid` (an entry without reason, editor, or date); `config-key-unknown` (a `ledgers:` section whose key has no receipt under `docs/provenance/`); `config-key-missing` (a slug holding several keys where the validated key has neither its own section nor a `defaults` section that covers the required fields).

**Completeness errors** (completeness mode only):
- `page-empty`: an in-scope page with no body or footnote content.
- `masthead-missing`: ledger page 1 of a full-article ledger has no title and author tags.
- `closing-missing`: a closing listed in this ledger key's `expectedClosings` is absent; the default for the four papers is `[dateline, received]`.
- `receipt-ledger-digest-mismatch`: the receipt's `transcription.ledgerSha256` is missing or differs from the ledger bytes.

**Warnings** (both modes; fixed or acknowledged in the allowlist):
- `short-line`: a physical line of one or two words inside a paragraph that is not the paragraph's last line, which suggests a printed line break was copied.
- `short-paragraph`: a paragraph of one or two words.
- `spaced-letters`: letter sequences such as `W ä r m e` not wrapped in `[[SPERR]]`.
- `modern-spelling`: forms from a curated list built only from spellings actually observed in these facsimiles, each entry citing a facsimile example (for example `dass` where the print has `daß`).
- `running-head-like`: a line matching this ledger key's `runningHeadPatterns` or the default author running head (`A. Einstein.`).
- `digit-letter-confusion`: `l`/`1` or `O`/`0` adjacent to digits in text.
- `ascii-quote`: straight quotation marks outside mathematics where German print uses „ and “.
- `double-space` and `trailing-whitespace`.

**Informational findings** (never blocking):
- `skeleton-page` (structural mode).
- `eq-label-repeats-across-sections`: the manifest must use section-qualified equation ids (`eq-s<n>-<printed>`) per `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`.
- `receipt-ledger-digest-stale` (structural mode: the receipt's `ledgerSha256` differs from the in-progress file).
- Per-page statistics.

### Output

`validateLedger(path, options)` returns:

`{ valid, clean, mode, ledgerStatus, ledgerKey, ledgerSha256, sourceAssetSha256, errors[], warnings[], info[], staleAllowlistEntries[], stats }`

- `valid` means no errors in the active mode.
- `clean` means valid, with no unacknowledged warning and no stale allowlist entry.
- Each finding carries `{code, severity, ledgerLine, ledgerPage, pdfPageIndex, printedPage, message, repair, excerpt}` (the excerpt is bounded to 120 characters). Warnings also carry `acknowledged` and the matching allowlist entry.
- `stats` is `{pages, skeletonPages, headings, paragraphs, displayEquations, inlineMathRegions, footnotes, closings, emphasisSpans, perPage: [{ledgerPage, printedPage, paragraphsStarting, displayEquations, footnotes, inlineMathRegions}], repeatedEquationLabels}`. Ledger, inventory, and receipt page-map tests compare these counts.

### Identity and digest binding

The ledger text carries no header, so its binding lives in the receipt (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`):
1. The validator derives the ledger key from the filename (`<key>-reviewed.txt`) and reads the receipt `docs/provenance/<key>.md` through `parseReceipt`: scope, `pageMap`, `scan.sha256`, and the `transcription` block. The key, not the slug, selects the configuration and allowlist entries below.
2. It emits `ledgerSha256` (the SHA-256 of the ledger bytes) and `sourceAssetSha256` (the receipt's `scan.sha256`). The ledger bead writes them into `transcription.ledgerSha256` and `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256`, and the receipt checker requires the latter to equal `scan.sha256`.
3. `content/source-blocks/<slug>/edition.yaml` (format owned by `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`) pins both, so an edition built from a stale ledger fails.

A key without a `Paper` record (the 1911 correction `ap-34-591`) validates through its own receipt and its own section of `ledger-config.yaml`.

### Allowlist and configuration

Both files live per slug and are keyed by `ledgerKey`, because one slug can hold several printed documents.

- **Allowlist.** `content/source-blocks/<slug>/ledger-allowlist.yaml` entries carry `{ledgerKey, code, ledgerPage, lineFingerprint, reason, editor, date}`. `lineFingerprint` is the first 16 hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 of the line text (NFC, whitespace collapsed). Only entries whose `ledgerKey` equals the validated ledger's key are considered; an entry that matches no current warning of that key is reported as stale.
- **Configuration.** `content/source-blocks/<slug>/ledger-config.yaml` is optional and has two top-level sections:
  - `defaults:` settings applied to every ledger of the slug;
  - `ledgers:` a map from `ledgerKey` to settings, which override the defaults per key.

  Settings in either section are `runningHeadPatterns[]`, `expectedClosings[]`, `printingAnomalies[]` (`label`, `section`, `typographicalErrorId`), and `modernSpellingList[]` additions with facsimile examples. Built-in defaults are documented in `LEDGER_FORMAT.md` and apply when neither section supplies a value.

  A slug with one ledger may write its settings under `defaults:` alone. A slug with several, such as `molecular-dimensions` (`ap-19-289` and `ap-34-591`), keys every setting that differs: the dissertation and the 1911 correction have different `expectedClosings` and different `printingAnomalies`, and the correction is a short document whose closings are recorded from its own facsimile rather than assumed. Settings are never read from another key's section, and the page scope never lives here; it is the receipt's `transcription.ledgerScopePages`.

### Mathematics parse settings

`ledgerMathSettings.ts` parses each math region through KaTeX's public API (`renderToString` with the output discarded; no internal parser API), using the version pinned by `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`.
- Settings: `throwOnError: true`, `strict: "error"`, `trust: false`, an empty macro table, and caps `maxExpand: 1000` and `maxSize: 20`.
- A German word written in math mode without `\text{…}` fails, because strict mode rejects Unicode text in math mode.
- The parse proves syntax only. Fidelity is the editor's image comparison and the human review.
- `am-eq-static-katex-7da` imports these settings as the baseline its publication renderer is compared against, so a ledger region that parses here parses there.

### CLI

`bun scripts/validate-ledger.ts <ledger path> [--paper <slug>] [--require-complete] [--allow-warnings]`
- Output: one JSONL diagnostic per finding on stdout, then a summary line naming the mode, the ledger key, and the configuration section used.
- Exit codes:
  - 0: clean;
  - 1: errors;
  - 2: unacknowledged warnings or stale allowlist entries;
  - 3: usage or identity failure (unknown key, missing or unparseable receipt, unreadable file, a configuration section for an unknown key).
- `--allow-warnings` is for work in progress. It turns exit 2 into 0 while printing a prominent notice, and the quality gate chain never uses it.

### Donor extraction

`am-gov-donor-audit-0wa` is to locate the donor's `validateReviewedTranscription` (named in the donor documentation as `src/data/patents/sourceTextValidation.ts`) at the pinned revision.
- **If the audit confirms it:** this bead extracts it with its license notice and rider (it is not in `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`'s list, so this bead owns the extraction) and extends it with the rules above.
- **If it is absent:** implement from this specification and record the absence with `br comments add am-gov-donor-audit-0wa`.

## Technical Approach

- A line-oriented state machine (marker, anchor, masthead, body, footnote area) over the tokens from `ledgerTokenizer.ts`. Math regions go to KaTeX with `ledgerMathSettings`, and each finding carries exact coordinates and a repair hint.
- Scope, page map, scan digest, and ledger status come from the receipt through `parseReceipt` (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`). Paper identity and printed ranges come from the `Paper` records of `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`. Configuration and allowlist entries are resolved by `ledgerKey` before any rule runs, and the resolved settings are reported in the summary. Tests log through the JSONL logging library (`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`).
- The validator is pure: it reads files and never writes into `content/`, `public/`, or `docs/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `LEDGER_FORMAT.md` specifies every rule above with a worked example page covering:
  - the masthead;
  - a heading;
  - a paragraph crossing a page break with a rejoined word;
  - a display inside a paragraph with a label;
  - inline math;
  - letter-spaced emphasis;
  - footnotes on two pages, including one that continues;
  - an omitted neighboring article;
  - the three closings;
  - a skeleton page;
  - a `ledger-config.yaml` with `defaults:` and two `ledgers:` keys.
- [ ] The validator enforces every structural rule in structural mode and adds the completeness rules in completeness mode. The mode follows the receipt's `ledgerStatus` or `--require-complete`.
- [ ] Draft-only OCR tokens produce `draft-token` errors with their repair messages.
- [ ] Every warning and informational rule is reported with its code and full coordinates.
- [ ] Allowlisted warnings require reason, editor, and date, match only their own `ledgerKey`, and stale entries are reported.
- [ ] Configuration is resolved by `ledgerKey` over `defaults`, a slug with two ledgers gets different `expectedClosings` and `printingAnomalies`, and an unknown key fails with `config-key-unknown`.
- [ ] `stats` counts are correct on fixtures, including per-page counts and skeleton pages.
- [ ] `ledgerSha256` and `sourceAssetSha256` are emitted, and receipt digest mismatches are reported per mode.
- [ ] A scoped ledger takes `N` from `transcription.ledgerScopePages` and accepts non-contiguous, strictly increasing anchors. The `ap-34-591` key validates through its receipt and its own configuration section.
- [ ] A 31-page ledger validates in under one second on a developer machine.
- [ ] The CLI emits JSONL and the documented exit codes, and its summary names the mode, key, and configuration section.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- **Line-end hyphens.** German compounds are legitimately hyphenated. Only a hyphen at a physical line end is an error, because the editor controls line breaks in the ledger and there is never a reason to break a line there.
- **Multi-line displays.** A multi-line printed display is one region. Splitting a printed system into separate displays changes the printed structure, and the edition must mirror the ledger exactly.
- **Syntax is not fidelity.** The KaTeX strict parse catches syntax only. Never retype a formula to satisfy a parser; if printed notation needs a construct the settings reject, record it and raise it with `br comments add` rather than changing the transcription.
- **Printed misspellings stay.** A heading that misspells a name, for example a §7 witness reading *Doppelerschen*, stays as printed if the scan confirms it, with a receipt typographical-error entry. The validator never corrects it and has no rule that would push an editor to.
- **Skeleton mode is not a loophole.** Completeness applies as soon as the receipt says `corrected`, and the ledger beads' tests assert it at that point.
- **One slug, two documents.** Never let a setting leak between ledger keys. The 1911 correction is two printed pages with its own closings and its own anomalies, and a shared `expectedClosings` would either excuse a missing closing in the dissertation or demand an absent one in the correction.
- **Shared markup.** The segmenter in `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` parses the same tags through `ledgerTokenizer.ts`, so a format change is a change to both beads.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: paper identity and printed ranges.
- `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: the JSONL logging library and failure-evidence helpers the tests use.
- `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: `parseReceipt`, the `pageMap`, `transcription.ledgerScopePages`, `ledgerStatus`, and the digest fields the validator reads.

Unblocks:
- `am-src-ledger-light-quanta-sxi`, `am-src-ledger-brownian-8cw`, `am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`, `am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`, `am-src-ledger-dissertation-ppm7`: ledgers are written to this format and validated with this tool; the dissertation bead writes two keyed configuration sections.
- `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`: segmentation reuses the tokenizer and the validator's statistics and digests.
- `am-eq-static-katex-7da`: the publication renderer's parity corpus compares against `ledgerMathSettings`.

Gate audit: 2 commits, +2 expect() and +106 assert.*, 0 assertions removed, 0 skips introduced.

RH-5 check - the tests discriminate rather than confirm. The strongest is
'Mutation matrix: each single mutation raises exactly its code and no unrelated code'. That is the
right shape for a validator: it is not enough that a bad ledger fails, it must fail for the INTENDED

# German source review of the Brownian translation and alignment

**Epic:** `am-ep-editions-1wa` · **Batch:** C · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels include:** human-gate · **Plan sections:** §4.3, §4.5 steps 4 and 7, §17.2, §17.7 items 2 and 9 (traceability only)

## Background

Machine-generated drafts never self-certify. A schema, renderer, or agent accepting a translation proves nothing about its fidelity. Before the Brownian motion translation can be published as reviewed, a qualified reader of German checks it against the German at the level of complete arguments, not isolated sentences. For every section, the reviewer can follow the facsimile, the ledger, the German edition, the English translation, and the notation map without guessing how they correspond.

Disagreements are resolved by returning to the facsimile and its context, never by majority vote among paraphrases. Substantive disagreements with historical translations are recorded in the provenance receipt.

The per-paper definition of done asks for two acceptances with reviewer names: German fidelity (the source layers match the facsimile) and translation accuracy. This review records both, as structured review records rather than prose.

This review runs in Batch C, before the Brownian gloss exists: that gloss follows the paper-4 conventions and the gloss face in Batch D. Reviewing the translation now lets its findings inform the Batch D mass–energy translation. The gloss is therefore reviewed by its own human gate, `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x`, which waits for this review's accepted term definitions.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies.** A fluent reader of early-twentieth-century scientific German who can follow the paper's mathematics, listed as this paper's German source reviewer (role `german-source-reviewer`) in `docs/OWNERS.md` (`am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`) with a short qualification statement and recorded consent to be named.
  - A second qualified German source reviewer listed there may take the German-fidelity part.
  - Nobody reviews units they drafted, translated, or checked as editor, including drafts made with machine help. The comparison is mechanical: the reviewer's id is checked against the `translator` and `editor` authorship entries of every covered `TranslationUnit` and the `editors` of `content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/edition.yaml`. A model is never a reviewer.
- **Evidence to record.**
  - `german-source` review records in `content/reviews/brownian-motion/`, in the schema of `am-edit-review-records-hofz`: reviewer id, `scope` listing every covered unit with its exact revision, `date`, `result` (`accepted`, `accepted-with-changes`, `rejected`, `needs-rereview`), `notes`, and `evidenceLocation`.
  - The disagreement log `content/reviews/brownian-motion/disagreements.yaml`.
  - The focus sign-off `content/reviews/brownian-motion/german-source-focus.yaml`.
  - The page-by-page image comparison record.
  - The receipt's editorial-acceptance section in `docs/provenance/ap-17-549.md`, rendered from the records by `scripts/render-review-acceptance.ts` (owned by `am-edit-review-records-hofz`).
- **What agents may prepare.**
  - The review packet: `bun scripts/build-review-packet.ts --paper brownian-motion` (`am-edn-review-packet-ee9t`).
  - Pre-filled record templates whose `result` field stays empty, and the focus file with empty sign-offs.
  - After the reviewer decides, new revisions applying the reviewer's corrections, with the reviewer's approval recorded, followed by a diff packet (`--since-packet <tool-run-id>`) of the changed units for re-review.
- **Agents never close this bead on their own judgment and never write a `result`.** It closes only when the evidence above exists, names the reviewer, and passes the checks below, with the reviewer's name, the date, and the record location in the close reason.

## Scope

In scope:
- **Translation accuracy.** Every `TranslationUnit`, `Alignment` edge, and `term` annotation of the paper; the modality register `docs/editorial/brownian-motion-modality-register.md`; notation kept as printed on both faces; every `math-order-differs` warning in the coverage report.
- **German fidelity.** The German blocks of every page compared with the page images. Pages carrying display equations are compared symbol by symbol. The ledger is consulted wherever a block and the image seem to differ.
- **Editorial notes** for unresolved readings that are intellectually important.

Out of scope:
- the interlinear gloss (`am-edn-gloss-brownian-or6t`), whose human gate is `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x`. Gloss units reach `reviewed` only through that review's records, and this review neither covers them nor blocks on them;
- physics review of derivations (`am-bm-review-physics-arfv`);
- readability review of the R2 readings (`am-bm-review-reader-x77h`);
- explanations.

## Requirements

1. Review whole sections as arguments. Check that every German sentence's content, modality, and qualification survive in English, including sentence splits and many-to-many edges.
2. Check that notation is kept exactly as printed on both faces, that display equations are referenced rather than retyped, and that inline mathematics matches.
3. Check each term annotation's definition against its occurrence. These accepted definitions are what the gloss review later checks token glosses against, so a definition left vague here costs twice.
4. Compare every page's German blocks with the page images for German fidelity. Record which pages were compared, by whom, and on which date.
5. For each disagreement, record in `disagreements.yaml`: the unit id, the German reading, the English rendering, the witness readings consulted, the resolution, the reason, and whether it is substantive. Substantive disagreements with historical translations also go into the receipt.
6. Record corrections against stable source and argument ids. A source correction identifies the affected translations and explanatory claims through the correction graph of `am-edit-review-records-hofz`, without marking unrelated visual work obsolete. Records covering a changed revision become stale and require re-review.
7. When accepted, the records cover the current revision of every translation unit and German block in scope, and review states become `reviewed` only through those records.

### Focus list for this paper

Each item is signed off in `german-source-focus.yaml` with the sentence ids examined:
- the introduction's four conditional statements: the possible identification with Brownian molecular motion, the reports too imprecise to judge, and the two conditional consequences;
- the §2 statistical-mechanical argument in full;
- §3's imagined force and Stokes drag, with $k$ as viscosity and $P$ as radius;
- §4's independence assumptions, the interval $\tau$, and the symmetry of $\varphi(\Delta)$;
- §5's printed numbers, units, and unit words as printed (the viscosity, the particle size as printed, $N$, and both displacement results, where a comparison witness reads `0,8 Mikron` and `ca. 6 Mikron`), and the formula for $N$, with "displacement" never rendered as a speed and no printed unit word silently modernized;
- the closing hope, in the section where it is printed;
- the outcome of the velocity-warning verification flag recorded in the receipt;
- the term definitions the gloss review will depend on.

## Technical Approach

1. Generate the packet with `bun scripts/build-review-packet.ts --paper brownian-motion` into `artifacts/review-packets/brownian-motion/<tool-run-id>/`. The packet contains:
   - the side-by-side German and English by section, with facsimile page references;
   - the modality register, term annotations, `math-order-differs` warnings, witness-difference list, and difficulties file;
   - pre-filled record templates.
2. The reviewer works from the packet and the facsimile and returns filled templates and the disagreement log.
3. `bun scripts/import-review-record.ts <filled template> --packet <tool-run-id>` validates each filled template against the schema and the packet's revisions, refuses stale revisions, self-review, unknown reviewers, and model reviewers, and writes the record.
4. Agents apply approved corrections as new revisions, regenerate a diff packet, and repeat until accepted.
5. Render the receipt section with `scripts/render-review-acceptance.ts`. Once the German-fidelity record is accepted, set the receipt's `transcription.ledgerStatus` to `reviewed` (the checker of `am-src-receipt-format-npo5` rejects `reviewed` without the acceptance record), run `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-549`, and run the checks below.
6. Record on `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x` (with `br comments add`) which term definitions were accepted and at which revisions, so the gloss review starts from them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Accepted `german-source` records cover the current revision of every translation unit of the paper, naming the reviewer and dates.
- [ ] Accepted German-fidelity records cover every page's German blocks, with the page comparison record complete.
- [ ] No record's reviewer appears in the `translator` or `editor` authorship entry of a unit it covers or in `edition.yaml`'s `editors`; every reviewer id is listed in `docs/OWNERS.md` with the `german-source-reviewer` role.
- [ ] The disagreement log is complete, and substantive witness disagreements are in the receipt.
- [ ] Every focus item is signed off with sentence ids.
- [ ] `assertEditionContract('brownian-motion', { layers: ['german', 'translation'], requireReviewed: true })` passes.
- [ ] The receipt's editorial-acceptance section is rendered from the records.
- [ ] The accepted term definitions and their revisions are recorded on `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- The review-record checks of `am-edit-review-records-hofz` run over `content/reviews/brownian-motion/` through `bun scripts/verify-content.ts`:
  - records validate;
  - no self-review against the authorship ids of the covered units;
  - reviewer ids appear in `docs/OWNERS.md` with the mapped role;
  - no model reviewer;
  - every `reviewed` state is covered by a non-stale accepted record.
- `src/content/editions/brownian.review.test.ts` (this bead creates the file; `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x` adds its gloss `describe` block):
  - `assertEditionContract('brownian-motion', { layers: ['german', 'translation'], requireReviewed: true })`;
  - no gloss unit is `reviewed` on the strength of a record written for this review: a fixture record whose `scope` lists a gloss unit id is rejected as out of scope;
  - every entry of `disagreements.yaml` references existing unit ids and has a resolution;
  - every focus item in `german-source-focus.yaml` has sentence ids that exist and a sign-off;
  - the page comparison record covers every PDF page in the article scope;
  - the receipt's editorial-acceptance section equals the output of `scripts/render-review-acceptance.ts` byte for byte.
- **Live canary** (run-scoped copy under `artifacts/test-tmp/review-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>/`, never deleted): bumping one unit's revision without a new record makes the contract fail on staleness.

### End-to-end tests

- `bun scripts/e2e-edition-pipeline.ts --paper brownian-motion --layers german,translation --require-reviewed` passes every stage from `ledger` through `coverage`. When the reader routes exist, it also passes `static-html` with no draft marker on reviewed units. Evidence is retained under `artifacts/test-logs/edition-pipeline/<log-run-id>/evidence/<stage>/`.
- The paper's browser journey (`am-bm-e2e-complete-gmdb`) confirms that reviewed units render without draft labels, with screenshots, traces, and DOM snapshots retained on failure.

### Structured logging

JSONL goes to `artifacts/test-logs/review-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library.
- Fields: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-edn-review-german-brownian-cfh"`, `paper: "brownian-motion"`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.
- `extra`: `{section, unitId, unitRevision, reviewRecordId, reviewerId, toolRunId, check, evidencePath}`, where `toolRunId` is the packet run the record cites.
- Logs carry reviewer ids only as consented in `docs/OWNERS.md`, never contact details.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Review is about the German; do not let a fluent English rewrite override a faithful but plainer rendering.
- Hedges and definitions are the most common casualties of fluent translation; check them first.
- A reviewer who shaped a draft, even through suggestions, is a drafter for that unit.
- A source correction found here is a source-layer change with its own history. Record it against the block id, never silently in the translation.
- This review closing does not make the paper's gloss reviewed, and the definition of done waits for the gloss review's records. Never widen a record's scope to cover gloss units.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-edn-translation-brownian-rest-h0z`: the complete translation of the paper.
- `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`: reviewer assignment, qualification, and consent.
- `am-edit-review-records-hofz`: the review-record schema, self-review and staleness checks, and the acceptance renderer.
- `am-edn-review-packet-ee9t`: the packet export and the record import check.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-review-german-gloss-brownian-1s9x`: the gloss review works from the term definitions and German blocks this review accepted.
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`: the per-paper definition of done requires recorded German fidelity and translation acceptance.
