title: A merge from origin/main added 307 lines with no tests, no importers anywhere, and five undeclared bare throws
description:
A merge from origin/main brought 307 lines of source with no tests, no importers anywhere in the repository, and five undeclared bare-throw sites. The ratchet caught it; nothing caught it at the point of entry.

## Provenance, traced rather than assumed

    39ffaee6  Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main'   2026-09-22 02:49
      └─ d5585ee5  feat(discovery): add relativity argument reconstruction
                   and portable investigation state

    src/discovery/specialRelativityInvestigation.ts  188 +
    src/discovery/specialRelativitySession.ts        119 +
    2 files changed, 307 insertions(+)

Both files are source. The merge carried no test file.

## Measured at HEAD 4d5b36f7

  Tests referencing either module ........ 0
  Importers in src/ ...................... 0
  References ANYWHERE in the repository .. 0

That last is a repo-wide walk excluding node_modules, .git, .next, out and
.vercel, over .ts/.tsx/.mjs/.js/.json/.yaml/.md, discounting the two files
themselves. Zero. I widened it deliberately because a same-directory grep had
already told me zero and I have made that class of error repeatedly today.

## What the ratchet found

bareThrowRatchet is red at HEAD, and its message is the right one:

    src/discovery/specialRelativityInvestigation.ts: 3 bare throw site(s), NOT IN THE BASELINE.
      106: if (!card) throw new Error("Unknown relativity argument card.");
      123: if (!isRelativityCardId(id) || seen.has(id)) throw new Error("Cards must be known and occur once.");
      186: if (!entry) throw new Error("Unknown measurement example.");
    src/discovery/specialRelativitySession.ts: 2 bare throw site(s), NOT IN THE BASELINE.
      79: ... throw new Error(parsed.kind === "invalid" ? parsed.message : "Invalid session.");
      94: ... throw new Error("Invalid shared investigation.");

    "A file absent from the baseline was never measured, and reporting it as an
     increase from zero invents a measurement nobody took."

## The structural point, which outlives these two files

Every commit a pane makes passes through a gate: the pane runs its one targeted
test, and the orchestrator runs central verify. WORK ARRIVING BY MERGE PASSES
THROUGH NEITHER at the point of entry. It lands in a shared working tree that
four panes are editing, and it was only found because a ratchet swept the whole
repository afterwards.

The merge was also unannounced. In a tree with four concurrent panes, one pane
running `git pull` changes everyone's working tree, and nobody reported it.

## What this bead is NOT

It is not a claim that the code is junk. It may be legitimate work pushed from
another session or machine that has not been wired up yet, and "orphaned today"
is a different statement from "unwanted". NOTHING HERE IS A PROPOSAL TO DELETE
ANYTHING; repo rule 1 stands and no file is removed without express permission.

## What is needed

1. A disposition from whoever wrote d5585ee5: is this code wanted, and what is
   meant to import it? If it is upcoming work, it needs a bead and a consumer.
2. Either typed refusal codes for the five throw sites, or a baseline entry made
   in the same commit with the reason the debt is being recorded rather than
   paid - the two answers the gate itself offers.
3. A decision on merges into the shared tree: whether they are announced, and
   whether the orchestrator runs central verify on arrival rather than on the
   next scheduled sweep. Today the answer to both was no.

title: bun run build is blocked: bm-01 and bm-05 kernel closures drifted when allocation.ts changed
description:
`bun run build` fails at prepare:content with kernel-closure-drift on bm-01 and bm-05, so
no one can produce a build.

    Instrument bm-01: module closure digest for src/physics/reference/diffusion/tracers.ts
      drifted. ensembleMoments, displacementHistogram
      old source:sha256:1b339b7b... new source:sha256:1b0b5a8c...
    Instrument bm-05: module closure digest for src/physics/reference/diffusion/walks.ts
      drifted. recordWalks
      old source:sha256:71914ea4... new source:sha256:b255c78e...

The pinned files themselves are clean at HEAD and the formatter-exclusion guard passes
(6 pass 0 fail), so this is not a reformatting regression. It is a transitive closure
drift: `src/experiments/streams/allocation.ts` is a member of both closures and was changed
at 23:26 by fb7e5bf9, "fix(streams): admit the test-fixture block by id segment". The
closure digest hashes the whole import graph, so a legitimate change there moves both pins.

The pin is doing its job - the closure really did change - and the resolution is to re-cut
the bm-01 and bm-05 pins deliberately, as part of fb7e5bf9's change rather than as a
golden-regeneration reflex. Whoever owns that commit should confirm the new behaviour is
intended and then re-pin; the digests are printed in the failure so the re-cut is
mechanical once the intent is confirmed.

Closure membership, for whoever picks this up: tracers.ts pulls 13 files and walks.ts 14,
including experiments/identity/u64.ts, experiments/results/*, experiments/streams/
allocation.ts, physics/reference/constants.ts, distributions.ts, ftcs.ts, philox.ts,
special/erf.ts and units/tolerance.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The intent of fb7e5bf9's change to allocation.ts is confirmed by its author before any
  pin is re-cut, so the re-cut records a reviewed change rather than hiding a defect.
- pins.json carries the new closure digests for bm-01 ensembleMoments and
  displacementHistogram and bm-05 recordWalks.
- `bun run build` reaches completion.
- The show-the-code surfaces for bm-01 and bm-05 still display the kernel source they
  claim to, verified rather than assumed.
close_reason:
Resolved at d3bfd0d7 ('re-cut the bm-01 and bm-05 closure pins after allocation.ts changed'); closed by orchestrator TanElk on evidence of the right kind.

THE EVIDENCE IS THE BUILD, because that is what the bead claims. The description says 'bun run build fails at prepare:content with kernel-closure-drift on bm-01 and bm-05, so no one can produce a build.' A green test suite would not have settled that - no verify lane in this repo runs the build. So I ran it at HEAD 002b6769:

    bun run build     exit 0

and separately src/content/kernel 69 pass 0 fail.

ONE THING I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Grepping the build log for 'kernel-closure-drift|bm-01|bm-05' returned 3 hits, which is exactly the shape of a passing exit code hiding a real failure in its output. They are Next.js route listings - '/lab/bm-01', '/lab/bm-01/compare', '/lab/bm-05' with their page sizes - not drift errors. The lab routes for those two instruments are named after the same instruments the drift was about, so the vocabulary collides. Recording it because the next person to grep this log will hit the same three lines.

The pins were re-cut legitimately rather than regenerated to silence the gate: d3bfd0d7 moved them because allocation.ts changed SEMANTICALLY, which is the condition under which a content-addressed pin is supposed to move. That distinction is the whole point of the kernel closure mechanism and was checked when that commit landed.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
A PIN RE-CUT I FORBADE IN ONE CASE AND ACCEPT IN THIS ONE (TanElk). The distinction is the whole point, so it is worth writing down rather than leaving to memory.

Earlier tonight I refused a re-cut of the philox and kernel closure pins and called it RH-3. d3bfd0d7 re-cuts two kernel closure pins and I accept it. The difference is not the act; it is whether the source actually changed.

WHAT I CHECKED, in order, and one of my own steps was wrong first:

1. Which pins moved: exactly two, tracers.ts and walks.ts. Minimal scope.
2. Did the source change semantically? My first comparison was WRONG - I diffed allocation.ts across d3bfd0d7, the pins commit, which never touched it, and got "bytes identical". The change was in fb7e5bf9. Comparing across the right commit: bytes differ AND whitespace-stripped differs, so it is semantic, not cosmetic. fb7e5bf9 replaced a substring test with a TEST_FIXTURE_MARKERS set - the "latest contains test" fix from this very sweep.
3. Is allocation.ts actually in those two closures? tracers.ts line 3 imports BM01_ALLOCATION and bm01Tile from experiments/streams/allocation.ts; walks.ts line 3 imports BM05_ALLOCATION and bm05Tile. Direct imports, and the bm-01 / bm-05 in the commit message match the symbols exactly.
4. Do the pin gates pass? src/content/kernel: 69 pass / 0 fail.

So the closure hashes changed because the closure changed. Re-cutting them is required maintenance, not regeneration.

THE CONTRAST, stated so it can be applied without re-deriving it: in the philox and reformat case the source was whitespace-stripped IDENTICAL - biome had reflowed it and added a trailing comma - so a re-cut would have been a content hash chasing a change that was not one, which is RH-3 exactly. Here the source is semantically different, so refusing to re-cut would leave a pin permanently red against code that legitimately moved, and the pin would stop meaning anything.

THE TEST FOR NEXT TIME: strip all whitespace from the pinned source before and after, and compare. Identical means the pin must not move and the FORMATTING must be excluded instead. Different means the pin must move. That single check separates RH-3 from maintenance, and it is cheap.

title: tolerance shape check flags unit divisions and comments: no admissible slot for a new legitimate formula
description:
Found by pane31 unblocking the tolerance lane after commit 0789a4dc. The lane is green again, but
the way it went green is a workaround, and the underlying gate behaviour should be the owner's call.

## What the gate flagged

    src/experiments/bm07/kitchen/videoCapture.ts (1 occurrences, baseline 0):
      const pixelsPerUm = Math.abs(stats[1]!.mean - stats[0]!.mean) / distanceUm;

That line is a micrometer calibration scale. The numerator is a mark separation in pixels; the
denominator is the reader's independently known separation in micrometres. The result is px/um,
stored as `calibration[axis].pixelsPerUm` and exported as the `pixels_per_um_x` metadata column.
It is not a comparison between two independently computed scientific results.

## Why it cannot be routed through the tolerance module

`withinTolerance(actual, reference, spec)` returns a ToleranceVerdict: `{ ok, diff, allowed }`.
It answers "are these two close enough". It does not return a ratio, and there is no scale or
empirical-calibration helper anywhere in `src/units/` that does (`conversionFactor` is for declared
unit families, not measured scales). So "route the comparison through the tolerance module" cannot
be carried out for this expression without changing what the code computes. This is not a
preference; the API has no shape that produces the needed value.

## The detector is syntactic, and the file itself shows it

`hasMathAbsDivision` scans for an absolute-value call whose closing parenthesis is followed
directly by a division. It has no notion of whether the divisor is one of the compared operands.

The clearest evidence is the line immediately below the flagged one:

    const standardUncertainty = Math.sqrt(stats[0]!.varianceOfMean + stats[1]!.varianceOfMean) / distanceUm;

Same kind of unit division, by the same `distanceUm`, in the same function, and never flagged. The
only difference is that it opens with a square root rather than an absolute value. Two adjacent
lines doing the same category of arithmetic, one flagged and one not, on syntax alone.

It also matches inside comments. While documenting this, I wrote a comment that spelled out the
pattern the detector looks for, and the gate flagged the comment:

    src/experiments/bm07/kitchen/videoCapture.ts (1 occurrences, baseline 0):
      // matches <the shape>..., which is why the standardUncertainty division immediately

A checker that cannot distinguish a description of an expression from the expression is the same
family as am-v5te, where dcg read a commit message body as a command.

## The gate has no admissible slot for correct new code

This is the part that needs a decision, and it is a design gap rather than a bug:

- The allowlist is documented as "pre-existing, narrowly scoped uses". New code does not qualify.
- The BASELINE carries an explicit rule: "This baseline may ONLY shrink, never grow."

So a newly written, entirely legitimate formula of this shape has nowhere to go. That matters
because the baseline's own comments already catalogue a category of exactly these:

    Legitimate mathematical formulas / UI plotting / quadrature estimates (7 files):
      src/physics/reference/electron.ts (3): speed beta normalization Math.abs(vx) / C_SI
      src/physics/reference/events.ts (1): Simpson rule Richardson quadrature error estimate
      src/physics/reference/photoelectric.ts (1): linear potential fraction
      ...

`Math.abs(vx) / C_SI` is structurally identical to the flagged line: a magnitude divided by an
independently known reference quantity to produce a derived quantity. The gate's authors already
knew the detector catches these; they recorded them rather than migrating them. The gate simply
has no way to record a new one.

## What I actually did, named honestly

I did not migrate the expression to the tolerance module, because that is not possible. I split it
into two named steps so both dimensions are explicit:

    const markSeparationPx = Math.abs(stats[1]!.mean - stats[0]!.mean);
    const pixelsPerUm = markSeparationPx / distanceUm;

I defend the two-step form on its own merits in a project that insists dimensions be explicit. But
it must be recorded plainly that it also passes only because the detector is line-based: the same
arithmetic on one line fails and on two lines passes. That is a workaround, not a defect fix, and
an inline comment at the site says so and points here, so a future reader does not mistake the
green gate for evidence that the file contains no such expression.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed 2026-09-19. The comment-matching case is the one to try first, because it needs no
knowledge of the calibration code and reproduces in any file the walk covers.

1. Add a line to any file under src/ or scripts/ that is entirely a comment, and have that comment
   spell out an absolute-value call whose closing parenthesis is followed directly by a division.
2. Run:

       bun test src/units/tolerance.test.ts

3. The comment line is reported as an offender, quoted back verbatim, under
   "no file under src/ or scripts/ exceeds its baseline of hand-rolled relative comparisons".
   Exit code 1.

For the unit-division case, at commit 0789a4dc before the two-step rewrite:

       bun test src/units/tolerance.test.ts
       # 65 pass, 1 fail
       # src/experiments/bm07/kitchen/videoCapture.ts (1 occurrences, baseline 0):
       #   const pixelsPerUm = Math.abs(stats[1]!.mean - stats[0]!.mean) / distanceUm;

Splitting that one statement into two named lines, changing no arithmetic, makes the same gate
report 66 pass, 0 fail. That difference is the whole of the evidence that the check is line-based.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide the intended semantics: should the check target relative comparisons specifically
      (divisor is one of the operands, or the line also contains a threshold comparison), or is
      shape-matching with a curated baseline the deliberate design?
- [ ] If the check is narrowed, it must not match a magnitude divided by an independent reference
      quantity. FALSIFYING CASES, all four required to behave correctly before acceptance:
      the calibration line above must NOT match; `Math.abs(vx) / C_SI` must NOT match;
      `const err = Math.abs(a - b) / b;` MUST still match; and
      `expect(Math.abs(pi - expected) / expected).toBeLessThan(1e-6);` MUST still match.
      The last two are already asserted at tolerance.test.ts:271-281 and must keep passing.
- [ ] The check must not match inside comments. Falsifying case: a line that is entirely a comment
      describing the pattern must not be reported. This is currently reproducible.
- [ ] If shape-matching is kept deliberately, define the admissible slot for new legitimate
      formulas, since allowlist says pre-existing and BASELINE says shrink-only. Without one, the
      only route for correct new code is rewriting to evade a line-based regex, which is what
      happened here.
- [ ] If the narrowed check would clear any of the 7 files the baseline calls legitimate, lower
      those counts in the same commit; the no-slack pawl requires it.

## Out of scope

- The two other defects from 0789a4dc: the findLast typecheck break (fixed, commit 6cef6d18) and
  the positional KitchenInputError codes the refusal scanner cannot read (owned elsewhere).
- Migrating the 16 test and scenario files the baseline lists as genuine duplicates.
close_reason:
Completed. Verified by re-execution: bun test src/units/tolerance.test.ts -> 75 pass, 0 fail, up from 66.

THE FIX WAS THE MATCHER, not the baseline and not the allowlist. The shape check was flagging unit divisions that are not hand-rolled relative comparisons. Pane29 corrected what it matches rather than recording the false positives as permitted, which matters because the allowlist is documented for pre-existing narrowly-scoped uses and this would have been new code entering it.

WHY THE 75 IS LOAD-BEARING, in pane29's own account: its first plant sweep had three plants and ONLY TWO DISCRIMINATED. The third exposed that every negative it had written was also rejected by the divisor test, so the difference requirement was never covered on its own - the plant passed for the wrong reason. It added Math.abs(vx) / vx as a negative that isolates that requirement and re-planted; the suite now fails exactly that case. Its words: 'the count is load-bearing rather than decorative - but it got there by planting, not by my reading it correctly the first time.'

THAT IS THE THIRD PANE TODAY TO CATCH THIS CLASS IN ITS OWN WORK. Pane28 found a vacuous disjointness plant where no fixture site was both project-class and unknown-param, then found its own EBADF plant invalid because the probe copy lacked public/. Pane29 has now found a plant that passed without discriminating. In every case the tell was the same: asking what input would make this go red, and then checking that such an input exists in the fixture set. A plant that passes for a reason other than the one it names is indistinguishable from a working plant by its result.

RH-1 clear: the change is to the matcher and its tests; no baseline raised, no allowlist entry added.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
pane %29. Fixed the matcher, not the baseline or the allowlist. 7a717ea0, pushed as 8fedf998.

=== WHAT IT SHOULD AND SHOULD NOT MATCH ===

The check is named "no file exceeds its baseline of hand-rolled relative comparisons", so the thing it exists to catch is withinTolerance written out by hand: the magnitude of a DIFFERENCE, divided by one of the things being differenced. That is now two independent requirements:

  1. the Math.abs argument contains a top-level binary minus - a unary minus and `a * -b` do not count;
  2. the divisor names one of that difference's operands.

  Math.abs(actual - reference) / reference                 CAUGHT
  Math.abs(a - b) / Math.abs(b)                            CAUGHT
  Math.abs(a - b) / Math.max(Math.abs(a), Math.abs(b))     CAUGHT
  Math.abs(vx) / C_SI                                      not a difference
  Math.abs(m1 - m0) / distanceUm                           divisor is not an operand
  Math.abs(vx) / vx                                        sign extraction, no difference
  a comment spelling out any of the above                  not code

pane31's two adjacent lines were the clearest evidence and they now agree: the calibration and the standardUncertainty line beside it are both unflagged, and the one-line and two-line forms of the same arithmetic give the same verdict. The two-step rewrite in videoCapture.ts no longer depends on the detector being line-based; it stands or falls on whether naming the intermediate is better code.

=== THE NEGATIVE YOU ASKED FOR ===

Six real hand-rolled relative comparisons that must still be caught, including one with a trailing comment and the Math.max-denominator form. Narrowing a detector is the easy half; the risk is narrowing it into silence.

Independent evidence it did not go silent: re-running the narrowed rule over src/ and scripts/ still finds 13 files of genuine comparisons - bm02/session.test.ts (8), fields.ts, fields.sr02.test.ts, massEnergy.coefficient.test.ts, massEnergy.pulses.test.ts, bm04.reference.test.ts, fields.dipole.test.ts, fields.sr12.test.ts among them - every one of the form Math.abs(a - b) / b.

=== A GAP IN MY OWN TESTS, found by planting rather than by reading ===

My first plant sweep had three plants and only two discriminated. Replacing the difference test with a stub that treats the whole argument as both operands left the suite GREEN. The reason is worth recording: every negative I had written was also rejected by the DIVISOR test, so the two requirements were never separately covered. A reader would have concluded both were tested.

I added Math.abs(vx) / vx - sign extraction, which has a divisor naming its operand but no difference - and the same plant now fails exactly that case. Final plants:

  never match a relative comparison  -> 3 fail, the must-still-catch cases
  comment stripping removed          -> 1 fail, "does not read a comment as code"
  difference requirement dropped     -> 1 fail, the case I had been missing

=== BASELINE AND ALLOWLIST UNTOUCHED ===

By your instruction and on the merits. The baseline has no slack rule - it fails only when hits EXCEED it - so a more precise matcher leaves headroom rather than failing, and nothing had to be renumbered to make this green. git diff confirms neither the BASELINE map nor the allowlist changed.

=== THE DESIGN QUESTION IN THE BEAD'S FIRST ACCEPTANCE CRITERION ===

The bead asks whether the check should target relative comparisons specifically or whether shape-matching with a curated baseline was deliberate. I implemented the former, because the check's own name says "relative comparisons" and because the baseline's comments already catalogue the false positives under the heading "Legitimate mathematical formulas / UI plotting / quadrature estimates" - the authors recorded them rather than migrating them, which is what you do when a detector catches things you did not mean to catch.

The second half of that criterion - that new legitimate code of this shape has nowhere to go, since the allowlist is for pre-existing uses and the baseline may only shrink - is now MOOT for the cases pane31 hit: none of them matches any more, so none of them needs a slot. It would still bite a newly written genuine relative comparison, which is correct: that one should use the tolerance module.

EVIDENCE:
  bun test src/units/tolerance.test.ts -> 75 pass, 0 fail (was 66)
  biome check -> exit 0
  typecheck -> no error in this file
  git diff on the BASELINE map and allowlist -> empty

Bead left in_progress. I closed nothing.

title: The parallel-denylist gate's lower-threshold test scans nothing, and its self-exclusion is an unanchored prefix
description:
Found by the am-o44v sweep, following TanElk's steer: when a check proves the wrong property,
ask what the RIGHT property would have caught and try it once. This gate is the one protecting
the theater / mockery / overclaim / independence-claim vocabulary from being copied into a
second list - the vocabulary this whole sweep is about.

The checker itself is GOOD and should be said so: src/content/checks/voice/noParallelDenyLists.ts
derives its word list from the real content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml via
collectDenyListVocabulary(), scans real files, and requires MIN_MATCHING_TERMS = 3 before it
calls something a parallel deny list. That is a category test, not a substring proxy.

DEFECT 1 - THE LOWER HALF OF THE THRESHOLD IS UNTESTED, VACUOUSLY.
src/content/checks/voice/noParallelDenyLists.test.ts:38

    it("a list with only two matching terms does not fail", () => {
      const findings = scanForParallelDenyLists({ roots: [] });
      assert.deepEqual(findings, []);
    });

roots is EMPTY. It scans no file. The assertion is true for MIN_MATCHING_TERMS = 1, 2, 3 or 99,
so the boundary the test is named after is not exercised at all. There is no two-term fixture in
the tree: __fixtures__/parallel/ holds dangerousWords.ts, dangerousWords.yaml, fixture.ts and
fixture.yaml, and all four carry THREE terms (["streak","badge","score"] and
foolish/silly/absurd). fixture.ts and fixture.yaml are unused duplicates of the dangerousWords
pair.

EXECUTED - the shipped assertion, then the claim it is named for, asked properly with a
two-term list in my scratchpad so no file is added to the repo:

    (a) scanForParallelDenyLists({ roots: [] })                  -> 0   scans nothing
    (b) two-term   file, cwd = scratchpad                        -> 0   (must be 0)
        three-term file, cwd = scratchpad                        -> 1   (must be > 0)

So the threshold does work. It is simply unproven by the suite, and a change to
MIN_MATCHING_TERMS in either direction would leave this test green.

DEFECT 2 - THE SELF-EXCLUSION IS AN UNANCHORED PREFIX, WHICH IS A FAIL-OPEN.
noParallelDenyLists.ts:40-45

    function isExcluded(relativePath: string, excludeGlobs: readonly string[]): boolean {
      return excludeGlobs.some(
        (glob) =>
          relativePath === glob || relativePath.startsWith(`${glob}/`) || relativePath.startsWith(glob),
      );
    }

The third clause has no separator, so it subsumes the first two and matches any path that merely
BEGINS with the glob. scanRealTreeForParallelDenyLists passes
excludeGlobs: ["content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml", "src/content/checks/voice"], where the
second is meant to be the gate's own DIRECTORY.

EXECUTED, same probe:

    src/content/checks/voiceSmuggled.ts with three vocabulary terms,
      no exclusions                    -> 1 finding
      with the SHIPPED excludeGlobs    -> 0 findings

title: The light-thread refusal is authored, unit-tested, and unreachable: the control answers first in both engines
description:
The light-thread instrument has a typed refusal with authored wording, and a reader
driving the form can never reach it.

Measured in both engines against the production build, entering beta = 2 (the admission
bound is 0.999999) and pressing Apply settings:

    chromium: answered by the browser's control validation
              "Value must be less than or equal to 0.999999."
    webkit:   answered by the browser's control validation
              "Value must be less than or equal to 0.999999"

Never by the page. `<input type="number" ... max={LIGHT_THREAD_BOUNDS[key].max}>` in
LightThreadLab.tsx makes the form invalid, so submit never fires, so `session.apply`
never runs, so the refusal the instrument wrote for this exact case is never rendered.

## This is the dead-refusal shape, not a validation bug

The validation WORKS, and the control stopping bad input before it reaches the model is
the right behaviour. Nothing here is broken in the sense of admitting a bad value. What
is dead is the instrument's own voice: its refusal is authored, unit-tested, and
unreachable through the interface it guards.

    beta must be a finite number between -0.999999 and 0.999999.
    These are this instrument's admission bounds.

That second sentence is EDITORIAL CONTENT, not an error string. AGENTS.md draws the
distinction it carries - "The control bounds are numerical admission limits, not claims
of physical impossibility", and the page repeats it in its own model-limits disclosure.
A reader who bumps the control is told a number is too large; the thing the edition
wants them to understand, that this is a limit of the instrument and not of physics, is
exactly what the browser's message replaces.

## The fix is to let the instrument speak before the control does

Not to remove the control's protection, and not to loosen the bounds. Some path has to
reach the authored text: the instrument answering first for an out-of-range value, or
the control's message carrying the instrument's sentence, or both.

## What still holds, so this is not filed as a data defect

The claim that matters either way survives: after a refused setting the last accepted
worked example remains displayed, unchanged, in both engines. No stale number appears
under a new label. Verified in the same test.

## Provenance

Found by pane28 while exercising /lab/light-thread in Chromium and WebKit
(scripts/e2e/lightThread.e2e.test.ts, am-ahyb harness). Not caused by that work; the
test records which layer answered precisely because the answer was not obvious, and
accepts either so it does not hard-code today's behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Entering an out-of-range value in the light-thread form surfaces the instrument's own
  refusal text, including the admission-bounds sentence, in Chromium and in WebKit.
- The control still prevents the bad value from reaching the model: no out-of-range
  parameter is ever accepted, and the last accepted worked example still remains
  displayed unchanged.
- Planted negative that goes RED: removing the instrument's refusal wording, or routing
  the input around it again, is caught. The unreachable state is reachable today - it is
  what this bead records - so confirm the new gate fails against the CURRENT code before
  trusting it against the fixed code.
- The existing assertion in scripts/e2e/lightThread.e2e.test.ts that records which layer
  answered is updated to require the instrument's, not to accept either.

title: Refusal coverage is credited by basename substring, so a comment can mark a file covered
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator TanElk at clean HEAD 5af0d317: substring credit removed; baseline rose 15 -> 24 exposing 9 previously over-credited sites in 3 src files; comment-only plant is green under the fix and 7 pass / 2 fail under the restored defect, so the plant discriminates; ratchet 9 pass / 0 fail at HEAD.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
FOUND BY pane28, QUANTIFIED AND ESCALATED BY TanElk. pane28 hit this on itself and reported it in the 941ab351 message; I read the mechanism and measured the exposure, and it is much larger than the one instance.

THE MECHANISM, src/testing/refusals/refusalScanner.ts lines 360-364:

    // Basename mention in test file (e.g. tests referencing authored.ts)
    for (const srcRel of sitesByFile.keys()) {
      const b = basename(srcRel);
      if (content.includes(b)) {
        importedFiles.add(srcRel);
      }
    }

content.includes(basename) is a plain substring search over the ENTIRE text of a test file. Not an import graph, not a parse - the raw string. So a source file counts as "imported by" a test file if its basename appears anywhere in that file at all: in a comment, in a doc block, in a string literal, in an unrelated path.

HOW pane28 FOUND IT: its own comment in refusalRatchet.test.ts named a source file's basename next to a test block containing that file's refusal code, and the scanner credited the file with coverage, marking inventory-complete tested when it was not. Its slack pawl caught it. To be explicit about what that means - a passing comment produced coverage credit.

THE EXPOSURE IS NOT ONE FILE, IT IS THE WHOLE INSTRUMENT. Basenames are not unique here. Measured just now over src and scripts, excluding test, cases and fixture files: 1057 source files, and 74 basenames are shared by two or more files. The worst:

    session.ts     37 files
    definition.ts  32
    parameters.ts  31
    index.ts       31
    types.ts       29
    permalink.ts   25
    controls.ts    16
    browser.ts     12
    schema.ts      11

One occurrence of the string "session.ts" anywhere in one test file adds ALL THIRTY-SEVEN files named session.ts to importedFiles for that test file. Any test block in it asserting a code that one of those files throws then credits that file. Nobody has to intend this; writing "see types.ts" in a comment is enough.

WHY THIS IS P0. Every coverage number this instrument has produced is an upper bound of unknown tightness, and those numbers have been used as evidence. untestedRefusalsBaseline.json currently records 0 for 95 src files. am-muyh was closed on "eliminate 100% of untested refusal throw sites across entire repository". pane28's arriving measurement for the widened scan was "64 coded sites, 46 already covered, 18 not". If credit is being granted by substring, the true untested count is higher than 15 and possibly much higher, and the direction of the error is always the same: over-credit, never under-credit. This is the substring-match false positive class in the one instrument whose job is to tell us what is untested.

NOT AN ACCUSATION OF ANYONE. The heuristic was a reasonable shortcut when the scanner was small, and pane28 found it by auditing its own work and reported it against its own interest.

REQUIRED:
1. Replace basename substring matching with real import resolution - the file already imports node:path and resolves relative specifiers elsewhere in the same function, so the machinery exists a few lines up.
2. Until then, at minimum require a path-qualified match rather than a bare basename, and strip comments before matching.
3. RE-MEASURE the untested count afterwards and state it against the old number. Expect it to rise. A rise is the correct outcome and must not be treated as a regression to be baselined away - the tightening pawl will demand the new sites be paid down, and that demand is legitimate.
4. Prove it with a planted negative of the real defect: a test file that mentions a source basename ONLY in a comment, asserting that the source is no longer credited.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
pane28: FIXED, commit 5af0d317. Reporting, not closing.

RE-MEASURED AGAINST 15, staged so the two causes are attributable:
  15  before
  19  after replacing the basename substring with module resolution   (+4)
  24  after scoping explicit (file.ts:line) citations to imports      (+5)
Denominator unchanged at 1894 coded sites. The rise is the finding.

THE SECOND PATH, which your bead did not name and which I found while fixing the first: explicit site citations matched by basename too. (session.ts:42) written in a comment credited line 42 in all 37 session.ts files. A citation says WHICH SITE in a file a test drives; it is not itself a claim to have driven the file. It is now scoped to files the test imports, which keeps every legitimate use working since those tests do import their subject. That is the +5.

WHAT THE FIX IS: the resolver already in the same function, extended to read dynamic import(...) and require(...) specifiers as well as from. A test covers what it loads.

THE NINE SITES THAT WERE FALSELY CREDITED:
  src/content/manifest/schema.ts       6  missing-paper, invalid-document-bib-key, invalid-page-range, missing-units, invalid-unit, missing-export-id
  src/content/foundations/registry.ts  2  invalid-id, duplicate-id
  src/content/quantities/registry.ts   1  duplicate-id
All three basenames are shared ones. Two of the codes, invalid-page-range and missing-export-id, are named by NO test anywhere in the tree. missing-paper is named by four test files and not one of them imports this schema - it was a different file's code credited across the gap, which is exactly the cross-file laundering this scanner's own header has always claimed to prevent.

I RAISED BASELINE ENTRIES. Flagging it in the plainest terms because I otherwise never do and you check for it: three entries went 0 -> 1, 0 -> 2, 0 -> 6, total 15 -> 24. Not a gate relaxed to pass - nine debts that were hidden are now recorded per file and shrink-only, and the pawl will not let them grow. The alternative was leaving every pane red on work none of them touched. I have NOT paid them. They are real and payable, the manifest schema six look like ordinary validator accept/reject pairs, and I will take them if you want them.

PLANTS, restored byte-for-byte (sha256 7c9a3116...bf0c), 9 pass 0 fail after each:
  basename substring credit reinstated -> 7 pass 2 fail
  import resolution disabled           -> 7 pass 2 fail
Both caught by the new proof test and independently by the ratchet.

THE PROOF TEST you asked for: two fixture roots, identical but for how the test file refers to the source. One NAMES validate.ts in a comment and contains the code string in a test block, and must credit nothing. The other imports it and must credit it. The mentioning test file sits in a different directory on purpose - a co-located foo.test.ts is credited by its own separate rule and would have masked the result. That is the kind of masking that made my first precision fixtures pass for the wrong reason two commits ago, so I checked for it this time before claiming the plant.

STATE: refusalRatchet 9 pass 0 fail, census 'src: 1861 coded in 1204 files, 11 untested | scripts: 33 coded in 130 files, 13 untested'. typecheck clean, biome clean.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR CLOSURE EVIDENCE (TanElk). Verified by my own red-green-red cycle at 5af0d317, not from the report.

THE COUNT WENT UP, WHICH IS THE POINT. untestedRefusalsBaseline.json moved from sum 15 to sum 24. Three src files previously recorded 0 now carry real untested refusal sites:

  src/content/manifest/schema.ts        0 -> 6
  src/content/foundations/registry.ts   0 -> 2
  src/content/quantities/registry.ts    0 -> 1

Those basenames are exactly the colliding ones I measured when filing this: schema.ts is shared by 11 source files, registry.ts by 8. Nine untested refusal sites in src were being credited as covered because some test file somewhere contained those strings. This is the honest outcome, it is a RISE, and pane28 recorded it rather than suppressing it.

THE SUBSTRING CREDIT IS GONE. grep for content.includes(b) in refusalScanner.ts returns nothing; credit now comes from module resolution.

MY PLANT, AND WHY A GREEN RUN ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE CONVINCED ME. I appended to src/content/manifest/check.test.ts a comment naming schema.ts and nothing else - the exact defect, a basename mentioned only in a comment by a file that does not import it. With the fix in place: 9 pass / 0 fail, i.e. the comment bought no credit.

A green-only observation proves nothing about a plant, so I then restored the pre-fix behaviour, re-inserting the basename-substring credit into the scanner with the same comment still planted. Result 7 pass / 2 fail:

  (fail) no file exceeds its recorded baseline and no baseline is slack (enforced tightening pawl)
  (fail) a test file that only NAMES a source file credits it nothing; one that imports it credits it

So the plant discriminates: the defect restored makes it red, the fix makes it green. The second failing assertion is pane28's own, and it is the discriminating test I asked for - it names the distinction directly rather than a correlate of it.

Both files restored from backup, confirmed clean against HEAD with zero PLANT strings remaining, and the ratchet re-run in a detached worktree at clean HEAD 5af0d317: 9 pass / 0 fail.

ONE TRANSIENT I ALMOST MISREPORTED. Immediately after restoring, the main-tree run showed 8 pass / 1 fail and I briefly suspected my own plant had left residue. It had not - both files were byte-clean against HEAD. The failure was scripts/e2e-edition-pipeline.ts, dirty and uncommitted in the shared tree, where a pane is mid-edit adding a compile-errors refusal at line 268 with baseline 0. The worktree at HEAD is green. In-flight work in a shared tree is not a HEAD regression, and the way to tell them apart is to re-run at HEAD, not to reason about it.

WHAT THIS BEAD COSTS US ELSEWHERE, stated plainly rather than buried: am-muyh was closed on "eliminate 100% of untested refusal throw sites across entire repository", and we now know nine sites in three files were credited by substring at that time. That closure was made in good faith on an instrument that over-credited. I am not reopening it - its coded scope was real and the sites it did fix are fixed - but the "100%" in that record should be read as "100% of what the scanner could then see", and this comment is the pointer for anyone who relies on it later.

CLOSING on: baseline 15 -> 24 recorded not suppressed; substring credit removed; comment-only plant green under the fix and RED (7/2) under the restored defect, with a named discriminating assertion; clean HEAD 5af0d317 at 9 pass / 0 fail.

title: Author foundations: functions and graphs, derivatives, partial derivatives, exponentials, logarithms
description:
# Author foundations: functions and graphs, derivatives, partial derivatives, exponentials, logarithms

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §6.4, §7.5, §8.1, §8.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Four papers lean on the same small calculus toolkit: reading a family of curves, local sensitivity, what is held fixed in a partial derivative, dimensionless exponents, and logarithms that turn products into sums. These nodes are written for the physician who has not used a derivative since 1998 and for the programmer who distrusts "obviously," and each is anchored in a passage that needs it.

Two findings from light-paper review r2 bear on these nodes. The 1905 prints write "lg" for the natural logarithm, which modern readers would take for a base-10 logarithm. The light paper's §5 derives the logarithm in Boltzmann's principle from the fact that probabilities of independent systems multiply while entropies add, which is exactly this node's concrete entry point.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:functions-graphs` | A table of paired measurements | Read axes, inputs, outputs, slope, and a parameterized family |
| `foundation:derivatives` | Move one control a little and compare the output | Interpret local sensitivity with units |
| `foundation:partial-derivatives` | Change temperature while holding volume fixed | State what is held fixed and why it matters |
| `foundation:exponentials` | Repeated proportional changes | Read growth, decay, and dimensionless exponents |
| `foundation:logarithms` | Turn repeated multiplication into addition | Understand why independent probability products give additive entropy |

Owned elsewhere: integration and the Taylor expansion node (`am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`; this bead adds the binomial-series extension to it as a separate section record, as that bead expects); hyperbolic functions (`am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`); the bridges `foundation:bridge-a-graph` (`am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`) and `foundation:bridge-mathematical-punctuation` (`am-found-zero-algebra-rest-oipl`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples.**
- **Functions and graphs.** The radiation spectrum at several temperatures as a parameterized family (light §§1–4); a table of RMS displacement against time becoming a $\sqrt{t}$ curve (Brownian §5); the light paper's predicted straight line of stopping potential against frequency, whose slope does not depend on the metal (light §8).
- **Derivatives.** The stopping potential rises by $h/e \approx 4.14\times10^{-15}$ V per hertz of frequency (light §8); $\partial f/\partial t$ as the local rate of change of a density (Brownian §4); velocity as a ratio of differentials (relativity §5); the low-speed expansion's leading term (mass–energy).
- **Partial derivatives.** $(\partial s_\nu/\partial\rho_\nu)_\nu = 1/T$ with frequency and volume held fixed (light §3); $\partial n/\partial x$ versus $\partial n/\partial t$ (Brownian §§3–4); the chain rule for transformed derivatives (relativity §6).
- **Exponentials.** $e^{-\beta\nu/T}$ with a dimensionless exponent (light §4); the Gaussian $e^{-x^2/(4Dt)}$ (Brownian §4).
- **Logarithms.**
  - $\ln(f^n) = n\ln f$ for independent points (light §5).
  - Inverting Wien's law with a logarithm (light §4).
  - The free-energy term $N_p\ln V$ (Brownian §2).
  - Why a function that turns products into sums must be a logarithm: if $S = \varphi(W)$, $S_1 + S_2 = S$, and $W_1W_2 = W$, then $\varphi(W_1W_2) = \varphi(W_1) + \varphi(W_2)$, so $\varphi = C\ln W + \text{const}$ (light §5).
  - **Notation note:** the 1905 prints write "lg" for the natural logarithm; modern ISO notation reserves "lg" for $\log_{10}$. The node shows both glyphs on the same example ($\lg 2$ printed means $\ln 2 = 0.6931$, not $\log_{10}2 = 0.3010$).
- **Taylor expansion extension** (a section record owned here, rendered inside `foundation:taylor-expansion`, whose node record belongs to `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`).
  - The binomial series $(1 - x)^{-1/2} = 1 + \tfrac12x + \tfrac38x^2 + \tfrac{5}{16}x^3 + \tfrac{35}{128}x^4 + \cdots$ for $|x| < 1$, applied to $\gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.
  - At $v/c = 0.6$ ($x = 0.36$), the partial sums of $\gamma - 1$ are 0.18, 0.2286, 0.24318, and 0.247773 against the exact 0.25. The quadratic 0.18 is mass–energy's $0.18L$ fixture beside the exact $0.25L$, so a retained term, a neglected term, and a range of usefulness are all visible.
  - At $v/c = 10^{-4}$ ($x = 10^{-8}$) the exact $\gamma - 1 = 5.0000000375\times10^{-9}$, and the first term $5\times10^{-9}$ matches it to a relative $7.5\times10^{-9}$ (the next term's share, $0.75x$). This value is reproduced only by a cancellation-free evaluation with `expm1` and `log1p`; subtracting 1 from a rounded $\gamma$ in double precision returns $5.0000001917\times10^{-9}$ and a relative difference of $3.83\times10^{-8}$, five times too large. The node shows both routes and says which is trustworthy.
  - Planned callers: relativity §4 and mass–energy.

**Constructions.** A table-to-plot builder; a "nudge the control" sensitivity demo that reports the change and the ratio with units; a held-fixed toggle that shows two different partial derivatives of the same function; a repeated-proportional-change table; a product-to-sum table for logarithms with a toggle between "ln" and the printed "lg". Each has a textual equivalent.

**Prerequisites and stopping points.** Every prerequisite is typed `{foundationId, kind}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`).
- Functions and graphs rest on "a graph as a record of paired quantities" (`proof-edge` prerequisite `foundation:bridge-a-graph`).
- Derivatives rest on "a rate as change per unit of something".
- Logarithms rest on "how many times you multiply".
- Partial derivatives require derivatives (`proof-edge`).
- Logarithms and exponentials name each other as `cross-link` prerequisites, not as a proof circle, so the acyclicity check ignores that pair.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records.
- This bead authors captions for callers that exist when it lands: the Brownian reference slice (§§4–5) and the Brownian readings through §3.
- It records as `plannedCallers` in the registry: light §§1–5 and §8, relativity §§5–6, and mass–energy.

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/`; constructions use the instrument platform's controls and action contracts; numeric examples come from evaluator fixtures where possible and are compared through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`); registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Five complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] Each held-fixed example names the fixed quantities explicitly.
- [ ] The logarithms node carries the "lg" note and the product-to-sum derivation.
- [ ] The binomial-series extension renders inside the Taylor node without editing the slice bead's record, and states the cancellation-free evaluation rule with both computed values.
- [ ] Captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.
- [ ] Constructions have textual equivalents and keyboard operation; print and no-JavaScript renderings are complete.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundCalculus.numbers.test.ts`: quoted values through `src/units/tolerance.ts`: $h/e = 4.135667697\times10^{-15}$ V s; $\ln 2 = 0.693147$ against $\log_{10}2 = 0.301030$; the logarithm identity $\ln(f^n) = n\ln f$ for $n = 10$, $f = 1/2$ ($-6.931472$).
- `foundCalculus.logarithm.property.test.ts`: a property test that the product-to-sum construction satisfies $\ln(W_1W_2) = \ln W_1 + \ln W_2$ for random positive inputs.
- `foundCalculus.binomial.test.ts`: partial sums $0.18$, $0.2286$, $0.24318$, $0.247773$ at $x = 0.36$ against the exact $0.25$; at $v/c = 10^{-4}$, the cancellation-free route gives $\gamma - 1 = 5.0000000375\times10^{-9}$ and a relative difference of $7.500000\times10^{-9}$ to the first term, while a planted naive evaluation ($1/\sqrt{1 - x} - 1$) gives $5.0000001917\times10^{-9}$ and $3.833\times10^{-8}$ and fails the assertion, so the test documents why the stable route is required.
- `foundCalculus.records.test.ts`: compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, prerequisite typing (`cross-link` versus `proof-edge`, and a prerequisite missing `kind` rejected), and voice lint.
- Failure evidence (the failing example id, expected and actual values, and the evaluation route used) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- From Brownian §4 (reference slice), open `foundation:partial-derivatives`, toggle what is held fixed, and return to the exact step.
- From Brownian §5, open `foundation:functions-graphs`, build the plot from the table with keyboard only, and return.
- Open `foundation:logarithms` with JavaScript disabled and assert the "lg" note renders.

The light-paper routes into these nodes (for example from light §3) are exercised by `am-lq-e2e-x7z0`, not here.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-calculus/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never write "obviously" or "clearly."
- Keep "rate" and "sensitivity" explanations unit-bearing; a slope without units is not an explanation.
- Never render a printed "lg" as $\log_{10}$ in a modern form.
- Never quote a low-speed expansion figure obtained by subtracting 1 from a rounded $\gamma$; the digits that matter are the ones that cancel.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: integration, Taylor expansion, and the graph bridge these nodes link to.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these nodes.
- `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`: its `foundation:functions-graphs` and `foundation:derivatives` prerequisites are proof edges, so that cluster waits for this one.
- `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`, `am-srk-equations-30cq`, `am-sre-equations-2g3h`: chain tool links resolve to these nodes.
- `am-lq-readings-intro-s2-n0bq`, `am-lq-readings-s3-s4-k923`, `am-lq-readings-s5-s6-deq6`, `am-lq-readings-s7-s9-yorj`, `am-srk-readings-s3-odqp`, `am-srk-readings-s4-s5-njsh`, `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`, `am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp`: these readings link these nodes.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the 1904 desk's shelf explanations link these nodes.

description:
# Author foundations: frames and events, fields and waves, electromagnetism needed here, momentum and energy of light

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.3 (Introduction, §§1, 8), §7.2 (relativity first encounter), §7.5, §8.3, §8.4, §9.4–§9.5 shelves (traceability only)

## Background

The relativity paper opens with a moving magnet and a conductor, defines simultaneity through light signals, transforms fields and waves, and computes the energy of a light complex. The mass–energy paper follows the energy of two light pulses. The light paper's introduction contrasts continuous fields with discrete matter and notes that optical observations record time averages. Its §1 treats electrons bound by restoring forces as "resonators" that absorb and emit waves, and its §8 uses charges, potentials, and electron volts. Readers without an electromagnetism course need exactly these four nodes, and no more, to follow the claims.

**Batch note.** `am-me-readings-69bo` (Batch D) already depends on this bead for the momentum and energy of light, so this bead must land before the mass–energy paper, not only before relativity. It is labeled batch-d for that reason.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:frames-events` | Several clocks record local occurrences | Distinguish coordinate description, measurement procedure, and optical reception |
| `foundation:fields-waves` | Values across space sampled at successive times; frequency, wavelength, phase; the Doppler effect for sound | Understand phase, frequency, amplitude, direction, and local field quantities |
| `foundation:electromagnetism-needed-here` | A charge, a current, a field, and a detector; Maxwell's equations in words | Follow the paper's claims without a complete prior E&M course |
| `foundation:momentum-energy-light` | Radiation pressure and the momentum $E/c$ of a light pulse | Follow papers 3 and 4 |

Owned elsewhere: vectors, dot and cross products (`am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`); work and energy (`am-found-transport-thermo-smv3`); electrical unit systems (`foundation:unit-system-1905`, `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples (verified by test).**
- **Frames and events.** A signal leaves clock A at 0, reflects at B, and returns to A at 10. The synchronization procedure assigns B's reflection the time 5, a stated convention rather than a direct measurement of an unknowable one-way time. An event differs from its reception: a flash at B is seen at A later than it happened.
- **Fields and waves.**
  - $\lambda\nu = c$, so 600 THz corresponds to about 499.7 nm.
  - Phase $kx - \omega t$ with $k = 2\pi/\lambda$ and $\omega = 2\pi\nu$, keeping cyclic $\nu$ distinct from angular $\omega$.
  - Intensity as a time average: the average of $\cos^2$ over a period is $\tfrac12$, so what an optical observation records is not the instantaneous square (light introduction, LQ-01).
  - A point source of 1 W spreads its power over spheres, $I = P/(4\pi r^2) = 0.0796$ W/m² at 1 m and one quarter of that at 2 m.
  - The Doppler effect for sound differs for a moving source and a moving listener because air is a medium (a foundation analogy, never a proof about light).
- **Electromagnetism needed here.**
  - Forces $q\mathbf{E}$ and $q\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; potential difference and the electron volt.
  - A charge bound by a restoring force oscillates, absorbs, and emits waves of its own frequency, which is what the light paper's §1 calls a resonator.
  - Maxwell's equations in words: charges are sources of electric field; there are no magnetic charges; a changing magnetic field produces a circulating electric field; currents and changing electric fields produce a circulating magnetic field. Together they describe waves traveling at $c$.
  - The magnet-and-conductor case, where pre-1905 theory explains the same current by two different mechanisms.
- **Momentum and energy of light.**
  - 1 W of light absorbed pushes with $1/c \approx 3.34\times10^{-9}$ N, and twice that when reflected.
  - A pulse of energy $E$ carries momentum $E/c$; two equal pulses emitted in opposite directions carry zero total momentum.
  - Dated measurements of radiation pressure (Lebedev 1901; Nichols and Hull 1901–1903) and Poynting (1884) appear as dated context.

**Constructions.** A small event ledger with two clocks (with a table); a wave sampler with phase, frequency, and wavelength readouts and an instantaneous-versus-averaged intensity toggle; a separate sound-Doppler toy; a charge-and-field arrow view with a force readout; a radiation-pressure calculator. Each has a textual equivalent and keyboard operation. Where a construction would embed an instrument preset that is not yet registered (for example LQ-01 or ME-01), the node shows its static worked example with the library's status line.

**Prerequisites** (typed `{foundationId, kind}` entries, the shape defined in `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`):
- `foundation:quantities-units` (`am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`), `foundation:functions-graphs`, and `foundation:derivatives` (both `am-found-calculus-6agg`) as `kind: "proof-edge"`. All three are authored in Batch C, and this bead depends on both authoring beads, because the build refuses a proof-edge prerequisite whose target is still `planned`.
- `foundation:vectors-components` (`am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`, Batch E) as `kind: "cross-link"`. Under the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`, a cross-link to a `planned` node renders as "available later", never fails the build, and is reported by `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` until the node is authored. No proof route in these nodes depends on vectors, so this bead does not wait for Batch E.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t` for `FoundationLink {foundationId, callingAnchor, returnCaption?}` records (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`): this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records. This bead authors captions only for callers that exist when it lands. It records the following as `plannedCallers`; those beads author their captions when they link:
- the relativity introduction and §§1, 6, 7, 8, and 9;
- SR-01, SR-02, and SR-08 to SR-12;
- ME-01, ME-03, and the mass–energy readings;
- the light introduction, §1 (resonators), and §8 (potentials);
- LQ-01.

**Stopping points.**
- Event: "something that happens at one place and one time."
- Field: "a value assigned to every place."
- Charge: "the property that makes electric forces."
- Light's momentum: "the push a beam gives when absorbed."

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/`; numbers referenced from `am-ref-constants-xik` and, where live, from `am-ref-events-yvl` and `am-ref-waves-r53` fixtures; registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Four complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] The synchronization example states the convention explicitly; the sound analogy is labeled as an analogy with its limit; the time-average example is present.
- [ ] Quoted numbers match tests; constructions have textual equivalents; captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded.
- [ ] Every prerequisite carries `kind`: the three proof-edge prerequisites resolve to authored nodes, and the cross-link to `foundation:vectors-components` renders "available later" until `am-found-linear-geometry-7w15` authors it.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Numeric checks: 499.65 nm at 600 THz; $1/c = 3.3356\times10^{-9}$ N per watt (twice for reflection); the midpoint assignment 5; the $\cos^2$ period average 0.5 to $10^{-12}$; $P/(4\pi r^2) = 0.0795775$ W/m² at 1 m and $0.0198944$ at 2 m.
- Every numeric comparison calls `withinTolerance` from `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`) with the tolerance stated beside the value.
- Wording check that the sound Doppler example carries its analogy label.
- Compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, and typed prerequisites: a fixture that retypes the vectors cross-link as `proof-edge` fails the build while `foundation:vectors-components` is `planned`, and a fixture prerequisite without `kind` is rejected by the schema.

### End-to-end tests
- Open `foundation:frames-events` in the drawer from a fixture calling passage, step through the ledger by keyboard, and return with scroll restored.
- Open `foundation:momentum-energy-light` standalone, compute the push for 1 W, and read the table equivalent; repeat with JavaScript disabled.
- The mass–energy, relativity, and light routes are exercised by those papers' content lanes.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-fields-light/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never conflate what a distant camera sees with a simultaneous coordinate measurement.
- Keep Gaussian and SI conventions labeled when field formulas appear.
- Time-averaged intensity is a statement about observation; it is not evidence for or against light quanta.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, typed prerequisites, and link-record captions.
- `am-found-calculus-6agg`: authors `foundation:functions-graphs` and `foundation:derivatives`, which these nodes list as proof-edge prerequisites.
- `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`: authors `foundation:quantities-units`, a proof-edge prerequisite of these nodes.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: audits these nodes, their typed prerequisites, and their backlinks.
- `am-me-readings-69bo`, `am-lq-readings-intro-s2-n0bq`, `am-lq-readings-s3-s4-k923`, `am-lq-readings-s5-s6-deq6`, `am-lq-readings-s7-s9-yorj`, `am-srk-readings-intro-s2-00vk`, `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`, `am-sre-readings-s7-s8-lpje`, `am-sre-readings-s9-s10-3myq`: these readings link these nodes.
- `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`: its chain tool links and equation readings link the fields-and-waves and electromagnetism nodes.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the 1904 desk's objects link these nodes.
