title: Build the foundation library routes, drawer, backlinks, return captions, and proof-route checks
description:
# Build the foundation library routes, drawer, backlinks, return captions, and proof-route checks

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 2, §6.4, §6.8, §7.5, §15.1, §16.2, §16.3, §19.4 reader-shell closure (traceability only)

## Background

Unfamiliar mathematics must open into an explanation with a worked example, a picture or manipulable construction, and a route back to the exact interrupted argument. The foundation library is that route. It must work in two ways:
- as a drawer inside the reader, so the return stack keeps the paragraph, selected expression, laboratory state, and scroll position;
- as standalone pages at `/foundations` and `/foundations/[concept]`.

The reader shell's closure condition applies here too: a deep-linked passage survives face switching and foundation return.

The library is shared by four papers authored across Batches B to H by different agents. Two structural choices keep that safe:
- A **registry** of canonical ids (defined in `am-ep-foundations-z1e`) fixes every node's identity and single owner before its content exists.
- **Return captions** come from the caller's link record or from the node's `returnCaptions[]`, under one precedence rule, so a later paper never has to edit a foundation record owned by another bead.

A third structural choice belongs here for the same reason. Every foundation and every bridge requires "one worked example", and nothing says what an example is made of, so the shape would be left to each of the nine authoring beads. The five-part shape below lands with the registry, before the cluster beads author content, so it costs one decision rather than nine revisits.

## Scope

In scope:
- routes and index; drawer mode;
- registration of the `foundation` clarification kind in the reader's closed kind registry;
- the registry file and its validation;
- rendering of `Foundation` records and zero-algebra bridge records;
- the five-part worked-example contract, its rendering, and its validation in this bead's compiler projection;
- the transfer-case content contract and its coverage findings;
- link records and computed backlinks; per-link return-caption validation;
- stopping-point display and "deeper derivation available" markers;
- print and no-JavaScript rendering; accessibility of embedded constructions;
- tests.

Out of scope: authoring foundation content (the cluster beads and `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`); the `Foundation`, `FoundationLink`, `WorkedExample`, and typed-prerequisite schemas themselves (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`, which adds the structured worked example with a schema-version bump at this bead's request); the return stack, its store, and the `?open=` parser (`am-read-return-stack-oxa`); the compiler's acyclicity check itself (`am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`); the `support` ladder field and its stage semantics on journeys (`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, which consumes this contract); the voice-lint engine and its vocabulary file (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`); search indexing (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`); the prerequisite dead-end audit (`am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`).

## Requirements

- **Registry.** `content/foundations/registry.yaml` lists all 46 canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e` (36 nodes, 10 bridges), each with `id` (`foundation:<slug>`), `kind` (`node` or `bridge`), `cluster`, `ownerBead`, `status` (`planned` or `authored`), and `plannedCallers` (anchor ids expected from later papers).
  - The compiler fails on a duplicate id, an id without exactly one owner, a record whose id is not in the registry, an `authored` entry without a record, and a record whose kind differs from its registry entry.
  - This bead creates the registry with all 46 entries `planned`; owning beads flip their entries to `authored` in the same change that adds the record.
- **Routes.** `/foundations` lists every authored node grouped by cluster with its concrete entry point, and lists bridges in a separate "Explain from the beginning" group. `/foundations/[concept]` renders one node or bridge, where `[concept]` is the id's slug. One canonical URL per id; planned entries return not-found, never a placeholder page. Drawer deep links on reader routes use `?open=foundation:<slug>`, the form used by `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`.
- **The `foundation` clarification kind.** `am-read-return-stack-oxa` owns a **closed** registry of clarification kinds and names this bead as the registrar of `foundation`. This bead therefore calls `registerClarificationKind("foundation", { parseId, render, staticHref, title })` exactly once, at module scope of the foundations feature:
  - `parseId` accepts `foundation:<slug>` where `<slug>` is the id's slug under the id grammar of `docs/CONTENT_IDS.md` (lowercase words and digits joined by hyphens, a dot only between two digits), resolves it against the registry, and returns the canonical `foundation:<slug>` id; an unknown, planned, or malformed slug returns no value so the return stack ignores the `?open=` value rather than opening an empty drawer;
  - `render` draws the record in the companion column or bottom sheet described under Drawer mode;
  - `staticHref` returns `/foundations/<slug>`, which is what a no-JavaScript reader follows and what print uses;
  - `title` returns the node's learning objective heading for the drawer header, the compass entry, and the browser history entry.
  - Registering the kind twice throws in development and fails a test, per the return-stack contract. No other bead registers `foundation`, and this bead registers no other kind (`example` and `obstacle` belong to `am-read-passage-actions-vbe`).
- **Record rendering.** Learning objective; compact explanation; full explanation; one worked example in the five-part shape below; an optional instrument or manipulable construction (by instrument id and preset id, following the action contract); a textual equivalent; prerequisites (links); the stated stopping point; backlinks. If a referenced instrument or preset is not yet registered, the construction renders its static worked example with a visible "interactive version not yet available" status, never a broken embed.

### A worked example has five authored parts

The most valuable part of a good example is the part an author is least likely to write unprompted, so `WorkedExample` is a structured record with five required parts, added to the `Foundation` entity by `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` with a schema-version bump (the pattern `am-read-notebook-tde` uses for `ArgumentNode.recap`; requested with a `br comments add` note). This bead owns the rendering and the projection-time validation.

| Part | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `question` | The specific thing this example settles, in one sentence, naming the quantity |
| `given` | The information the reader starts with: the numbers, the units, and what is held fixed |
| `plausibleFirstThought` | **One reasonable first move a reader actually makes here**, stated without irony, with one sentence on why it is reasonable |
| `decisiveStep` | The calculation or comparison that settles the question, with its arithmetic shown |
| `limitation` | Where this example stops: what it does not show, and what changes at a realistic scale |

`plausibleFirstThought` is the part that earns the change. The editorial voice already forbids "obviously", "clearly" and "it is easy to see" (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`), on the reasoning that a reader at "Show every step" would not be there if it were easy. An example that shows only the correct move breaks that rule structurally rather than lexically: it implies the move was the natural one. Naming the reasonable first thought is the same fair-hearing discipline the site applies to Nägeli and Exner, applied to the reader.

Worked values in existing content, authored by the beads that own those records and shown here as the shape:

- The Brownian entrance (`am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`): `question` is whether four observations summing to zero show no movement; `given` is $-3, -1, +1, +3$ units, labeled authored and not measured; `plausibleFirstThought` is "add them up, which gives zero, so nothing moved"; the `decisiveStep` compares mean absolute displacement 2 with mean square 5, and doubling to 4 and 20; `limitation` says the four entries are an arithmetic illustration and that the real growth law needs many independent steps.
- `foundation:ratios-scaling` (owned by `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`): `plausibleFirstThought` is "doubling the viscosity halves the displacement", the site's own adversarial fixture, and the `decisiveStep` shows the change is $1/\sqrt{2} = 0.70711$.

Rules:

- `limitation` may not be empty. An example with no stated limit is an example claiming to be general, which no example is.
- `plausibleFirstThought` may not be phrased as a mistake the reader should not have made. The voice lint gains a small rule set for it: no "of course", no "many people wrongly", no "the naive answer". It is registered with `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, not kept here, so no parallel deny list exists.
- The `decisiveStep` is **revealable immediately**. It renders inside a native disclosure open by default at Detail "Show every step" and closed at "Overview" and "Full explanation", with a control that opens it in one action. There is no gate, no attempt counter, and no record of whether the reader opened it. Struggling first is never required and revealing is never counted.
- The five parts render in order, statically, in print, and without JavaScript, where the disclosure is the browser's own.

### Transfer changes a condition, not a number

`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg` carries `support.transferCase` on every stage and owns that field. Its content contract belongs here, because a transfer case is a worked example with one condition moved, and the foundations projection is where examples are validated:

- A transfer case changes something **structural**: a different statistic, a different pair of events, a different system boundary. Changing only the numbers is not a transfer case, and the coverage pass reports it as `transfer-not-structural`.
- The three cases the site already has the instruments for:
  - after explaining mean square, ask about mean absolute displacement (BM-01, whose statistic control offers it as an `estimator-change`, and the entrance's own arithmetic module `src/reader/entrances/signedDisplacements.ts`);
  - after explaining contraction, ask for a different pair of endpoint events (SR-03, whose rod measurement is exactly a choice of two named events);
  - after an energy ledger, change the chosen system boundary (ME-03, whose boundary is a control).
- **Feedback contract.** The authored response to a transfer case names two things explicitly: **what remains valid** from the original example, and **which newly introduced condition changes the answer**. A response that only states the new answer fails the coverage pass with `transfer-feedback-incomplete`. This is what turns a transfer case from a second exercise into an account of what the reader now understands.
- Both findings are written in the input format of `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`, the format this bead's other coverage output already uses.
- Transfer feedback is never scored and never recorded as competence, consistent with this bead's "No tests or scores" requirement below.

- **Zero-algebra bridges.** A bridge record renders its small obstacle, concrete bridge, and "readiness shown without a test." "Explain from the beginning" in the reader lands on a bridge, never on another paragraph of abstract vocabulary. A bridge carries the same five-part worked example as a node.
- **Link records and backlinks.** Every reference to a foundation from a reading, equation tool link, derivation step, instrument caption, or "What is getting in the way?" response is a `FoundationLink` record `{foundationId, callingAnchor, returnCaption?}` (the shape defined in `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`), stored with the calling record and authored by its owner.
  - The compiler computes backlinks from link records; each backlink shows the calling anchor, a short context, and the caption.
  - **Return-caption precedence**, the contract this bead enforces when it computes backlinks: the link's `returnCaption` is used when present; otherwise the node's `returnCaptions[]` entry for the same `callingAnchor`; a link with neither caption fails the build; a link whose own caption and the node's entry for that anchor both exist and differ fails the build; a node `returnCaptions[]` entry whose anchor has no link is flagged as stale.
  - **Typed prerequisites.** Prerequisites are typed `{foundationId, kind: "proof-edge" | "cross-link"}` (the field name is `kind`, as landed in `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`; a prerequisite without `kind`, or with `kind: "proof"`, is rejected by the schema). A link from a calling passage, or a prerequisite of `proof-edge` type, to a `planned` or unknown id fails the build. A prerequisite typed as a `cross-link` to a `planned` id renders as "available later" and is reported by `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` until its target is authored. Cross-link prerequisites never enter a proof route's acyclicity check.
- **Return captions.** Authored per calling passage, naming the right quantity and what is held fixed there (for example, "Back to light quanta §3: $\partial\varphi/\partial\rho$ with volume and frequency held fixed").
- **Drawer mode.** Opening a foundation from the reader uses the companion column on desktop and a bottom sheet on phones; the return stack and compass restore the exact sentence, expression, laboratory state, and scroll position; one action closes all side explanations.
- **Proof routes.** Where a foundation is a tool in a selected proof route, the page shows the route back to entry assumptions and marks deeper derivations as available; concept-map cross-links are displayed as cross-links. A reader may stop at an understood result.
- **Print and no-JavaScript.** Full static HTML; drawers degrade to real links produced by the kind's `staticHref`; print expands essential parts, including the decisive step and the limitation, and never prints a collapsed heading alone.
- **No tests or scores.** Nodes never quiz the reader or record competence.

## Technical Approach

- Pages under `src/app/foundations/`; rendering components under `src/reader/`; registry, worked-example, transfer-case, link-record, backlink, and caption validation in the content compiler's route projection.
- The drawer uses the return-stack store from `am-read-return-stack-oxa`, and the `foundation` kind is registered against that bead's `registerClarificationKind` API; foundation pages consume only compiled, route-local payloads.
- `FoundationLink`, `WorkedExample`, and the typed prerequisite shape are imported from the shared schemas of `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`, never redeclared here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The registry exists with all 46 canonical ids, kinds, owners, and statuses, and its validation rules fail on the fixture violations listed below.
- [ ] The registry's node, bridge and id totals come from the canonical id table of `am-ep-foundations-z1e` rather than from a number typed here; a fixture registry holding 45 entries against that bead's 46-row table fails with both counts named.
- [ ] Index and node routes render every authored foundation and bridge statically; planned ids return not-found.
- [ ] The `foundation` clarification kind is registered exactly once with `parseId`, `render`, `staticHref`, and `title`; `?open=foundation:<slug>` opens the drawer for an authored id and is ignored for an unknown, planned, or malformed one; a second registration fails.
- [ ] Every backlink has exactly one return caption (from its link record or the node's `returnCaptions[]`) and every link resolves to an authored id; the build fails otherwise.
- [ ] A `proof-edge` prerequisite to a planned id fails the build, while a `cross-link` prerequisite to a planned id renders "available later" and is reported to the prerequisite audit.
- [ ] Drawer open and close restores the exact reading state on desktop and at 320 px.
- [ ] "Explain from the beginning" lands on bridge records.
- [ ] A construction whose instrument is unregistered renders its static worked example with the status line.
- [ ] Print and JavaScript-disabled renderings are complete, and every drawer link has a real `staticHref` target.
- [ ] Every authored `Foundation` and bridge carries a five-part `WorkedExample`; a record missing any part fails compilation with the part named and the foundation id.
- [ ] An empty `limitation` fails; an empty `plausibleFirstThought` fails.
- [ ] The five parts render in order on `/foundations/[concept]` and in the drawer, at every Detail, in print, and with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] `decisiveStep` is open by default at "Show every step" and closed at the other two Detail levels, opens in one action, and nothing about opening it is stored or logged as reader behavior.
- [ ] Voice lint fails a seeded `plausibleFirstThought` containing "of course", "many people wrongly" and "the naive answer", and passes the Brownian entrance's version.
- [ ] Every `support.transferCase` in a compiled journey changes a structural condition; a fixture that changes only numbers is reported as `transfer-not-structural`.
- [ ] Every transfer case's feedback names what remains valid and which new condition changes the answer; a fixture stating only the new answer fails with `transfer-feedback-incomplete`.
- [ ] The three named transfer cases resolve to `bm-01`, `sr-03` and `me-03` respectively, each naming an action its instrument's action contract offers.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundationRegistry.test.ts`, registry validation with fixtures:
  - a duplicate id fails;
  - an id with two owners fails;
  - a record missing from the registry fails;
  - an `authored` entry without a record fails;
  - a kind mismatch fails;
  - the real registry has exactly 36 nodes and 10 bridges, and every `ownerBead` is a bead id that exists;
  - a registry whose entry count differs from the canonical id table of `am-ep-foundations-z1e` fails naming both counts, and `foundation:two-measurements-two-unknowns` resolves to `am-found-statistics-inference-pzqv` with `kind: node`.
- `foundationRender.test.tsx`: rendering with fixture records: all parts present; optional construction absent renders cleanly; unregistered instrument renders the static example and status; a bridge renders obstacle, bridge, and readiness.
- `foundationKind.test.ts`: the clarification-kind registration: the kind registry contains `foundation` after the feature module loads; `parseId("foundation:mean-variance-rms")` resolves for an authored id; `parseId` returns nothing for an unknown slug, a `planned` id, an uppercase or dotted slug, and an over-long value; `staticHref` returns `/foundations/mean-variance-rms`; `title` returns the node's learning objective; a second `registerClarificationKind("foundation", ...)` throws.
- `foundationBacklinks.test.ts`, compiler projection tests: backlinks computed from fixture link records; a link whose caption comes from the node's `returnCaptions[]` passes; a link with no caption in either place fails with a message naming the calling anchor; a link caption and a node caption for the same anchor that differ fail; a stale node caption is flagged; a calling link or `proof-edge` prerequisite to a planned id fails, while a `cross-link` prerequisite to a planned id renders as available later and appears in the audit input; a prerequisite without `kind` is rejected by the schema; a bridge lacking a required field fails.
- `foundationProofRoutes.test.ts`: a fixture route with a cross-link cycle renders, while a cycle inside a selected proof route is rejected by the compiler check.
- `workedExample.schema.test.ts` (real schema, real fixture foundations):
  - all five parts required, each absence failing with the part named;
  - an empty `limitation` and an empty `plausibleFirstThought` fail;
  - the Brownian entrance's example validates, and its `decisiveStep` arithmetic is checked against `src/reader/entrances/signedDisplacements.ts`: signed sum 0, mean absolute 2, mean square 5, doubled 4 and 20, RMS $\sqrt5 = 2.2360680$ and $\sqrt{20} = 4.4721360$, compared through `withinTolerance` from `src/units/tolerance.ts`;
  - the `foundation:ratios-scaling` example's `decisiveStep` asserts $1/\sqrt{2} = 0.7071068$ and not $0.5$.
- `workedExample.render.test.tsx`: part order; disclosure open at Detail 2 and closed at 0 and 1; one action opens it; no storage write and no log event on open; native disclosure without JavaScript.
- `voiceLint.integration.test.ts` (addition): the `plausibleFirstThought` rule set, one passing and one failing fixture per banned phrase.
- `transferCase.test.ts` (against real compiled journeys):
  - a case that changes only a numeric input is reported as `transfer-not-structural`;
  - feedback missing either half fails with `transfer-feedback-incomplete`;
  - the three named cases resolve to `bm-01`, `sr-03` and `me-03` and each names an action present in that instrument's action contract;
  - both findings validate against the coverage ledger's input schema.

### End-to-end tests
- From a reading-face paragraph in the Brownian reference slice:
  - Open a foundation in the drawer, operate its construction, follow a prerequisite, and use the compass to return.
  - Assert sentence focus, selected expression, laboratory snapshot id, and scroll offset are restored, and the caption shown is the one the precedence rule selects.
  - Open the same node from a `?open=foundation:<slug>` deep link and assert the drawer opens at that id with its compass; request `?open=foundation:not-a-node` and assert the value is ignored and the passage still renders.
  - Repeat at 320 px (bottom sheet), keyboard-only, with reduced motion, and with JavaScript disabled (the drawer link degrades to the `staticHref` page).
- Print a foundation page and assert expanded content, including the decisive step and the limitation; request a planned id and assert not-found.
- In `e2e/foundations/worked-example.spec.ts`, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:
  1. Open a foundation from a Brownian §4 passage in the drawer, read the five parts in order, and reveal the decisive step in one action.
  2. Switch Detail to "Show every step" and assert the decisive step is already open.
  3. Assert the network log records no request and the storage layer records no write from opening it.
  4. Follow a transfer case from a journey stage, read the feedback, and assert it names both halves.
  5. Repeat with JavaScript disabled using the native disclosure, at 320 px, keyboard only, and in print.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/foundations-infra/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "foundations-infra"`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `returnAnchor`, `captionSource` (`link` or `node`), `prerequisiteKind`, restored state fields (`snapshotVersion`, scroll offset, expression id), `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `reducedMotion`, `message`; failure evidence (screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console log) retained under `artifacts/test-logs/foundations-infra/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.
- Worked-example and transfer lines add `kind` (`node` or `bridge`), `examplePartsPresent`, `limitationLength`, `firstThoughtLength`, `decisiveStepOpenByDefault`, `detail`, `transferCaseId`, `transferChangesCondition`, `feedbackHalvesPresent`, `instrumentId`, `rule`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, and `comparisonKind`.
- Logs never record whether a reader opened the decisive step; `decisiveStepOpenByDefault` records the authored default, not a reader action.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never let a foundation become an infinite cascade of definitions; the stopping point is part of the record.
- Do not duplicate foundation text inside readings; R2 embeds foundations by reference.
- Do not let a later bead edit another bead's foundation record to add a caption; a later caller's caption belongs on its own link record.
- Do not widen the clarification-kind registry: it is closed, and `foundation` is the only kind registered here.
- `plausibleFirstThought` is not a misconception entry. A misconception is a belief a reader carries in; a first thought is a move a reader makes here, and most first thoughts are partly right.
- Do not use the first thought to set up a reveal. It is stated, it is respected, and the decisive step shows what it does and does not settle.
- `limitation` is where the example stops, not where the physics stops. "Four entries are not a distribution" is a limitation of the example; "the diffusive law needs intervals long compared with the relaxation time" is a limitation of the model and belongs to the argument node.
- Never gate the decisive step behind an attempt. The site's own rule is that guessing is never a condition for continuing, and an example that hides its answer until the reader tries is a quiz.
- The transfer feedback's "what remains valid" half is the one authors drop. It is also the half that produces transfer: a reader who is told only the new answer learns a second fact, not a method.
- Nine beads author examples. Landing the shape after they start means nine revisits, so it belongs here, with the registry, before the cluster beads author content.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: App Router structure and reader shell.
- `am-read-return-stack-oxa`: return stack, compass, the `?open=` parser, and the `registerClarificationKind` API this bead calls.

title: Author foundations: vectors, matrices and linear maps, dot and cross products, hyperbolic functions and rapidity, conservation and symmetry
description:
# Author foundations: vectors, matrices and linear maps, dot and cross products, hyperbolic functions and rapidity, conservation and symmetry

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.3 (later aids), §4.7 (the $\beta$ collision), §7.5, §8.3 (constructed map, boost matrix, rapidity), §12.6 (observer change), §13.3 (boost fixtures) (traceability only)

## Background

The relativity paper and its instruments ask readers to:
- describe one event or one arrow in two frames;
- read a transformation as a rule that combines inputs;
- follow field components parallel and perpendicular to a boost;
- recognize what stays unchanged when the description changes.

These nodes supply those tools for the programmer who thinks in matrices and for the reader meeting them for the first time. Rapidity and spacetime geometry are later aids and are labeled as such; they never become premises of the 1905 route.

One notation hazard runs through this cluster. The usual modern shorthand $\beta = v/c$ collides with the site's most dangerous collision: Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$ in papers 3 and 4, and Wien's constant in paper 1. These nodes therefore write $v/c$ and never use $\beta$ for it.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:vectors-components` | Describe one arrow in two coordinate systems | Change components without confusing that with changing the object |
| `foundation:matrices-linear-maps` | Transform a grid and an event table together; determinants, eigenvectors | Read a matrix as a rule for combining inputs |
| `foundation:dot-cross-products` | Projection and oriented area | Follow field transformations and magnetic-force directions |
| `foundation:hyperbolic-functions-rapidity` | $\cosh$, $\sinh$, $\tanh$ and why boosts add like angles | Follow the composition of velocities (labeled as a later aid) |
| `foundation:conservation-symmetry` | Relabel an experiment or change frame | Identify a quantity or relation that should remain unchanged |

Owned elsewhere: frames and events (`foundation:frames-events`, `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`); exponentials and logarithms (`am-found-calculus-6agg`); the binomial series used for low-speed expansions (the Taylor extension authored by `am-found-calculus-6agg`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples (modern golden values, verified by test).**
- **Vectors and components.** One velocity of $0.6c$ along $x$ described in rotated axes. The same field vector split into components parallel and perpendicular to a boost. Changing the description is an observer change, not a change of the world.
- **Matrices and linear maps.**
  - The boost at $v = 0.6c$ acting on $(x, t)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}1.25 & -0.75c\\ -0.75/c & 1.25\end{pmatrix}$, with determinant 1.
  - Its eigenvectors lie on the light lines $x = \pm ct$, with eigenvalues 0.5 and 2.
  - Two events 10 light-seconds apart and simultaneous map to $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds.
  - Contrast the Galilean map $\begin{pmatrix}1 & -v\\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix}$, also of determinant 1, which does not keep light lines fixed.
  - The matrix view is a pedagogical aid, not the paper's §3 presentation. The diagonal entry is written $\gamma = 1.25$, with the note that the relativity paper prints this quantity as $\beta$.
- **Dot and cross products.** $\mathbf{E}_\parallel$ as a projection on the boost direction; the direction of $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ as a modern invariant check.
- **Hyperbolic functions and rapidity (later aid).**
  - $\gamma = \cosh\phi$, $\gamma\,v/c = \sinh\phi$, $v/c = \tanh\phi$.
  - $v/c = 0.6$ gives $\phi = \ln 2$. Two collinear boosts of $0.6c$ add rapidities to $\ln 4$, so $v/c = \tanh(\ln 4) = 15/17 \approx 0.8824$.
  - The eigenvalues $e^{\mp\phi}$ are the Doppler factors 1/2 and 2.
  - The node does not write $\beta$ for $v/c$, and its first-use note warns that Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$ (papers 3 and 4) and Wien's constant (paper 1).
- **Conservation and symmetry.** The light-speed postulate as a relation kept in both frames. In the two-pulse argument, energies differ between frames while each frame's balance holds. Interval preservation serves as a modern verification oracle, never a premise of the historical route.

**Constructions.** An arrow with draggable axes and a component table; a grid-and-event-table transformer with determinant and eigenvector readouts; a projection and oriented-area view; a rapidity adder; a "change the description, keep the world" comparison using the command-class vocabulary. Each has a textual equivalent and keyboard operation. Where a construction would embed an SR instrument preset (for example SR-04's matrix view) that is not yet registered, the node shows its static worked example with the library's status line.

**Prerequisites.** Every prerequisite is typed `{foundationId, kind}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`), each a link record with a caption: `foundation:quantities-units` and `foundation:functions-graphs` are `proof-edge` prerequisites (authored in Batch C); vectors is a `proof-edge` prerequisite of matrices and of the products node; `foundation:exponentials` and `foundation:logarithms` are `proof-edge` prerequisites of the rapidity node; `foundation:frames-events` is a `cross-link` from the conservation node, so the Batch D cluster's node may render "available later" without weakening any proof route.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records. This bead authors captions only for callers that exist when it lands. It records relativity §§3, 5, 6, and 7, SR-04, SR-06, SR-08, and mass–energy's two ledgers as `plannedCallers`; those beads author their captions when they link.

**Stopping points.**
- Vector: "an arrow with a length and a direction."
- Matrix: "a table of multipliers applied to inputs."
- Dot product: "how much of one arrow lies along another."
- Hyperbolic functions: "combinations of $e^x$ and $e^{-x}$."
- Symmetry: "a change that leaves the measured outcome unchanged."

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/`. Numeric examples are pulled from `am-ref-kinematics-tjq` fixtures at build time where constructions embed live values, and every comparison runs through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`). Later-aid labels are carried as historical-status metadata so `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2` can check them. Registry entries are flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Five complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] Rapidity and the matrix view carry later-aid labels; nothing presents interval preservation as a 1904 premise.
- [ ] No node uses $\beta$ for $v/c$; the collision note appears at first use of $\gamma$ and $v/c$.
- [ ] Quoted values match tests; constructions have textual equivalents; captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundLinearGeometry.numbers.test.ts`, through `src/units/tolerance.ts`: $\gamma = 1.25$ and $\gamma\,v/c = 0.75$ at $0.6c$; determinant $1.25^2 - 0.75^2 = 1$; eigenvalues 0.5 and 2; $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds for two simultaneous events 10 light-seconds apart; $\operatorname{artanh}(0.6) = \ln 2 = 0.6931471806$; $\tanh(\ln 4) = 15/17 = 0.8823529412$; the Galilean map's determinant is also 1 while its eigenvectors are not the light lines.
- `foundLinearGeometry.glyph.test.ts`: a check fails if any of these records binds $\beta$ to `speedRatio` or writes "β = v/c", and asserts the collision note is present at first use of $\gamma$.
- `foundLinearGeometry.records.test.ts`: anachronism lint over the records (later-aid labels present and dated); compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, and typed prerequisites.
- Failure evidence (the failing value or record id, expected and actual) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- Open `foundation:matrices-linear-maps` in the drawer from a fixture calling passage in the compiled test corpus, transform the event table by keyboard, read the determinant, and return to the fixture anchor with scroll restored.
- Open `foundation:hyperbolic-functions-rapidity` standalone and assert the later-aid label and the $\beta$ collision note; repeat with JavaScript disabled.
- The relativity routes (from SR-04 and §§3–7) are exercised by the relativity content lanes.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-linear-geometry/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Passive frame changes and active physical changes must never blur; say which one each example is.
- Non-collinear boost composition includes a rotation; the rapidity node restricts its adding rule to collinear boosts and says so.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-ref-kinematics-tjq`: the boost fixtures quoted here.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these nodes.
- `am-srk-readings-s3-odqp`, `am-srk-readings-s4-s5-njsh`, `am-sre-readings-s6-c5i4`: these readings link these nodes.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the 1904 desk's shelf explanations link the vector and symmetry nodes.

title: Audit the prerequisite graph for dead ends, stopping points, and complete backlinks
description:
# Audit the prerequisite graph for dead ends, stopping points, and complete backlinks

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 2, §6.4, §7.5, §19.3 H exit, §21 ("the arguments are reconstructible") (traceability only)

## Background

Batch H's exit evidence includes a prerequisite graph with no dead ends, and the launch definition requires that a reader can follow each main result without a missing prerequisite. Once the four papers have passed their definitions of done, this audit proves the foundation library actually closes every gap the papers open, and that every explanation ends at a stated stopping point instead of an infinite cascade.

The library's structure makes most of this mechanically checkable:
- the registry of 45 canonical ids with exactly one owner each (`am-ep-foundations-z1e`, `am-found-library-infra-002t`);
- link records that carry their own return captions;
- typed prerequisites, `{foundationId, kind: "proof-edge" | "cross-link"}` (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`), where a cross-link to a node still `planned` renders "available later" and is reported here until the node is authored;
- `plannedCallers` recorded by each owning bead for passages authored later.

## Scope

In scope: an automated audit across all four papers plus an editorial spot-check; a written report; issues filed against owning beads.

Out of scope: writing or fixing content (owning beads); the proof-route acyclicity check itself (`am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`), whose results the audit consumes; the readings-ownership audit (`audit-readings.ts`), whose `owner-unassigned` and `owner-conflict` results the papers' definition-of-done beads consume.

## Requirements

**Automated checks (`scripts/audit-prerequisites.ts`, run by `verify-content`).**
- **Registry.** All 35 foundation nodes and 10 bridges in `content/foundations/registry.yaml` are `authored`, each with exactly one owning bead; no entry is `planned`. Extension section records (for example the binomial-series section of `foundation:taylor-expansion` and the inference sections of the statistics nodes) name their owning bead and attach to an authored node.
- **Records.** Every foundation has a compact explanation, worked example, textual equivalent, prerequisites, stopping point, and at least one calling passage. A node with no calling passage is flagged for editorial review.
- **Planned callers.** Every `plannedCallers` entry either appears as an actual link record from that anchor, or is removed from the registry with a written reason.
- **Prerequisites.** Every prerequisite id resolves and carries its `kind`. Following `proof-edge` prerequisites from any node terminates at stopping points or bridges (no dangling chains). Cross-links are typed as cross-links and are excluded from the proof-route acyclicity check. **At audit time no cross-link prerequisite may still render "available later":** a cross-link whose target is still `planned` is a finding against the target's owning bead, because by Batch H every registry entry is `authored`.
- **Links and captions.** Every link record resolves to an authored id and carries a return caption that names a quantity or an operation. Every computed backlink therefore has a caption. No calling link points at a `planned` id.
- **Drawer addressing.** The `foundation` clarification kind is registered exactly once (by `am-found-library-infra-002t`), and every `?open=foundation:<slug>` appearing in compiled content parses to an authored registry id.
- **Entry to bridges.** Every "Explain from the beginning" action in the four papers lands on a bridge.
- **Tracked operations.** Every occurrence of a tracked mathematical operation in R1 and R2 readings, equation readings, and instrument captions either links a foundation or carries an authored inline explanation. The vocabulary is: derivative, partial derivative, integral, limit, series expansion, binomial series, logarithm (including the printed "lg" for the natural logarithm), exponential, Fourier series, variation with a Lagrange multiplier, vector, matrix, determinant, eigenvector, dot product, cross product, probability, variance, Gaussian, chi-square, hyperbolic function, and a unit-system conversion (abvolt, statvolt, gram-equivalent).
- **Proof routes and labels.** Selected proof routes are acyclic to their entry assumptions (consumed from the compiler), and later aids are labeled.
- **Glyph hygiene.** No foundation text uses $\beta$ for $v/c$ or otherwise binds a scoped paper glyph to a different meaning without its collision note.

**Editorial spot-check.** A reviewer samples at least two hard passages per paper at R2, follows every foundation link to its stopping point, and records whether the return lands on the exact argument with the caption naming the right quantity.

**Report.** `docs/acceptance/foundations-prerequisite-audit.md` with per-paper counts, the registry summary, the flagged items, and links to comments or reopened beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The automated audit passes with zero dead ends, zero missing captions, zero `planned` registry entries, zero cross-link prerequisites still rendering "available later", and zero unresolved planned callers.
- [ ] Every flagged orphan node is either linked from a calling passage or removed from the launch set with a written reason (no deletion of files without permission).
- [ ] The spot-check is recorded and its findings resolved.
- [ ] The report is published in the repository.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `auditPrerequisites.fixtures.test.ts`: the audit script's own tests with fixture graphs and registries. Each of the following fails with an actionable message naming the id and its owning bead:
  - a dangling prerequisite;
  - a prerequisite without `kind`;
  - a cross-link prerequisite whose target is still `planned` at audit time;
  - a link record without a caption;
  - a calling link to a planned id;
  - a registry entry with two owners;
  - an unresolved planned caller;
  - an untracked operation without a link;
  - an "Explain from the beginning" action landing on a non-bridge;
  - a `?open=foundation:<slug>` value that does not parse to an authored id;
  - an extension section attached to a missing node;
  - a proof-route cycle.
- A passing fixture proves a cross-link cycle is allowed while every registry entry is `authored`.
- Failure evidence (the finding list with ids, owning beads, and the check that produced each) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- A browser run that, for each paper, follows one tracked-operation link from R2 to its stopping point and back, asserting exact return and the caption text.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-prereq-audit/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `check`, `foundationId` or `anchor`, `prerequisiteKind`, `ownerBead`, `status`, `outcome`, and `message` for each finding; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The operation vocabulary is a heuristic; the editorial spot-check catches what it misses.
- Fix gaps by improving explanations first; adding a node must be justified by a calling passage.
- A finding is filed against the owning bead, never resolved by editing another bead's record.

## Dependencies

- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`, `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`, `am-dod-relativity-105y`, `am-dod-light-quanta-7as8`: the papers' readings and chains must be complete.

title: Author foundations: quantities and units, ratios and scaling, orders of magnitude, and the 1905 unit system
description:
# Author foundations: quantities and units, ratios and scaling, orders of magnitude, and the 1905 unit system

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.5, §8 intro (constant sets), §13.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Every paper mixes quantities across scales and unit systems: Einstein's printed viscosity in poise, Planck's constants in CGS, the light paper's photoelectric check in electromagnetic CGS units, Gaussian fields in the relativity paper, micrometers and seconds in Brownian motion. These four nodes let any reader place a number on a scale, check whether an equation's dimensions agree, and convert the printed historical values.

Light-paper review r2 found, through a comparison translation and a reviewer's recollection, that paper 1's 4.3 V check appears to use a gram-equivalent charge $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ in **electromagnetic** units, with $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ read as volts. An esu elementary charge with a statvolt factor is the documented alternative, and the facsimile decides. The 1905 unit system node therefore covers both CGS electrical systems.

## Scope

Nodes owned here (canonical ids from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`; each with compact explanation, one worked example, construction where useful, textual equivalent, prerequisites, stopping point):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:quantities-units` | Is a number in meters comparable with one in seconds? | Distinguish a quantity from its number; check an equation's dimensions |
| `foundation:ratios-scaling` | Double a length; compare area, volume, and a plotted effect | Predict proportional, inverse, and squared dependence |
| `foundation:orders-of-magnitude` | A water molecule versus a 1 μm grain; $v/c$ for a bullet, a jet, the Earth's orbit, Kaufmann's electrons; $h\nu$ for red, green, ultraviolet; molecular kicks per second on a grain | Place every number in the papers on a scale |
| `foundation:unit-system-1905` | Gaussian and CGS to SI, with Einstein's own numbers | Convert his printed values |

Owned elsewhere: scientific notation and units as a zero-algebra bridge (`foundation:bridge-scientific-notation-units`, `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`); functions and graphs (`am-found-calculus-6agg`).

## Requirements

**Worked examples (numbers verified by test against the reference evaluators and constant sets).**
- **Quantities and units.** $D = k_BT/(6\pi\eta a)$ has units m²/s. The light paper's $\rho_\nu$ is energy per volume per frequency (J s m⁻³), not per wavelength. The same letter can name different quantities in different sections (the light paper's $L$ is the speed of light in §§1–2 and absorbed light energy in §9), so a unit check starts from the quantity, not the glyph.
- **Ratios and scaling.** Doubling a sphere's radius halves $D$ and multiplies the RMS displacement at fixed time by $1/\sqrt{2}$, not by $1/2$. The classical energy with resonators up to a frequency $\nu_c$ grows as $\nu_c^3$, so a tenfold widening gives a thousandfold energy.
- **Orders of magnitude.**
  - A water molecule (about 0.3 nm) against a 1 μm grain (roughly 3 000 times larger).
  - $v/c \approx 3.3\times10^{-6}$ for a 1 000 m/s bullet, $8.3\times10^{-7}$ for a 250 m/s jet, $9.9\times10^{-5}$ for the Earth's 29.8 km/s orbit, and a large fraction of $c$ for Kaufmann's electrons (value taken from the cited dataset).
  - $h\nu \approx 1.91$ eV at 650 nm, 2.34 eV at 530 nm, 4.96 eV at 250 nm.
  - The light paper's printed hydrogen-atom mass: $1/N$ gram $= 1.62\times10^{-24}$ g.
  - Molecular kicks on a micrometer grain, an order-of-magnitude estimate shown with its assumptions. An ideal-flux estimate $\tfrac14 n\bar v A$ with liquid water's number density ($3.343\times10^{28}$ m⁻³ from 1 000 kg m⁻³ and 18.015 g mol⁻¹) and a mean molecular speed near 600 m/s gives about $1.6\times10^{19}$ per second on a 1 μm-diameter sphere and about $6\times10^{19}$ for a 1 μm radius, so the text says "$10^{19}$ to $10^{20}$ per second" rather than a single figure.
- **The 1905 unit system.**
  - Mechanical and thermal: Einstein's viscosity $1.35\times10^{-2}$ poise equals $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s; $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg/(mol K) equals 8.31 J/(mol K); Planck's $\alpha$ (computational value $6.10\times10^{-57}$ erg s⁴ cm⁻³; the printed exponent is verified in the light-paper beads) is $6.10\times10^{-58}$ J s⁴ m⁻³, close to the modern $8\pi h/c^3 = 6.18\times10^{-58}$.
  - **Electromagnetic CGS (the representation the witness indicates for the light paper's §8 and §9 checks).** The correspondences are **conventional, not exact**: since the 2019 SI revision the vacuum magnetic permeability is a measured quantity, so the constant sets mark every CGS-to-SI electrical correspondence `conventional` and never `exact`. By that conventional correspondence 1 abvolt is $10^{-8}$ V and 1 abcoulomb is 10 C.
    - The printed $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ abcoulomb per gram-equivalent is $9.6\times10^{4}$ C, beside the modern Faraday constant $96\,485$ C/mol (labeled modern), which it falls 0.50 percent short of.
    - $\Pi = R\beta\nu/E$ in abvolts, times $10^{-8}$, gives volts: $4.34\times10^{8}$ abvolt is 4.34 V, printed as about 4.3 V.
    - An energy per gram-equivalent divided by $E$ is a potential: $6.38\times10^{12}$ erg per gram-equivalent corresponds to 6.65 V, while 10 V corresponds to $9.6\times10^{12}$ erg per gram-equivalent.
  - **Gaussian (electrostatic) CGS (the relativity paper),** with the same conventional status: 1 statvolt is about 300 V (299.792458 V by the conventional correspondence); 1 statvolt per cm $\approx 3.0\times10^{4}$ V/m; 1 gauss $= 10^{-4}$ T. A contemporary per-electron charge of about $4.7\times10^{-10}$ esu is $1.568\times10^{-19}$ C; it belongs to the documented alternative representation of the light paper's check (4.306–4.309 V).
  - The distinction between "per gram-equivalent" (Einstein's $R$, $E$, $J$) and "per molecule" ($R/N$, $\varepsilon$) is shown explicitly.
  - The node converts units only. It never converts a historical constant's value into a modern constant's value, and it never calls a declared editorial input (the light paper's $R$ and $L$) a printed value.

**Constructions.** A unit-cancellation table (quantities); a scaling table with a slider for a length and its area, volume, and a $\sqrt{t}$ spread (ratios); a zoomable log scale placing the listed numbers (orders of magnitude, with a table equivalent); a conversion calculator restricted to documented conversions (mechanical, electromagnetic CGS, Gaussian CGS), which never converts between historical and modern constant values and which labels every electrical correspondence conventional.

**Prerequisites** (link records with captions, each typed `{foundationId, kind}`): `foundation:bridge-scientific-notation-units` and `foundation:bridge-fractions-ratios`, both `proof-edge` prerequisites to authored slice bridges.

**Calling passages and return captions.** Captions follow the rule in `am-found-library-infra-002t`: this bead records captions for callers that already exist in the node's `returnCaptions[]`, and later callers put theirs on their own link records.
- This bead authors captions for callers that exist when it lands: Brownian §3 and §5 in the reference slice and the complete Brownian readings.
- It records these as `plannedCallers` in the registry: light §1, §2, §8, and §9; relativity §6 and §10 (Gaussian units); mass–energy (energy and $L/V^2$ units).

**Stopping points.**
- Quantities: "a unit is a chosen amount of a kind of quantity."
- Ratios: "scaling as repeated multiplication."
- Magnitudes: "powers of ten as repeated multiplication by ten."
- Units: "a conversion factor as a ratio equal to one."

## Technical Approach

- Records under `content/foundations/` with instrument ids for the constructions; constant values referenced from the constant sets of `am-ref-constants-xik` rather than retyped where the build allows; registry entries flipped to `authored` in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Four complete records with all parts and stopping points, registered under their canonical ids with this bead as owner.
- [ ] Every number matches the constant sets or evaluator fixtures; historical and modern constants are never mixed silently; the light paper's check is described in the representation the facsimile prints, with the other named a documented alternative.
- [ ] Every CGS-to-SI electrical correspondence is presented as conventional, never as exact, in prose, in the calculator, and in the tests.
- [ ] Captions exist for every existing caller (in the node's `returnCaptions[]` or on the caller's link record); planned callers are recorded in the registry; every prerequisite carries its `kind`.
- [ ] Constructions have textual equivalents and keyboard operation.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `foundQuantities.numbers.test.ts`, numeric consistency for every quoted number, compared through `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`):
  - speed ratios: $1000/c = 3.3356\times10^{-6}$, $250/c = 8.3391\times10^{-7}$, $29\,800/c = 9.9402\times10^{-5}$;
  - photon energies: $h\nu$ = 1.9074, 2.3393, and 4.9594 eV at 650, 530, and 250 nm;
  - kicks per second: $1.575\times10^{19}$ and $6.301\times10^{19}$ from $\tfrac14 n\bar v A$ with $n = 3.343\times10^{28}$ m⁻³ and $\bar v = 600$ m/s, asserted to one significant figure and reported as an estimate;
  - the $\alpha$ conversion ($6.10\times10^{-58}$ J s⁴ m⁻³; modern $6.180645\times10^{-58}$);
  - electromagnetic conversions (4.3385 V; 6.6507 V; $9.6\times10^{12}$ erg; $9.6\times10^{4}$ C against the modern Faraday constant, 0.50 percent low);
  - Gaussian conversions ($2.997925\times10^{4}$ V/m; $1.5678\times10^{-19}$ C);
  - the hydrogen-atom mass $1.6206\times10^{-24}$ g.
- `foundQuantities.calculator.test.ts`: a request to convert a historical constant value into a modern constant value is refused with an explanation; every electrical conversion row carries the `conventional` marker read from the constant set, and a fixture row marked `exact` fails.
- Compiler checks for registry entries, link-record captions, typed prerequisites, and voice lint.
- Failure evidence (the failing row, its expected and actual values, and the constant-set entry consulted) is written beside the log and retained.

### End-to-end tests
- From Brownian §5 (reference slice), open `foundation:unit-system-1905`, convert Einstein's viscosity from poise to Pa·s, and return to the exact sentence; operate the electromagnetic tab, convert $4.34\times10^{8}$ abvolt to volts, and assert the conventional-correspondence note. Open `foundation:orders-of-magnitude` at 320 px and operate the table equivalent by keyboard. Repeat one route with JavaScript disabled. The light-paper routes into these nodes are exercised by the light-paper content lanes (`am-lq-e2e-x7z0`), not here.

### Structured logging
- JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/found-quantities-magnitudes/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `foundationId`, `callingAnchor`, check name, `constantSet`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A conversion calculator never converts between historical and modern constant values; it converts units only.
- Label order-of-magnitude estimates as estimates and state their assumptions.
- Describe the light paper's 4.3 V check in the representation the facsimile prints; the calculator supports both CGS electrical systems, so either representation converts correctly.
- Do not write "exactly" for an electrical CGS correspondence; the registry marks these conventional.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, and link-record captions.
- `am-ref-constants-xik`: the historical and modern constant sets, including the conventional CGS correspondences.
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: the prerequisite bridges for scientific notation and fractions must be authored for prerequisite links to resolve.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers these nodes.
- `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`: its `foundation:quantities-units` prerequisite is a proof edge, so that cluster waits for this one.
- `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`: its chain tool links and equation readings link these nodes.
- `am-lq-readings-intro-s2-n0bq`, `am-lq-readings-s3-s4-k923`, `am-lq-readings-s5-s6-deq6`, `am-lq-readings-s7-s9-yorj`: these readings link these nodes.

title: Author the foundation on reading a German physics sentence
description:
# Author the foundation on reading a German physics sentence

**Epic:** `am-ep-foundations-z1e` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.5, §6.9 (`gloss` face), §7.5, §7.11 (traceability only)

## Background

The German text is the source face. The interlinear gloss serves three audiences at once:
- readers who want to read Einstein in his own language with support;
- German learners, for whom a three-page physics paper is a fine first text;
- readers whose first language is neither German nor English.

This node gives all three the handful of grammatical and typographic patterns that unlock the papers' sentences.

The node lands in Batch H, after every paper's gloss face and German edition exist. Its callers are therefore older than the node itself, which is the one situation where the library's convention (the calling bead authors the link and its return caption) cannot apply directly; see Calling passages below.

The obvious shape for this node is the wrong one. A reader who opens "reading a German physics sentence" and is given vocabulary has been given the gloss face again. The gloss face already exists (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`, and the per-paper gloss beads), and it works word by word. This node's job is the layer above it: taking a long German scientific sentence apart into its claim, its condition, and its qualification, before any word-by-word gloss.

## Scope

Node owned here (canonical id from `am-ep-foundations-z1e`):

| Id | Concrete entry point | What the reader can do afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `foundation:reading-german-physics-sentence` | Word order, the Konjunktiv in hypotheses, *sei*, *es gilt*, *man erhält* | Read the source face with support |

Out of scope: term annotations and glosses themselves (`am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y`, `am-edn-gloss-light-quanta-ggj1`, and the other gloss beads); translation policy; the gloss face component (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`).

## Requirements

**Patterns, each illustrated with an exact sentence from the editions** (quoted from a reviewed German edition by source-block and sentence id, never from memory or from a translation witness):
- Verb-second main clauses and verb-final subordinate clauses; how to find the finite verb and the clause-final verb group.
- Separable prefixes and long compound nouns (*Energieinhalt*, *Lichtkomplex*, *Elementarquantum*, *molekularkinetische Theorie*), read from the last element backward.
- *Es sei …* ("let … be"), *es gilt …* ("… holds"), *man erhält …* ("one obtains …") in derivations.
- The subjunctive in hypotheses and comparisons, and why the translation must keep that modality. The light paper's §6 conclusion is the key example: radiation behaves "as though" it consisted of independent energy quanta. Transcribe its exact wording and verb form (expected *so, wie wenn sie aus … bestünde*; *bestände* is the other possible Konjunktiv II form) from the reviewed edition.
- Letter-spaced emphasis in the 1905 typesetting as a signal of emphasis.
- Period spellings and abbreviations as printed (for example *daß*, *Hrn.*, *l. c.* in the light paper's footnotes citing Lenard), kept on the source face.
- Printed numbers: decimal commas and the raised multiplication dot (for example the light paper's $6{,}17\cdot10^{23}$ and "4,3 Volt"), kept on the source face and rendered with decimal points on the English face.

### Structure before vocabulary: assertion, condition, qualification

The node teaches a reader to take a long German scientific sentence apart into three roles **before** any word-by-word gloss:

1. **The main assertion.** What is being claimed.
2. **Its condition.** Under what circumstances the claim is made (*unter der Voraussetzung, daß…*, *wenn…*, *für…*, *im Falle…*).
3. **Its qualification.** How strongly it is claimed, and what the author is not claiming (*es ist möglich, daß…*, *scheint*, *dürfte*, *müssen*, *so ergibt sich*, *heuristisch*).

Why this and not vocabulary: the site's translation contract turns on exactly this distinction. A close translation **preserves modality and qualification**, and "suggests," "must," "under these assumptions," and "to this approximation" are not interchangeable. A reader who cannot see which clause carries the qualification cannot check the English face against the German, which is the one thing the bilingual edition invites them to do.

- **The worked example is a real sentence from a reviewed ledger**, chosen by this bead's author from `public/papers/transcripts/<key>-reviewed.txt`, never typed from memory and never taken from a witness translation. The strongest candidate is the Brownian introduction's statement that the information available to Einstein about the reported observations was too imprecise for him to form a judgment: it is the paper's most misread sentence, it is a qualification rather than an assertion, and misreading it produces exactly the claim that `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2` flags as `observations-studied`. Verify its exact wording and extent on the pinned facsimile and the ledger before authoring, and record the source block and sentence id the example quotes.
- **The three roles are recorded as spans over that sentence**, so the marking can be rendered and checked rather than described in prose. The spans cover the sentence without overlapping.
- **Grammatical signals get their own short section.** An assumed quantity, an observed fact and a proposed conclusion carry different signals in German scientific prose, and the node names the signals it uses with an example of each from the corpus: a subjunctive or a modal for a proposed conclusion, a stated condition clause for an assumption, a plain past or present for a reported observation. It names the signals it teaches and stops; it does not attempt German grammar.
- **It does not require German.** The capsule supports reading the source face with the English face beside it. Its readiness sign is that a reader can point at which clause carries the qualification in a sentence they have not seen, with the translation available. That is a reading skill, not a language skill, and it is stated as an explanation the reader gives, never as a test: no score, timer or correctness mark appears.

**Construction.** An interlinear excerpt from the gloss face with word-order markers and a toggle between the literal gloss and the idiomatic translation, with a textual equivalent. The three role spans are distinguished by a channel other than color.

**Calling passages and return captions.**
- The gloss faces of all four papers, and the term annotation for the subjunctive at the light paper's §6 conclusion, exist before this node does.
- This bead therefore adds the two link references itself in one change: a face-level entry link in the gloss-face configuration, and a link on the §6 subjunctive annotation. Their return captions are recorded in this node's own `returnCaptions[]` ("Back to the gloss face at the same sentence"; "Back to light quanta §6: the conclusion in the subjunctive of comparison"), so the callers' records change only by the added link.
- It records each such edit with a comment on the owning bead (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`, `am-edn-gloss-light-quanta-ggj1`), and never changes anything else in those records.
- The node also links forward to `am-read-gloss-face-lp2` as the next step for a reader who now wants the words, so the two directions are complete: the gloss face opens this node for a reader who has the words and not the shape, and this node opens the gloss face for a reader who has the shape and not the words.
- Callers created after this node lands author their own links as usual.

**Stopping point.** "A clause frame: subject, finite verb in second position, the rest of the verb at the end," and, for a long sentence, "one claim, its condition, and how strongly it is made." The node never opens a second cascade into German syntax, and it says so.

## Technical Approach

- Record under `content/foundations/`; example sentences referenced by source-block and sentence ids so edits to the edition propagate; the three role spans stored on the record as offsets into the quoted sentence; registry entry flipped to `authored` in the same change as the record and the caller links.
- The node renders on its own route in the foundation library and in the drawer, both owned by `am-found-library-infra-002t`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The record has all parts, each pattern with at least one exact sentence reference, and the stopping point, registered under its canonical id with this bead as owner.
- [ ] The record carries the three roles as named parts, a grammatical-signals section, one worked example quoting a reviewed ledger sentence by its source block and sentence id, a textual equivalent, prerequisites, and the stopping point.
- [ ] Every example resolves to a reviewed German sentence id; none is retyped.
- [ ] The worked example's quoted German is byte-identical to the ledger text at that sentence id, checked by test, and the record names the ledger file and the id rather than embedding an unsourced string.
- [ ] The example sentence's three roles are marked in the record as spans over that sentence, so the marking can be rendered and checked rather than described in prose.
- [ ] The grammatical-signals section names each signal it teaches with one corpus example, and teaches no signal it does not exemplify.
- [ ] The node states its stopping point and opens no prerequisite into German grammar; the prerequisite audit of `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` reports no dead end from it.
- [ ] The readiness sign is stated as an explanation the reader gives, never as a test, and no score, timer or correctness mark appears.
- [ ] The gloss-face entry links and the §6 annotation link exist with return captions, each cross-bead edit is recorded on the owning bead, and the node's own forward link to the gloss face exists.
- [ ] The construction has a textual equivalent and works with keyboard and screen readers (language metadata marks German spans).
- [ ] The node renders on its foundation route and in the drawer, in print, without JavaScript, at 320 px, and by keyboard, with German diacritics and `ß` rendering correctly in all three themes (the glyph coverage `am-design-themes-typography-288q` owns).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Reference checks that every example id exists and its text equals the edition; a check that the §6 example's verb form equals the reviewed edition's text.
- Language-attribute checks on German spans; voice lint for English prose.
- Compiler checks for the registry entry and the caller link records with captions.
- `foundReadingGerman.example.test.ts`:
  - the quoted German equals the reviewed ledger text at the named sentence id, byte for byte, with original spelling preserved (for example `daß`), compared as an exact string;
  - the three role spans cover the sentence without overlapping and without gaps beyond punctuation;
  - the record names a ledger file that exists and a sentence id that parses under the id grammar of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`.
- `foundReadingGerman.signals.test.ts`: every signal named in the grammatical-signals section has at least one corpus example attached, and every attached example resolves to a source block id.
- `foundReadingGerman.records.test.ts`: registry entry flipped to `authored` with this bead as owner; stopping point present; textual equivalent present; no banned abstract vocabulary; voice lint passes.
- `foundReadingGerman.glyphs.test.ts`: the rendered example's German characters are covered by the subset fonts in all three themes, reusing the glyph coverage assertions of `am-design-themes-typography-288q` rather than a second check.

### End-to-end tests

In `e2e/foundations/reading-german.spec.ts`, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:

1. From the mass–energy gloss face, open the node, toggle literal and idiomatic readings by keyboard, and return to the exact sentence.
2. From the light paper's §6 conclusion annotation, open the node and return.
3. From the Brownian German face at the introduction, open the node in the drawer, read the three roles marked over the example sentence, and return to the exact sentence through the return stack.
4. Follow the node's forward link to the gloss face, then follow the gloss face's entry link back to this node.
5. Assert the three roles are visibly distinguished by a channel other than color, under forced-colors emulation and in monochrome print.
6. Verify screen-reader language switching on German examples.
7. Repeat keyboard only, at 320 px, at 200 percent zoom, and with JavaScript disabled using the node's standalone route (real links).

Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot and console log under `artifacts/test-logs/foundations/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
- Bead-specific fields: `foundationId` (`foundation:reading-german-physics-sentence`), `ledgerFile`, `sentenceId`, `roleSpans`, `signalCount`, `signalsWithExamples`, `callingAnchor`, `returnCaptionSource`, example sentence ids, `rule`.
- Standard fields: `timestamp`, `suite` (`foundations`), `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-found-reading-german-u8oc`), `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `durationMs`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind` (`bitwise` for the ledger comparison), `outcome`, `message`.
- Path: `artifacts/test-logs/foundations/<log-run-id>.jsonl`; failure evidence retained.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Keep grammar explanations minimal and tied to real sentences; this is not a German course and must never grow into one. The reader has the English face open; the skill is seeing the shape of the claim, and the stopping point is written to stop exactly that growth.
- Preserve printed spellings, abbreviations, and number formats on the source face even when modern usage differs.
- The cross-bead link edits are the only exception to caller-owned links and must stay limited to adding link records.
- Choose the example from the ledger, not from a translation. A sentence taken from a witness translation and rendered back into German would be a fabricated source, which is the one thing the source layers exist to prevent.
- The Brownian introduction candidate is valuable because misreading it produces a documented anachronism the lint already flags. If the pinned facsimile's wording turns out to be less clear than expected, pick another sentence and record why.
- Do not mark the roles with color alone. A reader who cannot distinguish the three spans learns nothing, and the semantic-color rule applies here as everywhere.
- *müssen* in a physics paper is often logical necessity within a model, not a claim about the world. The qualification section should say so, because that is the exact modality the translation contract protects.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: rendering, the registry, the route and drawer, and link-record captions.
- `am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`: German spans, alignment, and gloss rendering used by the examples.
- `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`: the gloss face whose configuration receives the entry link and whose route the end-to-end test starts from.

Unblocks:
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the audit covers this node.
- `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`: the Batch H exit evidence includes the foundation library's completion.
