title: asupersync wasm-browser-prod omits runtime-core, so no consumer can build it standalone
description:
## Background

Found while fixing the feature-unification defect in `am-fs-asupersync-unification-n8hi`. That bead's consumer-side change works around this; it does not close it.

`asupersync`'s wasm browser profile is not self-sufficient. A consumer that asks only for `wasm-browser-prod` under `default-features = false` cannot compile the library.

## The defect

`~/projects/asupersync/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
runtime-core            = ["dep:serde"]
desktop-runtime-profile = ["runtime-core", "native-runtime"]
wasm-browser-prod       = ["wasm-runtime", "browser-io"]
wasm-browser-dev        = ["wasm-runtime", "browser-io"]
wasm-browser-minimal    = ["wasm-runtime"]
```

`dep:serde` is enabled only by `runtime-core`. The desktop profile includes it; every `wasm-browser-*` profile omits it. But 247 non-test source files use serde, and the core ones are ungated:

```
src/evidence.rs:34   use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
src/monitor.rs:42    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
```

The only nearby cfg found in the sample guards on `feature = "tls"` (src/remote.rs), unrelated to runtime-core.

## Observed failure

Setting `default-features = false, features = ["wasm-browser-prod"]` on fs-exec and fs-fft produced **716 errors**, all `unresolved import serde` / `cannot find module or crate serde`, inside asupersync itself. Exit 101 after 124354ms of remote compilation. The native-runtime feature defect was genuinely cleared at the same time (cargo tree went from 1 native-runtime occurrence to 0), so this is a distinct, second defect and not a recurrence.

## Evidence limits, stated plainly

- 4 of the 247 non-test files were read directly. The rest were counted, not inspected.
- An earlier figure of mine, '424 files mention serde, 0 carry a runtime-core guard', is RETRACTED: the conformance and e2e modules are gated at their `pub mod` declaration in lib.rs (`#[cfg(all(test, feature = "legacy-internal-test-harnesses"))]`), which an inside-the-file grep cannot see. Do not cite 424/0.

## Candidate fix

Add `runtime-core` to `wasm-browser-prod`, and probably to `wasm-browser-dev`, `wasm-browser-deterministic` and `wasm-browser-minimal`. Then every consumer works unmodified and none needs to hand-add features.

Verify that this does NOT pull `native-runtime` transitively, since that is forbidden on wasm32 at `src/lib.rs:129` and is the defect the sibling bead exists to fix.

## Untested prediction

Six sibling crates declare bare `features = ["wasm-browser-prod"]` with `default-features = false`: `fs-goddard-wasm`, `fs-flyer-wasm`, `fs-cmaes-viz-wasm`, `fs-crump-wasm`, `fs-edison-wasm`, and `fs-wasm` itself. If this analysis is right, all six are latently broken the same way. Each is its own workspace with its own lock, two untouched since August, so none may have been built recently. **This was not tested** — a build would have contended with the verification run in flight.

Note that `fs-wasm`'s own declaration remains incomplete even after the sibling bead's fix: it compiles only because fs-exec and fs-fft now supply `runtime-core` to a graph whose root never requested it. That is fragile and is the strongest argument for fixing this upstream instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A crate depending on asupersync with `default-features = false, features = ["wasm-browser-prod"]` and nothing else compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- [ ] `cargo tree -e features --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` shows `native-runtime` absent, so the fix does not reintroduce the forbidden feature.
- [ ] The six sibling wasm crates are actually built, and the prediction above is confirmed or refuted in writing.
- [ ] Native builds of asupersync consumers are unaffected.
- [ ] A failing command is never retried to manufacture a green run.

title: Audit FrankenSim capabilities with a build probe and write docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md
description:
# Audit FrankenSim capabilities with a build probe and write docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md

**Epic:** `am-ep-frankensim-9kg` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Labels:** frankensim, upstream-frankensim · **Plan sections:** §2.2, §12.2, §12.3, §12.4, §12.9, §12.10 (traceability only)

## Background

The plan's first physics task is a bounded audit and build probe, because crate names mislead. `fs-frame`, `fs-flux`, `fs-lattice`, and `fs-spectral` do not establish spacetime frames, moving-conductor electromagnetism, Brownian dynamics, or Planck spectra; the planning audit already found that `fs-lattice` is infill optimization and `fs-flux` is Navier–Stokes. Reusing a crate on the strength of its name would ship wrong physics under a FrankenSim label. Creating a new crate merely because a suitable owner has a less obvious name would fragment the numerical ecosystem. The audit decides which owner computes each law and settles the design gaps in the plan before any export is written.

A quick name search during planning (frankensim `5bbbfae6f7de614422f6f97f5798a3e00f8ad813`, 2026-09-13) found no crate implementing Brownian motion, Stokes–Einstein, Planck spectra, photoelectric laws, or Lorentz boosts. Hits were incidental (for example `fs-render` mentions Planck in a rendering context, `fs-rand` has gamma sampling in `dist.rs` rather than chi-square quantiles, and several crates mention "boost" or "mobility" in unrelated senses). Absence in a search is not proof of absence; this bead inspects semantics.

Several downstream contracts depend on exact facts this audit records: the TypeScript Philox port must reproduce `fs-rand` bit for bit; the runtime's stream allocation must use the same registry kernel ids the exports use; the protocol maps upstream refusal codes onto a shared registry; and whether a cross-engine comparison can honestly be bitwise depends on the arithmetic each export performs.

The kernel id table is also the site's only defence against two logical streams quietly sharing one identity. Every consumer that draws scientific randomness reads an id from this table, so a consumer that arrives without an allocated id has only two options, both bad: borrow another stream's id, or invent one. Decision (c) therefore allocates an id for every consumer the graph already knows about, including consumers outside the instrument set.

The audit also has to answer a question the upstream map alone cannot: which instrument in this repository needs each capability, and how far that capability has actually been accepted here. AGENTS.md fixes the rule ("Add a capability only when a named instrument uses it; the site never waits for unrelated FrankenSim crates to compile for the browser"), and requirement 7 makes it enforceable.

## Scope

In scope: pinning the FrankenSim revision, toolchain, and sibling revisions; verifying the planning findings with file and line evidence; mapping each §12.3 capability family to existing owners or gaps; the capability matrix indexed by consuming instrument; a native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build probe; the decisions (a) through (i) below, including the complete kernel id table with its production and test-fixture blocks; writing `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`.

Out of scope: implementing exports (`am-fs-export-brownian-frames-nhm`, `am-fs-export-philox-normals-xnv`, `am-fs-export-diffusion1d-cew`), building the shipped artifact (`am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`), implementing upstream owners (`am-fs-diffusion-owner-sey` and the `fs-owner-*` beads), the exercise checker that consumes the exercise stream id (`am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`), and the runtime's allocation registry (`am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`, which mirrors this bead's kernel id table and carries the tile formulas). This bead changes no FrankenSim code and writes nothing into `~/projects/frankensim` or its sibling repositories, including build outputs.

## Requirements

1. **Pin.** Record the FrankenSim revision (from `am-gov-donor-audit-0wa`), `rust-toolchain.toml` (`nightly-2026-07-06`, rustc 1.99.0-nightly, at the planning audit), and the sibling revisions the browser build reaches: `fs-wasm`'s `wasm32` dependencies include `wasm-bindgen = "0.2"`, `getrandom = "0.4"` with `wasm_js`, and a path dependency on the sibling `asupersync` repository with `wasm-browser-prod`; `fs-sparse` has optional (off by default) path dependencies on `franken_networkx` and `franken_numpy`.
2. **Verify each finding at the pinned revision, with file and line evidence:**
   - `fs-wasm` depends on `fs-rand` and `fs-sparse` and, unconditionally, on the upper-stack and campaign crates; it is its own nested workspace with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`, `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, no `[features]` table, and no `crates/fs-wasm/tests/` directory.
   - `fs-rand` depends only on `fs-math`; `fs-math` has no dependencies; `fs-sparse`'s constellation dependencies are optional.
   - `heat_frames(n, frames, steps_per_frame)` clamps inputs (`n` to 3–96, frames to 1–240, steps per frame to 1–40), hard-codes two Gaussian blobs, and steps `u -= dt * A u` with a dimensionless `dt = 0.20` on `laplacian_5pt`, which assembles the SPD operator ($4$ on the diagonal, $-1$ off it, that is $-\Delta$ up to the $1/h^2$ scale). It takes no diffusion coefficient, spacing, or profile and is not an honest owner for any diffusion instrument.
   - `fs-rand`: `StreamKey { seed: u64, kernel: u32, tile: u32 }`; counter words `[index_low, index_high, tile, kernel]` and key words `[seed_low, seed_high]`; the Philox round `[hi1 ^ c1 ^ k0, lo1, hi0 ^ c3 ^ k1, lo0]` with `(hi0, lo0) = mulhilo(0xD2511F53, c0)` and `(hi1, lo1) = mulhilo(0xCD9E8D57, c2)`, ten rounds, key incremented by `0x9E3779B9` and `0xBB67AE85` before every round after the first; the three Random123 known-answer vectors in `philox.rs`; `STREAM_SEMANTICS_VERSION = 1`; `STREAM_CHECKPOINT_VERSION = 1`; `next_u64 = (block[1] << 32) | block[0]` with `wrapping_add` on the index; `next_f64 = (next_u64 >> 11) as f64 * 2^-53`; `next_normal` is `u = 1 - next_f64(); v = next_f64(); det::sqrt(-2 ln u) * det::cos(2π v)` on `fs_math::det` strict functions and consumes exactly two draws; `next_below` uses Lemire's method with deterministic rejection consumption; `fill_f64` is bitwise identical to sequential `next_f64`; the ziggurat normal is a fast path not admitted to strict mode; a stream is positioned at an index with `Stream::resume(StreamCheckpoint::current(key, index))`; the canonical checkpoint frame is 83 little-endian bytes (magic `FSRCKPT\0`, the 43-byte domain `org.frankensim.fs-rand.stream-checkpoint.v1`, checkpoint version, stream-semantics version, seed, kernel, tile, next index).
   - `fs-sparse`: `Coo::new`, `Coo::push`, `Coo::assemble` (stable sort by row and column, duplicates accumulated in insertion order) to `Csr`, and `Csr::spmv`, which accumulates each row in ascending column order with fused multiply-add.
   - `fs-math`: `det::sqrt` is the hardware square root (correctly rounded); `det::ln` and `det::cos` are strict deterministic implementations.
   - `fs-qty`: `Dims([i8; 6])` over `[m, kg, s, K, A, mol]`.
   - `fs-demo-physics-wasm`: typed envelopes `{"ok": {...}}` and `{"refusal": {"code", "message", "ranked_repairs"}}`, a `KERNEL_VERSION` constant baked into envelopes, and a `CONTRACT.md` with no-claim boundaries (the `fs-flyer-wasm` pattern).
   - `fs-evidence`: `Evidence<T>` with numerical, statistical, model-evidence, and sensitivity slices. `fs-blake3`: `hash_bytes` and a domain-separated hasher.
   - `fs-lattice` and `fs-flux` semantics as stated above.
3. **Map every §12.3 family** (radiation spectra; idealized quantum energy transfer; diffusion and stochastic transport; diffusion inference; flat-spacetime kinematics; relativistic electrodynamics; prescribed-field particle dynamics; relativistic energy accounting; evidence and uncertainty) to: candidate crates and exact functions, their `CONTRACT.md` determinism class (`Deterministic`, `DeterministicPerIsa`, or `Fast` per `docs/DETERMINISM_CLASSES.md`), existing tests, whether they compile to `wasm32`, gaps, and a proposed owner decision.
4. **Build probe.** In an ignored build root in this repository (`artifacts/wasm-build/probe-<revision>/<tool-run-id>/`, a new directory for every probe execution, never reused or cleared), populated with `git archive` exports of the pinned FrankenSim and sibling revisions that preserve their relative layout, run and log: a native `cargo test` of the audited slice; `cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for `fs-wasm`; `wasm-pack build --dev --target web -- --locked` (the command FrankenSim's `docs/CI_GATES.md` uses); `cargo tree` for `fs-wasm`; and, in the scratch copy only, a probe capability crate depending on `fs-rand`, `fs-sparse`, and `fs-math` to measure its graph and `.wasm` size. Record the exports actually present and the sizes beside the donor museum's 4.9 MB full package. `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and every output path stay inside the build root. The `<tool-run-id>` uses the logging standard's timestamp-plus-hex format and carries the same value as the probe's JSONL `logRunId`, so every record points at its artifacts.
5. **Resolve and record these decisions before implementation:**
   - (a) **Kernel scaling for `brownian_frames`.** Document every step kernel's per-step distribution, variance, draw consumption, and exact arithmetic. Recommended physical scaling with per-step variance $2D\,dt$: coin, one draw, step $+s$ when the top bit of `next_u64` is 1 and $-s$ otherwise, with $s$ computed as `(2.0 * diffusion * dt).sqrt()`; uniform, one draw, step `(2.0 * next_f64() - 1.0) * h` with $h$ = `(6.0 * diffusion * dt).sqrt()` (support $[-h, h)$, variance $h^2/3 = 2D\,dt$); Gaussian, two draws, step `next_normal() * s`; positions accumulate `x = x + step` from 0.0. Under physical scaling the plan's kernel 2 ("Gaussian") and kernel 3 ("Gaussian with the exact D") coincide in distribution, so the record must state what distinguishes them; two ids with silently identical meaning are not allowed. The two admissible resolutions:
     - kernel 2 gets a distinct documented meaning, for example a dimensionless unit-variance Gaussian for a step-unit teaching mode, which the export refuses to label physical; or
     - id 2 is a documented alias of id 3 with an explicit stream-semantics decision: whether ids 2 and 3 produce bitwise-identical trajectories for the same seed and arguments, whether the alias is part of the golden and stream-semantics surface (so removing it later is a versioned change), and how tapes, scenarios, and manifests record which id a run used.

     If kernels 0–2 stay dimensionless teaching walks instead, say so and make the export refuse to label them physical. `am-fs-export-brownian-frames-nhm`, `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`, `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, and `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl` follow the recorded resolution exactly. Whatever the resolution, the record gives every step kernel's position unit (metres for physically scaled kernels, step units for a dimensionless kernel) and the canonical quantity id its output binds. A dimensionless output binds a dimensionless id from `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7` (requested there if none exists), never the length id `positionCoordinate1d`, so the protocol decoder's unit check can never accept step units as metres.
   - (b) **Refusal channel.** A bare `Vec<f64>` cannot carry a code. Choose one pattern for all fallible exports: an admission function returning the typed envelope paired with a data function that refuses inadmissible input, or a `Result` whose error maps to a typed JavaScript refusal object. Record a mapping table from every upstream code to a registered code in `src/experiments/results/refusalCodes.ts` (for example `ftcs-unstable` for the FTCS diffusion-number limit, `unsupported-kernel`, `nonfinite-input`, `invalid-parameter`, `stream-index-overflow`) or, for output and step budgets, to the execution outcome `budget-exhausted`. Every target code must exist in `src/experiments/results/refusalCodes.ts`: `am-rt-typed-results-mqb` registers `invalid-parameter` and `stream-index-overflow` beside its other initial codes, and any further target code this table introduces is registered, with its reader text, by `am-rt-worker-protocol-gaq` in the change that implements the table. The runtime protocol's refusal mapping implements exactly this table.
   - (c) **Stream keys and kernel ids.** Map "(seed, particle index)" to `StreamKey { seed, kernel: <registered id>, tile: <allocation-defined tile> }` with the draw index counting draws. Record a kernel id table for every Annus Mirabilis logical stream, with values checked against existing FrankenSim kernel id usage so none collide. The table has two blocks, and the boundary between them is part of the decision:
     - **Production ids**, at least: the Brownian latent stream used by BM-01's three-axis allocation and BM-05's walk; the Brownian localization-noise stream; the synthetic inference latent and noise streams; the LQ-05 configuration stream; and the **exercise stream**, described below.
     - **A reserved block of test-fixture ids** for the runtime fixture experiments and the seeded suites of the statistical test policy, which production allocations never use.

     **The exercise stream.** `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2` draws per-exercise Philox sample points: beside its frozen Halton grid, each exercise part draws 8 further points whose `StreamKey` seed is the first 64 bits of the SHA-256 of `<exerciseId>/<partIndex>`, encoded as a canonical decimal string. Those draws are scientific in the sense that matters here: they decide whether a reader's answer is judged equivalent, and they must be reproducible from the exercise id alone. That checker states that it "uses the registered id and never invents one", and before this decision no bead allocated one, so the table allocates it now:
     - **Name.** The exercise sample-point stream, a **production** id outside the reserved test-fixture block. It is a production allocation even though its purpose is checking a reader's answer, because it runs in the shipped site; the checker's own `property.test.ts` generator is the thing that uses a reserved test-fixture id, and the two must not be confused.
     - **Why it cannot borrow.** Its draw pattern matches no existing allocation. The Brownian latent stream is keyed by particle and axis, the localization-noise stream by particle, and the inference generator streams by particle and substep; the exercise stream is keyed by the variables of an algebraic expression and is drawn at build-independent points that have nothing to do with a physical path. Borrowing any of those ids would interleave two meanings on one stream while every digest still compared equal, which is the failure `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` requirement 6 exists to prevent.
     - **Tile formula.** `tile = v`, the zero-based index of the variable in the part's declared variable order, so each variable of a part draws on its own stream; `index` counts draws, so candidate $j$ takes index $j$ under the checker's 64-candidate ceiling. The seed already distinguishes the exercise and the part, so the tile distinguishes the variable and nothing else. `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` mirrors this formula and registers the allocation with its declared maxima.
     - **Numeric value.** Assigned when the table is written, from the production block, checked against existing FrankenSim kernel id usage so it collides with none, and recorded in the same fenced block as the rest of the table.

     The plan's `philox_normals(seed, index, count)` is ambiguous; the recommended explicit form is `(seed, stream_kernel, tile, start_index, count)` with `start_index` counting draws. `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` copies this table exactly.
   - (d) **Distribution path.** Scientific exports use strict `next_normal`; the ziggurat fast path is excluded until upstream admits it to strict mode.
   - (e) **Determinism class** for each new export, with the evidence FrankenSim requires (G5 lanes); do not claim cross-ISA bitwise identity without it.
   - (f) **Slim-bundle mechanism.** Either add default-off cargo features to `fs-wasm` that gate module groups and make heavy dependencies optional, or create a small capability crate (for example a diffusion WASM crate depending only on `fs-rand`, `fs-sparse`, and `fs-math`) following FrankenSim's per-application browser crates. Record the evidence: every `fs-wasm` dependency is unconditional; the capability crate needs no `asupersync`, `getrandom`, or upper-stack crate; measured graphs and sizes. AGENTS.md sketches the exports as feature-gated additions to `crates/fs-wasm/src/lib.rs` with tests in `crates/fs-wasm/tests/`; if the evidence favors a capability crate, record the departure and raise it with the user before the export beads start. The user decides: this bead stays open until the user's answer is recorded with `br comments add am-fs-capability-audit-byc`, quoting the user and giving the date, and no agent records that answer on the user's behalf.
   - (g) **Targets.** One native test target and one single-threaded browser target for the Brownian slice; threads, shared memory, and SIMD specialization deferred.
   - (h) **Reproducible build method.** Record how the shipped bundle is built so bytes are identical across machines and directories: sources from `git archive` of pinned revisions; `--locked` with the crate's lockfile; `RUSTFLAGS` with `--remap-path-prefix` for the build root and the Cargo registry path so no absolute paths enter panic strings; a pinned `wasm-pack` version with a `wasm-bindgen` CLI matching the lockfile; `wasm-opt` either disabled or pinned to a recorded binaryen version; any `RUSTFLAGS` required by `getrandom`'s backend if it is in the graph. The probe records whether two builds in different directories match.
   - (i) **Naming.** The step kernel parameter of `brownian_frames` is named `step_kernel`, and registry ids are "stream kernel ids", so the plan's overloaded `kernel` never appears ambiguously in Rust, TypeScript, or documentation.
6. **Write `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`** with: pinned revisions and toolchain; the verified findings; the capability map; the capability matrix of requirement 7; existing and planned export signatures with semantics and buffer layouts; decisions (a) through (i) with the kernel resolution, the kernel id table, and the refusal mapping table in machine-readable fenced blocks; build commands, exit codes, durations, and measured sizes; gaps and proposed upstream work (each to be proposed in FrankenSim's own tracker under its conventions).
7. **The capability matrix, indexed by consuming instrument.** Requirement 3 maps each §12.3 family to candidate crates, exact functions, determinism class, existing tests, `wasm32` status, gaps and a proposed owner decision. That is a map of the **upstream**. It does not say which instrument in this repository needs each capability, or whether the capability has been accepted here, so nothing else in the graph enforces AGENTS.md's rule that a capability is added only when a named instrument uses it.

   `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md` therefore carries a machine-readable capability matrix, one row per **(capability, consuming instrument)** pair, in a fenced `capability-matrix` block parsed by the same parser that reads the kernel resolution block, the kernel id table and the refusal mapping table:

   | Column | Meaning |
   |---|---|
   | `capabilityId` | Stable id of the capability, for example `diffusion.free-gaussian`, `radiation.spectral-density`, `relativity.boost` |
   | `family` | One of the nine §12.3 families |
   | `instrumentId` | The instrument that needs it, as its owner registers it with `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: one of the 33 core catalogue ids (`lq-01`…`lq-09`, `bm-01`…`bm-08`, `sr-01`…`sr-13`, `me-01`…`me-03`), a registered composite laboratory id such as `avogadro-lab`, or a declared mode address such as `bm-04:kicks-off`. A capability with no consuming instrument is recorded with `instrumentId: none` and an explicit reason |
   | `upstreamStatus` | `present` (owner and exact function named), `new-upstream` (to be implemented in FrankenSim), or `host-only` (an audited TypeScript reference evaluator is the only admitted owner, with the reason) |
   | `owner` | Crate and function, or the reference-evaluator module and function |
   | `nativeTestTarget` | The upstream test target that exercises it, or `none` with a reason |
   | `browserExport` | The exported symbol in the shipped artifact, or `not-exported` |
   | `admittedDomain` | The domain the owner admits, in canonical SI, as its `CONTRACT.md` states it |
   | `sourceReference` | The paper section, equation id, or model reference the law comes from |
   | `releaseArtifact` | The slim-artifact bundle that carries it, or `none` |
   | `acceptanceState` | `not-started`, `owner-decided`, `implemented`, `exported`, `verified`, or `adopted`. A row reaches `verified` only when a scenario in `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3` names that owner and passes; it reaches `adopted` only when an accepted snapshot in this repository carried that owner in its provenance |

   Rules the parser and its test enforce:

   1. **A crate with a related name is not a completed row.** A row whose `upstreamStatus` is `present` must name an exact function, not only a crate, or the parse fails.
   2. **No orphan capabilities.** A row with `instrumentId: none` is permitted, but the matrix's summary counts them and the binding document states each one's reason. A row whose `instrumentId` names no registered id fails the parse, so a capability cannot be justified by an instrument that does not exist. The core catalogue is closed at 33 rows and its exhaustiveness test owns that fact; a laboratory id outside it is accepted only when the experiment registry registers it.
   3. **No unowned consumers.** Every instrument that this audit's owner map says needs a computed output appears in at least one row, so a planned instrument cannot silently arrive without a named owner.
   4. **Acceptance is evidence, not intent.** `verified` and `adopted` may be written only with an accompanying `evidence` field naming the scenario id or the `logRunId` that established it. A row that claims `verified` without an `evidence` field fails the parse.
   5. **The matrix is the shipping gate's input.** `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` reads this document already for its pinned revisions and decisions (f) and (h); it builds only bundles whose rows list a `releaseArtifact`, and a capability at `acceptanceState: not-started` never enters a shipped bundle.

   The matrix rows for the three first exports are written by this bead with their expected acceptance states (`owner-decided` at the time the binding document is written), so `am-fs-export-brownian-frames-nhm`, `am-fs-export-philox-normals-xnv` and `am-fs-export-diffusion1d-cew` each advance exactly one row and nothing else.

## Technical Approach

Read-only inspection of `~/projects/frankensim` at the pinned revision through `git -C ~/projects/frankensim show <rev>:<path>` and `git archive`: `CONTRACT.md` files, `src/lib.rs` public items, `tests/`, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/DETERMINISM_CLASSES.md`, `docs/GOLDEN_POLICY.md`, `docs/CI_GATES.md`. Search by mathematical function (for example `erf`, quantile, `spmv`, "Stokes", "Wien", "boost"), then open the code to confirm semantics. Raw probe outputs and command transcripts go to `artifacts/frankensim-probe/<tool-run-id>/` (ignored by git, one directory per probe execution) and are summarized in the binding document. If a local build is slow, offload it through the project's remote build tooling rather than skipping the probe.

The kernel id table is written as one fenced block with a `block` column naming `production` or `test-fixture`, so the production and reserved ranges are machine-checkable rather than a matter of reading the surrounding prose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md` exists with every section in requirement 6.
- [ ] Every finding in requirement 2 is confirmed or corrected with file and line evidence at the pinned revision.
- [ ] Every §12.3 family has a recorded owner decision or an explicit gap.
- [ ] Native and `wasm32` probe commands, exit codes, durations, dependency graphs, and artifact sizes are recorded, including the probe capability crate.
- [ ] Decisions (a) through (i) are recorded with reasons, including the kernel 2 versus kernel 3 resolution (with its stream-semantics decision if id 2 is an alias), the kernel id table, the refusal mapping table, and the reproducible build method; any departure from the AGENTS.md sketch is flagged for the user, and the user's recorded answer is quoted in a bead comment before this bead closes.
- [ ] Decision (c)'s table allocates an exercise sample-point stream kernel id in the production block, outside the reserved test-fixture block, with its tile formula `tile = v` (the variable index within the part) and its draw-counting index, so `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2` reads a registered id instead of inventing one; the value collides with no existing FrankenSim kernel id and with no other row.

- [ ] Every instrument the owner map says needs a computed output appears in at least one row.
- [ ] A row with `upstreamStatus: present` and no exact function name fails the parse; a row claiming `verified` or `adopted` without an `evidence` field fails the parse.
- [ ] Rows with `instrumentId: none` are counted in the document's summary and each carries a stated reason.

- [ ] The three export beads can be implemented without further design questions.
- [ ] Probe JSONL records use the logging standard's path and `logRunId` field, and every failing probe command has its transcript, exit code, and environment retained under `artifacts/frankensim-probe/<tool-run-id>/` and referenced from its record.
- [ ] No file inside `~/projects/frankensim` or its sibling repositories was created or modified by this bead.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/verify-frankensim-binding.test.ts` (Bun; runnable with `bun test scripts/verify-frankensim-binding.test.ts` before the quality gates exist and picked up by `bun run test` afterward): the binding document exists, contains the required headings, pins a 40-character FrankenSim revision identical to `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md`, lists signatures for the three first exports and decisions (a) through (i), and its kernel resolution block, kernel id table, and refusal mapping table parse (the same parser `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` and the protocol reuse). A kernel resolution block that declares ids 2 and 3 with identical meaning and no alias decision fails. So do a kernel entry without a position unit and quantity id, a kernel id table whose test-fixture block overlaps a production id, and a refusal mapping row with an empty target or with an execution outcome other than `budget-exhausted`.
- The same file covers the kernel id table's consumer coverage: the exercise sample-point row exists, sits in the `production` block, carries the tile formula `tile = v` and a draw-counting index, and its numeric id appears in no other row and in no recorded FrankenSim kernel id usage; a fixture table placing that row in the `test-fixture` block fails naming the block, since the checker ships in the site; a fixture table omitting the row while a consumer names an exercise stream fails with the consumer named; and a fixture in which the exercise row reuses the Brownian latent id fails with both row names, which is the borrowing case `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` rejects at registration.
- The same file covers the capability matrix: the `capability-matrix` block parses and its column set matches requirement 7 exactly, a missing column failing with its name; a row whose `instrumentId` is not a registered id and is not `none` fails, naming the id; a row with `upstreamStatus: present` whose `owner` names only a crate fails; a row at `acceptanceState: verified` without `evidence` fails while the same row with a scenario id passes; a fixture owner map listing an instrument that appears in no row fails with the instrument id named; the three first-export rows exist with the expected acceptance states; and a round trip re-serialises the parsed matrix to the same block, so the document is the single source and no second copy is kept in code.

### End-to-end tests
- The build probe is the integration check; its commands are rerun unchanged by `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` as a regression lane.
- A tree check records `git -C ~/projects/frankensim status --porcelain` before and after the probe and lists any difference in the report. FrankenSim's tree is busy, so the probe's no-write guarantee is proven structurally rather than inferred from that listing: every logged command's working directory, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, and output paths resolve inside the build root, and the check fails if any resolves inside `~/projects/frankensim` or a sibling repository. A difference caused by another agent's concurrent edits is reported, never mistaken for a probe write or hidden.
- A failing command fails the probe with its exit code, duration, and transcript path in the JSONL record and the transcript kept on disk; a failed command is never retried to get a green run.

### Structured logging
Probe JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/frankensim-probe/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, following the field names and `logRunId` format of the logging standard (`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`; the probe may run before that library exists, so the probe script writes records in the documented schema and the logger's schema test validates them once it lands): `timestamp`, `suite` (`frankensim-probe`), `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-fs-capability-audit-byc`), `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and in `extra`: `command`, `workingDirectory`, `frankensimRevision`, `siblingRevisions`, `toolchain`, `target`, `exitCode`, `artifactPath`, `artifactBytes`, `dependencyCount`, `upstreamTreeUnchanged`, `transcriptPath` (the raw output under `artifacts/frankensim-probe/<tool-run-id>/`), `capabilityId`, `family`, `instrumentId`, `upstreamStatus`, `acceptanceState`, `browserExport`, `releaseArtifact`, `streamKernelId`, `streamKernelBlock`, `orphanCapabilityCount`, and `unownedConsumerCount`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- `fs-wasm`'s house style clamps inputs (`n_in.clamp(3, 96)`); new scientific exports must refuse instead of clamping. Record this explicitly so implementers do not copy the pattern.
- The browser build of `fs-wasm` reaches the sibling `asupersync` repository; a fresh machine needs that prerequisite and its revision pinned.
- Heavy upper-stack dependencies in `fs-wasm` are why the full package is large; the slim decision must remove them from the shipped graph.
- Absolute build paths embedded in panic messages change artifact digests between machines; remap them.
- Never substitute assumptions for probe evidence, and never "fix" upstream while auditing it; proposals go to FrankenSim's tracker.
- An alias that is not part of the stream-semantics surface can be removed without a version bump and silently break every tape that used it.
- A consumer that draws randomness and has no allocated id will borrow or invent one, and both failures are silent. The table is the place to notice a missing consumer, which is why it lists streams that belong to no instrument, such as the exercise stream.
- "Test" is not the same as "test-fixture block". The exercise checker runs in the shipped site and judges a reader's answer, so its stream is a production allocation; only the checker's own property-test generator uses a reserved id. Putting the exercise stream in the reserved block would let a production draw collide with a fixture suite.
- The matrix is an inventory of obligations, not a roadmap. A row at `not-started` with a named instrument is honest; a row that claims `verified` because a crate compiles is not.
- Keep one row per (capability, instrument) pair rather than one row per capability with a list of instruments. A shared capability that fails for one instrument's domain must be visible as one failing row, not hidden inside a list.
- Resist widening `admittedDomain` to cover a second instrument. Two instruments with different admitted domains are two rows, and the narrower one is what that instrument may claim.
- `adopted` is the only state that proves the browser path works end to end, because it requires an accepted snapshot in this repository to have carried the owner. Do not treat `exported` as adoption.

The build probe is a genuine negative result, not a failure to report: 15 of 17 commands failed, and the failures are the finding. rch refused local fallback under critical pressure, the kitchen-sink wasm32 build dies on an asupersync feature conflict (fs-cheb, fs-fft, fs-geom, fs-rep-mesh and fs-render pull asupersync with default features including native-runtime, which asupersync forbids on wasm32 at src/lib.rs:129, while fs-wasm requests wasm-browser-prod at Cargo.toml:104), and the audited native slice cannot build from the root workspace because unrelated member fs-flywheel-e2e reaches frankensqlite.

title: fs-couple: ModalAcousticTimeModel missing held_force_for_port_velocity method blocks fs-wasm wasm32 build
description:
## Background

Found while verifying am-fs-asupersync-unification-n8hi. That bead's fix (target-scoped
asupersync deps in fs-exec/fs-fft) is confirmed working: a real remote build of
`cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` from `crates/fs-wasm` now compiles
asupersync v0.5.0, fs-exec, and fs-fft cleanly with ZERO native-runtime/serde errors.
The build proceeds past all of those and fails later, in a completely different,
previously undiscovered crate: fs-couple.

## Evidence

Real remote build (rch exec, worker-verified, not a local run), exit 101 after 162769ms:

```
error[E0599]: no method named `held_force_for_port_velocity` found for struct `ModalAcousticTimeModel` in the current scope
   --> crates/fs-couple/src/bowed_string.rs:410:30
    |
409 |                         model
    |                             .held_force_for_port_velocity(
    |                             -^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ method not found in `ModalAcousticTimeModel`
    |
   ::: crates/fs-couple/src/modal_acoustic_time.rs:214:1
    |
214 |   pub struct ModalAcousticTimeModel {
    |   --------------------------------- method `held_force_for_port_velocity` not found for this struct
error: could not compile `fs-couple` (lib) due to 1 previous error
```

Checked directly: `grep -rn held_force_for_port_velocity crates/fs-couple/src/` finds only the
one call site at bowed_string.rs:410. `modal_acoustic_time.rs`'s `impl ModalAcousticTimeModel`
block (line 283 onward) has no method by this or a similarly-named signature — only
`try_new`, `modes`, `states`, `restore_states`, `initialize_static_equilibrium`,
`observer_pressure_with_transfers`, `observer_pressure_with_transfers_about_static_equilibrium`,
`step`, `step_duration`. The call site is unconditional Rust (no `#[cfg(...)]` guard on the
module in `lib.rs:38` or nearby in `bowed_string.rs`), so this is not wasm32-specific: it
should fail an equivalent native build of fs-couple identically.

fs-couple is a DIRECT dependency of fs-wasm (`crates/fs-wasm/Cargo.toml`, Tier IV section),
so this alone blocks every wasm32 build of fs-wasm regardless of the asupersync fix, and
therefore blocks the same three downstream export beads that am-fs-asupersync-unification-n8hi
was blocking (am-fs-export-brownian-frames-nhm, am-fs-export-diffusion1d-cew,
am-fs-export-philox-normals-xnv).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified: was this method renamed/removed, or never implemented? (git log/blame
      on bowed_string.rs and modal_acoustic_time.rs should show which.)
- [ ] fs-couple compiles (native and wasm32) with the method either implemented correctly or the
      call site corrected to the right existing method.
- [ ] `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` from crates/fs-wasm reaches fs-couple and
      compiles it without this error (does not need to make the whole build green if other
      unrelated defects remain — record what it does reach).
- [ ] A failing command is never retried to manufacture a green run.

comments.author: PlumHawk
comments.text:
FIXED AND PUSHED (PlumHawk, 2026-09-16). Commit a526cae7 on frankensim main
(rebased onto origin/main 7710893a, which had drifted 68 commits ahead from
unrelated concurrent work by the project owner; no overlap with fs-couple, clean
rebase, pushed 7710893a..a526cae7).

## Root cause

Commit e8589b00 (2026-09-10) rewired `bowed_string.rs` to call
`model.held_force_for_port_velocity(...)`, documented the contract for it in
`CONTRACT.md`, and DELETED the old inline "acceleration cancellation" pinning
formula it replaced -- but never added the method itself to
`ModalAcousticTimeModel`. Confirmed via `git show e8589b00 --stat`: it touched
only `CONTRACT.md`, `bowed_string.rs`, `stribeck_friction.rs`, never
`modal_acoustic_time.rs`. Not a rename, not wasm-specific (the call site is
unconditional Rust) -- a genuinely incomplete commit.

## The fix

Implemented `held_force_for_port_velocity` per CONTRACT.md's own description
("the exact-ZOH scalar endpoint constraint from free modal motion plus
unit-port-force mobility, with conjugate force and velocity projections"):
for each mode, evaluate the existing `advance_exact_zoh(_cached)` transition
(the same one `step_duration` uses) at force 0 and force 1 -- the transition
is provably affine in the held force, so this reads off free port velocity
and unit-force port mobility without re-deriving any coefficients, and can
never drift from production step semantics. Solves the resulting scalar
affine equation for the port force. Refuses a wrong-length shape vector, a
nonpositive/nonfinite duration, nonfinite inputs, or nonpositive/nonfinite
mobility (a real physical case: an undamped port sampled at a duration whose
sine term is negative). Never mutates state (`&self`).

## Tests added (same file, real, not stubs)

- `g3_held_force_for_port_velocity_reaches_target_in_every_damping_regime`:
  round-trips force -> step_duration -> achieved port velocity within 1e-9,
  across 5 damping regimes (undamped/near-zero/underdamped/critical/
  overdamped), a mixed-sign 2-mode port, and full/half/subsample durations.
- `g1_held_force_for_port_velocity_beats_the_old_acceleration_cancellation_heuristic`:
  reproduces the OLD deleted formula verbatim from the e8589b00 diff and shows
  it misses the endpoint target by >1e-4 over a non-small step, while the new
  exact solve hits it to <1e-9 -- matching CONTRACT.md's own stated intent for
  a "G1" test ("demonstrates the old pinning error").
- `g0_held_force_for_port_velocity_refuses_malformed_inputs_and_never_mutates`:
  zero/negative/NaN duration, shape-count mismatch, NaN shape, NaN target
  velocity, and a constructed negative-mobility case (undamped mode sampled
  at omega*dt = 3*pi/2, where sin = -1 robustly, not a near-zero rounding
  coin-flip), asserting state is untouched after every refusal.

## Real build verification (rch exec, not local, not silenced)

`cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` from `crates/fs-wasm`, worker
hz3, run TWICE:
  1. Cold cache: exit=0 in 206681ms ("Finished `dev` profile... in 3m 26s")
  2. Warm cache (retry): exit=0 in 54591ms ("Finished `dev` profile... in 54.09s")
Both runs: `fs-couple` compiles with exactly 1 warning, an unrelated
pre-existing dead-code lint in `cinematic_stem.rs:35` (`const INTERNAL` never
used) -- nothing from my change. Zero `^error` lines in either full log. The
E0599 this bead was filed for is gone.

Both runs then hit RCH-E309 ("remote compile ... SUCCEEDED but build
artifacts could not be retrieved ... timed out after 30000ms") pulling the
compiled .wasm back to this machine -- a worker-hz3 artifact-transfer network
timeout, distinct from and after the actual compile, which is what
`Remote command finished: exit=0` measures. `rch status` does not list hz3 as
unhealthy. Flagging this to BoldHarbor as a possible rch infra issue worth a
`rch workers probe hz3` look, separate from this bead.

## Not run: cargo test -p fs-couple

Attempted via `rch exec -- cargo test -p fs-couple --lib modal_acoustic_time`;
failed in 464ms, before touching fs-couple at all:
  error: failed to select a version for the requirement `fsci-special = "=0.1.0"`
  candidate versions found which didn't match: 0.2.0
  required by package `fs-math v0.0.1`
This is the SAME pre-existing, unrelated root-workspace lock-staleness residue
that also blocked native fs-exec/fs-fft verification on the sibling bead
(am-fs-asupersync-unification-n8hi) -- reproduced identically, not caused by
this change, out of scope for both beads. My new tests are therefore verified
by careful manual review (cross-checked field names, iterator/zip patterns,
and the heuristic formula against proven-compiling existing code in the same
file) and by the production method compiling cleanly inside a full successful
wasm32 build, but NOT by an actual green `cargo test` run. Stating this
plainly per this project's evidence rules.

## Acceptance criteria status

- [x] Root cause identified (never implemented in e8589b00, not renamed/removed)
- [x] fs-couple compiles for wasm32 with the method implemented (2x verified)
- [ ] fs-couple compiles for native -- blocked by the same fsci-special
      residue as `cargo test`; not independently verified
- [x] `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` from crates/fs-wasm
      reaches fs-couple and compiles it without the E0599 (fully verified,
      build reaches "Finished" twice)
- [x] no retried-to-green: both build attempts show identical, honest results
