    rank    1 of 2423   4c0af995   37/43 foreign
    rank   10 of 2423   ca2b4d29    3/64 foreign
    rank 1113 of 2423   511d13e4    0/2  foreign

Directory spread does not work either: ca2b4d29 spans 47 directories, a02a35a6
spans 70 honestly.

THE GATE. Of 445 commits carrying a (beads) scope, 440 - 98.9% - touch nothing
outside .beads/. That is a categorical rule the repository already follows, not
a threshold anyone picked. The five exceptions (4c0af995, 75dbe3a4, aca14ae2,
18f1f4bd, fa281691) are baselined; a sixth fails. Two-sided: an entry that stops
violating also fails, so the list cannot rot into a permanent excuse. A
denominator test refuses a vacuous run below 300 commits found.

PLANTED AGAINST THE REAL SHAS, not fixtures. Removing 4c0af995 from the baseline
turns 'no unrecorded (beads) commit' RED naming it (2 pass 1 fail); adding a sha
that does not violate turns 'the list cannot rot' RED (2 pass 1 fail); restored
byte-identically by cmp, 3 pass 0 fail.

NOT CAUGHT, AND NOT CATCHABLE THIS WAY:

  ca2b4d29  fix(mobile), 64 files, 47 directories. Ranks below six legitimate
            commits on every predicate measured.
  511d13e4  refactor(chrome), 1 file, correct scope, honest message. It carried
            a peer's 37-line block inside a file that genuinely belonged to its
            message. The contamination is INTRA-FILE. No commit-metadata
            predicate can see it - this is a property of the defect, not a gap
            in the gate, and I would rather say so than build a detector that
            fires on honest wide commits.

If the 511d13e4 shape is to be caught at all it has to be caught BEFORE the
commit, by the author knowing what is staged, not after by inspecting history.
That is a different bead and probably a different kind of answer.

LANE NOTE: node, and bunfig ignores it. bun cannot spawn git in this
environment - execFileSync and Bun.spawnSync both fail with EBADF on
posix_spawn, at module scope and inside a test body alike. outFreshness.fixture
and trackedImports are already node-lane for the same reason.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ADJACENT NOTE, filed here because this is the process-hygiene bead in play.

The anchored process-check norm is now in AGENTS.md (a2295d72), beside the build
norm. Three panes made the ps-piped-to-grep error within two hours: pane29 named
two zsh shells as live builds, TanElk reported 3 builds one tick after
correcting pane29 for the same thing, and I read 3, believed a build was racing
my plant, and moved out/ back on a false alarm.

VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE BUILD rather than taken on report:

    ps aux | grep -cE "[n]ext build"             4
    of the five matching lines, four were        /bin/zsh -c source .../snapshot-zsh-*.sh
    two of those had been created by             that very command, a second earlier
    pgrep -fl "node_modules/.bin/next build"     1, pid 16930, the real build

The sharpest part is not that the naive form overcounts but that it is UNSTABLE:
the act of measuring creates matches, so the same command a second apart can
return different numbers. The `[n]ext` bracket trick defeats a literal
self-match and does nothing about a wrapper shell whose argv carries the whole
pipeline string.

NO GATE PROPOSED, and the dispatch asked me to say why rather than build one.

The error occurs in ad-hoc shell commands a pane types interactively. No
repo-level lint can observe that surface - nothing about it is ever committed.
A lint on `ps` piped to `grep` inside scripts/ would police a different
population, and mostly a legitimate one: a script grepping for a process name it
does not itself contain is fine, which is exactly the false-positive surface that
makes the rule hard to state without exceptions.

So the note is the whole intervention. If it happens a fourth time the right
response is to find out why the note was not read, not to add a gate that cannot
see the place it happens.

Related, and the reason I think the note is sufficient: the shape is the same as
the unanchored-pattern class already in AGENTS.md (`grep -ciE "MIT"` matching
`Emit`, `sort -u -t: -k2` deduping by the wrong field). That section is
prose too, and it is the one I checked my own measurements against all session.

title: Two smoke-journey checks report PASS when the feature is absent, and the theme-toggle selector never matched the shipped control
description:
## What is wrong

Two of the four checks in the smoke journey report `ok: true` on the branch that runs when the feature is not found. They cannot fail for the reason they exist.

```
scripts/e2e/smoke.ts:138-145
} else {
  checks.push({
    check: "theme-toggle",
    ok: true,
    message: "Theme toggle not yet mounted (am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31 pending)",
    ...
```

`command-palette` is built the same way at lines 173-180. Both the found branch and the not-found branch push `ok: true`; only a thrown exception produces `ok: false`.

## The theme-toggle check is also pointed at markup that does not exist

The selector is `[data-theme-toggle], button[aria-label*='theme' i]`.

```
data-theme-toggle in the built site (out/**/*.html): 0 files
```

The shipped control is a fieldset of radios, present on every page:

```
out/index.html
<fieldset class="theme-toggle"><legend>Theme</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="_R_8lb_-theme"/>Annalen</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="_R_8lb_-theme"/>Kramgasse Night</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="_R_8lb_-theme"/>Slate</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="_R_8lb_-theme"/>Follow system</label>
</fieldset>
```

There is no button and no `data-theme-toggle` attribute, so the selector never matches, the check takes the not-found branch, and it reports:

```
[PASS] smoke theme-toggle (11ms): Theme toggle not yet mounted (am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31 pending)
```

The theme toggle shipped. The check has never once exercised it, reports a pass, and attributes the supposed absence to a bead that is not responsible for it.

## Measured

`bun scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts --smoke` against the real static build served on 127.0.0.1:3088:

```
[PASS] smoke home-page (87ms): HTTP 200 with product identity
[PASS] smoke not-found-page (15ms): Status 404 indicating not found
[PASS] smoke theme-toggle (11ms): Theme toggle not yet mounted ... pending
[PASS] smoke command-palette (1ms): Command palette not yet mounted ... pending
SMOKE_RC=0
```

Two of four checks are vacuous. `command-palette` at least states an absence that is currently true (0 matches in the home page build); `theme-toggle` states one that is false.

## Why this matters now

"The smoke journey passes against the real production build" is an acceptance criterion of am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh, which blocks 81 beads. It is currently satisfied vacuously, and a 1ms check that asserts a feature is missing is not evidence that the build works.

## Acceptance

1. The not-found branch of each check reports `ok: false` with a message naming what was searched for, or the check is removed. A check that passes on absence does not stay.
2. `theme-toggle` locates the shipped `fieldset.theme-toggle` radios, selects a theme other than the current one, and asserts `document.documentElement` carries the corresponding theme attribute afterwards.
3. Planted negative: removing the theme fieldset from a fixture page makes the check fail, proving it is live.
4. `command-palette` either targets the real palette once mounted, or is deleted and its absence recorded in docs/PAPER_E2E_HARNESS.md rather than reported as a passing check.

## What is not wrong

The rest of the harness measured clean today at e3045fa. All 11 lanes pass end to end - desktop, tablet, touch-320, webkit-real, keyboard-only, reduced-motion, zoom-400, text-200, no-webgl, js-disabled, print - and the runtime-conformance journey runs 9 events including two planted negatives (`planted-randomness-nav-fails`, `planted-stale-teardown-fails`) that are required to fail and do. This finding is narrow and concerns the smoke journey only.

## Provenance

Found by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 while triaging am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh after its last blocker closed. Measured by running the journey against the real build and grepping the built HTML, not inferred from the source.
close_reason:
Closed by orchestrator TanElk at 1960117. Two stacked defects, both fixed and both re-executed rather than reasoned about.

AC1, the absent branch must fail and name what it searched for. Both chrome checks now do. Measured on a fixture with no theme control: "[FAIL] theme-toggle: No visible theme control matched \"fieldset.theme-toggle\"", and the palette check names both selectors it tried plus the component path.

AC2, the theme check drives the shipped control. It locates fieldset.theme-toggle, checks the Slate radio, waits for document.documentElement's data-theme to equal "slate", then does the same for Annalen. Against the real static build on 127.0.0.1:3088: "[PASS] smoke theme-toggle (152ms): data-theme started at annalen and followed the radio group through slate then annalen". The previous check reported "[PASS] theme-toggle (11ms): Theme toggle not yet mounted" - about a toggle that ships on every page - because it searched for [data-theme-toggle], which appears in zero built HTML files, while ThemeToggle renders a radio group.

AC3, planted negative. Proven twice and independently. First by accident: before the navigation fix, the same check ran on the not-found page and failed naming the selector. Then deliberately, as scripts/e2e/smoke.test.ts "an absent theme control fails the check instead of passing it", which asserts ok === false, the message naming fieldset.theme-toggle, and the whole journey ok === false.

AC4, the palette. It is not deleted and it is not softened. It fails live, naming both selectors and the unmounted component, and docs/PAPER_E2E_HARNESS.md now records the exact message, that the red is a real gap in the built site rather than a harness defect, and that --smoke is reachable only through its flag so the red does not enter CI (the browser-acceptance gate step invokes the runner with no flags).

The third defect, which the bead did not know about: the journey has exactly two page.goto calls, the home page and /__e2e_nonexistent_smoke_route__, and never navigated back, so every check after the second ran on a page with no chrome. That is the reason the wrong selector was never noticed.

scripts/e2e/smoke.test.ts was itself the lock. It served a fixture with no toggle and no palette and required both checks to report ok: true, which is RH-5 written into a test. It now proves the check is live in both directions and holds 5 passing tests. The fixture proves the check; that the real site honours the same contract is proven by the run against the build, not by the fixture.

Evidence at this revision: node --experimental-strip-types --test scripts/e2e/smoke.test.ts 5 pass / 0 fail; bun run typecheck rc=0; bunx tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json --noEmit unchanged at 206 errors, so no new type debt; biome clean on both changed files.

title: Build shared SVG and Canvas view primitives that only project accepted snapshots
description:
# Build shared SVG and Canvas view primitives that only project accepted snapshots

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §8.1 (coordinate traps), §8.2 (rendering rules), §8.3 (diagram scaling), §10.9, §12.5, §12.7, §15.5, §16.2, §16.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Almost every instrument is two-dimensional: histograms, trajectories, spectra, event diagrams, energy ledgers. The plan is emphatic that 2D comes first, and Three.js is reserved for the few spatial cases. A shared view kit keeps visual semantics consistent. More importantly, it encodes the rendering rules that protect scientific meaning:

- a logarithmic axis never redefines what a density means;
- a path leaving the viewport stays in the ensemble;
- a smooth polyline is a rendering convention, not a velocity;
- a point distribution at $t = 0$ is not an infinite bar;
- ultraviolet and infrared are never shown as visible colors without a false-color legend;
- rendering a subset of particles never changes the ensemble used for results;
- a histogram shows bins the owner computed, never bins a view invented from raw positions.

Every primitive consumes accepted snapshot data and projects coordinates into pixels. None computes physics or statistics. The primitives take snapshot slices as props, so they need neither the registry nor any instrument: the dispatcher binds instrument views to instances, and instrument views pass data down.

Browser evidence comes from a **fixture application registered with the harness**, not from a build flag: `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` owns the single fixture bundler (`scripts/e2e/fixtures/bundleFixtures.ts`), its registry (`scripts/e2e/fixtures/fixtureApps.ts`), and the fixture server, and this bead registers the application `view-kit` there.

## Scope

In scope: `src/visuals/kit/` primitives for axes, plots, histograms with comparison series, trajectories, event diagrams, intervals, ledgers, legends, scale bars, and typed-result rendering; performance tiers; accessibility hooks; term-selection highlighting by attribute; the `view-kit` fixture application and its registry entry.

Out of scope:
- specific instruments;
- Three.js (`am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`);
- dataset loading (`am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`);
- description text generation (`am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`, integrated here through hooks);
- performance budget enforcement (`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`);
- the equation selection store itself (`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`);
- the fixture bundler and fixture server (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`).

## Requirements

### Common contract

- **Inputs.** Every primitive receives typed data from an accepted snapshot: typed arrays, typed results from `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`, and the identity fields `instanceId`, `runId`, and `snapshotVersion`.
- **Identity attributes.** Every primitive renders `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, and `data-snapshot-version` so tests can prove that all views show one state.
- **No scientific state.** No primitive keeps a private copy of a scientific parameter in React state or derives a scientific value.

### `RepresentationScale`: five independent fields, declared once

Representational scales are independent fields: spatial magnification, physical elapsed time, playback multiplier, particle glyph size, and quantity normalization. A label such as "real time" means model seconds per wall-clock second, not physically life-size rendering. A light pulse can be shown with a greatly slowed playback rate without pretending its physical speed has changed, and a microscope view can be magnified while its displacement values remain in micrometres.

Three of those five are owned in three places today and none of them together: the scale bar and the histogram's stated normalization here, the 1:1 playback clock with labeled speed factors in `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez`, and nothing at all for magnification or glyph size. The gap has already produced a local invention: `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei` declares its own control, "Displacement magnification, none, ×10¹⁵ to ×10²⁰ for the readout, default ×10¹⁷, presentation-change", because there is no shared field to declare it in, no validator to check it against, and no rule carrying that factor into the accessible table or the print view. A reader who sees a $1.112650\times10^{-17}$ m displacement drawn at a visible size has no contracted way to learn that the picture is magnified by $10^{17}$, and a screen-reader user has none at all.

This adds one typed view-state object and five rules. It adds no primitive, no view, and no physics.

Every view that draws a physical quantity publishes a `RepresentationScale` beside the snapshot it projects. Its five fields are independent, none is derived from another, and changing any one is a `presentation-change`:

```
representationScale:
  spatialMagnification:  { appliesTo: "scene" | <outputId>, factor: number, note?: string }
  simulatedElapsedTime:  { quantityId, value, unit }   # the model time this frame represents
  playbackMultiplier:    number                        # model seconds per wall-clock second
  glyphSize:             { drawnPx: number, represents: "none" | <quantityId> }
  quantityNormalization: { kind: "none" | "per-bin-width" | "per-total" | "per-peak" | <quantityId>, note?: string }
```

1. **`playbackMultiplier` defines "real time."** The label "true rate" or "real time" renders only when `playbackMultiplier` is exactly 1, and it means model seconds per wall-clock second, never that the drawing is life-size. The "true rate" and "25 times faster" labels of `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez` render from this field rather than from the controller's own state; the controller sets it.
2. **`glyphSize.represents: "none"` is the default and the honest case.** A drawn particle marker is a marker. A view may set `represents` to a quantity id only when the drawn size is calibrated to that quantity and the legend says so; otherwise a reader may not infer a physical size from a glyph, and a test asserts that no caption relates glyph size to a physical extent while `represents` is `"none"`.
3. **`spatialMagnification.factor` is 1 unless a view deliberately amplifies.** `appliesTo` distinguishes a magnified scene from an amplified readout: BM-01's microscope view magnifies the scene, and `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei` amplifies one output, its displacement. A factor other than 1 is rendered as a visible statement ("drawn one hundred million times larger than life", or the readout's own wording), and it never changes the value shown in the units strip: the view is magnified while the displacement values remain in micrometres.
4. **The same five facts reach the nonvisual summary and the print view.** The accessible table (`am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`) and the print stylesheet (`am-plat-print-3orn`) render the scale facts from this object, so a reader who never sees the scene is told what the scene's scale was. A view that publishes a `RepresentationScale` no accessible surface renders fails the audit.
5. **The scale bar is derived, never independent.** `ScaleBar` is drawn from the manifest's `realRate.scaleBar` calibrated length and `spatialMagnification`; a view that draws a scale bar without publishing a `RepresentationScale` fails.

The existing consumers, restated as declarations:

| View | `spatialMagnification` | `playbackMultiplier` | `glyphSize.represents` | `quantityNormalization` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BM-01 microscope view (`am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`) | scene, the factor that makes a 1 μm bar the drawn bar length | 1 at true rate, or the accelerated factor | `"none"` (a tracer marker is not a particle radius) | `none` |
| BM-01 displacement histogram | scene, 1 | 1 | `"none"` | `per-bin-width` or `per-total`, matching the bin-probability versus density toggle |
| `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei` box view | `centerOfMassShift` (the displacement output id), factor $10^{17}$ by default, range $10^{15}$ to $10^{20}$ | 1 | `"none"` | `none` |
| SR-03 strip view | scene, 1 | 1 | `"none"` | `none` |
| SR-10 bounding-sphere view | scene, 1 | 1 | `"none"` | `none` |

The box's existing control is unchanged in behaviour; it becomes a declared instance of `spatialMagnification` with `appliesTo` naming its output, which is what lets its factor reach the accessible table and the print view for the first time.

A scene shows a scale bar, a time legend, and a short caption, and no more: the scene is never covered with telemetry that distracts from the relation being taught. The full five-field statement lives in the accessible table, the print view, and the model note where a factor other than 1 is in force.

### Term selection without a store dependency (decided here and in `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`)

`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8` lists this kit's series and tables among the subscribers of its selection store. The kit does **not** import that store, and there is no edge from this bead to `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`, because every Batch B instrument would then wait on the equation component.

- Every series, mark, legend entry, axis label, and table cell that represents a quantity renders `data-quantity-id` with its exact canonical id.
- The equation island publishes the current selection on the argument-context root it already owns, as `data-selected-quantity-id` and `data-selected-node-id`. SVG primitives highlight through a CSS attribute match scoped to that root, so selection works with no JavaScript in the kit and no import in either direction.
- Canvas layers cannot be styled by CSS, so they accept an optional `selectedQuantityId` string prop and redraw the emphasized layer. The kit neither subscribes nor polls: the component that subscribes to the selection store and passes the prop is a downstream bead (the reading-face composer and the interaction ladder), which is where every JavaScript subscriber lives.
- Highlighting is presentation: it never changes snapshot data, never issues a command, and never enters a scientific digest.

### Axes and units

- Axes take a canonical quantity id and a display unit from the quantity registry. Tick labels format through the units adapter, never through ad hoc strings.
- **Logarithmic axes.** The primitive requires the snapshot to declare the density kind of its vertical data: `per-frequency`, `per-wavelength`, `per-ln-interval`, `per-decade`, or `total`. A log horizontal axis with a per-frequency density is labeled as such. Switching to a per-log-interval view is a data transform supplied by the owner, not a relabel.
- Frequency and wavelength axes are distinct quantity ids. A selected band can be preserved across representations using owner-supplied mappings.
- **Log-log plots.** Model reference lines carry their slope label (for example "slope 1/2"); both the line values and the slope come from the snapshot.

### Plot primitives

- **`LinePlot` and `ScatterPlot`** have three visually distinct classes: theoretical curves, historical fitted laws, and empirical points (markers with uncertainty bars). The class is part of the data contract.
- **`Histogram`** has explicit bin semantics. The owner supplies edges, counts, overflow counts, and bin probabilities. The view offers a bin-probability versus density toggle, shows the bin width, and states the normalization. An optional **comparison series** draws aligned bars or markers of a second class, such as a numerical grid result beside exact bin probabilities, with non-color identity.
- **`IntervalShade`** shades a selected interval, with the probability value supplied by the snapshot.
- **`AnalyticLimitMarker`** renders an `analytic-limit` point distribution as a labeled marker with interval probabilities, never an infinite bar.

### Trajectories and fields of view

- **`TrajectoryLayer`** draws sampled positions from typed buffers without copying them into React state. It supports up to 10 000 tracers with batched Canvas drawing and instancing where available.
- **Viewport exits.** Paths leaving the viewport are not wrapped, reflected, replaced, or dropped from the ensemble, and the API offers no option to do so. The view shows an off-screen count as a presentation census. The microscope boundary is a camera viewport, not a wall.
- **Initial layout.** Initial on-screen positions (for example a deterministic lattice) are presentation layout supplied by the instrument and are excluded from scientific digests.
- **Polylines.** Smooth lines between samples are labeled a rendering convention in the model note; no primitive derives velocity from a polyline.
- **Subsets.** Rendering a subset for performance is allowed only for display; result panels always read ensemble statistics from the snapshot.

### Event and spacetime diagrams

`EventDiagram`:
- uses coherent axis scaling so light lines are at 45 degrees;
- supports light-seconds units with the conversion shown;
- marks events by id with frame labels;
- never lets camera zoom imply changed physics;
- carries the label that spacetime diagrams are a later aid (Minkowski 1908).

### Ledgers and legends

- `EnergyLedger`: bars and tables for channel accounting, with boundaries drawn from snapshot data.
- `QuantityLegend`: keyed by quantity id and role color from the semantic color system, plus a non-color identity (label, shape, outline, or pattern), so meaning survives color-vision differences and monochrome print.
- `FalseColorLegend`: required whenever a spectral view shows frequencies outside 380–750 nm.
- `ScaleBar`: a calibrated physical length and time scale from snapshot and manifest data.

### Performance and lifecycle

- 60 Hz on capable desktops and a stable 30 Hz mobile tier. UI summaries are published at a bounded rate, and display interpolation is kept separate from scientific stepping.
- A depleted budget reduces visual detail (point size, drawn subset, resolution) and never alters the model, time step, or sample.
- Canvas contexts, listeners, and animation frames are released on unmount; invisible views pause.

### Accessibility hooks

- Each primitive exposes a description provider consumed by `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`, with three layers: a statement of what is compared, the current relation after an intentional action, and optional detailed data as a table.
- No 60 Hz live-region updates; committed comparisons only.
- Reduced motion pauses animation and shows the current state.

### The `view-kit` fixture application

Registered as `{ id: "view-kit", entry: "src/testing/e2e/fixture-apps/view-kit/", outDir: "artifacts/e2e-fixtures/view-kit/", owner: "am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r" }`, bundled by the harness bundler and served at `/apps/view-kit/`. It renders the kit over deterministic fixture snapshots and emits the harness DOM contract attributes. There is no fixture flag, route, or conditional import in the application.

## Technical Approach

- React components over SVG for axes and annotations, and Canvas 2D for dense layers. Data is passed as typed arrays and snapshot references.
- Deterministic fixture snapshots live in `src/visuals/kit/__fixtures__/`, generated from runtime fixtures, never from ad hoc math in tests.
- Tests use SVG snapshots and, only where rendering is stable across CI browsers, pixel hashes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All primitives exist, take quantity ids and units, render only from snapshot data, and expose identity attributes.
- [ ] Every quantity-bearing mark, legend entry, and table cell carries `data-quantity-id`; SVG highlighting follows `data-selected-quantity-id` on the argument-context root with no import of the selection store, and Canvas layers highlight from the `selectedQuantityId` prop.
- [ ] A density-kind declaration is required for log axes; a test proves a per-frequency density cannot be silently shown under a per-log-interval axis label.
- [ ] Histograms accept only owner-supplied bins; a test proves no API accepts raw positions for binning. Comparison series are distinguishable without color.
- [ ] Trajectories leaving the viewport remain counted, and wrap and reflect are impossible through the API.
- [ ] Analytic-limit markers render correctly with interval probabilities.
- [ ] Legends show non-color identity, and the false-color legend appears for non-visible frequencies.
- [ ] 10 000 fixture tracers render with frame times logged against the agreed device profile; the drawn subset never changes result panels.
- [ ] Views release resources on unmount: no growth in listener or context counts across 50 mount cycles.
- [ ] The `view-kit` fixture application is registered, bundles, and serves at `/apps/view-kit/`.
- [ ] Every view primitive that draws a physical quantity publishes a `RepresentationScale` with all five fields; a fixture view omitting one fails with the view id and field named.
- [ ] The labels "true rate" and "real time" render only when `playbackMultiplier` is exactly 1; a fixture rendering either at 25 fails.
- [ ] `glyphSize.represents` defaults to `"none"`, and a caption relating glyph size to a physical extent while `represents` is `"none"` fails the caption audit.
- [ ] A `spatialMagnification.factor` other than 1 renders a visible statement of the factor, and the value shown in the units strip is unchanged by it, asserted by comparing the rendered value at factor 1 and at $10^{17}$.
- [ ] `appliesTo` distinguishes a scene magnification from a named-output amplification, and `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`'s displacement magnification validates as the latter.
- [ ] The accessible table and the print view render all five facts from the object; a view whose scale facts reach neither fails the audit.
- [ ] A view drawing a scale bar without publishing a `RepresentationScale` fails.
- [ ] Changing any of the five fields is a `presentation-change`: `runId`, `seed`, every scientific digest, and the accepted snapshot are unchanged, and no worker message is sent.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `axes.test.tsx`: unit formatting through the adapter; density-kind enforcement on log axes; slope labels.
- `histogram.test.tsx`: owner bins with overflow counts total the ensemble size; the toggle between bin probability and density; bin width stated; the comparison series class; rejection of a raw-position input.
- `trajectories.test.tsx`: an off-screen count matches a fixture with 37 of 400 tracers outside the viewport; no wrap or reflect option; the drawn-subset flag leaves the result-panel data untouched.
- `eventDiagram.test.tsx`: 45-degree light lines under coherent scaling; the Minkowski 1908 label.
- `legends.test.tsx`: non-color identity; the false-color legend for a 300 nm fixture.
- `analyticLimit.test.tsx`: a $t = 0$ fixture renders a marker with probabilities 1 and 0 and no bar.
- `selection.test.tsx`: every quantity-bearing element carries `data-quantity-id`; setting `data-selected-quantity-id` on the context root highlights exactly the matching SVG marks and no others; a Canvas layer highlights from the prop; the kit imports no module from `src/equations/`.
- `lifecycle.test.tsx`: 50 mount cycles with counted listeners, contexts, and animation frames.
- `representationScale.test.tsx`, against the real primitives and the real runtime: a fixture view omitting each field in turn fails, and the defaults (`factor: 1`, `represents: "none"`, `kind: "none"`) validate; `playbackMultiplier` of 1 renders "true rate" and 25 renders "25 times faster", while a fixture rendering "real time" at 25 fails with the multiplier named; a property test over a fixed seeded list of 200 combinations asserts that setting each field leaves the other four unchanged, so no field is silently derived from another; the box fixture rendered at factors $10^{15}$, $10^{17}$, and $10^{20}$ shows the same displacement value $1.112650\times10^{-17}$ m in its units strip at every factor and three different drawn extents, and a fixture that scales the displayed value by the factor fails; a caption reading "each dot is one particle, drawn at its true size" fails while `represents` is `"none"` and passes only when `represents` names a calibrated quantity id whose legend states the calibration; changing each field through the real command router leaves `runId`, the scientific digest of `snapshotVersion`, the seed, and the draw counter unchanged and produces zero worker messages, using the assertions `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez` makes for its toggle; for each of the five consumer views the accessible table and the print output both contain all five facts, and removing a fact from either surface fails the audit with the view id; a fixture drawing a scale bar with no published `RepresentationScale` fails, and one whose bar length disagrees with `realRate.scaleBar` times `spatialMagnification.factor` fails.
- `forbiddenCalls` coverage: the registry's view guard runs over `src/visuals/kit/`.

### End-to-end tests

On the `view-kit` fixture application (`/apps/view-kit/`), through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:
- drive fixture tracers out of the viewport and assert the ensemble count and the statistics panel are unchanged;
- set the selected quantity on the context root and assert the highlighted marks all carry that `data-quantity-id`;
- the reduced-motion lane shows a static state;
- the 320 px lane has no horizontal overflow;
- the performance lane records frame times with device profile metadata.
- toggle true rate and read the rendered label at both multipliers; open the accessible table by keyboard and read all five scale facts; print the page in the print lane and assert the facts appear.
- on the BM-01 and box lanes, set the magnification to $10^{15}$ and $10^{20}$ by keyboard and assert that the units strip is unchanged while the drawn extent changes and `data-run-id` and `data-snapshot-version` are unchanged. Lanes: keyboard only, 320 px, reduced motion, JavaScript disabled (the static worked example still states its scale facts), and WebKit.

The instrument-specific lanes (for example BM-01 viewport exits) run in the instrument beads and `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`.

### Structured logging and retained evidence

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/view-kit/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `component`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `drawnCount`, `ensembleCount`, `offscreenCount`, `selectedQuantityId`, `frameTimeP95Ms`, `deviceProfile`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `evidence`, and `message`, and in `extra`: `viewId`, `spatialMagnificationFactor`, `spatialMagnificationAppliesTo`, `simulatedElapsedTime`, `playbackMultiplier`, `glyphDrawnPx`, `glyphRepresents`, `quantityNormalizationKind`, `renderedScaleLabel`, `accessibleScaleFactsPresent`, and `printScaleFactsPresent`.

A failing browser test retains a screenshot, a trace, a DOM snapshot, and the console log through the harness evidence recorder, named by the log line's `evidence` field. A failing scale case additionally retains the rendered markup, the accessible-tree snapshot, the print output, and the published `RepresentationScale` under `artifacts/test-logs/view-kit/<log-run-id>/failures/<testId>/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Keep four distinctions visible: trajectory versus ensemble; position versus displacement; signed coordinate versus radius; mean square versus square of the mean.
- Never compute a physical value or a statistic in a view helper "for convenience."
- A histogram binned by the view from a drawn subset would silently use fewer samples than the result panel. That is why bins come from the owner.
- Highlighting by attribute keeps the kit off the equation component's critical path; do not "simplify" it later by importing the selection store.
- The five fields are independent because conflating any two produces a specific lie. Magnification times playback would make a slowed pulse look slow and small; glyph size folded into magnification would turn a marker into a claimed particle radius; normalization folded into magnification would make a density look like a count.
- "Real time" is a statement about clocks, never about size. A random walk at true rate is still drawn under a microscope's magnification, and the caption must be able to say both things at once.
- A magnified readout is not a magnified scene. The box's $10^{17}$ amplifies one number's drawn representation; nothing about the box is drawn $10^{17}$ times larger. `appliesTo` keeps those apart, and an author who set it to `"scene"` for the box would be claiming something absurd.
- Do not let the five facts colonise the scene. A scale bar, a time legend, and a short caption are the visible budget; the rest belongs to the accessible table, the print view, and the model note.
- A view may not compute a scale from the data it is drawing. The magnification is a declared presentation choice, and inferring it from the range of the values would make the scale change when the physics changes, which is the one thing a scale must never do.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`: snapshot types and identity fields.
- `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`: the status union rendered by analytic-limit and outside-domain presentations.
- `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`: role colors keyed to quantity ids.
- `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`: quantity ids, units, and formatting.
- `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`: the description providers the primitives implement.

The harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`) owns the fixture bundler this bead registers with; it reaches this bead through `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7` and the runtime beads, so no direct edge is needed.

The `RepresentationScale` shape is declared in `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` beside `realRate` and its `scaleBar`, as an additive view-state type, and is never duplicated here. That schema bead reaches this one through `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`, so no direct edge is added. `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`, which this bead already depends on, and `am-plat-print-3orn` both render the five facts from this one object instead of each asking views for scale information.

Unblocks:
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`, `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`, `am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`, `am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`, `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez` (whose "true rate" and "25 times faster" labels render from `playbackMultiplier` instead of from controller state).
- `am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`, `am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb`, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`.

10. The view-kit fixture app is registered, bundles and serves at /apps/view-kit/: PARTLY MET. src/testing/e2e/fixture-apps/view-kit exists; I did not measure bundling or serving.
11. Every quantity-drawing view publishes a RepresentationScale with all five fields, and omitting one fails naming the view and field: MET per the representationScale tests.
12. "true rate" and "real time" appear only at playbackMultiplier 1, and a fixture at 25 fails: MET per tests (8 test files carry the strings).
13. glyphSize.represents defaults to "none", and a caption relating glyph size to extent fails the caption audit: MET per tests (13 files).
14. A spatial magnification other than 1 shows its factor, and the units strip is unchanged at factor 10^17: MET per tests (14 files). I did not trace the 10^17 case specifically.
15. appliesTo separates scene magnification from named-output amplification, and ME-03's displacement magnification validates as the latter: MET per me03/box.representationScale.test.
16. The accessible table and the print view render all five facts: MET per printRepresentationScale.test and representationScale.descriptions.test.
17. A scale bar drawn without a published RepresentationScale fails: PARTLY MET (ScaleBar takes a scale; not traced to a failing fixture).
18. Changing any scale field is a presentation-change that leaves run, seed, digests and snapshot unchanged and sends no worker message: PARTLY MET (not traced).

title: Build the HistoricalDataset loader, digitization pipeline, and visually distinct cited overlays
description:
# Build the HistoricalDataset loader, digitization pipeline, and visually distinct cited overlays **Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.2, §8.1 (stable evaluation and data honesty), §8.2 (synthetic versus real data), §10.7, §11.2 (HistoricalDataset), §13.1, §17.3 (digitize-datasets/) (traceability only) ## Background "Empirical points, historical fitted laws, and theoretical curves stay visibly distinct; the site never manufactures a convincing 1904 measurement by sampling a modern formula and adding noise." Historical measurements are typed `HistoricalDataset` records with citations, or they are absent. This bead builds the shared machinery every dataset and every overlay uses: - the record loader and validator; - the digitization pipeline that turns a cited table or figure into a canonical record with provenance and uncertainty; - the overlay component that shows data beside model curves with dates, citations, and honest styling. It also enforces the knowledge boundary: data published after 1904 never appears on the 1904 shelf, and every overlay says when the measurement was made. A dataset is a miniature critical edition, so a reader must be able to walk from the printed page to the plotted point. The record already captures a source page image and the overlay already offers points plus an accessible table, and nothing joins them. Two further gaps are honesty gaps rather than convenience gaps: nothing records which rows a fit excluded, and nothing distinguishes when a measurement was made, when it was published, and when this site analysed it. A third class of gap is about the cells themselves. A digitized historical table is not a rectangle of numbers: it has blanks the original author left, values the apparatus could only bound, columns the author fitted rather than measured, and a limited set of inferences its provenance actually supports. `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` declares the shape that records all four; this bead is the consumer that makes them mean something on screen and at build time, because a typed bound that is plotted as a point is no safer than an untyped one. Eligibility is decided per publication, not per dataset. Some datasets span the cutoff. Kaufmann's electron deflection results of 1901–1903 are pre-cutoff, but his 1906 analysis is not. Some values appear in more than one publication: the 1899–1900 blackbody measurements appear in a 1900 Berlin report and in a later 1901 *Annalen* paper, and shelf use must cite the earlier report. Two locations have two different jobs. The **canonical record** that the site loads is `content/datasets/.yaml` plus its CSV, under the `HistoricalDataset` schema. The **pipeline directory** `scripts/digitize-datasets//` keeps the provenance, the digitization log, and the validation that produced the canonical record; the site never reads it. A dataset's columns are canonical quantities, so this bead also fixes the order of work between a dataset and the quantity registry: the id exists in the registry before the dataset that uses it lands. One resolver decides that question for every dataset, so no child re-implements the check and no two datasets report a legacy spelling differently. ## Scope In scope: - the `HistoricalDataset` loader and validator in `src/content/datasets/`, reading canonical records only; - conventions and a validation harness for the `scripts/digitize-datasets/` pipeline; - the `DatasetOverlay` view component; - the bounded marker, the refusal of a mean estimator over a bound, and the missing cell in the accessible table; - the `dataset-inference-not-admitted` build failure; - the evidence reveal and its rights-governed crop; - the validation and rendering of declared fits; - the three separately typed dataset dates; - the typed refusal for uncited data; - the per-publication shelf-eligibility rule; - the column-quantity rule that keeps the registry the single source of quantity ids, resolved through the registry's own resolver; - one pipeline fixture. Out of scope: - individual datasets (the children of `am-ep-datasets-fsk`, such as `am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`); - the schema definition, including the `DataCell` union, the four `columns[].role` values, `allowedInferenceModelIds[]`, `calibrationIds[]`, `sharedInputIds[]`, `digitizationRevision`, the `fits[]` field shape and the three date fields (`am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`, which adds them in the same change; this bead owns their validation, rendering and consumer rules and keeps no second schema); - the shared-input registry the provenance pointers name, and the independence claims over it (`am-dataset-independence-registry-3dfb`); - the estimators themselves and their statuses (`am-ref-inference-2w9` and the other reference beads); - the quantity registry itself, its resolver implementation, its legacy-spelling records, and the addition of new ids (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`); - the corpus-wide compiler rule `quantity-id-not-exact` (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`), which applies the same resolver to every quantity id in content; - the rights policy (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`, whose vocabulary this bead validates against); - consumer instrument lanes (LQ-08, BM-07, the Fizeau shelf instrument), which run in their own beads. ## Requirements ### Canonical records - Each dataset is `content/datasets/.yaml` with a CSV beside it (`content/datasets/.csv`, or several CSVs for several series), whose path and SHA-256 the YAML records. A dataset split by the source into separately published series may have one record per series (for example `perrin-1909-displacements` and `perrin-1909-sedimentation`). - The CSV carries the values as printed, with printed units, plus canonical conversions in separate columns. - The loader reads only canonical records. A dataset present only as pipeline files fails the build. ### Column quantities come from the registry, through its resolver - Every column names an exact canonical quantity id from `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`. The loader resolves every column id through that registry's own `resolveQuantityId` (`src/content/quantities/resolveQuantityId.ts`) and never by its own string comparison, so one rule covers every dataset: - `{ok: true, quantity}` admits the column and supplies its dimension and permitted units; - `{ok: false, kind: "legacy-spelling", canonicalIds}` fails the build with the registry's own message from `legacySpellingMessage(id)`, which names the canonical id or ids (for example "use `electricFieldStationary`"); - `{ok: false, kind: "unregistered"}` fails the build naming the dataset, the column, and the id, and never offers a near match. - **Frame-tagged and harmonized ids the dataset children now bind**, with the spellings the registry records as legacy: - `electricFieldStationary` and `magneticFieldStationary` for apparatus fields at rest in Einstein's stationary system (Kaufmann, Bucherer); the unframed `electricField` and `magneticField` are legacy spellings; - `acceleratingPotential` (Ives–Stilwell and paper 3 §10); `acceleratingVoltage` is a legacy spelling; - `speedRatio` for the modern $\beta = v/c$ only; a speed printed in cm/s or m/s binds a speed quantity instead, and the conversion is a derived column; - `chargeToMassRatio`, whose record carries SI, Gaussian, and electromagnetic dimensions, so each column states the unit system its source printed. - A dataset that needs a quantity the registry does not yet hold is blocked on adding that id to the registry, in the registry's own change. The loader never accepts a local alias, a display label, or a near-match spelling in place of a registered id. - The registry now records the ids the dataset beads identified while its seed list was being written (`volumeFraction`, `relativeViscosity`, `relativeSpectralEmission`, `chargeToMassRatio`, `fringeShift`, `dragCoefficient`, and `speedRatio`), so today's children resolve. The rule stands for every later dataset: this bead's validator is what makes a premature dataset fail loudly instead of inventing an id. - Units are validated against the registry's permitted units for that quantity and must be dimensionally consistent with it. ### Record fields and validation **Required fields:** - a title; - the full citation (authors, title, journal, series, volume, year, pages) with the **table or figure number**; - the digitizer (name or agent id) and the digitization date; - the source scan asset id with its rights status, from the vocabulary of `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`; - columns with canonical quantity ids and units, and the rows (or the CSV path with its SHA-256); - uncertainty, keeping reported measurement uncertainty separate from digitization uncertainty for values read from figures; - notes: reduction choices, corrections applied by the original authors, and known reanalyses as secondary citations. **Publications and dates:** - `publications[]` lists each publication in which values appeared, with its own citation and date. - Each series or row names the publication it is taken from. - Shelf eligibility is computed from that publication's date. **Validation:** - Column quantity ids resolve through `resolveQuantityId`, and units exist in the registry and are dimensionally consistent with the column's quantity. - Row counts match the documented source table. - Uncertainty columns are non-negative and aligned with their rows. - The CSV digest matches the YAML record. - A dataset lacking a table or figure citation fails the build; if loaded dynamically, it produces a typed refusal at runtime. - Each column declares whether it is a reported measurement or a quantity derived by the original author, through `columns[].role` below. ### Typed cells, column roles, admitted inferences, and provenance pointers `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` declares these four additions inside the `HistoricalDataset` shape. This bead is their consumer: it validates them where a schema cannot see across records, and it decides what each one means on screen, in the accessible table, and at build time. It declares none of them and keeps no second copy of their vocabularies. - **`DataCell`, a typed cell.** A row's `cells[]` are the closed union `{kind: "number", value, originalToken?}`, `{kind: "missing", reason}`, and `{kind: "bound", direction: "upper" | "lower", value, originalToken?}`. The loader rejects a bare number in a `cells[]` position with a message naming the union, and rejects a row whose cell count differs from the column count, naming both counts. - **A bound is drawn as a bound.** The overlay renders a `bound` cell with the bounded marker of the view kit: an arrow or bar showing the direction, never a point and never a point with an error bar, because a bound plotted as a point is a fabricated measurement. The direction is carried by marker shape and by the accessible name, not by color alone. - **A bound is refused by a statistic that would treat it as a value.** A mean, a least-squares fit, or any estimator over a series containing a `bound` cell in the estimated column returns `not-applicable` with the reason in words ("this series contains a value the apparatus could only bound, so its mean is not defined by these rows") and names the rows involved. It is never silently dropped, never substituted by its bound, and never counted as a value. A caller that wants an estimate over the unbounded subset asks for it explicitly, and the result says how many rows were excluded and why. - **A missing cell is absent from the plot and present in the table.** It contributes no point and no interpolation, and it appears in the accessible table as its authored `reason` in ordinary language ("not reported", "plate damaged", "excluded by the author as a misreading"), never as a blank, a dash, or a zero. A row that is entirely missing still occupies a table row, so the reader can see that the source had a row there. - **The printed token survives.** Where `originalToken` is present, the evidence reveal shows it exactly as printed, including a decimal comma, beside the canonical conversion. - **`columns[].role`, a four-value vocabulary.** `observed` (the author measured it), `controlled` (the author set it), `derived` (the author computed it from the others), and `reported-fit` (a value read off a line or curve the author fitted, including a digitized fitted line). The loader accepts exactly these four, rejects the retired boolean `derived` flag with a message naming all four, and requires a `fitDescription` on any `reported-fit` column. - **A `reported-fit` column is never styled as an observation.** The overlay draws it with the historical-fitted-law styling, distinct from empirical points and from theoretical curves by marker and line style rather than color, and labels it with what was fitted and by whom. Relabeling a fitted line as an observation would turn a theory-laden summary into apparent evidence, which is the failure this role exists to prevent. - The accessible table names each column's role in its header description, so the distinction survives without the plot. - **`allowedInferenceModelIds[]`.** Each dataset declares the inference models it admits, by the owner-function ids the scenario registry uses, each with a recorded reason. The list is required and may be empty; an empty list means the dataset is for display and citation only, and an absent list fails validation, so "we have not decided" can never read as "anything goes". - **The build failure.** An instrument, scenario, or overlay that feeds a dataset into a model outside its list fails the build with `dataset-inference-not-admitted`, naming the dataset, the model, and the admitted list. This bead owns that failure and emits it wherever both records are loaded together; it is a build failure rather than a runtime refusal because the pairing is authored, not chosen by a reader. - The list is authored by each dataset bead with its physics reviewer, not by this bead, and this bead never widens it. - **Provenance pointers for independence.** `calibrationIds[]` and `sharedInputIds[]` are lists of ids in the shared-input registry owned by `am-dataset-independence-registry-3dfb`, naming the calibrations a dataset's values depend on and the inputs it shares with other datasets or with a constant set. Until that registry's records exist both lists are optional and may be empty; the loader validates them as id lists so the two records cannot be invented twice with different spellings, and reports unresolved ids as a flag rather than an error while the registry is empty. - **`digitizationRevision`** (a positive integer) joins `digitizer`, so a re-digitization from the same scan is a new revision rather than a silent overwrite. The loader rejects 0, and the evidence reveal shows the revision beside the digitizer and the analysis date. ### The evidence reveal - **The action.** Every `DatasetOverlay` and every dataset table exposes one action, "Show where this came from", which opens a four-step disclosure for the selected series, in this order: 1. **The source region.** The page locator (scan asset id, PDF page index, printed page, table or figure number) and, where rights allow, a reviewed crop of that region. 2. **The extracted values** as printed, in the printed units and printed token form (so `1,35` stays `1,35` where the source prints a comma), including a `missing` cell's reason and a `bound` cell's direction as printed. 3. **The transformation** to canonical quantities: each conversion named with its factor, each column's role flagged, the digitization revision, and the normalization factor and method where one is used. 4. **The plotted result**, with the point that corresponds to the selected row highlighted in the plot and in the table. - **Rights govern the crop, not the reveal.** A crop is rendered only when its `SourceAsset`'s publication decision is `publish`, using the vocabulary of `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`. Under `pin-local-only` or `reference-only` the first step shows the locator, the rights statement, and a durable citation with the retrieval date instead of an image, and says so in one sentence. The crop is a separate content-addressed asset under `public/figures/` whose `SourceAsset.kind` is `figure-crop`, listed in the release manifest like every other source asset; the reveal never requests a `facsimile-scan`, so it can never pull a whole-volume or whole-issue scan in order to display a table, which is also the low-bandwidth rule of the evidence-rich-page budget. - **Without JavaScript** the four steps render as a static `
` per series containing the locator, the printed values, the transformation list, and the citation. The crop, where permitted, is a plain `` with its credit. - **Accessibility.** The reveal is reachable from the table view as well as the plot, each step is a heading with its own anchor (`#dataset---step`), and the highlighted row is announced once, not per pointer move. ### Declared fits The loader validates, and the overlay renders, an optional `fits[]` block on a `HistoricalDataset`. Each entry carries: - `fitId`, `objective` (for example `ordinary-least-squares` or `weighted-least-squares`, with the weights named), `parameters[]` with their canonical quantity ids, and `parameterConstraints[]`; - `uncertaintyAssumptions`: what the fit assumes about the errors, in one sentence; - `rowsUsed[]` and `rowsExcluded[]`, where every excluded row carries `rowId`, `reason`, and `excludedBy` (a contributor id from `docs/OWNERS.md`); - `fittedBy` and `analysisDate`. Validation: - `rowsUsed` and `rowsExcluded` together must cover every row of the series exactly once; a row in neither, or in both, fails the build naming the dataset, series, and row. - An entry in `rowsExcluded` with an empty or missing `reason` fails the build. There is no unexplained exclusion. - A fit whose `parameters[]` bind a quantity id that does not resolve through `resolveQuantityId` fails exactly as a column does, with the registry's own message. - A fit over a column containing a `bound` cell in a used row fails with the same refusal the estimators give, so a bound cannot enter a least-squares sum through a fit. Rendering: - Where a fitted line is drawn, the overlay shows the fit's objective and the count of used and excluded rows beside it, and the excluded rows remain in the table, marked "not used in this fit" with their reason on request. An excluded row is never removed from the data the reader can see. - A fitted parameter is labeled "fitted here"; a parameter taken from elsewhere is labeled with its source, which is the rule that a theory's parameters are labeled as fitted here or established elsewhere. The first consumer is `am-data-millikan-1916-zh2q`, whose acceptance already recomputes a least-squares slope against Millikan's reported value and compares slopes rather than $h$: Millikan's $h/e$ from his printed $h = 6.57\times10^{-27}$ erg·s and $e = 4.774\times10^{-10}$ esu is $1.3762\times10^{-17}$ statvolt·s, which is $4.1258\times10^{-15}$ V·s against the modern exact $h/e = 4.1356677\times10^{-15}$ V·s, about 0.24 percent low. That fit must now declare its objective, its weights, and any excluded row, or the build fails. ### The three dates Every series carries three separately typed dates, none of which may stand in for another: - `observationDate` (or interval): when the measurement was made. Millikan's sodium results are "measured 1915–1916". - `publicationDate`: the date of the publication the values are taken from, which is already per-publication and already governs shelf eligibility. - `analysisDate`: when this site produced the derived quantity being shown, that is the digitization or fit date, in the `fits[]` entry and in `digitizer.date`. The overlay's label and the accessible table show the observation and publication identities; the reveal's transformation and fit steps show the analysis date and the digitization revision. A single date field used for two of these fails the build. ### Digitization pipeline (`scripts/digitize-datasets//`) The pipeline directory keeps provenance, logs, and validation, and writes the canonical record: - `source.md`: the citation, scan asset, page, and table or figure locator. - `digitization-log.md`: the method (transcription from a table, or figure digitization with axis calibration points), tool, date, operator, and the digitization revision this run produced. It includes a spot-check list of at least three rows re-read from the scan in a second pass. - `validate.test.ts`: checks the canonical record's schema, units, quantity ids through `resolveQuantityId`, row count, cell kinds, spot-check values, conversions, and CSV digest. A child's own legacy-spelling fixture (for example a Kaufmann row binding `electricField`) asserts the registry's message rather than a locally worded one. - Optional raw working files (for example axis calibration exports) may live here; they are never loaded by the site. - Pipeline artifact directories are named with ``, and any record or log event that points at such a run carries it in the validated field `toolRunId`. ### Overlay component - **Styling.** `DatasetOverlay` renders points with uncertainty bars, bounded markers for `bound` cells, and a separate digitization band where applicable. It uses the view kit's empirical-point class, distinguished from theoretical curves and from historical fitted laws (including `reported-fit` columns) by marker, line style, and label, not color alone. - **Dates.** The overlay always shows the short citation and publication year. On a view set before the 1905 cutoff (the discovery shelf stages), any later publication's data shows "later evidence, published YYYY." - **Normalization.** If an overlay requires a scale factor (for example for relative spectral intensities), the factor, its method, and its uncertainty are displayed and recorded. No hidden fitting. - **Accessibility.** A table view exposes the same plotted rows, with citations, and its headers name the column quantities through the registry's plain-word `name` and state each column's role. Missing cells appear with their reasons and bounded cells with their direction in words. ### Shelf eligibility - A shelf stage may cite only series or rows whose source publication is dated on or before the end of 1904. - Examples: - Fizeau 1851: eligible. - The 1899–1900 spectra: eligible, citing the 1900 report. - Kaufmann's 1901–1903 series: eligible; his 1906 analysis is not. - Perrin 1909 and Millikan 1916: never on the shelf. - A shelf step that cites a later series fails the compiler check; the check integrates with `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`'s shelf rules through the publication dates. ## Technical Approach - The loader produces route-local data payloads from canonical records. - The overlay consumes model curves from accepted snapshots and static dataset rows. - Cell kinds, column roles, and the admitted-model list are read through the schema's inferred types from `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`; this bead declares no union, no role list, and no second vocabulary, and a scan asserts it. - The pipeline runs under `bun test` and emits JSONL. - Browser tests use a fixture bundle served by the harness fixture server. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] The loader reads canonical records from `content/datasets/` only; a dataset present only in a pipeline directory fails the build. - [ ] The loader validates all required fields and the CSV digest; uncited datasets fail the build. - [ ] Every column id is resolved through `resolveQuantityId`: an unregistered id fails the build naming the dataset, column, and id; a recorded legacy spelling fails with the registry's `legacySpellingMessage` naming the canonical id; no alias, label, or near match is accepted in either case. - [ ] Per-publication dates are recorded, and eligibility is computed per series or row. - [ ] The pipeline template and validation harness exist and are exercised by the fixture dataset, writing its canonical record. - [ ] The overlay styles empirical points, fitted laws, and theoretical curves distinctly without relying on color; citations and years are always visible. - [ ] Later series are rejected in shelf stages and earlier ones accepted, including a dataset that spans the cutoff. - [ ] Normalization factors are displayed and recorded when used. - [ ] The table view exposes the same rows and citations. - [ ] The four schema additions are consumed correctly and declared nowhere here: a `bound` cell renders as a bounded marker with its direction and is refused by a mean or fit over that column with a named reason and the rows listed; a `missing` cell contributes no point and appears in the accessible table as its authored reason; a `reported-fit` column renders with fitted-law styling, carries its `fitDescription`, and is never styled as an observation; `allowedInferenceModelIds` is required, an absent list fails validation, an empty list validates as display-and-citation-only, and a pairing outside the list fails the build with `dataset-inference-not-admitted` naming the dataset, the model, and the list; `calibrationIds[]` and `sharedInputIds[]` validate as optional id lists; `digitizationRevision` is a positive integer shown in the reveal; and a scan finds no local declaration of the cell union, the role list, or the model-id list under `src/content/datasets/`. - [ ] Every overlay and dataset table exposes "Show where this came from" with the four ordered steps, reachable by keyboard and present as static `
` without JavaScript. - [ ] A crop renders only for a `publish` asset; a `pin-local-only` or `reference-only` asset shows the locator, the rights statement, and a durable citation instead, and the reveal never requests a `facsimile-scan`. - [ ] `rowsUsed` and `rowsExcluded` partition the series exactly; an uncovered row, a duplicated row, or an exclusion without a reason fails the build with the dataset, series, and row named. - [ ] Excluded rows stay visible in the table with their reason, and the drawn fit states its objective and its used and excluded counts. - [ ] `observationDate`, `publicationDate`, and `analysisDate` are separate fields, all three are rendered in the places named above, and a record reusing one for another fails. - [ ] A fitted parameter is labeled "fitted here" and an imported parameter names its source. ## Test Plan ### Unit and integration tests - `datasetLoader.test.ts`: required fields; quantity-id resolution against the real registry through `resolveQuantityId`; unit and dimension checks; uncertainty alignment; rights status in the policy vocabulary; a missing table number fails; a CSV whose digest differs from the record fails; a pipeline-only dataset fails. - `datasetCells.test.ts`, against the real schema from `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` and the real overlay: a fixture series carrying one `number` cell with `originalToken: "0,001"`, one `missing` cell with the reason "not reported", and one `bound` cell with `direction: "upper"` validates and renders three ways, with the bounded cell drawn as a bounded marker whose direction is in its accessible name and never as a point or a point with an error bar; a mean over the bounded column returns `not-applicable` with the reason in words and the row named, and a least-squares fit using that row fails the same way, while the same statistic over a series without bounds succeeds and an explicit unbounded-subset request reports how many rows it excluded; the `missing` cell contributes no plotted point, produces no interpolation, and appears in the accessible table as its reason rather than a blank, dash, or zero; a bare numeric cell, a `missing` cell without a reason, and a `bound` cell without a direction each fail with the union named; a row whose cell count is one short fails naming both counts; the `originalToken` survives into the reveal byte for byte, comma included; a `reported-fit` column without a `fitDescription` fails, one with it renders with fitted-law styling distinct from empirical points by marker and line style with color removed, and a fixture styling it as an observation fails the styling assertion; the four role values are accepted and the retired boolean `derived` flag is rejected with all four named; `allowedInferenceModelIds` absent fails, empty validates as display-and-citation-only, and a fixture scenario pairing the dataset with a model outside the list fails the build with `dataset-inference-not-admitted` naming dataset, model, and list, while the same pairing inside the list passes; `calibrationIds[]` and `sharedInputIds[]` validate as optional id lists and report unresolved ids as a flag while the shared-input registry is empty; `digitizationRevision: 0` fails and `2` renders in the reveal beside the digitizer; and a scan of `src/content/datasets/` finds no local cell union, role list, or model-id vocabulary. - `datasetQuantityIds.test.ts`, against the real registry and its resolver: - a fixture column binding `electricField` fails with the registry's message naming `electricFieldStationary`, and the same row passes once it binds `electricFieldStationary`; - `magneticField` and `acceleratingVoltage` fail the same way, naming `magneticFieldStationary` and `acceleratingPotential`; - a fixture speed column printed in cm/s that binds `speedRatio` fails the dimension check, while a ratio column binding `speedRatio` passes; - an invented id (`electricFieldStationry`) fails as unregistered with no near match offered; - a column binding `chargeToMassRatio` validates under each declared unit system and fails when its unit belongs to another system; - the loader contains no second list of legacy spellings: a test asserts that every legacy-spelling message the loader emits came from `legacySpellingMessage`. - `datasetShelf.test.ts`: a fixture dataset with one 1903 series and one 1906 series. A shelf stage citing the 1903 series passes; citing the 1906 series fails with a named error. A value published in both 1900 and 1901 is eligible only through the 1900 citation. - `datasetOverlay.test.tsx`: styling classes and non-color identity; citation rendering; the "later evidence, published YYYY" label on a pre-1905 view; normalization display; the table view with registry-named headers and stated column roles. - `datasetEvidenceReveal.test.tsx`: the four steps render in order with their anchors; a fixture asset with each of the three publication decisions produces the crop, the locator-only form, and the locator-only form respectively; the selected row highlights in both plot and table; the static `
` form contains the locator, printed values, transformation list, and citation. - `datasetFits.test.ts`: a fixture series of six rows with a fit using four and excluding two validates; the same fixture with one row in neither fails naming the row; with one row in both fails; with an exclusion whose `reason` is empty fails; a fit parameter binding a legacy spelling fails with the registry's `legacySpellingMessage`. - `datasetDates.test.ts`: a fixture with `observationDate` 1915-01-01 to 1916-12-31, `publicationDate` 1916, and `analysisDate` 2027-03-04 renders all three in their places; a fixture that omits `analysisDate` on a `fits[]` entry fails; a fixture whose `observationDate` is later than its `publicationDate` fails. - `datasetRevealRights.test.ts`: a static scan asserts the reveal component requests only assets whose recorded `kind` is `figure-crop`, never a `facsimile-scan`. - **Pipeline fixture:** a small, synthetic-free, three-row table transcribed from a public-domain source, chosen and cited in the fixture with its scan asset and rights recorded. It exercises the harness end to end, including the second-pass spot check, and writes its canonical record under a fixture content root. ### End-to-end tests On a fixture bundle served by the harness fixture server, with the fixture dataset over a fixture model curve: - the citation and year are visible; - the shelf-view label appears; - the table view is keyboard navigable; - a 320 px layout; - print shows the citation. On the same fixture bundle, added to the existing dataset lane: - open the reveal from the plot and again from the table; walk all four steps by keyboard; assert the highlighted row matches in both views; - with JavaScript disabled, assert the `
` form and a working citation link; - with the fixture's asset set to `reference-only`, assert no image and a visible rights statement; - at 320 px assert the crop scales and the page body does not scroll horizontally; - print the page and assert the locator and citation appear. Consumer lanes run in their own beads: the LQ-08 Millikan overlay, BM-07's Perrin data, and the Fizeau shelf instrument. ### Structured logging and retained evidence JSONL through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp` at `artifacts/test-logs/datasets/.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `datasetId`, `seriesId`, `recordPath`, `csvDigest`, `toolRunId` (when a pipeline run produced the record), `publicationDate`, `observationDate`, `analysisDate`, `digitizationRevision`, `rowCount`, `cellKinds` (counts per kind), `columnRoles`, `allowedInferenceModelCount`, `inferenceAdmitted`, `quantityIds`, `quantityIdResolution` (`registered`, `legacy-spelling`, or `unregistered`, per column), `units`, `validationErrors`, `shelfEligible`, `normalizationFactor`, `revealStep`, `cropRendered`, `assetPublicationDecision`, `fitId`, `fitObjective`, `rowsUsedCount`, `rowsExcludedCount`, `exclusionReasonsPresent`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `evidence`, and `message`. Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log through the harness evidence recorder, named by the log line's `evidence` field; a failing pipeline validation retains its digitization log and the differing values; a failing reveal test retains the rendered markup, the requested asset ids, and the rights statement it read; a failing `dataset-inference-not-admitted` case retains the dataset id, the model id, and the admitted list. ## Considerations and Pitfalls - Digitizing from figures adds uncertainty that must not be confused with the original measurement uncertainty. - A reanalysis is a separate cited source, never silently merged into the historical values. - A single dataset-level date would wrongly bar pre-cutoff series or admit post-cutoff ones; keep dates per publication. - Two copies of the data (one in the pipeline, one in content) drift; the canonical record is the only copy the site reads, and its CSV digest ties it to the validation run. - A dataset that invents a column quantity id would create a second naming authority; the registry adds the id first, and the resolver is the only judge of whether an id is registered, legacy, or unknown. - An unframed field id would lose exactly the distinction paper 3 §6 is about, which is why the registry records `electricField` and `magneticField` as legacy spellings rather than as usable ids. - A crop is a scan, so it carries the scanning institution's terms. Publishing one to make the reveal prettier is a rights decision, not a design decision. - An exclusion list invites tuning. The reason field exists so that "removed to improve the fit" has to be written down; a reviewer reading `rowsExcluded` should be able to decide whether the exclusion was principled. - Do not let `analysisDate` drift into the citation. A reader comparing historical results needs the observation and publication dates; the analysis date belongs to the site's own work and is the one date a future correction will change. - The reveal is for one series at a time. A reveal that opens for a whole dataset will show transformations that do not apply to the row the reader asked about. - A typed bound that the plot draws as a point has bought nothing. The type exists so the picture and the statistic both behave differently, which is why the refusal and the marker are specified together. - Dropping a bounded row from a mean is as dishonest as averaging it in: both answer a question the data cannot answer while looking like they answered the original one. Refuse, name the rows, and let the caller ask a narrower question. - A blank cell is not a zero and not a small number. Rendering it as either invents a measurement, and rendering it as nothing at all hides that the source had a row there. - `reported-fit` is the role most likely to be mislabeled, because a digitized fitted line looks exactly like a series of points. The `fitDescription` requirement is what makes the author say out loud what was fitted. - An empty `allowedInferenceModelIds` is a real decision and must stay distinguishable from a missing one. The first says "cite this, do not infer from it"; the second says nobody has thought about it yet. ## Dependencies Blocked by: - `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`: the `HistoricalDataset` schema, including the `DataCell` union, the four `columns[].role` values, `allowedInferenceModelIds[]`, `calibrationIds[]`, `sharedInputIds[]`, `digitizationRevision`, the `fits[]` shape and the three date fields, which land in the same change as this bead's validation of them. - `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`: plot classes, the bounded marker, legends, and table hooks. - `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`: the rights vocabulary recorded for each scan asset and for the reveal's crop decision. The quantity registry (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`) arrives transitively through the view kit; it owns every column and fit-parameter quantity id this bead validates against, the `resolveQuantityId` resolver and `legacySpellingMessage` this loader calls, and the legacy-spelling records they report. Unblocks: `am-dataset-independence-registry-3dfb` (which owns the shared-input registry this bead's `calibrationIds[]` and `sharedInputIds[]` point into); `am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`, `am-data-bancelin-1911-94um`, `am-data-millikan-1916-zh2q`, `am-data-blackbody-1899-1900-1193`, `am-data-kaufmann-1902-1906-52ya`, `am-data-bucherer-1908-w3mf`, `am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp`, `am-data-fizeau-1851-tgl8`. Each child follows this loader's pipeline layout, its column-resolution rule, its cell-kind rules, and its fit-declaration rule, and none re-implements the checks.
