# Later and unscheduled: the 1906 Brownian follow-up, the 1907 review, printable broadsides, community translations

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P4 · **Labels:** companion-dissertation, later · **Plan sections:** §3.7, §19.7 "Later, unscheduled" (traceability only)

## Background

The plan closes its delivery section with work it deliberately leaves unscheduled: "the 1906 Brownian follow-up and the 1907 review article as further companion records; a printable broadside per paper; community translations of the readings against the same alignment." These extend the edition without changing its identity. The molecular-dimensions dissertation establishes the companion pattern first (`am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`): a companion is labeled as such, never appears on the hero, never becomes a flagship by accretion, and never delays the four papers.

**Why later:** each item depends on patterns proven by the launch (companion records, print styles, review records, the license decision). **Start only when all of these hold:**

1. the dissertation companion record exists and has been reviewed;
2. the four-paper edition has launched (`am-launch-public-release-5nkq`);
3. for broadsides, the print policy and styles have shipped (`am-plat-print-3orn`); for community translations, the license decision is recorded (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`) and review capacity exists (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`);
4. the user chooses one item and the choice is recorded here.

This bead is a **holding record**. It writes no code and ships nothing. When an item starts, it is split into its own bead with a full specification, and this bead records that bead's id.

## Scope

In scope: specifying the three items well enough to split each into a complete bead later, and recording the split beads' ids.

Out of scope: starting any item without the conditions above; adding a fifth flagship; changing the four-paper framing.

## Requirements

**1. Further companion records.**

- The 1906 Brownian follow-up, "Zur Theorie der Brownschen Bewegung," *Ann. Phys.* (4) **19**, 371–381 (1906), which among other things discusses the apparent velocity measured over an observation interval. It is the natural home for that discussion, and the "not a mean velocity" warning is attributed to Einstein 1906 unless the 1905 facsimile shows it.
- The 1907 review, "Über das Relativitätsprinzip und die aus demselben gezogenen Folgerungen," *Jahrbuch der Radioaktivität und Elektronik* **4**, 411–462 (1907), with Einstein's 1908 corrections (expected in *Jahrbuch* **5**, 98–99).
- **Every bibliographic detail above is unverified planning data. Verify volume, pages, year, and title against a pinned facsimile before any of it is published**, and record the verification in the record's provenance receipt.
- Each record follows the same source pipeline as the four papers: rights check and `publicationDecision`, pinned facsimile with SHA-256, provenance receipt, bounded cloud OCR only (never local OCR), a hand-corrected diplomatic ledger, a translation made from the German, many-to-many alignment, a human-gated German source review, a physics review, and the companion label. Scope each record to what readers need, as the dissertation is scoped to the Avogadro lab.

**2. Printable broadsides.**

- One printable sheet per paper, built fresh from the edition and the design system: the printed German title, the author line, the date-line, the working English title, the paper's central result as printed with its modern reading, an R0 summary, and the site URL as text.
- The donor's broadside printing is on the do-not-port list, and the project forbids theater, so this is new work with no QR codes, no invented metrics, and no completeness percentage.
- It uses the print stylesheet and page-break rules of `am-plat-print-3orn` rather than a second print system, keeps a real text layer and an accessible reading order, is tested at A4 and US Letter, and stays intelligible in monochrome through the non-color cues of `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`.
- Copy is reviewed under the editorial voice rules (no em dashes, no hype words, no "obviously").

**3. Community translations of the readings.**

- A contribution workflow through the public repository (pull requests), aligned to the same explanation record ids, with no accounts on the site.
- Contributions carry attribution and the license chosen in `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`; the site shows them only after review, labeled "community translation, reviewed by <name>"; unreviewed contributions never appear in a public build.
- Language metadata, direction, and right-to-left rules come from `am-later-language-editions-sp4e`; this item adds no second localization mechanism.
- Review load is the limit: do not open contributions before review capacity exists in `am-edit-review-records-hofz`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The start conditions and the user's choice of item are recorded here before any work begins.
- [ ] When an item starts, a dedicated bead is created with a full specification (background, requirements, acceptance criteria, unit tests, end-to-end lanes, structured logging, dependencies), and this bead records its id.
- [ ] Each companion record carries the companion label, cites verified bibliographic details from its pinned facsimile, and passes the same source and review gates as the four papers.
- [ ] Broadsides contain no QR codes or invented metrics and pass the print and accessibility checks at A4 and US Letter.
- [ ] Community translations appear only after named review, and an unreviewed unit is excluded from a public build by a compiler check.
- [ ] Nothing in this bead delayed or displaced core work, and no split bead became a dependency of a launch bead.

## Test Plan

This bead ships nothing, so it has no code of its own to test. Two things are still tested:

### Unit and integration tests

- **This bead's own check:** a governance test in the later epic's audit asserts that every item marked started here names an existing split bead id, and that no split bead is a dependency of `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`, `am-launch-final-product-test-nzhn`, or `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`.
- **Required of each split bead, at minimum:** compiler checks for companion labeling and review state; print-style snapshot tests for broadsides at A4 and US Letter; a check that unreviewed community units are excluded from public builds; and for a companion record, the same ledger, alignment, and receipt tests the four papers use.

### End-to-end tests

Specified in each split bead: companion routes and their labels; a print lane for broadsides including monochrome; a contribution-to-publication path test for community translations; and the standard lanes (320 px, keyboard only, reduced motion, JavaScript disabled) for any reader-facing surface.

### Structured logging

Each split bead writes one JSON line per check to `artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with the standard fields (`timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`) and its own bead-specific fields. Pipeline runs (OCR dispatch, digitization, review packets) name their artifact directories with `<tool-run-id>` and are referenced from records and log events as `toolRunId`. Failures retain their evidence, which is never deleted.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A companion must never crowd the hero or the four-paper framing. The catalogue shows four papers and records labeled "companion".
- Community work multiplies review load; do not open contributions before review capacity exists.
- Do not let a 1906 or 1907 record become the home for a claim the 1905 papers should carry. A companion explains context; it never substitutes for a missing core section.
- Bibliographic details in this bead are planning data. Publishing an unverified citation would break the rule that every numerical or bibliographic claim traces to a pinned source.
- Splitting this bead is the only way to start an item. Do not grow this bead into an implementation.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:

- `am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`: the companion pattern is proven on the dissertation first.
- `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`: nothing here starts before the four-paper edition is public.
- `am-ep-later-gap` (parent): later work that must never displace the core.

Reached transitively, and named above where this bead relies on them: `am-plat-print-3orn` (broadside print styles), `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (review records and capacity), `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps` (the license for contributed text), and `am-later-language-editions-sp4e` (language metadata and direction rules).

Unblocks: none.

title: Optional deep dive: optical appearance versus coordinate geometry
description:
# Optional deep dive: optical appearance versus coordinate geometry

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P3 · **Labels:** later, paper-relativity · **Plan sections:** §5.3, §7.6 (paper 3 misconceptions), §8.3, §10.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Special relativity's length contraction is a statement about measurements that use frame-simultaneous endpoint events. What a camera or an eye records at one instant is different: light arriving together was emitted at different times from different parts of the object. The plan's anachronism controls require separating "simultaneous-coordinate measurement from received light and optical appearance," and the paper 3 misconception ledger lists both "length contraction is an optical illusion" and "the rod is physically squashed." The optional modern deep dives include "optical appearance versus coordinate geometry." The classic analyses are later work (Penrose showed a sphere's outline stays circular; Terrell showed small objects appear rotated rather than contracted, both 1959), so this is a labeled later lens, never part of the 1905 route.

**Why later:** the core rod-measurement instrument (`am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`) must first teach the operational meaning of a length measurement, and `src/physics/reference/events.ts` must already own the event ledger and the measurement procedures this dive contrasts with. **Start only when all of these hold:**

1. SR-03 has shipped with its coordinate-measurement caption and its action contract;
2. `am-dod-relativity-105y` records the relativity paper as meeting its definition of done, or records that the audit is complete without this dive;
3. `am-ref-waves-r53` is closed, so the aberration formula this dive checks against is audited;
4. a reader need connected to the two misconception entries is recorded in this bead.

## Scope

In scope: a 2D instrument mode comparing a coordinate snapshot with an optical image for a moving object, the emission-time solver, the labels, the fixtures, and the tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: color and brightness rendering beyond an optional, clearly labeled Doppler shading; 3D rendering unless 2D demonstrably loses information (the spacetime block view is `am-later-deep-spacetime-block-7dai`); the event ledger, the synchronization procedure, and rod measurement (`am-ref-events-yvl`, used by `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`); the Doppler and aberration formulas (`am-ref-waves-r53`); the misconception ledger's text (the paper 3 misconceptions bead).

## Requirements

1. **Two views of one world.** The same accepted snapshot of worldlines drives both pictures:
   - the **coordinate picture**: endpoint events simultaneous in the chosen frame, exactly as SR-03 defines a length measurement;
   - the **optical picture**: for an observer at $\mathbf{x}_o$ receiving light at time $t_o$, each object point appears at its retarded position $\mathbf{x}(t_e)$, where $|\mathbf{x}_o - \mathbf{x}(t_e)| = c\,(t_o - t_e)$ with $t_e < t_o$.
2. **Emission-time solver.** Closed form for uniform straight-line motion (solve the quadratic in $t_e$ and take the retarded root), with a checked high-precision numeric fallback. A geometry with no retarded root returns a typed `outside-domain` result with a readable reason, never a clamp or a `NaN`.
3. **Camera choices and command classes.** A camera at rest in the frame where the object moves, and a camera co-moving with the object. Choosing which camera records the image is a `measurement-change` (a different observation model over the same latent worldlines); re-describing the same world in another frame is an `observer-change`. Neither creates events, changes event ids, consumes randomness, or starts a new run.
4. **Fixtures** (each an assertion, not an illustration):
   - a sphere's apparent outline remains circular (Penrose 1959);
   - a small object at closest approach has an image corresponding to a rotation rather than a contraction (Terrell 1959); at $\beta = 0.6$ the apparent rotation is $\arcsin\beta = 36.87^\circ$, with the convention stated;
   - a rod approaching along the line of sight appears stretched, and a receding rod appears shortened, by light-travel-time effects;
   - every image-direction result agrees with the aberration formula in `waves.ts`, $\cos\theta' = (\cos\theta - \beta)/(1 - \beta\cos\theta)$; at $\theta = 90^\circ$ and $\beta = 0.6$ this gives $\cos\theta' = -0.6$, that is $\theta' = 126.87^\circ$.
5. **Labels.** "Later lens: Penrose and Terrell (1959)" (verify the exact citations against the papers before publishing them: Penrose, *Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.* **55**, 137 (1959); Terrell, *Phys. Rev.* **116**, 1041 (1959)). A plain statement that the coordinate picture is what "contraction" refers to and the optical picture is what a camera records. Links to both misconception entries and to the §4 source passage on the sphere measured as an ellipsoid.
6. **Instrument contract.** Action contract (choose named object points and read emission times and apparent positions in a table, and compare two named points), `notModeled` (finite exposure time, lens optics, brightness and color unless the labeled shading is on, diffraction, gravitational effects, non-inertial motion), predict mode or a recorded exemption, show-the-code with pinned hashes, tape identity, permalink, 320 px, keyboard, reduced motion, and a static worked case without JavaScript.
7. **Identity.** If it ships as a mode of SR-03, it is declared in SR-03's manifest as `sr-03:optical-appearance` with `historicalStatus: later-development`; if it ships as its own small laboratory, it takes an instrument id from the registry's grammar. Either way it is declared before use: no undeclared colon id ever appears.

## Technical Approach

Add `retardedEmissionTime` and `apparentPositions` to `src/physics/reference/events.ts`, owned by `am-ref-events-yvl`, following that module's conventions, tolerances, and tests; reuse its event and frame model and the transforms in `kinematics.ts` rather than writing a second transform. If no dependency path from this bead to `am-ref-events-yvl` exists when the work starts, add that edge before authoring. Render both pictures side by side at one shared scale with explicit units (light-seconds where helpful).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The start conditions, including the recorded reader need, are in this bead before work begins.
- [ ] The solver and every fixture pass, including the sphere outline, the Terrell rotation angle, and aberration consistency.
- [ ] The coordinate and optical pictures consume one accepted snapshot; switching cameras or frames preserves `runId`, event ids, and worldlines.
- [ ] Labels separate measurement from appearance, date the later lens, and link both misconceptions and the §4 passage.
- [ ] A no-retarded-root geometry returns `outside-domain` with a readable reason.
- [ ] The nonvisual table gives every value the pictures show.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

Against the real reference module; no mocked solver.

- **Emission-time solver:** closed form versus a high-precision numeric root finder at several speeds, directions, and observer distances, agreeing within a relative $10^{-12}$ through `withinTolerance` from `src/units/tolerance.ts`; refusal cases; the symmetry that a source at rest gives $t_e = t_o - |\mathbf{x}_o - \mathbf{x}|/c$.
- **Sphere outline:** sample outline points, fit a circle, and require the residual below a stated tolerance for several speeds and directions.
- **Terrell rotation:** for a small object at closest approach at $\beta = 0.6$, the apparent orientation matches $\arcsin 0.6 = 36.8699^\circ$ within a stated tolerance, with the convention recorded in the test.
- **Aberration:** apparent directions computed from retarded positions equal the `waves.ts` formula within $10^{-12}$ radians for uniform motion, including the $\theta = 90^\circ$, $\beta = 0.6$ case ($\theta' = 126.8699^\circ$).
- **Identity:** an observer change and a camera change each leave `runId`, event ids, and worldlines identical, compared before and after.

### End-to-end tests

Browser lane through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: toggle between the coordinate and optical views at $\beta = 0.6$; read the table of emission times and apparent positions with the keyboard; confirm the later-lens label, the misconception links, and the source-passage link; confirm both pictures share one scale; run the no-WebGL, reduced-motion, 320 px, and JavaScript-disabled static-fallback lanes. Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot, accessibility-tree snapshot, console log, and the snapshot JSON.

### Structured logging

One JSON line per check at `artifacts/test-logs/deep-optical/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with the standard fields (`timestamp`, `suite` `deep-optical`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper: special-relativity`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `message`) and the bead-specific fields `beta`, `camera`, `pointId`, `emissionTime`, `apparentX`, `apparentY`, `apparentAngleDeg`, and `refusalCode`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The deep dive must strengthen, not blur, the core distinction: never describe contraction itself as "what you see," and never let the optical picture appear on the 1905 source route as though it were the paper's content.
- Keep scales identical across both pictures, or readers will attribute a zoom to physics.
- Terrell's result is about small objects subtending a small angle; do not generalize it to an extended scene, and say so in the caption.
- Penrose's circular outline is about the outline, not about the surface markings, which do shift; the caption says which.
- The optical picture is a model of light arrival, not a photograph: finite exposure, optics, and brightness are in `notModeled`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:

- `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`: the coordinate measurement this dive contrasts with must already be taught, with its own action contract and caption.
- `am-ref-waves-r53`: the audited aberration, Doppler, and light-complex formulas the fixtures check against.
- `am-dod-relativity-105y`: the paper's definition of done comes first, so optional work never substitutes for a core row.
- `am-ep-later-gap` (parent): later work that must never displace the core.

Named above where this bead extends it: `am-ref-events-yvl`, which owns `src/physics/reference/events.ts`. Add that edge before authoring if no dependency path exists then.

Unblocks: none.

title: Optional deep dive: spacetime block view, rapidity, four-momentum, and later confirmations
description:
# Optional deep dive: spacetime block view, rapidity, four-momentum, and later confirmations

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P3 · **Labels:** later, paper-relativity · **Plan sections:** §8.3, §8.4, §9.4, §10.2, §10.9, §13.2 (traceability only)

## Background

The 1905 relativity paper derives its results without spacetime diagrams, rapidity, or four-vectors; those are later aids (Minkowski 1908 for the geometry; Thomas 1926 and Wigner 1939 for the rotation in non-collinear boost composition). The plan keeps the source route free of them but lists as optional modern deep dives "rapidity and non-collinear boost composition, four-momentum, and later experimental confirmations," and names "an optional spacetime block view (later)" as one of the few places Three.js may be justified. Spacetime diagrams must use coherent axis scaling so light cones sit at 45 degrees, and a camera zoom must never imply changed physics.

**Why later:** the core kinematics instruments (SR-04's constructed map, with rapidity only as a labeled aid, and SR-06 velocity composition) and the mass–energy ledger must ship first. **Start only when all of these hold:**

1. `am-sr-06-velocity-composition-7ni4` has shipped, including its non-collinear rotation, so this dive extends a tested composition rather than inventing one;
2. `am-dod-relativity-105y` and `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2` record both papers as meeting their definitions of done;
3. `am-inst-three-studio-y0y0` exists with disposal, context-loss handling, and the no-WebGL fallback;
4. `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-disc-timeline-xzef`, and `am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp` are in place, so the four-momentum extension, the confirmation cards, and the dataset overlay have their homes;
5. a reader need is recorded in this bead.

## Scope

In scope: a 2+1D spacetime block view, a rapidity panel, non-collinear composition with the Thomas–Wigner rotation, a four-momentum ledger extension, and a gallery of dated later confirmations linked to the timeline.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: general relativity of any kind; replacing or re-deriving any source-route result; the core composition instrument (`am-sr-06-velocity-composition-7ni4`); the 1905 two-ledger argument (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`); the studio framework (`am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`); timeline card records (`am-disc-timeline-xzef`); dataset digitization (`am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp`, `am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`); inventing or digitizing data without citations.

## Requirements

1. **Spacetime block view.** Worldlines and events from the event ledger rendered in a 2+1D block with light cones at 45 degrees in consistent units (light-seconds and seconds). Changing the observer frame is an `observer-change`: it re-describes the same events and never alters event ids, worldlines, `runId`, or draw counters. Camera controls are `presentation-change` only. A 2D diagram is the fallback without WebGL, and the same events are inspectable in a table.
2. **Rapidity.** $\phi = \operatorname{artanh}\beta$, $\gamma = \cosh\phi$, $\gamma\beta = \sinh\phi$. Collinear boosts compose by adding rapidities: $0.6c$ then $0.6c$ gives $\tanh(2\operatorname{artanh}0.6) = 15/17 = 0.882353$, with $\gamma(0.6) = 1.25$. Labeled a later aid, never used to derive a source-route result.
3. **Non-collinear composition.** Compose two boosts in different directions as full $4\times4$ Lorentz matrices and decompose the product into a pure boost times a spatial rotation. Display the rotation angle and axis, and never force the result into a pure boost with parallel axes. For two perpendicular boosts of $\beta = 0.6$ each, the stated-convention closed form $\tan\theta_W = \gamma_1\gamma_2\beta_1\beta_2/(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)$ gives $\tan\theta_W = 0.225$, that is $\theta_W = 12.68^\circ$; the test computes the angle from the matrix decomposition and uses the closed form only as a cross-check, with the boost order and frame convention recorded beside it. Labeled with Thomas (1926) and Wigner (1939).
4. **Four-momentum ledger.** $p^\mu = (E/c, \mathbf{p})$, invariant mass $M^2c^4 = E^2 - |\mathbf{p}|^2c^2$. Fixtures: one pulse of energy $L$ has invariant mass 0; two collinear pulses of $L/2$ each have total $E = L$, $|\mathbf{p}| = L/c$, invariant mass 0; two opposite pulses of $L/2$ each have $E = L$, $\mathbf{p} = 0$, and invariant mass $L/c^2$, which belongs to the system and not to either pulse (for $L = 1$ J that is $1.1126501\times10^{-17}$ kg). Labeled a modern formalism with a distinct model identity from the 1905 two-ledger argument, which never initializes a body's energy with $Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$.
5. **Later confirmations.** Dated cards for Ives–Stilwell (1938), muon lifetime measurements (Rossi and Hall, 1941), flown atomic clocks (Hafele–Keating, 1971), and satellite clock corrections, each with a full citation, linked to `/timeline`, and clearly outside the 1904 shelf. **Each card that involves gravity separates the contributions**: the flown-clock and satellite results combine a special-relativistic term with a gravitational term that this site does not model, and the card says so and stops, rather than presenting the total as a test of the 1905 kinematics. Data overlays come only from typed, cited `HistoricalDataset` records (for example `content/datasets/ives-stilwell-1938.yaml`); no manufactured points and no digitization without a citation.
6. **Instrument contract.** Action contracts (select events and frames from tables; enter boost components and read the decomposition), `notModeled` (gravity, curved spacetime, accelerated frames beyond instantaneous rest frames, quantum effects, finite object extent in the block), predict mode or a recorded exemption, show-the-code with pinned hashes, tape identity, permalink, 320 px, keyboard, reduced motion, and a static worked case without JavaScript.
7. **Resources.** WebGL contexts, geometries, textures, programs, and listeners are reported through the single test-build lifecycle diagnostics entry `src/experiments/lifecycle/diagnostics.ts` (`am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`); this bead adds no second registry.

## Technical Approach

Extend `src/physics/reference/kinematics.ts` with rapidity helpers, full $4\times4$ boost construction, and a numerically stable decomposition into boost and rotation; add a four-momentum section beside the mass–energy ledger in `src/physics/reference/massEnergy.ts` with its own model identity; build the block view on the adapted Three.js studio with procedural geometry that follows accepted snapshots. No physics runs in a render loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The start conditions, including the recorded reader need, are in this bead before work begins.
- [ ] Rapidity, composition, decomposition, and four-momentum fixtures pass, including $15/17$ and the perpendicular-boost rotation angle with its convention.
- [ ] Observer changes in the block view preserve event ids, worldlines, and `runId`; camera changes change no scientific digest.
- [ ] Every element carries its later-aid label and date; confirmation cards carry citations, and every gravity-involving card separates the contributions and says what is not modeled.
- [ ] No-WebGL and reduced-motion paths show a 2D diagram and the current state, with the same inspectable table.
- [ ] Repeated mount and unmount leaves WebGL contexts, geometries, textures, and listeners flat, counted through the single diagnostics entry.
- [ ] Nothing in this dive appears on a 1905 source route or inside a historical derivation chain.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

Against the real reference modules; no mocked matrices.

- **Rapidity:** additivity for collinear boosts (the $15/17$ fixture to a relative $10^{-12}$); $\gamma = \cosh\phi$ and $\gamma\beta = \sinh\phi$ at several speeds; $\beta \to 1$ handled as `outside-domain` rather than overflow.
- **Matrix identities:** $\det\Lambda = 1$ and $\Lambda^{\mathsf{T}}\eta\Lambda = \eta$ within $10^{-12}$ for every constructed boost and for composed products.
- **Non-collinear composition:** the product equals (pure boost) times (rotation) within $10^{-12}$; the rotation angle for perpendicular boosts matches the closed-form cross-check with the stated convention; the rotation is the identity for collinear boosts; tiny boosts ($\beta = 10^{-8}$) decompose stably, since the decomposition is ill-conditioned near the identity.
- **Four-momentum:** all three pulse fixtures, including the invariant mass $L/c^2$ for two opposite pulses, compared through `withinTolerance`; a fixture asserting that no ledger initializes a body energy with $Mc^2$.
- **Identity:** an observer change leaves event ids, worldlines, and `runId` unchanged.
- **Cards:** a seeded confirmation card that omits the gravitational-contribution statement fails the label check; a card citing an undigitized dataset fails.

### End-to-end tests

Chromium and WebKit lanes through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: rotate the block (presentation only, no digest change); change frame (world unchanged, event ids identical); read an event table with the keyboard; verify 45-degree light cones by measuring rendered slopes in scene units; open a confirmation card and follow its timeline link; force `WEBGL_lose_context` and assert the 2D fallback and the unchanged `runId` on restore; confirm no growth in context count after repeated route changes; run the reduced-motion, no-WebGL, 320 px, and JavaScript-disabled lanes. Failures retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, accessibility-tree snapshot, console log, and the snapshot JSON.

### Structured logging

One JSON line per check at `artifacts/test-logs/deep-spacetime/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with the standard fields (`timestamp`, `suite` `deep-spacetime`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `message`) and the bead-specific fields `case`, `boosts`, `rapidity`, `rotationAngleDeg`, `rotationAxis`, `invariantMass`, `eventIds`, `webglContexts`, `geometries`, `textures`, `listeners`, and `datasetId`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The block view is seductive; it must never appear on the 1905 source route as though it were the paper's presentation, and it never becomes a prerequisite for understanding §§1–5.
- Numerical decomposition near the identity is ill-conditioned; use stable algorithms and test tiny boosts.
- Rapidity makes composition look trivial; the site still shows the printed composition law, because the reader's obstacle is the law, not its parameterization.
- A confirmation is not a premise. These experiments postdate 1905 and never enter the 1904 shelf or a historical derivation chain.
- Flown-clock and satellite results mix special-relativistic and gravitational terms. Presenting the total as a test of the 1905 kinematics would be dishonest; say what each card does and does not establish.
- Keep the camera out of the physics: a zoom is presentation, and the scale bar says so.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:

- `am-sr-06-velocity-composition-7ni4`: the core composition instrument and its non-collinear tests come first.
- `am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`: the block view uses the adapted studio with disposal, context-loss handling, and fallbacks.
- `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`: the four-momentum extension sits beside the 1905 ledger and must not be confused with it.
- `am-disc-timeline-xzef`: the confirmation cards are typed, dated timeline cards.
- `am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp`: the only admitted data overlay for the transverse-Doppler card.
- `am-dod-relativity-105y` and `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`: both papers meet their definitions of done before this optional dive starts.
- `am-ep-later-gap` (parent): later work that must never displace the core.

Reached transitively, and named above where this bead relies on them: `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws` (the single diagnostics entry), `am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`, and `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`.

title: Optional deep dive: underdamped Brownian motion and the ballistic crossover

# Optional deep dive: underdamped Brownian motion and the ballistic crossover

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P3 · **Labels:** later, paper-brownian · **Plan sections:** §3.9 (paper 2 margin item d), §5.3, §8.2, §10.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Einstein's 1905 argument assumes the observation interval $\tau$ is long compared with the time over which a particle forgets its velocity. For shorter intervals the motion is ballistic, $\langle x^2\rangle \propto t^2$, a regime measured in gas in 2010 (Li et al., *Science* **328**, 1673) and in liquid in 2011 (Huang et al., *Nature Physics* **7**, 576); verify both citations against the papers before publishing them in the margin. The plan allows "an underdamped Langevin extension (labeled 1908)" to "illustrate the ballistic-to-diffusive crossover at $m/(6\pi\eta a)$, about $10^{-7}$ s for a micron particle," while the historian's margin notes the late measurement; "it is not required before the core paper ships." It is one of the optional modern deep dives that "follow the core and never substitute for a missing core row." Langevin's 1908 equation is a modern lens relative to the 1905 paper and is never presented as Einstein's derivation.

**Why later:** the core Brownian paper, its eight instruments, and its honest inference come first. **Start only when all of these hold:**

1. `am-dod-brownian-2k4y` records the Brownian paper as meeting its definition of done;
2. `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` has frozen the runtime and instrument abstractions, so a later mode does not reopen them;
3. `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` is closed, so this extends an audited evaluator rather than a moving one;
4. a reader need or an editorial decision for the deep dive is recorded in this bead before work begins.

## Scope

In scope: an analytic and stochastic underdamped model, a labeled later-lens mode of the tracer instrument, the historian's-margin link, fixtures, and tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: hydrodynamic memory and added-mass effects (declared in `notModeled`); any change to the default behavior of BM-01 through BM-08; the core diffusion laws (`am-ref-diffusion-lr3`); the mode-id grammar (`am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`) and the `ExperimentMode` schema (`am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`); stream allocation bookkeeping (`am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`); the margin record's editorial text (`am-bm-margin-entries-7fa4`).

## Requirements

### Model (Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, per coordinate)

$m\,dv = -\zeta v\,dt + \sqrt{2\zeta k_BT}\,dW$ with $\zeta = 6\pi\eta a$, momentum relaxation time $\tau_p = m/\zeta$, stationary velocity variance $s^2 = k_BT/m$, and $D = k_BT/\zeta = s^2\tau_p$. For a particle whose initial velocity is drawn from the thermal distribution, the one-dimensional mean-square displacement is

$$\langle \Delta x^2(t)\rangle = 2D\left[t - \tau_p\left(1 - e^{-t/\tau_p}\right)\right],$$

with limits $\langle \Delta x^2\rangle \to (k_BT/m)\,t^2$ for $t \ll \tau_p$ and $\to 2D(t - \tau_p) \to 2Dt$ for $t \gg \tau_p$.

### Controls

Each with dimension, display unit, model domain, numerical domain, pedagogical default, and mapping: radius $a$ (0.1–5 μm), particle density $\rho_p$ as an explicit input (for example silica about 2000 kg/m³, polystyrene about 1050 kg/m³), viscosity $\eta$ (0.5–20 mPa·s), temperature $T$ (273–330 K), and a logarithmic time axis spanning at least $10^{-9}$ to $1$ s. Mass is derived: $m = \rho_p \tfrac{4}{3}\pi a^3$. Temperature never silently supplies a viscosity law; $\eta$ stays an explicit parameter, as in BM-01.

### Fixture (recomputed for this revision)

With $a = 0.5$ μm, $\rho_p = 2000$ kg/m³, $\eta = 1.000$ mPa·s, $T = 293.15$ K, and $k_B = 1.380649\times10^{-23}$ J/K:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| $m = \rho_p\frac{4}{3}\pi a^3$ | $1.047198\times10^{-15}$ kg |
| $\zeta = 6\pi\eta a$ | $9.424778\times10^{-9}$ kg/s |
| $\tau_p = m/\zeta$ | $1.111111\times10^{-7}$ s |
| $D = k_BT/\zeta$ | $4.294396\times10^{-13}$ m²/s (0.4294 μm²/s) |
| thermal speed $\sqrt{k_BT/m}$ | $1.965949\times10^{-3}$ m/s |
| $\langle\Delta x^2\rangle$ at $t = 1$ ns | $3.853387\times10^{-24}$ m², against the ballistic form $(k_BT/m)t^2 = 3.865\times10^{-24}$ m² (0.3 percent below, as the series predicts) |
| $\langle\Delta x^2\rangle$ at $t = \tau_p$ | $2D\tau_p e^{-1} = 3.510711\times10^{-20}$ m² (RMS 0.187 nm) |
| RMS at $t = 1$ s | $9.2676\times10^{-7}$ m |

$\tau_p \approx 1.1\times10^{-7}$ s matches the plan's "about $10^{-7}$ s for a micron particle". The 1 s RMS differs from Einstein's printed 0.795 μm because his inputs are $T = 290.15$ K and $\eta = 1.35\times10^{-2}$ poise (1.35 mPa·s); the mode states its own inputs and never relabels one number as the other.

### Stochastic sampler

Exact discretization of the OU pair $(x, v)$ over each step, never Euler. With $\theta = \Delta t/\tau_p$ and $s^2 = k_BT/m$, conditional on $(x_n, v_n)$:

- means: $\mathbb{E}[v_{n+1}] = v_n e^{-\theta}$, $\mathbb{E}[x_{n+1}] = x_n + \tau_p v_n (1 - e^{-\theta})$;
- $\operatorname{Var}(v_{n+1}) = s^2\left(1 - e^{-2\theta}\right)$;
- $\operatorname{Var}(x_{n+1}) = s^2\tau_p^2\left(2\theta - 3 + 4e^{-\theta} - e^{-2\theta}\right)$, which expands to $\tfrac{2}{3}s^2\tau_p^2\theta^3$ for small $\theta$;
- $\operatorname{Cov}(x_{n+1}, v_{n+1}) = s^2\tau_p\left(1 - e^{-\theta}\right)^2$.

Adding the contribution of a thermally drawn $v_0$ reproduces the analytic MSD above, and a unit test asserts that identity symbolically at several $\theta$.

Draws use logical Philox streams per particle. **This mode's draw pattern differs from BM-01's three-axis latent path, so it registers its own allocation in `docs/STREAM_ALLOCATION.md` and `allocation.ts` (`am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`)** rather than reusing BM-01's tile scheme. Render cadence never changes draws; a display subsample consumes none; common random numbers are never called independent trials.

### Outputs, labels, and contract

- MSD curve with both asymptotes drawn and labeled, a crossover marker at $\tau_p$, and typed statuses: `value` inside the model, `outside-domain` with a readable reason outside it (for example a requested time far below the fluid's own momentum-transfer scale, where the neglected hydrodynamic memory dominates).
- **Labels:** "Later lens: Langevin (1908)". The margin states the 2010 and 2011 measurements with citations and dates, and links the 1905 source passage about the observation interval.
- **`notModeled`:** hydrodynamic memory (the Basset history force) and added mass, which dominate the measured crossover in liquids (Huang et al. 2011), so the OU curve is a teaching model of the crossover and not a prediction of that measurement; near-wall hindrance; non-spherical particles; polydispersity; active motion; compressibility of the fluid.
- **Mode id:** `bm-01:underdamped`, declared in BM-01's manifest as an `ExperimentMode` with `historicalStatus: later-development` and a lens label, following the id grammar of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` (a colon id only for a declared mode). It has its own model identity and tape identity.
- Standard instrument contract: action contract (enter a time and read MSD, both asymptotes, and the ratio; compare two named times), predict mode or a recorded exemption, show-the-code with pinned hashes, permalink tape, 320 px, keyboard, reduced motion, and a static worked example without JavaScript.
- **BM-01's default behavior is unchanged.** The mode is opt-in, and the core instrument's snapshots, scenarios, tapes, and captions are untouched.

## Technical Approach

Add `underdampedMsd`, `momentumRelaxationTime`, and `ouExactStep` to the audited TypeScript reference evaluator as a new section of `src/physics/reference/diffusion.ts` (or a sibling re-exported from it, following that module's one-entry-point rule, `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`). Bind the mode through the existing instrument registry and an explicit dispatcher case. Propose the capability upstream to the FrankenSim diffusion owner only after the TypeScript version is proven here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The start conditions, including the recorded reader need, are in this bead before work begins.
- [ ] Analytic MSD, both limits, and every fixture row above pass their tests.
- [ ] The exact-discretization sampler matches the analytic MSD within prespecified statistical bounds, and an Euler variant is shown to fail the same bounds near $\tau_p$.
- [ ] The mode is labeled a 1908 lens, links the source passage, and lists the hydrodynamic omissions.
- [ ] The mode's stream allocation is registered, and a display-cadence change leaves draws identical.
- [ ] BM-01's default behavior, scenarios, and tapes are unchanged.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

Against the real evaluator; no mocked kernel.

- **Analytic:** the small-$t$ series equals $(k_BT/m)t^2$ to leading order; the large-$t$ slope equals $2D$; every fixture row matches to a relative $10^{-10}$ using `withinTolerance` from `src/units/tolerance.ts`; dimensions pass the rational-dimension validator ($\tau_p$ in seconds, $D$ in m²/s).
- **Exact-step identity:** composing the conditional moments above with a thermal $v_0$ reproduces $2D[t - \tau_p(1 - e^{-t/\tau_p})]$ at $\theta = 10^{-3}, 0.1, 1, 10$.
- **Stochastic:** with fixed seeds and a documented ensemble size, the sample MSD at several times lies within chi-square-derived bounds computed before the test runs (`am-ver-statistical-policy-grj`); the velocity autocorrelation decays as $e^{-t/\tau_p}$ within bounds; changing render cadence leaves the draw sequence identical; a seeded Euler implementation is rejected by the same bounds near $\tau_p$.
- **Typed states:** an out-of-model request returns `outside-domain` with its reason, never `NaN` or a clamp.

### End-to-end tests

Browser lane through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: open the mode from BM-01, move the time axis across the crossover, confirm both asymptote labels, the crossover marker, the later-lens label, and the source-passage link; read the nonvisual table by keyboard; run the reduced-motion, 320 px, and JavaScript-disabled lanes; confirm BM-01's default mode is unchanged after leaving. Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot, accessibility-tree snapshot, console log, and the snapshot JSON.

### Structured logging

One JSON line per check at `artifacts/test-logs/deep-underdamped/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with the standard fields (`timestamp`, `suite` `deep-underdamped`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper: brownian-motion`, `instrumentId: bm-01:underdamped`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `message`) and the bead-specific fields `seed` (decimal string), `streamVersion`, `allocationId`, `ensembleSize`, `tSeconds`, `tauP`, `expectedMsd`, `sampleMsd`, `bound`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The crossover must never be used to criticize the 1905 paper, which explicitly restricts its interval. The mode shows where the model's premise stops.
- Euler discretization of the velocity equation introduces time-step bias near $\tau_p$; use the exact update and test that the shortcut fails.
- In a liquid, the real crossover is shaped by hydrodynamic memory. Saying "this is what the 2011 experiment measured" would be false; say what the OU model does and does not include.
- A sampled MSD that agrees at one time proves little; test several times and the velocity autocorrelation.
- Do not let the mode's logarithmic time axis imply that the instrument can resolve $10^{-9}$ s in a rendered animation; the axis is analytic, and the animation stays at human rates.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:

- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: the runtime and instrument abstractions are settled before a later mode is added.
- `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`: this extends the audited diffusion reference evaluator and its tolerance and scenario conventions.
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`: the paper's definition of done comes first, so optional work never substitutes for a core row.
- `am-ep-later-gap` (parent): later work that must never displace the core.

Reached transitively, and named above where this bead relies on them: `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly` (the host instrument and its manifest), `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` (stream allocation), `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (the explicit dispatcher case), `am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`, and `am-ver-statistical-policy-grj`.

Unblocks: none.

title: Add reviewed editions in other languages and interface localization
description:
# Add reviewed editions in other languages and interface localization

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P3 · **Labels:** later, translation · **Plan sections:** §4.8, §7.11, §19.7, §21 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers whose first language is neither German nor English are part of the intended audience, and the gloss face plus the overview reading is designed as their most direct route. The plan designs content ids, citation locators, number formatting, and layout for multiple languages from the beginning (`am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g`), but publishes "the German source and the English scientific edition first; add other languages as reviewed editions with their own translators, scientific reviewers, revision status, and correspondence to the source and explanation records." It separates interface localization from scientific translation: "a translated menu does not establish that a paper, its commentary, or its captions have been reviewed in that language." Machine drafts "may help; they never silently replace the default explanation." At launch, "full English publication does not imply that every language edition is reviewed."

**Why later:** reviewed scientific translation is expensive and multiplies correction work; the innovation sequence allows additional languages to expand only "after the access need is tested and the publication and revision path is reliable." **Start only when all of these hold:**

1. all four papers meet their definitions of done;
2. the correction graph of `am-edit-review-records-hofz` reliably flags affected units, so a German source correction cannot leave a translated unit silently stale;
3. a reader need for a specific language is recorded here, with its evidence (not a vanity list);
4. named translators and scientific reviewers for that language are available and listed in `docs/OWNERS.md`.

## Scope

In scope: per-language editions of the paper translations and of the readings; interface localization bundles; language routing, metadata, and `hreflang`; right-to-left support; per-language search; review records; and tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: community contributions without review (`am-later-companions-broadsides-umbq` owns that workflow); German-face narration and reviewed narration (`am-a11y-reviewed-narration-r28u`); the i18n record fields themselves (`am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g`); the search index implementation (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`, which gains per-language indexes rather than a second index); the notation concordance's content (`am-not-*` beads).

## Requirements

1. **Per-language team and records.** Named translators and scientific reviewers per language. Every translated unit carries `lang`, direction, `translationRevision`, review state, and reviewer. Unreviewed units never appear in a public build, and a machine draft is never marked reviewed because a schema accepted it.
2. **Correspondence.** Paper translations are made from the German and aligned to German source ids, many-to-many, exactly as the English edition is. Reading translations align to explanation record ids. A language edition never realigns or renumbers source ids.
3. **Notation is not translated.** Symbols stay as printed on every face in every language. The concordance's labels, definitions, and scope notes are localized; its glyphs are not. A global find-and-replace across a translated face is prohibited, as it is in English.
4. **The German source face stays the source face** in every language edition, and the English scientific edition remains the default. A language edition adds a projection; it never replaces the source.
5. **Interface localization is a separate bundle** with its own review state. A localized interface over an English edition says so plainly on the page, not only in a settings menu.
6. **Direction and mathematics.** Explicit `lang` and `dir` on every text container. In right-to-left prose, mathematics stays left-to-right and isolated (`dir="ltr"` on math elements, bidi isolation for inline symbols). Graph axes, equations, and derivation step order are never mirrored. German passages keep `lang="de"` inside any language's page.
7. **Numbers.** Locale-aware display only. Canonical transport never changes: SI values, decimal-string seeds and draw indices, constant-set ids, and tape payloads are identical in every language. Switching display language never changes a seed, a unit meaning, a source passage, an accepted snapshot, or an experiment identity.
8. **Routing and search.** A stable per-language URL scheme with correct `hreflang` and canonical links; per-language search indexes built by the search owner's pipeline, with the same document-type coverage table, so a language edition cannot ship with unsearchable record types; the default remains the English edition.
9. **Editorial voice.** Each language adopts equivalent voice rules (no hype, no "obviously", no em dashes where the language's typography makes them a hype marker), reviewed by a fluent editor.
10. **Corrections.** A German source correction flags affected units in every language through the correction graph. A changed English reading never silently marks another language current. The site states which editions are reviewed, to what revision, and which interface languages exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The start conditions and the chosen language's recorded need are in this bead before work begins.
- [ ] Compiler checks reject a public unit without reviewer and review state in the added language, and reject a translated unit whose alignment to German source ids is incomplete for its published scope.
- [ ] Right-to-left fixtures render mathematics left-to-right with correct isolation, and no axis, equation, or step order is mirrored.
- [ ] Language switching preserves the anchor, the seed, units, source passages, and experiment identities, verified in a browser lane.
- [ ] The site states which editions are reviewed and which interface languages are available, and a localized interface over an English edition says so on the page.
- [ ] A seeded German source correction marks the corresponding unit stale in every language.
- [ ] The per-language search index covers every document type in the coverage table.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

Against the real compiler and real records; no mocked records.

- Compiler tests: an unreviewed unit in a public language fails the build; alignment to German source ids is complete for the language's published scope; interface bundles carry review states; a notation glyph altered in a translated face fails.
- Formatting tests: locale display versus canonical transport for large and small numbers, uncertainties, intervals, and units, including a language whose decimal separator differs; a decimal-string seed is byte-identical across locales.
- Bidi rendering snapshot tests with right-to-left fixtures: inline symbols, display equations, mixed numerals, a derivation step list, and a table.
- Correction-graph test: a corrected German source block marks its English and other-language units stale, and an English-only reading change does not.

### End-to-end tests

Browser lanes per added language, through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:

1. Open a paper, switch language mid-reading, and confirm the anchor is preserved and the German source face is unchanged.
2. Run an instrument, then confirm the seed in `?tape=` and the accepted snapshot identity are unchanged across the language switch.
3. Search a localized term and open a result at its anchor.
4. Check `hreflang` and canonical tags on every language route.
5. Run the right-to-left lane at 320 px, keyboard only, with reduced motion, and with JavaScript disabled.

Failures retain a screenshot, DOM snapshot, accessibility-tree snapshot, and console log; evidence is never deleted.

### Structured logging

One JSON line per check at `artifacts/test-logs/languages/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with the standard fields (`timestamp`, `suite` `languages`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `anchor`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`) and the bead-specific fields `lang`, `dir`, `route`, `unitId`, `reviewState`, `translationRevision`, `seed`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, and `check`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A translated menu is easy and creates a false impression of a reviewed edition; label it on the page, not only in the settings.
- Right-to-left layout mistakes are subtle in mathematics; involve fluent readers early and test with a real screen reader in that language.
- Do not let a machine draft become the default explanation in any language, and never mark one reviewed because it validated.
- Adding a language multiplies correction work permanently. Adding one well is better than adding three that go stale.
- Locale number formatting must never touch transport values; a comma decimal separator inside a seed or a tape is a bug that silently changes a scientific identity.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:

- `am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g`: language, direction, and locale-aware number handling exist in the content model from the start.
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`, `am-dod-light-quanta-7as8`, `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`, `am-dod-relativity-105y`: other languages follow complete, reviewed English editions of all four papers.
- `am-ep-later-gap` (parent): later work that must never displace the core.

Reached transitively, and named above where this bead relies on them: `am-edit-review-records-hofz` (review records and the correction graph), `am-plat-search-index-snx1` (per-language indexes and the document-type coverage table), and `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (the browser lanes).
