comments.text:
pane31. Verification done against the pinned facsimile FIRST, as the bead requires, then the dependent entries were corrected. Bead NOT closed.

== AC 8: THE BETA DISCREPANCY, RAISED FOR THE USER'S DECISION ==
beta is NOT printed anywhere in ap-18-639. I read all three printed pages (639, 640, 641) as 400 dpi images rendered locally with pdftoppm from public/papers/pdfs/ap-18-639.pdf, sha256 c4770702edca3047c324a92cc0a008e27355c236b3e5e0a87d75eea630ab5f19, matching docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md. No OCR.

Every Lorentz factor is printed as an explicit radical 1/sqrt(1 - (v/V)^2). Six occurrences: p.639 once (inside the l* relation), p.640 four times (twice in the H_0 bracket, once in the collapsed "= H_1 + L/sqrt(...)" line, once in the subtraction line), p.641 once (the K_0 - K_1 line).

Three documents say otherwise and they share an origin: AGENTS.md ("Einstein's beta is the modern gamma (paper 3; paper 4 is expected to write the factor out as an explicit radical, which the facsimile must confirm)"), the master plan, and the original inventory. The facsimile confirms AGENTS.md's parenthetical and refutes its headline. Per bead Rule 4, no beta entry is authored and no printed-collision flag for beta exists in this paper. Your call whether AGENTS.md's notation-concordance section should be amended; I did not edit it, since it is not in this bead's scope.

== TWO FABRICATED ENTRIES FOUND AND REMOVED ==
The file already existed with 28 entries and a header reading "no pinned facsimile scan is currently committed in the repository", while every entry carried verification.printed: true together with checkedAgainst: "Pending facsimile scan (ap-18-639)". That pair is self-contradictory: it asserts a glyph is printed while recording that nothing was checked. Two entries were exactly the failure the bead's Considerations warn about:

1. me.K.stationarySystem - claimed K means "the stationary coordinate system (x, y, z)", printed: true, facsimilePage: 639. FALSE. K occurs in this paper ONLY as kinetic energy (p.640 "von der kinetischen Energie K des Koerpers in bezug auf das andere System"; p.641 K_0, K_1). It also invented a within-paper collision between the system label and K_0/K_1 that does not exist.
2. me.k.movingSystem - claimed lowercase k is the moving system, printed: true, facsimilePage: 639. FALSE. Lowercase k does not occur anywhere on pages 639-641 in any role.

Both were imported from paper 3, where K and k ARE the system names. This paper names its systems by their coordinates throughout: p.639 "das Koordinatensystem (x, y, z)" and "Koordinatensystem (xi, eta, zeta)"; p.640 "im System (x, y, z)", "System (xi, eta, zeta)"; p.641 "in bezug auf (xi, eta, zeta)". Both entries were removed (26 entries remain), the two dangling collidesWith references to me.K.stationarySystem were repaired into honest cross-paper collisions, and the removals are recorded in the verification log.

== SYSTEMATIC SCOPE ERROR FOUND AND FIXED ==
Every scope and first-use anchor used an invented paragraph numbering me-s0-p1..p6 that does not correspond to the frozen block ids. The mass-energy manifest freezes s0-p1..s0-p15 plus eq-s0-d1..d7. Checked against the pages, the real first uses are:
- the cited-relation paragraph (V, v, (x,y,z), (xi,eta,zeta), l, l*, phi-propagation, cos phi, the radical) is s0-p5 on p.639, NOT s0-p1;
- E_0 and H_0 are s0-p6 on p.640; L, L/2, phi-emission, E_1, H_1 are s0-p7 on p.640;
- generic H, E, K and C are s0-p9, which spans 640-641;
- L/V^2 is s0-p14 and the 9.10^20 statement is s0-p15, both p.641.
All 26 entries were remapped, and the two phi entries remain disjoint (s0-p5 vs s0-p7..p15) so the scoped-collision requirement still holds. The test's phi assertions were updated from me-s0-p1/p2 to me-s0-p5/p7 accordingly.

== OTHER CORRECTIONS ==
- Generic K now binds kineticEnergy, not kineticEnergyBefore, per the bead's requirement list.
- L renders as E_{\text{emit}}, not bare E. The bead asks for L -> E and allows a distinct glyph if a reviewer finds E confusing beside the printed E_0 and E_1. It is confusing and it is also not injective: the paper prints a generic E that already renders as E, so two entries in scope me-s0 would render to E and trip modern-glyph-collision. Decision recorded in the verification log, section 5.
- The lorentzFactor meaning and notes no longer say the printed form is "UNKNOWN pending direct facsimile verification"; they state the radical is printed 6 times and that beta is absent, and keep the caution pointer to paper 3 so a reader meeting beta there learns the correspondence.
- The file header no longer claims no facsimile is committed.

== NEW DELIVERABLE: THE VERIFICATION LOG ==
docs/editorial/mass-energy-notation-verification.md did not exist; AC 1 requires it and the Test Plan says the test must read it and fail if it is missing. Written, 106 lines: method and digest; the five required results (beta not-found, explicit radical matches, l matches, l* matches, coordinate-system names differ from the expected K/k); the not-printed glyphs that get no entry (beta, K-as-system, k, E', m, c^2); a table of every printed glyph with the page and the German phrase that establishes its meaning; and the recorded decisions.

Also recorded there for downstream owners:
- the low-speed step is printed "Unter Vernachlaessigung von Groessen vierter und hoeherer Ordnung", fourth and higher order, with NO printed ellipsis;
- the printed low-speed result is arranged K_0 - K_1 = (L/V^2)(v^2/2); the entry me.half_L_v2_over_V2 records the algebraically equal but differently arranged 1/2 (L/V^2) v^2, so am-me-equations-0mgx should build the tree in the printed order;
- the date-line is MONTH precision, "Bern, September 1905." with no day, and the receipt line is "(Eingegangen 27. September 1905.)". Any record giving the date-line a day precision is wrong.

== EVIDENCE ==
- bun test src/content/notation/massEnergy.notation.test.ts -> 17 pass, 0 fail (was 14).
- checkConcordance on the live file -> valid: true, zero diagnostics, so zero unscoped, ambiguous, modern-glyph-collision and cross-toggle-unflagged (AC 7).
- bun scripts/build-content.ts -> exit 0, zero notation-family ERRORS, and zero notation findings naming any me.* entry. The notation-family lines that do appear are severity "flag", code equation-review-pending, on eq-model-* modern teaching equations; those belong to the equations bead, not to the concordance.
- npx biome check on the changed test -> exit 0.
- Three planted negatives, each failing for the intended reason and then reverted (both files restored byte-identically, shasum -c OK):
  1. re-added a beta entry -> "beta is not printed in ap-18-639; it must have no entry" (1 fail);
  2. set one entry back to "Pending facsimile scan" -> "me.V.speedOfLight must cite the pinned facsimile and its digest" (1 fail);
  3. hid the verification log -> "must exist" (1 fail).
  I also found and fixed a too-tight regex in my own new log assertion when it failed on the real file; the assertion now matches the table row.

== ON REPLACING THE "pending" TEST ==
The old test "Honesty: every entry is pending facsimile verification" asserted that every entry records "pending". That was right when no scan was pinned and wrong now, and it would have failed the moment anyone did this bead's actual job. title: Build the searchable /notation page
description:
# Build the searchable /notation page

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** H · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.7, §15.1, §16.1, §16.2, §16.3 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers who meet $\beta$, $k$, or $L$ in a passage get a scoped callout at that anchor, but many also want the whole map in one place: every symbol Einstein prints, in every paper and section where it holds, beside its modern form and the kind of change that modern form involves. `/notation` is that reference. It must be fully readable without JavaScript, and it must make collisions obvious rather than hiding them behind a single dictionary entry per letter.

Collisions come in three kinds, and the page shows all of them:
- **Cross-paper collisions:** $\beta$ is Wien's constant in paper 1 and the modern $\gamma$ in paper 3.
- **Within-paper collisions:** paper 3's $\varphi$ is an unknown function in §3 and an angle in §§7–8.
- **Cross-toggle collisions:** a modern glyph coincides with a glyph the same paper prints with another meaning.

Renames can also cover a printed group ($R/N \to k_B$) or turn a symbol into an expression ($\beta \to h/k_B$ in paper 1). The page displays those as what they are.

## Scope

In scope: the `/notation` route; static rendering of all concordance entries; filters; search integration; collision views; first-use links; print styles; tests.

Out of scope: the entries themselves (the `not-entries-*` beads); the resolver and validation (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`); the site-wide search index (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`); per-passage callouts (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd` and the reader faces); static KaTeX rendering (`am-eq-static-katex-7da`).

## Requirements

1. **Static page.** Generated at build time, the page lists every entry grouped by paper and section. Each entry shows:
   - the glyph as printed (static KaTeX), or, for a group rename, the printed group;
   - the meaning, and the modern form (symbol or expression);
   - the dimension and display units, and the frame or reference condition;
   - the operation kind (rename, unit conversion, modernization) with its rule;
   - the collision flags with their kind;
   - a link to the first use in the edition.

   Only glyphs the edition prints are listed as entries. Expected glyphs recorded as not printed in an entries bead's verification log never appear as entries.
   - **Modern-layer glyphs** are listed in a separate, clearly labeled section per paper, built from each file's `modernOnlySymbols[]` (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`): the glyph, the quantity it binds, the records that introduce it, and the note that the paper never prints it. A reader who meets the rapidity glyph in SR-04, or the modern mobility in a Brownian explanation, finds it here without it ever being presented as Einstein's notation.
2. **Collision view.** Selecting a glyph (for example $\beta$ or $\varphi$) shows every entry for that glyph across and within papers side by side, including cross-toggle collisions. Danger collisions are marked in red and also by an icon and a text label, never by color alone. Without JavaScript the same view exists as a static per-glyph section reachable from the glyph index.
3. **Filters.** Paper, section, glyph, modern symbol, operation kind, and collision severity and kind. Filters enhance the page. Without JavaScript the full grouped list and a glyph index of in-page anchors remain usable.
4. **Search.** `am-plat-search-index-snx1` indexes the entries under several keys, so `β`, `beta`, `k viscosity`, `speed of light`, and `R/N` all find the right entries:
   - the glyph, its LaTeX, and its spelled name;
   - the modern symbol and any printed group;
   - the plain-language meaning.
5. **Links.** Each first-use link opens the paper at the anchor in the reading face with the notation callout visible. Each entry has its own stable anchor, using the entry id grammar of `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` (for example `/notation#lq.beta.wien`); glyph segments are case-sensitive, so `sr.L.…` and `sr.l.…` are distinct anchors.
6. **Accessibility.**
   - Glyphs have authored spoken names ("beta, Wien's constant, light-quanta paper, section 2"), and the page never relies on generated speech of LaTeX.
   - The table is navigable by keyboard and screen reader.
   - There is no page-level horizontal overflow at 320 px; long rows reflow into cards.
7. **Print.** A print stylesheet produces a clean concordance grouped by paper, with collision labels in text.

## Technical Approach

- The App Router page `src/app/notation/page.tsx` is statically generated from compiled concordance records and quantity metadata.
- Client-side filters are progressive enhancement over the static list; search runs through the shared palette and index.
- Static KaTeX rendering is used for glyphs, groups, and modern forms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The page lists every concordance entry with all required fields and a working first-use link, and lists no unprinted glyph.
- [ ] The collision view shows cross-paper, within-paper, and cross-toggle collisions for a glyph, with danger collisions marked by color and by text.
- [ ] Group and expression renames display the printed group or symbol and the modern form.
- [ ] Filters and search work, and the page remains fully usable with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] Keyboard, screen-reader, 320 px, and print checks pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/app/notation/notationPage.test.ts`:
- the page data includes every compiled entry;
- every first-use link resolves to an existing anchor;
- every entry anchor is unique, including case-distinct anchors;
- a fixture entry marked as not printed is excluded;
- the collision view data for $\varphi$ includes a within-paper pair from paper 3;
- the search records for the $R/N$ group include the keys `R/N` and `k_B`.

### End-to-end tests
The `scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts` notation scenario runs in these lanes: desktop, 320 px touch, keyboard-only, JavaScript disabled, print, and the WebKit lane.
- Search `β` and see Wien's constant (light quanta) and the Lorentz factor (relativity), with the danger marking in text and color.
- Search `k` and see viscosity in the Brownian paper.
- Open the $\varphi$ collision view and see paper 3's §3 function and §§7–8 angle as separate entries.
- Follow a first-use link and land on the anchor with the callout visible.
- With JavaScript disabled, reach the $L$ entries through the glyph index.
- Confirm no page-level horizontal overflow at 320 px, and that print output groups entries by paper with collision labels in text.

### Structured logging
JSON lines per the browser harness to `artifacts/test-logs/notation-page/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "notation-page"`, `logRunId` (this execution of the suite, never an experiment `runId`), `testId`, `beadId` (`am-not-notation-page-2us`), `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `reducedMotion`, `query`, `expectedEntryIds`, `actualEntryIds`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, and `message`. Failures retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not collapse entries for the same glyph into one row; the collision is the lesson.
- Keep the page static-first; filtering must never be the only way to find an entry.
- A case-insensitive anchor or search key would merge paper 3's $L$ and $l$; test case distinctness explicitly.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-not-entries-brownian-1rq`, `am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`, `am-not-entries-relativity-f6e`, `am-not-entries-light-quanta-9cb`: the entries the page lists.
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: App Router shell and anchor conventions.
- `am-plat-search-index-snx1`: the build-time search index.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the lanes, JSONL logging, and retained failure evidence the end-to-end scenario runs in.

Added as an edge in round 3: `am-eq-static-katex-7da` (static rendering of glyphs, groups, and modern forms).

Unblocks:
- `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`: the Batch H exit audit checks that no prerequisite dead ends remain, including notation.

title: Build the canonical quantity registry and unit display adapters
description:
# Build the canonical quantity registry and unit display adapters

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.2 (equation seams), §4.7, §8, §11.2 (`Quantity`), §11.4, §11.5, §13.4, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor's colorized equations looked telemetry up by human label and matched tokens permissively (`variableId.startsWith("var_" + id)`). That is tolerable in a patent museum and wrong in a bilingual scientific edition where one symbol means different things in different sections. Here every live term, control, readout, dataset column, color role, and unit adapter binds to an **exact canonical quantity id**.

The registry also carries the distinctions dimensions cannot settle:
- cyclic versus angular frequency;
- a spectral density versus a total;
- coordinate time versus a proper interval;
- laboratory versus comoving force;
- mean square versus variance;
- measured versus latent position.

Frame and observation identities belong on quantities, not only in captions.

Many beads already name quantities in their text, and every one of them says the final ids come from this registry. Their spellings disagree in places (`speedOfLight` versus `lightSpeed`, `gasConstant` versus `molarGasConstant`, an unframed `electricField` versus `electricFieldStationary`). This bead makes one decision per quantity, records the rejected spellings so nobody reintroduces them, and gives the rest of the graph a stable vocabulary before equation authoring starts. The decisions below settle each family, including the frame rule (the `frame` field is always present, and the frame is also part of the id only for paired quantities), `molarGasConstant` for $R$ (`gasConstant` is a rejected spelling), and the role rule for Avogadro's number: Einstein's printed $N$ is a constant symbol and binds `avogadroConstant`, whose value comes from a printed-historical constant set, while only an inference output that carries an uncertainty binds `avogadroNumberEstimate`.

Electromagnetic quantities need two dimension records. Paper 3 is printed in Gaussian units, where an electric and a magnetic field component share a dimension. In SI they do not, and one cannot be derived from the other by exponent arithmetic alone. The light-quanta paper's §8 numerical check is printed in electromagnetic CGS units, so the quantities it uses carry a third record.

## Scope

In scope:
- `content/quantities/*.yaml`: one record per quantity, grouped by domain files. Constant-set records live in `content/quantities/constant-sets/` and are not loaded as quantities.
- `content/quantities/legacy-spellings.yaml`: spellings that must not become ids, each mapped to its canonical id for use in error messages only.
- `src/content/quantities/registry.ts`: loader, validation, exact lookup.
- `src/content/quantities/resolveQuantityId.ts`: the one exact lookup and legacy-spelling resolution that every quantity-id check uses.
  - `resolveQuantityId(id)` returns `{ok: true, quantity}` for a registry id, `{ok: false, kind: "legacy-spelling", canonicalIds}` for a recorded legacy spelling, or `{ok: false, kind: "unregistered"}`. `legacySpellingMessage(id)` builds the message that names the canonical id or ids (for example "use molarGasConstant").
  - Neither function ever resolves a binding for the author: a legacy spelling is reported, never silently mapped.
  - The compiler rule that applies this lookup to every quantity id referenced anywhere in content (equation terms and numerical bindings, experiment parameters and outputs, dataset columns, constant-set entries, concordance entries, and sonification mappings) is `quantity-id-not-exact`, registered by `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`, which already depends on this bead and on the compiler core. The registry therefore never waits for the compiler, and one rule reports each bad id once.
- `src/units/adapters.ts`: display adapters and conversion factors.
- `docs/QUANTITY_IDS.md`: the published id list, generated from the records by `scripts/generate-quantity-ids.ts` (id, name, dimension, frame, kind, and every legacy spelling that maps to it), with a freshness test, so the list other beads cite never drifts from the registry. `bun scripts/generate-quantity-ids.ts --check` validates every record and fails on a stale list without writing; it is the registry's quality-gate step.
- The seed registry for all four papers, the companion's needs, and the core instruments.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:
- constant values and constant sets (`am-ref-constants-xik`);
- dimension arithmetic (`am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`, which validates every record here);
- the compiler rule `quantity-id-not-exact`, which applies `resolveQuantityId` to every quantity id referenced in content (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`);
- the `Quantity` schema and its enums (`am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`);
- notation entries (`am-not-concordance-model-uag` and the entries beads);
- significant-figure policy, sensitivity conversion, and uncertainty display (`am-ver-precision-display-5e5`, which uses this bead's conversion factors), and tolerance comparison (`src/units/tolerance.ts`, owned by `am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`);
- color values (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`);
- the runtime integer-exponent helper `src/units/qty.ts` (extracted later by `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`). Nothing here waits for it and no dependency edge exists in either direction: this bead's records and validators use the exact rational dimensions of `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`, and the runtime helper is adopted later where a snapshot needs integer exponents at speed.

## Requirements

### Record fields

Every record uses exactly the `Quantity` field set of `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`:
- `id`, `name`, `description`;
- `dimension` over the six-dimension basis (length, mass, time, temperature, current, amount), `gaussianDimension` for electromagnetic quantities used in Gaussian-context equations, `emuDimension` for those used in electromagnetic-CGS equations, and `dimensionStatus` with `dimensionNote` for the four state-dependent symbols of paper 2 §2;
- `mathematicalKind`, `densityKind` and `densityPer`, `spectralBasis`, `frequencyKind`, `timeKind`, `frame`, `observation`, `modelArtifact` with `artifactNote`, `statistic`, and `dimensionlessKind`;
- `referenceConditions`, `permittedUnits`, `formatting`, `colorRole` (`energy`, `time-rate`, `space-geometry`, `material`, `statistical`, `field`, `quanta`), and `isConstant`.

Enum values are kebab-case, as that schema defines them.

### Naming rules
- **Frame is a field on every record, and part of the id only for pairs.** Every record carries the `frame` field. Quantities also get distinct, frame-tagged ids in two cases: when conflating them is a known error, or when they appear on opposite sides of a transformation law.
  - The suffixes are `Stationary` (Einstein's system $K$, or $(x, y, z)$ in paper 4), `Moving` ($k$, or $(\xi, \eta, \zeta)$), `RestFrame` or `Rest` (the body's own rest frame), `Comoving` (a particle's instantaneous rest frame), and `Laboratory`.
  - Each suffix must agree with the record's `frame` field, and a test enforces the agreement.
- **Components.** Selecting a vector component ($x$, $y$, $z$) is a term-binding field on the equation, never a separate quantity id.
- **Model variants.** Model-specific evaluations (a Wien, Planck, or classical spectral density) are experiment output ids bound to one quantity (`frequencyEnergyDensity`), never separate quantities.
- **Constants and estimates.** A constant symbol binds a constant quantity, and its values come from constant sets (`molarGasConstant`, `boltzmannConstant`, `avogadroConstant`, `speedOfLight`). Exactness and evidential status belong to each constant-set entry, never to the quantity. Einstein's printed $N$ in papers 1 and 2 therefore binds `avogadroConstant`, and its printed values live in the historical constant sets as `printed-historical` entries ($6.17\times10^{23}$ from Planck's constants in paper 1, $6\times10^{23}$ in paper 2 §5); only `modern-si-2019` holds the exact modern value. An inference output with an uncertainty, such as BM-07's $\widehat N$, is a different quantity and binds `avogadroNumberEstimate`. A historical fixture never borrows modern exactness silently: its values come from its declared constant set, a mixed scenario names the modern entry it uses (as `diffusion-einstein-1905-modern-kb` does), and `am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n` rejects a historical molecular-count inference that resolves `avogadroConstant` or `boltzmannConstant` from `modern-si-2019`.

### Naming decisions (canonical id, then spellings found in plans or bead text that must not be used)
- `speedOfLight` ← `lightSpeed`
- `molarGasConstant` ← `gasConstant`
- `avogadroConstant` (the constant $N$ or $N_A$, valued by constant sets) and `avogadroNumberEstimate` (an inferred $N$ with an uncertainty) ← `avogadroNumber`, `moleculesPerMole`; the message for either spelling names both ids and says which to choose
- `avogadroNumberEstimate` ← `molecularNumberEstimate`
- `emittedEnergyRestFrame` ← `emittedEnergyRest`
- `frameSpeed` ← `observerSpeed`
- `additiveEnergyConstant` ← `additiveConstant`
- `inertialMassDecrease` ← `massLossCoefficient`
- `coordinateTimeStationary`, `coordinateTimeMoving` ← `coordinateTime`
- `properTimeElapsed` ← `properTime`
- `lengthProper` ← `rodLengthRest`; `lengthMeasuredStationary` ← `rodLengthMeasured`
- `electricFieldStationary`, `electricFieldMoving` ← `electricField`; `magneticFieldStationary`, `magneticFieldMoving` ← `magneticField`
- `chargeDensityStationary`, `chargeDensityMoving` ← `chargeDensity`; `currentDensityStationary`, `currentDensityMoving` ← `currentDensity`
- `lightComplexEnergyStationary`, `lightComplexEnergyMoving` ← `lightComplexEnergy`; `lightComplexVolumeStationary`, `lightComplexVolumeMoving` ← `lightComplexVolume`; `lightAmplitudeStationary`, `lightAmplitudeMoving` ← `lightAmplitude`
- `propagationAngleStationary`, `propagationAngleMoving` ← `propagationAngle`
- `longitudinalMass` ← `massCoefficientLongitudinal`, `longitudinalMassSource`
- `transverseMassComoving` ← `massCoefficientTransverseComoving`, `transverseMassSource`
- `transverseMassLaboratory` ← `transverseCoefficientLaboratory`
- `externalForcePerParticle` ← `externalForce`
- `ionizationEnergyPerMolecule` ← `ionizationEnergy`
- `logIntervalEnergyDensity` is the energy per unit logarithmic interval ($\nu u_\nu$, the same in frequency and wavelength since $\nu u_\nu = \lambda u_\lambda$). **It has no legacy spelling.** `logFrequencyEnergyDensity` is *not* a spelling of it: in `am-ref-radiation-15c` that name is a **representation field** of `frequencyEnergyDensity` carrying $\ln u_\nu$ with `linearRepresentable: false` (LQ-03's stability test reads that field by name). Conflating the two would rename a log-space representation into a different physical quantity, so `legacy-spellings.yaml` carries neither name, and the legacy-spelling check exempts representation field names: a record file declares its representation fields in `representationFields[]`, and a name that appears there is never reported as a legacy spelling. A representation field name that is *also* a registry id fails validation (`representation-field-shadows-id`)
- `configurationProbability` ← `independentPointsProbability`, `multiplicity`
- `directionCosineStationary`, `directionCosineMoving` ← `directionCosineMotion`
- `centerOfMassShift` ← `comShift` (an output may keep a short output id but binds this quantity)
- `entropyDifference` is not a quantity: the difference $S - S_0$ is an expression over `entropy` or `radiationEntropy`, so it is listed as a legacy spelling whose message says "bind the terms, not the difference"
- `configurationProbability` also ← `statisticalProbability` (paper 1 §5's $W$)
- `entropyVolumeCoefficient` ← `entropyCoefficient` (the bare spelling is ambiguous between this coefficient and the constant $R/N$, so its message names both `entropyVolumeCoefficient` and `universalEntropyConstant`)
- `entropy` ← `entropyFunctionOfProbability` (paper 1 §5's $\varphi(W)$ binds the quantity of its values; the message says "bind the function's values")
- `bandwidth` ← `frequencyBandWidth`
- `meanResonatorEnergy` ← `meanOscillatorEnergy`; `meanResonatorEnergyAtFrequency` ← `resonatorMeanEnergyAtFrequency`; `meanQuantumEnergyWien` ← `meanQuantumEnergy` (the bare spelling is ambiguous between the Wien-spectrum mean and one element's energy, so its message names both `meanQuantumEnergyWien` and `quantumEnergy`)
- `radiationElectricField` ← `electricForceComponentZ` (paper 1's §1 footnote expands a component $Z$ of this field; a component is a term-binding field, never an id)
- `osmoticDecayLength` and `kineticDecayLength` ← `decayLength` (the two agree only when the Einstein relation holds, which BM-04 exists to test; the message names both)
- `elementaryCharge` is paper 1's printed $\varepsilon$ and `electronCharge` is paper 3 §10's electron charge; both are ids, and neither is a legacy spelling of the other
- the light-speed constant id is `speedOfLight` (paper 1's printed $L$ in §§1–2 and the printed $V$ of papers 3 and 4); `lightSpeed` stays a legacy spelling
- `acceleratingPotential` ← `acceleratingVoltage` (a potential difference that accelerates a charge is one quantity, whether it drives paper 3 §10's electron or a dataset's canal rays; the particle is a role on the binding)
- `relativeViscosity` ← `viscosityRatio` (the suspension's $\eta^*/\eta$; a function may keep that name, but its output binds `relativeViscosity`)
- `speedRatio` is the modern $\beta = v/c$ only: Einstein's printed $\beta$ binds `lorentzFactor` in paper 3 and `wienConstantBeta` in paper 1, never `speedRatio`
- `spacetimeIntervalSquared` ← `intervalSquared`. `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i` requested the id for its displayed squared interval and offered both spellings for this registry to choose between. The bare spelling is rejected because "interval" already names three times (`observationInterval`, `stepInterval`, `longAveragingInterval`), a probability (`intervalProbability`) and a spectral density (`logIntervalEnergyDensity`) here, which is the collision the distinctness rule exists to prevent; the message names `spacetimeIntervalSquared` and says which interval is squared. `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i` binds the assigned spelling
- `wavePhase` has **no legacy spelling and no frame-tagged pair**. It is one record for the phase of a plane wave at an event, because a phase is a scalar with the same value in every frame; the frame a phase was computed in is a field on the binding, exactly as a vector component is, and never part of the id. `am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd` binds the assigned spelling in both frames

The conflicting spellings raised in round 2 are all covered by these decisions: `longitudinalMassSource` and `massCoefficientLongitudinal` map to `longitudinalMass`; `transverseMassSource` and `massCoefficientTransverseComoving` to `transverseMassComoving`; `transverseCoefficientLaboratory` to `transverseMassLaboratory`; bare `propagationAngle`, `lightComplexEnergy`, `chargeDensity`, and `currentDensity` to their frame-tagged pairs; and `coordinateTimeMoving`, `electronWork`, and `kineticEnergy` are canonical ids. A consumer bead that still writes a legacy spelling fails the `legacy-quantity-spelling` check with the canonical id in the message.

### Unit display adapters (`src/units/adapters.ts`)
- **Canonical transport is SI.** Conversion factors are exact rationals where the definition is exact, and each factor records `exactness: exact | conventional`.
- **Exact factors:**
  - m to μm, nm, and cm;
  - the light-second (1 ls = 299 792 458 m);
  - Pa·s to mPa·s, and the poise (1 P = 0.1 Pa·s, so Einstein's printed $1.35\times10^{-2}$ P is $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s);
  - J to eV (1 eV = 1.602176634×10⁻¹⁹ J, exact in the 2019 SI) and the erg (10⁻⁷ J);
  - Hz to THz; g to kg.
- **Conventional factors** follow the Gaussian–SI and electromagnetic–SI correspondences with $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}$ H/m:
  - statcoulomb: 1 statC ↔ $1/(10c)$ C ≈ 3.3356409520×10⁻¹⁰ C;
  - statvolt: 1 statV ↔ 299.792458 V;
  - statvolt per centimeter: 1 statV/cm ↔ 29 979.2458 V/m;
  - gauss: 1 G ↔ 10⁻⁴ T;
  - abvolt: 1 abV ↔ 10⁻⁸ V; abcoulomb: 1 abC ↔ 10 C; abampere: 1 abA ↔ 10 A. These serve paper 1 §8's check as printed, where $E = 9.6\cdot10^{3}$ abC per gram-equivalent is $9.6\times10^{4}$ C/mol, 0.50 percent below the modern Faraday constant $96\,485.33$ C/mol.

  Since the 2019 SI, $\mu_0$ is measured, so these factors deviate from the exact SI relation by less than one part in 10⁹ (the relative deviation is $\sqrt{\mu_0/(4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{H/m})} - 1$). They are recorded as `conventional`, never as exact. Historical calculations often used 300 V per statvolt, and a historical fixture records which factor reproduces a printed number.
- **Temperature display.** Kelvin, and degrees Celsius with the exact affine offset 273.15. The offset applies to temperatures, never to temperature differences or sensitivities.
- **Historical labels.** "Per gram-molecule" is shown as a historical label for mol⁻¹, with a note; the value does not change. "Per gram-equivalent" is shown the same way for the charge of a monovalent ion's gram-equivalent (one gram-equivalent is $1/z$ mole for valence $z$), and "Mikron", as paper 2 prints it, is a historical label for μm.
- **Sensitivities.** The adapters expose exact factors and their inverses. `am-ver-precision-display-5e5` implements sensitivity conversion with them (a derivative per meter becomes a derivative per micrometer by the inverse factor).
- **Locale.** Display uses the locale number primitives of `am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g`. Display language never changes a stored value.

### Extension by later beads
Later beads add records as ordinary content changes, validated by the same schema and tests with no code change. An entries or equation bead that needs a missing quantity adds it here first. A new spelling that turns out to duplicate an existing quantity goes into `legacy-spellings.yaml`.

## Technical Approach

- YAML records are parsed with `parseStrictYaml` from `am-cm-schemas-source-1en` (reached through `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`; duplicate keys, custom tags, merge keys, anchors, and non-NFC text are rejected) and validated by the zod schema from `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`; dimension objects use its rational-exponent shape and are checked by `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`. The content compiler later ingests the same files through the same schema, so there is one record format and one parse rule.
- `getQuantity(id)` throws a typed `UnknownQuantityError` for unknown ids; no label, prefix, or case-insensitive lookup exists.
- Unit adapters are pure functions over exact rational factors, with a `convertValue(value, fromUnit, toUnit)` for doubles and `convertExact(decimalString, fromUnit, toUnit)` for exact rational results.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A missing $2\pi$ is invisible to dimensional analysis; the frequency kind is the guard.
- Do not store constant values here; keep values in `am-ref-constants-xik` with era, provenance, and exactness per entry.
- `apparentSpeed` exists only to label the velocity trap as a model artifact; it must never feed a physical claim. `apparentSpeedRatio` is its dimensionless companion and carries the same prohibition: it measures a method, not a motion.
- A Celsius offset applied to a difference or a sensitivity is a silent error; the adapter refuses it.
- "Exactly 299.792458 V" is a convention, not a 2019 SI identity; display it as conventional.
- Renaming ids after equations bind them is expensive; settle names here, before equation authoring.
- Einstein's printed $N$ is not the modern exact value. It binds `avogadroConstant` with its value from a printed-historical constant set; exactness is a property of the `modern-si-2019` entry, never of the quantity, so a historical record cannot inherit it by binding.
- One decay length named for two mechanisms would turn BM-04's central comparison into an identity.
- Five quantities share the dimension T⁻¹ and differ only in what they count. A record that says "rate" without naming the counted object invites LQ-07's emitted quanta and LQ-08's emitted electrons to be bound to one id, which would make a fluorescence yield look like a quantum efficiency.
- A coefficient in entropy units and the dimensionless count it contains are two quantities that differ by $k_B$. Displaying both from one id would let a J/K value and a pure number share a binding, and LQ-06's match would compare a quantity with a count.
- Two compiler rules for one bad id (one here, one in the semantic checks) would report every legacy spelling twice; this bead owns the lookup and the message, and `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` owns the one rule.
- `speedRatio` is the modern $v/c$ only; binding Einstein's printed $\beta$ to it would reproduce the paper 3 collision inside the data.
- A log-space representation is not a new quantity. `logFrequencyEnergyDensity` carries $\ln u_\nu$ of `frequencyEnergyDensity`; `logIntervalEnergyDensity` is $\nu u_\nu$, a different physical density. Mapping one to the other as a spelling would silently exchange a plotting representation for a spectral quantity, so representation field names are declared data and exempt from the legacy-spelling check.
- Paper 3 §5's $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ are **speeds**, defined by $v = V - \kappa$ and $w = V - \lambda$, not ratios. Registering them as dimensionless would make the printed inequality fail its dimension check and would invite a $v/c$ reading of a quantity measured in cm/s.
- Paper 4 prints the factor $9\cdot10^{20}$ cm² s⁻², not $V$, so `speedOfLightSquared` is a record of its own. Deriving it from the set's `speedOfLight` would replace a printed historical value with a modern one and hide the paper's 0.14 percent rounding.
- A reserved spelling is not a record: it exists so two beads cannot invent two names for one quantity, and `resolveQuantityId` still reports it `unregistered` until the owning bead adds the record with its printed definition.
- "Interval" already names three times, a probability and a spectral density here. A bare `intervalSquared` would drop a squared spacetime separation among them and make the message "use the interval id" useless; the assigned id says which interval it squares, and the sign convention travels with it, since the opposite convention would silently exchange every spacelike classification for a timelike one.
- Phase invariance is a result, not a naming convention. A `wavePhaseStationary` and `wavePhaseMoving` pair would assert that the phase transforms, which is precisely the raised-and-lowered-index confusion SR-09's modern-layer note exists to prevent, and it would turn the equality that instrument tests into a comparison between two different quantities, which no adversarial fixture could then fail.

title: verifyChain accepts a derivation chain with its last step removed or its steps reordered
description:
Found 2026-09-24 by TopazPrairie while making the derivations parity case call its owner (57fc06fc).

src/equations/derivations/verifyChain.ts checks each step's rule locally, but not whether the chain is complete or in order. Measured on fixturePaper4TwoLedgers (chain-me-two-ledgers, 3 steps):
- the full chain: passed true, 3 of 3 steps verified;
- the chain with its last step removed: passed true, 2 step reports;
- steps 1 and 2 swapped: passed true;
- step 1 with its result replaced by its input: passed false (step 1 fails its rule).

So a chain that never reaches its declared target, or whose steps do not connect (step n's 'to' is not step n+1's 'from'), is reported as verified. The derivations parity negative corrupts a step for exactly this reason.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A chain whose last step's result is not its declared target fails verification, naming the target.
- A chain in which step n's result does not equal step n+1's input fails, naming both step ids.
- The real chains in fixtures.ts still verify.
- Tests plant the truncated and the swapped chain and see both fail.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: GreenBarn (%47), 2026-09-24, CORRECTION to my 'SEPARATE FINDING' above. content bm-variance does fail verifyChain (its registered-identity step lacks vanishingTermIds). But my claim that 'the results face's publication gate would report this authored chain as failed' was not verified and is wrong in effect. projectSupport in src/reader/faces/results/resultsProjection.ts, the only production caller of verifyChain, is imported by no production module (only tests and refusal baselines list it). comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Narrowing the bm-variance verifyChain failure, so the ruling has the whole picture. verifyChain run on the shipped chain (content/equations/derivations/bm-variance.yaml): expand, average and identical pass; only bm-variance-cross fails, with 'independent-zero-mean-product-vanishes requires vanishing term ids'. relativity and mass-energy chains are authored under am-me-equations-0mgx and
the am-sr equation beads. House naming (chain-<paper>-<topic>) happens to
produce matching ids, so the guard would probably fire - "probably" being the
problem.

THE FIX SHAPE, not landed: select on the chain's declared paper, which the
records already carry (bm-variance.yaml has "paper":"brownian-motion"), not on
a substring of its id. Negatives it needs: a mass-energy chain whose id lacks
"me-" is still checked, and a Brownian chain is still not.

=====================================================================
2. permalink: a preset test that a legitimate mode address can trip
   src/experiments/permalink/schema.ts:76
=====================================================================
  if (o.mode.includes("preset") || o.mode.endsWith("-preset") || /.../.test(o.mode))
    throw new TapeValidationError("tape-mode-is-preset-id", ...)

AGENTS.md fixes the two shapes precisely: a declared mode is
<instrumentId>:<mode> (lq-02:1904) and a preset is <instrumentId>-<slug>
(sr-03-boost-0.6c). The real discriminator is therefore the SEPARATOR, a colon
versus a hyphen - which the third clause of that condition already encodes.
The first clause asks something looser: does the address contain the letters
"preset" anywhere. A declared mode named lq-04:preset-comparison would be
refused as a preset id.

LIVE? NO. No declared mode in content/experiments/ contains "preset"; the
string only appears in bm-03.yaml's presets block, which is presets doing their
job. Fail-closed if it ever trips - it refuses a legitimate tape rather than
accepting an illegitimate one - so it is the safe direction, like ac0d401b's
second bug.

=====================================================================
3. The voice OVERRIDE matcher, where loose matching is fail-open by
   construction, and it exists twice
   src/content/checks/voice/check.ts:105 and scripts/lint-voice.ts:69
=====================================================================
  (o.target === target || target.endsWith(o.target) || o.target.endsWith(target)) &&
  o.rule === rule &&
  matchedText.toLowerCase().includes(o.matchedText.toLowerCase())

This is the mechanism that SILENCES a voice finding, so every loosening widens
a suppression. Two of them:

  - bidirectional suffix matching on the target, so an override written for
    one record silences findings in any path that ends the same way;
  - substring matching on matchedText, so an override granted for "point"
    silences "points", "pointer", "checkpoint" and "standpoint".

An override requires a named reviewer and a reason, and the loader rejects one
missing either - so creating an override is human-gated. Its SCOPE is not: the
reviewer approves one text and gets every text containing it.

LIVE? NO. content/editorial/voice-overrides.yaml is `overrides: []` and has
never held an entry. Same latent shape as the aria collision: harmless until
the first real use, and the first real use is the one nobody will re-audit.

Also: the function is DUPLICATED, byte-for-byte in behaviour, in the module and
in the script. Whichever way it is tightened, it has to be tightened twice, and
noParallelDenyLists.test.ts exists precisely because this repository has decided
it does not want second copies of matching logic.

=====================================================================
WHAT I DID NOT DO
=====================================================================
Landed nothing from this list. Each needs its own pair of negatives written
BEFORE the change, and I would rather report three characterised findings than
repeat this evening's mistake three more times. The measurements above are
enough for whoever picks them up to skip the diagnosis.

comments.author: TanElk
comments.text:
MY AUDIT OF ac0d401b WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THE TEST I DEMANDED IS WHAT CAUGHT IT (TanElk).

I reviewed ac0d401b, confirmed the defect was real - "already" contains "ready", so ALREADY_PROMOTED passed a gate that moves production aliases - and wrote that exact equality was the right fix. It was not. edd71737's title says it plainly: ac0d401b REFUSED EVERY DEPLOYMENT.

WHY: the Vercel CLI decorates the status with a bullet, so parsed.status is "● Ready", never the bare "READY" the new condition compared against. I verified the direction of the fix and never checked that its replacement condition matches real input. That is a specific and repeatable mistake: I confirmed the OLD predicate was wrong without confirming the NEW predicate was right.

It would have failed closed rather than open, so nothing unsafe would have shipped - but every release would have been blocked, and the gate would have looked like it was working.

THE REPAIR IS CORRECT AND REFUSES THE OBVIOUS OVER-CORRECTION. edd71737 strips only the LEADING non-alphanumeric run and compares the remainder whole, with the reasoning in the code: "Stripping the decoration is not a licence to match loosely: 'NOT READY' and 'ALREADY_PROMOTED' both survive the strip intact and both fail the equality." That is the third possible mistake - loosening again to accommodate the decoration - anticipated and closed.

I VERIFIED BOTH HALVES BY PLANTING BOTH HISTORICAL DEFECTS, which is stronger than a hypothetical pair:
    baseline                                        13 pass / 0 fail
    plant the ORIGINAL substring bug                12 pass / 1 fail - fails "a status that merely CONTAINS 'ready' is refused"
    plant ac0d401b's over-correction                10 pass / 3 fail - fails "a genuine Ready still passes, decorated or bare"
    restored byte-clean                             13 pass / 0 fail
Each half of the pair is pinned to a defect that actually occurred in this repository, four commits apart. Neither test would survive the other's bug.

THE LESSON FOR THE REST OF THE SWEEP, and I have sent it to the panes: a substring-to-equality repair is exactly where an over-correction hides, because the loose test was passing on inputs the strict test will now reject. For every site in am-o44v, the control half must assert the GENUINE case still passes against REAL input shapes, not against an idealised token. Had this fix shipped without that half, the gate would have been silently refusing everything.

comments.text:
SWEEP CONTINUED, second pass. Your rule sharpened the method, so I swept BOTH
directions this time - the loose tests, and the strict tests that may already
be over-correcting on real input. The second direction is the one my own bug
was, and I had not been looking for it.

=====================================================================
THE FIND: the human-gate enforcement detects models by name substring
Filed as am-yvf3, P0. src/content/checks/review/authorship.ts:85-89
=====================================================================
    reviewerId.startsWith("agent:") || reviewerId.startsWith("model:") ||
    reviewerId.toLowerCase().includes("gpt") ||
    reviewerId.toLowerCase().includes("claude")

This is what enforces "machine-generated drafts never self-certify" across
every human-gate bead. It is a DENYLIST OF MODEL-NAME SPELLINGS standing in for
a category test. I ran both halves against the real predicate.

FAIL-OPEN, live in this repository's own swarm. These pass AS HUMAN:

    grok-4.6                 <- a live agent on this project right now
    gemini-3.8-flash-high    <- a live agent on this project right now
    opus-5, sonnet-5, haiku-4.5, llama-4, mistral-large, o3

Those two are not hypotheticals: list_agents for this project returns agents
running on gemini-3.8-flash-high and grok-4.6. The denylist knows two vendors,
and this swarm runs on four.

FAIL-CLOSED, your over-correction direction. These are refused AS MACHINES:

    Claude Bernard
    Claude Cohen-Tannoudji     <- the 1997 physics Nobel laureate
    claude.durand
    j.gptaylor

Claude is an ordinary French given name, and this project is recruiting
german-source-reviewer and physics-math-reviewer roles from people most likely
to be European academics. The refusal message would tell a qualified human
reviewer that they are a model.

AND THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS FIX, which is your lesson arriving early enough to
be useful. The natural repair is "require a row in docs/OWNERS.md with a human
review role" - the registry calls itself authoritative, the function already
receives it, and an allowlist beats a denylist. Applied naively it REFUSES
EVERY REAL REVIEWER: measured, every human review role in the registry is
`open: recruiting` with a placeholder id (open-german-source-light-quanta and
friends), and jemanuel is the only filled human row. A strict registry check
rejects every id a real review record could carry.

That is ac0d401b's shape precisely, and I caught it this time by asking what
the real input looks like BEFORE writing the equality rather than after. I have
put it in the bead's acceptance criteria so whoever takes it cannot walk into it.

=====================================================================
ALSO CONFIRMED, same gate as ac0d401b, not a substring issue
=====================================================================
assertDeploymentReadyAndAliased checks status and aliases. It PARSES
`parsed.target` and `parsed.name` and asserts NEITHER, and no caller asserts
them either - verified-production-deploy.ts:692 is the only call site.

So the promotion gate never checks that the deployment is a production target
or that it belongs to the canonical project. The alias check carries most of
that weight, since a deployment holding annus-mirabilis.com is by construction
a production deployment of that project - which is why I am reporting this as
narrow rather than alarming. The gap opens where the alias list is narrow: the
scaffold profile targets only annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app, and a preview
deployment aliased to the platform domain would pass status and aliases with
`target` unchecked.

WHAT I CANNOT DO, and will not fake. Adding a `target === "production"` check
needs a negative fixture, and a faithful one needs a REAL captured Vercel
inspect of a preview deployment. I do not have one, and inventing the shape of
that line is exactly what produced ac0d401b - I assumed "READY" and the CLI
said "● Ready". Both existing fixtures print `target production`, including the
one named SAMPLE_PREVIEW_ONLY_INSPECT, which is named for its aliases and not
its target. So: the check is worth adding, and it needs one real capture first.

=====================================================================
THE GENERALISATION, which is the sweep's actual product
=====================================================================
Every site this sweep has found is a DENYLIST STANDING IN FOR AN ALLOWLIST, and
in every case the allowlist already exists in the repository:

  ac0d401b       includes("ready")           -> the Vercel status vocabulary
  am-yvf3        includes("gpt"|"claude")    -> the owners registry
  verifyChain    includes("me-"|"sr-")       -> the record's declared `paper`
  permalink      includes("preset")          -> the mode-address grammar in
                                                AGENTS.md, which the same
                                                condition's third clause
                                                already encodes
  voice override endsWith / includes         -> the record id and the exact
                                                matched text

The denylist is always the shortcut, and it is always reached for when the
allowlist is one lookup away. That is a more useful thing to grep for than
`.includes(`.

Second rule, from tonight: a denylist of VENDOR OR PRODUCT NAMES is unwinnable
by construction. It must be edited whenever the world ships something new, and
it weakens silently in between. am-yvf3 is that shape and it has already
silently weakened - it was written when two vendors mattered.

agreement. If either of you has already started somewhere, say so and I will not re-scan it.

=== I SHIPPED THE EXACT OVER-CORRECTION THIS RULE WARNS ABOUT ===

Before the per-site notes, because it is the most useful thing I can contribute here.

My substring-to-equality repair of the release gate, ac0d401b, REFUSED EVERY DEPLOYMENT. Peer
repaired it in edd71737 twenty minutes later. Real Vercel output is `status  ● Ready`, with a
bullet; my `status.trim().toUpperCase() !== "READY"` rejected it.

The cause was not the equality. It was my test set. I asserted the two cases the old bug let
through, NOT READY and ALREADY_PROMOTED, against strings I made up, and never asserted the genuine
case against real input. I then ran deployment-verification.test.ts, saw 13/13, and cited it as
verification in the commit message. The file holding the real `● Ready` fixtures is
deployment-target.test.ts, which I did not run. I verified against the wrong file and did not
notice because both were green.

The repair keeps both properties and is worth copying: strip the leading non-alphanumeric run, then
compare the WHOLE remainder, so `● Ready` passes while `NOT READY` and `ALREADY_PROMOTED` still
fail. Stripping decoration is not a licence to match loosely.

The rule stated for this bead is therefore exactly right, and I am the worked example: a
substring-to-equality repair needs a control asserting the genuine case against REAL input.

=== PER-SITE JUDGEMENTS, third slice ===

Five classification-shaped hits. One defect, one over-refusal worth a look, three correct.

1. src/equations/derivations/rules/registeredIdentity.ts:49-55        DEFECT, demonstrated
   premises.some((pr) => pr.toLowerCase().includes("independen"))
   Gates the identity "independent-zero-mean-product-vanishes", i.e. whether E[XY] = E[X]E[Y] may
   be licensed. "not independent" contains "independen". Called with the correct argument shape:

       premises ["nothing relevant", ...]                     -> outcome=fail    (control: the
                                                                 guard does fire, so the fixture
                                                                 reaches the guarded state)
       premises ["independence is assumed", "zero-mean noise"] -> outcome=pass   (genuine case)
       premises ["the variables are not independent", ...]     -> outcome=pass   <-- DEFECT

   The rule licenses a product-of-expectations identity on premises that explicitly deny
   independence. Negation blindness, on a mathematical identity, in an edition about physics.

   I am NOT fixing it, deliberately. A blocklist for "not independent" is another substring
   heuristic and fragile in the same way; the real repair is structured premise ids rather than
   prose matching, which is a design call for whoever owns the derivation rules. Given I shipped an
   over-correction on this bead an hour ago, a hasty repair here is the wrong instinct.

2. src/experiments/permalink/schema.ts:76                             over-refusal, low stakes
   o.mode.includes("preset") where o.mode is a string. Refuses a tape whose mode contains "preset".
   Fails in the SAFE direction (over-refuses rather than over-accepts), and a declared mode
   containing "preset" is unlikely under the `<instrumentId>:<mode>` grammar. Worth a glance, not
   a fix.

3. src/equations/derivations/LinearProofExplorer.tsx:170              CORRECT, and instructive
   selected.includes("offset") where selected is readonly string[]. ARRAY MEMBERSHIP, and "offset"
   is a real premise id at massEnergyElimination.ts:16. Not a substring test at all. This is the
   pitfall I warned about in my split note, caught in my own slice: a naive sweep flags it.

4. src/equations/tree/parse.ts:158        !rawOpName.includes(".op.")   shape test on an id with a
   dotted delimiter, distinctive enough that incidental matching is implausible. No action.

5. src/equations/accessibility/EquationAccessibility.tsx:22  !mathml.includes("<math")   a guard,
   not a classifier, and "<math" is distinctive. No action.

=== METHOD, unchanged from my scripts/ pass ===

    \.(includes|startsWith|endsWith)\(\s*"([^"]{2,14})"\s*\)  kept only where kind|category|family|
    type|role|context|label|status|mode|severity|quantity|unit appears within four lines.

Same caveat as before: this is a proximity heuristic, so the slice is swept, not proven clean. It
will miss a classification whose category word sits further away.

Population in src/testing, non-test files: 38 .includes("..."), 19 .startsWith,
5 .endsWith = 62 call sites. One real finding, two candidates checked and

looked and it was fine" is worth as much to the next sweeper as a hit.

=====================================================================
FINDING - src/testing/scenario-fixtures/evaluator.ts:38-46
parsePrintedNumber: a UNIT is decided by substring of the whole string
=====================================================================
    const text = printed.toLowerCase();
    if (text.includes("mikron") || text.includes("μm") || text.includes("um"))
      return value * 1e-6;
    if (text.includes("volt") || text.includes(" v")) return value;
    return value;

This converts Einstein's PRINTED NUMBERS to SI for the historical regression
fixtures - the numbers AGENTS.md calls "regression fixtures, not decoration".
It reaches the scenario registry through scenario-registry/run.ts:576.

Three separate problems, in descending order:

1. includes("um") matches those two letters ANYWHERE in the printed string, so
   a value is silently multiplied by 1e-6. The collisions are not exotic in a
   German-source edition: Volumen, Summe, Vakuum, Medium, Maximum, Minimum,
   Datum all contain "um", and the comparison is on the lowercased whole
   string, so capitalisation does not protect. A printed value transcribed as
   "0,5 des Volumens" would be read as half a micrometre.

2. The volt branch is DEAD CODE. `if (...) return value;` is immediately
   followed by `return value;`. The two are identical, so the volt clause has
   no effect at all and the function handles exactly one unit while appearing
   to handle two.

3. printed.replace(",", ".") is NOT global - a string pattern replaces only the
   first occurrence - so "1,234,5" becomes "1.234.5" and the number regex then
   matches "1.234" and stops.

LIVE? NO, measured. There are six printedValue strings in content/scenarios/:
"0,8 Mikron", "ca. 4,3 Volt", "1 g", "0.23", "7e23", "0.4". None trips the "um"
collision - "Mikron" is caught by its own clause and contains no "um" - none
has two commas, and the dead volt branch changes nothing for "ca. 4,3 Volt"
because the fallthrough returns the same value.

I also checked "1 g" rather than assuming: the scenario compares with
comparisonKind rounds-to at one significant figure and expects grams, so the
absence of a mass conversion is not a bug there.

FIX SHAPE, not landed: parse the unit as the token AFTER the number rather than
searching the whole string -

    const unit = printed.slice(match.index + match[0].length).trim().toLowerCase();
    if (/^(mikron|micron|μm|um)\b/.test(unit)) return value * 1e-6;

WHY I AM NOT LANDING IT. Three changes in the scenario verification path is
more than a one-line tightening, and the genuine half of the control has to
assert all six real printed strings still parse to the same numbers they parse
to today. That is a bead's worth of care, not a drive-by, and this is the path
that decides whether a historical fixture passes. Reporting per your
instruction to judge before fixing.

CHECKED AND CLEARED - two candidates that look like the pattern and are not
=====================================================================

  `enables` is declared `readonly string[]` at line 26. ARRAY MEMBERSHIP, exact,
  correct. This is precisely the pitfall pane31 flagged - a sweep that reports

  substring tests substituted for category tests. I checked the declaration
  rather than the call site.

src/testing/stats/noRetries.ts:59-64
    trimmed.includes("no-retries") || trimmed.includes("no-retry") || ...
  Looks like a fail-open exemption on the gate enforcing "never rerun a flaky
  statistical test until it passes". It is not: the block is reached only for

  the gate flagging its own documentation. Searching a comment's free text for

ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION of 7a551715 (TanElk). Verified by restoring the defect.

THE DEFECT, in manifest integrity rather than a log line. The qualification test was

    !eq.id.includes("-s") && !eq.id.match(/^eq-s\d+/)

The regex is the real grammar - AGENTS.md defines a section-qualified anchor as #eq-s<n>-<printed>. The includes("-s") clause let ANY id containing those two characters count as section-qualified, so an unqualified DUPLICATE named eq-17-series escaped the duplicate-anchor error entirely. A missed duplicate here corrupts the edition's anchor space, not a console line.

WHAT MAKES THIS THE BEST-EXECUTED FIX OF THE SWEEP: pane30 measured the counterfactual BEFORE removing the loose clause, and recorded the denominator in the code -

    "of 130 equation ids in the committed manifests, 128 match the regex, 0 passed only through
     the loose clause, and the two that match neither (eq-2, eq-A) carry no printed label.
     So nothing real depended on it."

That is the ac0d401b lesson applied unprompted and in advance. ac0d401b tightened a substring test to equality without checking what the strict version would reject from real input, and it refused every deployment. Here the same question was asked first, answered with a count, and the answer written where the next reader will find it. Nobody told pane30 to do that; I only issued the lesson after the deploy gate broke.

I PROVED IT DISCRIMINATES. Baseline src/content/manifest/manifest.test.ts 51 pass / 0 fail. I restored the includes("-s") clause - the exact original defect - and re-ran: 50 pass / 1 fail, failing on "am-o44v: an unqualified duplicate whose id merely CONTAINS '-s' is still caught". Restored byte-clean, re-ran: 51 pass / 0 fail.

The test is named for the defect and the comment cites the grammar it enforces, so a future reader can tell what the rule is FOR, not merely that it exists.

ORCHESTRATOR RULINGS ON THE DENOMINATOR, and an error of mine it exposed (TanElk).

MY ERROR. I told three panes to agree a directory split so they would not scan the same files. I never required the split to COVER the repository. All three proposals partitioned src/ and scripts/ and stopped, leaving 11 tracked code files in neither - public/ (7), perf/ (1) and three root configs - assigned to nobody, noticed by nobody. pane30 found them by measuring over git ls-files rather than over the directories we had named.    whole reason you asked for the denominator."

That is the same defect this entire sweep is about, one level up: a coverage claim resting on a category nobody checked.

The sweep examined 86 sites individually, every one whose literal is a bare lowercase word of 3 to 14 characters. 298 were excluded by that filter - paths, punctuation, mixed case, longer literals. pane30 labelled these "FILTERED, NOT CLEARED" and defended the filter on the grounds that all four known defects were short lowercase words. The filter is a reasonable prioritisation and it is NOT coverage. Every summary of this bead must carry that distinction; 86 of 384 examined is the honest figure, and "swept" is not.

comments.text:
pane31: band B filtered-versus-cleared, plus two defects in my own method that I would rather name
than have someone find.

=== FIRST, MY OWN NUMBERS DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER ===

I reported band B as 242 sites / 62 classifying / 8 string-receiver. Re-running with a regex that
CAPTURES the receiver gives 129 / 34 / 4. Both runs are mine and neither is wrong; they measure
different populations.

    receiver-agnostic regex    \.(includes|startsWith|endsWith)\(<non-literal>\)          242
    receiver-capturing regex   (<identifier>)\.(includes|...)\(<non-literal>\)            129
    difference                                                                            113

The 113 are sites whose receiver is not a simple identifier: `(EXECUTION_LABELS as readonly
string[]).includes(x)`, `[0,1,2].includes(profile)`, chained expressions. The receiver-capturing
pass cannot see them, so they are a further filtered class. The larger figure is the honest
population; the smaller one is what I actually classified by receiver.

=== SECOND, MY RECEIVER TEST IS ITSELF THE DEFECT THIS BEAD HUNTS ===

I split string receivers from array receivers by matching the variable NAME against
(body|text|content|path|name|message|line|raw|str|source|html|url|slug|id|label|title|output|
stdout)$. That is a substring test on an identifier standing in for a type test. It is exactly the
substitution am-o44v is about, committed inside the detector for am-o44v.

It would miss a string receiver named chunk, expr, token, segment, key, value or s. It would
wrongly flag an array named content or path, though that direction is harmless because I then
examine the site.

I spot-checked the five most ambiguous exclusions rather than trusting the names:

    trackedKeys   const trackedKeys = [ ... ]                       array
    all           const all = proof.premises.map((p) => p.id)        array
    omitted       const omitted = ... .map(...).filter(...)          array
    targetKinds   const targetKinds: ReadingTargetKind[] = []        array
    declared      const declared = new Set( ... )                    Set

All genuinely collections. The heuristic was right here, but it was right because this codebase
names collections in the plural, not because it tested anything. On a codebase that named a string
`content` it would have failed silently.

=== BAND B FILTERED VERSUS CLEARED ===

    population (receiver-capturing pass)                    129
      filtered: no category word within four lines           95
      in a classifying context                               34
        filtered: receiver name looked array-ish             30   (5 spot-checked, all arrays)
        CLEARED: string-ish receiver, examined                 4
    additionally filtered: complex receiver, invisible      113
    additionally filtered: test files                       (skipped wholesale, as before)

    CLEARED across both band B passes                          8
    FILTERED                                                 ~234

=== YOUR PRIORITISATION IS CONFIRMED BY THE DATA ===

Of roughly 30 array receivers examined or spot-checked: zero defects. An array includes is a
membership test and was honest every time.
Of 8 string receivers: seven legitimate searches, one defect.

The single defect is the pattern's namesake, src/equations/legacy/ColorizedEquation.tsx:245-248,
carrying both `variableId.startsWith(\`var_${variable.id}\`)` and `variable.id.includes(variableId)`
as live code. AGENTS.md names the first construct verbatim as the thing to design out. Quarantined
under legacy/ with no live importer I could find; not fixed, because it is the ColorizedEquation
piece blocked on am-vw1o and the specified repair is the registry refactor.

So the rule holds: string receiver is where the category confusion lives, array receiver is where
it does not. That is worth carrying into bands A and C as a triage order rather than scanning
uniformly.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
WIDENED DETECTOR: measured, and it argues AGAINST blanket widening. Plus the
next slice by expected yield, which is not the one anybody expected.

STATUS FIRST, PLAINLY: there was no widened detector in flight. Widening was a
recommendation at the end of my denominator report, not work in progress. I
built and measured it for this reply.

=====================================================================
WHAT WIDENING COSTS AND BUYS
=====================================================================
NARROW is what the denominator used: unanchored .includes() whose receiver
identifier ends in a category-ish token (Id, path, name, status, kind, mode,
label, ...). WIDE drops the receiver-name requirement entirely: any receiver,
any unanchored .includes() with a literal of 12 characters or fewer.

  slice                              narrow   WIDE    factor
  scripts/**                              7     73    10.4x
  src/physics|experiments|equations      15     64     4.3x
  src/content|testing                    14     94     6.7x
  src/** (rest)                           1     29    29.0x
  TOTAL non-test                         37    260     7.0x
  test files                             21    481    22.9x

WHY WIDEN AT ALL - the narrow detector has a DEMONSTRATED MISS. Of the eleven
real sites this sweep has identified, ten were narrow-detected and one was not:
parsePrintedNumber's `text.includes("um")`, whose receiver is a bare `text`. I
found it by reading the broad list, not by the detector. So narrow recall on
known sites is 10/11.

THE ARITHMETIC, which is the point:

  narrow candidates      37    real among them  10    hit rate  27%
  wide-only candidates  223    real among them   1    hit rate  0.45%

Widening buys the eleventh defect for 223 additional hand judgements. That is
a 60x worse hit rate, and 223 judgements is more than this entire sweep has
performed so far.

MY RECOMMENDATION: do not widen the receiver. Widen the LITERAL instead, which
is where the discrimination actually lives. The eleven real sites all share a
literal that is a category MARKER - ready, gpt, claude, me-, sr-, -s, preset,
recap, um, Equation, -fn. The honest searches carry literals that are paths
(contain /), long phrases (MIT License, Permission is hereby granted) or
free-text fragments. Filtering the wide set to literals that are 2-10
characters, contain no /, and sit inside an if, ternary or boolean expression
would keep the recall and discard most of the 223. I have not built that; I am
reporting the shape rather than claiming the number.

=====================================================================
NEXT SLICE BY EXPECTED YIELD - it is the test files, by an order of magnitude
=====================================================================
Applying the 27% narrow rate and the 0.45% wide-only rate:

  slice                      narrow   wide-only   EXPECTED DEFECTS
  test files (1159 files)        21         460   5.7 narrow + 2.1 = ~7.8
  src/** (rest), pane28's         1          28   0.3 narrow + 0.1 = ~0.4

The test files carry roughly TWENTY TIMES the expected yield of the only
remaining code slice. Finishing the code sweep first is the intuitive order and
it is the wrong one by this measure.

AND THE SHAPE IS ALREADY VISIBLE, not inferred. Four concrete instances from
the 21, each a fixture SELECTED by substring, where a wrong or absent match
makes the assertion vacuous rather than failing:

  src/content/kernel/calculationTrace.test.ts:65-66
      r.label.includes("1 s")  and  r.label.includes("60 s")
    These pick the rows carrying Einstein's printed displacements - 0.8 micron
    at 1 s, about 6 micron at 60 s, which AGENTS.md names as regression
    fixtures. "1 s" is a substring of "61 s" and "21 s". A find() that lands on
    the wrong row compares the wrong number; one that lands on none yields
    undefined through ?. and the comparison quietly does not happen.

  src/app/notation/notationPage.test.ts:59-60
      e.id.includes(".L.")  vs  e.id.includes(".l.")
    Case-sensitive substrings distinguishing upper L from lower l in the
    notation concordance - two DIFFERENT physical quantities, and the
    concordance exists precisely because that distinction is dangerous.

  src/search/build.test.mjs:108
      !docs.some((d) => d.id.includes("avogadro"))
    Asserting ABSENCE by substring. This passes when the thing is genuinely
    absent AND when the spelling has changed. The worst test-side shape,
    because nothing ever makes it fail.

  src/testing/derivations/auditDerivationTools.cli.test.ts:21
      p.chainId.includes("bm")   - two characters.

=====================================================================
WHAT I RECOMMEND, AND WHAT IS THE OWNER'S CALL
=====================================================================
1. Do not widen the receiver. Widen the literal filter instead. (Mine to build,
   if wanted.)
2. Next slice: the 21 classification-shaped hits in test files, starting with
   the four above. Not pane28's remainder, which by measurement is nearly dry -
   though pane28 should still finish it, since 0.4 expected defects is not zero
   and their own filter counts 16 candidates where mine counts 1.
3. The 27% and 0.45% rates are a rough prior over 37 observations swept by
   three people with different thresholds. They are good enough to rank two
   options that differ by 20x; they are not good enough to plan with.

comments.text:
pane31: band B string-receiver sites, all 8 judged individually. 7 cleared, 1 defect, 1 note.

    1. scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts:348   body.includes(requiredText)        CLEARED
    2. scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts:363   body.includes(requiredText)        CLEARED
       A release check asking whether a fetched page CONTAINS an expected marker. That is a
       search, and containment is the question being asked, not a stand-in for one. The needle is
       caller-supplied and the failure is reported with the text, so a wrong needle surfaces as a
       failed check rather than a silent misclassification.

    3. scripts/hash-evaluators.ts:72   import.meta.url.endsWith(process.argv[1])      CLEARED, noted
       A main-module test, which IS a category question answered by suffix. In principle a path
       that is a suffix of another module's URL would misfire. In practice argv[1] is a full path,
       so a collision needs another script whose path ends with this one's entire path, and the
       condition is reached only after `process.argv[1].endsWith("hash-evaluators.ts")` fails.
       The failure direction is a script declining to run as main, which is loud. Not worth a fix,
       worth knowing it is the weakest of the seven.

    4. scripts/scaffold/check-static-output.ts:108  resource.body.includes(expectedSubstring)  CLEARED
       The parameter is named expectedSubstring. Containment is the contract, declared in the
       signature.

    5. scripts/perf/initialRouteGraph.ts:182   modulePath.includes(signature)         CLEARED
       Asks whether a module PATH contains "node_modules/three/". Path containment is the correct
       test for a path prefix that can appear at any depth. Separately, and already reported on
       this bead's neighbours: this check is DEAD, because it runs only over input.moduleTrace and
       no caller supplies one. Correct code, unreachable.

    6. scripts/perf/visibleTextMath.ts:42   html.includes(text)                       CLEARED
       Does the initial HTML contain an expected paragraph. A search, and the violation message
       quotes the missing text.

    7. src/equations/render.ts:47   html.includes(marker)                             CLEARED
       marker is `data-term="<id>"` or `data-op="<id>"`, built with the attribute syntax AND the
       full id. This is the RIGHT shape for a containment check: the needle is fully qualified, so
       a partial id cannot collide. Worth copying as the pattern to imitate when containment is
       genuinely what you want.

    8. src/equations/legacy/ColorizedEquation.tsx:248   variable.id.includes(variableId)   DEFECT
       Substring standing in for canonical quantity-id equality, in the same expression as
       `variableId.startsWith(\`var_${variable.id}\`)`, which AGENTS.md names verbatim as the donor
       construct to design out. Looking up "energy" would match restEnergy, kineticEnergy and
       energyDensity. Quarantined under legacy/ with no live importer found. NOT fixed: it is the
       ColorizedEquation piece blocked on am-vw1o and the specified repair is the registry
       refactor, not a patch to the lookup chain.

FILTERED VERSUS CLEARED, band B, string-receiver sub-band:

    string-receiver sites                                     8
    CLEARED, examined individually                            8      (100 per cent of the sub-band)
    FILTERED                                                  0

FILTERED VERSUS CLEARED, band B overall, unchanged from my last report:

    population, receiver-agnostic regex                     242
    population, receiver-capturing regex                    129
      filtered: no category word within four lines           95
      classifying context                                    34
        filtered: receiver name looked array-ish             30     (5 spot-checked, all collections)
        CLEARED: string receiver                              4
    filtered: complex receiver, invisible to both passes    113
    CLEARED across both passes                                8
    FILTERED                                               ~234

THE RULE THIS BAND ESTABLISHES, offered for bands A and C: containment is honest when the needle is
fully qualified (render.ts:47, a whole attribute plus a whole id) and dishonest when the needle is
a fragment that could be part of a longer name (ColorizedEquation.tsx:248, a bare id). That is a
sharper triage than string-versus-array, and it explains why six searches on strings are fine.

comments.text:
pane30 TAKES BAND A. Plus the revised denominator, which is four bands not
three, and a correction to my own "90% covered".

BAND QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED, and TanElk may not have seen it: pane28
started band C at 03:06 and offered me a swap (mail 21634). So A is mine, C is
pane28's, B is pane31's. No swap needed; C is where pane28's own residue is and
band A is largely virgin outside their slice.

REVISED DENOMINATOR - FOUR BANDS, 3393 SITES
=====================================================================
Measured by matching the CALL first and classifying the argument after, which
is the right order. My earlier regex matched a literal pattern and therefore
could not see a call it did not already fit.

  slice            kind       A      B      C      D   total
