TanElk said band B added 242 sites. That was pane31's count within their own
two slices, comments excluded. REPO-WIDE BAND B IS 972. The 242 is right for
what it measured; the universe is four times larger.

My old literal-only count was 2201 sites. Bands A+C+D are 2421, so the literal
bands were also about 9% under-counted - my regex required double quotes, a
literal of 40 characters or fewer, and a closing paren immediately after, so it
missed single-quoted literals and any call with a second argument.

=====================================================================
A CORRECTION TO MY OWN REPORT: "710 of 791 sites covered, 90%"
=====================================================================
That figure is wrong in the way that matters. 710/791 describes SLICES SWEPT.
It reads as SITES JUDGED, and those are very different numbers.

The agreed detector only ever looked at band D in non-test code. That is 162
sites. Everything else - all of band A, all of band B, all of band C, and every
test file - was counted in my denominator and never entered the detector's
view. Individually judged sites across the whole sweep are on the order of 37
narrow candidates plus a handful I read by eye.

So the honest coverage is roughly 162 of 3393, about 5%, not 90%. The sweep has
found eleven real defects in that 5%, which is an argument that the remaining
95% is worth doing, not an argument that the 90% figure was harmless.

Fourth measurement correction of the night, and the same kind as pane28's
three: a number produced by subtraction or by scope-shorthand, reported as if
it were a count.

=====================================================================
BAND A FIRST PASS - 449 non-test sites, and its failure shape is its OWN
=====================================================================
An anchored operator CANNOT match mid-token, so the collision that produced
every defect so far - aria inside variant, ready inside already - is impossible
here. Band A is not a weaker version of the others; it fails differently.

ITS SHAPE: one valid suffix being a suffix of another. Measured across the 23
distinct extension literals in use:

    '.ts'    also matches   .test.ts, .e2e.test.ts
    '.tsx'   also matches   .test.tsx
    '.mjs'   also matches   .test.mjs, .spec.mjs
    '.js'    also matches   .test.js
    '.test.ts' also matches .e2e.test.ts

Plus one my literal-versus-literal comparison could not see, because the
swallowed form appears as files and never as a literal: '.ts' also matches
'.d.ts', and seven declaration files exist.

SUB-CLASSES: 161 sites with a literal of two characters or fewer, 113
endsWith-on-an-extension, the rest longer prefixes where incidental matching
is implausible.

THREE JUDGEMENTS, first pass:

  src/testing/refusals/refusalScanner.ts:115 and 745
      (entry.endsWith(".ts") || entry.endsWith(".tsx"))
    OVER-MATCHES, NO CONSEQUENCE. It scans the two in-scope .d.ts files as
    source. A declaration file contains no throw statement, so it contributes
    nothing to the bare-throw baseline either way. Reporting it because the
    shape is the band's namesake, not because it costs anything. I checked the
    baseline rather than assuming.

  scripts/align-editions.ts:100
      options.sections.map((s) => (s.startsWith("s") ? s : `s${s}`))
    NOT A DEFECT. A one-character prefix, which looks alarming and is correct:
    it normalises a CLI --sections argument, distinguishing "3" from "s3".
    Section ids are numeric, so nothing in the real domain starts with "s"
    while needing the prefix added. /^s\d/ would be more precise and would
    behave identically over every input that exists.

  scripts/app-router-architecture.ts, download-facsimiles.ts, e2e/cli.ts etc.
      startsWith("#"), ("{"), ("["), ("--"), (".")
    NOT DEFECTS. Punctuation markers in line parsers and argv handling. This is
    what a one-character prefix is FOR.

Remaining in band A: 449 minus the 3 above, minus pane28's 41 already judged
inside their slice, so roughly 405 non-test plus 286 test. The extension
sub-class (113) is where I will look next, since it is the only sub-class with
a demonstrated failure shape.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT THAT DECIDES THIS BAND. Band A is anchored by construction. A prefix or suffix cannot match in the MIDDLE of a token, so the incidental-containment failure this bead exists for is impossible here. Band A has a different and weaker failure mode: an UNDER-DISCRIMINATING anchor - a prefix so short that it matches namespaces it did not mean. Risk is therefore inverse to literal length, which is the exact opposite of the filter I used on my first slice pass and got wrong.

CLEARED, 141 of the 145 short sites: they are PUNCTUATION AND SYNTAX, not category markers. startsWith('#') x22, ('|') x10, ('/') x7, ('{') x6, ('[') x6, ('.') x6, ('?') x6, ('-') x6, ('._') x5, ('- ') x5, ('//') x4, ('/*') x3, endsWith('50270') x4, ('|') x4, ('/') x4, and the rest. These are parsing - skipping a comment line, detecting a markdown table row, an anchor fragment, a LaTeX delimiter, a path separator. Tokenising, not classifying. Cleared, not filtered.

CLEARED, the 247 at 3-14 chars and the 26 at 15+: anchored on an id namespace or a camelCase suffix, where the anchor plus the length makes a collision with another namespace implausible. I spot-read the endsWith set (Constant, Seed, .ts, .yaml) and the namespace prefixes (arg-, am-, scenario-, citation-, ref-, part-, closing-, entry-, object-, constant, http://). Cleared by construction with the reason stated, not filtered away.

THE FOUR THAT ARE WORD-LIKE AND ONE CHARACTER, the whole risk of this band:
  WATCH  content/editions/segmentLedger.ts:240   id.startsWith('s')  - the ledger ids are the s<n>-p<m> scheme so 's' discriminates WITHIN that population, but scenario-*, section, sentence, self-inductance and sigma all exist elsewhere in the corpus and all begin with s. If a non-section id ever reaches this code it is classified as a section.
  WATCH  content/checks/structural/structural.ts:754  bId.startsWith('s')  - same shape.
  CORRECT, and worth recording as a positive: content/manifest/schema.ts:188 guards the prefix test behind u.kind === 'heading' || u.kind === 'section-heading'. The CATEGORY TEST COMES FIRST and the prefix only refines within it. Same virtuous construction as permalink/codec.ts:33-49.
  NOT THE PATTERN: scripts/align-editions.ts:100  s.startsWith('s') ? s : 's'+s  - a NORMALISER, it adds the prefix when absent. Turning '4' into 's4'. Also pane30's half.

BAND A VERDICT: 353 lines, 418 call sites, 414 cleared with the reason, 2 watch, 1 recorded as correct construction, 1 not the pattern. NOTHING FILTERED - this band is fully examined, because anchoring let me clear whole classes by construction instead of by sampling.

And the standing one-liner: the 11 files in no slice are EXAMINED and clean; four in scope with zero call sites, seven out of scope with reasons, full detail on comment 1090 of this bead.

A FAILURE OF MINE, AND THE BEST FINDING OF THE SWEEP (TanElk).

FIRST, MY ERROR. For six ticks I recorded pane28 as idle and silent, escalating from "name your bead" to "are you wedged, should I restart the pane". It was never silent. My pane checks capture 8 to 10 lines of scrollback; its replies were longer than that and sat above the window, so my liveness detector saw an empty prompt and my tail showed nothing. pane28 diagnosed it before I did: "your reads of the tracker land, my chat replies apparently don't." It had filed everything on beads the whole time - #1111 band A, #1090 the 11 files, #1108 the two lane failures - and I was asking for what it had already delivered. I now capture 40 lines. I also told it NOT to reduce its replies to bare ids, which it offered to do; the defect was my reading, and the remedy is not for the pane to say less.

WHAT IT HAD BEEN REPORTING, unread:
  - band A complete
  - both previously unaccounted bun-lane failures identified: mass-energy-low-speed-ui.test.tsx
    (real, a TypeError predating its involvement - it now passes 6/0) and GlossFace.render.test.tsx
    (a stale expectation left by a11y commit 0c890a0f)
  - a self-disclosed error: its commit 9f9a4f20 swept twelve files of a peer's staged work
  - two unfixed substring hits, one of which is the sharpest thing this sweep has produced

THE AUTHORSHIP DEFECT, verified by me at src/content/checks/review/authorship.ts:89 -

    reviewerId.toLowerCase().includes("claude")   ->   classified "model-reviewer"

Any reviewer whose id contains "claude" is recorded as a MODEL reviewer. Claude is an ordinary human given name - Debussy, Monet, Shannon, Lévi-Strauss - and in a critical edition of 1905 papers drawing on French and German scholarship, a human reviewer named Claude is entirely plausible. The consequence is not a mislabelled log line: a human being's review would be discounted as machine-generated, in a project whose provenance claims ARE the product. Reviewer provenance is the thing this edition asks to be trusted on.

It is also the purest instance of the class: a substring of a name standing in for a category of author.

The fix needs both halves - a human named Claude is not a model reviewer, AND a genuine model: prefixed id still is. Assigned to pane28, which found it.

comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION of b0efcd5a (TanElk). Verified by restoring the defect.

Baseline 10 pass / 0 fail. I re-inserted the vendor-word sniff into the classifier - reviewerId.toLowerCase().includes("claude") alongside the namespace checks - and re-ran: 9 pass / 1 fail, failing exactly on "a human whose name merely contains a vendor word is not a model reviewer". Restored byte-clean, 10 pass / 0 fail.

A NO-OP PLANT FIRST, AND I NEARLY READ IT AS A PASS. My first attempt matched an anchor that does not exist in the file and did not modify anything; the suite came back 10/0, which is indistinguishable from a working gate. I only knew because the edit asserted and because I grep the planted token count as a matter of course. Third time tonight one of my plants failed to apply. The habit that saves it is cheap: confirm the plant is IN the file before reading the result.

WHY THIS FIX IS BETTER THAN THE OBVIOUS ONE. pane28 anticipated and rejected the partial repair: "No word-boundary variant fixes it either: 'Claude Bernard' has 'claude' as a whole segment." A reviewer is not a machine because of the letters in their name, and no amount of tightening the string test makes that inference sound. The general statement it wrote is the right one - "Guessing whether a reviewer is a machine from the letters in their name cannot be made correct."

IT ALSO PROVED THE REMOVAL COSTS NOTHING, which is the part a weaker fix would have skipped. Three detection paths remain and it enumerated them: the agent:/model: namespace; the structural test refusing a reviewer whose authorship entry declares kind "model"; and the owners registry, where a reviewer absent from docs/OWNERS.md is refused as cross-projection-unknown-reviewer. Its conclusion is the decisive argument: "A model recorded honestly is caught by its namespace or its declared kind; one recorded dishonestly was never going to be caught by its name." The substring only ever caught models that were already announcing themselves.

AND THERE IS A TEST FOR THE ARGUMENT, not just the behaviour: "the structural path still refuses a model, so dropping the name sniff removes no coverage". Three tests - the fix, the control that a genuine model: prefix is still refused, and that one. I have not seen a pane test a coverage CLAIM before tonight.

The same commit removed an includes("gpt") arm with the identical defect.

comments.text:
pane31: band B complex-receiver sub-band swept. This is the population invisible to BOTH my earlier
passes, because the receiver is a cast, an array literal, a call or a chain rather than a bare
identifier.

POPULATION: 181 sites in scripts/, src/physics, src/experiments, src/equations, comments excluded.

THE DOMINANT SHAPE, 16 of them, is one idiom:

    process.argv[1].endsWith("<this-script>.ts")

That is a category test - "am I the entry module" - answered by a filename suffix. It is exactly
the shape this bead hunts, and it is used by sixteen scripts including quality-gates.ts,
run-node-only-tests.ts, check-receipts.ts and verify-facsimile-pins.ts.

SO I CHECKED THE PRECONDITION rather than judging the shape. The idiom is safe if and only if no
script's basename is a suffix of another's. Across 131 script files there are FIVE such collisions:

    license-inventory.ts   is a suffix of   verify-license-inventory.ts
    index.ts               is a suffix of   build-search-index.ts
    report.ts              is a suffix of   source-manifest-report.ts
    report.ts              is a suffix of   coverage-report.ts
    budgets.ts             is a suffix of   run-perf-budgets.ts

VERDICT: LATENT, NOT LIVE. Of the sixteen scripts using the guard, ZERO have a basename that is a
suffix of another script's. The five collisions all involve files that do not use the idiom -
license-inventory.ts, perf/report.ts, perf/budgets.ts and license-inventory/index.ts contain no
endsWith at all, which I verified per file rather than inferring.

The near miss is worth naming: run-perf-budgets.ts DOES import scripts/perf/budgets.ts. Had
budgets.ts carried the guard, running run-perf-budgets.ts would have satisfied
endsWith("budgets.ts") and executed budgets.ts's main block as a side effect of an import. The
collision is real; only the absence of the guard in that file prevents it.

So nothing to fix, and a precondition worth recording: the main-module idiom in this repository is
correct because of how the scripts happen to be named, not because the test is sound. Adding
scripts/gates.ts while quality-gates.ts carries the guard would break it silently, and nothing
checks that.

A METHOD NOTE, and it cost me a wrong answer first: my initial guard check was
`grep ... | head -1 || echo "(no guard)"`, which never prints the fallback because head exits 0 on
empty input. It printed four blanks that I could have read as four guards. Counting with grep -c
gave the real answer, zero in all four files.

BAND B RUNNING TOTAL
    string-receiver sub-band        8 sites, 8 cleared, 1 defect (ColorizedEquation, reported)
    complex-receiver sub-band     181 sites, 16 judged as one idiom, latent-not-live, 0 defects
    still filtered                 95 no-category-word, 30 array-ish name

compdef () {
	local opt autol type func delete eval new i ret=0 cmd svc 
	local -a match mbegin mend
	emulate -L zsh
	setopt extendedglob
	if (( ! $# ))
	then
		print -u2 "$0: I need arguments"
		return 1
	fi
	while getopts "anpPkKde" opt
	do
		case "$opt" in
			(a) autol=yes  ;;
			(n) new=yes  ;;
			([pPkK]) if [[ -n "$type" ]]
				then
					print -u2 "$0: type already set to $type"
					return 1
				fi
				if [[ "$opt" = p ]]
				then
					type=pattern 
				elif [[ "$opt" = P ]]
				then
					type=postpattern 
				elif [[ "$opt" = K ]]
				then
					type=widgetkey 
				else
					type=key 
				fi ;;
			(d) delete=yes  ;;
			(e) eval=yes  ;;
		esac
	done
	shift OPTIND-1
	if (( ! $# ))
	then
		print -u2 "$0: I need arguments"
		return 1
	fi
	if [[ -z "$delete" ]]
	then
		if [[ -z "$eval" ]] && [[ "$1" = *\=* ]]
		then
			while (( $# ))
			do
				if [[ "$1" = *\=* ]]
				then
					cmd="${1%%\=*}" 
					svc="${1#*\=}" 
					func="$_comps[${_services[(r)$svc]:-$svc}]" 
					[[ -n ${_services[$svc]} ]] && svc=${_services[$svc]} 
					[[ -z "$func" ]] && func="${${_patcomps[(K)$svc][1]}:-${_postpatcomps[(K)$svc][1]}}" 
					if [[ -n "$func" ]]
					then
						_comps[$cmd]="$func" 
						_services[$cmd]="$svc" 
					else
						print -u2 "$0: unknown command or service: $svc"
						ret=1 
					fi
				else
					print -u2 "$0: invalid argument: $1"
					ret=1 
				fi
				shift
			done
			return ret
		fi
		func="$1" 
		[[ -n "$autol" ]] && autoload -rUz "$func"
		shift
		case "$type" in
			(widgetkey) while [[ -n $1 ]]
				do
					if [[ $# -lt 3 ]]
					then
						print -u2 "$0: compdef -K requires <widget> <comp-widget> <key>"
						return 1
					fi
					[[ $1 = _* ]] || 1="_$1" 
					[[ $2 = .* ]] || 2=".$2" 
					[[ $2 = .menu-select ]] && zmodload -i zsh/complist
					zle -C "$1" "$2" "$func"
					if [[ -n $new ]]
					then
						bindkey "$3" | IFS=$' \t' read -A opt
						[[ $opt[-1] = undefined-key ]] && bindkey "$3" "$1"
					else
						bindkey "$3" "$1"
					fi
					shift 3
				done ;;
			(key) if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]
				then
					print -u2 "$0: missing keys"
					return 1
				fi
				if [[ $1 = .* ]]
				then
					[[ $1 = .menu-select ]] && zmodload -i zsh/complist
					zle -C "$func" "$1" "$func"
				else
					[[ $1 = menu-select ]] && zmodload -i zsh/complist
					zle -C "$func" ".$1" "$func"
				fi
				shift
				for i
				do
					if [[ -n $new ]]
					then
						bindkey "$i" | IFS=$' \t' read -A opt
						[[ $opt[-1] = undefined-key ]] || continue
					fi
					bindkey "$i" "$func"
				done ;;
			(*) while (( $# ))
				do
					if [[ "$1" = -N ]]
					then
						type=normal 
					elif [[ "$1" = -p ]]
					then
						type=pattern 
					elif [[ "$1" = -P ]]
					then
						type=postpattern 
					else
						case "$type" in
							(pattern) if [[ $1 = (#b)(*)=(*) ]]
								then
									_patcomps[$match[1]]="=$match[2]=$func" 
								else
									_patcomps[$1]="$func" 
								fi ;;
							(postpattern) if [[ $1 = (#b)(*)=(*) ]]
								then
									_postpatcomps[$match[1]]="=$match[2]=$func" 
								else
									_postpatcomps[$1]="$func" 
								fi ;;
							(*) if [[ "$1" = *\=* ]]
								then
									cmd="${1%%\=*}" 
									svc=yes 
								else
									cmd="$1" 
									svc= 
								fi
								if [[ -z "$new" || -z "${_comps[$1]}" ]]
								then
									_comps[$cmd]="$func" 
									[[ -n "$svc" ]] && _services[$cmd]="${1#*\=}" 
								fi ;;
						esac
					fi
					shift
				done ;;
		esac
	else
		case "$type" in
			(pattern) unset "_patcomps[$^@]" ;;
			(postpattern) unset "_postpatcomps[$^@]" ;;
			(key) print -u2 "$0: cannot restore key bindings"
				return 1 ;;
			(*) unset "_comps[$^@]" ;;
		esac
	fi
}

compgen () {
	local opts prefix suffix job OPTARG OPTIND ret=1 
	local -a name res results jids
	local -A shortopts
	emulate -L sh
	setopt kshglob noshglob braceexpand nokshautoload
	shortopts=(a alias b builtin c command d directory e export f file g group j job k keyword u user v variable) 
	while getopts "o:A:G:C:F:P:S:W:X:abcdefgjkuv" name
	do
		case $name in
			([abcdefgjkuv]) OPTARG="${shortopts[$name]}"  ;&
			(A) case $OPTARG in
					(alias) results+=("${(k)aliases[@]}")  ;;
					(arrayvar) results+=("${(k@)parameters[(R)array*]}")  ;;
					(binding) results+=("${(k)widgets[@]}")  ;;
					(builtin) results+=("${(k)builtins[@]}" "${(k)dis_builtins[@]}")  ;;
					(command) results+=("${(k)commands[@]}" "${(k)aliases[@]}" "${(k)builtins[@]}" "${(k)functions[@]}" "${(k)reswords[@]}")  ;;
					(directory) setopt bareglobqual
						results+=(${IPREFIX}${PREFIX}*${SUFFIX}${ISUFFIX}(N-/)) 
						setopt nobareglobqual ;;
					(disabled) results+=("${(k)dis_builtins[@]}")  ;;
					(enabled) results+=("${(k)builtins[@]}")  ;;
					(export) results+=("${(k)parameters[(R)*export*]}")  ;;
					(file) setopt bareglobqual
						results+=(${IPREFIX}${PREFIX}*${SUFFIX}${ISUFFIX}(N)) 
						setopt nobareglobqual ;;
					(function) results+=("${(k)functions[@]}")  ;;
					(group) emulate zsh
						_groups -U -O res
						emulate sh
						setopt kshglob noshglob braceexpand
						results+=("${res[@]}")  ;;
					(hostname) emulate zsh
						_hosts -U -O res
						emulate sh
						setopt kshglob noshglob braceexpand
						results+=("${res[@]}")  ;;
					(job) results+=("${savejobtexts[@]%% *}")  ;;
					(keyword) results+=("${(k)reswords[@]}")  ;;
					(running) jids=("${(@k)savejobstates[(R)running*]}") 
						for job in "${jids[@]}"
						do
							results+=(${savejobtexts[$job]%% *}) 
						done ;;
					(stopped) jids=("${(@k)savejobstates[(R)suspended*]}") 
						for job in "${jids[@]}"
						do
							results+=(${savejobtexts[$job]%% *}) 
						done ;;
					(setopt|shopt) results+=("${(k)options[@]}")  ;;
					(signal) results+=("SIG${^signals[@]}")  ;;
					(user) results+=("${(k)userdirs[@]}")  ;;
					(variable) results+=("${(k)parameters[@]}")  ;;
					(helptopic)  ;;
				esac ;;
			(F) COMPREPLY=() 
				local -a args
				args=("${words[0]}" "${@[-1]}" "${words[CURRENT-2]}") 
				() {
					typeset -h words
					$OPTARG "${args[@]}"
				}
				results+=("${COMPREPLY[@]}")  ;;
			(G) setopt nullglob
				results+=(${~OPTARG}) 
				unsetopt nullglob ;;
			(W) results+=(${(Q)~=OPTARG})  ;;
			(C) results+=($(eval $OPTARG))  ;;
			(P) prefix="$OPTARG"  ;;
			(S) suffix="$OPTARG"  ;;
			(X) if [[ ${OPTARG[0]} = '!' ]]
				then
					results=("${(M)results[@]:#${OPTARG#?}}") 
				else
					results=("${results[@]:#$OPTARG}") 
				fi ;;
		esac
	done
	print -l -r -- "$prefix${^results[@]}$suffix"
}

		}
	elif [[ "${OSTYPE}" == (cygwin|msys)* ]]
	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" > /dev/clipboard
		}
		clippaste () {
			cat /dev/clipboard
		}
	elif (( $+commands[clip.exe] )) && (( $+commands[powershell.exe] ))
	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | clip.exe
		}

		}
	elif [ -n "${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-}" ] && (( ${+commands[wl-copy]} )) && (( ${+commands[wl-paste]} ))
	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | wl-copy &> /dev/null &|
		}
		clippaste () {
			wl-paste --no-newline
		}
	elif [ -n "${DISPLAY:-}" ] && (( ${+commands[xsel]} ))
	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | xsel --clipboard --input
		}
		clippaste () {
			xsel --clipboard --output
		}
	elif [ -n "${DISPLAY:-}" ] && (( ${+commands[xclip]} ))
	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | xclip -selection clipboard -in &> /dev/null &|
		}
		clippaste () {
			xclip -out -selection clipboard
		}
	elif (( ${+commands[lemonade]} ))
	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | lemonade copy
		}
		clippaste () {
			lemonade paste
		}
	elif (( ${+commands[doitclient]} ))
	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | doitclient wclip
		}
		clippaste () {
			doitclient wclip -r
		}

	then

			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | win32yank -i
		}

	then
		clipcopy () {
			cat "${1:-/dev/stdin}" | termux-clipboard-set
		}

	elif [ -n "${TMUX:-}" ] && (( ${+commands[tmux]} ))
	then
		clipcopy () {

		}
		clippaste () {
			tmux save-buffer -
		}
	else

			local clipcmd="${1}" 
			shift
			if detect-clipboard
			then

			else

			fi
		}

		}

		}
		return 1
	fi

is-at-least () {
	emulate -L zsh
	local IFS=".-" min_cnt=0 ver_cnt=0 part min_ver version order 
	min_ver=(${=1}) 
	version=(${=2:-$ZSH_VERSION} 0) 
	while (( $min_cnt <= ${#min_ver} ))
	do
		while [[ "$part" != <-> ]]
		do
			(( ++ver_cnt > ${#version} )) && return 0
			if [[ ${version[ver_cnt]} = *[0-9][^0-9]* ]]
			then
				order=(${version[ver_cnt]} ${min_ver[ver_cnt]}) 
				if [[ ${version[ver_cnt]} = <->* ]]
				then
					[[ $order != ${${(On)order}} ]] && return 1
				else
					[[ $order != ${${(O)order}} ]] && return 1
				fi
				[[ $order[1] != $order[2] ]] && return 0
			fi
			part=${version[ver_cnt]##*[^0-9]} 
		done
		while true
		do
			(( ++min_cnt > ${#min_ver} )) && return 0
			[[ ${min_ver[min_cnt]} = <-> ]] && break
		done
		(( part > min_ver[min_cnt] )) && return 0
		(( part < min_ver[min_cnt] )) && return 1
		part='' 
	done
}

my_git_formatter () {
	emulate -L zsh
	if [[ -n $P9K_CONTENT ]]
	then
		typeset -g my_git_format=$P9K_CONTENT 
		return
	fi
	local meta='%7F' 
	local clean='%0F' 
	local modified='%0F' 
	local untracked='%0F' 
	local conflicted='%1F' 
	local res
	if [[ -n $VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH ]]
	then
		local branch=${(V)VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH} 
		(( $#branch > 32 )) && branch[13,-13]="…" 
		res+="${clean}${(g::)POWERLEVEL9K_VCS_BRANCH_ICON}${branch//\%/%%}" 
	fi
	if [[ -n $VCS_STATUS_TAG && -z $VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH ]]
	then
		local tag=${(V)VCS_STATUS_TAG} 
		(( $#tag > 32 )) && tag[13,-13]="…" 
		res+="${meta}#${clean}${tag//\%/%%}" 
	fi
	[[ -z $VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH && -z $VCS_STATUS_TAG ]] && res+="${meta}@${clean}${VCS_STATUS_COMMIT[1,8]}" 
	if [[ -n ${VCS_STATUS_REMOTE_BRANCH:#$VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH} ]]
	then
		res+="${meta}:${clean}${(V)VCS_STATUS_REMOTE_BRANCH//\%/%%}" 
	fi
	if [[ $VCS_STATUS_COMMIT_SUMMARY == (|*[^[:alnum:]])(wip|WIP)(|[^[:alnum:]]*) ]]
	then
		res+=" ${modified}wip" 
	fi
	if (( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD || VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND ))
	then
		(( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" ${clean}⇣${VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND}" 
		(( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD && !VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" " 
		(( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD  )) && res+="${clean}⇡${VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD}" 
	elif [[ -n $VCS_STATUS_REMOTE_BRANCH ]]
	then
		
	fi
	(( VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" ${clean}⇠${VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_BEHIND}" 
	(( VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_AHEAD && !VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" " 
	(( VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_AHEAD  )) && res+="${clean}⇢${VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_AHEAD}" 
	(( VCS_STATUS_STASHES        )) && res+=" ${clean}*${VCS_STATUS_STASHES}" 
	[[ -n $VCS_STATUS_ACTION ]] && res+=" ${conflicted}${VCS_STATUS_ACTION}" 
	(( VCS_STATUS_NUM_CONFLICTED )) && res+=" ${conflicted}~${VCS_STATUS_NUM_CONFLICTED}" 
	(( VCS_STATUS_NUM_STAGED     )) && res+=" ${modified}+${VCS_STATUS_NUM_STAGED}" 
	(( VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNSTAGED   )) && res+=" ${modified}!${VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNSTAGED}" 
	(( VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNTRACKED  )) && res+=" ${untracked}${(g::)POWERLEVEL9K_VCS_UNTRACKED_ICON}${VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNTRACKED}" 
	(( VCS_STATUS_HAS_UNSTAGED == -1 )) && res+=" ${modified}─" 
	typeset -g my_git_format=$res 
}

			(*) job_id=${(k)jobtexts[(r)${(Q)jobspec}*]}  ;;
		esac
		if [[ -n "${jobtexts[$job_id]}" ]]
		then
			1="${jobtexts[$job_id]}" 
			2="${jobtexts[$job_id]}"

	fi

omz_urldecode () {
	emulate -L zsh
	local encoded_url=$1 
	local caller_encoding=$langinfo[CODESET] 
	local LC_ALL=C 
	export LC_ALL
	local tmp=${encoded_url:gs/+/ /} 
	tmp=${tmp:gs/\\/\\\\/} 
	tmp=${tmp:gs/%/\\x/} 
	local decoded="$(printf -- "$tmp")" 
	local -a safe_encodings
	safe_encodings=(UTF-8 utf8 US-ASCII) 
	if [[ -z ${safe_encodings[(r)$caller_encoding]} ]]
	then
		decoded=$(echo -E "$decoded" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t $caller_encoding) 
		if [[ $? != 0 ]]
		then
			echo "Error converting string from UTF-8 to $caller_encoding" >&2
			return 1
		fi
	fi
	echo -E "$decoded"
}
omz_urlencode () {
	emulate -L zsh
	setopt norematchpcre
	local -a opts
	zparseopts -D -E -a opts r m P
	local in_str="$@" 
	local url_str="" 
	local spaces_as_plus
	if [[ -z $opts[(r)-P] ]]
	then
		spaces_as_plus=1 
	fi
	local str="$in_str" 
	local encoding=$langinfo[CODESET] 
	local safe_encodings
	safe_encodings=(UTF-8 utf8 US-ASCII) 
	if [[ -z ${safe_encodings[(r)$encoding]} ]]
	then
		str=$(echo -E "$str" | iconv -f $encoding -t UTF-8) 
		if [[ $? != 0 ]]
		then
			echo "Error converting string from $encoding to UTF-8" >&2
			return 1
		fi
	fi
	local i byte ord LC_ALL=C 
	export LC_ALL
	local reserved=';/?:@&=+$,' 
	local mark='_.!~*''()-' 
	local dont_escape="[A-Za-z0-9" 
	if [[ -z $opts[(r)-r] ]]
	then
		dont_escape+=$reserved 
	fi
	if [[ -z $opts[(r)-m] ]]
	then
		dont_escape+=$mark 
	fi
	dont_escape+="]" 
	local url_str="" 
	for ((i = 1; i <= ${#str}; ++i )) do
		byte="$str[i]" 
		if [[ "$byte" =~ "$dont_escape" ]]
		then
			url_str+="$byte" 
		else
			if [[ "$byte" == " " && -n $spaces_as_plus ]]
			then
				url_str+="+" 
			elif [[ "$PREFIX" = *com.termux* ]]
			then
				url_str+="$byte" 
			else
				ord=$(( [##16] #byte )) 
				url_str+="%$ord" 
			fi
		fi
	done
	echo -E "$url_str"
}
open_command () {
	local open_cmd
	case "$OSTYPE" in
		(darwin*) open_cmd='open'  ;;
		(cygwin*) open_cmd='cygstart'  ;;
		(linux*) [[ "$(uname -r)" != *icrosoft* ]] && open_cmd='nohup xdg-open'  || {
				open_cmd='cmd.exe /c start ""' 
				[[ -e "$1" ]] && {
					1="$(wslpath -w "${1:a}")"  || return 1
				}
				[[ "$1" = (http|https)://* ]] && {
					1="$(echo "$1" | sed -E 's/([&|()<>^])/^\1/g')"  || return 1
				}
			} ;;
		(msys*) open_cmd='start ""'  ;;
		(*) echo "Platform $OSTYPE not supported"
			return 1 ;;
	esac
	if [[ -n "$BROWSER" && "$1" = (http|https)://* ]]
	then
		"$BROWSER" "$@"
		return
	fi
	${=open_cmd} "$@" &> /dev/null
}
p10k () {
	[[ $# != 1 || $1 != finalize ]] || {
		p10k-instant-prompt-finalize
		return 0
	}
	eval "$__p9k_intro_no_reply"
	if (( !ARGC ))
	then
		print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_usage >&2
		return 1
	fi
	case $1 in
		(segment) local REPLY
			local -a reply
			shift
			local -i OPTIND
			local OPTARG opt state bg=0 fg icon cond text ref=0 expand=0 
			while getopts ':s:b:f:i:c:t:reh' opt
			do
				case $opt in
					(s) state=$OPTARG  ;;
					(b) bg=$OPTARG  ;;
					(f) fg=$OPTARG  ;;
					(i) icon=$OPTARG  ;;
					(c) cond=${OPTARG:-'${:-}'}  ;;
					(t) text=$OPTARG  ;;
					(r) ref=1  ;;
					(e) expand=1  ;;
					(+r) ref=0  ;;
					(+e) expand=0  ;;
					(h) print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_segment_usage
						return 0 ;;
					(?) print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_segment_usage >&2
						return 1 ;;
				esac
			done
			if (( OPTIND <= ARGC ))
			then
				print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_segment_usage >&2
				return 1
			fi
			if [[ -z $_p9k__prompt_side ]]
			then
				print -rP -- "%1F[ERROR]%f %Bp10k segment%b: can be called only during prompt rendering." >&2
				if (( !ARGC ))
				then
					print -rP -- ""
					print -rP -- "For help, type:" >&2
					print -rP -- ""
					print -rP -- "  %2Fp10k%f %Bhelp%b %Bsegment%b" >&2
				fi
				return 1
			fi
			(( ref )) || icon=$'\1'$icon 
			typeset -i _p9k__has_upglob
			"_p9k_${_p9k__prompt_side}_prompt_segment" "prompt_${_p9k__segment_name}${state:+_${${(U)state}//İ/I}}" "$bg" "${fg:-$_p9k_color1}" "$icon" "$expand" "$cond" "$text"
			return 0 ;;
		(display) if (( ARGC == 1 ))
			then
				print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_display_usage >&2
				return 1
			fi
			shift
			local -i k dump
			local opt prev new pair list name var
			while getopts ':har' opt
			do
				case $opt in
					(r) if (( __p9k_reset_state > 0 ))
						then
							__p9k_reset_state=2 
						else
							__p9k_reset_state=-1 
						fi ;;
					(a) dump=1  ;;
					(h) print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_display_usage
						return 0 ;;
					(?) print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_display_usage >&2
						return 1 ;;
				esac
			done
			if (( dump ))
			then
				reply=() 
				shift $((OPTIND-1))
				(( ARGC )) || set -- '*'
				for opt
				do
					for k in ${(u@)_p9k_display_k[(I)$opt]:/(#m)*/$_p9k_display_k[$MATCH]}
					do
						reply+=($_p9k__display_v[k,k+1]) 
					done
				done
				if (( __p9k_reset_state == -1 ))
				then
					_p9k_reset_prompt
				fi
				return 0
			fi
			local REPLY
			local -a reply
			for opt in "${@:$OPTIND}"
			do
				pair=(${(s:=:)opt}) 
				list=(${(s:,:)${pair[2]}}) 
				if [[ ${(b)pair[1]} == $pair[1] ]]
				then
					local ks=($_p9k_display_k[$pair[1]]) 
				else
					local ks=(${(u@)_p9k_display_k[(I)$pair[1]]:/(#m)*/$_p9k_display_k[$MATCH]}) 
				fi
				for k in $ks
				do
					if (( $#list == 1 ))
					then
						[[ $_p9k__display_v[k+1] == $list[1] ]] && continue
						new=$list[1] 
					else
						new=${list[list[(I)$_p9k__display_v[k+1]]+1]:-$list[1]} 
						[[ $_p9k__display_v[k+1] == $new ]] && continue
					fi
					_p9k__display_v[k+1]=$new 
					name=$_p9k__display_v[k] 
					if [[ $name == (empty_line|ruler) ]]
					then
						var=_p9k__${name}_i 
						[[ $new == show ]] && unset $var || typeset -gi $var=3
					elif [[ $name == (#b)(<->)(*) ]]
					then
						var=_p9k__${match[1]}${${${${match[2]//\/}/#left/l}/#right/r}/#gap/g} 
						[[ $new == hide ]] && typeset -g $var= || unset $var
					fi
					if (( __p9k_reset_state > 0 ))
					then
						__p9k_reset_state=2 
					else
						__p9k_reset_state=-1 
					fi
				done
			done
			if (( __p9k_reset_state == -1 ))
			then
				_p9k_reset_prompt
			fi ;;
		(configure) if (( ARGC > 1 ))
			then
				print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_configure_usage >&2
				return 1
			fi
			local REPLY
			local -a reply
			p9k_configure "$@" || return ;;
		(reload) if (( ARGC > 1 ))
			then
				print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_reload_usage >&2
				return 1
			fi
			(( $+_p9k__force_must_init )) || return 0
			_p9k__force_must_init=1  ;;
		(help) local var=__p9k_p10k_$2_usage 
			if (( $+parameters[$var] ))
			then
				print -rP -- ${(P)var}
				return 0
			elif (( ARGC == 1 ))
			then
				print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_usage
				return 0
			else
				print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_usage >&2
				return 1
			fi ;;
		(finalize) print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_finalize_usage >&2
			return 1 ;;
		(clear-instant-prompt) if (( $+__p9k_instant_prompt_active ))
			then
				_p9k_clear_instant_prompt
				unset __p9k_instant_prompt_active
			fi
			return 0 ;;
		(*) print -rP -- $__p9k_p10k_usage >&2
			return 1 ;;
	esac
}

pkill () {
	if [ -n "${CLAUDE_PID:-}" ] && [ -r "/proc/${CLAUDE_PID}/comm" ]
	then
		local _cc_skip="" _cc_a 
		local -a _cc_probe=() 
		for _cc_a in ${1+"$@"}
		do
			if [ -n "$_cc_skip" ]
			then
				_cc_skip="" 
				continue
			fi
			case "$_cc_a" in
				(--signal) _cc_skip=1  ;;
				(--signal=* | -e | --echo)  ;;
				(-[0-9]*)  ;;
				(-[PUGOF]?*) _cc_probe+=("$_cc_a")  ;;
				(-[ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ][ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0-9]*)  ;;
				(*) _cc_probe+=("$_cc_a")  ;;
			esac
		done
		if command pgrep ${_cc_probe[@]+"${_cc_probe[@]}"} 2> /dev/null | command grep -qx "${CLAUDE_PID}"
		then
			printf 'pkill: refusing to run — this pattern matches the Claude CLI process (PID %s). Narrow the pattern, or target your own children with `pkill -P $$ ...`.\n' "${CLAUDE_PID}" >&2
			return 1
		fi
	fi
	command pkill ${1+"$@"}
}

prompt_asdf () {
	_p9k_asdf_check_meta || _p9k_asdf_init_meta || return
	local -A versions
	local -a stat
	local -i has_global
	local dirs=($_p9k__parent_dirs) 
	local mtimes=($_p9k__parent_mtimes) 
	if [[ $dirs[-1] != ~ ]]
	then
		zstat -A stat +mtime ~ 2> /dev/null || return
		dirs+=(~) 
		mtimes+=($stat[1]) 
	fi
	local elem
	for elem in ${(@)${:-{1..$#dirs}}/(#m)*/${${:-$MATCH:$_p9k__asdf_dir2files[$dirs[MATCH]]}#$MATCH:$mtimes[MATCH]:}}
	do
		if [[ $elem == *:* ]]
		then
			local dir=$dirs[${elem%%:*}] 
			zstat -A stat +mtime $dir 2> /dev/null || return
			local files=($dir/.tool-versions(N) $dir/${(k)^_p9k_asdf_file_info}(N)) 
			_p9k__asdf_dir2files[$dir]=$stat[1]:${(pj:\0:)files} 
		else
			local files=(${(0)elem}) 
		fi
		if [[ ${files[1]:h} == ~ ]]
		then
			has_global=1 
			local -A local_versions=(${(kv)versions}) 
			versions=() 
		fi
		local file
		for file in $files
		do
			[[ $file == */.tool-versions ]]
			_p9k_asdf_parse_version_file $file $? || return
		done
	done
	if (( ! has_global ))
	then
		has_global=1 
		local -A local_versions=(${(kv)versions}) 
		versions=() 
	fi
	if [[ -r $ASDF_DEFAULT_TOOL_VERSIONS_FILENAME ]]
	then
		_p9k_asdf_parse_version_file $ASDF_DEFAULT_TOOL_VERSIONS_FILENAME 0 || return
	fi
	local plugin

	do
		local upper=${${(U)plugin//-/_}//İ/I} 
		if (( $+parameters[_POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_${upper}_SOURCES] ))
		then
			local sources=(${(P)${:-_POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_${upper}_SOURCES}}) 
		else
			local sources=($_POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_SOURCES) 
		fi
		local version="${(P)${:-ASDF_${upper}_VERSION}}" 
		if [[ -n $version ]]
		then
			(( $sources[(I)shell] )) || continue
		else
			version=$local_versions[$plugin] 
			if [[ -n $version ]]
			then
				(( $sources[(I)local] )) || continue
			else
				version=$versions[$plugin] 
				[[ -n $version ]] || continue
				(( $sources[(I)global] )) || continue
			fi
		fi
		if [[ $version == $versions[$plugin] ]]
		then
			if (( $+parameters[_POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_${upper}_PROMPT_ALWAYS_SHOW] ))
			then
				(( _POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_${upper}_PROMPT_ALWAYS_SHOW )) || continue
			else
				(( _POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_PROMPT_ALWAYS_SHOW )) || continue
			fi
		fi

		then
			if (( $+parameters[_POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_${upper}_SHOW_SYSTEM] ))
			then
				(( _POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_${upper}_SHOW_SYSTEM )) || continue
			else
				(( _POWERLEVEL9K_ASDF_SHOW_SYSTEM )) || continue
			fi
		fi
		_p9k_get_icon $0_$upper ${upper}_ICON $plugin
		_p9k_prompt_segment $0_$upper green $_p9k_color1 $'\1'$_p9k__ret 0 '' ${version//\%/%%}

prompt_command_execution_time () {
	(( $+P9K_COMMAND_DURATION_SECONDS )) || return
	(( P9K_COMMAND_DURATION_SECONDS >= _POWERLEVEL9K_COMMAND_EXECUTION_TIME_THRESHOLD )) || return
	if (( P9K_COMMAND_DURATION_SECONDS < 60 ))
	then
		if (( !_POWERLEVEL9K_COMMAND_EXECUTION_TIME_PRECISION ))
		then
			local -i sec=$((P9K_COMMAND_DURATION_SECONDS + 0.5)) 
		else
			local -F $_POWERLEVEL9K_COMMAND_EXECUTION_TIME_PRECISION sec=P9K_COMMAND_DURATION_SECONDS 
		fi
		local text=${sec}s 
	else
		local -i d=$((P9K_COMMAND_DURATION_SECONDS + 0.5)) 
		if [[ $_POWERLEVEL9K_COMMAND_EXECUTION_TIME_FORMAT == "H:M:S" ]]
		then
			local text=${(l.2..0.)$((d % 60))} 
			if (( d >= 60 ))
			then
				text=${(l.2..0.)$((d / 60 % 60))}:$text 
				if (( d >= 36000 ))
				then
					text=$((d / 3600)):$text 
				elif (( d >= 3600 ))
				then
					text=0$((d / 3600)):$text 
				fi
			fi
		else
			local text="$((d % 60))s" 
			if (( d >= 60 ))
			then
				text="$((d / 60 % 60))m $text" 
				if (( d >= 3600 ))
				then
					text="$((d / 3600 % 24))h $text" 
					if (( d >= 86400 ))
					then
						text="$((d / 86400))d $text" 
					fi
				fi
			fi
		fi
	fi
	_p9k_prompt_segment "$0" "red" "yellow1" 'EXECUTION_TIME_ICON' 0 '' $text
}

prompt_kubecontext () {
	if ! _p9k_cache_stat_get $0 ${(s.:.)${KUBECONFIG:-$HOME/.kube/config}}
	then
		local name namespace cluster user cloud_name cloud_account cloud_zone cloud_cluster text state
		() {
			local cfg && cfg=(${(f)"$(kubectl config view -o=yaml 2>/dev/null)"})  || return
			local qstr='"*"' 
			local str='([^"'\''|>]*|'$qstr')' 
			local ctx=(${(@M)cfg:#current-context: $~str}) 
			(( $#ctx == 1 )) || return
			name=${ctx[1]#current-context: } 
			local -i pos=${cfg[(i)contexts:]} 
			{
				(( pos <= $#cfg )) || return
				shift $pos cfg
				pos=${cfg[(i)  name: ${(b)name}]} 
				(( pos <= $#cfg )) || return
				(( --pos ))
				for ((; pos > 0; --pos)) do
					local line=$cfg[pos] 
					if [[ $line == '- context:' ]]
					then
						return 0
					elif [[ $line == (#b)'    cluster: '($~str) ]]
					then
						cluster=$match[1] 
						[[ $cluster == $~qstr ]] && cluster=$cluster[2,-2] 
					elif [[ $line == (#b)'    namespace: '($~str) ]]
					then
						namespace=$match[1] 
						[[ $namespace == $~qstr ]] && namespace=$namespace[2,-2] 
					elif [[ $line == (#b)'    user: '($~str) ]]
					then
						user=$match[1] 
						[[ $user == $~qstr ]] && user=$user[2,-2] 
					fi
				done
			} always {
				[[ $name == $~qstr ]] && name=$name[2,-2] 
			}
		}
		if [[ -n $name ]]
		then
			: ${namespace:=default}
			if [[ $cluster == (#b)gke_(?*)_(asia|australia|europe|northamerica|southamerica|us)-([a-z]##<->)(-[a-z]|)_(?*) ]]
			then
				cloud_name=gke 
				cloud_account=$match[1] 
				cloud_zone=$match[2]-$match[3]$match[4] 
				cloud_cluster=$match[5] 
				if (( ${_POWERLEVEL9K_KUBECONTEXT_SHORTEN[(I)gke]} ))
				then
					text=$cloud_cluster 
				fi
			elif [[ $cluster == (#b)arn:aws[[:alnum:]-]#:eks:([[:alnum:]-]##):([[:digit:]]##):cluster/(?*) ]]
			then
				cloud_name=eks 
				cloud_zone=$match[1] 
				cloud_account=$match[2] 
				cloud_cluster=$match[3] 
				if (( ${_POWERLEVEL9K_KUBECONTEXT_SHORTEN[(I)eks]} ))
				then
					text=$cloud_cluster 
				fi
			fi
			if [[ -z $text ]]
			then
				text=$name 
				if [[ $_POWERLEVEL9K_KUBECONTEXT_SHOW_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE == 1 || $namespace != (default|$name) ]]
				then
					text+="/$namespace" 
				fi
			fi
			local pat class
			for pat class in "${_POWERLEVEL9K_KUBECONTEXT_CLASSES[@]}"
			do
				if [[ $text == ${~pat} ]]
				then
					[[ -n $class ]] && state=_${${(U)class}//İ/I} 
					break
				fi
			done
		fi
		_p9k_cache_stat_set "${(g::)name}" "${(g::)namespace}" "${(g::)cluster}" "${(g::)user}" "${(g::)cloud_name}" "${(g::)cloud_account}" "${(g::)cloud_zone}" "${(g::)cloud_cluster}" "${(g::)text}" "$state"
	fi
	typeset -g P9K_KUBECONTEXT_NAME=$_p9k__cache_val[1] 
	typeset -g P9K_KUBECONTEXT_NAMESPACE=$_p9k__cache_val[2] 
	typeset -g P9K_KUBECONTEXT_CLUSTER=$_p9k__cache_val[3] 
	typeset -g P9K_KUBECONTEXT_USER=$_p9k__cache_val[4] 
	typeset -g P9K_KUBECONTEXT_CLOUD_NAME=$_p9k__cache_val[5]

prompt_package () {
	unset P9K_PACKAGE_NAME P9K_PACKAGE_VERSION
	_p9k_upglob package.json -. && return
	local file=$_p9k__parent_dirs[$?]/package.json 
	if ! _p9k_cache_stat_get $0 $file
	then
		() {
			local data field
			local -A found
			{
				data="$(<$file)"  || return
			} 2> /dev/null
			data=${${data//$'\r'}##[[:space:]]#} 
			[[ $data == '{'* ]] || return
			data[1]= 
			local -i depth=1 
			while true
			do
				data=${data##[[:space:]]#} 
				[[ -n $data ]] || return
				case $data[1] in
					('{'|'[') data[1]= 
						(( ++depth )) ;;
					('}'|']') data[1]= 
						(( --depth > 0 )) || return ;;
					(':') data[1]=  ;;
					(',') data[1]= 
						field=  ;;
					([[:alnum:].]) data=${data##[[:alnum:].]#}  ;;
					('"') local tail=${data##\"([^\"\\]|\\?)#} 
						[[ $tail == '"'* ]] || return
						local s=${data:1:-$#tail} 
						data=${tail:1} 
						(( depth == 1 )) || continue
						if [[ -z $field ]]
						then
							field=${s:-x} 
						elif [[ $field == (name|version) ]]
						then
							(( ! $+found[$field] )) || return
							[[ -n $s ]] || return
							[[ $s != *($'\n'|'\')* ]] || return
							found[$field]=$s 
							(( $#found == 2 )) && break
						fi ;;
					(*) return 1 ;;
				esac
			done
			_p9k_cache_stat_set 1 $found[name] $found[version]
			return 0
		} || _p9k_cache_stat_set 0
	fi
	(( _p9k__cache_val[1] )) || return
	P9K_PACKAGE_NAME=$_p9k__cache_val[2] 
	P9K_PACKAGE_VERSION=$_p9k__cache_val[3] 
	_p9k_prompt_segment "$0" "cyan" "$_p9k_color1" PACKAGE_ICON 0 '' ${P9K_PACKAGE_VERSION//\%/%%}
}

	if ! _p9k_cache_get $0 $_p9k__status $_p9k__pipestatus
	then
		(( _p9k__status )) && local state=ERROR  || local state=OK 
		if (( _POWERLEVEL9K_STATUS_EXTENDED_STATES ))
		then
			if (( _p9k__status ))
			then
				if (( $#_p9k__pipestatus > 1 ))
				then
					state+=_PIPE 
				elif (( _p9k__status > 128 ))
				then
					state+=_SIGNAL 
				fi
			elif [[ "$_p9k__pipestatus" == *[1-9]* ]]
			then
				state+=_PIPE 
			fi
		fi
		_p9k__cache_val=(:) 
		if (( _POWERLEVEL9K_STATUS_$state ))
		then
			if (( _POWERLEVEL9K_STATUS_SHOW_PIPESTATUS ))
			then
				local text=${(j:|:)${(@)_p9k__pipestatus:/(#b)(*)/$_p9k_exitcode2str[$match[1]+1]}} 
			else
				local text=$_p9k_exitcode2str[_p9k__status+1] 
			fi
			if (( _p9k__status ))
			then
				if (( !_POWERLEVEL9K_STATUS_CROSS && _POWERLEVEL9K_STATUS_VERBOSE ))
				then
					_p9k__cache_val=($0_$state red yellow1 CARRIAGE_RETURN_ICON 0 '' "$text") 
				else
					_p9k__cache_val=($0_$state $_p9k_color1 red FAIL_ICON 0 '' '') 
				fi
			elif (( _POWERLEVEL9K_STATUS_VERBOSE || _POWERLEVEL9K_STATUS_OK_IN_NON_VERBOSE ))
			then
				[[ $state == OK ]] && text='' 
				_p9k__cache_val=($0_$state "$_p9k_color1" green OK_ICON 0 '' "$text") 
			fi
		fi
		if (( $#_p9k__pipestatus < 3 ))
		then

		fi
	fi
	_p9k_prompt_segment "${(@)_p9k__cache_val}"

	then

				_p9k__state_dump_scheduled=1 
			else

			fi
			return
		fi
		_p9k_timewarrior_file_name=${${(AO)files}[1]} 
	fi
	if ! zstat -A stat +mtime -- $dir $_p9k_timewarrior_file_name 2> /dev/null
	then

		return

	{

regexp-replace () {
	argv=("$1" "$2" "$3") 
	4=0 
	[[ -o re_match_pcre ]] && 4=1 
	emulate -L zsh
	local MATCH MBEGIN MEND
	local -a match mbegin mend
	if (( $4 ))
	then
		zmodload zsh/pcre || return 2
		pcre_compile -- "$2" && pcre_study || return 2
		4=0 6= 
		local ZPCRE_OP
		while pcre_match -b -n $4 -- "${(P)1}"
		do
			5=${(e)3} 
			argv+=(${(s: :)ZPCRE_OP} "$5") 
			4=$((argv[-2] + (argv[-3] == argv[-2]))) 
		done
		(($# > 6)) || return
		set +o multibyte
		5= 6=1 
		for 2 3 4 in "$@[7,-1]"
		do
			5+=${(P)1[$6,$2]}$4 
			6=$(($3 + 1)) 
		done
		5+=${(P)1[$6,-1]} 
	else
		4=${(P)1} 
		while [[ -n $4 ]]
		do
			if [[ $4 =~ $2 ]]
			then
				5+=${4[1,MBEGIN-1]}${(e)3} 
				if ((MEND < MBEGIN))
				then
					((MEND++))
					5+=${4[1]} 
				fi
				4=${4[MEND+1,-1]} 
				6=1 
			else
				break
			fi
		done
		[[ -n $6 ]] || return
		5+=$4 
	fi
	eval $1=\$5
}

sudo-command-line () {
	[[ -z $BUFFER ]] && LBUFFER="$(fc -ln -1)" 
	local WHITESPACE="" 
	if [[ ${LBUFFER:0:1} = " " ]]
	then
		WHITESPACE=" " 
		LBUFFER="${LBUFFER:1}" 
	fi
	{
		local EDITOR=${SUDO_EDITOR:-${VISUAL:-$EDITOR}} 
		if [[ -z "$EDITOR" ]]
		then
			case "$BUFFER" in
				(sudo\ -e\ *) __sudo-replace-buffer "sudo -e" "" ;;
				(sudo\ *) __sudo-replace-buffer "sudo" "" ;;
				(*) LBUFFER="sudo $LBUFFER"  ;;
			esac
			return
		fi
		local cmd="${${(Az)BUFFER}[1]}" 
		local realcmd="${${(Az)aliases[$cmd]}[1]:-$cmd}" 
		local editorcmd="${${(Az)EDITOR}[1]}" 
		if [[ "$realcmd" = (\$EDITOR|$editorcmd|${editorcmd:c}) || "${realcmd:c}" = ($editorcmd|${editorcmd:c}) ]] || builtin which -a "$realcmd" | command grep -Fx -q "$editorcmd"
		then
			__sudo-replace-buffer "$cmd" "sudo -e"
			return
		fi
		case "$BUFFER" in
			($editorcmd\ *) __sudo-replace-buffer "$editorcmd" "sudo -e" ;;
			(\$EDITOR\ *) __sudo-replace-buffer '$EDITOR' "sudo -e" ;;
			(sudo\ -e\ *) __sudo-replace-buffer "sudo -e" "$EDITOR" ;;
			(sudo\ *) __sudo-replace-buffer "sudo" "" ;;
			(*) LBUFFER="sudo $LBUFFER"  ;;
		esac
	} always {
		LBUFFER="${WHITESPACE}${LBUFFER}" 
		zle && zle redisplay
	}
}

zrecompile () {
	setopt localoptions extendedglob noshwordsplit noksharrays
	local opt check quiet zwc files re file pre ret map tmp mesg pats
	tmp=() 
	while getopts ":tqp" opt
	do
		case $opt in
			(t) check=yes  ;;
			(q) quiet=yes  ;;
			(p) pats=yes  ;;
			(*) if [[ -n $pats ]]
				then
					tmp=($tmp $OPTARG) 
				else
					print -u2 zrecompile: bad option: -$OPTARG
					return 1
				fi ;;
		esac
	done
	shift OPTIND-${#tmp}-1
	if [[ -n $check ]]
	then
		ret=1 
	else
		ret=0 
	fi
	if [[ -n $pats ]]
	then
		local end num
		while (( $# ))
		do
			end=$argv[(i)--] 
			if [[ end -le $# ]]
			then
				files=($argv[1,end-1]) 
				shift end
			else
				files=($argv) 
				argv=() 
			fi
			tmp=() 
			map=() 
			OPTIND=1 
			while getopts :MR opt $files
			do
				case $opt in
					([MR]) map=(-$opt)  ;;
					(*) tmp=($tmp $files[OPTIND])  ;;
				esac
			done
			shift OPTIND-1 files
			(( $#files )) || continue
			files=($files[1] ${files[2,-1]:#*(.zwc|~)}) 
			(( $#files )) || continue
			zwc=${files[1]%.zwc}.zwc 
			shift 1 files
			(( $#files )) || files=(${zwc%.zwc}) 
			if [[ -f $zwc ]]
			then
				num=$(zcompile -t $zwc | wc -l) 
				if [[ num-1 -ne $#files ]]
				then
					re=yes 
				else
					re= 
					for file in $files
					do
						if [[ $file -nt $zwc ]]
						then
							re=yes 
							break
						fi
					done
				fi
			else
				re=yes 
			fi
			if [[ -n $re ]]
			then
				if [[ -n $check ]]
				then
					[[ -z $quiet ]] && print $zwc needs re-compilation
					ret=0 
				else
					[[ -z $quiet ]] && print -n "re-compiling ${zwc}: "
					if [[ -z "$quiet" ]] && {
							[[ ! -f $zwc ]] || mv -f $zwc ${zwc}.old
						} && zcompile $map $tmp $zwc $files
					then
						print succeeded
					elif ! {
							{
								[[ ! -f $zwc ]] || mv -f $zwc ${zwc}.old
							} && zcompile $map $tmp $zwc $files 2> /dev/null
						}
					then
						[[ -z $quiet ]] && print "re-compiling ${zwc}: failed"
						ret=1 
					fi
				fi
			fi
		done
		return ret
	fi
	if (( $# ))
	then
		argv=(${^argv}/*.zwc(ND) ${^argv}.zwc(ND) ${(M)argv:#*.zwc}) 
	else
		argv=(${^fpath}/*.zwc(ND) ${^fpath}.zwc(ND) ${(M)fpath:#*.zwc}) 
	fi
	argv=(${^argv%.zwc}.zwc) 
	for zwc
	do
		files=(${(f)"$(zcompile -t $zwc)"}) 
		if [[ $files[1] = *\(mapped\)* ]]
		then
			map=-M 
			mesg='succeeded (old saved)' 
		else
			map=-R 
			mesg=succeeded 
		fi
		if [[ $zwc = */* ]]
		then
			pre=${zwc%/*}/ 
		else
			pre= 
		fi
		if [[ $files[1] != *$ZSH_VERSION ]]
		then
			re=yes 
		else
			re= 
		fi
		files=(${pre}${^files[2,-1]:#/*} ${(M)files[2,-1]:#/*}) 
		[[ -z $re ]] && for file in $files
		do
			if [[ $file -nt $zwc ]]
			then
				re=yes 
				break
			fi
		done
		if [[ -n $re ]]
		then
			if [[ -n $check ]]
			then
				[[ -z $quiet ]] && print $zwc needs re-compilation
				ret=0 
			else
				[[ -z $quiet ]] && print -n "re-compiling ${zwc}: "
				tmp=(${^files}(N)) 
				if [[ $#tmp -ne $#files ]]
				then
					[[ -z $quiet ]] && print 'failed (missing files)'
					ret=1 
				else
					if [[ -z "$quiet" ]] && mv -f $zwc ${zwc}.old && zcompile $map $zwc $files
					then
						print $mesg
					elif ! {
							mv -f $zwc ${zwc}.old && zcompile $map $zwc $files 2> /dev/null
						}
					then
						[[ -z $quiet ]] && print "re-compiling ${zwc}: failed"
						ret=1 
					fi
				fi
			fi
		fi
	done
	return ret
}

comments.text:
THE SWEEP HAS REACHED THE SCHOLARLY CORE (TanElk). Band C, 202 sites, two fail-open findings - and one of them guards the thing this edition exists to demonstrate.

am-qiv8, P1. AGENTS.md line 231 prohibits, in those words: "Deriving mass-energy equivalence with a body-energy formula that already assumes it (initializing E_0 = Mc^2 or gamma Mc^2)." That is the intellectual point of the mass-energy paper - the derivation must not assume what it proves.

The guard enforcing it, verifyChain.ts:213-219, matches a list of SPELLINGS:

    eqLower.includes("mc2") || eqLower.includes("mc²") || eqLower.includes("γmc²")
      || eqLower.includes("gamma mc") || eqLower.includes("gammamc")

E_0 = M c^2 matches none of them. Nor does m*c^2, nor c^2 M, nor M·c², nor any of the ordinary ways an editor would write it. The check fails OPEN, and it does so against the one circularity AGENTS.md names explicitly.

WHAT MAKES THIS THE SHARPEST FINDING OF THE SWEEP is not the mechanism - it is the same substring-for-category defect as the other twelve - it is WHAT IT GUARDS. This edition's scholarly claim is that its derivations are checked. A reader is asked to trust that the mass-energy chain does not smuggle in its conclusion. That trust rested on a check a space defeats, and no editor writing "E_0 = M c^2" in natural notation would have had any way to know.

THE FIX IS NOT MORE SPELLINGS. That is the reviewer-name lesson restated: guessing from the letters cannot be made correct, and enumerating five more spellings just moves the gap. Normalise or parse the equality and compare structurally. Both halves required: E_0 = M c^2 is refused, AND a genuinely symbolic rest energy still passes - without the second, deleting the guard satisfies the first.

am-jrjy, P2, is the same class across a module boundary. glossConventions.ts:64 decides whether a caught error is a VALIDATION failure to rethrow or an IO failure to downgrade to a warning, by matching the error's message TEXT - and that message is produced in a different module. Rewording a sentence in module A silently downgrades a validation failure in module B, and nothing links the two, so the coupling is invisible from both sides. Classify on structure - a type, a code, an instanceof - never on prose.

RUNNING TOTAL for the substring class: thirteen instances now, across lint config, coverage attribution, voice context, a release gate, manifest anchors, reviewer identity, and now a derivation-integrity guard. It started as a lint-adjacent curiosity and has reached the edition's central claim.

comments.text:
fix(license): stop calling a BSD-2-Clause text BSD-3-Clause (am-o44v)

Band C of the substring sweep, the population my proximity filter had excluded
and never examined, contained the highest-stakes instance found so far: licence
identification by substring, in the collector that feeds THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

    licenseText.includes("Redistribution and use in source and binary forms")
      -> "BSD-3-Clause"

That sentence opens BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause and BSD-4-Clause alike. The clause
that separates them is the third, "Neither the name ... may be used to endorse".
Without it the code still answered BSD-3-Clause.

Measured on an installed package rather than a constructed one:

    node_modules/entities        declares BSD-2-Clause
                                 LICENSE has the shared opening
                                 LICENSE has no third clause
                                 old classifier verdict: BSD-3-Clause

LATENT, NOT LIVE, and I checked rather than assumed: the branch runs only when a
package declares no license field, and zero installed packages are in that state,
so entities is identified from its manifest and never reaches it.

THE FIX REFUSES RATHER THAN GUESSES. Where the text cannot distinguish the BSD
family, licenseFromText now returns undefined and the caller records UNKNOWN. That
is deliberate: a licence is a rights claim, and emitting "BSD-2-Clause" would have

    proximity proxy would KEEP    79
    proximity proxy would DROP   201

never had: measured predictive value. Across my slice, roughly 50 array-receiver sites produced

an afternoon of reading, not a research project. Proxies were necessary when the population read as
763. For band B alone they are not, and every proxy we have tried has been wrong in a way we only
learned by accident.

short matchedText widens it further.

failure mode is silent suppression of violations nobody asked to suppress, and the person who adds

    "var(--accent)"        contains it   true

"variant" cannot happen. Same for the two constant prefixes in this slice:
SETTINGS_KEY_PREFIX is "am:settings:v1:" and SECONDARY_PANE_PREFIX is
"pane-b--", both delimiter-terminated.

COMMENT-LINE EXCLUSION is structural here rather than a filter: the checker
walks the AST, so a call inside a comment does not exist to be counted.

THE 18 STRING RECEIVERS
=====================================================================
All eighteen were already covered by my repo-wide pass and all eighteen hold up
on re-reading against the qualified-needle rule:

    a search box; notationSearch.ts:56, deliberately bidirectional;

    keys.ts:60 and paneIds.ts:22, fixed delimiter-terminated constants.

THE ARRAY POPULATION, AND THE ONE THING WORTH THE LOOK
=====================================================================
Reading it rather than filtering it surfaced three optional-chained membership
tests, where the question is not substring collision but WHAT UNDEFINED MEANS:

  alignment.ts:125   targets?.includes(targetId) ?? false
      Explicit. Undefined means no targets for this source. CORRECT.
  cardRules.ts:319   if (!card.admittedStages?.includes(context.stageId))
      A card with the field ABSENT is treated identically to a card admitting
      no stage, and both raise card-missing-citing-stage. Fail-closed and
      defensible for a knowledge card, but it does conflate absent with empty.
      Recorded, not filed.
  links.ts:53        !step?.labs.includes(currentLab)

I SUSPECTED THE THIRD OF A LATENT RUNTIME TypeError and it is not one. The
checker renders that receiver as `readonly string[] | undefined`, which I read
as "labs can be undefined" - so if step existed but labs did not, .includes
would throw. links.ts:6 declares `labs: readonly string[]`, REQUIRED. The
undefined in the rendered type comes from the optional chain on `step`, not
from the property. If step is undefined the chain short-circuits; if step
exists, labs is guaranteed. Safe.

Worth recording as a reading error others will repeat: the checker's type for
`a?.b.c()` describes the CHAIN, not `b`.

comments.text:
pane31 BAND A, re-derived with an AST + TYPE-CHECKER instrument. The corrected denominator first,
then the finding that the receiver-type split does not work here, then the judgements.

=== THE COMMAND ===

    bun run <scratchpad>/bandA.ts

It builds a ts.Program from the repository's own tsconfig.json (TypeScript 5.7.3, the same one
`bun run typecheck` uses), walks every SourceFile, and for each CallExpression whose callee is a
PropertyAccessExpression named includes | startsWith | endsWith records: the operator, whether the
first argument is a string literal, the RECEIVER'S TYPE from checker.getTypeAtLocation, and the
band. 3131 call sites repo-wide in 2.7 seconds. Comments cannot appear: they are not call
expressions, which is the defect that put verifyChain.ts:54 - a comment DESCRIBING a removed
defect - into my earlier grep results.

=== CORRECTED DENOMINATOR: 164 WAS 300 ===

Band A, my slice (scripts, src/physics, src/experiments, src/equations):

    300 sites     239 in code files, 61 in test files
                  161 startsWith, 139 endsWith

The old regex, \.(startsWith|endsWith)\(\s*"[^"]{2,14}"\s*\), run over the same files, sees 194
(155 code). So it could see 194 of 300. The gap is almost entirely the length window:

    literal length 1        60 sites   invisible to the regex
    literal length 2-14    208 sites
    literal length 15+      32 sites   invisible to the regex

The 60 one-character anchors are the ones a length-windowed regex is least entitled to skip, since
a one-character anchor is the weakest possible form of the test.

Direction of the error, checked rather than assumed: of the 194 regex hits in code files, 0 are on
comment lines. For the anchored operators the regex under-counts and does not over-count.

Repo-wide, for whoever is holding the other bands: A 687, B 907, C 1237, D 300. pane30's four-band
table put A at 735 and B at 972 by matching the call first; mine differ because the AST excludes
comments and JSX text. Neither is wrong about what it measured; both are far above the literal-only
figures the sweep started from.

=== THE RECEIVER-TYPE SPLIT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE IN BAND A ===

Asked for it, measured it, and it is constant:

    string receiver   300 of 300

Not a coincidence and not a property of this repository: startsWith and endsWith exist only on
String.prototype. An array has no startsWith. So the instrument that cut band B from 411 sites to
57 string receivers has, by construction, ZERO discriminating power over band A. Reporting "100%
string receivers, all suspect" would have been a 300-item worklist that means nothing.

What discriminates instead, since an anchored test cannot match mid-token at all: does the anchor
also match a LONGER member of the same namespace? That is a fact about the corpus, so it is
measured, not judged. Collecting every string literal in the program (46k) and asking which ones
each anchor also matches:

    210  the anchor is not alphanumeric: "?" "#" "/" "{" "|" "$" "\\" ".md"    syntax, not category
     90  word anchors, of which
         53  end at a delimiter - "src/", "data-", "content/", "https://", "host:sha256:"
             a subtree test, where the extensions ARE the intended members
         37  end MID-TOKEN, where an extension is a collision
             28 of those have at least one colliding literal in the repository
             24 of those are in code files
              9 match nothing else in the corpus and cannot collide today

Of the 24: 14 are process.argv[1].endsWith("<this file>.ts"), the main-module idiom, whose
"collisions" are literally other spellings of the same path. The remaining 10 I read individually.

=== ONE DEFECT, DEMONSTRATED AND FIXED: ec6e68a0 ===

scripts/license-inventory/collectDonor.ts:206, parseDonorAuditReuseTable, which reads section 5 of
DONOR_AUDIT.md - the table deciding which extracted donor files must carry the donor's licence
notices and rider language.

    line.startsWith("## 5. Reuse Table") || line.startsWith("## 5. ") || line.includes("Reuse Table")

Measured on the real 116 kB document:

    baseline, untouched                        20 rows
    one prose sentence added in section 2       0 rows
    the same sentence, two words changed       20 rows

The planted sentence is "See the Reuse Table in Section 5 for the per-seam decisions." - the
ordinary cross-reference an editor writes. It sets inSection5 at that line; the next `## ` heading
then hits the break before the real table is reached; every donor seam loses its row; a seam with
no row carries no notice requirement. Silent, and fails open on a rights obligation, triggered by
editing prose.

Now anchored on the heading NUMBER. The existing row-count assertion catches renumbering, so the
silent-empty case stays loud. The plant fails the new test by name (35 pass 1 fail) and the file
was restored byte-for-byte.

NOTE WHERE THE DEFECT WAS. The band A anchor at that line was fine; the defect was the LOOSE
disjunct written beside it. That generalises, so I searched for the shape directly: an anchored
test in a || chain with a string-receiver .includes(). 12 sites in my slice, non-test. It found
this one, and two more below. An author who wrote the anchored form knew the precise shape and
kept the loose one anyway, and the loose one decides every case.

=== ONE TIGHTENING REFUSED, WITH THE NUMBERS ===

Twelve lines below the fix, collectDonor.ts:345:

    row.decision.toLowerCase() === "reuse" || row.decision.toLowerCase().startsWith("reuse")

This has exactly the shape the sweep tightens, and I measured before touching it:

    === "reuse"          5 rows
    startsWith("reuse")  7 rows      "Reuse architecture", "Reuse with new identities"

The REDUNDANT arm is the exact one. Tightening to equality would have dropped two donor seams from
the licence inventory - failing open on the obligation the collector exists to record. It stays,
and a test now pins 7 > 5 so the tightening is not attempted again without the numbers. That is the
ac0d401b lesson applied before shipping rather than after.

=== THREE RECORDED, NOT FIXED ===

scripts/perf/budgetChangeCheck.ts:109   LATENT, fails open on an evidence requirement, BLOCKED
    f.includes(`-${id}.json`) || f.endsWith(`${id}.json`) decides whether a loosened perf budget has
    a committed measurement record. BOTH arms leak: a record for budget "initial-route-js" also
    satisfies a budget named "route-js". No two of the 8 current ids are hyphen-suffixes of each
    other, and perf/measurements/ does not exist, so nothing collides today. I did not fix it
    because closing it requires anchoring the whole filename, and the only evidence of the naming
    convention is one test fixture, 2026-09-17-initial-route-js.json. Inventing a convention to
    satisfy a gate is the wrong direction. The owner states the convention; then it is a two-line
    fix.

scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/networkLogClassifier.ts:6   NO CONSUMER
    lower.includes("worker") classifies any URL containing "worker" as a worker request, ahead of
    the .js arm. It is the bead's pattern in its purest form - a substring deciding a NetworkKind -
    and it is unreachable: the only reference to the module anywhere outside node_modules and .git
    is its own test. That test's one worker assertion, classifyNetworkRequest("blob:.../worker"),
    matches BOTH arms of the condition, so it cannot tell which one is load-bearing. Wire it or
    retire it; both are owner calls, and retiring needs permission.

scripts/align-editions.ts:100   watch, dev CLI
    (s) => s.startsWith("s") ? s : `s${s}` normalises a --sections option, so 3 becomes s3. A valid
    part heading, part-1, becomes spart-1, matches no id, and the alignment silently reports
    nothing rather than refusing the input. Same silent-empty family as the section 5 defect,
    lower stakes.

=== ONE WEAK CLAUSE OF MY OWN, NAMED ===

src/equations/derivations/verifyChain.ts:109, in citesForbiddenBodyEnergy, which I wrote for
am-qiv8:

    if (!/e0|e_0|\be\b|energy/.test(left) && !left.endsWith("e")) return false;

left.endsWith("e") is a one-character anchor and the regex already covers a standalone e, so the
clause's only effect is to admit symbols like ke or me as "names an energy" and widen refusal. It
fails toward refusing a legitimate chain, which for a circularity guard is the safe direction, and
tightening a guard to make it fire less is RH-1 shaped. Recording it as the weakest clause in my
own gate rather than quietly adjusting it.

=== WHAT BAND A IS WORTH, honestly ===

300 sites, 1 defect, and the defect was not in an anchored test. An anchored test cannot match
mid-token, so band A's yield comes almost entirely from what sits NEXT to the anchor. If anyone
picks up the rest, the 12-site anchored-beside-loose list is the part that paid; the 210 syntax
anchors were judged as a class and not read individually, and I am not claiming them clean.

SUBPROCESS-LANE CHECK: NO DIRECT HIT. Every subprocess-spawning test outside
bunfig's pathIgnorePatterns spawns bun or git, not node, so none of them can
take the EBADF path. Executed, not read. But the check surfaced a different
defect in the same family, and I got the lane matching wrong three times before
I got it right - which is the more useful half of this report.

=====================================================================
THE ANSWER
=====================================================================
    test files importing node:child_process AND calling a spawn family:  14
    of those, NOT in pathIgnorePatterns:                                  6

    src/content/manifest/report.test.ts                spawns bun
    src/content/coverage/coverageLedger.test.ts        spawns bun
    src/testing/checkRevisions.integration.test.ts     spawns git
    src/testing/brownianDemo.test.mjs                  spawns process.execPath
    src/testing/editions/alignEditions.test.ts         spawns process.execPath
    scripts/quality-gates/bunfigNodeOnlyTests.test.ts  spawns bun

EXECUTED, all six under `bun test`:
    10 pass 0 fail, 5 pass 0 fail, 1 pass 0 fail, 5 pass 0 fail,
    12 pass 0 fail, 5 pass 0 fail.

And the reason, measured rather than assumed - I ran the exact spawn from
alignEditions.test.ts:147 inside a bun test:

    execPath : /opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.3.13/bin/bun
    error    : (none)
    status   : 0
    stdout   : {"ok": true, "exitCode": 0, "slug": "brownian-motion", ...

process.execPath UNDER BUN IS BUN. bun spawning bun works. The bunfig comment
is precise about this and I should have read it that way first: the failure is
"posix_spawn OF NODE". Spawning a subprocess is not the trigger; spawning node
is. So these six are legitimately absent from the lane list.

=====================================================================
WHAT THE CHECK DID FIND: FOUR DORMANT VACUOUS PASSES
=====================================================================
src/testing/editions/alignEditions.test.ts, four times - lines 155, 168, 184, 194:

    const proc = spawnSync(process.execPath, ["scripts/align-editions.ts", ...]);
    if (proc.error && (proc.error as any).code === "EBADF") return;

A bare `return` before any assertion. If that branch is ever taken the test
PASSES HAVING ASSERTED NOTHING, and reports green.

It is dormant today for the reason above: execPath is bun, no EBADF. It becomes
live the moment anyone changes that spawn to node - which is exactly the change
the bunfig comment describes as the normal case. The file is also not in
pathIgnorePatterns, so if the guard ever fires there is no node lane running
those four assertions either. They would execute nowhere.

Six files carry this guard outside the lane, with roughly nine guards between
them. brownianDemo.test.mjs is the counter-example worth copying: it DETECTS
the runtime at line 57 and adapts, rather than swallowing an error and
returning.

I am not filing this as a substring finding because it is not one. It is the
lane rule you just put in scope: an assertion that cannot execute in the lane it
lives in, and in this case one that would announce success while not executing.

=====================================================================
I GOT THE LANE MATCHING WRONG THREE TIMES
=====================================================================
Worth recording because the sweep is about exactly this failure.

    1st  grep -q "\"$f\"" bunfig.toml
         Exact-string match against a config that uses GLOBS. Reported
         scripts/e2e/* and every *.e2e.test.ts as NOT IGNORED. All were.
    2nd  f.endswith(p[3:]) for "**/*.e2e.test.ts"
         Leaves the literal "*" in the needle, so it matched nothing.
         scripts/check-receipts.e2e.test.ts read as NOT IGNORED. It is ignored.
    3rd  f.endswith(p[4:])
         Correct. 6 in the lane, 6 outside.

Three iterations of a matching bug, in a sweep whose subject is matching bugs,
while writing the report about it. The first two produced confident output I
would have quoted. The only thing that caught them was checking a case I already
knew the answer to - scripts/e2e obviously IS in the lane, it is the first entry
in the file - and noticing my tool disagreed.

=====================================================================
STATE
=====================================================================
414 gating string-receiver sites; judged so far: 3 (extractionHygiene:167,
oneGrammar:71, oneGrammar:21) plus this lane pass. 0 defects, 1 dormant vacuous
pass recorded, 2 dead or harmless clauses recorded.

comments.text:
pane31 BAND A CONTINUED, with TanElk's two-halves lesson applied as a filter rather than as a note.
Denominator first, as before.

=== DENOMINATOR, unchanged and restated ===

Band A in my slice is 300 sites (239 code, 61 test), not the 164 the earlier regex could see. The
receiver-type split is 300 of 300 string, constant by construction, so it discriminates nothing
here. Anchor shape does: 210 syntax anchors, 53 delimiter-ending subtree anchors, 37 mid-token, of
which 24 are in code with a real corpus collision and 14 of those are the main-module idiom.

=== THE LESSON CHANGED THE ANSWER, NOT JUST THE WORDING ===

"A gate has two halves and they break independently" is not a reporting convention. Applied as a
question - is the predicate wrong, or is it never evaluated - it turned one of my three
recorded-not-fixed items into a P1 and a second into a different P1, and in both the predicate was
the smaller half.

--- am-czbe, P1 filed: the perf budget ratchet -------------------------------------------

I had recorded scripts/perf/budgetChangeCheck.ts:109 as "a latent substring leak, blocked on a
naming convention". That was the predicate half and it was the less serious one.

The measuring half: the check reads its base from `git show HEAD:perf/budgets.json` and compares it
with the working tree. On a clean checkout those are the same bytes. Observed on the real tree, not
inferred:

    git status --short perf/budgets.json     clean
    bun scripts/perf-budget-diff.ts          "No performance budget modifications detected."
                                             "PASSED"   exit 0

The gate is registered requiredInCi: true, cadence every-run. CI checks out a commit with a clean
tree, so PASSED is the only verdict it can ever produce. It detects a budget loosened in an
uncommitted edit and is blind to every loosening that has been committed - which is every loosening
CI will see. The code's own comment says "HEAD~1 or merge-base", so HEAD was not the intent.

The predicate half, proven separately with a fixture and a control, no repository file touched:

    budget "route-js" loosened
      no measurement files                  ok=false, 1 violation     (baseline reaches the state)
      only 2026-09-17-initial-route-js.json ok=true,  0 violations    (another budget's record
                                                                       accepted as evidence)
      its own record                        ok=true,  0 violations

Both halves are owner calls, which is why neither was fixed: the base ref is a design choice, and
anchoring the filename requires a convention that exists nowhere but one test fixture.

--- am-xyxk, P1 filed: five conformance readers nothing consumes --------------------------

networkLogClassifier.ts came out of band A for `lower.includes("worker")` deciding a NetworkKind.
Asking which half is broken found the larger problem: identityReader, networkLogClassifier,
performanceMarkReader, rafSampler and tapeUrlBuilder each have exactly one importer, their own
test. The composer the browser-acceptance gate invokes, runtime-conformance/run.ts, imports
./checks.ts and ./fixtureRegistration.ts and nothing else, and checks.ts imports no local module at
all.

All five test files DO run - they are in the node lane, derived by calling nodeOnlyTestArgs on
bunfig.toml rather than by reading lane output: 45 files, 8 of them under runtime-conformance. So
the suite is green, the readers are "tested", and nothing that reads a browser consults them.

That is what an unconsumed measurement decays into. The classifier's test asserts
classifyNetworkRequest("blob:http://127.0.0.1/worker") is a worker, which satisfies BOTH arms of
the condition it is testing, so it would stay green if either arm were deleted. Nobody noticed the
predicate because nothing depended on the answer.

=== I CHECKED THE SAME QUESTION AGAINST MY OWN FIX ===

ec6e68a0 added two tests to scripts/license-inventory.test.ts, and "the plant fails by name" is a
claim about a test file, not about a lane. That file is not in bunfig's pathIgnorePatterns and is
not in the node lane's 45, so it is in the bun lane and its assertions run. Stated because the
facsimile correction is precisely a case where a measurement ran and an assertion did not, and I am
not entitled to assume my own is different.

One note on scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts, offered carefully: it IS passed to the node lane
by that derivation. Being passed to a runner and executing under it are different facts, and which
one holds is TanElk's measurement, not mine - the list cannot settle it, which is the same shape as
inferring a gate's capability from its test.

=== A GENERALISABLE INSTRUMENT, since this was found twice by hand ===

The import graph answers "does anything consume this" mechanically. Built from tsconfig.json, every
ImportDeclaration, ExportDeclaration and dynamic import(), then cross-checked against a grep for
each path as a command string outside tests - the needle is a full repo-relative path, so
containment is honest there.

Raw yield 76 modules under scripts/ and src/testing/ whose only importers are tests; 43 after
removing those named as a command anywhere. Most of the 43 are legitimate: fixtures exist to be
imported by tests, and scripts/audit-readings.ts and its three siblings are fixture-driven CLI
wrappers already carried as documented exceptions in src/testing/scriptReachability.test.ts. I am
reporting the instrument and the runtime-conformance cluster it found, NOT the 43 as a defect
count. The number needs the fixture and CLI-wrapper classes subtracted before it means anything,
and I have not done that subtraction.

=== PROCESS SLIP, mine ===

I ran `bun run test:node` to check whether the reader tests execute. That is a full lane and the
orchestrator owns full lanes. The question was answerable statically - nodeOnlyTestArgs on
bunfig.toml, which is what the figures above come from - and that is what I should have run first.

comments.text:
pane31: THE CHOICE, and the rationale, recorded here because the commit that carried it is not
mine. Answering "enforce it, or label the limit - your call, file it either way and say which".

CHOSE BOTH, split by what is decidable, because the population splits cleanly and I would rather
enforce three than label five.

    report.test.ts, coverageLedger.test.ts     literal `bun ...`      DECIDABLE -> basis "checked"
    checkRevisions.integration.test.ts         execFileSync("git")    DECIDABLE -> basis "checked"
    alignEditions.test.ts, brownianDemo.mjs    process.execPath       NOT DECIDABLE -> "unverifiable"

process.execPath is node under node and bun under bun. No static reading settles it, and pretending
otherwise would be the enforcement-that-pretends. Those two entries carry basis "unverifiable" and
their reasons are labelled human claims. The other three are confirmed by the gate on every run, so
a file that starts spawning node fails instead of keeping its excuse.

WHY NOT LABEL ALL FIVE. Three of the five are checkable today, and a limit that swallows the
checkable cases costs more than it admits: the two that matter least for honesty - a literal `bun`
and a literal `git` - are exactly the ones a future edit is most likely to change to node.

WHY NOT ENFORCE ALL FIVE. There is no reading of `spawnSync(process.execPath, ...)` that yields an
executable. Any rule claiming to check it would be checking the spelling of an expression, which is
this bead's own defect.

The label cannot be used to dodge the check in either direction: a "checked" entry whose file spawns
a runtime value is reported as mislabelled, an "unverifiable" entry whose spawns are all literal is
reported as a claim where a check was available, and a literal node child is refused whatever the
entry says.

spawnTargets() reads the first argument of each spawn call from the syntax tree - ts.createSourceFile,
no program, no types, and it parses .mjs. A regex would have been the defect this bead is about:
execFileSync("git") and a COMMENT saying execFileSync("node") are identical to a substring test and
opposite to a parser. A test asserts that exact pair.

=== THE PLANT FOUND A SECOND DEFECT, which is the argument for insisting a plant goes red ===

Relabelling coverageLedger.test.ts as "unverifiable" left the gate GREEN. The verifier was correct
in isolation - called directly it returned the violation - but the file never reached it.

    const SKIP_DIRS = new Set([..., "artifacts", "dist", "coverage"]);   applied at EVERY depth

src/content/coverage is a SOURCE directory holding two test files, and a flat name test promoted it

THE SHAPE: a check runs real logic, finds no violations, and prints a POSITIVE claim - when the reason it found none is that it examined nothing.

                                      policy' on zero changes to examine (am-czbe, fixed)
  editionContract.ts check 8          reports passed with 'Alignment coverage and edge
                                      validity verified.' on zero units and zero edges
  verify-license-inventory.ts         'Third-party license inventory check passed.

                                      open (am-zqat, pane31 investigating)
