title: Implement the post-promotion smoke test, coherent rollback, and cache policy
description:
# Implement the post-promotion smoke test, coherent rollback, and cache policy

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §12.8,
§16.3, §18.3, §21 "The publication is maintainable" (traceability only)

## Background

Even a fully checked candidate can fail after promotion: an alias can attach to the wrong
deployment, the edge can serve something unexpected, or a hostname can resolve incorrectly. The plan
asks for "a short live smoke test (the mass–energy paper, because it is quick, plus its German
edition endpoint)" after promotion. It also requires that "a rollback restores a coherent site,
content, and kernel set and never points old HTML at incompatible new WASM," that the previous
verified deployment and its immutable assets stay available, that immutable content-addressed
figures and WASM get long-lived caching, and that manifests and HTML "never reference a removed
artifact." The donor's `smoke-test-deployment.ts` fetches core routes and checks HTTP 200 and
minimum body sizes; this bead adapts that idea and adds profile awareness, automatic rollback,
deployment retention, and the cache policy.

The runtime behavior that makes old HTML safe (the WASM loader refusing a module whose digest does
not match with the `artifact-mismatch` execution outcome, and the laboratory pausing while the book
stays usable) is owned by `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` and `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`. This bead
proves the release-level guarantees around it and exercises that behavior in its drill; it does not
reimplement it.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/smoke-test-deployment.ts` (adapted, profile-aware), the rollback routine in the
release script, the verified-deployment history and retention check, the cache and MIME header
policy (in `vercel.json` headers or Next.js `headers()`), the output content-addressing test, and
the `cache-headers` candidate check.
Out of scope: pre-promotion candidate checks (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`); DNS
(`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`); service-worker caching (`am-plat-installable-offline-oit3`); the
search index's own sharding and content addressing (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`, whose files this
policy classifies); the loader digest check and laboratory pause (`am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`,
`am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`).

## Requirements

**Smoke test** (`bun scripts/smoke-test-deployment.ts --base https://<host> --profile
<scaffold|preview|launch> --release-id <id> [--tool-run <tool-run-id>]` for each promoted hostname):
- Every profile: `/`, `/robots.txt`, and `/sitemap.xml` return 200; `/release-manifest.json` carries
the promoted `releaseId` (once `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna` has landed).
- `preview` and `launch`: `/papers/mass-energy` (reading face) returns 200 with the paper's German
title *Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig?* and a non-trivial body;
the German edition endpoint (`/papers/mass-energy?view=german`, plus the machine-readable German
edition export if `am-cm-machine-readable-exports-xgy` has shipped) returns the complete German
text, including the date-line as edited ("Bern, September 1905", verified against the facsimile).
- Once DNS is attached: `http://annus-mirabilis.com` redirects to `https://annus-mirabilis.com`, and
`https://www.annus-mirabilis.com` redirects permanently to the apex.
- Target runtime under one minute; no browser needed.
- The smoke record belongs to the release: it carries the release's `toolRunId` and its own
`logRunId`, per `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`.

**Rollback:**
- Before promotion, `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` records the deployment currently serving each
hostname as the rollback target, together with its `releaseId` and manifest digest from the retained
release history.
- On smoke failure: re-alias every promoted hostname to its rollback target, confirm `vercel
inspect` shows Ready and the target id, run the smoke test against the restored deployment, log both
results, and exit non-zero. If rollback itself fails, print exact manual recovery commands and the
recorded ids.
- Rollback always moves whole deployments. On Vercel each deployment serves its own HTML, content
payloads, and WASM, so re-aliasing restores a coherent set. Never mix assets across deployments.
- Retention: the retained history keeps at least the last three verified deployments as rollback
targets, plus any audited candidate awaiting `--promote`. Before promotion, the script reads the
project's deployment retention settings (as recorded by `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk` and re-checked
through the Vercel CLI or API) and refuses if they would delete a recorded rollback target or
audited candidate before its intended use. Deleting a Vercel deployment or changing retention
settings requires the user's written permission (AGENTS.md Rule 1 applies to remote artifacts too).
- A manual rollback outside a release is an outward-facing action and requires the user's explicit
authorization in the current conversation, recorded in an authorization file like any other alias
move.

**Version coherence:**
- Every WASM URL referenced by HTML or route payloads is content-addressed (a digest in the path or
filename). No `latest.wasm` style URL exists.
- The release-level drill confirms that a page served by an old deployment loads its own WASM and
that a digest mismatch produces the runtime's `artifact-mismatch` outcome with the laboratory paused
and the text readable.

**Cache and MIME policy** (applied by URL pattern, never by directory):
- Paths whose file name or directory contains a content digest (for example
`/wasm/<bundle>/<sha256-prefix>/…`, `/figures/<name>.<hex>.<ext>`, and the search index's
content-addressed shards under `/search/`, whose file names carry the SHA-256 prefix of their bytes)
and `/_next/static/*`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (31,536,000 s = 365
days). WASM also gets `Content-Type: application/wasm` for streaming instantiation.
- HTML, `/release-manifest.json`, the search index manifest `/search/index-manifest.json`, and route
JSON fragments: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. Edge caching is allowed only
where invalidated per deployment. The index manifest names the shards and therefore must never be
served stale beside fresh shards; the shards themselves never change under a name, which is why the
two search-index classes differ (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`).
- Facsimile PDFs and any other asset whose URL does not contain a digest must not be marked
`immutable`; use revalidation with ETag. Prefer moving immutable assets to content-addressed paths.
- A non-content-addressed file placed under `/figures/` or `/search/` never receives an immutable
header; the pattern, not the parent directory, decides.
- Register a `cache-headers` check in the candidate-check catalogue (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`)
that asserts these headers on the deployed candidate, including one asserted path per class
(content-addressed WASM, a hashed search shard, the search index manifest, HTML, and a facsimile
PDF).

## Technical Approach

Keep the smoke test dependency-free (`fetch` with timeouts) so it can run during an incident.
Implement rollback as a small state machine in the release script with injectable command execution.
Add a build-time test that walks the output and asserts every referenced WASM, figure, and search
shard path is content-addressed and present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The smoke test runs after every promotion on every promoted hostname, with checks appropriate
to the profile, and its records carry the release's `toolRunId`.
- [ ] A smoke failure triggers automatic rollback, proven by a state-machine test and a documented
drill on the platform alias.
- [ ] The retained history lists at least three verified rollback targets with release ids and
manifest digests, and the retention check refuses when settings would delete one.
- [ ] Header tests confirm the cache and MIME policy for all five classes; no immutable header lands
on a non-content-addressed URL, including the search index manifest.
- [ ] An output test proves HTML never references a missing or non-content-addressed WASM, figure,
or search shard.
- [ ] The drill shows an old deployment loading its own WASM, and a digest mismatch producing the
`artifact-mismatch` outcome with a paused laboratory.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/smoke-test-deployment.test.ts` against an in-process fixture HTTP server: pass per
profile; 404 on the paper; wrong `releaseId`; missing date-line; redirect loop; `scaffold` profile
does not request paper routes; a supplied `--tool-run` appears in every event.
- `scripts/rollback.test.ts`: smoke fails then rollback succeeds; rollback alias failure then manual
recovery instructions; no recorded target then refusal before promotion; retention settings that
would delete a target cause refusal; a manual rollback without an authorization file refuses.
- `scripts/cache-policy.test.ts`: parse the configured headers and assert per-path rules for the
five classes; a digest-free file under `/figures/` and a digest-free file under `/search/` each get
no `immutable`; `/search/index-manifest.json` is must-revalidate while a hashed shard beside it is
immutable; walk an in-memory listing of a fixture output tree and assert content addressing.
### End-to-end tests
- Rollback drill on the platform alias during an authorized release window: promote a candidate,
force a smoke failure through a test-only flag of the smoke script (never a flag or conditional
import in the application), observe automatic rollback, and record evidence.
- In the browser harness, load an old deployment's HTML directly by deployment URL and confirm its
WASM loads from the same deployment; serve a tampered WASM through request interception and confirm
the `artifact-mismatch` outcome, a paused laboratory, and readable text.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>.jsonl` records `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `toolRunId`,
`stage` (`smoke`, `rollback`, `retention`), `profile`, `hostname`, `url`, `expected`, `actual`,
`releaseId`, `rollbackTargetId`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. The release history appends
promotion, smoke, and rollback events under the release's `toolRunId`. A failing smoke or rollback
retains the response bodies, headers, and `vercel inspect` output under
`artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>/evidence/<stage>/`, copied and never deleted.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Browser caches can hold old HTML for a long time; content addressing plus per-deployment assets is
what keeps that HTML working.
- Do not "fix" a failing smoke test by loosening its assertions during an incident; roll back first.
- Keep the smoke test short, as the plan asks. The exhaustive checks already ran before promotion.
- An immutable header on a manifest is the quiet failure mode: readers get shard names that no
longer exist. Test the manifest class explicitly, not only the shard class.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`: promotion and smoke testing follow passing candidate checks, and
this bead registers `cache-headers` in that catalogue.
- `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`: the drill exercises the runtime's pause on artifact mismatch.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`: a public preview needs smoke testing and rollback.
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: "rollback restores a coherent version" is a launch criterion.
- `am-plat-installable-offline-oit3`: the offline edition reuses this cache policy and the proven
rollback.
- `am-rel-cloudflare-hosting-experiment-n7re`: any hosting comparison re-validates this behavior.

title: Create the Vercel project and deploy the empty site to the Vercel alias with explicit authorization
description:
# Create the Vercel project and deploy the empty site to the Vercel alias with explicit
authorization

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-a · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** human-gate ·
**Plan sections:** §4.6, §18.1, §19.1 exit evidence (traceability only)

## Background

Batch A ends with three pieces of exit evidence, one of which is "the empty site deploys to the
Vercel alias." Deploying early proves the release path before content exists, so the first paper
does not also have to debug hosting. The site is hosted on Vercel through the verified prebuilt
workflow built in `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`; `vercel.json` already disables git-triggered
deployments (`{"git": {"deploymentEnabled": false}}`), so pushes to GitHub never deploy on their
own. Creating a Vercel project, linking the repository, and deploying are outward-facing actions.
The plan explicitly does not authorize them, so this is a human-gate bead.

**What already exists, and why this bead stays open.** On 2026-09-14, at the user's direct request
for a temporary placeholder and outside the verified script (which did not exist yet), the Vercel
project `annus-mirabilis` was created in the team `dicklesworthstones-projects` and a static
in-preparation page was deployed to production with the Vercel CLI; `annus-mirabilis.vercel.app`
belongs to another account, so the project's platform alias is `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`,
and the apex and `www` were attached and serve that placeholder. The placeholder's source lived in a
session scratch directory, not this repository. None of that is release evidence: a deploy made
outside the verified script never counts. This bead still owes the verified-script scaffold deploy,
the pinned project constants, and the recorded project settings.

This deploy is the one publication that does not wait for the license decision
(`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`): it serves only an in-preparation placeholder page and code
that is already public in the repository under the provisional LICENSE, with no translation or
explanatory prose.

## Scope

In scope: confirming or linking the Vercel project, pinning its identity in the release script,
confirming project settings (framework, Node.js version, Deployment Protection, deployment
retention), confirming the platform alias, and one authorized scaffold-profile deploy to
`annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`.
Out of scope: the Cloudflare zone, the records, and what the custom domains serve
(`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`); preview or launch releases (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`,
`am-launch-public-release-5nkq`); the release script itself (`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`).

## Requirements

1. **Authorization first.** Obtain the user's explicit written authorization in the current
conversation to (a) confirm or link the Vercel project and (b) run the scaffold deploy. Record the
exact quote and timestamp. Authorization for one step does not cover the other or any later release,
and the 2026-09-14 placeholder authorization covers neither. Write the scaffold deploy authorization,
verbatim, to `artifacts/releases/authorizations/<ISO timestamp>-scaffold-full.md` with its scope
(profile `scaffold`, full mode, hostname `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`, the commit), because
the release script refuses without it.
2. **Account check.** `vercel whoami` must show the user's account (the donor project used
`dicklesworthstone`). Stop if it does not.
3. **Project.** Confirm the existing project `annus-mirabilis` (or create and link one, with the
name confirmed by the user). Keep git deployments disabled. Confirm the framework preset and output
settings are compatible with prebuilt deploys, and that the project's Node.js version matches
`engines.node` in `package.json`. Record whether Deployment Protection is on for previews, because
candidate checks depend on it, and whether a Protection Bypass for Automation secret exists (never
record the secret itself). Record the project's deployment retention settings, because rollback
targets and audited candidates must not be deleted automatically; any change to those settings
requires the user's authorization.
4. **Pin identity.** Copy `projectId`, `projectName`, and `orgId` from `.vercel/project.json` into
`CANONICAL_PRODUCTION_PROJECT` in `scripts/deployment-target.ts` and the matching constants in
`deployment-verification.ts`, and commit them. `.vercel/` itself stays ignored by git.
5. **Platform alias.** The platform alias is `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`. The plain
`annus-mirabilis.vercel.app` belongs to another Vercel account, so Vercel assigned this alias when
the project was created on 2026-09-14. Use it in the script constants; AGENTS.md and the plan
already do.
6. **Dry run, then deploy.** Run `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile scaffold
--dry-run` and show the user its output; then run `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts
--profile scaffold --authorization <file>`. The scaffold profile promotes only the platform alias.
The custom domains are already attached to the project from the placeholder work, so this run must
not pass `--include-custom-domains`: without it the script moves no custom alias and the apex and
`www` keep serving whatever they serve until `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm` moves them under its own
authorization.
7. **Verification.** `vercel inspect https://annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` shows status Ready
and the candidate id; `/`, `/robots.txt`, and `/sitemap.xml` return 200 with the expected
placeholder content; an unknown path returns 404 with the not-found page; `/papers` is checked only
if that route exists at the deployed commit; the served page contains no draft paper text and no
claim that an edition is available.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** the user (repository owner) gives authorization; an agent may execute the
commands only after that.
- **Evidence to record** (as a `br comments add` on this bead and in the deploy JSONL log): the
authorization quotes and timestamps, the authorization file path, the Vercel account, project name
and ids, Node.js version setting, Deployment Protection and bypass status, deployment retention
settings, the deployment URL and id, the release `toolRunId`, `vercel inspect` output for the alias,
and the log path.
- **Agents may prepare:** the checklist, the dry-run output of the script, and the constants patch
with placeholders.
- **Agents never close this bead on their own judgment**, never write an authorization file without
the user's actual words, and never treat the 2026-09-14 placeholder as evidence that this bead's
work is done.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Authorization quotes and timestamps are recorded for the project step and for the scaffold
deploy, and the deploy authorization file matches the run's scope.
- [ ] Canonical project constants are committed and the identity check passes against
`.vercel/project.json`.
- [ ] `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` serves the scaffold deployment with status Ready.
- [ ] The deploy was performed only through the verified script with the scaffold profile; no direct
`vercel deploy --prod` was run.
- [ ] Protection, bypass availability, Node.js version, and retention settings are recorded.
- [ ] This bead attaches no custom domain and moves none. The apex and `www` were already attached
on 2026-09-14 for the interim placeholder, and the scaffold deploy leaves them serving whatever they
serve.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- After pinning, rerun `scripts/deployment-target.test.ts` and
`scripts/deployment-verification.test.ts`; add `scripts/canonicalProject.test.ts` asserting the
committed constants have the expected shapes (`prj_` and `team_` prefixes, lowercase hostnames) and
that none equals a value on the forbidden donor identity list in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md`.

### End-to-end tests
- The verified script's dry run, then its candidate and promotion stages in scaffold profile.
- A post-deploy fetch loop against the alias for `/`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, and an unknown
path, asserting status codes, minimum body sizes, and the absence of third-party origins in the
HTML, logged to JSONL.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>.jsonl` from the script (each event carrying the release's
`toolRunId`), plus a `setup` record `{timestamp, suite: "vercel-setup", logRunId, toolRunId, stage:
"setup", account, projectName, projectIdPrefix, nodeVersion, deploymentProtection, bypassConfigured,
retention, authorizationRef, aliasVerified, outcome, message}`. A failed verification retains the
response bodies, headers, and `vercel inspect` output beside the log, copied and never deleted; no
secret or bypass token is ever logged.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Linking the wrong project is the failure the identity check guards against; confirm the ids before
committing them.
- If Deployment Protection is enabled, unauthenticated fetches of the candidate return 401. That is
expected and is why candidate checks use the protected-preview adapter.
- The custom domains are already attached, so a scaffold run with `--include-custom-domains` would
change what the public sees. That move belongs to `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm` under its own
authorization.
- Never touch the classic-patents.com Vercel project.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`: the only supported deploy path must exist and be tested first.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`: the zone work verifies and corrects what the domains attached to
this project serve.

THE HUMAN GATE APPEARS SATISFIED BY EVENTS. Recording the evidence rather than closing: this bead carries the human-gate label and says in terms that deploying is an outward-facing action the plan does not authorize, so the owner closes it, not me.

## What the owner authorised, verbatim

2026-09-22, after the placeholder had been live for a week: "i really need you to
deploy the site for real, this is nuts that you refuse to do so."

That is explicit authorisation to deploy, and it is stronger than the "empty
site" this bead contemplates - it authorises the real edition.

## What was deployed, and how

Twice, both through the prebuilt workflow this bead names rather than a
git-triggered build:

    vercel pull --yes --environment production
    vercel build --prod            # exit 0
    vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod

First at 23:21 from the pre-overhaul tree. Again after the design campaign, from
HEAD in an isolated git worktree so that no pane's in-flight work could ship.

## Verified live, not assumed

    annus-mirabilis.com and www      HTTP 200, age 0, x-vercel-cache MISS
    title                            Annus Mirabilis - four papers, one year
    h1                               Einstein's four papers of 1905
    theme control                    Light (Annalen) / Dark (Kramgasse Night) / System
    routes sampled                   7 of 308, all 200, including
                                     /papers/brownian-motion/view/german at 103 KB
                                     and /notation at 3.2 MB
    homepage bytes                   byte-identical to the locally built out/index.html

vercel.json still disables git-triggered deployments, so nothing deploys on a
push; every release has gone through the prebuilt path deliberately.

## The caveat that belongs on this bead

The prebuilt path is not a preference, it is a workaround. Vercel's own build has
failed since 2026-09-17 with UnhandledSchemeError on node:crypto, node:fs,
node:path and node:url - four consecutive production deployments - and it is
filed as am-t84m. Until that lands, a release that goes through Vercel's builder
rather than a local prebuild will fail. Whoever closes this bead should decide
whether "the release path is proven" is true while that is outstanding, because
the path that is proven is the local one.

## What I am not claiming

That the exit evidence for batch A is complete, or that any other gate in
am-ep-release-as1 is met. Only that the deployment this bead describes has
happened, was authorised in the owner's own words, and is verifiable at the URL.

title: Adapt the verified candidate-then-promote release script for annus-mirabilis.com
description:
# Adapt the verified candidate-then-promote release script for annus-mirabilis.com

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-a · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §2.3
(reuse table), §18.1, §18.3, §19.6, §21 (traceability only)

## Background

The plan reuses the donor's release workflow because it is fail-closed: it refuses stale or partial
artifacts, validates a fresh prebuilt deployment under an unpromoted URL, and only then moves public
hostnames. Classic Patents learned this after stale `.vercel/output` directories and concurrent
builds put wrong content live. Annus Mirabilis inherits the workflow and extends it for a scientific
edition whose releases must bind source texts, translations, and WASM kernels together. This bead
writes the script and its tests. **It never performs a real deployment**; the first real deploy
happens in `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk` under the user's explicit authorization.

Two extensions matter for launch honesty. The launch audit and the final product test examine one
specific deployment; if the public release then rebuilt and deployed a fresh candidate, the bytes
readers get would be a different deployment from the one that was audited and tested. The script
therefore has a `--candidate-only` mode (build, deploy unpromoted, check, record, stop) and a
`--promote <deployment>` mode (re-verify a recorded candidate and promote it without rebuilding).
And because deploying is an outward-facing action that only the user may authorize, every mode that
deploys or moves an alias requires an authorization file containing the user's verbatim words, which
the script checks for scope and copies into the release record. The script cannot prove the words
are genuine; agents must never write such a file without the user's actual authorization in the
current conversation.

One release spans more than one process: `--candidate-only` builds and records a candidate today,
and `--promote` moves it days later. Following `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, that persistent
release is a **tool run** with a `toolRunId`, which names the release record and every event that
points at it, while each process run of the script has its own `logRunId` naming its JSONL log file.
`runId` never appears here; it belongs to an experiment realization.

Donor files to adapt (read-only source at the revision pinned in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md`):
`scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts`, `scripts/deployment-target.ts` (+ `.test.ts`),
`scripts/deployment-verification.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), `scripts/smoke-test-deployment.ts`. Extraction
with license notices happens in `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`; this bead turns the extracted copies
into Annus Mirabilis code.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts`, `scripts/deployment-target.ts`,
`scripts/deployment-verification.ts`, their tests, publication profiles, modes, authorization files,
the release record, the `publication-contract` gate step, deploy logging, and documentation in
AGENTS.md "Vercel Deployment Standards".
Out of scope (owned elsewhere): creating the Vercel project and first deploy
(`am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`); manifest generation (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`); the full
candidate check suite (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`); smoke test, rollback, retention, and caching
(`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`); DNS (`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`); the gate registry and
runner (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`).

## Requirements

The script is the only supported production entry point:

`bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile <scaffold|preview|launch> [--dry-run |
--candidate-only | --promote <deployment-id-or-url>] [--authorization <path>]
[--include-custom-domains]`

It must preserve every donor safety behavior, re-targeted:

1. **Exclusive local lock.** Bind `127.0.0.1` on a dedicated TCP port with `exclusive: true`;
`EADDRINUSE` means another Annus Mirabilis release is running and the script refuses. Use a port
distinct from the donor's (the donor port is on the forbidden identity list) so the two sites'
releases stay independent. Release the lock in `finally`.
2. **Canonical project identity.** `.vercel/project.json` must match `CANONICAL_PRODUCTION_PROJECT`
(`projectId`, `projectName`, `orgId`, custom domains `annus-mirabilis.com` and
`www.annus-mirabilis.com`, platform domain `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`). The ids are unknown
until `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`; until they are filled in, the script refuses with a message naming
that bead. Never copy the donor's ids.
3. **No conflicting builds.** Scan `ps -Ao pid=,ppid=,etime=,command=` for `next build|dev`, `vercel
build|deploy`, and `bun run build|dev` processes whose working directory (via `lsof -p <pid> -a -d
cwd -Fn`) is inside this workspace; wait up to 120 s, then refuse. Check at preflight, after the
application build, after the Vercel build, and before promotion.
4. **Clean tree and fixed commit.** `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` must be empty
apart from a small documented allowlist (for example `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, `next-env.d.ts`,
`.beads/`). Record `HEAD` at preflight and refuse if it changes at any later stage. In `--promote`
mode `HEAD` must equal the candidate's recorded commit.
5. **Quality gates before building.** Run `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --profile <profile>
--fail-fast`; exit code 2 (a required step is not available) and exit code 1 (a step failed) both
refuse the release. The profiles' step lists live in the gate registry, not in this script:
`scaffold` requires the architecture test, typecheck, lint, format check, unit tests, `ubs --diff`,
`ubs --staged`, and build; `preview` and `launch` additionally require `publication-contract`,
`verify-content`, `verify-wasm-artifacts`, `scenarios`, `license-inventory`, `voice-lint` (until
folded into `verify-content`, after which the registry entry changes so the voice check never runs
or reports twice), `browser-acceptance`, and `perf-budgets`. This bead registers the
`publication-contract` step (a fast `bun test` subset of the edition, dispatcher, architecture, and
determinism tests, ordered first). A profile's list only grows.
6. **Fresh prebuilt artifact.** `vercel pull --yes`, then `vercel build --prod` with
`AM_RELEASE_PROFILE=<profile>` set for the manifest generator, then validate:
`.vercel/output/config.json` exists, parses, and has `version: 3`; `.vercel/output/static/` exists;
the config was written after this attempt's build start (1 s tolerance); the file count is above a
documented floor; for `preview` and `launch`, the release manifest is present and valid
(`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`), while `scaffold` records the manifest's absence explicitly in the
deploy log until that bead lands; profile-specific content assertions pass (below).
7. **Build-output hygiene without silent deletion.** The donor deletes `.next` before building.
AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids agents deleting files without written permission. Either record the user's
explicit approval for the script to clear its own build output directories (quote and date in the
script header and AGENTS.md), or build into a fresh per-release output location and rely on the
timestamp freshness check. Do not add a deletion silently.
8. **Unpromoted candidate.** `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --skip-domain --json`; extract the
last `https://*.vercel.app` URL from stdout and stderr. Validate protected previews through **one
adapter** (`protectedFetch` in `scripts/deployment-verification.ts`), never through scattered call
sites: `vercel curl --deployment <url> <path> -- --silent --show-error --write-out
"\n<MARKER>%{http_code}"` when the locked Vercel CLI provides that subcommand, otherwise `curl` with
the `x-vercel-protection-bypass` header whose secret is read from an environment variable and never
logged; parse the status marker. Whether `vercel curl` exists in the locked CLI version is not
assumed here: `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax` probes and records the availability of every
Vercel CLI command these scripts use, with the replacement mechanism for any that is missing, and
the adapter reads that recorded decision (or probes once and refuses with a message naming that
bead if no record exists). Invoke `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` here, before any alias moves. The
donor ran its full sweep after promotion; that ordering is not inherited.
9. **Release record.** After candidate checks pass, mint a `toolRunId` (the shared
`newRunIdentity()` format `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-<8 hex>` from `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`) for this
release and write `artifacts/releases/<commit>-<tool-run-id>.json` with profile, mode, commit,
`toolRunId`, the `logRunId` of this process, candidate deployment id and URL, manifest digest and
determinism digest, candidate-check summary and log path, and the authorization reference.
`--candidate-only` stops here and prints the candidate id and the `toolRunId`. Later processes of
the same release (`--promote`, the smoke test, a rollback) append their events to the same record
and carry the same `toolRunId` with their own `logRunId`.
10. **Promotion with atomic intent.** Before moving anything, record the deployment currently
serving each hostname (`vercel inspect https://<host>`) as the rollback target, with its `releaseId`
and manifest digest when it serves `/release-manifest.json`. For each hostname: `vercel alias set
<candidate> <host>`, then `vercel inspect https://<host>` must parse to status Ready and the
candidate's id. Then assert the composite alias set (`assertDeploymentReadyAndAliased`,
`assertDeploymentHasRequiredAliases`). If any step fails after the first alias moved, re-point the
moved aliases to the recorded previous deployment, verify them, and exit non-zero with both failures
reported.
11. **`--promote <deployment>`.** No rebuild. Take the lock; check identity, conflicts, clean tree,
and `HEAD`; load the candidate's release record (found by deployment id or by `toolRunId`), which
must exist, name the same profile, and show passing candidate checks; fetch the candidate's deployed
`/release-manifest.json` and require its digest to equal the recorded digest; rerun
`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` against the candidate for fresh evidence; then promote as in
Requirement 10 and hand off to the smoke test. The rerun's events carry the record's `toolRunId`.
12. **Post-promotion.** Hand off to the smoke test in `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`; a smoke
failure triggers that bead's rollback.
13. **Publication profiles.** `scaffold` promotes only `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`, and, with
`--include-custom-domains` and an authorization that names the custom domains, also the apex and
`www` to serve the in-preparation placeholder as an honest holding page; it requires the
architecture, build, and placeholder route checks. `preview` requires the release manifest's
`publishedPapers` to be exactly the papers whose definition-of-done beads are closed, and "in
preparation" states for the rest (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`); it promotes the platform alias, and
the custom domains only when the authorization names them. `launch` requires all four papers
complete and promotes all three hostnames. A profile can never weaken a gate that applies to a paper
it publishes.
14. **Authorization files.** Every mode except `--dry-run` requires `--authorization <path>`
pointing to a Markdown file under `artifacts/releases/authorizations/` containing the user's
verbatim authorization text, its timestamp, and the scope it grants (profile, mode, hostnames, and
commit or `releaseId`). The script refuses when the file is missing, when its scope does not cover
this profile, mode, commit or candidate, or when it names fewer hostnames than the run would move.
The reference is copied into the release record and the deploy log. A human gate is never
self-certified: no agent writes such a file without the user's actual words in the current
conversation, and no mode infers authorization from a plan document, a bead, or an earlier release.
15. **Help and refusal messages.** `--help` prints usage. Every refusal names the stage, the failed
assertion, and the next action. Exit code 1 on any refusal or failure.

## Technical Approach

Keep `deployment-target.ts` as pure parsing and assertion functions (`parseDeploymentInspect`,
`assertDeploymentReadyAndAliased`, project-identity validation) so they are unit-testable with
fixtures. `deployment-verification.ts` holds constants, alias assertions, the `protectedFetch`
adapter, and the reader sweep adapted to paper routes
(`/papers/<slug>?view=german|english|reading`), checking a `data-source-delivery` style marker and
forbidding draft or hold strings on published faces (for example unreviewed-draft banners).
`authorization.ts` parses and scope-checks authorization files. The main script composes them as a
stage machine whose command runner is injected. All child processes go through one `run()` wrapper
that logs and throws on non-zero exit, with a 64 MB output buffer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No donor identity (project id, org id, hostnames, Wright or patent routes, lock port) remains
in the adapted code.
- [ ] Every safety behavior in Requirements 1–15 is implemented and covered by a test.
- [ ] Running the script without a linked canonical project refuses before any build or network
call.
- [ ] Partial-promotion failure restores previously serving deployments (proven with fixture-driven
tests of the promotion state machine).
- [ ] `--candidate-only` never moves an alias, and `--promote` never builds (proven by recorded
command lists in tests).
- [ ] One release keeps one `toolRunId` across `--candidate-only`, `--promote`, smoke, and rollback
processes, while each process writes its own `logRunId` log file.
- [ ] Every protected-preview request goes through the single adapter, and no test or code path
calls `vercel curl` or a bypass header directly.
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Vercel Deployment Standards" matches the implemented behavior, including the lock
port, profiles, modes, authorization files, and the release record path.
- [ ] No real deployment was run by this bead.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/deployment-target.test.ts`: inspect-output fixtures (Ready, Error, Building, missing
aliases, extra aliases, trailing slashes, `╶` bullets, an unknown format that must fail closed);
project.json fixtures (missing file message, invalid JSON, wrong name, wrong id, wrong org).
- `scripts/deployment-verification.test.ts`: alias normalization; required-alias refusal text;
reader-sweep route manifest for the four papers and their faces; forbidden-string detection on
fixture HTML; `protectedFetch` selects the `vercel curl` path when the recorded CLI capability says
the subcommand exists, selects the bypass-header path when it does not, refuses when neither the
capability record nor the bypass secret is available, and never writes the secret into a logged
command line or a JSONL event (assert on the captured log buffer).
- `scripts/authorization.test.ts`: a missing file refuses; a file for `preview` used with `launch`
refuses; a file naming only `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` refuses a run that would move the
apex; a file naming a different commit refuses; a complete file passes and its reference appears in
the record.
- `scripts/verified-production-deploy.test.ts`: `ps` and `lsof` fixture parsing for conflicting
builds; porcelain filtering with the allowlist; deployment URL extraction from mixed JSON and text;
protected-preview status-marker parsing (2xx pass, 401, 404, missing marker); artifact validation on
fixture trees (missing config, version 2, stale mtime, too few files); gate runner exit code 2 and
exit code 1 each refuse; profile rules (scaffold cannot promote custom domains without
`--include-custom-domains` and a matching authorization; preview lists only closed papers; launch
requires all four); promotion state machine with injected command results, including failure on the
second hostname; `--candidate-only` records a candidate and issues no `vercel alias set`;
`--promote` refuses on a missing record, a record with failed checks, a manifest digest mismatch,
and a `HEAD` mismatch, and issues no `vercel build` or `vercel deploy`; the record written by
`--candidate-only` and the events written by a later `--promote` share one `toolRunId` and differ in
`logRunId`.
- Tests use fixed fixture files and injected command runners. They never create or delete temporary
files in the repository and never call Vercel or git for real.

### End-to-end tests
- A dry-run mode (`--dry-run`) executes every local stage (lock, identity, conflicts, tree, gates,
build, artifact validation, manifest validation) and prints the deploy and promotion commands it
would run without executing them. CI runs the dry run against the scaffold profile once
`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx` exists, asserting exit code 0, the printed command list, and a JSONL
log containing one event per stage.

### Structured logging
- Each process run writes `artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the shared logger of
`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, with `timestamp`, `suite: "verified-production-deploy"`,
`logRunId`, `toolRunId` (the release this process belongs to), `testId` (the stage), `profile`,
`mode`, `stage`, `command`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, `commit`, `candidateUrl`, `deploymentId`,
`hostname`, `check`, `expected`, `actual`, `authorizationRef`, `outcome`, and `message`
(script-specific fields under `extra` where the schema requires it). On refusal it retains the
failing response body excerpt, HTTP status, and inspect output under
`artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>/evidence/<stage>/`, copied and never moved or truncated.
Secrets and bypass tokens are never logged.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- `vercel inspect` output formats change; parsing must fail closed on unknown formats, never assume
Ready.
- A stale `.vercel/output` from another checkout is the failure this whole script exists to prevent;
freshness checks are mandatory even in dry run.
- Deployment Protection on previews means plain `fetch` of the candidate returns 401; use the
protected-preview adapter for candidate checks.
- A recorded candidate can disappear if the project's deployment retention settings delete it;
`--promote` must refuse with that explanation rather than rebuild silently.
- The script must never touch `~/projects/classic-patents.com` or its Vercel project.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`: the donor scripts must be extracted with license notices before
they are adapted.
- `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`: the gate registry and profile runner the script calls.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`: the first authorized deploy uses this script.
- `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`: the script validates the manifest inside the artifact.
- Beads of the separate iPhone app plan (`am-app-verified-release-1jbu`, `am-app-universal-links-re8v`)
also depend on this bead for the release identity and the association-file host; app work never
delays a website batch, and this bead makes no commitment to it.

Reads without a dependency edge: `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax` records which Vercel CLI
commands the locked version provides. That decision is a Batch A governance item on a separate path;
if the record is missing when this script runs, the adapter probes once and refuses with a message
naming that bead rather than assuming `vercel curl` exists.

comments.text:
pane %29, DIAGNOSIS of scripts/publication-contract.test.ts (3 pass, 2 fail). I changed nothing and adjusted no expected count.

=== THE ANSWER: A GENUINE CONTRACT IS FAILING, AND THE SUITE IS CORRECTLY REPORTING IT ===

Not a leak. Four measurements:

1. The architecture gate fails ON ITS OWN, independently of this suite:
     bun scripts/app-router-architecture.ts   -> exit 1
     'Architecture Gate Failed (1 violation found)'
     [rule-4-root-allowlist] Unapproved unignored root entry '=' is not in scripts/architecture-allowlist.json.
   There is a file in the repository root literally named '=': untracked, zero bytes, created 2026-09-19 18:50:44. It is a RULE 2 rogue root entry and the gate is right to refuse it.

2. verifyPublicationContract runs that same check as 'preflight-architecture' BEFORE any spawn, and the preflight does not go through spawnFn at all. So an injected mock runner cannot make it pass.

3. THE PREFLIGHT IS NOT LEAKING. I built a clean temp root and called verifyPublicationContract with rootDir pointed at it. The preflight scanned THAT root, not the live one - it reported 'probe.ts' and 'scripts' as unapproved entries, which are the temp root's own contents against an empty allowlist. It honours the rootDir it is given.

4. The two failing tests pass rootDir: process.cwd() deliberately, so the preflight correctly scans the live repository and finds the real violation.

That explains both symptoms exactly:
  'runs successfully with an injected mock runner returning exit code 0' expects success true and gets false, because preflight-architecture legitimately failed before the mock ran.
  'fails with exit code 1 if an executed contract test returns non-zero' expects failedCount 1 and gets 2 = preflight-architecture (real) + the injected one. Your read of that second shape was right, and the extra failure is a true positive rather than a stray mock.

=== THE ROGUE FILE IS NOT MINE, and I did not delete it ===

'=' was created at 18:50:44. My session's scratchpad directory was created at 19:13:42, twenty-three minutes later, so the file predates my session. I cannot attribute it further - a zero-byte file named '=' is the signature of a mis-parsed shell redirection, and several panes are running commands in this tree.

I have NOT removed it. AGENTS.md RULE 1 forbids me deleting files without express permission, and that applies to a scratch file whoever created it. It is one command and I will run it the moment someone with the authority says so. It is also the only violation the gate reports, so removing it clears the gate and both tests go green on their own.

=== THE LATENT ISOLATION WEAKNESS, reported but deliberately NOT fixed today ===

These two tests are named for an injected mock runner, but their outcome depends on the live tree's architecture health, because preflight-architecture is not injectable and rootDir is process.cwd(). That is the same class as the bare-throw ratchet I split in af4eb67: a test that fails for a reason unrelated to what it names.

I did not fix it, and I want to be explicit about why, because the fix is easy and tempting. Making the preflight injectable today would turn both tests green WHILE A REAL ARCHITECTURE VIOLATION STANDS. That is the golden-regeneration reflex wearing a better disguise: not adjusting the expected numbers, but adjusting the test's reach until the true positive falls outside it. The right order is to clear the rogue file first, confirm the suite goes green for the real reason, and only then decide whether the preflight should be injectable - and if it is made injectable, at least one test must keep exercising it against the live tree, or this suite stops noticing architecture violations altogether.

EVIDENCE:
  bun test scripts/publication-contract.test.ts  -> 3 pass, 2 fail (unchanged; I fixed nothing)
  bun scripts/app-router-architecture.ts         -> exit 1, 1 violation, the root entry '='
  injected clean rootDir probe                   -> preflight scans the injected root, so no live-state leak
  ls -la '='                                     -> untracked, 0 bytes, 2026-09-19 18:50:44

No files changed.

title: Release records assert candidate checks that never ran: candidateChecksPassed is hard-coded true
description:
## Background

Every live deploy goes through `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts`. AGENTS.md ("Vercel Deployment Standards") says it validates the unpromoted candidate before any alias moves. The candidate checks must load:
- all four complete paper texts;
- representative foundation pages and every instrument bundle;
- one no-JavaScript source-text check;
- one real accepted WASM result per numerical capability;
- one deliberate typed refusal;

all against the deployed assets rather than the build directory.

## What is wrong (measured 2026-09-24, reality check)

- `scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts:736` writes `candidateChecksPassed: true` into the release record unconditionally.
- The six checks in `scripts/deployment-verification.ts` (about lines 191-211) are placeholders, and `runCandidateChecks` has no callers.
- So 24 of 24 release records under artifacts/releases, including every live deploy today, state that checks ran on the deployed candidate. None did.
- The only real post-deploy verification is `/` returning 200 with at least 1000 bytes.

This is a false record, not a missing feature: anyone reading a release record is told something that did not happen. AGENTS.md "Evidence discipline" and RH-2 apply.

## What to do

1. **Stop the false claim first,** as its own commit. The record says what executed: `candidateChecks: "not-implemented"` and `candidateChecksPassed: false` while the checks don't exist, with the reason written in the record.
   - Promotion does NOT depend on the flag until step 2 lands, so releases keep flowing under the owner's standing deploy authorization.
   - The record simply stops lying.
   - When step 2 lands (together with am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y), promotion refuses unless every check ran and passed.
2. **Implement the six candidate checks** against the unpromoted candidate URL (the `--skip-domain` deployment):
   - each of the 4 paper pages returns 200 and contains its first-encounter heading and at least N characters of explanation;
   - one representative foundation page per group;
   - every /lab/<id>/ route and its JS chunks load without console errors;
   - one no-JS source-text check: German face text present in the raw HTML for a paper with a German face;
   - one deliberate typed refusal (e.g. BM-01 with an out-of-domain temperature through its URL parameter, where supported) renders the refusal text;
   - the WASM check records exactly what is bound today. Until a FrankenSim capability reaches a reader (see am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh), the check records "no WASM capability bound" and passes as vacuous-by-declaration, stating so in the record. It never claims a WASM result.
3. Each check writes its own result, with what it examined (URLs, counts) into the release record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The release record's candidate section lists each of the six checks with examined URLs/counts and a pass/fail each. `candidateChecksPassed` is computed from them, never a literal.
- Step 1 alone: a new release record reads `candidateChecks: "not-implemented"` and `candidateChecksPassed: false`, and the deploy still promotes. After step 2, a deliberately broken candidate is refused before any alias moves. Planted negatives: a paper page returns 500; a lab chunk 404s; the refusal text is absent. Each is refused for its own reason.
- `rg -n 'candidateChecksPassed: true' scripts` finds 0 literal assignments.
- One real deploy, with its record, is shown to the orchestrator.

## Tests

- Unit tests for each check against a local served build, with a planted failing variant each.
- An integration test of the promote path refusing when any check fails.
- The gate change commits alone (AGENTS "Gate, test, and validator changes commit alone").
- Structured JSONL logs under artifacts/deploy-logs/ with each check's result.

Related: am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y (the original feature bead), am-rel-release-manifest-3gna.

A failed check refuses promotion before any alias moves (tested with a fake fetcher: a changed byte, a 404 chunk, a missing anchor, an empty tree; planted comparison-always-true, 3/8 red). title: Per-section review kits that let a German reader, a physicist or a non-physicist review a section in under an hour
description:
## Background

Every "reviewed" state needs a person, and 54 of 55 reviewer slots are empty (docs/OWNERS.md). The roles: German source fidelity, physics derivations, R2 readability by a non-physicist, the fifteen-minute tour, and the §21 final product test. Nobody can review a section today without learning the repo.

## What to do

A generator writes, per paper section, one self-contained review kit. It is a private file under artifacts/review-kits/, never a public page. It contains:
- **German fidelity:** the plate images beside the ledger lines;
- **translation:** the draft English beside each German sentence, once it exists;
- the explanation at R0 and R2;
- a short checklist per role;
- the §21 product-test prompts;
- a return block (name, date, role, findings) the reviewer fills and sends back, which an agent records in the receipt and the review beads.

This extends am-edn-review-packet-ee9t (the German source review packet export and review-record import) to the physics, R2-readability and product-test roles. Reuse its export and import path, and don't build a second one.

Mass-energy first: its kit is what makes the owner's review session possible (am-decision-how-review-happens-sepc).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A mass-energy kit exists that a reviewer can use offline, with every one of its 25 source units present.
- A dry run by an agent, filling the return block with a clearly fake test name that is never recorded, proves the recording path puts findings into the receipt format.
- Kits are regenerated from the records, and a stale kit is detectable by the content revision it names.

## Tests and logging

- Generator unit tests: every source unit of the section is present, and a stale kit names its content revision.
- A dry-run import of a filled return block into the receipt format, with a clearly marked fake name that is never committed.

Structured logs: each suite writes JSON lines to artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>.jsonl with the AGENTS.md fields that apply (timestamp, suite, logRunId, testId, beadId, paper, anchor, instrumentId, expected, actual, outcome, browser, viewport, jsEnabled, message). A failing browser test keeps a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot and console log.

title: Build the route and canonical-URL registry with an indexing audit
description:
# Build the route and canonical-URL registry with an indexing audit

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** C · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** platform, reader, release · **Plan sections:** ASTRA_V2 §18.8; AGENTS.md naming conventions and "Canonical document URLs never multiply into an index of slider positions" (traceability only)

## Background

Every route family in the graph declares its own canonical, indexing and sitemap facts, in prose, in its own bead:

- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: the `reading` face is canonical at the paper or section route; the `german` and `english` fallback pages are self-canonical, carry reciprocal `hreflang` alternates and are listed in the sitemap; `gloss`, `parallel`, `split`, `results` and `facsimile` fallback pages declare the paper route as canonical and are omitted; `rel=canonical` omits `?view=`, `?detail=`, `?lens=`, `?notation=`, `?units=`, `?open=` and `?tape=`.
- `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`: three static fallback pages per section declare the section route as canonical and are excluded from the sitemap.
- `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`: reuses the same pattern for R3 with its own parameters.
- `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: tape variants are `noindex`, canonicalise to the document URL, and are never listed in sitemaps.
- `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`: `/embed/*` is `noindex` and canonical to the lab page, and is the only framable prefix.
- `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`, `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, `am-disc-capstones-infra-3352`, `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`, `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`: each states its own rules, and the preview policy adds `noindex` plus sitemap exclusion for in-preparation pages.
- `am-tours-infra-g518`: `/tours`, `/tours/[id]`, the printable `/tours/[id]/sheet`, and `/tours/full-course/syllabus`. That bead declares the sheet self-canonical and excluded from the sitemap so it does not duplicate the tour it projects, and requires an entry here before it ships. Because it is self-canonical, invariant 1 requires it to address a content identity of its own rather than the tour's, so its entry keys on `tour-sheet:<id>` beside the tour page's `tour:<id>`: the sheet is a different document, the printable projection of a tour, not a second address for the tour itself. If its owner instead intends one identity for both, the honest entry is `noindex` with the tour page as canonical. The registry records whichever the owner declares; what it cannot record is a page that is indexable and self-canonical under an identity another indexable page already owns.

The sitemap itself is produced by `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2` (`src/app/sitemap.test.ts` asserts the empty-corpus output), and `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` fetches a short hand-written list of routes against the deployed candidate.

Nothing checks the set as a whole. With eleven owners writing prose about one shared surface, the predictable failures are duplication (two routes claiming to be the canonical home of one content identity), leakage (a `noindex` route reaching the sitemap, or a state parameter surviving into a canonical), and drift (a route family added later with no policy at all). The graph already contains one near miss: `am-disc-capstones-infra-3352` records that "A coordinator ruling briefly said the opposite; it was withdrawn after reading the owner's specification", about whether capstones live at `/capstones/<paper slug>` or `/discover/<paper slug>/capstone`.

The stakes are not only tidiness. `/about` publishes citation formats "for the edition, a paper, a section anchor, an equation or result anchor, and an instrument permalink, each including the content and translation revision identities". A citation is only as good as the guarantee that its URL is the canonical, stable address of that content identity, and that a second address for the same content does not exist.

ASTRA states the requirement: "Every route has a stable content identity and an edition/version relationship. Canonical URLs do not depend on the current array position of a result, translation paragraph, or tour stop. Internal citations use stable IDs; routing aliases can change without rewriting the scientific content."

## Scope

In scope: the declarative route registry; the content-identity key; canonical, indexing, sitemap and parameter policy per family; the sitemap and robots generation reading from the registry; `scripts/audit-routes.ts` and its quality-gate step; the report.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:
- the routes themselves and their rendering (every route-owning bead listed above);
- anchors, alias redirects and scroll restoration (`am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o`);
- the id and anchor grammar (`am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`);
- Open Graph image routes (`am-design-og-images-pwok`);
- the preview policy's decisions about what a preview contains (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`), whose outcomes this registry records;
- cache headers (`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`);
- structured bibliographic metadata, proposed separately as `am-scholarly-metadata-mjrx`.

## Requirements

### The registry

`src/app/routeRegistry.ts` declares one entry per route family. It is data, imported by the sitemap route, by `robots`, and by the audit; no route file states these facts independently.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pattern` | The App Router path, for example `/papers/[paper]/[section]/view/[face]` |
| `owner` | The bead id that owns the route |
| `identityKey` | The content identity this route addresses, as a template over stable ids, for example `paper:<paper>` or `section:<paper>/<section>` or `experiment:<experiment>`. Never an array position |
| `canonical` | `self`, or a template naming another family's URL |
| `indexing` | `index` or `noindex` |
| `inSitemap` | boolean; must be false whenever `indexing` is `noindex` |
| `alternates` | Language alternates as `{ hreflang, pattern }`, reciprocal by construction |
| `admittedParameters` | The query parameters this family may carry, each marked `presentation` or `state` |
| `profileVisibility` | Which release profiles serve it (`development`, `preview`, `launch`), so preview-only and in-preparation behaviour is data |

### Invariants the audit proves

Against the **built output**, not against the source:

1. **One indexable document per identity.** For every `identityKey` value produced by the fixture corpus, exactly one built route is `index` **and** self-canonical. Two self-canonical routes sharing an identity fail, naming both.
2. **Canonical targets exist.** Every non-self canonical resolves to a route that is built, is `index`, and is itself self-canonical. A canonical pointing at a `noindex` page fails.
3. **No state parameter in a canonical.** No emitted `rel=canonical` contains any parameter declared `state` anywhere in the registry. This is checked on the built HTML, so a route that forgets to strip one is caught even though its own bead's prose says it does not.
4. **Sitemap agreement.** The sitemap contains exactly the routes with `inSitemap: true` for the active profile, every entry returns 200 in the built output, and no `noindex` route appears. `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`'s sitemap route is generated from the registry rather than from a hand list.
5. **Reciprocal alternates.** Every `hreflang` alternate is mutual: if A lists B, B lists A, and both are self-canonical. This is the condition ASTRA sets before `hreflang` is added at all, and it is exactly what `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` specifies for the German and English face pages.
6. **No orphan routes.** Every route the build emits appears in the registry. A new route family added without an entry fails the build with its pattern, which is what prevents the next capstone-style drift.
7. **Identity keys are id-based.** An `identityKey` template that interpolates anything other than a stable id from `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` fails, so a canonical can never depend on a result's, paragraph's or tour stop's position.
8. **Framing policy agreement.** Exactly the `/embed/*` prefix carries `frame-ancestors *`; every other route denies framing, and no `X-Frame-Options` header is sent, matching the single-mechanism rule of `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`.
9. **Profile agreement.** Under `preview`, routes whose `profileVisibility` excludes preview are absent from the build and from the sitemap, which gives `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`'s leak audit a second, structural check.

### The report and the gate

10. `scripts/audit-routes.ts` writes `docs/audits/ROUTE_AUDIT.md`: every family with its owner, identity key, canonical, indexing, sitemap membership, alternates, admitted parameters and profile visibility, plus the counts of built routes per family and every violation found.
11. The audit registers a `routes` step in `scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts` (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`): family `fast`, required in CI and in the `preview` and `launch` profiles, owned by this bead.
12. `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` enumerates the registry instead of a hand-written list, so every route family is fetched against the deployed candidate and a new family cannot ship unchecked.

## Technical Approach

- `src/app/routeRegistry.ts` (data plus types), `src/app/routeRegistry.test.ts`, `scripts/audit-routes.ts`.
- The audit reads the built output: the static HTML for `rel=canonical`, `robots` meta and `hreflang`; the generated `sitemap.xml`; and the emitted route manifest for the built route list. It starts `next start` on a free port exactly as `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`'s static-output check does, and fetches over plain HTTP.
- The sitemap route and `robots` import the registry, so there is one source and the audit's job is to prove the built output matches it rather than to restate it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/app/routeRegistry.ts` declares every route family with all nine fields, and the sitemap route and `robots` read from it.
- [ ] Every invariant 1 to 9 is checked against the built fixture-corpus output, and each has a seeded violation that fails with a readable message naming the routes involved.
- [ ] `/tours/[id]/sheet` has an entry naming `am-tours-infra-g518` as owner, `canonical: self`, `inSitemap: false`, and an identity key distinct from the tour it projects, and the audit proves the built sheet pages match it.
- [ ] A route family emitted by the build with no registry entry fails with its pattern.
- [ ] An `identityKey` interpolating a non-id value fails.
- [ ] A `noindex` family with `inSitemap: true` fails validation before the build runs.
- [ ] Under the `preview` profile, excluded families are absent from the build and the sitemap.
- [ ] `docs/audits/ROUTE_AUDIT.md` is generated with every column and the violation list.
- [ ] The `routes` gate step is registered with this bead as owner and fails the build on any violation.
- [ ] `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` fetches its route list from the registry.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `routeRegistry.test.ts`: every entry has all fields; `noindex` with `inSitemap: true` fails; a canonical naming an unknown family fails; a non-reciprocal alternate pair fails; an `identityKey` with a non-id interpolation fails.
- `auditRoutes.test.ts`, against a built fixture corpus, with one seeded violation per invariant:
  - two self-canonical `index` routes sharing `paper:brownian-motion`;
  - a canonical pointing at a `noindex` page;
  - a built page whose `rel=canonical` retains `?tape=`;
  - a sitemap entry for a `noindex` route, and a sitemap entry returning 404;
  - a one-way `hreflang` pair;
  - a built route absent from the registry;
  - an `/embed/*` page denying framing and a non-embed page allowing it;
  - a preview build containing an excluded family;
  - a tour sheet declared `index` and self-canonical under the tour's own `tour:<id>` identity, which invariant 1 must reject naming both routes.

  Each must fail with the route or routes named, and the clean corpus must pass.
- `sitemapFromRegistry.test.ts`: the sitemap output equals the registry's `inSitemap` set for each profile; `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`'s existing empty-corpus assertion still holds.

### End-to-end tests

- The `routes` gate runs on the production build of the fixture site in CI, in the `development`, `preview` and `launch` profiles, and writes the report each time.
- A browser lane fetches every sitemap entry and asserts 200 with a non-trivial body, and fetches one representative `noindex` route per family and asserts the meta tag is present and the URL is absent from the sitemap.

### Structured logging

Through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, suite `route-audit`, file `artifacts/test-logs/route-audit/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `pattern`, `owner`, `identityKey`, `builtRouteCount`, `canonical`, `indexing`, `inSitemap`, `alternates`, `admittedParameters`, `profile`, `invariant`, `violation`, `offendingRoutes`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.

A failing invariant retains, under `artifacts/test-logs/route-audit/<log-run-id>/failures/<invariant>.json`, the offending routes, their emitted canonical and robots tags, the sitemap entry if any, and a one-line reproduction command.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Check the built output, not the source. Every one of these facts is already stated correctly in prose somewhere; the failures come from emission, not from intent.
- The registry must not become a second place to decide policy. Each route's owner still decides its own rules; the registry records them in one machine-readable place so they can be checked together.
- Do not add a route family to the registry to silence the orphan check without its owner agreeing to the fields. An unowned entry is worse than a failing build.
- Resist making `identityKey` clever. It exists to answer one question: which built documents claim to be the same thing?
- A `noindex` page is still a page a reader can reach and cite from. It is excluded from the index, not from the site, and its canonical must point somewhere real.
- **A dedicated static-figure route for embeds was proposed and is declined.** `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`'s no-frames alternative points at `/lab/<id>`, which already renders the instrument's question, the static worked example with its printed numbers and constant set, the execution label, the `notModeled` line and real links back to the source passages, without JavaScript and without framing; `am-plat-print-3orn` prints a captioned static figure of an accepted state from that same page. A separate figure family would therefore be a second address for the `experiment:<experiment>` identity that `/lab/<id>` already owns, which invariant 1 rejects, and it would have to be either framable, which would add a second framable prefix against invariant 8 and the single-mechanism rule of `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`, or unframable, which is what `/lab/<id>` already is. No entry is recorded and no route is added. A later proposal needs, in this order, a reader obstacle `/lab/<id>` cannot meet, a named owner willing to hold the fields, and its own identity key.
- This bead adds no route and removes none. If the audit shows that two families genuinely need to share an identity, that is a finding for their owners, not a licence for the registry to pick a winner.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: the first and largest route family, its canonical, `hreflang` and sitemap policy, and the static face fallback pages.
- `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`: the application, the `sitemap` and `robots` routes the registry feeds, and the static-output check pattern the audit reuses.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: browser lanes and failure evidence.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`: enumerates the registry instead of a hand-written route list.
- `am-plat-search-index-snx1`: every search document's route resolves to a declared canonical target.
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: the route report is launch evidence that the edition has one address per content identity.
- The proposed `am-scholarly-metadata-mjrx` bead: structured metadata is emitted on the canonical document of each identity and nowhere else.

title: constant sets exist twice and nothing compares them: a wrong value in the YAML record passes verify-constant-sets
description:
Found by pane31 on am-unwired-audits-uwot while planting a negative against the newly wired
`verify-constant-sets` gate. The plant passed, and the reason is the defect.

## The two copies

The modern and historical constant sets exist twice:

- `content/quantities/constant-sets/*.yaml` — eight content records
- `src/physics/reference/constants.ts` — the same constants hardcoded in TypeScript, e.g.
  `exact("molarGasConstant", "8.31446261815324", "J/(mol K)", ...)` at line 306

`src/physics/reference/constants.ts` contains no `readFileSync`, no YAML import and no reference
to `constant-sets`. It does not read the records. `getConstantSet()` returns the TypeScript copy.

## What that does to the audit

`scripts/verify-constant-sets.ts` does both of these, but never joins them:

- check 1 loads and schema-validates every YAML record
- check 3(a) asserts `R === N_A * k_B` using `getConstantSet("modern-si-2019")`, i.e. the TS copy

So the headline invariant is checked against TypeScript while the content records are checked only
for shape. Nothing compares a record's value to the constant the physics actually uses.

## Observed, both directions

Planted `molarGasConstant: 8.31446261899999` in
`content/quantities/constant-sets/modern-si-2019.yaml`, breaking `R = N_A * k_B` in the record:

    bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --only verify-constant-sets   ->   exit 0, PASSED

Reverted (`shasum -a 256 -c`, OK). Planted the identical defect in `src/physics/reference/constants.ts`:

    bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --only verify-constant-sets   ->   exit 1, FAILED
    field: molarGasConstant | expected: 8.31446261899999 | actual: 8.31446261815324

Reverted, sha256 verified, chain green again.

The gate works. It is aimed at one of the two copies.

## Why this matters here specifically

AGENTS.md treats constant provenance as a build gate, not a style preference: modern constants are
the exact 2019 SI values, historical constants carry their era and precision, and the two sets are
never mixed in one calculation without saying so. A content record carrying a value the physics
does not use is exactly the silent mixing that rule exists to prevent, and a reviewer reading
`content/quantities/constant-sets/` has no way to tell the record is decorative.

This is the same family as the licence table in am-niyd: no false sentence anywhere, an artifact
that looks authoritative, and nothing checking whether it is.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Edit `content/quantities/constant-sets/modern-si-2019.yaml` and change the `molarGasConstant`
   `value` and `exactDecimal` to `8.31446261899999`, breaking the exact product it documents.
2. Run `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --only verify-constant-sets`.
3. Observed: exit 0, PASSED. Expected: a failure naming the record.
4. Revert, then make the same change to the `exact("molarGasConstant", "8.31446261815324", ...)`
   call in `src/physics/reference/constants.ts` and rerun: exit 1, FAILED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide which copy is the source of truth. Either the TS constants are generated from the
      records, or the records are generated from the TS constants, or neither is and a check
      compares them entry by entry.
- [ ] Whichever is chosen, `verify-constant-sets` gains a check that fails when a record's value
      disagrees with the constant the physics uses, compared by quantity id across every set.
- [ ] FALSIFYING CASE required before acceptance: the YAML plant above must take the gate red.
      It currently passes, so this is a live red-to-green case rather than a hypothetical.
      Restore the file byte-identically afterwards and verify with `shasum -a 256 -c`.
- [ ] The comparison must cover the historical sets too, not only `modern-si-2019`. The printed
      Einstein sets are where an era mix-up would be hardest to spot by eye.

## Out of scope

- Whether `verify-constant-sets` belongs in the chain. It was wired in on
  am-unwired-audits-uwot at d7476734 and passes.
