title: Scaffold the Next.js App Router application with strict TypeScript, Biome, Bun tests, and an empty corpus
description: # Scaffold the Next.js App Router application with strict TypeScript, Biome, Bun tests, and an empty corpus **Epic:** `am-ep-scaffold-5wh` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.5, §2.4, §15.1, §15.2, §16.4, §16.6, §19.1 (traceability only) ## Background Batch A requires "`typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, and the architecture test green with an empty corpus" (§19.1). This bead creates that application: the single Next.js App Router root under `src/app`, strict TypeScript, Biome for lint and format, Bun for tests and scripts, and the planned directory layout that every later bead writes into. It deliberately contains no content, no physics, and no instruments, so later work lands in a clean, verified structure. The scaffold must already respect the product's non-negotiables: the reading experience works without JavaScript, without a GPU, and without running a simulation (§1.5); the initial reading route has no Three.js, pdf.js, or WASM in its dependency graph and at most 200 KiB of compressed first-route JavaScript (§16.4); no third-party scripts, fonts, or requests (§16.6); and the home page makes no claim that an edition exists before it does. Because three later beads need to prove the initial-route absence (this one, the UI extraction that introduces pdf.js and Three.js, and the performance budgets), this bead creates the single shared check they all use. One more shared mechanism belongs here for the same reason. Several reader and platform beads set a `data-` attribute on `` before first paint with a tiny inline script, and each records its script's hash "in the build's inline-script hash manifest, consumed by `am-plat-security-f644`": the theme script (`am-design-themes-typography-288q`), the Detail script (`am-read-detail-axis-sfc`), the view script and the root-arming script (`am-read-shell-routes-3ua`), the perspective, notation, and units script (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`), the storage key constants (`am-plat-local-storage-km8f`), and the generated offline chapter's shared Detail script (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`). Nothing owned generating that manifest, and the security bead (Batch C) only consumes it: its own text records the gap and recommends this bead. The scaffold is the right owner, because it owns the root layout that hosts inline scripts and the build that emits them, and the manifest must exist in Batch A, when the first inline script lands, not in Batch C. With the manifest owned here, a missing entry becomes a build failure instead of a silent Content-Security-Policy relaxation. ## Scope In scope: project initialization with the locked versions, runtime pins, TypeScript and Biome configuration, Bun test configuration, the directory layout, the root layout, a placeholder home page, error and not-found routes, `robots` and `sitemap` routes for an empty corpus, package scripts, the shared initial-route graph check, the inline-script registry and its hash manifest emitter, the local static-output check, and first real unit tests. Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the architecture gate (`am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`); donor extractions (`am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`, `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`, `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`); themes and fonts, including the first real inline script (`am-design-themes-typography-288q`); the reader routes (`am-read-shell-routes-3ua`); the gate registry and CI (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`); structured test logging (`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`); the Content-Security-Policy header, its hash directives, and the verification that every emitted inline script is registered (`am-plat-security-f644`, which consumes the manifest this bead emits); byte budgets and transferred-size measurement (`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`, which extends the graph check). ## Requirements 1. **Versions:** exactly those recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` by `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`; exact pins in `package.json`; `bun.lock` committed; `engines.node` set to the recorded Node.js version; `packageManager` set to the recorded Bun version so CI reads the same string. 2. **TypeScript:** `strict: true`, `noEmit`, bundler module resolution, path alias `@/*` to `src/*`. Enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` unless the stack decision records a reason not to. 3. **Directory layout** (plan §15.2), documented in `content/README.md`, `src/README.md`, and `public/README.md` rather than placeholder files: - `content/` with `papers/`, `source-blocks/`, `translations/`, `glosses/`, `annotations/`, `arguments/`, `foundations/`, `misconceptions/`, `historical-premises/`, `equations/`, `quantities/`, `experiments/`, `scenarios/`, `datasets/`, `tours/`, `bibliography/`; - `src/` with `app/` (the only App Router root), `content/`, `reader/`, `equations/`, `experiments/`, `workers/`, `physics/reference/`, `visuals/`, `units/`, `search/`, `testing/`; - `public/` with `papers/pdfs/`, `papers/transcripts/`, `wasm/`, `figures/` (only assets admitted for redistribution); - `docs/` with `provenance/`; `scripts/`; - `docs/README.md` and `scripts/README.md` layout notes that also list the source-layer paths other beads create, so nobody invents a second location or mistakes them for stray files: `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/` (per-key download configuration, `am-src-download-script-15ar`); `scripts/sources/ocr-plans/` and `scripts/sources/ocr-instructions/` (`am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`); receipts at `docs/provenance/.md` and survey records at `docs/provenance/survey/` (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`, `am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`); `docs/editorial/RECEIPT_FORMAT.md` (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`); `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml` (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`); and the gitignored root `sources/` directory for local-only pins and parent scans (its `.gitignore` entry is added by `am-src-download-script-15ar`). The scaffold creates none of these paths; it documents them. 4. **Routes:** `src/app/layout.tsx` (``, `metadataBase` `https://annus-mirabilis.com`, minimal chrome, no heavy imports, no remote font loading, system font stack until the typography bead lands); `src/app/page.tsx` (a static placeholder that says the edition is in preparation and links to the repository, with no claim that papers, translations, or instruments are available and no promised dates); `src/app/error.tsx`; `src/app/global-error.tsx`; `src/app/not-found.tsx`; `src/app/robots.ts`; `src/app/sitemap.ts` (lists only `/` for the empty corpus). Do not add scripts for tools that do not exist yet (`gates` arrives with `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`). 6. **Biome:** formatter and linter enabled; generated directories ignored. 7. **Shared initial-route graph check** `scripts/perf/initialRouteGraph.ts`: after a production build, determines the client JavaScript the `/` route loads and fails if it contains Three.js, pdf.js, a WASM file, or a WASM or worker loader. title: Wire the local and CI quality gate chain
description:
# Wire the local and CI quality gate chain

**Epic:** `am-ep-scaffold-5wh` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §17.1, §17.3,
§17.7 item 9, §18.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The per-paper definition of done requires `verify-content`, typecheck, lint, format, build, `ubs
--diff`, the WASM artifact test, and the Playwright vertical slice to be green (§17.7 item 9), and
the release workflow runs the quality gates before deploying anything (§18.3). Those gates must
exist as one ordered, reproducible chain that every agent runs the same way locally, that GitHub
Actions runs on every push and pull request, and that the release script runs for each publication
profile. If the release script kept its own list of gate commands, the two lists would drift; so
this bead builds **one typed gate registry**, and every consumer (local runs, CI, the release
profiles, the nightly job) selects steps from it.

Two principles from AGENTS.md shape the chain. First, **never weaken a gate** to get green: no
skipped lanes, loosened tolerances, deleted evidence, or reruns of flaky statistical tests. Second,
**a command that does not exist yet is never reported as passing**; the chain shows it as
`not-available` until the bead that creates it registers it, and a release profile that requires it
refuses. And CI never deploys: releases go only through the verified prebuilt workflow
(`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`).

## Scope

In scope: the gate registry, the runner script, the `gates` package script, release-profile
selection and refusal, the GitHub Actions workflow for the fast chain, the nightly workflow for
steps that are too slow for every push, log retention, and tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the individual gates' implementations (architecture
`am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`, content `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`, WASM `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`,
voice `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, license inventory `am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz`, scenarios
`am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`, browser `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, performance
`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`, resource stress `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu`, receipts
`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`, facsimile configuration `am-src-download-script-15ar`); the
browser-acceptance workflow file (`.github/workflows/browser-acceptance.yml`, owned by
`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`); deployment (`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`).

## Requirements

1. **Registry** `scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts`: a typed list of `GateStep` entries with `id`,
`title`, `command` (argument array), `family` (`fast`, `browser`, `perf`, or `apple`), `cadence`
(`every-run` or `nightly`), `requiredInCi` (boolean), `requiredInProfiles` (a subset of `scaffold`,
`preview`, `launch`), `availability` (a script path that must exist or a tool that must be on
`PATH`), and `owner` (the bead id that registered the step). Registry validation rejects duplicate
ids, unknown profiles, unknown families, and steps without an owner. The `apple` family exists
because AGENTS.md runs Apple validation locally and never in the website's CI: an `apple` step is
never selected by the CI workflow and is never required in a website release profile.
2. **Initial steps, in order:** `architecture` (`bun scripts/app-router-architecture.ts`),
`typecheck`, `lint` (`biome check`), `format-check`, `unit-tests` (`bun run test`), `ubs-diff` (`ubs
--diff`), `ubs-staged` (`ubs --staged`), `build` (last among the fast steps). All are `fast`,
`every-run`, and required in the `scaffold`, `preview`, and `launch` profiles; all except the two
`ubs` steps are required in CI.
3. **Later registrations** (each by its owning bead, in the same change that creates the command):

   | Step id | Owner | Family | Cadence | Notes |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `publication-contract` | `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` | fast | every-run | A `bun test` subset of the edition, dispatcher, architecture, and determinism tests, ordered first so release refusals come early |
   | `verify-content` | `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34` | fast | every-run | |
   | `verify-wasm-artifacts` | `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` | fast | every-run | |
   | `voice-lint` | `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` | fast | every-run | Until `verify-content` absorbs it |
   | `license-inventory` | `am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz` | fast | every-run | |
   | `scenarios` | `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3` | fast | every-run | |
   | `receipts` | `am-src-receipt-format-npo5` | fast | every-run | `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts`, with `--surveys`; no network |
   | `facsimile-config` | `am-src-download-script-15ar` | fast | every-run | `bun scripts/download-facsimiles.ts --check-config`; no network |
   | `perf-budget-change` | `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` | fast | every-run | The diff check that a change to a byte budget carries a committed measurement record and a decision entry |
   | `browser-acceptance` | `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` | browser | every-run | Separate CI job |
   | `perf-budgets` | `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` | perf | nightly | Measurement run against recorded profiles |
   | `resource-stress` | `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu` | perf | nightly | Repeated route changes and mounts; required in `preview` and `launch`, never on every push |

   Each later step is required in CI and in the `preview` and `launch` profiles unless its owner
   records a reason otherwise; a `nightly` step is required in those profiles but excluded from the
   every-push workflow. Two owners (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5` and `am-src-download-script-15ar`)
   have no dependency edge to this bead, so whichever of the two beads lands second adds the entry,
   and the registry test's availability probe proves the command exists.
4. **Runner** `scripts/quality-gates.ts`, with modes:
   - `--fail-fast` (local default): run available steps of the selected families in registry order,
   stopping at the first failure;
   - `--all` (CI): run every step of the selected families and summarize;
   - `--profile <scaffold|preview|launch>` (used by the release script): run exactly the steps
   required in that profile, regardless of cadence, fail-fast; any required step whose availability
   check fails is `refused`, and the run exits with code 2 before running anything;
   - `--cadence <every-run|nightly|all>` (default `every-run` in `--fail-fast` and `--all`, `all` in
   profile mode), and `--family <fast|browser|perf|apple>` and `--only <ids>` filters.
5. **Outcomes:** `passed`, `failed`, `not-available` (the step's script is absent), `skipped` with a
reason (`tool-unavailable` for an absent tool in a mode where the step is not required,
`not-required-in-ci`, or `cadence`), and `refused` (profile mode only). `not-available` and
`skipped` are never counted as passing. Exit codes: 0 when every required step passed, 1 on any
failure, 2 on refusal.
6. **Package script:** `bun run gates` runs `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --fail-fast --family
fast`.
7. **GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`): triggers on push and pull request to
`main` (never `pull_request_target`); `permissions: contents: read`; checkout pinned by commit SHA
with `persist-credentials: false`; the Bun version read from `package.json` `packageManager` and the
Node.js version from `engines.node`; `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts
--all --family fast --cadence every-run`; uploads `artifacts/test-logs/` as a workflow artifact on
failure; all third-party actions pinned by commit SHA; a concurrency group cancels superseded runs
on the same ref; no secrets; **no deployment, alias, or DNS step of any kind**. A second workflow
file `.github/workflows/nightly-gates.yml` runs `--all --family perf --cadence nightly` on a
schedule with the same permissions and artifact upload; it never runs `apple` steps.

## Technical Approach

The runner spawns each command, streams output, measures duration, records an outcome per step, and
exits with the codes above. It writes a summary table to stdout and JSON lines to the logs
directory. Registry entries are plain data plus an availability probe, so the runner's tests can
pass fixture registries whose commands are real processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bun run gates` passes locally on the empty-corpus scaffold.
- [ ] `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --profile scaffold` passes locally when `ubs` is installed, and
exits with code 2 naming the missing tool when it is not.
- [ ] The workflow passes on `main` and fails the job when any required step fails, with logs
uploaded.
- [ ] Not-yet-available steps are reported as such and never counted as passing.
- [ ] A `nightly` step is excluded from the every-push workflow and still required in the `preview`
and `launch` profiles.
- [ ] No `apple` step runs in either workflow.
- [ ] The workflow contains no deploy, alias, or DNS command and requests only read permission.
- [ ] README.md and AGENTS.md reference `bun run gates` and the profile flag consistently.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`scripts/quality-gates.test.ts` runs the real runner with small fixture registries whose commands
are real processes:
- a step running `bun -e "process.exit(0)"` passes; a step running `bun -e "process.exit(3)"` fails
and stops the chain in fail-fast mode;
- in `--all` mode later steps still run and the exit code is 1;
- a step whose script path does not exist reports `not-available` in `--all` mode and is not counted
as passing;
- in `--profile preview` mode, a required step whose script is absent produces `refused`, exit code
2, and no step runs;
- a required tool absent from `PATH` is `skipped: tool-unavailable` in `--all` mode when not
required in CI, and `refused` in profile mode;
- a `nightly` step is `skipped: cadence` under `--cadence every-run` and runs under `--cadence
nightly` and in profile mode;
- an `apple` step is never selected by `--family fast|browser|perf` and never by the CI invocation
used in the workflow;
- registry validation rejects a duplicate id, an unknown profile name, an unknown family, and a step
without an owner;
- the JSONL output contains one line per step with the fields below plus a summary line.

`scripts/quality-gates/workflowScan.test.ts`: reads every file in `.github/workflows/` and fails on
`vercel`, `deploy`, `alias`, `wrangler`, `cloudflare`, `pull_request_target`, or a `permissions`
block granting write access; a fixture workflow containing `vercel deploy` fails; a fixture workflow
invoking `--family apple` fails.

### End-to-end tests
The CI workflow itself on a pull request; a deliberately failing fixture step in the test suite
(never in the real registry) proves failure propagation, and its run directory, stdout, stderr, and
JSONL log are retained under `artifacts/test-logs/quality-gates/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
One JSON line per step `{timestamp, suite: "quality-gates", logRunId, mode, profile, cadence,
stepId, owner, family, command, outcome, reason, exitCode, durationMs, message}` to
`artifacts/test-logs/quality-gates/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, plus a summary line with counts per outcome.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Browser and performance families are slow; they run in separate workflow jobs owned by their
beads, but they are never dropped from the definition of done or from the `preview` and `launch`
profiles. `cadence: nightly` moves a step off every push without removing it from a profile.
- Keep the build step last among the fast gates so earlier failures surface quickly.
- CI minutes must not become a reason to skip gates; if the chain is slow, profile it.
- A release profile's step list only grows; removing a step from a profile requires a recorded
decision.
- The `apple` family is registered here so there is one registry, but it runs only on the owner's
machine; never add it to a website workflow.

comments.author: MaroonTiger
comments.text:
MaroonTiger: root cause found for the CI-only lang-required divergence on
structural.test.ts:49 (CI run 35203818634 at f2e0816, "Received length: 7").
Reporting precisely, including what I did NOT do -- I did not apply this fix,
another lane already had, and I want to be clear about that before anything
else.

WHAT I RULED OUT MYSELF, empirically, before finding the real cause (so the
next person doesn't re-walk this path):
- Stale generated/ artifact: fresh `bun run prepare:content` + direct run of
  structural.test.ts alone still gives 16 pass / 0 fail locally. Matches your
  own disproof.
- Cross-file registry pollution via simple sequential leftover state: I ran
  `bun test --isolate --timeout 60000` against exactly
  `verifyContent.test.ts check.test.ts structural.test.ts` together, 15
  times in a row -- zero reproductions. Also ran the FULL local suite exactly
  as `bun run test` would (`bun test --isolate --timeout 60000 src scripts`,
  756 files, 223s) -- 5275 pass / 4 fail, the 4 unrelated (a11y focus-trap
  test, not mine, not lang-required). structural.test.ts's own beforeEach
  (clearRegisteredChecksForTests() + registerStructuralChecks()) genuinely
  defends against leftover pollution when --isolate is used, in every
  configuration I could construct.
- The corpus itself containing a real German-term-without-lang or
  missing-lang TranslationUnit: I wrote a standalone script that imports the
  REAL compiler, REAL createBaseCorpus(), and explicitly force-registers
  registerI18nCheck() alongside the structural checks (simulating the worst
  case of a registry leak), then runs compileContent() on it for real. Result:
  0 lang-required diagnostics. The base corpus fixture is clean; even with the
  check forcibly active, nothing in it fires. So "the check leaked in AND the
  corpus deserved it" is not the explanation either -- if it fired, it must
  have fired on something other than what createBaseCorpus() currently
  produces, or through a path I have not identified at the diagnostic level.
- test-runner.ts's file classification producing a different LOCAL file set:
  ruled out as a real question, because I confirmed test-runner.ts is not
  actually reachable from any other module except its own test
  (quality-gates.test.ts) as of the registry.ts I first read -- but that
  registry.ts I first read was already stale, see below.

THE ACTUAL DIVERGENCE. I pulled the raw stdout and meta.json out of the CI
artifact for the failing run (test-logs-fast-gates, run 35203818634):

  quality-gates/20260917T091301Z-57f116a4/evidence/unit-tests.meta.json:
    "command": ["bun", "scripts/quality-gates/test-runner.ts"]

Every local reproduction attempt anyone made for this bug -- yours and mine --
ran `bun test --isolate --timeout 60000 src scripts` (the package.json `test`
script) directly, or a subset of it. At f2e0816, CI's actual "unit-tests" gate
step was NOT that command. It called test-runner.ts, which does its own file
discovery, partitions files into a "Bun runner suite" and a "Node runner
suite," and spawns each with spawnSync. The unit-tests.stdout.txt for that run
confirms it: "Discovered 770 test files: Bun runner suite: 502 files, Node
runner suite: 268 files."

At f2e0816, test-runner.ts's own bun invocation was:

    spawnSync("bun", ["test", ...partition.bunFiles], { cwd: rootDir, stdio: "inherit" })

No --isolate. No --timeout. That is the entire divergence: CI was running 502
files in one bun test process with isolation OFF, while every local
reproduction ran with isolation ON. That is sufficient on its own to explain a
failure that is 100% reproducible on CI and 0% reproducible locally regardless
of how many times or in what combination anyone re-ran it locally -- it isn't
a flaky race, it's a categorically different invocation.

The concrete mechanism isolation would have been guarding against: src/content/audits/verifyContent.test.ts calls registerVerifyContentChecks()
(which includes registerI18nCheck()) in three separate tests, and
src/content/checks/i18n/check.test.ts calls registerI18nCheck() directly.
Neither file has an afterEach/afterAll that calls
clearRegisteredChecksForTests() -- only a logger-flush afterAll in each. The
registry those functions write into (src/content/compiler/checks/registry.ts)
is a bare module-level `const registry = new Map()`. structural.test.ts's own
beforeEach clears and re-registers before each of its tests, which is why it
withstands ordinary leftover pollution -- but that defense assumes isolation
resets the module graph between files. Bun's own --help text is explicit that
--isolate means "a fresh global object; leaked handles from one file cannot
affect another," which is a narrower guarantee than "the module cache is
rebuilt," so a bare Map singleton surviving across files even under --isolate
is plausible; without --isolate at all, there is no defense whatsoever, which
matches what I could and could not reproduce.

I could not pin the exact diagnostic-level trigger further than this (my
forced-registration probe against the current base corpus gives 0, so
whatever fired in CI's un-isolated 502-file batch was not simply "the i18n
check saw createBaseCorpus() and correctly flagged it" -- something about the
un-isolated multi-file execution itself produced the 7). I am reporting that
gap honestly rather than asserting a mechanism I have not directly observed.

THIS IS ALREADY FIXED, NOT BY ME. Commit a02a35a ("fix(ci): resolve structural
i18n fixtures and browser-safe webpack bundling", am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx,
already on HEAD, 10 commits ahead of f2e0816) changed two things:
  1. scripts/quality-gates/test-runner.ts's own spawnSync call now passes
     ["test", "--isolate", "--timeout", "60000", ...partition.bunFiles].
  2. scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts's "unit-tests" step command was
     changed from ["bun", "scripts/quality-gates/test-runner.ts"] to
     ["bun", "run", "test"] entirely, bypassing test-runner.ts's partition
     model for the actual gate path.

I confirmed via `gh run view 35205167744 --log-failed` (the CI run for
a02a35a) that the lang-required/structural failure is gone: that run failed
for two unrelated reasons instead -- "Failed to spawn bun run test... ENOBUFS
(stdout or stderr buffer reached maxBuffer size limit)" on the unit-tests step
itself, and a voice-lint failure -- both of which line up with the next
commit's own title (1da6467, "resolve voice lint dashes, subprocess buffer
limits, and next config registry probe"). A run for current HEAD (1da6467,
run 35205749249) was in_progress when I checked; I have not waited on it or
polled further.

I am not claiming this bug as mine to close -- it was already fixed under
am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx by the time I finished tracing it. I'm posting
this because the mechanism (bare module-level check registry singleton, two
test files that register into it with no cleanup, defended only by other
files' own beforeEach and by --isolate) is a real, still-present latent
fragility even though the gate no longer exercises the vulnerable path. If
anyone ever runs these suites without --isolate again (a debug session, a
future tool), the same class of cross-file leak is possible. I have not added
afterEach cleanup to verifyContent.test.ts or check.test.ts myself since I
don't own that area and the immediate gate risk is already closed by
switching to `bun run test` -- flagging it for whoever does own test hygiene
there, not fixing it unilaterally.

pane31. AUDIT of the six gates carrying requiredInCi false, filed here because this bead owns the chain and two of the six. NOTE: this bead is CLOSED, so route it if it needs work. Nothing edited; report only.

NONE of the six is silently disabled. All six are deliberate, and the runner distinguishes the reasons in code (GateSkipReason = "tool-unavailable" | "not-required-in-ci" | "cadence"). But FOUR of the six are named in a release profile despite never being able to fail CI, so "advisory" and "load-bearing" are both true of them at different moments, which is the part worth knowing.

== THE TWO MECHANISMS, so the per-gate verdicts below are readable ==
CI, mode --all: quality-gates.ts:452 computes unmetRequiredSteps as
    stepDef?.requiredInCi && r.reason !== "cadence" && r.outcome !== "passed"
so a step with requiredInCi false CANNOT fail the CI run whatever it returns. That is the design, not an oversight.
RELEASE, mode --profile: quality-gates.ts:207-211 selects only steps whose requiredInProfiles includes the profile, and 218-250 REFUSES the entire profile with exit 2 if any selected step is merely UNAVAILABLE. So requiredInProfiles, not requiredInCi, is what makes a gate load-bearing at release.

== PER GATE, with evidence ==

1. ubs-diff            VERDICT: deliberately advisory in CI, LOAD-BEARING at release
   command ["ubs","--diff"], family fast, cadence every-run, owner am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx
   requiredInProfiles ["scaffold","preview","launch"]
   availability: AVAILABLE here. `ubs` resolves to /Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/ubs
   Why advisory in CI is right: ubs is a developer-local binary, not installed on a CI runner.
   THE RISK, and it is real: because it is in all three profiles, a release-profile run on any
   machine WITHOUT ubs refuses the whole profile at exit 2. Launch verification therefore cannot
   be completed on a clean machine that lacks a tool living in one developer's home directory.
   That is fail-closed rather than fail-open, which is the right direction, but it means the
   launch profile has an undeclared host dependency.

2. ubs-staged          VERDICT: identical to ubs-diff in every field except the command
   command ["ubs","--staged"], same profiles, same owner, availability AVAILABLE.
   Same host-dependency risk.

3. voice-lint          VERDICT: deliberately SUPERSEDED, honestly labelled, not a gap
   requiredInProfiles [] - named in NO profile - and requiredInCi false.
   Its registry title says so out loud: "Editorial voice lint (folded into verify-content as
   family voice)". Confirmed at the other end: scripts/verify-content.ts:55-56 reads "The
   standalone voice-lint quality-gate step is folded into this command as the registered check
   family 'voice'." verify-content IS requiredInCi true, so the enforcement did not vanish, it
   moved into a required gate.
   The only wart: the superseded entry still sits in the registry, which is what made me count
   "6 gates not required in CI" in my first sweep as if all six were equivalent. They are not.

4. perf-budgets        VERDICT: deliberately advisory in CI, LOAD-BEARING at release, and
                                decorative in substance - see am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww
   requiredInProfiles ["preview","launch"], cadence nightly, availability AVAILABLE.
   It DOES run: .github/workflows/nightly-gates.yml and perf-budgets.yml at 03:00 UTC. It
   reports PASSED. I filed the substance separately on its owning bead: its one budget row
   cannot fail for byte reasons by construction, proven by calling the evaluator both ways.

5. resource-stress     VERDICT: deliberately advisory in CI, LOAD-BEARING at release
   requiredInProfiles ["preview","launch"], cadence nightly, availability AVAILABLE.
   Runs 6/6 scenarios in about 114 ms total. It is in-process - it imports HeavyFixtureLaboratory
   from src/testing/runtime-fixtures/heavyFixture.ts and no browser driver - BUT it exercises the
   REAL production modules, src/experiments/lifecycle/concurrency.ts and
   src/visuals/three/dispose.ts, against that fixture. So unlike perf-budgets it can still catch
   a regression in disposal or suspension logic. I did not audit it further and am not calling it
   decorative; I am recording the distinction so the two nightly gates are not tarred together.

6. apple-quality       VERDICT: deliberately NOT YET BUILT, and correctly cannot block anything
   requiredInProfiles [] - named in NO profile - requiredInCi false.
   availability: NOT AVAILABLE, kind "script-missing", details "Script 'scripts/dsr-apple-quality.sh'
   does not exist". Confirmed by hand: that script is absent and ios/ is absent, though xcodebuild
   itself IS present at /usr/bin/xcodebuild.
   This is consistent with AGENTS.md, which says nothing under ios/ exists yet, and the entry
   names its owner am-app-apple-quality-gate-q6gs. Because requiredInProfiles is empty it is never
   selected in profile mode, so its absence cannot refuse a release. Correct as it stands.

== ANSWERS TO THE TWO QUESTIONS ASKED ==
Silently disabled: NONE. Six of six are deliberate, and two of them (voice-lint, apple-quality)
say so in their own registry text.
Named in preview or launch despite not running in CI: FOUR - ubs-diff and ubs-staged (also
scaffold), perf-budgets and resource-stress.

== AGAINST AGENTS.md's CREATION-GATE TEST ==
"The boundary test is whether running code branches on the artifact." All six pass it: four are
branched on by the profile selector at quality-gates.ts:207 and the availability refusal at 218;
voice-lint's enforcement is branched on inside verify-content as family "voice"; apple-quality is
branched on by the availability check, which is exactly what keeps it from blocking a release it
cannot yet verify. None of the six is process for its own sake.

== THE ONE THING I WOULD ACT ON ==
The ubs host dependency. Everything else here is working as designed. If launch verification is
ever meant to run somewhere other than this machine, ubs-diff and ubs-staged will refuse the
profile, and that will look like a broken release rather than a missing binary.

title: Emit ScholarlyArticle and translation metadata with a strict attribution separation
description:
# Emit ScholarlyArticle and translation metadata with a strict attribution separation

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** C · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** platform, source, search · **Plan sections:** ASTRA_V2 §18.12; AGENTS.md "Sources, Rights, and Provenance" and "Rights layers stay separate" (traceability only)

## Background

The site is a critical edition whose purpose is that people can read, cite and find four 1905 papers. It already holds, as validated records, everything a bibliographic description needs:

- per paper, the bibliographic key, printed German title, author line, typed dates by kind (date-line, receipt, issue publication), the journal record with `name`, `series: 4`, `volume`, `wholeSeriesVolume`, `issue`, `issueSource`, `pages: {first, last}`, `doi` and `doiVerifiedAt`, plus `laterEditionDois[]` (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`, and the receipts written through `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`);
- the verified DOIs themselves: `10.1002/andp.19053220607`, `10.1002/andp.19053220806`, `10.1002/andp.19053221004`, `10.1002/andp.19053231314`, `10.1002/andp.19063240204`, with the 2005 reissue DOI correction recorded (Crossref records `10.1002/andp.200590007` as the reissue of the light-quanta paper, not of paper 4);
- translator and editor credits with review dates and reviewer names, and the correction graph (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`);
- `contentRevision` and `translationRevision`, kept separate by design;
- distinct language documents: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` makes the `german` and `english` face pages self-canonical with reciprocal `hreflang="de"` and `hreflang="en"` alternates, which is exactly the precondition ASTRA sets before `hreflang` is meaningful;
- citation formats published on `/about` "for the edition, a paper, a section anchor, an equation or result anchor, and an instrument permalink, each including the content and translation revision identities" (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`).

None of it is emitted in a machine-readable form. A graph-wide search for `ScholarlyArticle`, `schema.org` and `JSON-LD` returns nothing.

The gap matters twice. The first reason is ordinary discoverability: a scholar, a library tool or a reference manager that meets `/papers/special-relativity` learns nothing about what it is looking at. The second reason is the site's own honesty rule, and it is the one that makes this bead more than plumbing. AGENTS.md keeps rights and authorship layers strictly separate: "Original historical text, facsimile scans, the new translation, new explanatory prose, interactive code, numerical libraries, fonts, images, and historical datasets each carry their own recorded rights status." The characteristic failure of a naive metadata block is to collapse them: it emits one record per page with Einstein as `author` and 1905 as `datePublished`, thereby attributing the site's own English translation and explanatory prose to Einstein and backdating them by 120 years. That is precisely what ASTRA warns against: "Do not identify a new commentary as an article published in 1905 or attribute it to Einstein."

ASTRA also states the limit, which this bead must state too: structured metadata improves machine readability; it does not guarantee search ranking or a rich-result display.

## Scope

In scope: the metadata projection and its generator; the two-entity model and the attribution separation; emission on canonical document pages only; the validator and its build gate; the human-readable citation block's shared source; tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:
- receipts, their parser, checker and `receiptToSourceAsset` mapping (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`);
- the paper, journal and citation record schemas (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`);
- the rights vocabulary and per-asset rights statements (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`), and the license decision (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`);
- reviewer names, consent and the correction graph (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`, `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`);
- `/sources`, `/about` and the how-to-cite prose (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`), which this bead feeds rather than duplicates;
- canonical URLs, `hreflang` and the sitemap (`am-read-shell-routes-3ua`, and the proposed `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6`);
- the search index (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`);
- later reviewed editions in other languages (`am-later-language-editions-sp4e`), which this bead's model must not block.

## Requirements

### Two entities, never one

1. **The historical article.** For each paper, a `ScholarlyArticle` describing the document Einstein published:
   - `name`: the printed German title, exactly as the source face carries it;
   - `author`: Albert Einstein, with no other author;
   - `inLanguage`: `de`;
   - `datePublished`: the issue publication date at its recorded precision; `dateReceived` where the record carries it;
   - `isPartOf`: the journal record as a `PublicationIssue` inside a `PublicationVolume` inside a `Periodical` named *Annalen der Physik*, carrying `volumeNumber`, the whole-series volume as an additional property, `issueNumber`, `pageStart` and `pageEnd`;
   - `identifier`: the verified DOI, and `laterEditionDois[]` emitted as clearly labelled later editions, never as the citation DOI;
   - `sameAs` is emitted only for identifiers the receipt verified, with its `verifiedAt` date recorded in the projection.
2. **The site's edition.** A separate entity for what this site publishes about that paper:
   - a translation entity for the English face, with `translator` naming the site's translator and editor credits, `inLanguage: en`, `translationOfWork` pointing at the historical article, `datePublished` the edition's own date, and `version` the `translationRevision`;
   - a commentary entity for the explanatory prose of that paper's reading face, with its own `author` (the site's named contributors and roles, including editorial agents by model where `am-design-sources-about-zumd` records them), `isBasedOn` the historical article, and `version` the `contentRevision`;
   - `license` from the license-status projection of `am-design-sources-about-zumd`. While the status is `provisional`, the `license` field is **omitted** rather than guessed, and the projection records why.
3. **Disjoint attribution, enforced.** A validator fails the build when:
   - Einstein appears as `author` or `translator` of any entity other than the historical article;
   - any entity other than the historical article carries a `datePublished` in 1905 or 1906;
   - the translation entity lacks `translationOfWork`, or the commentary entity lacks `isBasedOn`;
   - the historical article carries a `translator`, a `version`, or a `license` (the German text is public domain and the site grants nothing over it);
   - a DOI appears on any entity other than the historical article.

### Where it is emitted

4. Metadata is emitted **only on the canonical document** of a content identity, so a `noindex` variant, a face fallback page that canonicalises elsewhere, a tape URL and an embed never carry it. On the German and English face pages, which are self-canonical language documents, the emitted set is the historical article plus the entity for that language face, and nothing else.
5. Emission is server-rendered into the static HTML, so it is present without JavaScript and identical in the offline chapter files where those carry the same identity.
6. Under the `preview` profile, a paper absent from `getPublishedPapers()` emits nothing at all, rather than a partial record, so the preview leak audit of `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g` has nothing to find.

### One source for the human and machine forms

7. The projection that builds the structured metadata also supplies the fields for the human-readable citation block on `/about` and on each paper page, so the printed citation and the machine record cannot disagree. `am-design-sources-about-zumd` renders the block from this projection instead of composing its own fields, and a test asserts the two forms carry identical values for title, author, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI, date and revision identities.

### Honest limits

8. `/sources` gains one sentence, passing the voice lint, stating that the site publishes structured bibliographic metadata to make the edition machine-readable, that the historical article and the site's own translation and commentary are described as separate works with separate authorship, and that such metadata does not determine how any search engine ranks or displays the pages.
9. No claim of indexing, ranking or rich-result eligibility appears anywhere in the repository, and a phrase scan enforces it.

## Technical Approach

- `src/content/metadata/scholarlyProjection.ts` builds both entities from the compiled paper record and the parsed receipt, using `parseReceipt` and `receiptToSourceAsset` rather than re-reading the receipt file.
- `src/content/metadata/attributionCheck.ts` implements requirement 3 and runs in the content compiler, so a violation fails `bun run build` rather than a later audit.
- `src/content/metadata/JsonLd.tsx` is a server component emitting one `application/ld+json` script per canonical document; the payload is serialised through a strict encoder that rejects any key not in the declared shape.
- The citation-block fields are exported from the same projection and consumed by `am-design-sources-about-zumd`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each published paper's canonical document carries exactly two or three entities: the historical article, and the language or commentary entity appropriate to that document.
- [ ] The historical article carries the printed German title, Einstein as sole author, `inLanguage: de`, the typed publication date at its recorded precision, the full journal record including the whole-series volume, the verified DOI, and later-edition DOIs labelled as such.
- [ ] The translation entity carries the site's translator and editor credits, `inLanguage: en`, `translationOfWork`, and the `translationRevision` as its version; the commentary entity carries the site's authors, `isBasedOn`, and the `contentRevision`.
- [ ] Each of the five attribution violations in requirement 3 fails the build with a message naming the entity and the field; a seeded record with Einstein as translator, and one with a 1905 `datePublished` on the commentary, each fail.
- [ ] While the license status is provisional, `license` is omitted and the reason is recorded; with a decided fixture it is emitted from `NOTICE.md`.
- [ ] No `noindex` route, face fallback page canonicalising elsewhere, tape URL or embed carries metadata; the German and English face pages carry the article plus their own language entity only.
- [ ] Metadata is present in the served HTML with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] Under `preview`, an unpublished paper emits nothing.
- [ ] The human citation block and the structured record carry identical values for title, author, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI, date and revision identities.
- [ ] `/sources` carries the limits sentence, and the phrase scan finds no ranking or rich-result claim.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `scholarlyProjection.test.ts`, against the real compiled fixture records and fixture receipts: every field above for each of the five keys; the whole-series volume is emitted as an additional property and not as `volumeNumber`; `laterEditionDois[]` are labelled later editions; the paper-4 reissue-DOI correction is respected, so `10.1002/andp.200590007` never appears as paper 4's identifier.
- `attributionCheck.test.ts`: the five violations, each failing with the entity and field named; a correct record passing; a record with no `license` while provisional passing with its recorded reason.
- `jsonLdEmission.test.tsx`: emission on a canonical document; no emission on a `noindex` route, a face fallback page canonicalising elsewhere, a tape URL and an embed; the German and English face pages emit the article plus their own language entity; the strict encoder rejects an undeclared key.
- `citationParity.test.ts`: the human block and the structured record agree field by field for every fixture paper; a seeded divergence fails, naming the field.
- `previewProfile.test.ts`: an unpublished paper emits nothing under `preview`.
- `metadataClaims.test.ts`: the phrase scan over repository prose and page copy rejects seeded claims such as "improves our search ranking" and "guarantees a rich result".

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, against the production build of the fixture site:

1. Load each paper's canonical document with JavaScript disabled, parse the emitted `application/ld+json`, and assert the two-entity shape and the disjoint authorship.
2. Load the German and English face pages and assert the article plus one language entity each, with the reciprocal `hreflang` alternates `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` emits.
3. Load a tape URL, an embed and a Detail fallback page and assert no metadata is present.
4. In a `preview`-profile build, assert an unpublished paper's page carries none.
5. Assert that the visible citation block on the paper page and the parsed record agree on every shared field.

### Structured logging

Through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, suite `am-scholarly-metadata-mjrx`, file `artifacts/test-logs/scholarly-metadata/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `route`, `entityTypes`, `articleAuthor`, `translationTranslator`, `commentaryAuthor`, `doi`, `laterEditionDois`, `datePublished`, `datePrecision`, `contentRevision`, `translationRevision`, `licenseEmitted`, `licenseStatus`, `attributionViolations`, `emittedOnCanonicalOnly`, `profile`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`.

A failing attribution or parity case retains, under `artifacts/test-logs/scholarly-metadata/<log-run-id>/failures/<testId>.json`, the emitted payload, the offending entity and field, the record it was built from, and a one-line reproduction command.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- One record per page is the tempting shape and the wrong one. The page carries an 1905 article **and** a 2026 translation **and** a 2026 commentary, by different people under different rights, and the whole point of the edition is that those layers stay distinct.
- Never emit a DOI for the site's own work. A DOI on the translation entity would assert an identifier the site does not hold and would invite a citation of Einstein's paper that resolves to this site.
- The whole-series volume is not `volumeNumber`. Annalen's series-4 volume 17 and its whole-series number are different facts, both recorded, and collapsing them produces a wrong citation that looks right.
- Emit nothing while the license is undecided rather than guessing a permissive one. An omitted field is honest; a wrong license statement is a claim about other people's rights.
- Metadata must never become a second source of bibliographic truth. Build it from the receipts and the paper records, and let the citation block read the same projection, or the two will disagree the first time a date precision changes.
- Say the limit out loud. Structured metadata makes the edition machine-readable; it decides nothing about how anyone ranks or displays it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: the `Paper`, journal and `Citation` record shapes the projection reads.
- `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`: the receipt parser, checker and mapping that supply verified DOIs, typed dates and translation credits.
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: the canonical documents metadata is emitted on, and the self-canonical German and English language pages with their reciprocal alternates.
- `am-design-sources-about-zumd`: the license-status projection, the authorship and translation policy, and the citation block that consumes this projection.
- `am-edit-review-records-hofz`: translator and editor credits and their review states.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: browser lanes and failure evidence.

Related without an edge:
- The proposed `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6` decides which document is canonical for each identity; this bead emits only there. Until it exists, emission follows each route owner's declared canonical.
- `am-later-language-editions-sp4e`: a later reviewed edition adds one more language entity per paper under the same two-entity model, with no change to the historical article.

Unblocks:
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: machine-readable bibliographic identity is launch evidence that the edition can be cited and found.

title: OWNER DECISION: where a sentence's boundaries are recorded, and against which text
description:
# OWNER DECISION: where a sentence's boundaries are recorded, and against which text

## The decision, in one sentence

**When a paragraph is cut into sentences, in what record are the resulting BOUNDARIES written
down, and against which string are their offsets measured - so that two independent cuts of the
same paper can be compared with each other, and so that a frozen sentence id keeps meaning the
text it was frozen against?**

Everything below is measured at `30bbbc89` on 2026-09-21. Nothing here is a proposal to change
a frozen id, and nothing here says the Brownian freeze is wrong.

## The measured status quo: the record exists, is guarded, and is empty

The span field is not missing. It is specified by this bead's neighbour
`am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` ("Span revisions", section C.9) and it is **built**:

- `src/content/schemas/spans.ts` defines `SpanAnchor { start, end, blockRevision, textDigest }`.
- `src/content/schemas/source.ts:642` defines `SentenceSpan { id, span }`, and `:665` makes
  `sentenceSpans: readonly SentenceSpan[]` a field of every `SourceBlock`, validated on load
  against that block's own plain text and revision.
- `src/content/editions/editionContract.ts:271` implements check 15, reporting
  `span-revision-stale` and `span-digest-mismatch` **separately**, exactly as the bead requires.
- Alignment edge endpoints already carry `range?: SpanAnchor` (`source.ts:1085`, `:1089`).

That design answers the coordinate-system question properly: a span is an offset into a named
block's text at a named revision, with a digest of the sliced text, so a re-cut or re-worded block
makes its own spans fail rather than silently re-point.

**It has no data.** Measured: zero occurrences of `sentenceSpans` anywhere under `content/`, and
no `edition.yaml` exists in the tree, so `reconciliationRunId` - the field that would name "the
accepted segmentation tool run" - has no instance either. Check 15 run against all four papers
today reports, for each:

    not-available - "Check 15 (Span revision currency over source blocks and alignment edges)
                     could not run: no spans were supplied"

Credit where it is due: it refuses rather than passing over an empty set.

## Three span vocabularies, and the one that reaches the records is the one that is thrown away

1. `SentenceProposal { index, text, start, end }` - what the segmenter computes
   (`segmentSentences.ts:42`).
2. `SegmentSpan { start, end, text?, id? }` - what `validateSegmentation` checks
   (`segmentSentences.ts:307`). No revision, no digest. It has **no production call site**: every
   call in the tree is from a test.
3. `SpanAnchor` - the specified, guarded, empty one above.

The offsets die at `segmentLedger.ts:174-182`, which maps `{index, text, start, end}` to
`ProposedSentence { id, text, inlineMathIds }`. The cut is computed, used to slice the text, and
discarded in the same expression.

## The manifest, where the frozen ids actually live, records no position below the page

`ManifestUnit.locators` is `{ page, column?, line?, region?, splitPage? }`. Measured over the 90
frozen Brownian sentence units: they use exactly six fields - `id`, `kind`, `section`,
`containedIn`, `locators`, `destination` - and **zero** of them carry `region`, `line` or
`column`. Every sentence on page 549 carries the identical locator `page: 549`. Their only
ordering is the `-s1`, `-s2` suffix in the id.

So the manifest records that a division happened, and its order, and not its boundaries. Two
different cuts of one paragraph into the same number of sentences produce byte-identical manifests.

The special-relativity manifest names this itself, and its note is now half-stale:

    unfrozenRequiredUnitKinds:
      - kind: sentence
        blockedBy: am-cm-source-manifest-6qa
        reason: MANIFEST_UNIT_KINDS has no sentence kind and locators are page-scoped.

The first clause stopped being true with the owner's 2026-09-20 ruling on `am-xz2d` ("Add a
sentence kind"). The second is still exactly true, and is this bead.

## The immediate consequence, measured on Brownian

`am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg` froze 90 sentence ids at `2026-09-21T20:58:37Z`. Its own snapshot
header says they were "cut on 2026-09-21 **from plate reads of all twelve pages**".

Re-running `segmentLedger` over today's ledger - unchanged since 20:25:32Z, 33 minutes before the
freeze - gives a different division:

| | manifest (plate read) | segmentLedger (machine-draft ledger) |
|---|---|---|
| sentence ids | 90 | 97 |
| paragraphs carrying them | 32 | 50 |

Every manifest paragraph id is reproduced; the segmenter adds 18 more. And for the 32 paragraph
ids present on both sides, **18 carry a different number of sentences**: `s3-p8` is 5 against 1,
`s3-p2` is 6 against 2, `s4-p6` is 7 against 3.

I tested the obvious mechanical explanation - that the segmenter splits paragraphs the plate read
kept whole, so the extras are continuation halves - by merging each extra paragraph into the
manifest paragraph it follows. **It does not reconcile them**: 13 match, 19 still differ, and now
in both directions (`s1-p3` is 5 frozen against 8 merged). So no single mechanism is claimed here.
The two divisions differ at both the paragraph and the sentence layer.

**This is not a claim that the freeze is wrong.** The manifest was cut from the plates; the ledger
is a machine draft (`ap-17-549-machine-draft.txt`) whose paragraph structure nobody has reviewed.
The plate-read division is the more likely correct one. The point is the opposite: the better
division is probably the frozen one, and there is still no record in this repository that could
demonstrate that, or notice the day it stops being true. Same ids, different divisions, nothing
compares them - and the one function that could (`validateSegmentation`) checks contiguity inside
one division, never agreement between two.

## The options

### Option 1 - Spans live on the `SourceBlock` only; fill the record that exists

The manifest keeps page-scoped locators. `SourceBlock.sentenceSpans` becomes the single home for
boundaries, and the segmenter emits `SpanAnchor`s into it instead of discarding offsets. The
manifest's sentence units keep the frozen ids and gain nothing.

Cost: source-block records must exist before any boundary is recorded, and today none do. Until
then check 15 stays `not-available` and the Brownian division stays unrecorded.

Gain: one coordinate system, already guarded by revision and digest, already checked. No schema
decision to make. The SR blocker note loses its second clause by becoming somebody else's field.

### Option 2 - The manifest unit gains a span as well

`ManifestUnit` gets an optional span alongside its locators, so the inventory can record what it
cut without waiting for source blocks.

Cost: a span into a string the manifest does not hold. The manifest records no text at all, so
the offsets would have to name an external coordinate system - which ledger file, at which
digest - and that is a second span vocabulary with its own staleness rules, next to the one that
already has them. It also reopens a closed P0 (`am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`) and touches four
frozen inventories.

Gain: the plate-read division becomes recoverable now, not after the editions are authored.

### Option 3 - Record the division as a run, and compare, without moving either record

Neither record gains a field. The segmentation run is recorded (the `reconciliationRunId` hook
already specified in `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` section D), and a harness check compares the
manifest's sentence ids against `segmentLedger`'s output for each paper, reporting disagreement
as a flag rather than an error while the ledger is a machine draft.

Cost: does not record boundaries, so it cannot tell a re-cut from a re-numbering. It compares
id sets, which is strictly weaker than comparing spans.

Gain: it is buildable today, needs no schema decision, and it would have surfaced the 18
paragraph disagreements above the moment the freeze landed.

## What no option here settles

- **Which division is right.** That is an editorial question answered at the plates, by the
  inventory author, not by any record shape.
- **Whether a machine-draft ledger is an admissible coordinate system at all.** Recording spans
  against `ap-17-549-machine-draft.txt` would pin boundaries to unreviewed machine structure. If
  spans are measured against the ledger rather than against an authored source block, this
  question has to be answered first.
- **Whether `validateSegmentation` should get a production call site.** It guards contiguity
  within one division; it is not the thing that compares two. Under every option it stays a
  library function until something calls it, and that is a separate, smaller decision.

## Routing, if it is wanted

- `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` (in_progress, P0) owns every piece of Option 1 and Option 3:
  the segmenter, `SourceBlock.sentenceSpans`, check 15 and the harness.
- `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa` (**closed**, P0) owns the manifest schema and the locator
  validator. Only Option 2 disturbs it.
- The four inventory beads (`am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg`, `-light-quanta-skp`,
  `-relativity-0u9`, `-mass-energy-g2d`, all in_progress, all P0) hold the frozen ids and the
  half-stale blocker note that this bead retires.

## Recommendation (pane31 / AmberFalcon - mine, not the orchestrator's and not the owner's)

**Option 3 now, Option 1 as the destination, Option 2 not at all.**

Option 2 is the one that looks most responsive and is the trap: it puts an offset in a record
that holds no text, which is how a second staleness vocabulary gets born beside a good one.

Option 1 is right and cannot be done yet, because the record it fills does not exist for any
paper. Its one cheap piece can be done today and should be: make the segmenter carry its offsets
through as `SpanAnchor`s instead of dropping them at `segmentLedger.ts:174`, so the day a source
block is authored the division is recorded rather than recomputed.

Option 3 is the part that pays now. A harness check comparing manifest sentence ids to
`segmentLedger` output is small, needs no decision from anyone, and is the difference between
finding this in a dispatch and finding it in a lane. It should report a flag and not an error
while the ledger is a machine draft, because on today's evidence the disagreement is most likely
the ledger's fault and an error would pressure somebody into "fixing" a plate-read division to
match a machine one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The owner (or the orchestrator on delegation) picks an option, or rejects the framing.
- [ ] The decision is recorded the way the `am-xz2d` ruling was: verbatim in the bead, and
      quoted at the code it governs. (Checked: `am-xz2d` is not in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; its text
      lives in the bead and is quoted in `src/content/manifest/types.ts`, `validator.ts` and
      `schema.ts`. A dated `D-2026-..-..` entry in `docs/DECISIONS.md` is available if the owner
      prefers one, but that is not where the precedent put it.)
- [ ] The chosen work lands on the named beads above; this bead is closed by the orchestrator
      when the routing exists, not when the work is done.
- [ ] If any option other than 2 is chosen, the `unfrozenRequiredUnitKinds` note in the
      special-relativity manifest loses its "locators are page-scoped" clause or gains the
      decision's id, so no inventory stays blocked on a resolved question.
notes: HOLD, 2026-09-21, orchestrator (TanElk). Do NOT act on the recommendation's 'can be done today and should be' line. The cheap piece of Option 1 - carrying the segmenter's offsets through as SpanAnchors instead of dropping them at segmentLedger.ts:174-182 - is explicitly deferred, verbatim reason: 'If the segmenter's division turns out to be the wrong one, preserving its offsets is preserving the wrong boundaries with better fidelity, and it would be much harder to argue against once recorded.' The three named cases s3-p8, s3-p2 and s4-p6 are with the inventory pane to adjudicate against the plates. The span decision does not go to the owner until that comes back, because if the plate read does not hold on some paragraphs this stops being a question about recording boundaries and becomes one about frozen ids and alias retirement. The orchestrator rules on the sequence then.

comments.text:
ANSWER TO THE ORCHESTRATOR'S QUESTION, 2026-09-21: does Option 3 key on labels or compare text?

IT KEYS ON LABELS. The orchestrator is right and so is the worry. My own wording was "a harness
check compares the manifest's SENTENCE IDS against segmentLedger's output", and both measurements
in this bead's description are label-keyed: an id-set difference, and per-paragraph sentence
counts grouped by containedIn. Against an allocation history with four withdrawn labels, that
reports collisions as disagreements. As specified it would reproduce the hand error automatically
and at scale.

IT CAN BE RE-SPECIFIED WITHOUT SPANS, and not by comparing text. The two records share no
text-derived key today - the manifest has a page and no text, the segmenter has text and no page -
so a text comparison does need boundaries. But there is a third key that is a function of the
text on BOTH sides and is not an allocation history: THE PRINTED PAGE.

  - manifest side: every sentence unit carries locators[0].page, read off the plate.
  - ledger side: the ledger carries its own "[[ANNALEN-PAGE n]]" line, once per sheet, in all
    four ledgers (12, 17, 31 and 3 occurrences, one per TRANSCRIPTION PAGE marker). No offset is
    inferred and nothing is hard-coded.

Neither number is allocated by an editor; both are properties of the plate. So a page-keyed
comparison does not depend on Option 1.

MEASURED, so the claim is not just structural. Assigning each segmenter sentence to the page whose
text contains it, and comparing per-page counts with the manifest's:

  brownian-motion   90 sentences, 12 pages:  6 agree, 6 differ
                    deltas p550 +1, p553 +1, p555 -1, p556 +1, p557 +4, p558 +1
                    0 sentences unplaced, 0 matching more than one page

Page 557 carrying +4 is a specific, checkable claim about one plate rather than a label artifact.

AND A TRAP THE SAME RUN WALKED INTO, which the harness has to avoid by construction: light-quanta
and mass-energy have ZERO sentence units in their manifests today, so the same comparison reports
17 and 3 "differing" pages that are nothing of the kind. A page-keyed harness must report
not-available when a manifest carries no sentence units, the way editionContract check 15 already
reports not-available when no spans are supplied. Brownian is currently the only paper where this
comparison means anything.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, so nobody mistakes it for the destination: it is blind to a boundary that moves
WITHIN a page. Two divisions with the same per-page count and different cuts are indistinguishable
to it. It is a screen, not a proof, and strictly weaker than comparing spans.

ONE PIECE OF WORK IT NEEDS, which does not exist: the segmenter discards the page. segmentLedger.ts
:100 strips the markers with .replace(PAGE_MARKER, "\n"), and ProposedBlock.locators is declared in
the type and never populated - every paragraph block comes back with locators undefined. The
measurement above worked around that by re-finding each sentence's whitespace-normalised text in
the raw ledger, which is an approximation and should NOT be the implementation; populating
locators from the markers the segmenter already parses is.

Worth noticing together: the segmenter reads both text-derived keys it has and throws both away -
the page at :100 and the offsets at :174 - and keeps only the label, which is the one key that is
not a function of the text.

CONCLUSION. Option 3 does not depend on Option 1, provided it is re-keyed from labels to printed
pages and reports not-available where a manifest has no sentence units. The recommendation is
unchanged: Option 3 now, Option 1 as the destination, Option 2 not at all.

THE CORRECTION IS RIGHT AND THE REASON IT IS RIGHT IS NOT THE ONE GIVEN. My guard encoded the

So special-relativity would not in fact have cleared a zero-check. That does not rescue the

THE HARNESS KEYS ON THE PRINTED PAGE. Both records carry it independently and neither
allocates it:

  manifest  - read from the plate
  ledger    - its own [[ANNALEN-PAGE n]] line

Orchestrator verified the independence rather than accepting it: ANNALEN-PAGE is only ever
parsed and validated in this repository. ledgerTokenizer.ts:183 reads it; validateLedger.ts
checks it is strictly increasing, non-duplicated, and inside the journal's page range. No
code writes it from a manifest. The ledger side therefore has its own integrity check on
the key.

Measured by pane31 on Brownian: 12 pages, 6 agree, 6 differ, every sentence placed on
exactly one page. Orchestrator confirmed the page counts independently: ap-17-549 has 12
ANNALEN-PAGE lines.

## Caveat that must be fixed before the harness is trusted

pane31's not-available guard is a ZERO-check, keyed on the value it observed rather than
the condition that matters.

  light-quanta        0 sentence units, 17 ledger pages   -> guarded correctly
  mass-energy         0 sentence units,  3 ledger pages   -> guarded correctly
  special-relativity  1 sentence unit,  31 ledger pages   -> CLEARS the zero-check

pane31's own first run produced exactly 17 and 3 phantom disagreements, which are precisely

The determination must be PER PAGE, on whether that page has sentence coverage to compare,
not per paper on a zero total. Then special-relativity falls out correctly without being
named, and even a Brownian page with no sentence units is reported not-available rather
than disagreeing. The harness must state its denominator: how many pages comparable, how
many not-available, so a reader can tell 6-of-6 from 6-of-31.

## Not settled by this decision, and unchanged

Which division is right remains an editorial question answered at the plates. The Brownian
freeze is not reopened: every frozen sentence id resolves to a paragraph that exists, and
per-parent sentence numbering is 1..n with no gaps or duplicates.

Assigned to pane31, which specified the option and found the page key.
