title: Pin the facsimile and write the provenance receipt for ap-18-639 (inertia and energy)
description:
# Pin the facsimile and write the provenance receipt for ap-18-639 (inertia and energy)

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.1, §3.2,
§3.6, §4.1–§4.3, §19.1 (traceability only)

## Background

*Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig?* is three printed pages with no
sections, and it is the first paper the project plans to complete in full (Batch D) because it
proves the complete-paper contract cheaply. Brevity makes a missing premise easy to hide, so the
source layer is held to the same standard as the long papers: exact pinned bytes, recorded rights,
and a receipt that locates every paragraph, display equation, and footnote, including the footnote
that points to the relativity paper.

The candidate research is done beforehand by the scan survey (`am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`) in
`docs/provenance/survey/ap-18-639.md`. This bead confirms it at pinning time, pins the file, decides
the rights fields, and writes the receipt in the shared receipt format
(`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`).

## Scope

In scope: confirming the survey's recommended candidate (or recording why the fallback was used);
filling `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/ap-18-639.yaml`; pinning the scan; recording
`rightsStatus`, `publicationDecision`, and `cloudProcessing` with their bases; verifying identity
and completeness by visual inspection; writing `docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md`; locating comparison
witnesses.

Out of scope: the candidate survey (`am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`); the receipt format and checker
(`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`); OCR (`am-src-ocr-mass-energy-3yo`); the ledger
(`am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`); the inventory and page-map refinement
(`am-edn-inventory-mass-energy-g2d`); translation and review (`am-edn-translation-mass-energy-f3b`,
`am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`).

## Requirements

### Bibliographic identity (record all, dates typed with the `Paper` date types)

| Field | Value to record and verify |
|---|---|
| Bibliographic key | `ap-18-639` |
| Route slug | `mass-energy` |
| Printed German title | *Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig?* |
| Working English title | Does the Inertia of a Body Depend on Its Energy Content? (editorial) |
| Author line as printed | "von A. Einstein" |
| Date-line as printed | "Bern, September 1905" (type `date-line`, precision month) |
| Receipt date | 27 September 1905 (type `received`); record the printed received note as it appears
in the scan |
| Issue publication date | 21 November 1905 as recorded by the Einstein Papers Project (type
`issue-publication`); confirm against issue matter when visible and record `confirmedFromScan` |
| Journal | *Annalen der Physik* (4) volume 18; whole-series volume 323; issue 13 as recorded by
Wiley (Crossref, checked 2026-09-14) |
| Pages | 639–641 (3 journal pages) |
| DOI | `10.1002/andp.19053231314` is the canonical citation DOI; verify it against the publisher
landing page at pinning time |
| Later edition | `10.1002/andp.2005517s114` (*Annalen der Physik* 517, issue S1, 2005, pp. 225–228,
per Crossref on 2026-09-14), type `later-edition`; verify at pinning time. **Correction:** the
plan's §3.1 (and earlier drafts of this bead) called `10.1002/andp.200590007` a reissue DOI for this
paper; Crossref records that DOI as the 2005 reissue of the light-quanta paper (pp. 164–181). Do not
record it here, and note the correction in the receipt's identity notes |
| Collected Papers | Vol. 2, Doc. 24 (comparison edition only) |

### Source selection, rights, pinning, verification

- Start from `docs/provenance/survey/ap-18-639.md`: confirm that the recommended candidate is still
served, its terms are unchanged (re-quote with a new retrieval date if they changed), and its host
checksums match; otherwise use the fallback and record why.
- Plan order of preference: (1) a library or archive scan of bound *Annalen* volume 18 (1905) with
stated open terms, whole issue preferred; (2) the Augsburg facsimiles as comparison witness; (3) the
Collected Papers Vol. 2 Doc. 24 as comparison edition, never the pinned file, pinned by
bibliographic identity; (4) German Wikisource as a ledger comparison source, never the source face.
Never pin a subscription publisher PDF; quote every terms statement verbatim, including notices
inside the file. The pinned file comes from volume 18, not volume 17 like the other three papers, so
it does not share their parent scan.
- Record `rightsStatus`, `publicationDecision` (with `publicationReason` unless `publish`), and
`cloudProcessing` with `cloudProcessingBasis`, per `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`. If `cloudProcessing`
is `unknown`, ask the user in a bead comment; pinning may proceed, but `am-src-ocr-mass-energy-3yo`
waits for the decision.
- Pin with `am-src-download-script-15ar` and inspect all three rendered pages: masthead, every
paragraph, every display equation, the footnotes, the closing remarks, the date-line, and the
received note. Confirm that page 641 is complete if a following article begins on it, and that page
639 is not preceded in the extract by the end of another article without a map entry. No OCR or
text-layer extraction for verification. Record `embeddedTextLayer` as reported by the script.

### Receipt `docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md` (receipt format; written before editorial copy)

1. **Identity**: the `paper` block with the table above, typed dates, verification dates, and the
DOI correction note.
2. **Scan and rights**: the `scan` block from the download script's stub plus `termsStatements`
verbatim.
3. **Page map** for every page, with `contents` from the receipt format's closed set
(`front-matter`, `usage-notice`, `masthead`, `article-text`, `other-article`, `plate`,
`back-matter`), covering the argument blocks in printed order. The printed forms below are
expectations to confirm against the page image; where the paper writes a radical instead of a named
symbol, or a lowercase letter where planning notes used another, the receipt records the printed
form:
   - the opening reference to the results of a recently published electrodynamic investigation, with
   the footnote citing the relativity paper (*Ann. d. Phys.* 17, p. 891, 1905), and any second
   footnote (expected: a remark that the principle of the constancy of the velocity of light is
   contained in Maxwell's equations);
   - the imported light-energy relation, expected in the form $l^* = l\,\frac{1 -
   \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1 - (v/V)^2}}$ with lowercase $l$ for the energy of the plane wave
   system, and the statement that $V$ is the speed of light;
   - the two equal and opposite emissions of $\tfrac{1}{2}L$;
   - the energy balances in the two systems, expected as $E_0 = E_1 + \tfrac{1}{2}L + \tfrac{1}{2}L$
   and $H_0 = H_1 + \tfrac{1}{2}L\,\frac{1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}} +
   \tfrac{1}{2}L\,\frac{1 + \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}} = H_1 +
   \frac{L}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}}$, and their difference;
   - the identification of $H - E$ with the kinetic energy $K$ plus an additive constant $C$, and
   $K_0 - K_1 = L\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}} - 1\right\}$;
   - the remark that the kinetic energy diminishes independently of the body's properties and
   depends on velocity like the kinetic energy of the electron;
   - the low-speed result $K_0 - K_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}\frac{L}{V^2}v^2$, with its statement about
   neglecting terms of fourth and higher order;
   - the conclusion that a body giving off energy $L$ as radiation loses mass $L/V^2$; the
   generalization that the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content; and the numerical
   statement expected as a mass change of $L/9\cdot10^{20}$ with energy in ergs and mass in grams;
   - the conditional remark about bodies with highly variable energy content (radium salts);
   - the closing remark that, if the theory corresponds to the facts, radiation carries inertia
   between emitting and absorbing bodies;
   - the date-line and received note.
   Record paragraphs, footnote marks, numbered display equation labels, and counts of unnumbered
   display equations per page. The paper has no section structure; its blocks later use the `s0`
   section id. `am-edn-inventory-mass-energy-g2d` refines the entries, marks them `refinedBy`, and
   replaces the unnumbered counts with ids.
4. **Comparison witnesses**: Collected Papers Vol. 2 Doc. 24; the Augsburg facsimile record; German
Wikisource (as of 2026-09-14 the author page listed this paper with a scan link only and no
transcription page; recheck and record `availability`, and the page title and revision id if a
transcription exists); historical translations as witnesses only: Perrett and Jeffery (Methuen,
1923; public domain in the United States by date, not reused), the Fourmilab electronic text
(derived, with changed notation), and Beck (Princeton, 1989; in copyright).
5. **Editorial boundaries**, with planned paths marked "planned, not yet created": source face
`content/source-blocks/mass-energy/`; ledger `public/papers/transcripts/ap-18-639-reviewed.txt`;
English face `content/translations/mass-energy/`; gloss `content/glosses/mass-energy/`; research
evidence `artifacts/ocr-runs/ap-18-639/`.
6. **Pending sections** with owners: transcription method (`am-src-ocr-mass-energy-3yo`, then
`am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`); translation and gloss credits
(`am-edn-translation-mass-energy-f3b`); suspected historical typographical errors
(`am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`); editorial acceptance (generated section,
`am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y` through `am-edit-review-records-hofz`).
7. **Transcription watch list** (`watchList` entries with `result: pending`, checked against the
image by `am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`): $L$ is emitted energy in this paper (not the speed of
light as in paper 1) and $V$ is the speed of light; whether the paper uses the symbol $\beta$
anywhere or writes the radical $1/\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}$ throughout (planning notes wrote $\beta$; record
the printed form, and if $\beta$ never appears, flag it for the notation concordance owner); the
lowercase $l$ and $l^*$ of the imported relation; $E_0, E_1, H_0, H_1, K_0, K_1$, and the additive
constant $C$ as printed; the fourth-order statement; $L/V^2$ and the $9\cdot10^{20}$ factor with its
units, which is the only numerical constant the paper prints and which
`am-ref-constants-xik` registers as the printed-historical set `einstein-1905-mass-energy-printed`
(the printed factor implies $V^2 = 9\times10^{20}\ \mathrm{cm^2\,s^{-2}}$, that is $V =
3\times10^{10}$ cm/s; its labeled ratio to the modern $c^2$ is 1.0013851, computed there and never
in this receipt); the radium remark; the closing inertia remark; both footnotes; $E = mc^2$ does not
appear, and the receipt must not paraphrase the paper as if it did.

## Technical Approach

Read the survey record and confirm the candidate; enter `candidates`, `articlePages`, and `rights`
(including `cloudProcessingBasis`) in `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/ap-18-639.yaml`; run `bun
scripts/download-facsimiles.ts --check-config`, `--dry-run --key ap-18-639`, and then `--key
ap-18-639`; render the pages locally into `artifacts/facsimile-renders/ap-18-639/` for inspection;
check the canonical DOI landing page and the Crossref records of both the canonical and the
later-edition DOI with the required user agent; write the receipt; run `bun

title: Pin the facsimile and write the provenance receipt for ap-17-891 (electrodynamics of moving bodies)
description:
# Pin the facsimile and write the provenance receipt for ap-17-891 (electrodynamics of moving
bodies)

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.1, §3.2,
§3.5, §3.6, §4.1–§4.3, §19.1 (traceability only)

## Background

*Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper* is the longest paper (thirty-one pages, ten numbered sections
in two parts) and the one whose second half (§§6–10) popular accounts drop. It is also the source of
the only formula that leaves the paper: the §8 transformation of the energy of a light complex that
the September mass–energy paper imports. The pinned facsimile and its page map therefore serve two
papers, and the receipt must locate the §8 result precisely.

The candidate research is done beforehand by the scan survey (`am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`) in
`docs/provenance/survey/ap-17-891.md`. This bead confirms it at pinning time, pins the file, decides
the rights fields, and writes the receipt in the shared receipt format
(`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`). Unlike the other three papers, this one has a German Wikisource
transcription (index file `Einstein-Elektrodynamik.djvu`, made from a microfilm scan). It is a
useful comparison witness, and it has already exposed readings that must be checked against the
pinned page images (see the watch list).

## Scope

In scope: confirming the survey's recommended candidate (or recording why the fallback was used);
filling `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/ap-17-891.yaml`; pinning the scan; recording
`rightsStatus`, `publicationDecision`, and `cloudProcessing` with their bases; verifying identity
and completeness by visual inspection; writing `docs/provenance/ap-17-891.md`; locating comparison
witnesses.

Out of scope: the candidate survey (`am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`); the receipt format and checker
(`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`); OCR (`am-src-ocr-relativity-8ty`); the ledger
(`am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`); the inventory and page-map refinement
(`am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`); translation credits and reviews
(`am-edn-translation-relativity-s0-s5-hm8`, `am-edn-translation-relativity-s6-s10-qkn`,
`am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`).

## Requirements

### Bibliographic identity (record all, dates typed with the `Paper` date types)

| Field | Value to record and verify |
|---|---|
| Bibliographic key | `ap-17-891` |
| Route slug | `special-relativity` |
| Printed German title | *Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper* |
| Working English title | On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies (editorial) |
| Author line as printed | "von A. Einstein" |
| Date-line as printed | "Bern, Juni 1905" (type `date-line`, precision month) |
| Receipt date | 30 June 1905 (type `received`); record the printed received note as it appears in
the scan |
| Issue publication date | 26 September 1905 as recorded by the Einstein Papers Project (type
`issue-publication`); confirm against issue matter when visible and record `confirmedFromScan` |
| Journal | *Annalen der Physik* (4) volume 17; whole-series volume 322; issue 10 as recorded by
Wiley (Crossref, checked 2026-09-14). The microfilm item behind the Wikisource transcription is
labeled "Vol 17 Iss 5" by its host; that label is a microfilm segment, not the journal issue |
| Pages | 891–921 (31 journal pages) |
| DOI | `10.1002/andp.19053221004`, verified against the publisher landing page at pinning time |
| Later edition | `10.1002/andp.2005517s113` (*Annalen der Physik* 517, issue S1, 2005, pp. 194–224,
per Crossref on 2026-09-14), type `later-edition`; never the citation DOI |
| Collected Papers | Vol. 2, Doc. 23 (comparison edition only) |

### Source selection, rights, pinning, verification

- Start from `docs/provenance/survey/ap-17-891.md`: confirm that the recommended candidate is still
served, its terms are unchanged (re-quote with a new retrieval date if they changed), and its host
checksums match; otherwise use the fallback and record why.
- Plan order of preference: (1) a library or archive scan of bound *Annalen* volume 17 with stated
open terms, whole issue preferred; (2) the Augsburg facsimiles as comparison witness; (3) the
Collected Papers Vol. 2 Doc. 23 as comparison edition, never the pinned file, pinned by
bibliographic identity; (4) German Wikisource as a ledger comparison source, never the source face.
Never pin a subscription publisher PDF; quote every terms statement verbatim, including notices
inside the file.
- If the chosen scan is the volume 17 parent shared with `am-src-facsimile-light-quanta-t4n` and
`am-src-facsimile-brownian-mox`, the script reuses it by digest; note the shared parent digest on
all three beads.
- Record `rightsStatus`, `publicationDecision` (with `publicationReason` unless `publish`), and
`cloudProcessing` with `cloudProcessingBasis`, per `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`. If `cloudProcessing`
is `unknown`, ask the user in a bead comment; pinning may proceed, but `am-src-ocr-relativity-8ty`
waits for the decision.
- Pin with `am-src-download-script-15ar` and inspect rendered pages visually: the masthead; both
part headings; the §3 transformation pages; the §4 clock pages; the §6 field-transformation pages;
the §7 Doppler and aberration pages; the §8 light-energy and mirror pages; the §10 electron pages;
and the final page with the acknowledgment to M. Besso, the date-line, and the received note.
Confirm all 31 journal pages are present and legible. No OCR or text-layer extraction for
verification. Record `embeddedTextLayer` as reported by the script.

### Receipt `docs/provenance/ap-17-891.md` (receipt format; written before editorial copy)

1. **Identity**: the `paper` block with the table above, typed dates, and verification dates.
2. **Scan and rights**: the `scan` block from the download script's stub plus `termsStatements`
verbatim.
3. **Page map** for every PDF page, with printed page, `contents` from the receipt format's closed
set (`front-matter`, `usage-notice`, `masthead`, `article-text`, `other-article`, `plate`,
`back-matter`), and `sectionIds`: the introduction (the magnet and conductor asymmetry, failed
attempts to detect motion relative to the light medium, the two postulates, the light ether declared
superfluous, and the theory's reliance on the kinematics of the rigid body); part I, kinematics
(expected heading "I. Kinematischer Teil."): §1 definition of simultaneity; §2 the relativity of
lengths and times; §3 the theory of the transformation of coordinates and times from the stationary
system to one in uniform translation relative to it; §4 the physical meaning of the equations
obtained, concerning moving rigid bodies and moving clocks; §5 the addition theorem of velocities;
part II, electrodynamics (expected heading "II. Elektrodynamischer Teil."): §6 the transformation of
the Maxwell–Hertz equations for empty space and the nature of the electromotive forces arising from
motion in a magnetic field; §7 the theory of Doppler's principle and of aberration; §8 the
transformation of the energy of light rays and the theory of the radiation pressure exerted on
perfect mirrors; §9 the transformation of the Maxwell–Hertz equations with convection currents taken
into account; §10 the dynamics of the (slowly accelerated) electron; the closing acknowledgment and
date-line. Record every footnote with its printed mark and page. Expected footnotes include the §1
note that the imprecision in the concept of simultaneity of two events at (approximately) the same
place is not discussed, the §2 note on what "time" means there (the time of the stationary system
and the hand position of the moving clock at the place in question), and the §4 note defining a
rigid sphere as a body that has spherical form when examined at rest; record all others found.
Record numbered display equation labels and counts of unnumbered display equations per page.
**Locate the §8 energy relation exactly** (page and region), expected in the printed form
$\frac{E'}{E} = \frac{1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1 - (v/V)^2}}$, which equals $\beta(1 -
\frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$ with $\beta = 1/\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}$, together with its head-on special case
and the remark that the energy and the frequency of a light complex change with the observer's state
of motion by the same law, because paper 4 imports this result.
`am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9` refines the entries, marks them `refinedBy`, and replaces the
unnumbered counts with ids.
4. **Comparison witnesses**: Collected Papers Vol. 2 Doc. 23; the Augsburg facsimile record; German
Wikisource (the transcription page "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper" with index file
`Einstein-Elektrodynamik.djvu`, whose source is the microfilm item
`sim_annalen-der-physik_1905_17_5`; record the page and index revision ids at pinning time and note
that its readings may inherit that scan's defects); historical translations as witnesses only:
Perrett and Jeffery (Methuen, 1923; Dover reprint; public domain in the United States by date, not
reused), the Fourmilab electronic text (derived from Perrett and Jeffery with changed notation,
including $m$ for Einstein's $\mu$ and $c$ for $V$, which makes it unsuitable as a notation
witness), and Beck (Princeton, 1989; in copyright).
5. **Editorial boundaries**, with planned paths marked "planned, not yet created": source face
`content/source-blocks/special-relativity/`; ledger
`public/papers/transcripts/ap-17-891-reviewed.txt`; English face
`content/translations/special-relativity/`; research evidence `artifacts/ocr-runs/ap-17-891/`.
6. **Pending sections** with owners: transcription method (`am-src-ocr-relativity-8ty`, then
`am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`); translation credits (`am-edn-translation-relativity-s0-s5-hm8`,
`am-edn-translation-relativity-s6-s10-qkn`); suspected historical typographical errors
(`am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`); editorial acceptance (generated section,
`am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr` through `am-edit-review-records-hofz`).
7. **Transcription watch list** (`watchList` entries with `result: pending`, checked against the
pinned page images by `am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`; the witness readings quoted here are checks,
never sources; the §8 entry carries the id `s8-energy-relation` so downstream beads can cite it):
   - $V$ for the speed of light; $\beta = 1/\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}$ as defined in §3 (the modern
   $\gamma$);
   - the §3 auxiliary Galilean coordinate $x' = x - vt$, which is not the moving-frame coordinate
   (the modern notation form later gives it a distinct glyph); the moving-frame coordinates $\xi,
   \eta, \zeta, \tau$; the systems $K$ and $k$;
   - §4: the clock lag per second $1 - \sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}$ and, to fourth and higher order,
   $\tfrac{1}{2}(v/V)^2$, and the lag $\tfrac{1}{2}t(v/V)^2$ for a clock carried for time $t$, as
   printed;
   - §5: $U = \frac{v + w}{1 + vw/V^2}$ and the general form with the angle $\alpha$;
   - §6: the Gaussian field components $X, Y, Z$ and $L, M, N$ and the component transformations as
   printed;
   - §7: the Doppler relation, expected with an explicit radical, $\nu' = \nu\,\frac{1 -
   \cos\varphi\cdot\frac{v}{V}}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}}$, and the aberration formula; and the spelling of
   Doppler's name in the §7 heading (the German Wikisource witness reads "Doppeler"; if the page
   image agrees, record the printed spelling and a suspected typographical error without correcting
   the ledger);
   - §8 (`s8-energy-relation`): the printed forms of $A'^2/A^2$, $S'/S$, and $E'/E$, and the
   mirror-pressure expressions in Gaussian units; in particular the denominator of the $A'^2$
   relation (the German Wikisource witness shows $\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}$, but consistency with $A' =
   A\,\frac{1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}}$ and with the printed $E'/E =
   (A'^2/A^2)(S'/S)$ requires $1-(v/V)^2$; if the page image shows the radical, record the printed
   reading and a suspected typographical error);
   - §10: the electron mass is $\mu$, not $m$ (the Fourmilab text substitutes $m$); the equations
   $\mu\,d^2x/dt^2 = \epsilon X$ with the printed charge glyph; longitudinal mass
   $\mu/\left(\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}\right)^3$ and transverse mass $\mu/(1-(v/V)^2)$; the kinetic energy
   chain $W = \int\epsilon X\,dx = \ldots = \mu V^2\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}} - 1\right\}$,
   checking whether the middle member $\int_0^v \beta^3 v\,dv$ carries the factor $\mu$ in print
   (the witness shows it without $\mu$; if the page agrees, record a suspected typographical error);
   the potential-difference relation for $P$ and the curvature-radius relation for $R$;
   - the acknowledgment to M. Besso and the date-line; the paper cites no literature.

## Technical Approach

Read the survey record and confirm the candidate; enter `candidates`, `articlePages`, and `rights`
(including `cloudProcessingBasis`) in `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/ap-17-891.yaml`; run `bun
scripts/download-facsimiles.ts --check-config`, `--dry-run --key ap-17-891`, and then `--key
ap-17-891`; render pages locally into `artifacts/facsimile-renders/ap-17-891/` for inspection; check
the DOI landing page and the Crossref record with the required user agent; record the Wikisource
revision ids through its public interface with the required user agent (reading the witness for
comparison, never copying it into the receipt beyond short identifying readings on the watch list);
write the receipt; run `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-891` and `bun
scripts/download-facsimiles.ts --verify --key ap-17-891`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The candidate choice is traced to the survey record, and any fallback is explained.
- [ ] The scan is pinned with origin URL, verbatim terms from every location, retrieval date, host
checksums verified, SHA-256, page count, parent digest and indices if any, embedded text layer,
`rightsStatus`, `publicationDecision` (with reason if not `publish`), and `cloudProcessing` with its
basis.
- [ ] All identity fields are recorded with typed dates; the DOI was verified; the later-edition DOI
is recorded as such.
- [ ] The page map covers all pages with closed-set contents, both part headings, all ten sections,
every footnote, and the closing, and it locates the §8 energy relation precisely in its printed
form.
- [ ] Witnesses are identified with the Wikisource revision ids; historical translations are
witness-only; the Fourmilab notation caveat is recorded.
- [ ] Editorial boundaries use planned paths marked as planned; pending sections name their owners;
the transcription watch list, including the §7 spelling check, the `s8-energy-relation` entry, and
the §10 $\mu$ checks, is present.
- [ ] `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-891` reports no errors (only pending flags);
`--verify` reports `ok` or, for a local-only asset on a machine without it, `not-available`.
- [ ] No OCR or text-layer extraction was used; nothing was replaced or deleted.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- The receipt passes the receipt checker (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`): `bun
scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-891`.
- `src/content/editions/relativity.facsimile.test.ts` recomputes the pinned file's SHA-256 and page
count and matches the receipt and `scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/ap-17-891.yaml`; for a

`am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z` cite when they trace paper 4's imported relation.

### End-to-end tests
- None in this bead; `am-read-facsimile-face-er0` exercises the file in the browser. The close
reason records the `--verify` output.

### Structured logging
- The receipt references the download log `artifacts/facsimile-logs/ap-17-891/<tool-run-id>.jsonl`,

`expectedSha256`, `actualSha256`, `expectedPageCount`, `actualPageCount`, `outcome` (`passed`,
`failed`, `not-available`), and `message`, and retains the computed digest and receipt front matter
under `artifacts/test-logs/facsimile-digest/<log-run-id>/evidence/` on failure.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Both halves get the same care; do not let page mapping thin out after §5.
- The 1905 manuscript was discarded; Einstein's 1943 handwritten copy (Library of Congress) is not
the source and not a facsimile candidate.
- Printed Gaussian units stay as printed; unit conversion is a notation-concordance operation, not a
receipt edit.

# Hand-correct the reviewed diplomatic German ledger for ap-17-549

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A (transcription runs in parallel with implementation) · **Priority:** P0 (the Batch B reference slice needs §§4–5 first; correct those pages first) · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §3.4, §4.3, §4.4, §17.2, §17.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The reviewed ledger is the page-marked, diplomatic German transcription of the Brownian-motion paper, *Über die von der molekularkinetischen Theorie der Wärme geforderte Bewegung von in ruhenden Flüssigkeiten suspendierten Teilchen* (introduction, five numbered sections, date-line "Bern, Mai 1905"). It is **comparison evidence**, not the visitor-facing text: the continuous German edition is built from it in `am-edn-german-edition-brownian-phe`, and edition tests later prove that every edition block is contained in this ledger and that no page markers leak into the edition. A diplomatic transcription preserves mathematical content, meaningful punctuation, paragraph order, original spelling, and original notation, and it normalizes only declared typography such as line-break hyphenation. The cloud OCR draft is only a starting point: every line is corrected by hand against the facsimile page image, and **every equation is retyped by the editor and compared directly with the image**. Parsed PDF text, including any OCR layer embedded in the scan by its host, is never accepted for an equation.

The file name keeps the project's established `-reviewed.txt` suffix, but agents never certify review. This bead brings the ledger to `corrected-second-read`; the status `reviewed` is set only when the human German source review (`am-edn-review-german-brownian-cfh`) records acceptance.

The ledger file carries no header, so it never declares its own digest or source. The validator of `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv` emits `ledgerSha256` (the SHA-256 of the ledger bytes) and `sourceAssetSha256` (the receipt's `scan.sha256`). This bead writes them into the receipt as `transcription.ledgerSha256` and `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256`; the receipt checker of `am-src-receipt-format-npo5` requires the latter to equal `scan.sha256`. `content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/edition.yaml` (written by the German edition bead in the format of `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`) pins both, so an edition built from a stale ledger fails.

## Scope

In scope: producing `public/papers/transcripts/ap-17-549-reviewed.txt` for all 12 journal pages (549–560); recording the transcription method, editors, dates, witness differences, watch-list results, suspected historical typographical errors, the ledger digests, and the ledger status in `docs/provenance/ap-17-549.md`; the optional `content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/ledger-config.yaml` and the warning allowlist entries this ledger needs.

Out of scope: the ledger format and validator (`am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`); block and sentence ids (`am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg`); the continuous German edition (`am-edn-german-edition-brownian-phe`); translation (`am-ep-editions-1wa` translation beads); formal German-source acceptance (`am-edn-review-german-brownian-cfh`, a human gate that also confirms ledger fidelity for the sections it reviews).

**Never run OCR on this machine.** If a page needs a new machine draft, request a cloud job through `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`; if the cloud path is unavailable, pause and report the blocker. Starting a ledger page from the image alone, without a cloud draft, is allowed only if `docs/OCR_DISPATCH.md` records the user's yes on draft-free ledger authoring (with its conditions); it is never an agent's call.

## Requirements

1. **Format** exactly as defined in `docs/editorial/LEDGER_FORMAT.md` by `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`:
   - **Encoding:** UTF-8, Unicode NFC, LF line endings, a final newline, no tabs or control characters, and nothing before the first marker.
   - **Page markers:** the first line is `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---`, followed by the complete ordered sequence `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE k OF N ---`, one marker per in-scope PDF page of the receipt's `pageMap` (pages marked `other-article` excluded), in `pdfPageIndex` order.
   - **Anchors:** `[[ANNALEN-PAGE <n>]]` on the line after each marker, equal to the receipt's `printedPage` for that page.
   - **Masthead** on ledger page 1: the optional `[[ARTICLE-NUMBER <as printed>]]` for the issue's article number, then `[[TITLE]]…[[/TITLE]]` and `[[AUTHOR]]…[[/AUTHOR]]`, with separator punctuation printed between title and author line outside the tags. Text of a neighboring article on page 549 (above the title) or page 560 (after the receipt line) is not transcribed; `[[OTHER-ARTICLE-OMITTED]]` marks where it was omitted.
   - **Headings:** `[[HEADING s<n>]] <heading as printed>` for §§1–5, keeping the printed § number and wording; the introduction before `[[HEADING s1]]` belongs to `s0`.
   - **Paragraphs:** separated by exactly one blank line, in printed order; soft line breaks join with one space. No physical line ends with a hyphen immediately after a letter: rejoin words hyphenated by line wrapping, and keep genuine compounds hyphenated mid-line. A paragraph continuing onto the next page ends its first part with `[[CONTINUES]]`, and a word hyphenated across the page break is written whole before `[[CONTINUES]]`.
   - **Display equations:** `$$ <LaTeX> $$`, one region per printed display (a multi-line display under one brace or label is one region), inside the paragraph in which it is printed, with no blank line around it unless the print starts a new paragraph. `[[EQ-LABEL <label exactly as printed>]]` follows on the next line when a label is printed, keeping parentheses. Inline mathematics is `$ … $`; words printed inside a formula use `\text{…}` with the printed spelling.
   - **Emphasis:** `[[SPERR]]…[[/SPERR]]` for letter-spaced emphasis and `[[EM]]…[[/EM]]` for non-mathematical italics, never nested.
   - **Footnotes:** `[[FN-MARK <label>]]` inline at the occurrence; `[[FN <label>]] <text>` at the foot of the same page; a footnote running onto the next page ends its first part with `[[FN-CONTINUES]]` and resumes at the foot of the next page with `[[FN-CONT <label>]] <text>`. Labels are as printed and can restart on each page.
   - **Closings:** `[[DATELINE]] <as printed>` (expected `Bern, Mai 1905.`) and `[[RECEIVED]] <as printed>` (the journal's receipt line, expected in the form `(Eingegangen 11. Mai 1905.)`). The paper has no acknowledgment, so the validator's default `expectedClosings` (`dateline`, `received`) applies.
   - **Forbidden:** running heads, bare page numbers, and scan furniture; the draft-only tokens `[[RUNNING-HEAD …]]`, `[[PAGE-NUMBER …]]`, and `[[ILLEGIBLE]]` (validator `draft-token` errors with repair messages); draft placeholders (`[[MATH-REGION`, `unverified`, `TODO`, `???`), U+FFFD, `[?]`, `<unk>`, and OCR confidence tokens; unknown `[[…]]` tags; HTML-like tags outside mathematics.
   - **Declared normalizations only:** rejoin line-wrap hyphenation and resolve ligatures. Keep original spelling (for example `daß`), capitalization, punctuation, printed abbreviations with their spacing, decimal commas, units as printed (for example the word `Mikron` or a glyph), and printed misspellings. Never modernize.
   - **Mathematics** parses under the validator's `ledgerMathSettings` (KaTeX strict mode, no trust, no macro definitions). Parsing proves syntax only; fidelity is the image comparison.
2. **Skeleton first, then pages.** Create the ledger with the complete marker sequence and anchors taken from the receipt's page map, leaving uncorrected pages empty; the skeleton passes the validator in structural mode (each empty page is an informational `skeleton-page` finding). Correct pages in priority order (the §§4–5 pages first, then the rest), committing after each page with the validator passing in structural mode. Reserve the ledger file through Agent Mail while editing; if several agents correct different pages, record page claims in bead comments and integrate one page at a time. Set `transcription.ledgerStatus: in-progress` in the receipt when the skeleton is committed.
3. **Method**, page by page:
   - render the pinned page at 300 dpi or more and correct the cloud draft line by line against the image;
   - retype every mathematical region from the image, never from the draft's LaTeX or any PDF text layer;
   - compare with the comparison witnesses recorded in the receipt only to surface candidate differences. As of 2026-09-14 German Wikisource had no transcription of this paper, so no machine-readable witness is expected: compare visually against the Collected Papers Vol. 2 Doc. 16 page images or print (in copyright, consulted, never copied). If a machine-readable witness appears, its text may sit only in a gitignored working file under `artifacts/ledger-work/ap-17-549/witness/`. Resolve every difference by returning to the facsimile, never by majority vote and never by copying witness text;
   - when every page is corrected, run the validator with `--require-complete`, then set `ledgerStatus: corrected` and record the current `transcription.ledgerSha256` in the same change, because from `corrected` on the validator runs in completeness mode (`page-empty`, `masthead-missing`, `closing-missing`, `receipt-ledger-digest-mismatch`);
   - make a complete second read of the whole ledger against the images, by a different editor or agent where possible, recording honestly if the same agent did both; update `ledgerSha256` after every edit made during it; then set `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read`.
4. **Suspected historical typographical errors** go into the receipt's `typographicalErrors` with the locator, original reading, proposed correction, reasoning, evidence, `layer: source`, recorder, and date. The ledger keeps the original reading. A printed equation label repeated within one section is listed in `content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/ledger-config.yaml` under `printingAnomalies` with the id of its `typographicalErrors` entry.
5. **Transcription watch list for this paper.** Transcribe from the image; the expected readings below come from comparison texts and planning notes and are checks, never sources. Write each result to the receipt's `watchList` (`matches`, `differs`, or `not-found`, with `checkedBy` and `checkedAt`):
   - the introduction's conditional claim that the motions discussed may be identical with so-called Brownian molecular motion, and Einstein's stated uncertainty about the reports, word for word;
   - §1: $p = \frac{RT}{N}\nu$ with $\nu$ as number density;
   - §2: the free-energy argument in full;
   - §3: $K\nu = \frac{RT}{N}\frac{\partial\nu}{\partial x}$, $K = 6\pi kPv$, $D = \frac{RT}{N}\frac{1}{6\pi kP}$;
   - §4: $\partial f/\partial t = D\,\partial^2 f/\partial x^2$ and $D = \frac{1}{\tau}\int\frac{\Delta^2}{2}\varphi(\Delta)\,d\Delta$ with the printed integration limits;
   - §5: $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$ and $N = \frac{t}{\lambda_x^2}\frac{RT}{3\pi kP}$;
   - the printed numbers of §5, expected with decimal commas: the temperature 17° (the site converts it to 290.15 K); the viscosity of water $k = 1{,}35\cdot10^{-2}$; the particle diameter 0,001 mm (so the radius $P$ is 0.5 μm); $N = 6\cdot10^{23}$; the displacement expected as "$\lambda_x = 8\cdot10^{-5}$ cm = 0,8 Mikron" for one second and "ca. 6 Mikron" for one minute, with the unit recorded exactly as printed (a word or a glyph);
   - whether §5 prints a numerical value for $R$ (it is expected not to, which is why the numeric check below declares $R$ as an editorial input);
   - $k$ is viscosity and $P$ is radius in this paper; the printed equation numbers; the date-line and the received note;
   - the verification flag on the mean-velocity warning (see Considerations).
6. **Receipt updates**: the transcription method (the `toolRunId` of each cloud draft run, and the correction process), editors and their roles and pages, correction and second-read dates, witness differences worth noting, `typographicalErrors`, `watchList` results, `ledgerSourcePdfSha256` (equal to `scan.sha256`), `ledgerSha256` of the current file from `corrected` on, and `ledgerStatus`. The receipt checker must pass after every update.
7. **Status honesty**: machine drafts never self-certify, and neither does an agent's correction. `corrected-second-read` requires the validator to report `clean: true` in completeness mode (valid, no unacknowledged warning, no stale allowlist entry), every watch-list item checked, and the second read complete.

## Technical Approach

- Keep a per-page checklist in the working notes: text lines, headings, emphasis, footnotes and continuations, inline math, display math with labels, page anchor, continuation marker, closings.
- Run `bun scripts/validate-ledger.ts public/papers/transcripts/ap-17-549-reviewed.txt --paper brownian-motion` after each page (exit 0 clean, 1 errors, 2 unacknowledged warnings or stale allowlist entries, 3 identity failure). `--allow-warnings` is for work in progress only and is never used by a gate. Acknowledge a justified warning in `content/source-blocks/brownian-motion/ledger-allowlist.yaml` with `{ledgerKey, code, ledgerPage, lineFingerprint, reason, editor, date}`.
- Log every witness difference and its resolution in `artifacts/ledger-work/ap-17-549/differences.jsonl`, and summarize the substantive ones in the receipt.
- Run `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-549` after each receipt update.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ledger covers every in-scope PDF page with the full ordered marker sequence and printed-page anchors that match the receipt's page map, and no page is empty.
- [ ] The masthead, the five `[[HEADING s<n>]]` headings, `[[DATELINE]]`, and `[[RECEIVED]]` are present as printed, and any neighboring-article text is omitted with `[[OTHER-ARTICLE-OMITTED]]`.
- [ ] Every display equation and inline formula is retyped LaTeX that parses under `ledgerMathSettings` and matches the page image.
- [ ] All footnotes are present at their printed positions with marks paired and continuations tagged; no draft-only or forbidden token remains; no physical line ends with a hyphen.
- [ ] The validator reports `clean: true` in completeness mode; every acknowledged warning has a recorded reason, editor, and date.
- [ ] Every watch-list item has a recorded result in the receipt, and the retyped §5 values pass the numeric consistency check.
- [ ] The receipt records method (with draft `toolRunId` values), editors, dates, witness differences, the typographical-error register, `ledgerSourcePdfSha256`, `ledgerSha256`, and `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read`, and the receipt checker passes.
- [ ] No OCR ran locally; no text was copied from witnesses or historical translations; the bead never set `ledgerStatus: reviewed`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/editions/brownian.ledger.test.ts`, against the real ledger, receipt, and validator, logging through `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp` and comparing numbers with `expectClose` and digests with `expectBitwise`:
- the validator reports `valid: true` in structural mode while `ledgerStatus` is `in-progress`, and `clean: true` in completeness mode from `corrected` on; before `corrected` the completeness assertions are logged `skipped` with the reason "ledger in progress", never silently;
- `stats.pages` equals the number of in-scope pages in the receipt's `pageMap`, and anchors run 549–560 in order, each equal to the mapped `printedPage`;
- the findings contain no `math-parse`, `fn-mark-orphan`, `fn-text-orphan`, `fn-continuation-orphan`, `draft-token`, `forbidden-token`, `unknown-tag`, `nested-emphasis`, or `line-end-hyphen` code;
- `[[HEADING s1]]` to `[[HEADING s5]]` appear once each in order (`stats.headings` is 5), and the title and author tags are on ledger page 1;
- exactly one `[[DATELINE]]` and one `[[RECEIVED]]` appear, on the last in-scope page;
- the receipt's `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256` equals `scan.sha256`;
- from `corrected` on: `transcription.ledgerSha256` equals an independent SHA-256 of the file; per-page display-equation and footnote counts in `stats.perPage` equal the receipt's `pageMap`; no watch-list item is `pending`;
- **numeric consistency of the retyped §5 values.** Parse the retyped $k$, the diameter (halved to $P$), $N$, and the temperature from the ledger. With $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg/(mol·K) declared in the test as an editorial input (paper 2 does not print it; the same value is used by the constant set `einstein-1905-brownian-printed`) and $T = 290.15$ K, compute $D = \frac{RT}{N}\frac{1}{6\pi kP}$ and $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$: $7.948\times10^{-5}$ cm (0.795 μm) at 1 s and $6.156\times10^{-4}$ cm (6.16 μm) at 60 s. Compare each with its printed reading through `expectClose` with an absolute tolerance of half the last printed digit: $8\cdot10^{-5}$ cm within $0.5\times10^{-5}$ cm, 0,8 Mikron within 0.05 μm, and 6 Mikron within 0.5 μm. A mismatch fails and names the retyped values, unless the receipt's `typographicalErrors` records a printing error for exactly those readings (the ledger keeps them). The check catches retyping slips: an exponent slip in $k$ gives 2.51 μm at 1 s, an exponent slip in $N$ gives 0.251 μm, and treating the 1 μm diameter as the radius gives 0.562 μm, and each fails. Using 290 K instead of 290.15 K changes $\lambda_x$ by 0.026 percent, far inside the printed rounding. Values recomputed with python3 on 2026-09-14;
- every watch-list item with result `differs` carries a note, and where a printing error is suspected, a matching `typographicalErrors` entry with evidence;
- after `am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg` lands, per-page counts of paragraphs, display equations, and footnotes equal the inventory's counts;
- wiring checks over copies in `artifacts/test-tmp/ledger-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>/`: inserting one `[[MATH-REGION page=1]]` token must fail with `forbidden-token`, and changing the retyped viscosity exponent from $-2$ to $-3$ must fail the numeric check.

### End-to-end tests
- No browser test. The close reason records the JSONL output of `bun scripts/validate-ledger.ts public/papers/transcripts/ap-17-549-reviewed.txt --paper brownian-motion --require-complete` over the final file and of `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-549`. The edition contract tests in `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` consume this ledger.
- A failing ledger test retains the validator's JSONL output and the receipt front matter through `retainEvidence` under `artifacts/test-logs/ledger-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
The test writes JSON lines to `artifacts/test-logs/ledger-brownian-motion/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite: "ledger-brownian-motion"`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId: "am-src-ledger-brownian-8cw"`, `paper: "brownian-motion"`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome` (`passed`, `failed`, `skipped`), `durationMs`, `message`, and `extra` `{ledgerKey, ledgerStatus, mode, check, code, ledgerPage, pdfPageIndex, printedPage, ledgerLine}`. Correction sessions log witness-difference resolutions to `artifacts/ledger-work/ap-17-549/differences.jsonl`, a working record rather than a test log, with `timestamp`, `editor`, `pdfPage`, `line`, `ledgerReading`, `witness`, `witnessReading`, `resolution`, and `evidence`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A line that would look wrong beside a careful human transcription is not done: no mid-word wrap hyphens, no one-word lines, no glued paragraphs, no ligature misreadings, no machine tokens.
- Do not normalize units, exponents, decimal commas, or notation; the notation concordance is a separate layer.
- Do not fix a suspected printing error in the ledger; record it.
- Draft markup that already looks like ledger markup is still a draft; correct every line against the image.
- The numeric check proves that the retyped printed values are consistent with the printed results; it does not claim that Einstein used exactly these editorial inputs.
- **Verification flag:** record whether the 1905 text warns that the observable is not a mean velocity. Einstein's explicit apparent-velocity discussion appears in his 1906 paper "Zur Theorie der Brownschen Bewegung" (Ann. Phys. 19, 371); if the 1905 text lacks it, note that in the receipt so later layers attribute the warning to 1906.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-ocr-brownian-n6q`: the cloud OCR draft checkpoints and coverage report.
- `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`: the ledger format specification and validator; through it the receipt parser (`am-src-receipt-format-npo5`), the logging library (`am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`), and the tolerance module (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`) are already in place when this bead starts.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-german-edition-brownian-phe`: the continuous German edition is built from this ledger.

Related without an edge: `am-src-ocr-dispatch-interface-m1ur` records whether draft-free ledger authoring is ever allowed.

title: Produce the scoped reviewed German ledgers for the dissertation and its 1911 correction
description:
# Produce the scoped reviewed German ledgers for the dissertation and its 1911 correction

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** H · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.7, §4.3,
§4.4, §17.2, §17.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The companion record needs a reviewed German source for exactly the passages it uses, produced by
the same pipeline as the four papers: a pinned facsimile, bounded cloud OCR drafts as research
evidence, and a hand-corrected diplomatic ledger. This bead owns that transcription for the
dissertation (`ap-19-289`) and the 1911 correction (`ap-34-591`). The companion is scoped: it covers
what the Avogadro lab needs, and it must never imply that the whole dissertation is edited. The
scope is declared block by block in the source manifest.

A further reason for care: the numbers the lab and fixtures rely on come from more than one printing
and more than one data set. The 1905 thesis printing reports about $2.1\times10^{23}$; the 1906
*Annalen der Physik* printing is reported to add a supplement with newer data giving about
$4.15\times10^{23}$; and the 1911 correction (*Annalen* (4) 34, 591–592) applies the corrected
coefficient and gives about $6.56\times10^{23}$. Since $N$ scales as the square root of the
coefficient of $\varphi$ and $4.15 \times \sqrt{2.5} = 6.5617$ (python3, 2026-09-15), the 1911 value
appears to reuse the supplement's inputs; the ledgers and receipts must establish that from the
pages rather than assume it. Every fixture input is traced to the printing and page it comes from.

Einstein prints $k$ for the viscosity itself, so the printed relation reads $k^* = k(1 + \varphi)$
with the coefficient of $\varphi$ equal to 1 in the 1906 printing and $5/2$ after the 1911
correction. **The coefficient of $\varphi$ is never called $k$**, and the modern $[\eta]$ appears
only in modern-notation layers, marked as modern.

Neither ledger declares a digest in its own text: the validator emits `ledgerSha256` and
`sourceAssetSha256`, each receipt records them as `transcription.ledgerSha256` and
`transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256` (the checker requires the latter to equal `scan.sha256`), and
`content/source-blocks/molecular-dimensions/edition.yaml` pins them per key.

## Scope

In scope: cloud OCR drafts for the scoped page ranges; hand-corrected diplomatic ledgers; scoped
source-manifest entries; receipt updates.

- The dissertation passages the companion needs: the statement of the suspension viscosity result,
its combination with the diffusion coefficient, the sugar-solution data, and the numerical
determination of $N$ and the molecular radius, plus any supplement in the 1906 printing.
- The whole 1911 correction.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): pinning the facsimiles and page maps
(`am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp`); the companion edition blocks, translation, readings, and
narrative (`am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`); the evaluator
(`am-ref-viscosity-suspension-c9lp`); the companion's human reviews.

**Never run OCR on this machine.** All drafts come from cloud GPT-5.6 Luna workers through
`am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0` and the cloud adapter (`am-src-ocr-cloud-adapter-7wa1`). If the cloud
path is unavailable, pause and report the blocker with `br comments add`; there is no local
fallback.

## Requirements

1. **Preconditions** (recorded before any dispatch): each receipt records `cloudProcessing:
permitted` with its basis (`forbidden` blocks that scan; `unknown` goes to the user);
`docs/OCR_DISPATCH.md` records authorization and a spending cap covering these pages; the
orchestrator and adapter test suites pass.
2. **Job plans** `scripts/sources/ocr-plans/ap-19-289.yaml` and
`scripts/sources/ocr-plans/ap-34-591.yaml`, with digests copied from the receipts, `pdfPageRange`
covering only the in-scope pages from each receipt's page map (a non-contiguous scope uses one plan
per contiguous range, each named `<key>-<n>.yaml`), `chunkSize` 2, `maxConcurrency` 1,
`cloudProcessing: permitted`, `instructionsVersion: v1`, and `expectedCounts` from the page maps.
Run each with a dry run first, then a first-chunk format check, then the remaining chunks; summarize
and write coverage reports. Each run's artifacts live in `artifacts/ocr-runs/<key>/<tool-run-id>/`,
and the receipt records the run as `transcription.ocrRuns[].toolRunId`.
3. **Mathematics and tables retyped by the editor** and compared directly with page images; parsed
PDF text is never accepted for an equation or a numerical table. The watch list for these documents:
$k^*$ and $k$ as printed for the suspension and pure-liquid viscosities; the printed coefficient of
$\varphi$ (expected 1 in 1906) and the corrected coefficient (expected $5/2$ in 1911), with the
printed glyph for the volume fraction; the sugar-solution diffusion and viscosity inputs with their
temperatures and units; the printed radius and $N$ in each printing; any recomputation in the 1906
supplement with its own inputs, radius, and value; the corrected value in 1911 and, explicitly,
whether the correction reprints the supplement's inputs, refers to them, or states new ones.
4. **Diplomatic transcription** in the format of `docs/editorial/LEDGER_FORMAT.md`
(`am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`), using its typed tag set: page markers with `[[ANNALEN-PAGE <n>]]`
anchors; masthead tags for scan furniture and `[[OTHER-ARTICLE-OMITTED]]` for neighboring articles;
`[[HEADING s<n>]]` with section ids; `[[CONTINUES]]` for paragraphs crossing a page;
`[[SPERR]]…[[/SPERR]]`, `[[EM]]…[[/EM]]`, `[[FN-MARK <label>]]`, `[[FN <label>]]`, and the
continuation tags `[[FN-CONTINUES]]` and `[[FN-CONT]]`; retyped display equations in `$$ … $$` with
`[[EQ-LABEL (<printed label>)]]` where a label is printed; typed closings `[[DATELINE]]`, `[[ACK]]`,
and `[[RECEIVED]]` as the receipt's `expectedClosings` requires. Preserve mathematical content,
punctuation, paragraph order, original spelling and notation; normalize only declared typography. **A
hyphen at a line end is a validator error, not a warning**: rejoin it unless the facsimile
hyphenates the word in its own right, and record that case with the validator's explicit marker.
Draft-only tokens (`[[MATH-REGION`, `unverified`, `[[RUNNING-HEAD`, `[[PAGE-NUMBER`,
`[[ILLEGIBLE]]`) must be gone before a ledger is marked `corrected`.
5. **Ledger files**: `public/papers/transcripts/ap-19-289-reviewed.txt` and
`public/papers/transcripts/ap-34-591-reviewed.txt` (or a recorded non-public location if a scan's
terms forbid redistribution of derived page text, which should not arise for public-domain text),
each beginning `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---`, where `N` equals the number of PDF
pages listed in the receipt's `transcription.ledgerScopePages`. Printed-page anchors are strictly
increasing and may skip out-of-scope pages. Each ledger is built skeleton first (markers and anchors
from the receipt, pages empty until corrected) and passes the validator after every page.
6. **Correction and second read.** Correct each in-scope page line by line against the image; set
`ledgerStatus: corrected` when every in-scope page is done; make a complete second read (by a
different editor or agent where possible, recorded honestly) and set `ledgerStatus:
corrected-second-read`. The status `reviewed` comes only from the companion's human German source
review (`am-companion-review-pfh8`).
7. **Scoped coverage.** Author `content/source-blocks/molecular-dimensions/manifest.yaml` in the
format of `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`, listing in-scope blocks with ids and locators and every
out-of-scope block explicitly with its scope marked out and a reason, so the unit-with-no-destination
rule does not fail on passages the companion deliberately omits. If that format has no per-unit
scope field, ask its owner in a bead comment for `scope` and `scopeReason` fields instead of
inventing a parallel file. No completeness claim is made for the dissertation as a whole.
8. **Printing provenance.** Each receipt's `transcription.printingProvenance` records which printing
(`thesis-1905`, `annalen-1906`, `correction-1911`) supplies each transcribed passage and each
numerical input, with PDF page index and printed page, so `am-ref-constants-xik` can build the sets
`einstein-1905-thesis-printed`, `einstein-1906-dissertation-printed`, and
`einstein-1911-correction-printed` without guessing.
9. **Witnesses.** As of 2026-09-14 German Wikisource listed neither document as a transcription;
compare visually against the Collected Papers transcriptions (in copyright, consulted, never copied)
and, where available, the separately printed 1905 thesis. Resolve every difference against the
pinned facsimile and log it.
10. **Receipt updates**: OCR runs with their `toolRunId`, method, editors, dates, witness
differences, `typographicalErrors`, `watchList` results, `ledgerScopePages`, `printingProvenance`,
`ledgerSourcePdfSha256`, `ledgerSha256`, and `ledgerStatus`, passing the receipt checker.

## Technical Approach

- Use the orchestrator with the adapter; store drafts under
`artifacts/ocr-runs/ap-19-289/<tool-run-id>/` and `artifacts/ocr-runs/ap-34-591/<tool-run-id>/`.
- Correct line by line against the page images; retype every equation and table; run `bun
scripts/validate-ledger.ts <ledger>` after each page and `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key <key>`
after each receipt update.
- Log witness differences to `artifacts/ledger-work/<key>/differences.jsonl`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The preconditions are recorded, and every draft came from a recorded cloud run named by its
`toolRunId`.
- [ ] Both ledgers validate with complete marker sequences for their in-scope pages, no empty pages,
typed headings and closings, and no draft-only tokens or line-end hyphens.
- [ ] Every equation and numerical table in scope is retyped and checked against the page image, and
every watch-list item has a result, including whether the 1911 correction reuses the supplement's
inputs.
- [ ] The source manifest declares in-scope and out-of-scope blocks explicitly, with reasons for
every out-of-scope block.
- [ ] The receipts record method, scope pages, printing provenance for every passage and numerical
input, review dates, digests, and `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read`, and pass the receipt
checker.
- [ ] No text produced here calls the coefficient of $\varphi$ "k".
- [ ] No OCR process ran on the development host, and the bead never set `ledgerStatus: reviewed`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/editions/dissertation.ledger.test.ts`, against the real ledgers, receipts, manifest,
and validator:
- the validator returns `valid: true` with zero unacknowledged warnings for both files, and no
`line-end-hyphen` error;
- each marker count equals the length of the receipt's `ledgerScopePages`, and printed-page anchors
are strictly increasing and inside 289–306 or 591–592;
- every math region parses in KaTeX strict mode; footnote marks pair and every `[[FN-CONTINUES]]`
has a matching `[[FN-CONT]]`; headings carry section ids; closings match `expectedClosings`; no
draft-only token appears;
- each receipt's `ledgerSourcePdfSha256` equals its `scan.sha256`;
- completeness checks from `ledgerStatus: corrected` on (logged `skipped` before, never silently):
no empty page; per-page display equation and footnote counts equal the page maps; no pending
watch-list items; `ledgerSha256` matches from `corrected-second-read` on;
- the manifest test: every in-scope block has a ledger locator on a page in `ledgerScopePages`, and
every out-of-scope block has a reason;
- every numerical input listed in `printingProvenance` names a printing, a PDF page index, and a
printed page that exists in the corresponding page map;
- a coefficient consistency check: where both a printed coefficient of $\varphi$ and a printed $N$
are transcribed for two printings, the ratio of the two $N$ values equals the square root of the
ratio of the coefficients within 2 percent, or the test names the mismatch for the editor (with the
1906 supplement's $4.15\times10^{23}$ and the 1911 $6.56\times10^{23}$ this ratio is 1.5807 against
$\sqrt{2.5} = 1.5811$; python3, 2026-09-15). The check never edits a printed value;
- a scan test: neither ledger, manifest entry, nor receipt text calls the coefficient of $\varphi$
"k", and the modern symbol $[\eta]$ appears in none of them;
- a wiring check over a copy in `artifacts/test-tmp/ledger-molecular-dimensions/<log-run-id>/` with
one `[[MATH-REGION page=1]]` token inserted must fail.

### End-to-end tests
- The OCR runs are the pipeline tests on real data (dry run, first-chunk format check, dispatch,
checkpoint, summarize, coverage), with `toolRunId` values and evidence paths in the close reason. No
browser test here; the companion record's lane renders the scoped German text. A failing validation
retains the validator output and JSONL log under
`artifacts/test-logs/ledger-molecular-dimensions/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
- The orchestrator's `run.jsonl` per run (`timestamp`, `logRunId`, `toolRunId`, `beadId`, `key`,
`chunkIndex`, `pdfPages`, `imageSha256`, `adapter`, `workerIdentity`, `jobId`, `status`,
`errorCode`, `message`, `durationMs`).
- The ledger test's JSON lines to
`artifacts/test-logs/ledger-molecular-dimensions/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`,
`logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `key`, `ledgerStatus`, `pdfPage`, `annalenPage`, `check`,
`expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `lineNumber`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Letter-spaced emphasis, Greek, fractions, and numerical tables in 1905, 1906, and 1911 typesetting
defeat OCR; expect heavy correction.
- Do not let the 1905, 1906, and 1911 printings silently merge; keep printing provenance per passage
and per number, and treat the square-root relation as a check, not a source of values.
- $k$ is the viscosity here; the coefficient of $\varphi$ has no letter in project text.
- A scoped ledger must never read as a complete edition of the dissertation.
- If the companion is deferred by the launch decision, this bead is deferred with it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp`: the pinned facsimiles, page maps, and `cloudProcessing`
determinations.
- `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`: bounded, checkpointed cloud OCR orchestration.
- `am-src-ocr-cloud-adapter-7wa1`: the working, authorized adapter.
- `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`: validation of the ledger format and forbidden leftovers.
- `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: the manifest format for the scoped entries.

Unblocks:
- `am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`: the companion needs reviewed German source for its scoped
passages.
- `am-companion-review-pfh8`: the German source and physics review reads these ledgers and sets
`ledgerStatus: reviewed`.
