comments.text:
FINDING from am-src-ledger-light-quanta-sxi (LilacValley), 2026-09-21, while assessing this paper as a next transcription target. Not claiming this bead; leaving evidence for whoever does.

THE ap-19-289 PAGE MAP IS POSITIVELY WRONG, not merely unrefined. All 18 entries carry 'numbered: []' and the bare 'unnumbered: 0' shape, and NONE carries refinedBy. Measured against the plate: printed page 298 (pdfPageIndex 10) prints TWO NUMBERED equations, (8) and (7b), plus a braced three-line system and a three-line coordinate definition. So the map asserts zero displays and zero numbered equations on a page that has both.

Why that matters more than it looks. On ap-17-132 exactly 3 of 17 entries had this same unrefined shape (pages 132, 133, 145) and I verified each from the plate; there the 'unnumbered: 0' happened to be TRUE. Here it is false on the first page I opened. Anyone transcribing against this map would get no cross-check at all, and worse, a disagreement between their page and the map would read as THEIR error rather than the map's. The whole-paper cross-check that made ap-17-132 trustworthy - the map's 52 display ids and 13 footnote marks independently matching the validator's count of my transcription - is unavailable here until the map is refined.

NO INVENTORY BEAD EXISTS FOR THIS PAPER. mass-energy, relativity, brownian and light-quanta each have one (am-edn-inventory-*); the dissertation has none. So nobody currently owns refining this map.

THE SCOPE THIS BEAD REQUIRES DOES NOT EXIST YET. The description says the companion 'is scoped: it covers what the Avogadro lab needs ... The scope is declared block by block in the source manifest.' Measured: there is no content/source-blocks/molecular-dimensions/ (or dissertation) directory - only brownian-motion, light-quanta, mass-energy and special-relativity exist - and transcription.ledgerScopePages is unset in both docs/provenance/ap-19-289.md and ap-34-591.md, though the Transcription schema provides that field. So a transcriber today would have to either do all 18 pages, which this bead explicitly forbids implying, or choose the scope themselves, which is an editorial decision belonging to the companion record and the Avogadro lab rather than to the transcriber.

SUGGESTED ORDER, for whoever routes this: declare ledgerScopePages and the block-level scope first, refine the page map for the in-scope pages second, transcribe third. Two of those three are not transcription work.

Also worth flagging for the eventual transcriber: this paper has NUMBERED equations, which neither ap-17-132 nor ap-17-549 had. LEDGER_FORMAT 4.4.1 requires [[EQ-LABEL (n)]] on the line immediately after the closing $$, and that tag has never been exercised in a real ledger in this repository. First use should be checked against the validator deliberately rather than assumed.

title: Hand-correct the reviewed diplomatic German ledger for ap-17-132
description:
# Hand-correct the reviewed diplomatic German ledger for ap-17-132

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A (transcription runs in parallel with implementation) ·
**Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §3.3, §4.3, §4.4, §17.2, §17.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The reviewed ledger is the page-marked, diplomatic German transcription of the light-quanta paper,
*Über einen die Erzeugung und Verwandlung des Lichtes betreffenden heuristischen Gesichtspunkt*
(introduction, nine numbered sections, date-line "Bern, den 17. März 1905"). It is **comparison
evidence**, not the visitor-facing text: the continuous German edition is built from it in
`am-edn-german-edition-light-quanta-eou`, and edition tests later prove that every edition block is
contained in this ledger and that no page markers leak into the edition. A diplomatic transcription
preserves mathematical content, meaningful punctuation, paragraph order, original spelling, and
original notation, and it normalizes only declared typography such as line-break hyphenation. The
cloud OCR draft is only a starting point: every line is corrected by hand against the facsimile page
image, and **every equation is retyped by the editor and compared directly with the image**. Parsed
PDF text, including any OCR layer embedded in the scan by its host, is never accepted for an
equation.

The ledger file carries no header, so it never declares a digest. The binding lives outside the
text: the validator emits `ledgerSha256` and `sourceAssetSha256`, the receipt records them as
`transcription.ledgerSha256` and `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256` (the receipt checker requires
the latter to equal `scan.sha256`), and `content/source-blocks/light-quanta/edition.yaml` pins both.

The file name keeps the project's established `-reviewed.txt` suffix, but agents never certify
review. This bead brings the ledger to `corrected-second-read`; the status `reviewed` is set only
when the human German source review (`am-edn-review-german-light-quanta-khv`) records acceptance.

## Scope

In scope: producing `public/papers/transcripts/ap-17-132-reviewed.txt` for all 17 journal pages
(132–148); recording the transcription method, editors, dates, witness differences, watch-list
results, suspected historical typographical errors, the ledger digest, and the ledger status in
`docs/provenance/ap-17-132.md`.

Out of scope: block and sentence ids (`am-edn-inventory-light-quanta-skp`), the continuous German
edition (`am-edn-german-edition-light-quanta-eou`), translation (`am-ep-editions-1wa` translation
beads), and formal German-source acceptance (`am-edn-review-german-light-quanta-khv`, a human gate
that also confirms ledger fidelity for the sections it reviews).

**Never run OCR on this machine.** If a page needs a new machine draft, request a cloud job through
`am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`; if the cloud path is unavailable, pause and report the blocker.
Starting a ledger page from the image alone, without a cloud draft, is a policy decision for the
user, never an agent's call.

## Requirements

1. **Format** exactly as defined in `docs/editorial/LEDGER_FORMAT.md` by
`am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`, using its typed tag set:
   - the first line is `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---`, and the complete ordered marker
   sequence follows, one marker per PDF page in the article scope recorded in the receipt;
   - a printed-page anchor `[[ANNALEN-PAGE <n>]]` follows each marker;
   - masthead and running-head furniture uses the validator's masthead tags, and a page region
   belonging to a neighboring article uses `[[OTHER-ARTICLE-OMITTED]]`;
   - paragraphs are separated by blank lines and keep the printed order; a paragraph continuing
   across a page break ends its first part with `[[CONTINUES]]`;
   - headings use `[[HEADING s<n>]]` with the section id and keep the printed § numbers and wording;
   - display equations are retyped LaTeX inside `$$ … $$` followed by `[[EQ-LABEL (<printed
   label>)]]` when one is printed; inline mathematics uses `$ … $`;
   - letter-spaced emphasis uses `[[SPERR]]…[[/SPERR]]`, non-mathematical italics `[[EM]]…[[/EM]]`,
   footnote marks `[[FN-MARK <label>]]`, and footnote text `[[FN <label>]]` at their printed
   positions (footnote numbering in *Annalen* can restart on each page; record the printed label); a
   footnote crossing a page boundary uses the validator's continuation tags `[[FN-CONTINUES]]` and
   `[[FN-CONT]]`;
   - closings are typed: `[[DATELINE]]` for the date-line, `[[ACK]]` for an acknowledgment if the
   page shows one, and `[[RECEIVED]]` for the journal's printed receipt line; the receipt's
   `expectedClosings` says which this paper has;
   - running heads, bare page numbers, scan furniture, and every draft-only token (`[[MATH-REGION`,
   `unverified`, `[[RUNNING-HEAD`, `[[PAGE-NUMBER`, `[[ILLEGIBLE]]`) never appear in the ledger;
   - declared normalizations only: rejoin words hyphenated by line wrapping, resolve ligatures, keep
   original spelling and punctuation (for example `daß`), never modernize. **A hyphen at a line end
   is a validator error, not a warning**: rejoin it unless the facsimile hyphenates the word in its
   own right, and record that case with the validator's explicit marker.
2. **Skeleton first, then pages.** Create the ledger with the complete marker sequence and anchors
taken from the receipt's page map, leaving uncorrected pages empty; that skeleton passes the
validator's structural rules. Correct pages in order (or in claimed page ranges if several agents
work in parallel, recorded in bead comments and integrated one page at a time), committing after
each page with the validator passing and reserving the file through Agent Mail while editing. Set
`transcription.ledgerStatus: in-progress` in the receipt when the skeleton is committed.
3. **Method**, page by page:
   - render the pinned page at 300 dpi or more and correct the cloud draft line by line against the
   image;
   - retype every mathematical region from the image, never from the draft's LaTeX or any PDF text
   layer;
   - compare with the comparison witnesses recorded in the receipt only to surface candidate
   differences. As of 2026-09-14 German Wikisource had no transcription of this paper, so no
   machine-readable witness is expected: compare visually against the Collected Papers Vol. 2 Doc.
   14 page images or print (in copyright, consulted, never copied). If a machine-readable witness
   appears, its text may sit only in a gitignored working file under
   `artifacts/ledger-work/ap-17-132/witness/`. Resolve every difference by returning to the
   facsimile, never by majority vote and never by copying witness text;
   - when every page is corrected, set `ledgerStatus: corrected`; then make a complete second read
   of the whole ledger against the images, by a different editor or agent where possible, recording
   honestly if the same agent did both, and set `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read`.
4. **Suspected historical typographical errors** go into the receipt's `typographicalErrors` with
the locator, original reading, proposed correction, reasoning, evidence, `layer: source`, recorder,
and date. The ledger keeps the original reading.
5. **Transcription watch list for this paper** (transcribe from the image; the expected values below
are checks, never sources), with each result written to the receipt's `watchList` (`matches`,
`differs`, or `not-found`, with `checkedBy` and `checkedAt`):
   - the word *heuristisch* and every qualifying phrase exactly as printed;
   - Planck's constants in §2 (expected $\alpha = 6.10\times10^{-57}$ and $\beta =
   4.866\times10^{-11}$ in CGS, printed result $N = 6.17\times10^{23}$; an exponent of $-56$ would
   be a transcription error, which the check $N = 8\pi R\beta/(\alpha L^3)$ exposes);
   - **whether §2 prints $R$ and $L$ at all, and in what form.** `am-ref-constants-xik` treats $R =
   8.31\times10^{7}$ erg mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ as an editorial input to the printed-historical sets, because
   paper 2 does not print it and paper 1 §2 appears not to print it either. Record the answer here;
   no layer may claim $R$ is printed in this paper unless this item resolves to `matches`;
   - the §1 relation $\rho_\nu = \frac{R}{N}\frac{8\pi\nu^2}{L^3}T$;
   - the §3 relation $\partial\varphi/\partial\rho = 1/T$ as printed;
   - the §4 result $S - S_0 = \frac{E}{\beta\nu}\log\frac{v}{v_0}$ with the printed volume glyph and
   logarithm symbol;
   - the §5 relation $W = (v/v_0)^n$ with the printed glyphs;
   - the §6 exponent $NE/(R\beta\nu)$;
   - §8: the relation $\Pi\varepsilon = \frac{R}{N}\beta\nu - P$ as printed; the printed charge of
   one gram equivalent of a monovalent ion (expected $E = 9.6\times10^{3}$ in electromagnetic CGS)
   and which glyph the page uses for it; the printed factor $10^{-8}$ that converts to volts; and
   the printed statement that $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ gives about 4.3 volts
   (with those printed values $R\beta\nu/E = 4.338\times10^{8}$ electromagnetic units, that is 4.34
   volts; python3, 2026-09-15). The electrostatic-unit route is a modern restatement and is never
   transcribed as the paper's own;
   - the §9 bound on energy per ion;
   - $L$ means the speed of light in this paper and $\beta$ is Wien's constant, not the relativity
   factor; the date-line and the received note.
6. **Receipt updates**: the transcription method (cloud draft `toolRunId` values, correction
process), editors and their roles and pages, correction and second-read dates, witness differences
worth noting, `typographicalErrors`, `watchList` results, `ledgerSourcePdfSha256` (equal to
`scan.sha256`), `ledgerSha256` of the final file, and `ledgerStatus`. The receipt checker must pass
after every update, and it refuses `ledgerStatus: reviewed` while any watch-list item is still
`pending`.
7. **Status honesty**: machine drafts never self-certify, and neither does an agent's correction.
`corrected-second-read` requires the validator to pass with no unacknowledged warnings, every page
non-empty, every watch-list item checked, and the second read complete.

## Technical Approach

- Keep a per-page checklist in the working notes: text lines, headings, emphasis, footnotes, inline
math, display math with labels, page anchor, continuation marker.
- Run `bun scripts/validate-ledger.ts public/papers/transcripts/ap-17-132-reviewed.txt --paper
light-quanta` after each page; acknowledge any justified warning in
`content/source-blocks/light-quanta/ledger-allowlist.yaml` with a line fingerprint, reason, and
editor name.
- Log every witness difference and its resolution in
`artifacts/ledger-work/ap-17-132/differences.jsonl`, and summarize the substantive ones in the
receipt.
- Run `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-132` after each receipt update.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ledger covers every PDF page in scope with the full ordered marker sequence and
printed-page anchors that match the receipt's page map, and no page is empty.
- [ ] Every display equation is retyped LaTeX that parses in KaTeX strict mode and matches the page
image; every inline formula likewise.
- [ ] All footnotes are present at their printed positions with marks paired, continuation tags used
where a footnote crosses a page; headings carry section ids; closings are typed; no draft-only token
remains; no line ends with an unjustified hyphen.
- [ ] The validator passes; every acknowledged warning has a recorded reason and editor.
- [ ] Every watch-list item has a recorded result in the receipt, including the printed-$R$ question
and the §8 charge and volt-conversion items.
- [ ] The receipt records method, editors, dates, witness differences, the typographical-error
register, `ledgerSourcePdfSha256`, `ledgerSha256`, and `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read`, and
the receipt checker passes.
- [ ] No OCR ran locally; no text was copied from witnesses or historical translations; the bead
never set `ledgerStatus: reviewed`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/editions/lightQuanta.ledger.test.ts`, against the real ledger, receipt, and validator:
- the validator returns `valid: true` with zero unacknowledged warnings, and reports no
`line-end-hyphen` error;
- the marker count equals the receipt's PDF page count for the article scope, and printed-page
anchors run 132–148 in order;
- every `$$ … $$` and `$ … $` region parses with KaTeX in strict mode;
- footnote marks and footnote texts pair on each page, and every `[[FN-CONTINUES]]` has a matching
`[[FN-CONT]]` on the next page;
- every heading tag carries a section id, and the closing tags match the receipt's
`expectedClosings`;
- no draft-only token appears;
- the receipt's `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256` equals `scan.sha256`;
- completeness checks, which run when the receipt's `ledgerStatus` is `corrected` or later and are
logged as `skipped` with the reason "ledger in progress" before that (never silently): every page is
non-empty; per-page counts of display equations and footnote marks equal the receipt page map; every
watch-list item is no longer `pending`; `ledgerSha256` equals the SHA-256 of the file (from
`corrected-second-read` on);
- a numeric consistency check on the ledger's own §2 constants: parse the printed $\alpha$, $\beta$,
and $N$ from their retyped LaTeX; take $R$ and $L$ from the ledger when the watch list records them
as printed, and otherwise from the editorial inputs of the printed-historical set in
`am-ref-constants-xik`, naming in the log which source was used. Then $8\pi R\beta/(\alpha L^3)$
equals the printed $N$ within 1 percent (with the expected printed values, $6.1705\times10^{23}$
against $6.17\times10^{23}$, a difference of 0.01 percent; python3, 2026-09-15). A mismatch fails
and names the constants unless the receipt's `typographicalErrors` records a printing error for
exactly those constants (the ledger still keeps the printed readings), so an exponent slip in
retyping cannot pass;
- a second numeric check on §8 when the watch list records the printed charge and volt factor:
$R\beta\nu/E$ at $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ equals the printed volt value within 2
percent (4.34 against "about 4.3");
- every watch-list item with result `differs` carries a note, and where a printing error is
suspected, a matching `typographicalErrors` entry with evidence;
- after `am-edn-inventory-light-quanta-skp` lands, per-page counts of paragraphs, display equations,
and footnotes equal the inventory's counts;
- a wiring check: the same assertions over a copy of the ledger in
`artifacts/test-tmp/ledger-light-quanta/<log-run-id>/` with the §2 exponent of $\alpha$ changed from
$-57$ to $-56$ must fail the numeric consistency check.

### End-to-end tests
- No browser test. The close reason records the JSONL output of `bun scripts/validate-ledger.ts`
over the final file and of `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-17-132`. The edition contract
tests in `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` consume this ledger. A failing run retains the validator
output, the offending page render path, and the JSONL log under
`artifacts/test-logs/ledger-light-quanta/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
The test writes JSON lines to `artifacts/test-logs/ledger-light-quanta/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with
`timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `ledgerStatus`, `pdfPage`,
`annalenPage`, `check`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome` (`passed`,
`failed`, `skipped`), `lineNumber`, and `message`. Correction sessions log witness-difference
resolutions to `artifacts/ledger-work/ap-17-132/differences.jsonl` (`timestamp`, `editor`,
`pdfPage`, `line`, `ledgerReading`, `witness`, `witnessReading`, `resolution`, `evidence`).

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A line that would look wrong beside a careful human transcription is not done: no mid-word wrap
hyphens, no one-word lines, no glued paragraphs, no ligature misreadings, no machine tokens.
- Do not normalize units, exponents, or notation; the notation concordance is a separate layer.
- Do not fix a suspected printing error in the ledger; record it.
- Greek letters $\varphi$, $\rho$, $\nu$, $\beta$, $\alpha$ are easy to confuse in worn type; check
each against the image.
- The planning notes wrote some formulas with modern habits (for example $\ln$ and capital $V$ for
volume); the watch list flags them because the page decides.
- A value the paper uses is not always a value the paper prints; the $R$ item exists so no later
layer invents a printed provenance.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-ocr-light-quanta-k8w`: the cloud OCR draft checkpoints and coverage report.
- `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`: the ledger format specification and validator.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-german-edition-light-quanta-eou`: the continuous German edition is built from this ledger.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE INSTRUMENT: the photoelectric fixture should use the 4,3 volts and the 10^-8 conversion and never the 10^7 factor. AGENTS.md already names 'about 4.3 V for nu = 1.03e15' as a historical fixture, so the fixture is safe; the factor is not.

EVERY EXPONENT ON THIS PAGE was read from pixels because the text layer garbles all of them: 10^3 as '10%', 10^-8 as '10-<registered>', 10^7 as '107'. Not one was safe to copy. Two further pixel corrections: 'annimmt.' ends in a period where the layer gives a comma, and 'kinetischen' where the layer gives 'kinstischen'.

Concordance note: Einstein uses epsilon for the electron's electrical mass and E for the gram-equivalent charge within three lines. Both preserved; the glyphs must not be unified, and E gains another scope.

Not closing.

FORMAL ANSWER TO THE FREEZE CONDITION, asked explicitly by the orchestrator: NO. Pages 146, 147 and 148 turned up NO segmentation class that is neither a paragraph, an enumerator, nor a continuation.

Block-by-block, from the per-page plate readings the transcription was made from:

p146 - 4 body paragraph starts (Ist der Koerper / Setzt man / Um zunaechst / Ist die abgeleitete Formel) plus 1 carried continuation; 2 flush continuations ('wobei epsilon ... oder', 'wobei E ...'); 3 displays; 2 footnotes. No enumerator.

p147 - 5 paragraph starts (Mit den von Hrn. Lenard / Ueber die mutmasslichen / Im vorstehenden / Fuer die Kathodenlumineszenz / Wir werden anzunehmen haben); 1 flush continuation ('Bei den von Hrn. Lenard'); 2 displays; 2 footnotes. No enumerator.

p148 - 1 body paragraph start (Eine obere Grenze) plus 1 carried continuation; 2 flush continuations ('Nach Messungen Lenards', 'Diese Beziehung muss'); 3 displays; 2 footnotes; 2 closings.

Every block on all three pages is a paragraph, a continuation, a display, a footnote, or a closing. The enumerated list appears exactly once in this paper, on p145, and it is the third class behaving as the corrected rule predicts.

THE ONE NEW BLOCK KIND is the closings on p148, and it is NOT a segmentation class: LEDGER_FORMAT 4.7 defines [[DATELINE]] and [[RECEIVED]] with their own tags, both are transcribed in their printed positions, and neither creates a paragraph-boundary ambiguity.

ONE THING I AM DELIBERATELY EXCLUDING, named so the orchestrator can disagree rather than discover it: page-foot furniture (watch-page-foot-furniture, ruling-open) - the journal footer and printer's signature marks on p145 and p147, which the ledger records on no page and for which no tag exists. I exclude it because it is a content-INCLUSION question, not a segmentation one: it never creates, moves or merges a paragraph boundary, so it cannot change a sentence id. If the orchestrator reads 'segmentation' more broadly than I do, this is the item that would flip my answer, and it should be ruled on before the freeze rather than after.

BASIS AND ITS LIMIT. The answer rests on the per-page plate readings at 400 dpi that the transcription was made from, plus the layer's indent column as a second witness. It does NOT rest on the automated indent sweep I ran to re-check it: that screen has known noise - leading scan marginalia zero out an indent - and on this very run it mis-read p146's 'Ist der Koerper zum positiven Potential Pi' as sitting at the baseline. I zoomed that line at 400 dpi and it is plainly indented against the line below it, so the transcription was right and the screen was wrong. I am reporting the screen's failure rather than the screen's output.

Not closing.

title: Hand-correct the reviewed diplomatic German ledger for ap-18-639
description:
# Hand-correct the reviewed diplomatic German ledger for ap-18-639

**Epic:** `am-ep-sources-zbs` · **Batch:** A (transcription runs in parallel with implementation) ·
**Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §3.6, §4.3, §4.4, §17.2, §17.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The reviewed ledger is the page-marked, diplomatic German transcription of the mass–energy paper,
*Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig?* (three pages, no section
structure, date-line "Bern, September 1905"). It is **comparison evidence**, not the visitor-facing
text: the continuous German edition is built from it in `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv`, and
edition tests later prove that every edition block is contained in this ledger and that no page
markers leak into the edition. A diplomatic transcription preserves mathematical content, meaningful
punctuation, paragraph order, original spelling, and original notation, and it normalizes only
declared typography such as line-break hyphenation. The cloud OCR draft is only a starting point:
every line is corrected by hand against the facsimile page image, and **every equation is retyped by
the editor and compared directly with the image**. Parsed PDF text, including any OCR layer embedded
in the scan by its host, is never accepted for an equation.

Planning notes summarized this paper with modern shorthand ($\beta$, $E'/E$, $H_0 - H_1 = L\beta$).
The printed text is expected to use explicit radicals and lowercase $l$ for the light energy, so the
watch list asks for the printed forms.

The ledger file carries no header, so it never declares a digest. The binding lives outside the
text: the validator emits `ledgerSha256` and `sourceAssetSha256`, the receipt records them as
`transcription.ledgerSha256` and `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256` (the receipt checker requires
the latter to equal `scan.sha256`), and `content/source-blocks/mass-energy/edition.yaml` pins both.

The file name keeps the project's established `-reviewed.txt` suffix, but agents never certify
review. This bead brings the ledger to `corrected-second-read`; the status `reviewed` is set only
when the human German source review (`am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`) records acceptance.

## Scope

In scope: producing `public/papers/transcripts/ap-18-639-reviewed.txt` for all 3 journal pages
(639–641); recording the transcription method, editors, dates, witness differences, watch-list
results, suspected historical typographical errors, the ledger digest, and the ledger status in
`docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md`.

Out of scope: block and sentence ids (`am-edn-inventory-mass-energy-g2d`), the continuous German
edition (`am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv`), translation (`am-ep-editions-1wa` translation
beads), and formal German-source acceptance (`am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`, a human gate
that also confirms ledger fidelity for the sections it reviews).

**Never run OCR on this machine.** If a page needs a new machine draft, request a cloud job through
`am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`; if the cloud path is unavailable, pause and report the blocker.
Starting a ledger page from the image alone, without a cloud draft, is a policy decision for the
user, never an agent's call.

## Requirements

1. **Format** exactly as defined in `docs/editorial/LEDGER_FORMAT.md` by
`am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`, using its typed tag set:
   - the first line is `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---`, and the complete ordered marker
   sequence follows, one marker per PDF page in the article scope recorded in the receipt;
   - a printed-page anchor `[[ANNALEN-PAGE <n>]]` follows each marker;
   - masthead and running-head furniture uses the validator's masthead tags, and a page region
   belonging to a neighboring article (likely on page 641) uses `[[OTHER-ARTICLE-OMITTED]]`;
   - paragraphs are separated by blank lines and keep the printed order; a paragraph continuing
   across a page break ends its first part with `[[CONTINUES]]`;
   - the title uses `[[HEADING s0]]`, since this paper has no numbered sections and its blocks use
   the `s0` section id;
   - display equations are retyped LaTeX inside `$$ … $$` followed by `[[EQ-LABEL (<printed
   label>)]]` when one is printed; inline mathematics uses `$ … $`;
   - letter-spaced emphasis uses `[[SPERR]]…[[/SPERR]]`, non-mathematical italics `[[EM]]…[[/EM]]`,
   footnote marks `[[FN-MARK <label>]]`, and footnote text `[[FN <label>]]` at their printed
   positions (record the printed label); a footnote crossing a page boundary uses the validator's
   continuation tags `[[FN-CONTINUES]]` and `[[FN-CONT]]`;
   - closings are typed: `[[DATELINE]]` for the date-line and `[[RECEIVED]]` for the journal's
   printed receipt line; the receipt's `expectedClosings` says which this paper has (no
   acknowledgment is expected, so `[[ACK]]` should not appear unless the page shows one);
   - running heads, bare page numbers, scan furniture, and every draft-only token (`[[MATH-REGION`,
   `unverified`, `[[RUNNING-HEAD`, `[[PAGE-NUMBER`, `[[ILLEGIBLE]]`) never appear in the ledger;
   - declared normalizations only: rejoin words hyphenated by line wrapping, resolve ligatures, keep
   original spelling and punctuation (for example `daß`), never modernize. **A hyphen at a line end
   is a validator error, not a warning**: rejoin it unless the facsimile hyphenates the word in its
   own right, and record that case with the validator's explicit marker.
2. **Skeleton first, then pages.** Create the ledger with the complete marker sequence and anchors
taken from the receipt's page map, leaving uncorrected pages empty; that skeleton passes the
validator's structural rules. Correct the three pages in order, committing after each page with the
validator passing and reserving the file through Agent Mail while editing. Set
`transcription.ledgerStatus: in-progress` in the receipt when the skeleton is committed.
3. **Method**, page by page:
   - render the pinned page at 300 dpi or more and correct the cloud draft line by line against the
   image;
   - retype every mathematical region from the image, never from the draft's LaTeX or any PDF text
   layer;
   - compare with the comparison witnesses recorded in the receipt only to surface candidate
   differences. As of 2026-09-14 German Wikisource had no transcription of this paper, so no
   machine-readable witness is expected: compare visually against the Collected Papers Vol. 2 Doc.
   24 page images or print (in copyright, consulted, never copied). If a machine-readable witness
   appears, its text may sit only in a gitignored working file under
   `artifacts/ledger-work/ap-18-639/witness/`. Resolve every difference by returning to the
   facsimile, never by majority vote and never by copying witness text;
   - when every page is corrected, set `ledgerStatus: corrected`; then make a complete second read
   of the whole ledger against the images, by a different editor or agent where possible, recording
   honestly if the same agent did both, and set `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read`.
4. **Suspected historical typographical errors** go into the receipt's `typographicalErrors` with
the locator, original reading, proposed correction, reasoning, evidence, `layer: source`, recorder,
and date. The ledger keeps the original reading.
5. **Transcription watch list for this paper** (transcribe from the image; the expected forms below
are checks, never sources), with each result written to the receipt's `watchList` (`matches`,
`differs`, or `not-found`, with `checkedBy` and `checkedAt`):
   - the footnote citing the relativity paper (*Ann. d. Phys.* 17, p. 891, 1905) and any further
   footnote (expected: a remark that the principle of the constancy of the velocity of light is
   contained in Maxwell's equations);
   - the imported light-energy relation as printed here, expected as $l^* = l\,\frac{1 -
   \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}}$ with lowercase $l$; its source is the §8 result of
   `ap-17-891`, recorded in that receipt's watch-list entry `s8-energy-relation`, and the trace is
   by content, because the two papers print different letters;
   - the two emissions of $\tfrac{1}{2}L$;
   - $E_0 = E_1 + \tfrac{1}{2}L + \tfrac{1}{2}L$ and $H_0 = H_1 + \tfrac{1}{2}L\,\frac{1 -
   \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}} + \tfrac{1}{2}L\,\frac{1 +
   \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}} = H_1 + \frac{L}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}}$, with every
   intermediate line, and their difference;
   - the identification of $H - E$ with the kinetic energy $K$ plus the additive constant $C$, and
   $K_0 - K_1 = L\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}} - 1\right\}$;
   - the statement about neglecting quantities of fourth and higher order, and $K_0 - K_1 =
   \tfrac{1}{2}\frac{L}{V^2}v^2$;
   - the conclusion that the mass diminishes by $L/V^2$ and the sentence that the mass of a body is
   a measure of its energy content;
   - the numerical statement expected as a mass change of $L/9\cdot10^{20}$ with energy in ergs and
   mass in grams, which is the only numerical constant this paper prints and the sole entry of the
   printed-historical set `einstein-1905-mass-energy-printed` in `am-ref-constants-xik`;
   - the conditional remark about radium salts, and the closing remark that, if the theory
   corresponds to the facts, radiation carries inertia between emitting and absorbing bodies;
   - whether the symbol $\beta$ appears anywhere in this paper (if not, flag it for the notation
   concordance owner, `am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`, since planning notes assumed it);
   - $L$ is emitted energy in this paper; $V$ is the speed of light; $E = mc^2$ does not appear and
   must not be introduced;
   - the date-line and the received note.
6. **Receipt updates**: the transcription method (cloud draft `toolRunId` values, correction
process), editors and their roles and pages, correction and second-read dates, witness differences
worth noting, `typographicalErrors`, `watchList` results, `ledgerSourcePdfSha256` (equal to
`scan.sha256`), `ledgerSha256` of the final file, and `ledgerStatus`. The receipt checker must pass
after every update, and it refuses `ledgerStatus: reviewed` while any watch-list item is still
`pending`.
7. **Status honesty**: machine drafts never self-certify, and neither does an agent's correction.
`corrected-second-read` requires the validator to pass with no unacknowledged warnings, every page
non-empty, every watch-list item checked, and the second read complete.

## Technical Approach

- Keep a per-page checklist in the working notes: text lines, emphasis, footnotes, inline math,
display math with labels, page anchor, continuation marker.
- Run `bun scripts/validate-ledger.ts public/papers/transcripts/ap-18-639-reviewed.txt --paper
mass-energy` after each page; acknowledge any justified warning in
`content/source-blocks/mass-energy/ledger-allowlist.yaml` with a line fingerprint, reason, and
editor name.
- Log every witness difference and its resolution in
`artifacts/ledger-work/ap-18-639/differences.jsonl`, and summarize the substantive ones in the
receipt.
- Run `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-18-639` after each receipt update.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ledger covers every PDF page in scope with the full ordered marker sequence and
printed-page anchors that match the receipt's page map, and no page is empty.
- [ ] Every display equation is retyped LaTeX that parses in KaTeX strict mode and matches the page
image; every inline formula likewise.
- [ ] All footnotes are present at their printed positions with marks paired; the title heading
carries `s0`; the date-line and received line are typed closings; no draft-only token remains; no
line ends with an unjustified hyphen.
- [ ] The validator passes; every acknowledged warning has a recorded reason and editor.
- [ ] Every watch-list item has a recorded result in the receipt, including the printed forms of the
imported relation and the energy balances, the $9\cdot10^{20}$ statement, and whether $\beta$
appears.
- [ ] The receipt records method, editors, dates, witness differences, the typographical-error
register, `ledgerSourcePdfSha256`, `ledgerSha256`, and `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read`, and
the receipt checker passes.
- [ ] No OCR ran locally; no text was copied from witnesses or historical translations; the bead
never set `ledgerStatus: reviewed`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/editions/massEnergy.ledger.test.ts`, against the real ledger, receipt, and validator:
- the validator returns `valid: true` with zero unacknowledged warnings, and reports no
`line-end-hyphen` error;
- the marker count equals the receipt's PDF page count for the article scope, and printed-page
anchors run 639–641 in order;
- every `$$ … $$` and `$ … $` region parses with KaTeX in strict mode;
- footnote marks and footnote texts pair on each page, every `[[FN-CONTINUES]]` has a matching
`[[FN-CONT]]`, and at least one footnote cites volume 17, page 891;
- the heading tag carries `s0`, and the closing tags match the receipt's `expectedClosings`;
- no draft-only token appears, and the string `mc^2` does not appear anywhere in the ledger;
- the receipt's `transcription.ledgerSourcePdfSha256` equals `scan.sha256`;
- completeness checks, which run when the receipt's `ledgerStatus` is `corrected` or later and are
logged as `skipped` with the reason "ledger in progress" before that (never silently): every page is
non-empty; per-page counts of display equations and footnote marks equal the receipt page map; every
watch-list item is no longer `pending`; `ledgerSha256` equals the SHA-256 of the file (from
`corrected-second-read` on);
- a numeric consistency check: if the ledger contains the printed mass-energy factor, parsing it
gives exactly $9\times10^{20}$, which equals $(3\times10^{10})^2$ (python3, 2026-09-15); any other
value fails unless the receipt's `typographicalErrors` records a printing error for it (the ledger
still keeps the printed reading);
- every watch-list item with result `differs` carries a note, and where a printing error is
suspected, a matching `typographicalErrors` entry with evidence;
- after `am-edn-inventory-mass-energy-g2d` lands, per-page counts of paragraphs, display equations,
and footnotes equal the inventory's counts;
- a wiring check: the same assertions over a copy of the ledger in
`artifacts/test-tmp/ledger-mass-energy/<log-run-id>/` with the factor changed to $9\cdot10^{21}$
must fail the numeric check.

### End-to-end tests
- No browser test. The close reason records the JSONL output of `bun scripts/validate-ledger.ts`
over the final file and of `bun scripts/check-receipts.ts --key ap-18-639`. The edition contract
tests in `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` consume this ledger. A failing run retains the validator
output, the offending page render path, and the JSONL log under
`artifacts/test-logs/ledger-mass-energy/<log-run-id>/evidence/`.

### Structured logging
The test writes JSON lines to `artifacts/test-logs/ledger-mass-energy/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with
`timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper`, `ledgerStatus`, `pdfPage`,
`annalenPage`, `check`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome` (`passed`, `failed`,
`skipped`), `lineNumber`, and `message`. Correction sessions log witness-difference resolutions to
`artifacts/ledger-work/ap-18-639/differences.jsonl` (`timestamp`, `editor`, `pdfPage`, `line`,
`ledgerReading`, `witness`, `witnessReading`, `resolution`, `evidence`).

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A line that would look wrong beside a careful human transcription is not done: no mid-word wrap
hyphens, no one-word lines, no glued paragraphs, no ligature misreadings, no machine tokens.
- Do not normalize units, exponents, or notation; the notation concordance is a separate layer.
- Do not fix a suspected printing error in the ledger; record it.
- Three pages invite shortcuts; the complete second read is still required.
- Modern shorthand in planning notes is not the printed text; a radical stays a radical and
lowercase $l$ stays lowercase.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-src-ocr-mass-energy-3yo`: the cloud OCR draft checkpoints and coverage report.
- `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`: the ledger format specification and validator.

Unblocks:
- `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv`: the continuous German edition is built from this ledger.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ap-18-639 IS TRANSCRIBED. c01a7b6c (policy), the skeleton commit, f46fb572 (page 639), 7de75710
(pages 640-641 and the validator fix). LilacValley, 2026-09-20.

Validator: valid true, clean true, 0 errors, 0 warnings. 3 pages, 14 paragraphs, 7 display
equations, 2 footnotes, 2 closings, 4 Sperrdruck spans. The 7 display equations are exactly the
seven the receipt page map lists as eq-s0-d1 through eq-s0-d7 - one on 639, three on 640, three
on 641 - so the transcription and the inventory agree without either being adjusted to the other.

WHAT THIS IS, and it is written in the receipt rather than only here: a MACHINE DRAFT WITH HAND
CORRECTION. Drafted from the OCR layer the Internet Archive embedded in the pinned scan, then
corrected line by line against the pinned page images, under the owner's am-1hv0 decision-1
ruling of 2026-09-20 ("Both layer and pixels"). No OCR software was run on this host. It satisfies
NO acceptance criterion requiring human review. ledgerStatus is in-progress, editors is empty, and
docs/OWNERS.md shows open-german-source-mass-energy unfilled - measured, along with 53 other slots
marked "open: recruiting" against one named human.

AGENTS.md WAS AMENDED FIRST, not worked around, because the ruling required it and because a
document sitting behind practice on a resource rule is worse than one sitting ahead of it. The
bullet that conflated EXECUTING an OCR program with READING an artefact is now two bullets, and
the executable prohibition is restated in the same breath so nobody reads the permission as
reaching the engines. The OCR guard is untouched.

WHY READING THE IMAGES MATTERED, in the paper's own title. The embedded layer renders it:

    "Ist die Trdgheit eines Kerpers von seinem Eimergieinhalt abhaengig?"

Three errors, all mechanically valid ASCII, none findable by any checker. And on pages 640 and
641 every one of the six display equations is absent or destroyed in the layer - page 640's first
equation is simply not there, and the second survives as "H,= H,+". Subscripts are gone
throughout. Every equation was retyped from the image, as the bead and AGENTS.md both require.

A VALIDATOR DEFECT BLOCKED THIS OUTRIGHT AND IS FIXED IN 7de75710.
ledgerMathSettings.ts passed `macros: Object.freeze({})` to KaTeX, which writes its own
bookkeeping into that object for an environment. Every alignment environment therefore threw
"Attempting to define property on object that is not extensible", reported as `math-parse` - a
code that reads as "the editor mistyped the LaTeX". Page 641 prints a two-line aligned pair, so no
faithful transcription of this paper could ever have validated. Measured three ways: aligned +
frozen FAILS, aligned + plain PASSES, ordinary equation + frozen PASSES. Nothing was loosened -
the macro ban is a regex that runs before KaTeX - and three tests say so, including one proving
\def is still refused INSIDE an alignment environment. Plant: restore the frozen object and the
aligned test goes RED, 6 pass 1 fail.

TWO FINDINGS FILED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND SILENTLY:
  am-2e4y  LEDGER_FORMAT.md documents [[ARTICLE-NUMBER]]; validateLedger.ts has zero occurrences
           of it, so it parses as a two-word paragraph and warns short-line. Removed from this
           ledger, which the manifest agrees with - it has no unit for an article number either.
  am-7rkm  Every ledger's first line says "--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION ---" and the file is named
           <key>-reviewed.txt, but this one is a machine draft. The grammar token and the filename
           both say reviewed and the artefact is not. Nothing is mislabelled today because the
           receipt carries the status, but a reader who opens the .txt sees only the word REVIEWED.

NOT CLOSING. This bead's acceptance includes a German source review that no one can perform yet.
What changed is that there is now something to review.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
TAKING ap-17-891 (31 pages) after orchestrator approval. Facsimile digest VERIFIED: shasum -a 256 of public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-891.pdf = 60d21d560f6a3c87e581ac25016306d9bcb748e530fa2751652b84986da5296c, matching BOTH sha256 and ledgerSourcePdfSha256 in docs/provenance/ap-17-891.md.

STARTING STATE, measured: page map has 31 pages, 98 display ids, 0 footnote marks declared anywhere, and 28 of 31 entries carry refinedBy am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9. The 3 unrefined entries are printed 891, 892 and 893 - the opening - which use the bare 'unnumbered: 0' shape. Same pattern as ap-17-132, where 3 of 17 were unrefined and each had to be checked from the plate; on that paper the 0 was true each time. content/source-blocks/special-relativity/manifest.yaml (58 KB) and manifest.ids.snapshot.txt already exist. ledgerStatus: not-started, no ledgerPath.

The 98 declared display ids are the cross-check instrument: on ap-17-132 the map's 52 displays and 13 footnote marks independently matched the validator's count of my transcription, and that agreement is what made completion verifiable rather than self-reported. NOTE the 0 footnote marks across all 31 pages - that is a claim I will test page by page, not assume.

EQ-LABEL EXERCISED DELIBERATELY AND EARLY, on the orchestrator's instruction, instead of waiting to reach it. ap-17-891 has numbered equations on EXACTLY ONE page - printed 918, page 28 of 31, label (A) - so a format/implementation gap found there would have been the 'page twenty' case.

RESULT: [[EQ-LABEL]] IS IMPLEMENTED, and I am correcting my own earlier suspicion that LEDGER_FORMAT 4.4.1 might describe a tag nothing implements. validateLedger.ts implements eq-label-orphan, eq-label-duplicate-in-section and eq-label-repeats-across-sections; ledgerTokenizer.ts knows the token; segmentSentences.ts and segmentLedger.ts both CONSUME it, so the code that cuts sentence units handles it; validateLedger.test.ts already covers orphan and duplicate; and the shipped fixture two-page-valid.txt contains a live [[EQ-LABEL (1)]] that validates clean.

PLANTED TEST against the real label, because every existing test uses a DIGIT and p918 uses a LETTER. Run via validateLedger(content) on src/testing/fixtures/ledgers/fixture-clean-reviewed.txt:
  BASELINE digit (1)   -> valid=true, errors []
  GREEN letter (A)     -> zero eq-label errors (only receipt-ledger-digest-mismatch, which ANY mutation of a digest-pinned fixture raises)
  RED orphaned (A)     -> eq-label-orphan@14 FIRES
Letter labels are accepted; the orphan arm is not vacuous.

NEAR-MISS OF MINE, recorded because the shape recurs: my first run filtered to codes starting 'eq-label' and printed valid=false with an EMPTY list - which reads exactly like 'letter labels break the validator'. The real cause was the digest pin, invisible under my own filter. Filtering a measurement to the codes you expect is the same class as an unanchored grep: it hides the cause and leaves a plausible wrong one in its place. Widened before reporting, not after.

Not closing.

comments.text:
BLOCKED, NAMED, AND NOT FAKED - and the same blocker sits on the two papers already transcribed, which makes it a graph defect rather than a property of this one.

br REFUSES the claim: 'cannot claim blocked issue: am-src-ocr-relativity-8ty'. Measured across all three ledger beads, the dependency shape is identical: each is blocked by its paper's cloud-OCR bead, and EVERY OCR bead is still open - am-src-ocr-light-quanta-k8w, am-src-ocr-brownian-n6q, am-src-ocr-relativity-8ty, am-src-ocr-mass-energy-3yo. None has run. The chain beneath them is three deep and none of it exists either: am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0, am-src-ocr-cloud-adapter-7wa1, am-src-ocr-dispatch-interface-m1ur, all open.

So am-src-ledger-light-quanta-sxi and am-src-ledger-brownian-8cw are BOTH still open and still blocked, while both papers are transcribed end to end and committed. The blocker was never satisfied for them either; I simply never claimed those beads, and br would have refused if I had.
