title: Build /tours and /tours/[id] with ordered anchors, budget labels, and local progress
description:
# Build /tours and /tours/[id] with ordered anchors, budget labels, and local progress

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.3, §11.2 (Tour), §15.1, §16.2, §16.6, §17.7 item 8, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

The same content is offered through three curated attention budgets. Each is an ordered list of anchors, with progress kept locally and no accounts:
- **Fifteen minutes:** one paper's first encounter, the R0 readings of its introduction and key result, three or four instruments in predict mode, and the R0 line of the discovery path's move. Entirely without equations, and still true.
- **One evening:** one paper at R1, all its instruments, the front-door discovery journey, the misconception ledger, and the historian's margin for the paper's editorial boundaries.
- **The full course:** all four papers and the companion, both discovery doors, every foundation node, the connections, the essays, the exercises, and the capstones, with a printable syllabus listing prerequisites per session from the foundation graph.

The no-math tour is a first-class deliverable, not a fallback: a reader who never opens an equation must leave knowing what each paper claimed, why it was hard, and what it changed. Each paper's definition of done requires a reader with no physics background to complete its fifteen-minute tour and state the paper's claim in one sentence (the reader-review beads), so this infrastructure must be solid by batch C. Tours are optional paths through the site, never required navigation.

Design facts that shape this bead:
- **Equations on the reading face.** The reading face shows equations at every Detail level; Detail changes the scaffolding, not which equations are present. A fifteen-minute tour that opened paper pages could not be equation-free. Fifteen-minute tours therefore render their steps **inside the tour page**:
  - the R0 text of the step's anchor;
  - first-encounter records through the shared renderer;
  - instruments mounted through the dispatcher in predict mode with an equation-free `tour` presentation;
  - the move summary of the paper's journey.

  A link to the paper remains available and says that it leaves the equation-free path. One-evening tours and the full course open steps **in the reader**, where equations are expected.
- **Move summaries live in the journey.** The R0 line of a journey's move is authored once, as the journey record's `move.r0Summary` (`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`), and tours cite it by journey id. A tour never carries its own copy, which would drift from the journey it summarizes. The summary carries a review state (`draft` or `reviewed`); `reviewed` exists only when a named physics reviewer's `physics-math` review record covers the journey's revision (the review-status rule of `am-edit-review-records-hofz`). Production and preview tours accept only a reviewed summary.
- **Prompts, presets, and tapes are cited by id.** A fifteen-minute tour asks the question an instrument's reveal actually settles, so every instrument step cites the manifest's predict prompt by `promptId` (the contract of `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: one prompt per control or action, three candidates each) and the preset, tape, or mode that reaches the reveal by the id its owner registers. A tour never invents a question its instrument does not ask: when the id it needs is not registered, the build fails with the id named rather than accepting tour-authored wording.
- **No equations means no symbols either.** Hiding equation cards is not enough if a caption, a table header, or a prompt's own words still read "γ" or "D". In fifteen-minute tours, captions, labels, table headers, questions, choice labels, and choice descriptions use plain-word quantity names. When the manifest's wording contains symbols, the tour supplies a plain-words rendering bound to that `promptId`, with each choice naming the manifest candidate it renders, so the tape's `prediction` event is the same event the full instrument records.
- **A tour is also the site's teacher-facing artifact.** It is an ordered walk with a stated budget, a question per step, a preset per instrument, and a completion statement, which is exactly what a teacher running it with a room, or a reading group meeting without a teacher, needs on paper. The printable artifacts elsewhere are the full-course syllabus (this bead) and the eleven paired-learning sheets attached to chapter-end tasks (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`), and neither is a tour. The tour sheet below fills that gap as a projection of the tour record, which is why it is affordable: a renderer and a route, not an editorial program.
- **Schema ownership.** The `Tour` schema belongs to `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` (`id`, `budget`, `paper?`, `orderedAnchors[]`, `completionStatement`, `requiresEquations`, `syllabus`). This bead extends its `orderedAnchors[]` entries from bare anchors to step objects and adds the build rules; it does not create a second tour schema.
- **Honest time.** Estimated minutes are checked against a reading-rate lower bound, so a tour never understates its time to fit its label.
- **One voice list.** Reader-progress copy is checked with `checkVoice` from `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, never with a second vocabulary list kept here. That bead forbids parallel deny lists and already names this bead as a `checkVoice` caller.

## Scope

In scope:
- The step-object extension of the `Tour` schema and the tour build rules, including prompt, preset, tape, and move-summary resolution.
- `/tours` (index), `/tours/[id]` (tour page), `/tours/[id]/sheet` (printable group sheet), and `/tours/full-course/syllabus` (printable syllabus).
- In-tour and in-reader step presentation, the tour bar, and return-stack integration.
- Local progress; the visible-math and symbol-label measurements shared by build, sheet, and tests.
- The syllabus generator; the sheet renderer; fixture tours for each budget; tests.

Out of scope: authoring tours (`am-tour-15min-brownian-z034`, `am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`, `am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`, `am-tour-15min-light-quanta-yj70`, `am-tour-evening-and-course-5kcb`); the instruments, their prompts, presets, and tapes, the readings, first encounters, journeys (and their move summaries), and foundation content they point to; the dispatcher's `tour` mount option itself (`am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`); the review-record format and review-status check (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`); the voice rules and their vocabulary (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`); the transfer cases the sheet cites, which belong to `am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i` (`transferExamples[]`) and `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7` (revisit cards and the three rotating roles); the canonical and sitemap policy, which `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6` records for every route family including the sheet.

## Requirements

### Tour record (`content/tours/<id>.yaml`, extending `Tour`)

- `id` (for example `fifteen-minutes-brownian-motion`, `one-evening-light-quanta`, `full-course`), `budget` (`fifteen-minutes`, `one-evening`, `full-course`), `paper?`, `title`, `completionStatement`, `requiresEquations` (must be `false` for fifteen-minute tours).
- `orderedAnchors[]`, each a step object:
  - `anchor`: a content id, such as a section, paragraph, or sentence; `#entry-<paper slug>` (the first encounter, record id `entrance-<paper slug>`); `#arg-<id>` (a journey stage); `#lab-<id>`; `#result-<slug>`; or an essay or connections anchor.
  - `kind`: `reading`, `first-encounter`, `instrument`, `journey-stage`, or `page`.
  - `presentation`: `in-tour` or `in-reader` (fifteen-minute tours: `in-tour` only).
  - `detail`: 0, 1, or 2 (fifteen-minute tours: 0).
  - `instrumentPreset?`: `{ instrumentId, promptId?, modeId?, presetId? | tapeId? }`. `promptId` names a prompt in the manifest's `predictMode.prompts`; `modeId` uses the id scheme's `<instrumentId>:<mode>` form; presets use `<instrumentId>-<slug>` and prompts `<instrumentId>-predict-<slug>`; at most one of `presetId` and `tapeId`; neither means the manifest's default scenario. Every id is cited exactly as its owning instrument registers it.
  - `tourPrediction?`: `{ promptId, question, choices }`, the plain-words rendering of the manifest prompt `promptId`. `choices` holds exactly three `{ candidateId, label, response }` entries whose `candidateId`s are exactly the prompt's three candidate ids, each used once; `response` is one authored line. It is shown through predict mode's verbal-candidate form and recorded on the instrument's tape as `{ type: "prediction", instrumentId, promptId, form: "verbal", payload: { candidateId } }`, so the prediction is the same event the full instrument records. When absent, the manifest prompt's own question, labels, and descriptions are rendered through the same verbal-candidate form, and they must pass the math and symbol measurements. A prediction is never scored.
  - `moveSummaryOf?` (journey-stage steps only): the journey id (the paper slug) whose `move.r0Summary.text` the step renders verbatim. The step's `anchor` must be the stage whose reasoning references the move's derivation step. No field exists for authored move text; the closed schema rejects one.
  - `estimatedMinutes` (positive) and `purpose` (one line).
- `parts[]?` (one-evening only): named parts ("evening 1: kinematics") with their step ranges, used when honest estimates exceed one evening.
- `sessions[]` (full course only): `{ id, title, steps[] }`. Prerequisites are computed at build time; a hand-typed prerequisite field is rejected.

### Build rules (registered with the compiler)

- Every anchor, instrument, prompt, mode, tape, and preset resolves; each failure names the tour, the step, and the unresolved id (`tour-anchor-unresolved`, `tour-prompt-unresolved`, `tour-preset-unresolved`, `tour-tape-unresolved`, `tour-mode-unresolved`).
- **Prompts:**
  - a fifteen-minute instrument step must cite a `promptId` (`tour-instrument-step-missing-prompt`);
  - `tourPrediction.promptId` must equal the step's `instrumentPreset.promptId` (`tour-prediction-prompt-mismatch`);
  - the three `candidateId`s must be exactly the prompt's candidate ids (`tour-prediction-candidates-mismatch`, listing the expected ids);
  - a cited tape must contain at least one command on the prompt's control or action, because a tape that never touches the prompted control cannot reveal its answer (`tour-tape-does-not-reveal-prompt`);
  - in a fifteen-minute tour, a cited prompt rendered without a `tourPrediction` whose question, candidate labels, or candidate descriptions contain a symbol label fails `tour-instrument-renders-symbols`, naming the instrument, the prompt, and the token, so the fix is either a plain-words prompt in the manifest (as `sr-09-predict-approaching` has) or a `tourPrediction` here.
- **Budgets:**
  - fifteen-minute tours sum to at most 15 minutes;
  - each one-evening tour or part sums to between 60 and 240 minutes, and a tour that needs more declares parts;
  - each full-course session is at most 120 minutes, and the course shows its total.
- **Honest-time lower bound** (`tour-minutes-understated`, with the computed bound in the message):
  - reading steps take the visible word count at the step's detail divided by 200 words per minute, rounded up to the next half minute (a journey-stage step counts the words of the rendered move summary);
  - first-encounter steps take at least 3 minutes;
  - instrument steps take at least 2 minutes.
- **Fifteen-minute tours:**
  - every step is `in-tour` at detail 0;
  - the compiled step content (R0 text, first-encounter record text, tour questions, choices, and responses, rendered manifest prompt text, instrument captions at detail 0, the cited move summary) contains no math nodes (`tour-step-contains-math`);
  - a static render of each instrument's worked case in the `tour` presentation contains no visible math nodes (`tour-instrument-renders-math`, naming the instrument);
  - that render, the step text, and the rendered prediction contain no symbol labels as measured by `symbolScan` below (`tour-instrument-renders-symbols`, naming the instrument and the token);
  - an R0 reading that contains mathematics cannot be used; the build names it so the author can fix the reading or choose another anchor;
  - a `journey-stage` step must carry `moveSummaryOf`, and its anchor must be the stage that makes the move (`tour-journey-stage-not-move`);
  - the cited journey's `move.r0Summary` must exist (`tour-move-summary-missing`, naming the journey). In the production and preview profiles a summary whose `reviewState` is not `reviewed` also fails `tour-move-summary-missing`, with the reason "not reviewed". A draft build renders a missing summary as "in preparation" and a `draft` summary with the framework's draft marker, which never appears in production output.
- A fifteen-minute tour with `requiresEquations: true` fails (the rule from `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`).
- Full course: every foundation registry entry, nodes and zero-algebra bridges alike, appears in at least one session, with missing ids listed.

### Pages and behavior

- **`/tours`** groups tours by paper and budget, with title, budget label, honest estimated total, completion statement, and a plain note that tours are optional.
- **`/tours/[id]`** statically renders every step in order (anchors `#step-<n>`), with purposes and minutes, and the completion statement at the end.
  - With JavaScript, the page becomes step-by-step with a tour bar: step $n$ of $m$, Next, Previous, Leave tour.
  - **In-tour steps** render in the step region (`[data-tour-step]`): R0 text, a first encounter, the cited move summary, or an instrument mounted through `src/experiments/dispatch.tsx` with predict mode, the cited prompt, preset, tape, or mode, and `presentation: "tour"`.
  - **The `tour` presentation** is a `presentation-change` that hides equation cards, show-the-code, and expanded model notes, while keeping the question, the R0 caption, predict mode, the accessible table, and the execution label. Its captions, labels, and table headers use the quantity registry's plain-word `name` for each quantity instead of a symbol, and a cited `promptId` is offered through predict mode's verbal-candidate form. It is an additive mount option on the dispatcher contract (`am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`) and never changes an instrument's physics. A manifest that declares it cannot honor the `tour` presentation renders the dispatcher's "This experiment is available in the full reading" notice, and a fifteen-minute tour citing that instrument fails `tour-instrument-renders-math`.
  - For fifteen-minute tours, "See this in the paper" is an optional link labeled as leaving the equation-free path.
  - **In-reader steps** open `/papers/[paper]?view=reading&detail=<d>#<anchor>` (or the journey, lab, essay, or connections page) with a slim tour bar.
  - **Detours** through the return stack restore the tour context and step. The tour bar never covers content and never traps focus.
- **Local progress** uses `am-plat-local-storage-km8f` under `am:tours:v1`: `{ tourId, currentStep, visitedSteps[], updatedAt }`, resumable and clearable per tour and globally. Blocked storage leaves the tour fully usable without persistence and shows a notice.
- **No gamification.** No streaks, scores, timers, countdowns, percentages, or completion badges; progress reads "step $n$ of $m$"; the completion statement is a plain summary. The rule is enforced by `checkVoice` in the `reader-progress` context, not by a list kept in this bead.
- **Without JavaScript,** `/tours/[id]` remains complete: every step in order, in-tour steps with their R0 text, the first encounter's static route, each instrument's static worked case, the tour question with its three choices and responses in a native `<details>`, and the move summary, so fifteen-minute readers stay on the equation-free path.

#### The tour sheet: a printable page for a teacher or a reading group

The sheet is a **projection of the tour record**, generated from fields the record already carries. It authors no new content.

- `/tours/[id]/sheet`, a static page for every compiled tour, linked from `/tours/[id]` as "Print a sheet for a group". Its canonical, indexing and sitemap facts are declared in the route registry of `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6` like every other family here, as a self-canonical page excluded from sitemap duplication of the tour it projects.
- The sheet's header names the tour title, its honest estimated total (the computed value, never the label), its completion statement, and a printed link back to the interactive tour.
- Per step, the sheet renders, in this order:
  1. **The question**, taken from the step's `purpose` and, for a `first-encounter` or `instrument` step, the question the record already carries (the first-encounter record's question, or the manifest prompt rendered through `tourPrediction` where one exists).
  2. **The source passage**, as the step's `anchor` plus its printed locator (section and, where the receipt supplies it, the printed *Annalen* page), so the passage can be found in the facsimile or in print without a screen.
  3. **The selected preset**, by its registered id (`<instrumentId>-<slug>`), or the mode (`<instrumentId>:<mode>`) or tape id the step cites, with the step's short URL printed as text. No QR codes, matching the paired sheets.
  4. **The predicted comparison**: the three candidate labels of the cited prompt, in the record's order, with ruled space for the group's prediction. A prediction is never scored, and the sheet says so once.
  5. **The expected explanation**: the step's authored response line, or for a `journey-stage` step the journey's reviewed `move.r0Summary` text, rendered verbatim from the journey record exactly as the tour page does. The sheet never carries its own copy.
- **One transfer case per sheet**, cited by the id of the record that owns it, never authored here. It is, in order of preference: a `transferExamples[]` entry of an essay that one of the tour's steps links to, addressed by the essay record id together with that entry's `domain` key (the entries carry no id of their own today; if `am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i` gives them stable ids, the sheet cites those instead), or a revisit card for the tour's paper (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`), by card id. When neither exists for a tour, the section is omitted rather than invented, and the build records which tours have no transfer case so an editor can decide whether to add one.
- **Rotating roles.** The sheet reuses the three roles of the paired sheets, cited rather than restated: propose a prediction, operate the experiment or work the case, question the explanation, rotating across the tour's steps. It also carries the one-line instruction for a reader working alone, so the sheet works for one person.
- **No accounts, no surveillance, no external platform.** The sheet names no platform, collects nothing, and requires no login to use or to print.

**Rules the sheet inherits.**

- **A fifteen-minute tour's sheet contains no mathematics and no symbols.** The sheet's rendered text passes the same `mathScan` and `symbolScan` measurements this bead already owns, in the same shared implementation, and fails with `tour-sheet-contains-math` or `tour-sheet-renders-symbols` naming the tour and the step. This is the check only this bead can make: a sheet generated from an equation-free tour that prints "γ" in a caption has broken the tour's one promise.
- **Honest time.** The sheet prints the computed estimate, so a sheet can never advertise a shorter session than the tour rules allow.
- **Reviewed move summaries only.** In the production and preview profiles a sheet renders a `move.r0Summary` only when its `reviewState` is `reviewed`, exactly as the tour page does; otherwise the step's explanation section is omitted, with the framework's draft marker in draft builds and absent in production.
- **Voice.** Sheet copy passes `checkVoice` in the `reader-progress` context for the progress and role copy and `prose` for step text, through the shared function; this bead adds no vocabulary list.
- **Print.** The sheet applies the stylesheet of `am-plat-print-3orn` and prints legibly in monochrome at A4 and US Letter, with each step starting on a new block and no content lost at the page break. It is usable on screen as well, and it works without JavaScript because it is static.

### Visible-math and symbol measurements (shared by build rules, the sheet, and tests)

- **`src/discovery/tours/mathScan.ts`.** A visible math node is a `.katex`, `math`, or `[data-math]` element that is rendered and not inside a `[hidden]` subtree, a closed `<details>`, an `aria-hidden="true"` subtree, or a `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` subtree. It counts only inside the tour step region or the tour bar, and on the sheet inside the sheet's step blocks, and is measured after load and after each scripted interaction in the step. Math inside an optional disclosure the reader must open (model note, show the code) is excluded from the count but logged.
- **`src/discovery/tours/symbolScan.ts`.** Over the same visible text, including the rendered prediction question, labels, and descriptions, a symbol label is: a standalone token equal to a glyph of the paper's notation concordance entries (original or modern symbol, including Greek letters and primed forms); a letter joined to a superscript or subscript; or the operators `=`, `√`, and `∝` placed between such tokens. Unit symbols (μm, eV, THz) and plain digits are allowed. A per-tour `symbolAllowlist` records reviewed exceptions that are not quantities (for example station names "A" and "B"), each with a reason.

### Syllabus generator (full course)

- For each session, collect the foundation ids that the session's anchors reference, using the compiled backlinks from readings, equation tool links, derivation steps, and obstacle responses.
- Add their transitive prerequisites from `Foundation.prerequisites`, but never through cross-reference edges.
- Subtract the foundations already covered in earlier sessions, then order the rest topologically, breaking ties by foundation id.
- A cycle among prerequisite edges fails with the cycle named.
- `/tours/full-course/syllabus` renders the sessions with their prerequisites. It is static, uses print styles, stays monochrome-legible at A4 and Letter, and works without JavaScript.

## Technical Approach

- **Schema:** the `Tour` extension in `src/content/schemas/experiment.ts`.
- **Rules and components:** `src/discovery/tours/tourRules.ts` (compiler registration), `promptBinding.ts` (prompt, candidate, and tape resolution against compiled manifests and tapes), `TourIndex.tsx`, `TourPage.tsx`, `TourStep.tsx`, `TourBar.tsx`, `TourSheet.tsx`, `tourProgress.ts`, `syllabus.ts`, `mathScan.ts`, `symbolScan.ts`.
- **Routes:** `src/app/tours/page.tsx`, `src/app/tours/[id]/page.tsx`, `src/app/tours/[id]/sheet/page.tsx`, `src/app/tours/full-course/syllabus/page.tsx`.
- **Content:** `content/tours/`.
- **Voice:** reader-progress and completion strings are checked through `checkVoice(text, { context: "reader-progress", source })` from `src/content/checks/voice/index.ts`.
- **Fixtures:** `src/discovery/tours/__fixtures__/` holds a fixture instrument manifest with two predict prompts (each with three candidate ids, one prompt worded with a symbol and one without) and a tape, a fifteen-minute tour over fixture content (including a fixture journey with a move summary and a fixture `physics-math` review record covering its revision), a one-evening tour with two parts, a full course over a six-node fixture foundation graph with one bridge, a fixture essay carrying `transferExamples[]`, and a fixture revisit card.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tour records validate. Unresolved anchors, prompts, presets, tapes, and modes; understated minutes; over-budget tours; math-bearing fifteen-minute steps; instruments that render math or symbol labels in the tour presentation; instrument steps without a prompt; prediction choices that do not match the prompt's candidates; tapes that never touch the prompted control; journey-stage steps that do not cite a move; and missing or, in production, unreviewed move summaries all fail the build with named errors.
- [ ] A cited prompt is rendered through predict mode's verbal-candidate form in the `tour` presentation, and a symbol in its question, labels, or descriptions fails `tour-instrument-renders-symbols` unless a `tourPrediction` replaces it in plain words.
- [ ] `/tours` lists tours by paper and budget with honest totals.
- [ ] `/tours/[id]` walks in-tour and in-reader steps, and returns to the same step after a detour.
- [ ] A fifteen-minute fixture tour shows zero visible math nodes and zero symbol labels at every step, after load and after its prediction interaction, with and without JavaScript; its journey-stage step renders the fixture journey's `move.r0Summary.text` verbatim.
- [ ] A tour prediction records a `prediction` tape event carrying the manifest `promptId` and the chosen `candidateId`.
- [ ] `/tours/[id]/sheet` exists for every compiled tour, is static, works without JavaScript, is linked from the tour page, and has an entry in the route registry of `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6`.
- [ ] Each sheet step prints its question, source passage with printed locator, preset or mode or tape id with a text URL, three candidate labels with ruled space, and the expected explanation, all rendered from the tour and journey records with no second copy.
- [ ] One transfer case is cited by the id of its owning record, from an essay's `transferExamples[]` or a revisit card; a tour with neither omits the section and is listed in the build report.
- [ ] A fifteen-minute tour's sheet contains no visible math node and no symbol label, enforced by the shared measurements, with the failure naming the tour, step and token.
- [ ] The sheet's printed total is the computed estimate, not the budget label.
- [ ] In production and preview, a sheet renders no unreviewed move summary.
- [ ] The sheet prints legibly in monochrome at A4 and Letter, contains no QR code, and carries the solo instruction.
- [ ] No sheet names an external platform, collects data, or requires an account.
- [ ] Progress persists locally and clears; blocked storage does not break the tour.
- [ ] Reader-progress copy passes `checkVoice` in the `reader-progress` context, and this bead defines no vocabulary list of its own.
- [ ] The syllabus generator produces correct prerequisites on the fixture graph, includes the bridge, and prints cleanly.
- [ ] Keyboard, 320 px, reduced motion, and JavaScript-disabled rendering pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- **`src/content/schemas/tour.test.ts`.** Fixture tours of each budget validate. Invalid fixtures each fail with a named error:
  - an unresolved anchor;
  - a fifteen-minute tour with an `in-reader` step, a step at detail 1, `requiresEquations: true`, or 16 total minutes;
  - a reading step with 400 visible words and `estimatedMinutes: 1` (bound 2);
  - a one-evening part of 250 minutes;
  - a full-course session of 130 minutes;
  - a hand-typed prerequisites field;
  - a `tourPrediction` with two choices;
  - a step carrying an authored move-text field (rejected by the closed schema);
  - an `instrumentPreset` with both `presetId` and `tapeId`.
- **`src/discovery/tours/promptBinding.test.ts`,** against the compiled fixture manifest and tape:
  - a fifteen-minute instrument step without `promptId` fails `tour-instrument-step-missing-prompt`;
  - `promptId: "no-such-prompt"` fails `tour-prompt-unresolved` with the id in the message;
  - a `tourPrediction` whose `promptId` differs from the step's fails `tour-prediction-prompt-mismatch`;
  - choices naming two of the three candidate ids plus an unknown id fail `tour-prediction-candidates-mismatch` with the expected ids listed;
  - a tape that never commands the prompt's control fails `tour-tape-does-not-reveal-prompt`;
  - a valid step records `{ type: "prediction", instrumentId, promptId, form: "verbal", payload: { candidateId } }` through the real tape recorder;
  - the fixture prompt whose question contains "γ", cited without `tourPrediction`, fails `tour-instrument-renders-symbols` naming the prompt and the token, and passes once a `tourPrediction` renders it in words;
  - the fixture prompt written in plain words renders through the verbal-candidate form with no `tourPrediction` and passes both measurements.
- **`src/discovery/tours/mathScan.test.ts`,** on fixture fragments:
  - KaTeX in a visible paragraph counts 1, as does a MathML `math` element;
  - KaTeX inside `[hidden]`, inside a closed `<details>`, or inside an `aria-hidden` subtree counts 0;
  - math in an optional disclosure counts 0 and is logged;
  - an element outside `[data-tour-step]` is not counted.
- **`src/discovery/tours/symbolScan.test.ts`,** on fixture fragments with a fixture concordance: "γ = 1.25" flags two tokens; "D" as a table header flags; "diffusion coefficient" does not; "0.8 μm" does not; "x′" flags; a candidate label reading "β" flags; "station A" passes only with an allowlist entry that has a reason, and the allowlist entry without a reason fails.
- **`src/discovery/tours/tourStepContent.test.ts`,** on compiled fixture payloads through the real compiler, including the review-status check of `am-edit-review-records-hofz`:
  - an R0 reading with inline math fails `tour-step-contains-math`;
  - a fixture instrument whose tour-presentation render contains an equation card fails `tour-instrument-renders-math`;
  - a fixture instrument whose tour-presentation table header is a symbol fails `tour-instrument-renders-symbols`;
  - a journey-stage step anchored at a stage that does not make the move fails `tour-journey-stage-not-move`;
  - a fixture journey without `move.r0Summary` fails `tour-move-summary-missing` in the production profile and renders "in preparation" in drafts;
  - a fixture journey whose summary is `draft` fails `tour-move-summary-missing` with the reason "not reviewed" in the production and preview profiles, and renders with the draft marker in the draft profile;
  - a fixture summary marked `reviewed` without a covering `physics-math` review record is rejected by the review-status check; with the fixture record it passes;
  - the passing fixture tour has zero math nodes and zero symbol labels in every step, and its move step's text equals the journey record's summary text byte for byte.
- **`src/discovery/tours/tourSheet.test.tsx`:** from a fixture fifteen-minute tour, the sheet renders every step in order with all five parts; the candidate labels equal the prompt's three candidate ids in order; the explanation text is byte-identical to the journey record's `move.r0Summary.text`; a fixture that adds sheet-authored explanation text fails a static check.
- **`src/discovery/tours/tourSheetMath.test.ts`:** a fixture fifteen-minute tour whose instrument caption renders "γ" fails `tour-sheet-renders-symbols` naming the instrument and the token; the same tour with a `tourPrediction` in plain words passes; a one-evening tour's sheet may contain mathematics and is not scanned.
- **`src/discovery/tours/tourSheetTransfer.test.ts`:** a fixture tour linking an essay with `transferExamples[]` cites the first matching entry by the essay record id and the entry's `domain` key; a tour with no essay link but a revisit card for its paper cites the card by id; a tour with neither omits the section and appears in the build report; an invented transfer case written into the tour record fails the closed schema.
- **`src/discovery/tours/tourSheetTime.test.ts`:** the printed total equals the computed lower-bound total, and a fixture whose record understates its minutes fails with `tour-minutes-understated` before the sheet renders.
- **`src/discovery/tours/tourSheetVoice.test.ts`:** `checkVoice` reports no findings for the shipped sheets, and this bead contributes no vocabulary list (`noParallelDenyLists.test.ts` passes with these files in the scan set).
- **`src/discovery/tours/syllabus.test.ts`,** on a fixture graph where f3 requires f1, f4 requires f1 and f2, f5 requires f4, and f6 requires f3, with session S1 referencing f3 and the bridge b1 and session S2 referencing f5 and f6:
  - S1 lists f1, f3, b1;
  - S2 lists f2, f4, f5, f6 in that order;
  - every prerequisite appears once, before first use;
  - a cross-reference cycle between f5 and f6 is ignored;
  - a prerequisite cycle f1→f2→f1 fails with both ids named;
  - a course that omits b1 lists it as missing.
- **`src/discovery/tours/tourProgress.test.ts`,** with the real storage layer: working, throwing getter, `QuotaExceededError`, and corrupt JSON (quarantined); clearing one tour leaves another; no score fields exist.
- **`src/discovery/tours/TourPage.render.test.tsx`:** the static HTML lists every step with real links, minutes, and purposes; the tour question, choices, and responses sit in a native `<details>`; the completion statement comes last. Every reader-progress string, including the tour bar's "step 3 of 7", is passed to `checkVoice` with `{ context: "reader-progress" }` and returns no findings; a fixture tour bar reading "75% complete" and a fixture completion statement reading "Your streak: 3 days" each return the gate step's `theater` error from the same function. The test defines no vocabulary list of its own, and `noParallelDenyLists.test.ts` in `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` covers this file.

### End-to-end tests

`e2e/tours.spec.ts` through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`:
1. On the fixture fifteen-minute tour, start and step through the R0, first-encounter, instrument, and move-summary steps. Answer the tour prediction. After load and after each interaction, assert zero visible math nodes and zero symbol labels with the shared measurements; read `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, `data-snapshot-version`, and `data-execution-label` from the instrument root; assert that the tape's newest event is the `prediction` event with the fixture `promptId` and chosen `candidateId`.
2. Follow "See this in the paper," confirm the label, and return to the same step.
3. Reload and resume; clear progress.
4. On the fixture one-evening tour, open an in-reader step with the tour bar, detour to a foundation through the return stack, and return to the same step.
5. With JavaScript disabled, the fifteen-minute tour's static page shows all steps with static worked cases, the questions with their responses, the move summary, and zero visible math.
6. Build the fixture tour in the production profile with the fixture journey's summary set to `draft` and assert the build fails with `tour-move-summary-missing` ("not reviewed").
7. Print the fixture syllabus at A4 and Letter.
8. Open `/tours/fifteen-minutes-brownian-motion/sheet`; assert the five parts of each step and the text URL; print it and assert no clipped content at A4 and at Letter in monochrome; with JavaScript disabled assert the full sheet renders; at 320 px assert no horizontal overflow; follow the printed link back to the interactive tour and assert the tour opens at step 1.
9. Repeat the fifteen-minute walk at 320 px, keyboard only, and with reduced motion (animations paused, state shown), and with storage blocked.

Failing lanes retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log; failing print lanes also retain the generated PDF and rendered page images. The `logRunId`s of these lanes are recorded for the reader-review sessions.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/tours/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `tourId`, `budget`, `publicationProfile`, `stepIndex`, `stepKind`, `presentation`, `anchorId`, `detail`, `instrumentId`, `promptId`, `candidateId`, `presetId`, `tapeId`, `modeId`, `mathNodesVisible`, `mathNodesInDisclosures`, `symbolLabelsVisible`, `moveSummaryJourneyId`, `moveSummaryReviewState`, `predictionForm`, `estimatedMinutes`, `minutesLowerBound`, `rule`, `voiceFindings`, `storageState`, `sheetRoute`, `stepCount`, `transferCaseSource` (`essay`, `revisit-card` or `none`), `transferCaseId`, `mathNodesFound`, `symbolTokensFound`, `printedTotalMinutes`, `paperSize`, `jsEnabled`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, and `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- An equation-free tour must still be true; do not trade accuracy for simplicity.
- Do not count hidden readings or collapsed disclosures as visible math, and do not hide math the reader is actually shown.
- Never copy a journey's move summary into a tour record; cite it, so a reviewed change to the journey reaches every tour.
- A tour question that is not the instrument's prompt can be answered by a reveal that settles something else. Bind every question to a `promptId`, and let the tape or preset reach that prompt's reveal.
- A symbol in a table header or in a candidate's label is notation even without KaTeX; the tour presentation speaks in quantity names.
- Never keep a second gamification vocabulary here. Call `checkVoice` so the tour bar and the gate step agree.
- Tours are optional; never gate content behind them.
- A tour prediction is a question with three authored responses, never a quiz with a mark.
- An honest estimate may exceed a label; split the evening into parts rather than understating.
- A draft move summary may be exercised in draft builds and tests, so tour beads can be built before the physics review happens; publication waits for the review.
- A sheet is a projection. The moment it carries authored text of its own it becomes another place where a claim can drift, and the tour and the sheet will disagree the first time a journey's move summary is revised.
- The symbol rule is easy to lose on the sheet: a sheet that prints an instrument's caption verbatim will print the caption's symbols. Render captions through the same plain-word quantity names the `tour` presentation uses.
- Do not add a teacher's answer key beyond the expected explanation the tour already carries. An answer key invites the sheet to become an assessment, which the site does not do.
- Printing a preset as a URL is deliberate: a text URL can be typed, read aloud, and photocopied. A QR code cannot be read by a person and would be the first piece of the site a photocopier destroys.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o`: stable anchors and detail-aware navigation.
- `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`: failure-tolerant local progress.
- `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`: the `Tour` schema this bead extends and the `PredictPrompt` shape the prompt binding reads.
- `am-read-return-stack-oxa`: detours that return to the tour step.
- `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`: R0 readings and the `detail` parameter.
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: in-tour instrument mounting and the additive `tour` presentation with plain-word labels.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: predict mode, prompt ids, candidate ids, and the verbal prediction form.
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`: presets, teaching tapes, and the `prediction` tape event.
- `am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`: the shared first-encounter renderer.
- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: compiled foundation backlinks, prerequisites, and the node and bridge registry for the syllabus.
- `am-plat-print-3orn`: print styles for the syllabus and the sheet.
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: the `Journey` record whose `move.r0Summary` fifteen-minute tours cite.
- `am-edit-review-records-hofz`: the review-status check that decides whether a summary marked `reviewed` is backed by a covering `physics-math` record; the production-profile rule and its fixture test run through that check.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the browser lanes.
- `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`: `checkVoice` and its `reader-progress` context decide the tour bar's, sheet's, and completion statement's copy findings, and that bead's `noParallelDenyLists.test.ts` covers this bead's files, so no gamification vocabulary is kept here.

Real use without an edge: `am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i` (`transferExamples[]`) and `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7` (revisit cards and the three rotating roles) own the transfer cases and roles the sheet cites. Both land after this bead, and the sheet omits the transfer section and lists the tour in the build report when neither record exists, so no edge is added and this batch-C bead never waits for them.
- Blocked by, added as an edge in review: `am-route-canonical-registry-57b6` records the sheet route's canonical and sitemap facts, and its invariant 6 fails the build on a route family with no registry entry, so the entry exists before the sheet ships.

Unblocks: `am-tour-15min-brownian-z034`, `am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`, `am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`, `am-tour-15min-light-quanta-yj70`, `am-tour-evening-and-course-5kcb`.

title: Every equation on /papers/brownian-motion/ renders twice; axe landmark-unique does not catch it
description:
/papers/brownian-motion/ renders each of its three model equations TWICE. Measured on the build at 23d4071:

    data-equation-id total: 6   distinct: 3
       2x eq-model-bm-apparent-speed

title: scrollableRegions ratchet ignores RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING, so a measured non-overflowing region cannot drop its tabIndex
description:
The scrollable-regions ratchet documents RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING as the escape for a
region proven not to overflow, but countUnreachableScrollRegions never reads that map. It
only checks whether an element's className contains an AUDITED_SCROLL_CLASSES entry and
whether the tag has a tabIndex attribute. So a region that has been measured and proven
not to overflow still cannot have its tabIndex removed: the count goes up and the ratchet
fails, and the only lever left is BASELINE, which the test says may only shrink.

Found while measuring all 16 remaining a11y/noNoninteractiveTabindex sites against the
built site (am-6iz4). Concrete case: src/components/lab/lq09/IonizationLab.tsx:654,
className "table-scroll", measured 286/286 scrollWidth/clientWidth at 320x900 and 529/529
at 1280x900 on /lab/lq-09/. It does not overflow, so its tabIndex is a tab stop with
nothing to scroll, exactly what the ratchet's own header warns against - and the ratchet
is what prevents removing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- countUnreachableScrollRegions (or its caller) consults RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING so a
  recorded, measured element is not counted as unreachable when its tabIndex is absent.
- The entry granularity is finer than the class: "table-scroll" covers both overflowing
  and non-overflowing elements, so keying by class alone cannot express the case above.
- A planted negative proves the new path: an element recorded as non-overflowing but
  still carrying tabIndex, or one removed without a record, fails.
- IonizationLab.tsx:654 is recorded with its measurements and its tabIndex removed, and
  both the ratchet and a11y/noNoninteractiveTabindex are green on that file.

TWO GATES DEADLOCKED, AND THE DOCUMENTED WAY OUT IS DEAD CODE (TanElk). This is why CI step 3 has moved slowly, and it is not pane29's doing.

THE DEADLOCK:
  lint/a11y/noNoninteractiveTabindex  says remove tabIndex from a non-interactive element
  the scrollableRegions ratchet       counts that removal as a new unreachable scroll region and fails
  BASELINE                            may only shrink, by the ratchet's own rule

So a region measured and proven NOT to overflow still cannot legitimately drop its tabIndex. Sixteen a11y errors sit behind that.

THE ESCAPE EXISTS IN THE DOCUMENTATION AND NOT IN THE CODE. I verified this independently of pane30's report: RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING appears at src/testing/a11y/scrollableRegions.test.ts lines 21, 52, 170 and 235 - it is exported, typed to hold measurements, described in the header as the escape for a class "verified empirically NOT to overflow", and named in the gate's OWN failure message: "Add tabIndex={0} and an accessible aria-label, or document in RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING with measurements." countUnreachableScrollRegions references it ZERO times.

That is worse than an unimplemented feature. The gate tells you the remedy, you perform it exactly as instructed, and nothing changes - so it reads as your mistake rather than the gate's. A check that cannot be satisfied by following its own instructions is the inverse of the defect class this swarm has been chasing all night: not a check that cannot fail, but one that cannot legitimately pass.

THE EVIDENCE IS MEASURED, not argued. pane30 found it while measuring all sixteen sites against the BUILT site: IonizationLab.tsx:654, className "table-scroll", scrollWidth/clientWidth 286/286 at 320x900 and 529/529 at 1280x900 on /lab/lq-09/. It does not overflow at either viewport, so its tabIndex is a tab stop with nothing to scroll - precisely what the a11y rule exists to remove.

THE FIX MUST NOT BECOME AN RH-1 HOLE. Implementing an escape hatch in a ratchet is exactly where gate self-weakening lives. The requirement, and this swarm has built the same shape twice already: an entry must carry its measurements, and a STALE entry - a region that now DOES overflow - must FAIL. Both halves proven: a measured non-overflowing region may drop its tabIndex, and an overflowing one may not.

pane29 is told to hold the affected sites rather than work around the ratchet, and explicitly not to touch BASELINE.

title: Two table containers scroll with no tab stop, and the a11y ratchet cannot see either
description:
## What is wrong

Two table containers scroll and neither is reachable by keyboard. Their off-screen columns can
be dragged with a pointer and cannot be reached any other way. Measured on build
pxtJgboiQoxEaezRhezpq at a 320px viewport:

```
/foundations/partial-derivatives/  div.thermodynamics-held-fixed-comparison
                                   overflowX=auto  scrolls=true  tabindex=NONE  aria-label=NONE
/foundations/logarithms/           div.construction-table-wrap
                                   overflowX=auto  scrolls=true  tabindex=NONE  aria-label=NONE
```

`scrolls=true` is scrollWidth > clientWidth on the container itself, so these are genuinely
scrollable regions and not merely elements with an overflow property set.

## Why the a11y ratchet is green anyway

src/testing/a11y/scrollableRegions.test.ts matches AUDITED_SCROLL_CLASSES against `className`
occurrences in TSX. Neither container can be seen by it:

- `div.thermodynamics-held-fixed-comparison` scrolls because of
  `div:has(> table.data-table) { overflow-x: auto }` (globals.css, 0b505d9a). The selector
  carries NO class, so there is nothing for a class-based scan to match.
- `construction-table-wrap` has a class and is simply not in AUDITED_SCROLL_CLASSES.

So am-bc6s's green does not mean these regions are reachable. It means they are invisible to it.
The ratchet is honest about what it examines; the gap is that a CSS rule can now create scroll
regions without any TSX class for the scan to key on.

## Why this is the same trade, at scale

8ece778c contained /notation/'s table by wrapping it in .table-scroll and thereby made its
off-screen columns unreachable; central verify caught it and f6f8a9ea repaired it. That was one
element, caught because .table-scroll IS audited. This is the same trade across every overflowing
.data-table container, and the guard cannot report it.

Containing an overflow by letting a region scroll is exactly the move that puts its content out of
keyboard reach. The repair is the pair, always: the container AND a tab stop with a real
accessible name, in the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The two containers above are keyboard reachable with accessible names that say what is in them,
  or are recorded in RECORDED_NON_OVERFLOWING with measurements showing they do not scroll.
- The ratchet can see a scroll region created by CSS with no TSX class. A class-based scan cannot
  do this on its own; the detection has to look at the built pages or at the stylesheets, not only
  at className literals.
- A planted negative proves the new path: a scrolling, unfocusable, class-less container must fail
  it, and a focusable one must not.
- The check names its denominator - how many scrollable containers it examined - so that zero
  found is distinguishable from zero unreachable.

and mine was lucky rather than reasoned.

%31's 93434b3e traced the mechanism on the formula attribute: formulaOverflow.inline.ts marks the
tab stop by t=121ms, React reconciles against markup with no tabindex and removes it by t=215ms,
and the MutationObserver watches childList/subtree so an attribute removal never re-triggers it.

mutations re-ran the observer.

title: Six plan-specified audits exist, can fail, and are unreachable from every runner
description:
# Six plan-specified audits exist, can fail, and are unreachable from every runner

**Type:** task · **Domain:** testing · **Found by:** pane28 on am-muyh, at the orchestrator's request

## The measurement

Asked of every check-shaped script in `scripts/`: does anything BRANCH on its result?

Six do not. They are neither registry steps in `scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts`, nor
referenced in `package.json` scripts, nor invoked by any of the five `.github/workflows`
files, nor by any `*.sh`, nor imported by any test file. `scripts/quality-gates.ts` runs
`QUALITY_GATE_STEPS` and nothing else, so the chain cannot pick them up implicitly.

All six HAVE a failure path (`process.exit` non-zero or `process.exitCode`). They are not
advisory by design. They are unwired.

### Named in the MERGED plan (around line 3938), built to spec, never connected

- `scripts/audit-readings.ts` — R0–R3 present; heuristic R2-length gate with recorded overrides
- `scripts/audit-shelf.ts` — no premise after 1904 in a discovery step unless flagged
- `scripts/audit-instruments.ts` — registry entry, probes, notModeled, tape identity, kernel test,
  action contract, predict mode or exemption
- `scripts/audit-misconceptions.ts`

### Not investigated by the finder

- `scripts/validate-ledger.ts`
- `scripts/verify-constant-sets.ts`

These two are listed for completeness. No claim is made about whether they should run, what
they check, or whether they are waiting on something.

## What this measurement does and does not say

It says: **these six cannot currently fail anything.**

It does NOT say this is wrong. Several may be waiting on a bead, on content that does not
exist yet, or on an owner decision that the finder cannot see. Wiring one in before its
content exists would produce a red gate that teaches people to ignore red gates. Decide per
script, not as a batch.

## A framing correction, recorded so this bead is not misread later

`requiredInCi: false` is NOT the mechanism here, and these six are not `requiredInCi: false`
steps — they are not registry steps at all.

Seven registry steps do carry `requiredInCi: false`: `ubs-diff`, `ubs-staged`, `voice-lint`,
`facsimile-pins`, `perf-budgets`, `resource-stress`, `apple-quality`. Something DOES branch on
those. In `scripts/quality-gates.ts` the run fails whenever `failedCount > 0`, regardless of
`requiredInCi`; the flag only additionally hardens `--all` mode against a required step that
was *not-available* or *skipped* silently passing. So a `requiredInCi: false` step that runs
and fails still fails the chain. Those seven are gated. The six below are not.

## One deliberate advisory step, which must not be changed

`scripts/audit-reachability.ts` is a registry step with no failure path, and that is correct.
`am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih` specifies it: "Do not let the audit become a build gate.
A node missing a countermodel is an authoring queue item, and failing the build on it would
push authors toward stub countermodels." It is in scope for this bead only as a reference
point for what deliberate advisory looks like.

## Method, including an error the finder made and corrected

Scripts matched on `audit-|verify-|check-|lint-|validate-` naming in `scripts/`; 18 found.
Failure path detected by `process.exit(non-zero)` or `process.exitCode = non-zero`. Callers
searched across the gate registry, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/*`, `*.sh`, and every
`*.test.ts|tsx|mjs` under `src/`.

The first pass reported only ONE unwired script, because it counted a script as covered when
a test file merely CONTAINED its name. Five of those hits were string literals inside stubbed
return values in `src/content/audits/verifyContent.test.ts` — mocks naming the audit they
stand in for, not executions of it. Re-measuring on actual module imports took the figure from

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Filed by pane31 on TanElk's ruling while working am-unwired-audits-uwot. Fixed in the same change;
this record exists because the defect was real and should not be invisible in history.

## The defect

`scripts/verify-content.ts` is a registry step and it calls four audits. Two of them were called
with a filter that restricted them to a single item:

    readings      loadLiveReadingsAuditInput(root, { ownerBeadIds: ["am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly"] })
                  1 of 24 owner files in content/editorial/readings-owners/
    instruments   loadLiveInstrumentRows(root, { ids: ["bm-01"] })
                  1 of 38 catalogue ids

Both loaders default to the full population when no filter is passed (`options?.ids ?? CATALOGUE_IDS`;
the readings loader iterates every owner file unless `ownerBeadIds` is given), so the restriction was
deliberate at the call site rather than a limitation of the loaders.

The ruling: this is a defect even if the staging was deliberate, because nothing recorded the
restriction as intentional and nothing failed when the population grew. A twenty-fifth owner file or
a newly built instrument would simply not be audited, and every summary would still say the audit
ran and passed.

That is the same family as am-izth and the am-niyd licence table: no false sentence anywhere, and a
reader concludes the corpus was audited when one item was.

## Measured before the fix

    readings      scoped: 0 errors.  Full population: 23 errors across 3 of 24 owners.
    instruments   scoped: 1 row, ok.  Full catalogue: 38 rows, 83 findings across 34 of 38 ids.
                  Only bm-01, bm-05, sr-02 and me-02 are clean, consistent with AGENTS.md
                  recording that thirty of the thirty-three instruments are unbuilt.

So full population is red for both, and simply widening would have been a red-on-arrival change.

## The fix

Both audits now run over the whole population. Items that cannot pass yet are recorded in a keyed
map with a reason, and the entry expires: if a recorded item stops producing findings, the audit
raises `stale-audit-exemption` naming it, so the entry must be deleted rather than left behind as
stale prose. Same shape as `EXPECTED_UNREACHABLE` in `src/testing/scriptReachability.test.ts`.

Recorded exemptions: 3 readings owners, 34 instruments. 106 findings are now visible as flags that
were previously not computed at all, and audit errors remain 0.

## Planted negatives, both directions

    A. population audited    removed the am-sr-07-field-equations-xxes entry
                             -> ERROR: r3-citation-missing: sr-07 ... and r2-length: sr-07
                             -> audit errors 0 -> 2
    B. reason goes stale     added an entry for bm-01, one of the four clean instruments
                             -> ERROR: stale-audit-exemption: bm-01 is recorded as not yet
                                auditable, but the instruments audit now reports nothing against it
                             -> audit errors 0 -> 1

Both reverted; `shasum -a 256 -c` OK both times; baseline back to 0 audit errors.

## Not changed, deliberately

`shelf` and `misconceptions` still receive empty inputs. `content/historical-premises/` and
`content/misconceptions/` do not exist, so empty is honest there and inventing data would be worse.
Per the same ruling, they were left alone.

## Steps to Reproduce

Before the fix, at any commit where scripts/verify-content.ts passed a filter to either audit:

1. Note the call sites:

       grep -n 'ownerBeadIds: \["am-bm-01' scripts/verify-content.ts
       grep -n 'ids: \["bm-01"\]' scripts/verify-content.ts

2. Count the populations those filters exclude:

       find content/editorial/readings-owners -name '*.yaml' | wc -l     # 24
       # catalogue ids: loadLiveInstrumentRows(root) with no options returns 38 rows

3. Run `bun scripts/verify-content.ts`. The readings and instruments audits report on one item
   each and contribute 0 errors, while 23 readings errors and 83 instrument findings exist in the
   population and are never computed.

4. Add a new owner file or build a new instrument. Nothing changes and nothing fails, because the
   filter names the items to audit rather than the items to skip. That is the defect: the
   restriction is invisible and does not expire.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both audits run over the full population rather than one item.
- [x] Every restriction is recorded with a reason, in a keyed map.
- [x] A recorded reason expires: a listed item that stops failing raises an error naming it.
- [x] Planted negative in both directions, each confirmed red and reverted byte-identically.
- [ ] The 34 instrument exemptions shrink as instruments land. Each entry names its finding count
      at 2026-09-19, so a reviewer can see which are nearly clean.
- [ ] The 3 readings exemptions are resolved by their owning beads.

title: The refusal scanner cannot see a rule code whose value is a conditional, so the site leaves the count
description:
The refusal scanner counts a site from `rule: "literal"`, `code: "literal"` and friends. It does not
see the value when it is a CONDITIONAL over literals, so a site disappears from the coverage
measurement the moment someone makes its code depend on state.

FOUND BY TRIPPING IT MYSELF, which is how it came to notice.

    before am-zqat   scripts/license-inventory/logger.ts   rule: "inventory-complete"
                     1 site, baseline 1, untested

    after  am-zqat   rule: rights.pendingOwnerRuling > 0
                       ? "inventory-complete-with-open-rights-positions"
                       : "inventory-complete",
                     0 sites, so the ratchet's slack pawl demanded the baseline be tightened to 0

The file is not better covered than it was; the site left the scanner's view. Tightening the
baseline on that basis would have recorded an edit as an improvement, which is RH-2 shaped. I
tightened it - 0 IS what the scanner measures today - and wrote the missing assertions anyway, so
the coverage is real whether or not the scanner can see the site.

DIRECTION: fail-open on a coverage measurement. The same file's `block.includes(code)` (am-he9s)
fails open in the other way, crediting coverage that was never asserted. One under-counts sites, the
other over-counts coverage, and both make the ratchet report better than the truth.

SCOPE, measured: `rule:` and `code:` with a conditional value is rare today - this is the only
instance I found in the licence inventory - but the pattern is natural whenever a code varies with
state, which is exactly where a refusal is most worth testing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `rule:`/`code:`/`refusalCode:` property whose value is a conditional expression over string
  literals contributes a site per literal, at that line.
- Planted negative: converting a counted literal site to a conditional does NOT reduce the file's
  site count. The conversion in scripts/license-inventory/logger.ts is the real historical case and
  should be the fixture rather than a synthetic one.
- Other half: a genuinely removed site still reduces the count, so the fix does not make the scanner
  unable to see deletions.
- The baselines are re-measured after the change and any file whose count rises is inspected before
  its baseline is raised: a site returning to view is not a regression.
close_reason: Verified at HEAD, including an independent RH-1 review because the commit bundled scanner, test and baseline together after pane28 had kept them separate all session - and pane28 disclosed the departure rather than letting me find it. The review is clean: 9bcaa4c3 touches exactly three files (refusalScanner.ts, refusalRatchet.test.ts, untestedRefusalsBaseline.json) and neither src/content/editions/editionContract.ts nor src/equations/spoken/spokenFormCheck.ts appears in it, so the two raises - editionContract 0 to 5, spokenFormCheck 2 to 3 - record six pre-existing sites the improved scanner can now see, not debt the commit created. That is the only honest reason to raise a baseline. The stated reason for bundling also holds: baseline numbers are reviewable only beside the change that produced them, and splitting would leave main red between two commits in a shared tree. refusalRatchet 27 pass 0 fail, up from 23. The six newly-visible untested codes were reported and explicitly not absorbed into this bead. Separately, pane28 found bareThrowRatchet red on scripts/prepare-lane.ts and established it was NOT its own doing by restoring the pristine scanner and re-running rather than assuming; that red belongs to d354c065 and is routed to pane30.

title: segmentLedger divides paragraphs on a cue the plate contradicts: a flush-left resumption after a display equation is not a paragraph opening
description:
## The defect

`segmentLedger` treats a line that resumes after a display equation as a new paragraph. On the plate that line is set FLUSH LEFT, which is the 1905 compositor marking a continuation; a paragraph opening is INDENTED.

## Observed case (read from the plate, not inferred)

`public/papers/pdfs/ap-17-549.pdf`, printed p.554 (PDF page 6), rasterised at 200 dpi. Exactly three indented openings on the page:

- `In einer Flüssigkeit seien suspendierte Teilchen regellos…`
- `Es sei v die Anzahl der suspendierten Teilchen…`
- `Die Gleichung (1) benutzen wir…`

The resumptions `Es werde angenommen…`, `Die gesuchte Gleichgewichtsbedingung ist also:` and `Die letzte Gleichung sagt aus…` are all flush left. The segmenter ends its `s3-p2` at the first display equation (`Man hat also: delta F = delta E - T delta S = 0.`) and opens a new paragraph after it, reporting 2 sentences where the printed paragraph carries 6 and runs through five displays.

A second variant on printed p.555 (PDF page 7): five indents, three paragraphs. The two extra indents are the printed list items `1. einer Bewegung … Kraft K,` and `2. eines Diffusionsvorganges … aufzufassen ist.` Item 1 closes with a comma and item 2 with a full stop, so the pair completes one sentence opened on p.554 at `nämlich`. The compositor sets a numbered list item at paragraph depth, so indentation alone does not separate the two cases.

## Scale and bound

Over `ap-17-549` the segmenter emits 50 paragraphs against the plate-read manifest 32. It has ZERO non-test call sites, and so does its producer `segmentSentences` - the only non-test references are an import of `SENTENCE_ABBREVIATIONS` in `tokenizeGerman.ts:7` and two re-export lines in `segmentLedger.ts`. This is a latent defect in an unused component, not a live corruption.

## Not this bead

Nothing here is a claim about the manifest. The plate adjudication (am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg comment 1437) found the manifest division correct on all three sampled paragraphs and the freeze sound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The divider distinguishes an indented paragraph opening from a flush-left resumption after a display equation, or states in code why it cannot from a machine draft that may not preserve indentation.
- A fixture built from the p.554 case: the paragraph beginning `Es sei v die Anzahl` remains ONE paragraph across its five display equations. The fixture fails when the fix is reverted.
- A fixture for the p.555 numbered-list case: items `1.` and `2.` do not become paragraphs.
- The fix does not renumber or otherwise touch any frozen id.
