title: searchPalette browser check 10 times out: Chromium force-cache retains the corrupt shard body
description:
scripts/e2e/searchPalette.mjs check 10 (corrupt shard retry, around line 258) times out. Reported by SwiftForge while working am-xrel and confirmed unrelated to that bead - it is not a dialog-scoping problem and was explicitly NOT carried as evidence when am-xrel closed.

Observed: the retry path fetches a shard whose body is the literal string "invalid" and which is served 200 OK. The fetch uses `cache: "force-cache"`, so Chromium retains the corrupt 200 response and the subsequent retry never re-reaches the network. The check then waits for a recovery that cannot arrive.

## Why it matters

It is the only remaining known failure in the search browser lane, and a retry path that cannot actually retry is a real product weakness, not only a test problem: a reader who hits one corrupt shard would stay stuck on it for the life of the cache entry.

## Acceptance

1. Decide and record which side is wrong: the product retry (should it bypass or bust the cache on a failed parse?) or the test (is force-cache the wrong fixture for this scenario?). Name the decision and why.
2. If the product is wrong: the retry must be able to obtain a fresh response after a corrupt one. A negative that a naive fix would fail - a corrupt shard followed by a good one must recover WITHOUT disabling caching for healthy shards, since blanket no-store would silently cost every reader the cache.
3. scripts/e2e/searchPalette.mjs check 10 passes end to end, with the assertion unchanged in meaning.
4. Do not fix by deleting or skipping the check.

## No-claim

Green here proves one corrupt-shard scenario recovers. It says nothing about partial or truncated responses, which are a different failure mode.

## Provenance

Reported by SwiftForge 2026-09-17 during am-xrel; recorded by orchestrator TanElk rather than folded into that close, because a failure a bead did not cause is not that bead evidence.
close_reason:
Closed by orchestrator TanElk at 3428f1e. All four acceptance criteria verified by re-execution.

AC1, which side was wrong: the PRODUCT, and the fix is there. efb86d2 touches only src/search/loadIndex.ts and src/search/loadIndex.test.mjs. The retry path now takes a forceReload flag and issues cache: 'reload' instead of 'force-cache', with the comment naming the condition: a cached response under force-cache was corrupt or poisoned in browser cache. Normal loads still use force-cache.

AC2, the negative I required - recovery must not come at the cost of caching healthy shards: satisfied by construction. force-cache remains the default path and 'reload' is used only when hasFailed is set, so a corrupt shard followed by a good one recovers without disabling caching generally. loadIndex.test.mjs adds 45 lines covering it.

AC3: bun run test:search:browser -> exit 0 against the served build at this revision. The corrupt-shard check survives at scripts/e2e/searchPalette.mjs:248, 'corrupt shard produces a recoverable error, never partial results', driving the real fixture that serves the literal body 'invalid' for /search/s-* and then clicking 'Retry loading search'.

AC4, not fixed by deleting or skipping the check: scripts/e2e/searchPalette.mjs was NOT modified by efb86d2 at all - git log shows its last change is 9a12d56 (am-xrel, dialog scoping). 26 assert lines remain and there are zero .skip/.only/xit tokens in the file. The test was left exactly as it was and the product changed to satisfy it.

Also re-executed: bun test --isolate --timeout 60000 src/search -> 54 pass, 0 fail across 5 files.

Central verify at this revision: gates 20/20 PASSED, typecheck rc=0, test:node 188 pass 0 fail.

No-claim: this proves one corrupt-shard scenario recovers. It says nothing about partial or truncated responses, which are a different failure mode, as the bead already recorded.

title: dcg false positive: a guard cannot tell a command from a description of one
description:
Reported by pane %29 on 2026-09-19 while working am-uxh9. This is a report about the dcg tool (v0.5.2 at ~/.local/bin/dcg), not about this repository. Filed here because dcg has no local checkout, no config file and no issue tracker I could find, and this is the surface its owner reads.

WHAT HAPPENED

dcg blocked a `br comments add` command. No destructive operation was in it. The command was posting a bead comment whose PROSE contained the words of a git command I had tried and abandoned:

  "I also tried to revert with git checkout -- and the dcg guard blocked it..."

The guard matched the literal substring inside the quoted comment body and refused the whole command with rule core.git:checkout-discard. The blocked command's actual verb was `br comments add`.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN WORKING AROUND

The guard had just worked correctly one step earlier: it blocked a real `git checkout -- <path>` I reached for, and it was right - I reversed my own edit with a targeted rewrite instead, which is recoverable. So the same session contains one true positive and one false positive from one rule.

The false positive's cost is specific. I wanted to record, in the permanent bead history, that a guard had stopped me doing something unsafe. The guard prevented me from writing that down. An agent in a hurry learns to omit the sentence, or to obfuscate it, and the incident stops being recorded - which is the opposite of what a guard is for. A guard that cannot distinguish a command from a description of a command trains people to route around it, and a routed-around guard is a dead one.

I did not override it. I reworded the prose and the comment posted.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION, not a prescription

The discriminator is available without parsing English: the matched text was inside a quoted argument to a different program, not in command position. A rule that fires only when the dangerous token is the command being invoked - or at minimum, not when it sits inside a quoted string argument of an unrelated binary - would keep every true positive in this session and drop the false one. If that is hard to do safely, a narrower fallback is to skip the scan for a small allowlist of known-inert verbs (br comments add, gh issue comment, git commit -m) where the payload is always prose.

REPRODUCTION

  br comments add <some-bead> "text containing the two words git checkout followed by two hyphens"

Blocked, rule core.git:checkout-discard, with the full comment body echoed in the refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A command whose dangerous token appears only inside a quoted argument to an unrelated binary is not blocked.
- [ ] The true positive still fires: a bare destructive git invocation is still refused.
- [ ] A test covers both, so the two cannot be confused again.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Live reproduction from pane31, 2026-09-19, if a concrete instance helps this bead.

The blocked command was a plain two-path commit using a heredoc message.
Rule fired: core.git:restore-worktree.

No such git subcommand appeared in the command. The matched token was inside the COMMIT MESSAGE
BODY, describing what I had already done to a scratch copy of a file. The heredoc payload is
prose, not argv.

The identical message passed via -F <file> instead of -F - succeeded immediately (commit
6cef6d18), which isolates the cause to the message text sitting on the command line rather than
to anything the command does.

It then happened a second time, filing this very comment: the comment text quotes the rule and
the trigger word, so the guard blocked the bead comment describing the guard. Passing the same
text through `br comments add -f <file>` worked.

Cost was two retries, so low severity. Worth noting is the incentive it creates: the obvious
workaround is to stop naming destructive-sounding verbs in commit messages and bead comments,
and this repo's evidence discipline wants exactly the opposite. A message stating that a file was
put back byte-identically, with its digest, is the audit trail AGENTS.md asks for.

Suggested discrimination if it helps: argv position. A token is a command only in command
position; text after -m, inside a heredoc body, or after -F is payload.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Black-box characterisation by pane31, 2026-09-19, answering "does it match message bodies and
heredoc text, and what is the narrowest fix". dcg is an 18 MB stripped Mach-O binary at
~/.local/bin/dcg with no local source, so this is measured from outside rather than read off the
code. Every probe was harmless if it executed.

I hit this rule twice today before probing: once on a commit whose MESSAGE described a file I had
already put back, and once on the bead comment describing that block. Writing this comment was
blocked a third time, which produced the most useful evidence of the lot.

THE MATRIX. Rule throughout: core.git:restore-worktree. The dangerous token is spelled r-e-s-t-o-r-e
and I write it as RST below where quoting it would re-trip the guard.

   1  echo "... git checkout -- somefile"                                 ALLOWED
   2  echo "... the phrase git RST inside a quoted argument"              ALLOWED
   3  cat <<EOF ... the source RSTd byte-identically ... EOF              ALLOWED
   4  git status --porcelain && cat <<EOF ... RSTd ... EOF                ALLOWED
   5  git status --porcelain && cat <<EOF ... to RST typecheck ... EOF    ALLOWED
   6  echo "... git add <paths> && git commit -F - ... git RST ..."       ALLOWED
   7  git add -n <path> && cat <<EOF ... git RST <path> ... EOF           ALLOWED
   8  git commit --dry-run -F - <<EOF ... to RST typecheck ... EOF        BLOCKED
   9  git commit --dry-run -F - <<EOF ... put back ... RSTd ... EOF       ALLOWED
  10  git commit --dry-run -F - <<EOF ... exists to RST the lane ... EOF  BLOCKED
  11  cat > file.txt <<EOF ... <this comment's own text> ... EOF          BLOCKED

FIRST CONCLUSION: IT IS NOT NAIVE SUBSTRING MATCHING
Probes 1, 2 and 6 put the full phrase "git RST", and in 6 a complete "git add ... && git commit
-F -" sequence, inside a quoted argument to echo, and all passed. The original report's "matched
the literal substring" is close but not exact, and the difference is what makes a narrow fix
possible.

SECOND CONCLUSION: THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT DETECTORS, AND THEY FAIL DIFFERENTLY
They can be told apart by the reason line dcg prints.

Detector A, word-level, over a git command's own message payload. Probes 8 and 10 block with the
plain reason "git RST discards uncommitted changes". In probe 10 the matched word is neither
preceded by "git" nor followed by a path: the sentence is "this change exists to RST the typecheck
lane to green". Probe 9 proves it is the bare infinitive that matters, since "RSTd" passes. So
inside a commit message dcg is matching one English word.

Detector B, line-level, parsing heredoc bodies as embedded shell. Probe 11 is this very comment,
and it blocked with a different and much more informative reason:

    Embedded shell command blocked: git RST discards uncommitted changes. (line 1 of heredoc)

That detector parses heredoc content as commands and reports a heredoc line number. It is closer to
being right: probe 7 carries "git RST <path>" mid-sentence in a heredoc and passes, because the
line's first token is "PROBE". What tripped probe 11 is that the matrix above contains lines whose
first token is "git". In other words detector B already does roughly the command-position matching
that the question asks about, and the residual false positive is that a documentation table of
commands is indistinguishable from commands.

Note also that probe 11 names "line 1 of heredoc", which is prose containing no git at all. Line 1
ends mid-quote, the closing quote falling on line 2, so the reported line number is probably an
artifact of an unbalanced quote joining lines during tokenisation. Whoever fixes this should not
trust that line number without checking.

THE NARROWEST FIX

"Exclude quoted argument text" does NOT fix the reported defect. A heredoc body is not a quoted
argument, and probes 8, 10 and 11 are all heredocs. It would have fixed my second incident, a
quoted argument to br comments add, and neither of the other two.

"Match only the command position" fixes detector A completely and is right in principle: RST is
dangerous as a git subcommand, not as an English verb. Detector B already approximates it.

Narrower still, and the thing I would do first, because it is one flag list and no shell grammar:
STOP SCANNING THE MESSAGE PAYLOAD. Git states exactly where the message is, and those regions are
definitionally data, not commands:

    -m <msg>    --message=<msg>    -F <file>    --file=<file>    -F - with its heredoc or stdin

That kills detector A's false positives outright, fixes probes 8 and 10 and both of my real
incidents, and costs no coverage anywhere, because no indirect invocation such as bash -c, xargs or
find -exec lives inside a commit message payload.

RECOMMENDED ORDER
  1. Exclude the message payload of -m/--message/-F/--file including heredoc-fed stdin. Surgical,
     no coverage loss. This is detector A.
  2. For detector B, keep parsing heredoc lines but require the git invocation to be in command
     position on that line, which it nearly does already. Consider not scanning heredocs that feed
     a plainly non-executing sink such as cat > file.
  3. Do not stop at excluding quoted arguments; it misses every case that actually occurred.

WHY THE INCENTIVE MATTERS HERE
AGENTS.md requires recording the exact command run and the authorising text whenever a destructive
operation happens, and evidence discipline in this swarm means writing "the file was put back
byte-identically, md5 ..." into commit messages and bead comments. The guard currently makes the
honest sentence the expensive one. I reworded twice and resorted to a non-shell file write once,
rather than override, but an agent in a hurry learns to omit the sentence.

A FALSE-NEGATIVE CAUTION, not a finding
Probes 1, 2 and 6 show a quoted argument carrying a full git command is not inspected. I did NOT
test whether a genuinely destructive nested invocation such as bash -c with a git RST inside is
caught, because doing that safely needs a throwaway checkout and I had none. That should be tested
before anything is narrowed, so a fix does not widen a gap that already exists.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
pane31: the false-negative question I raised is now ANSWERED, and the answer changes the
recommendation. Tested, not reasoned.

THE OPEN QUESTION I LEFT: "a quoted argument carrying a full git command is not inspected. I did
NOT test whether a genuinely destructive nested invocation such as bash -c with a git restore
inside is caught, because doing so safely needs a throwaway checkout and I had none. That should be
tested before anything is narrowed, so a fix does not widen a gap that already exists."

THE TEST. Built a throwaway git repo outside this project, committed a file, then modified it so
there was real uncommitted work to destroy, and ran the destructive command nested in a quoted
argument:

    bash -c "git restore f.txt"

    -> BLOCKED. "Embedded shell command blocked: git restore discards uncommitted changes."
       Rule core.git:restore-worktree.

The uncommitted modification survived. dcg DOES inspect commands nested inside a quoted argument to
a shell, so the gap I was worried about is not there.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE FIX. My earlier recommendation warned that "match only the command
position" would cost coverage of bash -c, xargs and find -exec, which substring matching catches
today by accident. That warning is now weaker than I thought, because the coverage does not come
from substring matching: a separate detector recognises the nested command as a command. Narrowing
the message-payload matcher therefore does NOT remove bash -c coverage, because a different
mechanism provides it.

So the recommendation stands and is now safer than when I made it:

    1. Stop scanning the message payload of -m/--message/-F/--file including heredoc-fed stdin.
       Surgical, one flag list, and now demonstrably no coverage loss for nested commands.
    2. Then consider command-position matching for the line-level detector.
    3. Do not stop at excluding quoted argument text; it misses every case that actually occurred.

A DISCRIMINATION dcg ALREADY MAKES, which I had not credited it with:

    echo "... the phrase git restore inside a quoted argument"     ALLOWED
    bash -c "git restore f.txt"                                    BLOCKED

Both are a quoted argument containing the same two words. dcg distinguishes prose passed to a
harmless command from a command passed to a shell. That is the right distinction and it is already
implemented; the residual false positives are narrower than my first characterisation implied.

THE LOCATION LABEL IS STILL WRONG, and this run is cleaner evidence than my earlier one. The
blocked command contained no heredoc at all, and dcg still reported "(line 1 of heredoc)". Whoever
fixes this should not trust that field; it was misreporting in my earlier case too, where I guessed
an unbalanced quote was joining lines, and here there is no heredoc to misparse.

HOUSEKEEPING: the throwaway repo is at a mktemp path outside this project and I have NOT deleted
it, per the no-deletion rule. It holds one file and no history worth keeping; say the word and I
will remove it, or leave it to the OS temp reaper.

title: GuidedTourTrail reads useSearchParams during prerender: two BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING boundaries on every exported page (fix written and parked)
description:
GuidedTourTrail (src/discovery/tours/GuidedTourTrail.tsx) calls useSearchParams during render. The root layout mounts it twice, so every statically exported page carries two `<!--$!--><template data-dgst="BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING">` boundaries that the client renders from scratch. The query cannot be known at build time anyway. Found in dispatch 171 (hunting React #418); dev fuzz showed it is NOT the #418 cause (removing its Suspense still gave 3/100), so this is hygiene, not the P0.

## Evidence (GreenOx, dispatch 180, 2026-09-25)
- The fix is written and works: render nothing until mounted, then read the query in an inner component. 13 lines, component only; the layout's two Suspense wrappers can stay. Parked copies (NOT in the tree):
  - `$S/rm180/parked-trail/GuidedTourTrail.fixed.tsx` and `GuidedTourTrail.fix.diff` (the component was clean vs HEAD ebdc8a54-era when edited)
  - `$S/rm180/parked-trail/guidedTourTrail.prerender.test.tsx`
  - where `$S` = /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jemanuel-projects-annus-mirabilis-com/f25c8891-9df0-48a1-9ce9-f79bc4ac345e/scratchpad
- The test drives Next's real bailout, not a mock. `useSearchParams` bails out only when `window` is undefined and a `workUnitAsyncStorage` store of type "prerender" is active. So the test server-renders before installDom, inside `workUnitAsyncStorage.run({type:"prerender"})`, and asserts no `<!--$!-->`. A control component that reads the query during render must produce `<!--$!-->`. Then it hydrates with `?tour=not-in-the-catalogue...` and asserts no recoverable error and that `[data-tour-error]` appears after mount.
  - Run alone, unfixed: 1 pass 2 fail (control passes; both trail tests red).
  - Run alone, fixed: 3 pass 0 fail.

## Why it is parked, exactly
The test is ORDER-DEPENDENT in a multi-file bun run: `bun test src/testing/rootLayoutHydration.test.tsx src/discovery/tours/timedTour.test.tsx <trail test>` gives 10 pass 3 fail, in either order, and all 3 failures are the trail test's. Next creates its AsyncLocalStorage instances when its modules load (`next/dist/server/app-render/async-local-storage.js` reads `globalThis.AsyncLocalStorage` once, at load); without the global it creates a stand-in whose run() throws "Invariant: AsyncLocalStorage accessed in runtime where it is not available". Bun shares one module cache across files, and another file loads next/navigation first, so the test file's own `globalThis.AsyncLocalStorage ??= AsyncLocalStorage` before its dynamic imports comes too late. The control fails loudly (not vacuously), but committed as is it would turn the lane red.

## Next step
Set `globalThis.AsyncLocalStorage` (from node:async_hooks) before any test file loads, as Next's server runtime does: a bun preload in bunfig.toml. That is a test-infra change and commits ALONE, first. Then drop the test's own `??=` line (keep the dynamic imports or make them static), rerun the mixed three-file command above plus the file alone (expect 13/13 and 3/3), rerun it red against the unfixed component, then commit the component and test together. Alternatively, move the test to the node lane if a fresh process per file is available there; it is .tsx, so check that the node lane can run it first. After it lands, confirm on an export that `grep -c BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING out/index.html` goes from 2 to 0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- An exported page's HTML contains no BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING template from the tour trail (count before and after, on a built export).
- A test that prerenders the trail through Next's own bailout path, with a positive control, is red before the fix and green after, alone AND in a multi-file run.
- A tour link (`?tour=...`) still shows the guide after mount, with no recoverable hydration error.

title: Confirm every adversarial fixture fails for its intended reason
description:
# Confirm every adversarial fixture fails for its intended reason

**Epic:** `am-ep-verification-pxc` · **Batch:** I · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** verification · **Plan sections:** §13.5, §6.6 (meaning survives representation), §8.1–8.4, §12.6, §12.10 (traceability only)

## Background

Adversarial fixtures are deliberately plausible wrong results. Each targets a likely implementation or explanatory error that would look fine in a demo: halving diffusivity "halves displacement," a light packet "contracts like a rod," a large seed "fits in JSON." A fixture only has value if it fails for the intended reason when the wrong computation is used and passes when the right one is. This closure audit proves all fifteen do, with one row corrected from the plan.

## Scope

In scope: for each row, a named wrong computation kept inside tests (never shipped), the correct owner call, assertions that the wrong one fails the specified check and the correct one passes, browser checks for the two runtime rows, and a generated report.

Out of scope: writing the underlying evaluators and their own adversarial scenarios (owner beads); the misconception prose (paper beads), although the report cross-links matching misconception entries where they exist.

## Requirements

For each row: implement the plausible wrong computation as a clearly named test-only function (`wrong<Row>` in `src/testing/adversarial/`), run the specified check against both it and the owner, assert that the wrong one fails on the named assertion and the owner passes, and log both.

1. **Half the diffusivity means half the displacement** (`am-ref-diffusion-lr3`). Halving $D$ scales RMS displacement by $1/\sqrt{2} \approx 0.7071$, not 0.5; compare diffusivity scaling and RMS scaling separately.
2. **A radial distribution is an ordinary Gaussian** (`am-ref-diffusion-lr3`). With $p_r(r,t) = \frac{r}{2Dt}e^{-r^2/(4Dt)}$: normalization over $r \ge 0$, $\langle r^2\rangle = 4Dt$, $\langle r\rangle = \sqrt{\pi D t}$; the naive Gaussian in $r$ fails normalization and both moments.
3. **Camera noise leaves neighboring increments independent** (`am-ref-inference-2w9`). Neighboring measured increments have covariance $-\sigma^2$ (and $DT_e/3 - \sigma^2$ with uniform exposure $T_e$).
4. **An unbiased estimate stays unbiased after inversion** (`am-ref-inference-2w9`). $\mathbb{E}[C/\widehat{D}] = N\,q/(q-2)$ for $q > 2$ (1.25 at $q = 10$); the transformed interval is asymmetric.
5. **An arbitrary entropy-density constant cancels** (`am-ref-radiation-15c`). Retaining $C(\nu)$ adds $\Delta\nu\,C(\nu)(V - V_0)$ at fixed energy and band.
6. **A spectral-axis relabeling preserves density** (`am-ref-radiation-15c`). Matching band energies require $u_\lambda = u_\nu\,c/\lambda^2$; peaks do not correspond by substituting $\lambda = c/\nu$.
7. **A light complex contracts like material volume** (`am-ref-waves-r53`), **corrected fixture.** The plan says to test a transverse ray, but for a ray transverse in the unprimed frame ($\varphi = 90^\circ$) $q = \gamma(1 - \beta\cos\varphi) = \gamma$ and the packet-volume factor $1/q = 1/\gamma$ equals material contraction, so that case cannot expose the error. At $\beta = 0.6$ use $\varphi = 0$ ($1/q = 2$), $\varphi = \pi$ ($1/q = 0.5$), and $\cos\varphi = \beta$, the ray transverse in the moving frame ($1/q = \gamma = 1.25$), each against $1/\gamma = 0.8$. Keep $\varphi = 90^\circ$ as a documented coincidence check.
8. **Forces have equal numerical components in different frames** (`am-ref-electron-kfy`). At $\beta = 0.6$ the source-convention transverse coefficient is $1.5625m$ and the laboratory coefficient $1.25m$.
9. **Changing observer means starting a new experiment** (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`). After an observer change, event, worldline, and run identities are unchanged; the wrong implementation (a frame slider as `setup-change`) fails on `runId` and the event digest.
10. **A moving mirror receives the fixed-surface incident power** (`am-ref-waves-r53`). Intercepted power $IA_m(1 - \beta)$, reflected power, and mechanical work $Fv$ balance together; $IA_m$ does not.
11. **The low-speed proxy is the exact mass coefficient at every speed** (`am-ref-mass-energy-ht0`). At $v = 0.6c$ the proxy $2L(\gamma - 1)/v^2$ equals about $1.389\,L/c^2$; it approaches $L/c^2$ only as $v \to 0$, with excess about $\tfrac34(v/c)^2$.
12. **A large seed can be carried as a JSON number** (`am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`). `9007199254740993` survives canonical string transport; as a JSON number it becomes `9007199254740992`, a different stream.
13. **Radius = 1 μm reproduces Einstein's 0.8 μm** (`am-ref-diffusion-lr3`). With Einstein's printed constants only $a = 0.5\,\mu$m gives about 0.795 μm at 1 s; $a = 1\,\mu$m gives about 0.562 μm (0.561 μm with the modern $k_B$).
14. **The locked-position probability is $f^n$** (`am-ref-radiation-15c`). For $n$ perfectly locked, uniformly located positions the probability that all lie in fraction $f$ is $f$.
15. **A neutral conductor with current violates $|J/\rho| < c$** (`am-ref-fields-6l9`). The case is accepted.

Generate `docs/audits/ADVERSARIAL_AUDIT.md` with each row's wrong computation name, failing assertion id, owner result, evidence paths, and any linked misconception entry.

## Technical Approach

`scripts/audit-adversarial.ts` runs the registry's `adversarial` scenarios plus the paired wrong-computation tests in `src/testing/adversarial/`, and writes the report. The browser checks for rows 9 and 12 run as the `adversarial-runtime` suite in `scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All fifteen rows exist as adversarial scenarios with paired wrong computations.
- [ ] Every wrong computation fails on its declared assertion (not on a type error or another check), and every owner passes.
- [ ] Row 7 uses the corrected discriminating fixtures and documents the $\varphi = 90^\circ$ coincidence.
- [ ] No wrong computation is importable from production code (import scan).
- [ ] The browser checks for rows 9 and 12 pass.
- [ ] The report is attached to launch readiness evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `src/testing/adversarial/*.test.ts`: one file per row with wrong and right paths, each asserting the specific failing check id.
- `adversarialImports.test.ts`: production code never imports test-only wrong computations.

### End-to-end tests
- The `adversarial-runtime` suite in the harness's desktop and WebKit lanes: an observer change on SR-03 keeps `data-run-id` and the event digest; a BM-01 permalink with seed `9007199254740993` reproduces its latent digest after reload and differs from `9007199254740992`.

### Structured logging
Through the shared logger, suite `adversarial`, file `artifacts/test-logs/adversarial/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-ver-adversarial-audit-1ef`), `seed` (canonical decimal string), `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and for the browser rows `paper`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId` (the experiment realization read from `data-run-id`), `snapshotVersion`, `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, and `jsEnabled`; in `extra`: `row`, `scenarioId`, `constantSetId`, `wrongComputation`, `failingAssertion`, `wrongResult`, `ownerResult`, `status`.

A row that does not behave as specified (the wrong computation passes, fails on a different assertion, or the owner fails) retains, under `artifacts/test-logs/adversarial/<log-run-id>/failures/row-<n>.json`, both results at full precision, the assertion ids that fired, the constant set, and a one-line reproduction command, and its record names that path. Failing browser rows retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A fixture that fails for a different reason than intended (for example a type error) proves nothing; assert the specific failing check.
- Keep wrong computations obviously named and isolated so they never become fallbacks.
- Rows that use Einstein's numbers declare their constant set, so a constant-set mix-up cannot pass as an adversarial success.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`: adversarial scenario format and runner.
- `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`, `am-ref-inference-2w9`, `am-ref-radiation-15c`, `am-ref-waves-r53`, `am-ref-electron-kfy`, `am-ref-mass-energy-ht0`, `am-ref-fields-6l9`: owners for the physics rows.
- `am-rt-command-classes-dzp` and `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`: owners for the runtime rows.
- `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i` and `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`: the instruments for the browser checks of rows 9 and 12.

Unblocks:
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`.

title: Confirm every historical fixture and golden scenario exists, is labeled by kind, and passes
description:
# Confirm every historical fixture and golden scenario exists, is labeled by kind, and passes

**Epic:** `am-ep-verification-pxc` · **Batch:** I · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** verification · **Plan sections:** §13.3, §13.1, §10.1, §21 ("the computation is real and bounded") (traceability only)

## Background

The plan's fixture table is the public face of the site's numerical honesty: Einstein's printed numbers become regression fixtures, and modern golden scenarios check the plumbing. Individual evaluator beads write these scenarios; this closure audit proves the whole table is present, correctly labeled, run against the right owners with the right constant sets, and passing before launch. It also checks that readers see the right kind of label wherever a fixture appears.

Several corrections and transcription decisions apply to the plan's table, and the audit enforces each one:

- **Mean displacement.** The row's "6.1 μm" is the modern-$k_B$ value (6.146687 μm) at two significant figures. With the constants Einstein used the value is 6.156365 μm, which is 6.2 μm at two figures and 6.16 μm at three, printed "ca. 6 Mikron". Every displayed number names its constant set.
- **Molecular dimensions.** The plan's two values cannot come from one data set. Einstein prints $k$ for the viscosity itself ($k^* = k(1 + \varphi)$), so this bead calls the other number the coefficient of $\varphi$ (the code parameter `factor`). $N$ scales as the square root of that coefficient, so changing it from 1 to 5/2 alone multiplies $N$ by $\sqrt{2.5} \approx 1.5811$ ($2.1 \times 1.5811 \approx 3.3$, not 6.6). The record involves three printings: the 1905 thesis (about $2.1\times10^{23}$ with coefficient 1), the 1906 *Annalen* version's supplement with improved data (about $4.15\times10^{23}$ with coefficient 1), and the 1911 correction (about $6.56\times10^{23}$ with coefficient 5/2). Since $4.15 \times 1.5811 \approx 6.56$, the 1911 value appears to reuse the 1906 supplement's inputs (verify on `ap-34-591`).
- **Avogadro from Planck.** A comparison witness prints $\alpha = 6.1\cdot10^{-56}$, which gives $6.17\times10^{22}$; only $6.10\times10^{-57}$ (Planck's 1901 $h$ and $k$) reproduces the printed $N = 6.17\times10^{23}$. $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ and $L = 3\times10^{10}$ appear not to be printed in §2, so they are editorial inputs.
- **Stopping potential.** The 4.3 V fixture follows the printed representation: the gram-equivalent charge $E = 9.6\times10^{3}$ in electromagnetic CGS units, with $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ read as volts (4.338 V). The esu and statvolt computation (4.306 V) is a documented modern restatement.
- **Precision.** "Within rounding" is not a criterion until each row says which precision it means.

## Scope

In scope: a coverage audit over `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3` for all fifteen §13.3 rows (the molecular-dimensions row as three fixtures); value, constant-set, transcription, editorial-input, representation, and tolerance verification; cross-owner runs where FrankenSim owners exist; label checks in the rendered site; a generated report.

Out of scope: writing the scenarios (evaluator beads) and the adversarial rows (`am-ver-adversarial-audit-1ef`).

## Requirements

1. **Rows and expected results.** Each must exist with kind, constant set, units, equations, owner, tolerance, comparison kind, transcription status, and, for historical rows, editorial inputs and printed representation.

| Row | Input | Expected | Kind | Owner bead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Avogadro from Planck | Planck's $\alpha = 6.10\times10^{-57}$ and $\beta = 4.866\times10^{-11}$ as printed in paper 1 §2 (CGS); $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ and $L = 3\times10^{10}$ as declared editorial inputs | $N = \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\frac{8\pi R}{L^3} = 6.17\times10^{23}$ to three significant figures (full $6.170486\times10^{23}$); sensitivity $6.1858\times10^{23}$ with $R = 8.314\times10^{7}$ and $L = 2.998\times10^{10}$ | Historical | `am-ref-radiation-15c` |
| Stopping potential magnitude | $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, $P' = 0$, printed representation $\Pi E = R\beta\nu - P'$ with $E = 9.6\times10^{3}$ (gram-equivalent charge, electromagnetic CGS) and $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ in volts; documented alternative $\Pi\varepsilon = (R/N)\beta\nu - P$ in esu and statvolts | about 4.3 V (two significant figures; full 4.338 V, slope $4.212\times10^{-15}$ V·s); the restatement gives 4.306 V (4.309 V at 300 V per statvolt) | Historical | `am-ref-photoelectric-q6r` |
| Mean displacement | $a = 0.5\,\mu$m, $\eta = 1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s, $T = 290.15$ K (the site's conversion of 17 °C), $t = 1$ s and 60 s; $N = 6\times10^{23}$ and the viscosity $k$ as printed in paper 2 §5; $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ as a declared editorial input | 0.795 μm and 6.16 μm under `einstein-1905-brownian-printed` (full 0.7947833 and 6.156365 μm; 0.7946 and 6.155 μm at 290 K); 0.794 and 6.15 μm under `modern-si-2019` with the printed viscosity (0.7935339 and 6.146687 μm); printed "0,8 Mikron" and "ca. 6 Mikron" (one significant figure) | Historical | `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` |
| Molecular dimensions | three printings, each with its own transcribed inputs and constant set: `suspension-einstein-1905-thesis` on `einstein-1905-thesis-printed` (coefficient of $\varphi$ equal to 1); `suspension-einstein-1906-supplement` on `einstein-1906-dissertation-printed` (coefficient 1); `suspension-einstein-1911-correction` on `einstein-1911-correction-printed` (coefficient 5/2) | about $2.1\times10^{23}$, about $4.15\times10^{23}$, and about $6.56\times10^{23}$ | Historical (three fixtures) | `am-ref-viscosity-suspension-c9lp` |
| Photoelectric neutral | $\Phi = 2$ eV (hypothetical), 600 THz | $K_{\max} \approx 0.4814$ eV; threshold $\approx 483.6$ THz | Modern golden | `am-ref-photoelectric-q6r` |
| Brownian baseline | $T = 293.15$ K, $\eta = 1.000$ mPa·s, $a = 0.500\,\mu$m | $D = 0.4294396\,\mu$m²/s; RMS 0.9267573 μm at 1 s, 2.9306640 μm at 10 s | Modern golden | `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` |
| Boost | $v/c = 0.6$ | $\gamma = 1.25$; $\det = 1$; eigenvalues 2 and 0.5; events 10 ls apart and simultaneous map to $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s, $\Delta x' = 12.5$ ls | Modern golden | `am-ref-kinematics-tjq` |
| Composition | $0.6c$ then $0.6c$ collinear | $15/17\,c \approx 0.8824c$ | Modern golden | `am-ref-kinematics-tjq` |
| Dilation second order | $v/c = 10^{-4}$ | $\tfrac12 v^2/c^2 = 5\times10^{-9}$ (stable form) | Modern golden (printed form) | `am-ref-kinematics-tjq` |
| Doppler | $\beta = 0.6$ along and against | factors 0.5 and 2 | Modern golden | `am-ref-waves-r53` |
| Mirror | $\beta = 0.6$ normal incidence | reflected frequency 0.25 of incident; intercepted power $IA_m(1 - \beta)$ | Modern golden | `am-ref-waves-r53` |
| Transverse coefficients | $\beta = 0.6$ | $1.5625m$ (source convention) and $1.25m$ (laboratory) | Modern golden | `am-ref-electron-kfy` |
| Energy ratio versus Doppler ratio | any $v$, $\varphi$ | equal within $10^{-12}$ | Identity | `am-ref-waves-r53` |
| Mass–energy | $v = 0.6c$ | exact $0.25L$; quadratic $0.18L$; proxy about $1.389\,L/c^2$, exceeding $L/c^2$ by about $\tfrac34(v/c)^2$ at small $v$ | Modern golden | `am-ref-mass-energy-ht0` |
| Apparent speed | $\tau \to \tau/4$ | doubles | Identity | `am-ref-diffusion-lr3` |

2. **Printed constants, editorial inputs, and representations.**
   - Historical rows use constants transcribed from the pinned facsimiles (`transcription.status: verified` with the facsimile page, or `verified-suspected-misprint` with the printed reading, the corrected reading, and the receipt reference).
   - Inputs the cited section does not print are declared `editorialInputs` with their source; the audit fails a historical row that uses such an input without declaring it.
   - The audit fails a historical row whose constant set is modern, and a row whose transcription is pending counted as a pass.
   - **The $\alpha$ exponent.** The audit fails an Avogadro row that computes with $\alpha = 6.10\times10^{-56}$ (giving $6.17\times10^{22}$). It accepts a row whose facsimile shows $10^{-56}$ only when that row records the suspected typographical error, uses the corrected $6.10\times10^{-57}$, and cites the provenance receipt that keeps the original reading on the source face.
   - **The charge representation.** The audit fails a stopping-potential row whose `printedRepresentation` is not the representation the facsimile prints, or that omits the documented alternative. The comparison witness's result line "Π·10⁷ = 4.3 Volt" is recorded as a suspected misprint.
3. **Companion rows.** The three molecular-dimensions fixtures are audited under the ids and constant sets of requirement 1, each against the printing it encodes. The audit fails a row that derives two printed values from one data set, or that names a coefficient of $\varphi$ inconsistent with its printing. If `am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936` defers the companion, record all three as deferred with the decision reference; never mark them passing. The evaluator's pending-transcription state counts as not available, never as a pass.
4. **Precision made explicit.** Each historical row compares the evaluator's full-precision result, computed from the declared inputs, with the printed value at the printed precision: $6.17\times10^{23}$ to three significant figures, 4.3 V to two, 0.8 μm and 6 μm to one, and the molecular-dimension values at their printed precision. It separately records the full-precision value and the constant set. Golden and identity rows use the tolerance declared in their scenario files through `src/units/tolerance.ts`.
5. **Cross-owner runs.** Where a FrankenSim owner exists for a row's quantity, run both owners in the registry's cross-owner mode and record `bitwise` or `tolerance` with the tolerance value and maximum deviation.
6. **Reader labels.** Browser checks confirm that fixtures appear with the correct plain-language kind label (historical fixture, modern golden scenario, identity) and their constant set, and are never labeled as historical measurements. The checks run on BM-01 with the `einstein-0-8-micron` teaching tape (no displayed "6.1 μm" without the modern constant-set label), the LQ-08 printed check (the printed representation named), and the ME-02 coefficient view.
7. **Report.** Generate `docs/audits/FIXTURE_TABLE_AUDIT.md` with each row's status, owners, constant sets, transcription status, editorial inputs, printed representation and documented alternatives, precision rule, tolerances, full-precision values, and evidence paths.

## Technical Approach

`scripts/audit-fixture-table.ts` reads `docs/SCENARIO_COVERAGE.md` and the registry, runs `scripts/run-scenarios.ts` filtered to the rows, and writes the report. The label checks run as the `fixture-labels` suite in `scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All fifteen rows exist with correct kinds and pass (the molecular-dimensions row as the three fixtures named in requirement 1), or the companion fixtures are explicitly deferred.
- [ ] No historical row uses a modern constant set, no historical row is pending transcription, and every undeclared editorial input fails.
- [ ] The Avogadro row uses $6.10\times10^{-57}$ and, if the facsimile prints $10^{-56}$, records the suspected misprint and the correction.
- [ ] The stopping-potential row follows the printed representation and names the documented alternative.
- [ ] Each molecular-dimensions fixture carries the scenario id and constant set of requirement 1 and the coefficient of $\varphi$ its printing uses.
- [ ] Every historical row records its precision rule, full-precision value, and constant set.
- [ ] Cross-owner comparisons are recorded wherever two owners exist.
- [ ] Label checks pass on the sampled pages.
- [ ] The generated report is attached to the launch readiness evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`auditFixtureTable.test.ts` detects each of these on fixture rows:
- a missing row, a wrong kind, a modern constant set on a historical row;
- a pending-transcription row counted as a pass, and a silently passing deferred row;
- the $10^{-56}$ transcription slip used without a suspected-misprint record, while the same reading recorded as a suspected misprint with the corrected value passes;
- an undeclared editorial input ($R$ or $L$ in the Avogadro row, $R$ in the mean-displacement row);
- a stopping-potential row in the esu representation when the facsimile prints the gram-equivalent form, and a row missing its documented alternative;
- a molecular-dimensions row that derives two printed values from one data set with two coefficients of $\varphi$;
- a molecular-dimensions fixture whose scenario id and constant set do not pair as in requirement 1 (for example `suspension-einstein-1911-correction` on `einstein-1905-thesis-printed`), and one whose coefficient contradicts its printing;
- a stale "6.1 μm" expectation attached to the historical constant set.

### End-to-end tests
- The `fixture-labels` suite across the harness's desktop, WebKit, and 320-pixel lanes: BM-01's teaching tape, LQ-08's printed check, and ME-02's coefficient view show the correct kind labels and constant sets.

### Structured logging
Through the shared logger, suite `fixture-audit`, file `artifacts/test-logs/fixture-audit/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-ver-fixture-table-audit-nh5`), `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and in `extra`: `row`, `scenarioId`, `kind`, `constantSetId`, `transcription`, `editorialInputs`, `printedRepresentation`, `precisionRule`, `fullPrecisionValue`, `owners`, `maxDeviation`, `status`. A failing row retains, under `artifacts/test-logs/fixture-audit/<log-run-id>/failures/<row>.json`, the scenario file path, its registry evidence path, the full-precision value, the printed value and precision rule, the constant set, and a one-line reproduction command, and its record names that path. Label-check failures retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A passing golden proves plumbing, not physics; do not let the report imply more.
- A fixture that matches a remembered number rather than the facsimile is how order-of-magnitude slips enter; the transcription status exists to stop that.
- Equal agreement at the printed precision can hide a constant-set mix-up; record the full-precision value and the set every time.
- A borrowed input is not a transcription: $R$ in paper 2 and $R$ and $L$ in paper 1 §2 are declared editorial inputs until a facsimile shows otherwise.
- Two unit-system representations can both give "about 4.3 V"; the fixture reproduces the one Einstein printed.
- Three printings are three fixtures: pairing the 1911 coefficient with the 1905 thesis data reproduces nothing Einstein printed, and the square-root scaling makes such a mix look plausible.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`: the registry and runner.
- `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`, `am-ref-radiation-15c`, `am-ref-photoelectric-q6r`, `am-ref-kinematics-tjq`, `am-ref-waves-r53`, `am-ref-electron-kfy`, `am-ref-mass-energy-ht0`: the owners whose scenarios the table covers.
- `am-ref-inference-2w9`: an existing edge that no row of the fifteen needs; its scenarios run in the registry's `scenarios` gate.
- `am-ref-viscosity-suspension-c9lp`: the owner of the three molecular-dimensions fixtures and of the constant sets they use.
- `am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936`: whether the molecular-dimensions fixtures are required or deferred.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-lq-08-photoelectric-va5a`, `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`: the pages whose fixture labels are checked.

The constant sets (`am-ref-constants-xik`) and the harness arrive transitively.

Unblocks:
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: "the computation is real and bounded."
