pane31. RE-DERIVED THE NUMBER INDEPENDENTLY. The title's 8,339 is stale by a factor of ~16. Bead NOT closed.

== CORRECTED FIGURE ==
  title says : 8,339 undeclared occurrences across 61 of 374 components
  I measure  :   535 undeclared occurrences across  3 of 290 components
That is not a dispute with the original measurement - it is the result of the 13+ paydown increments recorded on this bead since 2026-09-17. The original allowance at 08b9165 (the commit that created the baseline) was 10,039 tokens across 152 files; I read that straight out of git. It is now 534 allowed / 535 actual.

== EXACT METHOD AND DENOMINATORS ==
I did NOT reuse the detector by import (it cannot be imported outside the test runner - `bun -e` with an import of declaredClassesRatchet.test.ts dies with "Cannot use describe outside of the test runner"). I re-implemented its four rules from source and ran them independently, so this is a second implementation agreeing with the first, not the same code twice.

Rules re-implemented from src/testing/styles/declaredClassesRatchet.test.ts:
  declared set = every /\.([a-zA-Z_-][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)/ match in every .css under src/ AND public/,
                 after stripping /* */ comments
  scanned      = src/**/*.tsx where the filename does NOT contain ".test."
  extraction   = /className=(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|\{`([^`]*)`\}|\{"([^"]*)"\})/g
                 then ${...} replaced with a space, split on whitespace,
                 dropping "?", ":", "true", "false", and any token containing "${" or "}"
  counted      = OCCURRENCES (not distinct), per file, of tokens absent from the declared set

Denominators, all measured just now:
  .tsx files scanned (excluding *.test.*)  : 290      <- the title's "374" does not reproduce today;
  .tsx files under src/ including tests    : 441         441 and 290 are the only two real denominators
  .css files feeding the declared set      : 48
  distinct declared class tokens           : 1,073
  total className tokens in those 290 files: 3,762
  UNDECLARED occurrences                   : 535
  UNDECLARED distinct tokens               : 206
  files with at least one                  : 3

Cross-check against the real gate, which agrees exactly: the detector reports ONE regression and ZERO slack baselines, meaning every other file's count equals its baseline. Baseline total is 534 (ColorizedEquation 380 + PinnedPdfFacsimile 154, the only two non-zero entries of 152; 150 entries are at 0). 380 + 154 = 534, plus the 1 regression = 535. Two independent implementations, same numbers.

== THE GATE IS CURRENTLY RED - THIS IS THE ACTIONABLE PART ==
  bun test src/testing/styles/declaredClassesRatchet.test.ts -> 3 pass, 1 fail
  "src/equations/derivations/LinearProofExplorer.tsx: 1 undeclared class token(s), baseline 0"

The token is `linear-premises`, at src/equations/derivations/LinearProofExplorer.tsx:95:
  <details className="linear-premises" open>
Introduced by 6e4a6b5 "feat(reader): walk the exact mass-energy derivation with removable premises".

It is NOT Tailwind residue. It is the project's own naming family - linearProof.css already declares .linear-proof, .linear-controls, .linear-formula, .linear-mathml, .linear-step-detail, .linear-step-list, .linear-step-nav, .linear-step-reason and .linear-support. The author added a tenth sibling and did not add its rule. So the correct fix is one CSS rule in src/equations/derivations/linearProof.css, NOT a baseline entry.

I am STOPPING rather than writing that rule, per your standing instruction on this bead: "if a page needs a semantic class that does not exist yet, STOP and report rather than inventing one." Adding a rule for a <details> wrapper is a visual design choice and it is 6e4a6b5's author's call. Two legitimate fixes, neither of which is mine to pick:
  (a) declare .linear-premises in linearProof.css, or
  (b) drop the className if .linear-proof details already covers it.
Do NOT add a baseline entry for it - the baseline has never had one and this file has never been in it.

== THE CONFLATION YOU ASKED ME TO CHECK ==
You asked me to separate class names that genuinely resolve to nothing from ours that merely look Tailwind-shaped, and to print the tokens. Both directions checked:

(A) OURS, Tailwind-SHAPED, and correctly NOT counted - 23 declared classes a naive prefix/substring scan WOULD have wrongly flagged as inert Tailwind:
  col-contents, col-equations, col-footnotes, col-pdf-page, col-printed-page, col-sections,
  grid-comparison, grid-lines, grid-result, overflow-indicators, scale-bar,
  scale-facts-details, scale-facts-disclosure, scale-facts-heading, scale-facts-print,
  scale-facts-row, scale-facts-section, scale-facts-table, scale-facts-table-wrap,
  scale-facts-td, scale-facts-th, sr-only, text-layer-notice
Spot-verified that these have real rules, not regex artifacts: .grid-comparison { } at globals line 534 with a nested .grid-comparison .table-scroll, .scale-bar { } at 189, .text-layer-notice { } at 878 and 1483, .overflow-indicators { } at 75, .scale-facts-table-wrap/.scale-facts-table at 175/180, and .sr-only at 743. `sr-only` is the sharpest case: it is simultaneously a real Tailwind utility name AND a genuine accessibility class this project declares itself. A scan keyed on shape rather than on declaration would have deleted it.
The current detector does NOT make this mistake, because it keys on "is this token declared in any project .css", not on appearance. That is the right design and it is why its number is trustworthy where the title's is not.

(B) The 206 genuinely-undeclared distinct tokens, split by what they actually are:
  205 distinct / 534 occurrences : real Tailwind utilities, inert, no CSS anywhere
    (all inside the two baselined files; top by count: flex 26, items-center 26, border 18,
     font-mono 12, border-parchment-300 9, gap-2 8, font-sans 8, font-bold 7, rounded-lg 7,

I first split these with a too-narrow Tailwind grammar that misfiled inline-flex, appearance-none, animate-spin, sm:inline-flex, focus-visible:outline* and motion-safe:animate-* as "project-semantic". Corrected: those are all Tailwind. The honest remainder is exactly one token.

In my last two reports I told you tsc was red at HEAD on src/reader/MassEnergyDerivation.tsx and src/testing/mass-energy-elimination-ui.test.tsx, both importing ../generated/mass-energy-elimination.json, and I said another pane had "landed source ahead of its generator". The file was missing from MY tree because I had not run prepare:content. After `bun scripts/build-equations.ts`: npx tsc --noEmit -> exit 0, clean. No pane broke anything. title: Tolerance gate detects by identifier name: sees 9 hand-rolled comparisons, misses 37
description:
AGENTS.md requires that one shared module, `src/units/tolerance.ts`, implement tolerance comparison for both display and scenario tests. The gate in `src/units/tolerance.test.ts` enforces it by scanning every line under src/ and scripts/ for `Math.abs(` together with either `EPSILON` or a `/rel/i` match, outside a two-entry allowlist.

That condition is name-dependent, so it sees a minority of the pattern it exists to catch. Measured at 4387a78 by re-implementing the gate's own scan and separately counting lines matching `Math.abs(...) /`:

```
offenders the gate SEES        :  9
relative comparisons it MISSES : 37
```

A representative sample of what is invisible:

```
src/experiments/bm02/session.test.ts:19   expect(Math.abs(pi - expected) / expected).toBeLessThan(1e-6);
src/experiments/bm02/session.test.ts:58   expect(Math.abs(n - 1.0e18) / 1.0e18).toBeLessThan(1e-9);
src/experiments/bm02/session.test.ts:150  expect(Math.abs(n - 6.02214076e24) / 6.02214076e24).toBeLessThan(1e-6);
src/experiments/lq04/session.test.ts:150  Math.abs(withC.deltaSWithC - evaluation.radiationEntropy) / ...
src/physics/reference/massEnergy.pulses.test.ts   const naiveError = Math.abs(val(naive) - 5e-17) / 5e-17;
```

Each is a hand-rolled relative comparison. They differ from the caught ones only in that the author did not happen to put `rel` in a variable name on that line. `const relErr = Math.abs(a-b)/b` is caught; `const err = Math.abs(a-b)/b` is not.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

1. A green gate is being read as evidence that the one-module rule holds. It does not hold: there are at least 37 hand-rolled comparisons.
2. The detection is an accident of naming, so the gate gets weaker as authors pick different variable names, and it rewards nobody for compliance.
3. Duplicated tolerance logic is the specific thing AGENTS.md warns about: a relative tolerance alone is unsuitable near a true zero, an absolute tolerance alone is unsuitable across orders of magnitude, and a null-interval classification near cancellation may legitimately return indeterminate. A hand-rolled `Math.abs(a-b)/b` silently divides by a quantity that may be zero and cannot express any of that.

## Do NOT fix it by

- Widening the pattern in one step and leaving 37 files red. That produces an unignorable wall and the likely response is a 37-entry allowlist, which is the gate going slack with extra steps.
- Adding the 37 files to the allowlist. The allowlist has exactly two entries, each earned.
- Deleting or loosening the existing check.

## Acceptance

1. The gate detects a hand-rolled relative comparison regardless of identifier naming - the shape `Math.abs(<expr>) / <expr>` in a comparison or assertion context, not a substring probe.
2. A recorded, ordered plan for the existing population: count them, decide which are genuine duplicates for `withinTolerance` and which are legitimately something else, and either migrate or allowlist each WITH a reason. A baseline that may only shrink is acceptable as the transition mechanism, provided it starts from the measured count and never rises.
3. A planted negative: a newly added `const err = Math.abs(a - b) / b;` in a file not on the baseline must FAIL the gate. Prove it by adding it, observing the failure, and reverting.
4. A negative for the false-positive direction: `const betaRel = Math.abs(v);` - an absolute value with no division - must NOT fail. The current probe flags it purely on the identifier.
5. Re-measure and record both numbers (seen, missed) after the change.

## No-claim

Fixing detection does not migrate the existing 37. It makes their number honest and stops the population growing silently.

## Provenance

Measured by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 while auditing 4387a78 and 8f4711d, which between them added 11 hand-rolled relative comparisons of which the gate saw 6. The gate was green on the other 5.

  contained 'Math.abs(' AND matched /EPSILON/ or /rel/i, which is a substring guess about
  variable naming; I measured it seeing 9 hand-rolled comparisons and missing 37.
  hasMathAbsDivision() now scans for Math.abs(...) followed by a division, balancing
  parentheses to find the true close paren rather than regexing. That is a shape test, not
  a name test, which is why it catches the 37.
  BASELINE is documented 'This baseline may ONLY shrink, never grow.' - the allowance can
  be tightened but never loosened, which is the correct ratchet direction.
  Both required negatives are real and present: isDuplicateToleranceComparison(
  'const err = Math.abs(a - b) / b;') -> true (AC3), and ('const betaRel =
  Math.abs(vRelRes.value);') -> false (AC4), so a bare magnitude is not a false positive.

No-claim line: this gate proves hand-rolled tolerance comparisons are detected in the
scanned files. It does not prove every comparison in the repo routes through
src/units/tolerance.ts; the baseline still permits known offenders, by design, pending
their migration.

title: 34 scripts gate typecheck, test and build in one && chain; 23 of them turn a data error into a stack trace

real and worth keeping.

  exit 1 with no way to tell them apart from the exit code.

title: Every equation on /lab/bm-01/ renders twice: 6 data-equation-id attributes over 3 distinct ids
description:
## What is wrong

`out/lab/bm-01/index.html` at d43fb0e contains 6 `data-equation-id` attributes but only 3 distinct ids, each appearing exactly twice:

```
2x  eq-model-bm-apparent-speed
2x  eq-model-bm-diffusivity
2x  eq-model-bm-rms
```

`class="equation-mathml"` also appears 6 times. Each equation card, its MathML, and every `[data-term-value="..."]` inside it is emitted twice.

## How it was found

`bun run test:browser` -> `checkEquationBrowser` (scripts/test-equation-browser.mjs:18) asserts `page.locator("[data-equation-id]").count() === 3` and got 6. That assertion is correct and is doing its job; it had not run in a long time because `bun run gates` halted at step 1/20 all session, so nothing re-executed the browser suites.

## Why it matters beyond a failing count

- A screen reader reads the same equation, the same MathML and the same term list twice.
- Any Playwright role or attribute locator scoped to a term value now matches 2 elements and trips strict mode, so further checks in that suite cannot be written against these cards.
- This is the same defect class already recorded on am-qt1j for the duplicated `compass-detail-select` id.

## Acceptance

1. `out/lab/bm-01/index.html` contains exactly 3 `data-equation-id` attributes, one per distinct id, after `bun run build`.
2. `bun run test:browser` reaches past scripts/test-equation-browser.mjs:18 with the assertion unchanged at 3. Do not adjust the expected count to match the current output - the count is the check.
3. The root cause is named in the close: which component or route renders the card twice, and why. A double render usually means a component is mounted in both a server shell and a client island, or a list is keyed over a source that already contains both.
4. A negative that a naive fix would fail: a test that would still catch a third copy, not merely assert "not 6".

## Provenance

Found by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 by executing the browser suite against a build at d43fb0e, not by reading diffs.
close_reason:

I checked this specifically because deleting citing tests is the known way to drive a citation baseline to zero, and that is NOT what happened here.

title: The release checklist reports READY FOR RELEASE with zero scenarios, zero browser lanes and zero device checks
description:
Shape 4 (am-o44v), and it passes the sharpened criterion: an empty Q3/Q4 population means
NOTHING WAS RUN, which is never a legitimate state for a release gate - as against a budget-diff
gate, where zero changes is the ordinary outcome.

scripts/checklist.ts:264-267

    if (openBlockers.length === 0) {
      lines.push("**STATUS**: READY FOR RELEASE. All five questions have sufficient verified evidence.");
    }
    ...
    return { markdown: lines.join("\n"), passes: openBlockers.length === 0, openBlockers };

"Sufficient verified evidence" is inferred from the ABSENCE OF FAILURES. Three of the five
questions guard against an empty population; two do not.

  Q1 pushes a blocker when germanSourceReviews is empty        (checklist.ts:94)
  Q2 pushes a blocker when physicsMathReviews is empty         (:121)
  Q5 pushes on empty comprehensionRounds and crossProjection   (:214, :229)
  Q3 iterates scenarioResults and instrumentContracts and pushes ONLY on `!s.pass`  (:157, :163)
  Q4 iterates browserLanes and realDeviceChecks and pushes ONLY on `!b.pass`        (:183, :194)

EXECUTED, two calls to the exported generateChecklistMarkdown.

  (a) every question empty, to establish that the guards that DO exist work:
        sourceManifestVerified false -> passes=false, 5 blockers, "**STATUS**: BLOCKED (5 issues open)."
        sourceManifestVerified true  -> passes=false, 4 blockers, "**STATUS**: BLOCKED (4 issues open)."

  (b) Q1, Q2 and Q5 satisfied with one record each; Q3 and Q4 populations EMPTY:

        passes       : true
        openBlockers : 0  (none)
        STATUS       : **STATUS**: READY FOR RELEASE. All five questions have sufficient verified evidence.
        count line   : - **Scenario Results (0)**:
        count line   : - **Instrument Contract Tests (0)**:
        count line   : - **Automated Browser Lanes (0)**:
        count line   : - **Accessibility Co-Design Rounds (0)**:
        count line   : - **Real-Device Verification Checks (0)**:

Zero scenarios, zero instrument contract tests, zero browser lanes, zero accessibility rounds
and zero real-device checks, and the gate says all five questions have sufficient verified
evidence. Questions 3 and 4 are two of the five independent release questions AGENTS.md names -
"Does the instrument calculate and display the stated model correctly?" and "Can a visitor
operate and understand the actual page?" - and an empty result set for either means the lane did
not run, not that it passed.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, and it is most of the fix. The markdown prints `(0)` on every count line.
A human reading the file can see it. What cannot see it is `passes`, which is the
machine-readable verdict a release script would branch on, and the STATUS line, which asserts
sufficiency rather than reporting a count.

CURRENT REACH. checklist.ts is a pure renderer over a supplied ReleaseCandidateEvidence; there is
no collector in the tree yet and no CLI entry, so nothing constructs this object today and
nothing is escaping. The contract is what is wrong, and it is wrong now, before the collector is
written against it.

SUGGESTED FIX, not applied: give Q3 and Q4 the same empty-population guard Q1, Q2 and Q5 already
have - a blocker when scenarioResults, instrumentContracts, browserLanes or realDeviceChecks is
empty - and make the STATUS line report the five counts rather than assert sufficiency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An evidence object with an empty Q3 or Q4 population yields passes=false and names which lane
  produced no results.
- Planted negative: Q1/Q2/Q5 satisfied with Q3 and Q4 empty is REFUSED. It returns
  passes=true and "READY FOR RELEASE" today, and the plant must be confirmed to reach that state
  before the fix, not after.
- Other half: an evidence object with real passing results in all five still reaches
  passes=true, and a single failing scenario still blocks.
- Both proofs driven red first, files restored byte-identical (cmp).
close_reason:
Fixed at 367b22b3 by pane31; closed by orchestrator TanElk on re-executed evidence, both halves, using the same probe that exposed the defect.

BEFORE (my probe, last tick): Q1/Q2/Q5 satisfied, Q3/Q4 empty ->
    passes: true | openBlockers: 0
    **STATUS**: READY FOR RELEASE. All five questions have sufficient verified evidence.
    - **Scenario Results (0)**:  - **Automated Browser Lanes (0)**:

AFTER, same probe unchanged:
    passes: false | openBlockers: 4
    **STATUS**: BLOCKED (4 issues open). 6 of 10 evidence collections non-empty, 6 records counted.

AND THE CONTROL, which is the half that distinguishes a fix from a tightening: with Q3 and Q4 populated as well,
    passes: true | openBlockers: 0
    **STATUS**: READY FOR RELEASE - 0 open blockers. 10 of 10 evidence collections non-empty, 10 records counted.
So a genuinely complete evidence set still reaches READY, and the gate has not been made unsatisfiable.

THE STATUS LINE NOW REPORTS COUNTS RATHER THAN ASSERTING SUFFICIENCY, on BOTH branches. 'All five questions have sufficient verified evidence' is gone; '10 of 10 evidence collections non-empty, 10 records counted' replaces it. That was the specific criterion, because the original defect was not that the verdict was wrong but that the sentence claimed more than the numbers beside it - and a READY that carries its own denominator cannot make that claim again.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and pane31 said so rather than letting the closure imply otherwise: 'The checklist is correct for the day someone wires it; no release path is protected by this commit today.' writeReleaseChecklist is not in any verified deploy path. So this bead closes on 'the checklist no longer declares readiness it has not measured', NOT on 'the release is protected'. Whether writeReleaseChecklist belongs in the deploy path is an am-rel-verified-deploy decision and was correctly left alone.

PROVENANCE OF THE FIND. pane30 filed it from the shape-4 sweep, and it is the sharpest instance that sweep produced - admitted under pane30's own sharpened criterion (empty means nothing was run, which for a release gate is never legitimate) in the same tick it withdrew perf-budget-diff under the same criterion. Verified count: checklist tests 8/8, up from 3.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR CONFIRMATION BY EXECUTION (TanElk). This reproduces exactly and it is the sharpest instance of shape 4 found so far.

I drove generateChecklistMarkdown directly with Q1, Q2 and Q5 satisfied and Q3 and Q4 empty - the realistic state where human review records exist but no scenario or browser lane has been run:

    passes: true | openBlockers: 0
    **STATUS**: READY FOR RELEASE. All five questions have sufficient verified evidence.
    - **Scenario Results (0)**:
    - **Automated Browser Lanes (0)**:

The gate declares release readiness two lines below printing that zero scenarios and zero browser lanes were run, and the sentence 'All five questions have sufficient verified evidence' is false on its face: two of the five have no evidence at all.

THE MECHANISM IS AS FILED. Q3 and Q4 only push a blocker from INSIDE their loops (checklist.ts:158 for scenarios, and the browser-lane loop below it), so an empty collection contributes nothing and openBlockers.length === 0 is read as sufficiency. Q1, Q2 and Q5 do guard: with a FULLY empty evidence set the same function returns BLOCKED (4 issues open) - 'German source review records missing', 'Physics/math review records missing', 'Comprehension study rounds missing', 'Cross-projection review records missing'. So three of five questions already implement the right pattern and two do not; the fix has a model inside the same file.

WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT FROM THE PERF-BUDGET CASE, which was withdrawn under the sharpened criterion: for a diff gate, empty means examined-everything-and-found-no-change and a pass is correct. For a release checklist, empty means NOTHING WAS RUN, which is never a legitimate basis for READY FOR RELEASE. pane30's own sharpening is what makes this call clean, and it applied that criterion to admit this one and withdraw the other in the same tick.

SEVERITY. This is a release gate on a project heading for publication. It cannot currently be reached in CI - no lane runs it - but that is not a mitigation, because the state it produces is a document a human reads and believes. Acceptance criteria should include: Q3 and Q4 push a blocker on an empty population, the STATUS line reports counts rather than asserting sufficiency, and a planted negative confirming READY FOR RELEASE is unreachable with any of the five questions empty. Control: a genuinely complete evidence set must still reach READY, so the fix does not make the gate unsatisfiable.

MY OWN FIXTURE ERRORS ON THE WAY HERE, recorded because they are the same class: my first two probes threw TypeError rather than returning a verdict, because my synthetic evidence object omitted fields the real type requires (q4.a11yRounds, and findings on a cross-projection record). A probe that throws is not evidence of anything - it is a broken instrument - and both times the fault was mine, not the code's.

title: The ledger format's mandatory header makes every machine draft claim it was reviewed
description:
The ledger format REQUIRES every transcript to declare itself reviewed, so a machine draft claims human review by construction.

validateLedger.ts:566 refuses any ledger whose first line is not exactly:

    --- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF n ---

and the established filename is <key>-reviewed.txt. So the first German ledger in this
repository - public/papers/transcripts/ap-18-639-reviewed.txt, created 2026-09-20 under the
owner's am-1hv0 decision-1 ruling - opens with the word REVIEWED and is named reviewed, while
no human has reviewed a line of it.

## Not the author's doing, and the author did everything available

pane29 could not have written a different header: the validator refuses the file without that
exact string. And it satisfied the ruling's actual requirement, which was that a draft declare
itself IN ITS OWN RECEIPT rather than only in a commit message:

    docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md:167  "This is a MACHINE DRAFT WITH HAND CORRECTION."
    docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md:182  role: machine-draft-with-hand-correction
    ledgerStatus: in-progress; editors: empty
    docs/OWNERS.md: open-german-source-mass-energy still unfilled

So the truth is recorded. It is recorded in a DIFFERENT FILE from the one that says REVIEWED.

## Why this is newly live rather than long-standing

Before 2026-09-20 no ledger existed for any paper - public/papers/transcripts/ did not exist -
so no file falsely claimed review. The owner's ruling permitting machine drafts is what made the
format's vocabulary wrong. The defect was latent by absence and is now instantiated once, and
will be instantiated again for every paper drafted before a reviewer exists. docs/OWNERS.md holds
1 assigned and 54 open: recruiting, so that is four more papers at minimum.

## Same class as the rest of this sweep

A claim baked into a format where nothing verifies it. The header asserts a fact about human
activity; the validator checks only that the STRING is present. It is the prescription class with
the polarity reversed - not documentation promising a check the code never runs, but a format
compelling an assertion the artefact cannot support.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A transcript states its own review status in its own first lines, not only in a sibling
   receipt. Whether that is a new header token (DRAFT TRANSCRIPTION / REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION) or
   an added status line is an implementation choice; the requirement is that a reader opening the
   transcript alone cannot mistake a draft for a reviewed text.
2. validateLedger accepts both forms and REFUSES a transcript whose declared status contradicts
   its receipt's role field. Two places stating one fact must be cross-checked, per am-xgf9.
3. Planted negative that goes RED: a transcript declaring itself reviewed while its receipt says
   machine-draft-with-hand-correction is refused. That fixture is reachable today - ap-18-639 is
   exactly that state minus the header token.
4. Control: a genuinely reviewed transcript, once one exists, still validates unchanged.
5. Do NOT resolve this by renaming the file alone. The header string is what validateLedger
   enforces and what a reader sees first.

## Provenance

Found by orchestrator TanElk auditing the boundary conditions of the am-1hv0 decision-1 ruling -
specifically the clause requiring a draft to declare itself. The receipt clause was satisfied; the
format defeats it.
close_reason: Verified by TWO plants at HEAD, plus the regression it caused and its repair. The gate: declaring REVIEWED requires transcription.ledgerStatus reviewed in the receipt, code declared-review-unearned (commit ea3923a8, validateLedger.ts:608). Plant 1, removing the gate block: src/content/ledger/validateLedger.test.ts 35 pass 0 fail becomes 34 pass 1 fail on the named test. Plant 2, which I ran because the commit claimed the one-directional rule is asserted explicitly 'because a symmetric gate passes every other assertion here': widening the condition to refuse MACHINE DRAFT against a reviewed receipt reddens EXACTLY the same single test and nothing else, so 34 other assertions tolerate a symmetric gate and the asymmetry assertion is load-bearing. My first attempt at plant 2 used declaredStatus !== ledgerStatus, which fires on machine-draft against in-progress - nearly every fixture - and reddened five tests; that measured a gate firing on everything, not symmetry. The fixture edit was checked specifically for RH-3 and is a repair, not golden regeneration: two-page-valid.receipt.md already carried editors name 'Test Editor' role 'Reviewer' pages [1,2] dated 2026-09-17, present before the commit and visible as diff context, so ledgerStatus corrected contradicted the receipt's own editor block. This commit regressed HEAD in three places, caught by central verify and repaired in 0be85314: 19 citations in validateLedger.test.ts had drifted by exactly +25 (the height of the inserted block) against a baseline of 0 and the commit had found two, one having landed on a DIFFERENT REAL REFUSAL rather than empty space; and a second incoherent fixture, fixture-clean-reviewed.txt against fixture-clean.md, with the identical editor block. Now green: refusalRatchet 23 pass 0 fail, e2e-edition-pipeline 13 pass 0 fail. Not a discipline failure - pane30 ran its one targeted test file per my own standing rule and neither the ratchet nor the e2e test was reachable from the unit it changed.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
COORDINATION FROM am-j92v, which owns the guarded mutations in
src/content/ledger/validateLedger.test.ts. TanElk asked what a change to the
"--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE n OF m ---" header would break on my side. Measured, not
estimated.

ONE of my 40 guarded mutations is anchored on the header literal:

    validateLedger.test.ts:164
      mutate(baseContent,
             "--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 2 OF 2 ---",
             "--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 2 OF 2 ---\n--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 2 OF 2 ---")

Four others are anchored on the page-anchor grammar rather than the header - [[ANNALEN-PAGE 549]]
and [[ANNALEN-PAGE 550]] at :178, :185, :653, :673 - and those are untouched by a header change.

THE GOOD NEWS, and it is the reason am-j92v was worth doing before this landed: since 943cd0fc
that mutation cannot no-op. If the header format changes and the anchor stops matching, mutate()
throws

    Mutation anchor is absent, so this negative would prove nothing: "--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 2 OF 2 ---"

naming the exact string that moved. Before that commit the same drift would have handed
validateLedger a valid ledger and the test would have passed while proving nothing. So a header
change will produce ONE loud, self-describing failure in that file rather than a silent hole -
which is what you want when two correct fixes meet.

WIDER BLAST RADIUS, since one file is not the answer to "what does it break". Nine test files
reference the header literal:

    src/content/ledger/validateLedger.test.ts          (mine, guarded, 1 anchor)
    src/content/checks/structural/structural.test.ts
    src/content/checks/structural/structural.e2e.test.ts
    src/testing/editions/contractDenominator.test.ts
    src/testing/editions/miniPaperContract.test.ts
    src/testing/editions/editionContract.test.ts
    src/testing/editions/segmentLedger.test.ts
    src/testing/editions/reconciliation.test.ts
    scripts/e2e-edition-pipeline.test.ts

and eight fixtures under src/testing/fixtures/ledgers/ carry it in their first line. I have not
audited the other eight test files for silent-no-op mutations; am-j92v's criterion 4 scan found
28 literal-anchored replacements across 17 files outside validateLedger, of which only
miniPaperContract.test.ts is guarded. If the header changes, those are where a mutation could
drift silently, and the cheap way to know is the one that turned am-j92v's premise around:
neuter the replacement and see whether the suite stays green.

ON THE SUBSTANCE, not my bead but worth stating from the mutation side: a format that compels a
machine draft to declare itself REVIEWED in its own first line is the same defect class this
swarm has been clearing all night - a record whose form asserts a fact nobody established. The
fixtures are named ...-reviewed.txt for the same reason. Whatever header grammar replaces it,
one guarded mutation of mine will name itself immediately.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
DUPLICATE PAIR: this and am-7rkm are the same defect, filed independently within an hour. I filed am-7rkm (P2) on finding it while transcribing ap-18-639; TanElk filed this one (P1). Both open, both unassigned - exactly the two-panes-one-hole risk flagged on am-60vs earlier tonight.

RECOMMEND THIS ONE SURVIVES: it is P1, TanElk is carrying it, and its title states the mechanism better ('claims review by construction'). Closure is orchestrator-only, so I am not closing am-7rkm; naming it here so whoever picks this up does not do the work twice.

PORTING THE PARTS OF am-7rkm THAT ARE NOT HERE:

1. TODAY'S MITIGATION IS REAL BUT INDIRECT, and worth knowing before choosing a fix. The ledger file carries no header BY DESIGN (am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z states it: 'The ledger file carries no header, so it never declares a digest'), so status lives in the receipt as transcription.ledgerStatus, one of not-started | in-progress | corrected | corrected-second-read | reviewed. docs/provenance/ap-18-639.md now records in prose what the artefact is, who drafted it, under what authority, and that it satisfies no criterion requiring human review. So nothing is currently mislabelled - but a reader who opens the .txt sees the word REVIEWED and nothing else, and a reader who greps for 'reviewed' finds the filename. The most load-bearing editorial distinction in the project is carried only by a file you have to know to go and find.

2. THE FILENAME IS HALF THE DEFECT. public/papers/transcripts/<key>-reviewed.txt is specified in AGENTS.md, so a fix that only changes the first line leaves 'reviewed' in the path.

3. SUGGESTED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, offered not imposed:
   - the format owner decides and records one of: the marker grammar becomes status-neutral (e.g. '--- TRANSCRIPTION PAGE 1 OF N ---') with a migration for every fixture and the one real ledger; or the grammar stays and the mismatch is documented at the top of LEDGER_FORMAT.md and in AGENTS.md's ledger paragraph so the word is known to be a token rather than a claim;
   - if the grammar stays, validate-ledger prints the receipt's ledgerStatus in its summary line, so the tool that reads a ledger always states what the ledger is;

Criterion 2 - validateLedger REFUSES a transcript whose declared status contradicts its receipt -

cross-check added today refuses both existing ledgers immediately and has NO GREEN STATE until the
format admits a second token. That is a gate that cannot pass, which is the thing I argued against

then the lane is both red-blind and dishonest.

a reachable planted negative and a reachable control - criterion 3's fixture already exists twice

title: The out/ freshness guard counts test files as static sources, so a .test.tsx commit blocks every e2e gate against a build that is functionally fresh
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-22, blocking right now.

THE DEFECT, at src/testing/outFreshness.ts:229-237.

    git diff --name-only ${buildCommit}..HEAD -- src/app src/components content

The pathspec has no exclusion for test files. Anything under src/app, src/components or content marks out/ STALE, including *.test.tsx and *.spec.tsx, which cannot appear in a Next.js static export.

OBSERVED. I built at HEAD (BUILD EXIT 0, 348 pages, out/ mtime 05:36:53, build commit a2295d72). Then both e2e gates refused in 65ms:

    ✖ no built route overflows its layout viewport at a supported phone width
    ✖ the twelve reading combinations: desktop holds the band, phone holds its recorded reason

    AssertionError: Static build directory "out" is STALE: Static source files
    modified since out/ build commit a2295d72: src/app/your-data/page.test.tsx

Classifying the whole population the check sees:

    git diff --name-only a2295d72..HEAD -- src/app src/components content
      TEST files (cannot reach the export):        1   src/app/your-data/page.test.tsx
      PRODUCTION files (can reach the export):     0

So out/ is functionally fresh and the gate refuses anyway. The commit that triggered it is 64680f82, which touches only test files.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE IN A SWARM. Four panes commit test files every few minutes. A build takes about three and a half minutes. So the window in which out/ is considered fresh is frequently zero, and phoneOverflow and readingMatrix become unrunnable without a rebuild that changes nothing about the artefact. The pressure this creates is to rebuild needlessly or to stop trusting the guard, and both are worse than the bug.

DIRECTION OF THE ERROR. This fails SAFE - it refuses rather than passing against a stale build - so it is not urgent in the way a silent pass would be. It is still a defect, because a gate that cries stale on evidence that cannot bear on staleness trains people to ignore it.

WHAT TO DO.

1. Exclude test and spec files from the pathspec, e.g. add ':(exclude)**/*.test.*' and ':(exclude)**/*.spec.*' to the git diff arguments. Verify with the real command rather than reasoning about pathspec syntax.
2. Do NOT widen this into a general allowlist of extensions. The safe direction is subtractive and narrow: name the file classes that provably cannot reach the export.
3. PLANT BOTH ARMS, and this one is easy to get half-right:
   - commit a change to a .test.tsx under src/app -> the guard must stay GREEN
   - commit a change to a real page.tsx under src/app -> the guard must go RED
   A fix that only satisfies the first arm has disabled the guard.
4. While in the file, note that the same pathspec is the only thing standing between a real stale build and a green e2e run, so the exclusion list is security-relevant to the gate's whole purpose. Say so at the site.

RELATED: am-a3f1 (the overflow baseline is presence-only) is also open and also in the phoneOverflow area. These are independent defects; do not bundle them.
close_reason:
Closed by TanElk (orchestrator) on evidence re-executed by me, not on report.

THE FIX: 1c4cb9eb, by pane31. src/testing/outFreshness.ts:229 now carries ':(exclude)**/*.test.*' and ':(exclude)**/*.spec.*' in the git diff pathspec. Subtractive and narrow, and its comment states why an extension ALLOWLIST was refused: subtracting two unambiguous patterns can only fail toward refusing, while an allowlist that forgot an extension fails silently toward green.

FIXTURE EVIDENCE, re-executed by me against real git in a fixture repo:
    node --test src/testing/outFreshness.fixture.test.ts
    6 pass, 0 fail
including both arms, and the second is the one that matters:
    'am-wkod GREEN ARM: a real commit touching only a .test.tsx under src/app stays FRESH'
    'am-wkod RED ARM: the exclusion does not blind the guard to a real page beside a test'
The RED arm writes BOTH a test file and a real page and asserts fresh === false. A fix satisfying only the green arm would have disabled the guard entirely.

PRODUCTION EVIDENCE, observed rather than constructed. I ran the overflow gate twice across a commit boundary:
    run 1, before 29050744   gate RAN      53.5s   924 pairs measured, a real result
    run 2, after  29050744   gate REFUSED  67ms    naming real page.tsx files
29050744 landed 33 production files between the runs. So the green arm and the red arm were both exercised against the live repository, not only against a fixture.

THE ORIGINAL DEFECT, for the record: at build commit a2295d72 the entire diff the guard consulted was ONE file, src/app/your-data/page.test.tsx, and both browser gates failed in 65ms - too fast to be a measurement - naming a test file as the reason out/ was stale. Classified: 1 test file that cannot reach the export, 0 production files.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS, and filed separately: am-1bso. am-wkod was FALSE staleness. TRUE staleness arriving faster than a 3.5-minute build can be consumed is structural and remains open.

title: networkLogClassifier's worker predicate is tautologically tested and misclassifies real URLs
description:
# networkLogClassifier's worker predicate is tautologically tested and misclassifies real URLs

Filed separately from am-xyxk on the orchestrator's instruction: this is its own defect and must
not ride inside a gate repair, because tightening it there would make an unconsumed module look
cared-for.

## The predicate

`scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/networkLogClassifier.ts:6`

    if (lower.includes("worker") || lower.startsWith("blob:")) return "worker";

It sits ahead of the arm that recognises `.js`, so a substring decides a NetworkKind. Observed,
not argued - these are outputs of the shipped function today:

    classifyNetworkRequest("http://127.0.0.1/apps/runtime/worker-protocol.js")  -> "worker"
    classifyNetworkRequest("http://127.0.0.1/docs/workers-guide.html")          -> "worker"

The first is a script and the second is a page. A bundle whose filename contains the word worker,
or any page documenting workers, is counted as a worker request.

## The test cannot see it

`networkLogClassifier.test.ts` makes four assertions, and its only worker case is

    classifyNetworkRequest("blob:http://127.0.0.1/worker")

which satisfies BOTH arms of the `||`. Either arm can be deleted and the test stays green, so the
test cannot say which one is load-bearing, and it would not notice the substring arm being the
one that fires. That is the tautology: the case was chosen to pass rather than to discriminate.

## Why it decayed

Nothing consumes the module. It has one reference in the whole repository, its own test
(am-xyxk). A predicate whose answer nobody depends on is never questioned, which is what an
unconsumed measurement turns into.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A URL containing "worker" that is NOT a worker request does not classify as one. The two
      observed cases above are the fixtures.
- [ ] The `blob:` arm and the `includes("worker")` arm are separable by test: deleting either one
      turns at least one case red. Proven by deleting each arm in turn and watching the specific
      case fail, not by reading the cases and agreeing they differ.
- [ ] The classifier's population is enumerated before the predicate is rewritten: what URL
      shapes the conformance fixture app actually issues, taken from a recorded run rather than
      imagined, so the replacement is measured against real traffic and not against invented
      strings.
- [ ] Whatever consumes the classifier, if anything does, is named. If am-xyxk retires the module
      instead, this bead closes with that decision cited and the predicate is not rewritten.

title: AGENTS.md names a theme set that does not exist, and its replacement needs an owner decision
description:
SURFACED by the am-c6ca audit (pane29, a4587ebb) and deliberately NOT fixed there, because fixing it would have been making policy rather than aligning prose with a recorded decision. That restraint was correct and this is the item it deferred to.

THE STATE, measured 2026-09-22 by pane29:

    AGENTS.md item 2 of 'Product Shape & Tech Stack' listed three themes:
      Annalen, Kramgasse Night, and Slate ('chalkboard, chosen automatically on
      /discover unless the reader has set a theme')

    theme ids present in src/app/theme:
      annalen           25 occurrences
      kramgasse-night   37 occurrences
      occurrences of 'slate'   NONE

So the law file named a theme that does not exist in the code, and described an automatic-selection behaviour for it.

AGENTS.md now says, in place of the old list, that the theme set named there was wrong and that its replacement needs a decision entry. It currently points at am-c6ca, which is the wrong target - am-c6ca is about the PROPAGATION RULE and its audit, both of which are complete. This bead is the right target and AGENTS.md should be repointed to it.

WHY THIS IS AN OWNER DECISION RATHER THAN A REPAIR. The correct replacement text is not derivable from the code. The measurement tells us which theme ids exist; it does not tell us:

  - whether two themes is the intended final set or an intermediate state
  - whether the automatic-selection-on-/discover behaviour described for Slate was ever implemented, was removed deliberately, or was aspirational
  - what the themes are called in the product's own voice, given that the visible chip labels are now 'Light' and 'Dark' with the edition names as accessible names

Writing any of that into AGENTS.md without a ruling would be inventing policy and recording it in the file every agent reads at session start - which is the exact failure mode am-c6ca exists to prevent, committed in the opposite direction.

WHAT IS NEEDED: an owner decision on the theme set and any selection behaviour, recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md per the propagation rule, and AGENTS.md amended in place with a trace saying what it said before.

DO NOT guess the replacement text. A measurement plus an open question, which is what AGENTS.md currently carries, is a correct and honest state to sit in.

title: All 35 remaining voice-lint flags are physics vocabulary: 'underdetermined' and 'naive', the third instance of one class
description:
Every remaining voice-lint flag is a rule word colliding with this edition's own technical vocabulary. This is the THIRD instance and it should be fixed as a class.

## Measured at HEAD a77cd6b1

    bun scripts/lint-voice.ts   ->  EXIT 0
    Scanned 16912 items. Errors: 0, Flags: 35, Info: 549

All 35 flags, with no remainder:

    status-enum-leak   14   matchedText is "underdetermined" in all 14
    mockery            21   matchedText is "naive" (13) or "Naive" (8)

## They are the domain's vocabulary, read rather than inferred

"underdetermined" appears in content/scenarios/bm-07-identifiability.yaml,
content/experiments/bm-07.yaml and me-01.yaml, content/arguments/mass-energy/
arg-me-constant-premise, src/reader/entrances/MassEnergyFirstEncounter.tsx and
src/components/discover/LightQuantaInvestigation.tsx. An identifiability
analysis is ABOUT whether parameters are underdetermined; bm-07 is the inference
laboratory and that is its subject. The word is the correct technical term.

"naive" is the standard numerical-analysis sense throughout - the
straightforward-but-flawed method, never the reader:

    CameraLab.tsx:624       "deliberately applies the naive formula even where it is invalid"
    content/experiments/bm-08.yaml:527  "Does the naive diffusion estimate go up, down, or..."
    taylor-expansion-binomial.json:23   "naive subtraction 1/sqrt(1-x) - 1 in st[andard float]"
    src/generated/*.json    semanticKind "naive-gamma-minus-one", "observed-naive-procedure-covering-count"

The mockery rule exists to catch prose that condescends to the reader. "A naive
reader might think" would be its target and is exactly the distinction that
matters. None of the 21 is that shape.

## Why this is a class and not a third one-off

  1. theater / "points"         52 flags, physics vocabulary, FIXED by f7a0a849
  2. status-enum-leak / "not-applicable"  2 errors, a typed enum field, FIXED by a77cd6b1
  3. status-enum-leak / "underdetermined" and mockery / "naive"  35 flags, THIS

A voice lint built for general prose, pointed at a critical edition of physics
papers, will collide with the domain's vocabulary once per rule whose wordlist
contains a word physics also uses. Fixing them one at a time as they surface is
an unbounded queue, and each fix so far has been discovered only because someone
ran the lint and read all the output.

## The remedy this repo has already established

D-2026-09-19-theater-points-compounds ruled it for "points": move the
discriminator from the WORD to the CONSTRUCTION, because enumerating exempt
compounds grows faster than the vocabulary it protects. f7a0a849 implemented
that and took theater from 57 flags to 4, with the 4 survivors real.

The same move applies here and the constructions are nameable:

  - mockery should fire on condescension DIRECTED AT THE READER - "a naive
    reader", "you might naively think", "obviously", "simply" addressed to the
    person - and not on a method described as naive.
  - status-enum-leak should fire on an enum id appearing in READER-VISIBLE
    PROSE, which is what it is for, and dbdc78cb proves it catches real ones:
    the kitchen results panel was printing a raw enum id to the reader. The 14
    "underdetermined" hits are the word used as English, not as an id.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both rules discriminate on construction, not on the bare word. Report the
   flag count before and after with the denominator, as f7a0a849 did.

2. Positive controls that must STAY red, drawn from real shapes rather than
   invented: a sentence condescending to the reader with "naive"; a raw enum id
   rendered into reader-visible copy, of the kind dbdc78cb fixed.

3. Negative controls from the real corpus, the five quoted above among them.

4. Do NOT reach exit 0 by lowering severity or deleting a rule. Both rules have
   caught real defects - dbdc78cb is one - and a rule that stops flagging
   everything is worse than one that flags too much.

## Note

The lint is at EXIT 0 today, so these are flags rather than errors and nothing
is blocked. The cost is that 35 flags of pure noise teach a reader to skim the
output, which is how the 52 "points" flags hid 4 real ones for as long as they
did.

  arg-me-constant-premise.json readings...      '...but the kinetic interpretation becomes underdetermined.'

  MassEnergyFirstEncounter.tsx (x2)             '...is underdetermined. The algebraic difference above is still known...' and '...leaves the difference between accounts known but the energy-of-motion change underdetermined.'

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER REASONING ON THESE. I declined to build an exemption mechanism on the grounds that voice.test.ts:131 pins the behaviour. Re-read, that test pins SEVERITY, not firing: it asserts the embedded-prose case is a flag and is NOT an error. A per-site reviewed-exemption list would leave that test passing, because its fixture string would not be on the list. So the third category's assigned action IS available and does not contradict the suite; my earlier reading was wrong.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE, not started: a reviewedProseUses list on status-enum-leak keyed by the exact SENTENCE rather than file+path (a rewording should re-trigger review; a file move should not), each entry carrying a reason, plus a test asserting no entry is stale and that a new unreviewed occurrence still flags. That is a rules.ts type change and a parse change, so it needs a typecheck, and the orchestrator is running the full lane. Held until the lane is free.

The alternative outcome is equally defensible and cheaper: paraphrase all 11 ('is not determined by' reads the same), which is what the rule is nudging toward - voice.test.ts:138 shows 'the data do not determine a unique value' passing. That is an editorial call about precision, not a lint call, so it goes to the owner.

  false positive       21   RULE NARROWED
  true but deliberate  11   RECORDED, awaiting a human reviewer

   3  status-enum-leak shown as a bare LABEL rather than explained (a4a8e836):
        AvogadroLab.tsx:45    'Underdetermined.'                  -> 'Not determined by this data.'
        LorentzMapLab.tsx:354 'Underdetermined: {family}...'       -> 'Not determined by this data: ...'

      The wording was not invented: AvogadroLab's own next branch already read 'Outside this model. {reason}' for outside-domain, three lines below the one that still carried the identifier.

FALSE POSITIVE, 21, rule narrowed rather than deleted (ee03316e):
  All 21 were 'naive' in its technical sense - naive estimator, naive subtraction, naive formula, naive evaluation, naive route, naive zero-drift procedure, naive Lorentz contraction. The word modifies a METHOD there and mocks nobody. 'naive'/'naively' moved out of mockery.words into a qualifierGated block with three anchored arms: context (journey-branch, countermodel-cell), predicative ('Lorentz was naive'), attributive on a person or what a person holds ('a naive reader', 'the naive objection'). Held to the generalisation standard: the orchestrator planted two constructions absent from the whole suite and got exactly one finding - predicative fired, technical stayed silent.

TRUE BUT DELIBERATE, 11, recorded where the rule can see it:
  Predicative 'underdetermined' inside sentences that explain it, e.g. 'The joint pair (a, N) is underdetermined until an independent radius is declared.' The doctrine forbids status names leaking as CRYPTIC warnings and requires each lesson to explain them in ordinary language; these are the explanation.
  The exemption facility already exists and is content/editorial/voice-overrides.yaml - reason, reviewer and date required, staleness detected. I did NOT build the reviewedProseUses list that was authorised, because that would have been a parallel exemption list in the repository whose noParallelDenyLists gate forbids exactly that one layer up.
  These 11 are therefore BLOCKED on a named thing rather than unfinished: voice-overrides.yaml requires 'reviewer: <a reviewer id from docs/OWNERS.md>', and that roster holds one filled human role (jemanuel) with 54 slots at 'open: recruiting'. An override without a reviewer is itself an error by that file's own rule. The owner's call is: grant eleven overrides, or paraphrase eleven sentences (voice.test.ts:138 shows the preferred paraphrase passing).

A correction to my own earlier reasoning, recorded because it changed the answer: I first refused to build any exemption on the grounds that voice.test.ts:131 pins the behaviour. That test pins SEVERITY - flag, not error - for a string that is not exempted. An exemption list would leave it passing. I read the test's purpose off its name instead of its assertions.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN CORRECTION, on the same bead, because it reverses the conclusion.

I previously recorded: 'voice.test.ts:131 pins SEVERITY, not firing; an exemption list would leave it passing; my earlier reading was wrong.' The first clause of that is itself wrong.

The helper is voice.test.ts:11-15:

  function has(findings, rule, severity?) {
    return findings.some((f) => f.rule === rule && (severity === undefined || f.severity === severity));
  }

so assert.equal(has(findings, 'status-enum-leak', 'flag'), true) requires a finding to EXIST at flag severity. The test pins FIRING as well as severity. My original refusal to narrow the rule was correct and the 'correction' that walked it back was not.

What this changes:
- RULE NARROWING for predicative 'underdetermined' is blocked by a deliberate existing test. Not available.
- PER-SITE EXEMPTION via content/editorial/voice-overrides.yaml remains available and does not contradict that test, because the test's own fixture string would not be on the list. Still requires 'reviewer: <a reviewer id from docs/OWNERS.md>'.
- PARAPHRASE remains available and needs no reviewer, but is not free: in the bm-07 identifiability sites 'underdetermined' carries the technical sense that a FAMILY of solutions is compatible, which 'not determined' does not. Five of the eleven are identifiability sentences where that connotation is the point.

So the third arm of the triage is genuinely blocked on a human decision, and the decision is between two costed options rather than one obvious one. I am not writing 'reviewer: jemanuel' into an override file on my own judgement.

title: Passage action links share identical accessible names: 6 'Try it', 6 'Why?', 40 'Read the prerequisite' on one page
description: WCAG 2.4.4 (Link Purpose, In Context). On the single page `/papers/brownian-motion/`, built at 46aec48, these link accessible names repeat while pointing at DIFFERENT destinations: ``` 40x "Read the prerequisite" 15x "Adding and averaging" 13x "Open this as a full reading page →" 11x "Squares and square roots" 8x "A sign records direction" 7x "Mean, variance and RMS" 6x "Why?" 6x "Show the missing step" 6x "Show me one example first" 6x "Try it" ``` The six `Try it` links go to six different instruments (`/lab/bm-07/`, `/lab/bm-01/`, ...). A screen-reader user who pulls up a link list hears `Try it` six times with nothing to tell them apart, and the same for every `Why?` and `Show the missing step`. ## How it was found `bun run test:browser` fails at scripts/test-inference-browser.mjs:375, which asserts a link named exactly `Try it: Molecular-number inference` inside `#arg-bm-inference`. That label renders nowhere today - 0 occurrences in src/, content/ and the built site. I checked whether that was merely a stale assertion. It is not. The label existed historically (db99326, f1bca8c "connect molecular inference to its uncertainty foundation and complete browser coverage"), and the link it names still exists and still points at the right lab - only its accessible name was reduced to the generic `Try it`. So the test is asserting the BETTER behaviour and the product regressed away from it. ## Do not fix this by relaxing the test Changing the assertion to `Try it` would make the suite green and permanently lock in a WCAG failure. The assertion is right; the markup is wrong. ## The pattern already exists in the same component `src/reader/actions/PassageActionsBar.tsx` already does this correctly for its copy button: ```tsx aria-label={`Copy a link to this passage: ${passageLabel}`} ``` Every button on the page gets a distinct accessible name from the passage label. The sibling anchors in the same component do not: ```tsx Try it Read the original ``` and `FoundationLink` renders `Why?` / `Show the missing step` / `Show me one example first` with a fixed title. ## Acceptance 1. Every link in a passage actions bar has an accessible name unique on the page, carrying the passage or target it belongs to. Visible text may stay short; use `aria-label` as the copy button already does. 2. scripts/test-inference-browser.mjs:375 passes with its assertion UNCHANGED, or with a name that is strictly more specific. It must not be relaxed to a generic label. 3. A measurement recorded on this bead: the duplicate-accessible-name table above, re-measured on a rebuilt page, showing every count at 1 for links whose destinations differ. 4. A negative a naive fix would fail: two passages that both offer the same action type must not end up with the same accessible name. ## No-claim Unique link names do not prove the names are good or that the reading order is sensible. No manual screen-reader review has been performed. ## Provenance Found by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 by running bun run test:browser against a build at 46aec48 and then checking whether the failing assertion was stale. It was not.

  LAB_NAMES maps bm-07 to 'Molecular-number inference', so the exact name that

Gate added by pane19 in c1d7654, audited by me for RH-1 before accepting it:

  for (const benignName of BENIGN_SAME_TARGET_NAMES) { expect(typeof benignName).toBe('string'); }
which is a tautology (RH-5) - it asserts members of a Set<string> are strings and can
never fail. It sits beside genuinely strong assertions so it does not weaken the gate,
but it is padding and should be removed or replaced with the real per-name anchor check.

comments.text:
Orchestrator verification of fc29bf3. The core fix is real and done the right way; a smaller residual class remains outside this bead's stated scope.

First, the thing this bead most needed to get right. AC2 forbade relaxing scripts/test-inference-browser.mjs:375. I checked that line directly: it is UNTOUCHED and still reads getByRole("link", { name: "Try it: Molecular-number inference", exact: true }). The markup was fixed instead. LAB_NAMES in PassageActionsBar.tsx maps bm-07 -> 'Molecular-number inference', with the chain actions.tryIt.label ?? LAB_NAMES[instrumentId] ?? instrumentId.

Proved by rendering, not by reading: I rendered the real PaperReader to static markup at this revision and confirmed aria-label="Try it: Molecular-number inference" is present. That is the exact string CI was timing out on, so gh run 35276591077's failure should clear.

Two other assertions in that file did change, from exact 'Why?' to /^Why\?:/u. That is adaptation to a now-unique label, not relaxation to a generic one - the product label became MORE specific ('Why?: <passage>'), so an exact match on the old bare string could not survive. I consider that within AC2's 'or with a name that is strictly more specific'.

The commit adds 10 assertions and removes 2, introduces no suppression tokens, and extends passageActions.schema.ts with a validated optional label (invalid-try-it refusal for empty or non-string). PassageActionsBar.test.tsx: 4 pass, 0 fail, 29 expect() calls, re-executed by me.

AC3 measurement, rendered at this revision. I measured link accessible names against their destinations, which is what the AC actually asks (duplicates are only a defect when destinations differ):

  distinct link names on the Brownian reader : 112
  names mapping to MORE THAN ONE destination : 10

  "In words"                          -> 5 destinations
  "Explanation"                       -> 2
  "Section-only reading ->"            -> 2
  "Zero average is not no movement"    -> 2
  "Why the square grows with time"     -> 2
  "From a step law to a density law"   -> 2
  "What the spreading curve predicts"  -> 2
  "Why viscosity changes the spread"   -> 2

Before this commit the same page carried 6x 'Try it', 6x 'Why?', 6x 'Show the missing step' and 40x 'Read the prerequisite', all to differing targets. Every one of those is gone.

The residual 10 are outline and navigation links, not passage action bar links, so they fall outside this bead's scope line ('Every link in a passage actions bar'). Several are also arguably benign: an outline entry and an inline heading link pointing at the same section under the same title. 'In words' at 5 destinations is the one that looks like a genuine defect.

Recommendation: close this bead on its stated scope once CI is green, and take the residual 10 as a separate bead rather than widening this one after the fact - that would be scope creep in the direction I normally complain about.

ORCHESTRATOR FAULT, recorded by TanElk against myself.

I closed this bead with the close reason "probe". That was not a decision, it was an accident: I had been using `br close <id> --reason "probe"` as a read-only way to ask br whether a bead still had open blockers, because br reports blockers in the skip message. On the three pane18 beads that worked as a probe, because br refused them. This bead had no open blockers, so the same command closed it outright.

That is my error and it is the same offence I reopened four beads for this session: a close with no cited evidence. The method was bad - I was using a mutating command as a query. br dep or br show reports dependencies without touching state, and that is what I should have used. I am not going to use a close as a probe again.

I have reopened the bead and am closing it properly in the same breath, with evidence I actually ran.

title: Two gates apply MISSING_VERIFIED_ANCHOR to the same configs and disagree: --check-config calls ap-34-591 valid while the pin gate refuses it
description:
Two independent gates enforce the same named rule on the same six configs and return opposite answers for one of them.

    bun scripts/download-facsimiles.ts --check-config
      X ap-19-289.yaml: INVALID (MISSING_VERIFIED_ANCHOR)
      + ap-34-591.yaml: valid
      X ap-17-549.yaml: INVALID (FACSIMILE_PAGE_OFFSET_MISMATCH)

    bun scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.ts
      REFUSED ap-34-591 [anchor/MISSING_VERIFIED_ANCHOR]
              Config 'ap-34-591' is missing a verified anchor.

## The pin gate is right and --check-config is wrong

Verified by TanElk against the file itself: scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/ap-34-591.yaml
contains no verifiedAnchor, and no parentPageIndex, printedPage or verifiedBy key at any
nesting level. grep returns nothing. So the config genuinely lacks the anchor and
--check-config reports it as valid anyway.

## What makes this worse than one wrong verdict

ap-19-289 has the SAME defect and --check-config DOES catch it. So the rule is not simply
unimplemented there - it is applied to one config and not to another that fails the same
way. That is the signature of a check keyed on something other than the property it
claims to test, which is the defect class am-o44v was opened for. A reader comparing the
two outputs would reasonably conclude ap-34-591's anchor is fine.

## Consequence

--check-config is the cheap, fast gate people will run while editing configs; the pin gate
needs the parent scans, which are git-ignored and absent in CI (registry.ts sets
requiredInCi false for it). So the gate that is ALWAYS available is the one that passes a
config the authoritative gate refuses. A missing anchor is not cosmetic: the pin gate's
own wording is 'Anchor data at the wrong nesting level looks like verification and is not
verification.'

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both gates give the same verdict on all six configs for the anchor rule. State which

title: Lane-level guard: fail the node lane if any test mutates generated/content
close_reason:
Verified and closed by orchestrator TanElk. Work by pane17, landed in a828b57 - see the
COMMIT HYGIENE note below, which is a real problem with that commit even though the work
in it is good.

THE GUARD WORKS. Planted negative, run by me:
  restored `emit: options.shouldEmit ?? true` in scripts/build-content.ts
  bun run test:node ->
    ❌ FATAL: Node lane mutated generated/content!
      Run `bun run prepare:content` to rebuild the canonical content corpus.
    lane failed
  Reverted; prepare:content; corpus back to 26 payloads.

That is acceptance (b) and (c): the LANE fails, independently of any individual test, and
the message tells the reader how to recover without needing this bead in front of them.

  bunx tsc --noEmit -> 0 errors
  Ratchets (tolerance, declaredClasses, scrollableRegions, nestedFormControls) -> green
  It lives in scripts/run-node-only-tests.ts, not in a test file, which is what I asked
  for: a test cannot guard the lane it is a member of.

COMMIT HYGIENE - a828b57 IS CONTAMINATED and I am recording it rather than quietly
accepting it:

  scripts/run-node-only-tests.ts        +122   <- this bead's actual work
  src/equations/alternateForms.test.ts  +666   <- pane20's work, am-eq-expression-tree-8kl
  src/equations/alternateForms.ts       +523   <- pane20's work
  src/equations/ast.ts                    +1   <- pane20's work

  pane17 staged broadly - git add -A or git commit -a - and swept pane20's uncommitted
  expression-tree work into a commit whose message says "lane-level generated/content
  mutation guard". 1189 of its 1309 inserted lines belong to a different bead.

  I am NOT rewriting history to fix it. The work is good, both bodies are green, and
  rewriting a shared branch while three panes hold uncommitted files is a worse risk than
  a mislabelled commit. What I am doing instead is recording the split here and on
  am-eq-expression-tree-8kl so that neither bead's evidence trail silently points at the
  wrong change.

  This is the mistake I have warned three panes about and made myself in this repo -
  `git add .beads/issues.jsonl && git commit` once swept fifteen of pane20's files into a
  chore commit of mine. The fix is always the same: commit by explicit path.

NO-CLAIM LINE: this closes the lane-level guard for generated/content specifically. It does
not guard any other generated directory, and it detects mutation rather than preventing it
- a test that writes there still writes there, the lane just refuses to report success
afterwards. That is the right trade: prevention would need sandboxing the whole lane.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR (TanElk). Follow-up to am-arlh, which I just closed. This is the half of its
acceptance that was NOT built, and I said so in the closure rather than pretending it was
complete.

WHAT am-arlh FIXED: one specific cause. scripts/build-content.ts forced emit: true, so the
CLI wrote into the repo's real generated/content whenever any test shelled it. pane17 fixed
that and added generatedContentIsolation.test.ts, whose emit-decision tests catch a
reintroduction of that exact bug. I verified both directions - the fix holds, and restoring
the `?? true` fails 3 of its 5 tests.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: the acceptance asked for a test that fails if ANY test writes into
generated/content during a run. What exists guards ONE route. A different test reaching
that directory by another path - a new e2e that shells a different script, a helper that
emits by mistake - would corrupt the corpus again and nothing would catch it until some
later content-dependent test failed for no visible reason. That is exactly how the
original bug hid: sitemap.test.ts failed forty minutes after passing, same commit.

THE SHAPE I WANT, and it is small:
  scripts/run-node-only-tests.ts already wraps the whole node lane. Have it
    1. hash generated/content/index.json (and ideally the payload files) BEFORE running,
    2. run the lane as it does now,
    3. hash again AFTER, and FAIL the lane if the digest changed - naming the file that
       changed and reminding the reader to run bun run prepare:content.
  That wraps every file in the lane rather than guessing which one might write, and it
  costs one hash per run.

WHY THE LANE RUNNER AND NOT A TEST: a test can only observe the directory at its own
moment in the order. The runner sees the whole lane. This is the difference between
detecting a symptom somewhere and pinning the invariant.

ACCEPTANCE (I re-execute all of it):
  a. bun run test:node on a clean tree -> passes, and generated/content still has 26
     payloads with papers ['brownian-motion'].
  b. Planted negative: reintroduce the `?? true` in build-content.ts. The LANE must fail
     with your new message naming generated/content, independently of whether
     generatedContentIsolation.test.ts also fails. Restore, show it passes. Paste both.
  c. The failure message must tell the reader how to recover (prepare:content), because
     the person who hits this will not have this bead in front of them.
  d. bunx tsc --noEmit -> 0 errors.

DO NOT make this a test file under src/testing. It belongs in the lane runner. A test
cannot guard the lane it is a member of.

CODE-FIRST: typecheck and your own targeted run only.
