title: A green CI certifies facsimile configs agreeing with each other: the only gate that reads the pinned bytes cannot run there
description:
Three facsimile gates are required in CI and none of them looks at a pinned PDF. The one
gate that does is the only one exempt, because its inputs are git-ignored. A green CI
therefore certifies that the CONFIGS agree with each other, and says nothing whatever
about the bytes that ship.

Measured from scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts, not inferred:

    verify-content            requiredInCi true    reads records
    facsimile-config          requiredInCi true    download-facsimiles.ts --check-config
    facsimile-page-anchors    requiredInCi true    verify-facsimile-anchors.ts, reads no PDF
    facsimile-pins            requiredInCi FALSE   the only gate that renders and compares

And the inputs:

    sources/                          GIT-IGNORED   6 parent scans, local only
    public/papers/pdfs/               tracked       all 6 pinned extracts ARE in CI
    scripts/sources/facsimile-sources tracked       all 6 configs are in CI

## Why this outlives today's pins

The three wrong pins will be repaired today. This will not be, because it is not about
those pins: it is that the only artefact-level check in the facsimile chain is
structurally unable to run where the chain is enforced, and the checks that can run
compare declarations with declarations.

The concrete failure it permits was demonstrated this tick on am-cf6m: with a corrected
anchor, ap-19-289's offset check PASSES, so both CI-required config gates go green while
the pinned PDF is still cut from parent page 97. Nothing in CI can tell. The refusal
that catches it comes from the one gate CI does not run.

This is the shape that gets rediscovered in six months by someone who trusts a green
pipeline. It should be a tracker entry, not a paragraph in a bead about three specific
extracts.

## The lever, and it is smaller than "get the parents into CI"

Only ONE SIDE of the comparison is missing. The pinned extracts are tracked and present
in CI; only the parent scans are not. Several real checks need one side only:

  - a pinned extract's own embedded text layer already yields its printed folio numbers.
    verify-facsimile-pins uses exactly that today to say "the extract's first page
    carries the folio of parent page 97". That reads only the pinned PDF and would run
    anywhere.
  - page count, page size, and the SHA-256 the config records are all properties of the
    tracked file.
  - the declared printed range versus the folios the pinned pages actually carry is a
    real contradiction check that needs no parent at all.

So the question is not only "can the parents reach CI" (licensing, size, and the
Cloud-OCR-only policy all bear on that, and none of them is mine to decide). It is also
"which artefact-level checks have been left in the unrunnable gate that do not belong
there".

## Not proposing the obvious wrong fix

Do not make facsimile-pins requiredInCi true as it stands. It would fail every CI run
for a missing input, which is a lane failing to start rather than a verdict - the exact
confusion am-yf6h was filed for - and it would be switched off within a week.

## Provenance

Observed by pane28 while porting verify-facsimile-pins into a lane that can spawn
(am-yf6h) and simulating the CI condition with the parents absent; sharpened by the
am-cf6m re-verification at e4094331, which showed a corrected anchor turning both config
gates green over a wrong extract. Not caused by either piece of work; both only made it
visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision, recorded with a name and a date, on whether the parent scans can reach CI
  at all - rights, size, and the local-only policy - so the answer stops being implicit
  in a git-ignore line.
- Whatever that answer is, the artefact-level checks that need only the PINNED file are
  identified and moved into a gate that is requiredInCi true. State how many checks
  moved and how many genuinely need both sides.
- Planted negative that goes RED IN CI: a pinned PDF whose pages carry folios outside
  its declared printed range is refused by a CI-required gate. Confirm that state is
  reachable first - ap-19-289 is in exactly that state today, so the fixture exists
  until it is repaired, and after that it must be constructed.
- Control: the checks that genuinely require the parent scans stay in facsimile-pins,
  stay requiredInCi false, and still refuse what they refuse today - this must not
  become a reason to weaken them.
- The registry records, per step, WHY a step is not required in CI, so "requiredInCi
  false" stops being a flag whose reason lives only in a code comment.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PARTIAL DELIVERY, recorded by orchestrator TanElk. Not closing.

SHIPPED (4708cf6a): the digest check. The pinned bytes are compared against recorded
digests in CI, requiredInCi true. Verified by re-execution: all six pinned extracts OK,
registry parses at 32 steps / 24 requiredInCi, registry tests 22 pass.

Two things about it are worth preserving beyond this bead. Its green states its own
limit, in the gate's text: "a digest check proves the bytes are the ones recorded, not
that the recorded bytes are the right pages." And its failure text closes the cheap
escape: "Do not repin to make this pass: establish which of the two is wrong first."
The planted negative moved a digest in a COPY of the configs under --config-dir rather
than flipping a byte in a pinned PDF, because those artefacts are irreplaceable.

NOT SHIPPED: the folio check - reading a pinned extract's own embedded text layer to
confirm the printed folio matches the recorded one. This is the check that actually
catches a wrong-article pin, and the one whose absence let three pins serve the wrong
article while --verify stayed green all night. It is blocked, and the blocker is a
contradiction inside our own guard rather than a missing capability.

THE EXACT CONTRADICTION, quoted from both sides.

scripts/ocr-guard-denylist.json:
    "pattern": "pdftotext",
    "category": "binary-or-spawn",
    "reason": "pdftotext text-layer extraction is forbidden in source-layer pipelines;
               historical facsimile text layers are unreliable and must not substitute
               for cloud OCR research drafts or editorial transcription."

AGENTS.md, Cloud OCR Only:
    "An agent may read the facsimile's own embedded text layer and the pinned page images."

The REASON forbids a USE: the layer standing in for a transcription source. The folio
check is not that use - it reads the layer for page identity and writes no edition text.
The PATTERN forbids every call in every file for every purpose. So the guard denies the
thing the policy permits, and it is the third denylist-standing-in-for-an-allowlist
instance found tonight.

Countervailing text, which is why no agent should narrow this unilaterally - AGENTS.md
also says the ruling "changes what an agent may LOOK AT. It changes nothing about what
may be EXECUTED. The denylisted engines stay denylisted in every call form." Whether
pdftotext is properly an "engine" is exactly the question: it starts no recognition
process and only reads characters already in the file. That is a reading of the owner's
words, and an agent should not make it on the owner's behalf.

BOTH OPTIONS MEASURED, so this is not a one-alternative verdict:

  A. Narrow the pdftotext denylist entry to match its own stated reason - deny it in
     source-layer/transcription pipelines, permit it for page identity. Smallest change.
     It is still a guard narrowing, which is the shape gate-weakening hides in, so it
     wants the owner's word and its own commit.

  B. Read the embedded text layer with a JS PDF library instead, spawning no denylisted
     binary at all. MEASURED: no such dependency exists here, and package.json carries
     15 dependencies total. Adding one to this project is itself an owner-level call,
     so B is not the cheap way around A.

  C. Leave the folio check unshipped and documented. This is what the pane did, and it
     was the right call with the options available.

Owner decision needed on A or B. Until then the bead stays open with the digest half
delivered, and the swarm should not rediscover this contradiction a fourth time.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
OWNER RULING, recorded by orchestrator TanElk. Unblocks the folio check.

Asked as a three-way choice (narrow the denylist / add a JS PDF reader / leave it
blocked). The owner selected, verbatim:

    "Add a JS PDF reader"

with the option stated as: "Read the embedded layer with a library instead, spawning no
denylisted binary at all. Keeps the guard untouched - but this project runs on 15
dependencies total, so a 16th is its own policy decision."

So option A is DECLINED: scripts/ocr-guard-denylist.json is not to be narrowed, and the
pdftotext pattern stays exactly as it is, denied in every call form. The guard is not the
thing that was wrong. The contradiction recorded in the previous comment gets resolved by
removing our need for the binary rather than by relaxing the rule against it - which also
means the denylist keeps its blunt, unarguable shape, and nobody has to reason about
whether a given call site is "page identity" or "transcription" at review time.

What this authorises, and only this:
  - one new dependency, 15 -> 16, a PDF library that reads a PDF's EMBEDDED TEXT LAYER
  - no recognition process, no denylisted binary spawned, no change to the OCR guard
  - the folio check in verify-facsimile-pins.ts implemented on top of it

Requirements before adding it, because a dependency is harder to remove than to add and
this project's 15-dependency posture is deliberate:
  - name the candidates actually evaluated, not one. Report for each: whether it runs
    under Bun, whether it pulls transitive dependencies, licence, and last release.
    "One alternative is not a verdict" applies to libraries too.
  - the library must read the embedded layer ONLY. Anything that also performs or bundles
    recognition is out regardless of how convenient it is, and its presence in the tree
    would be a standing invitation to violate the policy later.
  - verify-facsimile-pins.ts currently calls pdftotext at line 558 and requireTool at
    755. The existing pdfPageTexts() is the seam - replacing its internals leaves every
    caller and the gate's failure text intact.
  - the folio check ships requiredInCi TRUE, or it has not addressed this bead. The whole
    finding is that the only artefact-level check cannot run where the chain is enforced.

Its green must state its limit the way the digest check's does. Reading the printed folio
proves the extract is cut from the right PAGES; it does not prove the parent scan was the
right VOLUME. Say so in the gate's own text so nobody reads this green as "the pins are
correct" either.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
THE EXTERNAL REFERENT: reachable, and it is not the parent scan. Measured 2026-09-21, pane31.

The orchestrator asked what the external referent is and whether it is reachable before anything
is built. Answer: an external referent IS reachable in CI, the obstacle is not availability, and
one premise the work was queued on does not survive checking.

## What is reachable and what is not

  REACHABLE IN CI (tracked)
    public/papers/pdfs/          9 files, 6 pinned extracts plus 3 digest-suffixed, 0.2-4.6 MB
    scripts/sources/facsimile-sources/   the 6 configs
    poppler-utils                ALREADY INSTALLED by .github/workflows/quality-gates.yml
                                 ("Install system dependencies for rendering", apt-get
                                 poppler-utils), and by browser-acceptance.yml's Playwright step

  NOT REACHABLE
    sources/parents/             6 parent scans, 214.9 MB total, .gitignore:54

So the tooling question and the availability question come apart. The parents are 215 MB and
git-ignored; the extracts and the renderers are both already in CI.

## The referent itself

The true referent for "are these the right pages of Annalen 17" is the printed journal, and no
machine in this project can consult it. Of what can be consulted, ranked by independence from
the records being checked:

  1. THE PINNED EXTRACT'S OWN CONTENT - page count, page geometry, and the folio numerals its
     embedded text layer carries. This is the scanning institution's testimony, produced before
     this project existed and independent of every declaration we wrote. IN CI.
  2. The parent scan - the same kind of testimony, one level up. NOT in CI.
  3. The provenance receipt and the config - our own declarations. Not referents at all.

Every pinned extract carries a text layer: /Font objects 9 to 38 and text-show operators 2 to 82
across the six. The two with the fewest (ap-34-591 at 2, ap-18-639 at 7) are exactly the two
am-d1cz records as "not-measured (2 votes)" - an independent corroboration of that table from a
different measurement.

## THE PREMISE THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE CHECKING

The dispatch said the folio check "was unblocked by the owner's JS-PDF-reader ruling". I could
not find that ruling: no match in docs/DECISIONS.md, none in the bead graph. What I CAN quote is
the 2026-09-20 ruling in AGENTS.md, verbatim "Both layer and pixels", which answers am-d1cz's
first question - reading an embedded layer is not within the OCR prohibition - and which says in
the same breath that it "changes nothing about what may be EXECUTED", that "the denylisted
engines stay denylisted in every call form", and that proposing to relax the guard on its
strength "is out of scope and goes back to the owner".

And switching to a JS reader does not route around it. scripts/ocr-guard-denylist.json has 19
entries, and the last two are:

    pdftotext       "forbidden in source-layer pipelines; historical facsimile text layers..."
    getTextContent  "pdf.js getTextContent extraction is forbidden in source-layer pipelines..."

Both routes to a text layer are denied, by the same reason, which is a USE ("in source-layer
pipelines") stated through a PATTERN that denies every call - the same denylist-standing-in-for-
an-allowlist shape ocr-guard.test.ts already records as its one KNOWN_UNRESOLVED_VIOLATION. So
am-d1cz's question 2 is untouched by a change of library, and I have not built on a ruling I
cannot quote.

## What IS unblocked, and nobody has to decide anything for it

pdfinfo and pdftoppm appear NOWHERE in the denylist - 0 occurrences across all 19 entries. Only
text extraction is denied. So page count and page rendering of the PINNED file are available in
CI today with no ruling at all.

Classifying every check verifyPin performs:

  NEEDS ONLY THE PINNED FILE, NO DENYLISTED TOOL  (3)
    evaluateDeclaredAnchor          config only, touches no file
    pinned digest vs recorded       already covered by facsimile-digests, requiredInCi true
    pinned page count vs recorded   pdfinfo, not denylisted
  NEEDS ONLY THE PINNED FILE, DENYLISTED TOOL  (1)
    evaluateExtractFolios           the printed-range contradiction check - the valuable one -
                                    and it is not called by verifyPin at all today (am-d1cz)
  GENUINELY NEEDS BOTH SIDES  (6)
    parent existence; parent digest; parent page count; parent folio coverage; the four
    renderPageHash comparisons; locateExtractInParent and evaluateContentIdentity

So two checks could move to a CI-required gate today, one is the one everybody wants and is
blocked on a ruling that a change of library does not supply, and six genuinely need the parent.

## A structural finding the bead does not name

The pinned-only checks are not merely in the wrong gate. verifyPin RETURNS EARLY when the parent
is absent - `if (findings.some(f => f.check === "artifact")) return` after the two existence
probes - and then calls requireTool("pdftotext") unconditionally before any measurement. So even
the checks needing neither the parent nor a denylisted tool cannot run without both. Moving them
is not a registry change; it is a sequencing change inside verifyPin, and it can be made without
touching what the parent-side checks refuse.

## Not done, deliberately

No gate moved, no registry entry edited, no ruling assumed. The bead's first acceptance criterion
is a recorded decision on whether the parents can reach CI, and 215 MB of institutional scans
under an unresolved rights question is not mine to decide. Neither is the text-layer use question,
which am-d1cz already frames correctly and which this analysis does not advance except to remove
the JS-reader escape hatch from the options.

page-count contradiction is the reachable substitute and the gate already refuses it.

== THE ONE THING THE NEXT AGENT WOULD GET WRONG: KEY ON THE PAGE, NEVER ON THE LABEL ==

This is the reasoning the orchestrator asked me to preserve, and it is not obvious from the code.

If you compare a manifest's sentence division with a computed one, the tempting key is the id -
compare s3-p8 with s3-p8. IT IS WRONG, and wrong in a way that produces confident, plausible,
entirely false disagreement reports. A manifest's paragraph labels are an ALLOCATION HISTORY, not
a function of the text. Brownian's s3 labels run 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8; its s4 runs 1..6 then 9..12.
Labels have been withdrawn and there is no retirement record saying so. A computed division emits
CONTIGUOUS labels. So past the first gap the two sides' labels have slipped relative to each
other, and a shared label names different paragraphs. Every comparison after that point reports
collision as disagreement.

That is not hypothetical: it was done by hand on this exact data and produced "18 of 32 paragraphs
disagree", which was label collision and not disagreement about the page at all. The adjudication
found the frozen ids sound.

THE KEY THAT WORKS IS THE PRINTED PAGE, because both records carry it independently and neither
allocates it: the manifest reads it from the plate (locators[].page), and the ledger carries its
own [[ANNALEN-PAGE n]] line, once per sheet, in all four ledgers. Nothing in this repository
writes ANNALEN-PAGE from a manifest - it is only ever parsed and validated, and validateLedger
already checks it is strictly increasing, non-duplicated and inside the journal's page range. So
the key has an integrity check on one side and an allocation history on neither.

Two things that follow, both of which cost me a mistake to learn:

  1. The not-available determination is PER PAGE, on whether THAT page has sentence coverage - not
     per paper on a zero total. I first wrote a zero-check because the two papers I looked at had
     zero units. A paper with partial coverage clears a zero-check and then reports one phantom
     disagreement per uncovered page. The planted case in the test is exactly this and a
     per-paper check reddens it.
  2. State the denominator in every line. "6 agree, 6 differ" and "6 of 31 comparable" are
     different claims and only one is honest alone.

And the sharper general lesson, which applies well beyond this file: the page key is available
because I asked what the TEXT itself carries, rather than what the two RECORDS have in common.
Two records compared only to each other certify that they agree, which is the same shape as the
facsimile gates in am-xoxn - configs checked against configs while nothing reads the bytes. When
a comparison feels circular, look for the third thing neither side wrote.

== MEASUREMENT HABITS THAT PAID, in case they save someone a tick ==

Plant, do not read. Six times today a rule that looked right did not fire, and twice a plant I
wrote was itself vacuous. A green plant is a claim about the plant first.
Anchor the count and name the denominator; an unanchored grep fails toward the prose ABOUT the
thing, which correlates with absence.
zsh ate --include=*.ts twice and returned zeros that were not measurements. A zero from a failed
command looks exactly like a zero from a clean one.

title: Six simultaneous live regions on one reading page, five of them global chrome
description:
One page carries five simultaneous polite live regions. Observed on /lab/light-thread in the production build; four of the five are global chrome, so this is a whole-site question rather than a light-thread one. Enumerated by a strict-mode locator violation, which listed them: 1 the search launcher 2

3

inside Main navigation 4

inside the Theme group 5

the laboratory's own Only the fifth belongs to the instrument. The other four are present on every page that renders the layout. ## Why this is handed to accessibility rather than kept Whether five concurrent polite regions is a defect is not something a browser harness can settle. Announcement behaviour depends on the screen reader, its verbosity, whether regions are empty at page load, and how each is updated. The plausible failure - a reader hearing an unrelated chrome announcement interleaved with the instrument's result, or hearing nothing because a competing region won - is exactly the kind of thing AGENTS.md says must be tested with disabled readers using their own tools rather than inferred from markup. So this is a measured inventory, not a verdict. It may be fine. ## What the markup does say without a screen reader All five were empty at load in the run that found them, which is the recommended pattern (a live region present and empty, filled later). Two carry aria-atomic="true" and three do not, so the same event announces differently depending on which region reports it. ## Provenance Found by pane28 while exercising /lab/light-thread in Chromium and WebKit; an unscoped [role="status"] in my own test matched all five, which is how they were enumerated. My locator was the bug and is fixed by scoping to section.laboratory. The inventory is the by-product and is filed here so it is not lost in that fix. ## Acceptance Criteria - A decision, recorded with a name and a date, on whether five concurrent polite regions is acceptable on a reading page, taken with at least one screen reader actually running - not from the markup. - If the answer is no, the chrome regions are consolidated or scoped so an instrument's result is not competing with navigation and theme announcements. - The aria-atomic inconsistency across the five is resolved or recorded as deliberate per region. - Whatever is decided, a check exists that fails when a new global live region is added without that decision being revisited, so the count cannot drift upward unnoticed. - Planted negative that goes RED: a sixth global live region added to the layout is caught by that check. Confirm the fixture reaches that state before trusting it.

title: Bare dialog selectors in three browser suites now match the wrong element
description:
## What is wrong

A client-mounted `<dialog class="notebook-dialog">` is now inserted into the reader DOM ahead of the clarification dialog. Any selector that says just `dialog` therefore resolves to the notebook dialog, or to two elements.

I proved this live at d43fb0e by probing a real page after opening a clarification:

```
dialogCount: 2
[0] notebook-dialog      open: false
[1] clarification-dialog open: true
document.querySelector("dialog")  -> the CLOSED notebook dialog
```

In scripts/test-reader-browser.mjs this produced two distinct failures - a focus-containment assertion that read the wrong element and returned false, and a Playwright strict-mode violation on `locator("dialog")`. Both are fixed in d43fb0e by targeting `[data-clarification-dialog]`. The focus trap itself was never broken.

The same fragile pattern remains in three suites that I have not executed and must not edit blind:

```
scripts/test-equation-browser.mjs:287   page.locator("dialog").waitFor({state:"hidden"})
scripts/test-notebook-browser.mjs:138   document.querySelector("dialog")
scripts/e2e/searchPalette.mjs:146,149,179,226,231,236   page.locator("dialog")
```

## Why each needs judgement, not sed

- test-notebook-browser.mjs is the one suite where the notebook dialog IS the subject, so `querySelector("dialog")` may be returning the right element there today and would break if pointed elsewhere.
- searchPalette.mjs asserts `page.locator("dialog").count() === 0` in four places. If a notebook dialog is mounted on those routes, that assertion is now asserting something different from what it was written to assert, and changing it to a count of 1 would be silencing it. The correct fix is to scope it to the search dialog and keep the meaning "the search palette is closed".

## Acceptance

1. Each of the nine sites is scoped to the dialog it means, by a stable attribute, not by element name or DOM order.
2. Each of the three suites is executed against a real build and its result recorded. A suite that cannot be run is named as such and its sites are left unchanged.
3. No assertion changes what it asserts. In particular no `count() === 0` becomes `count() === 1` to accommodate an extra mounted dialog; if a dialog is legitimately present, scope the assertion to the one under test.
4. A negative: with the correct scoping, closing the subject dialog while another remains mounted must still fail the test if the subject stays open.

## Provenance

Found by orchestrator TanElk on 2026-09-17 while repairing scripts/test-reader-browser.mjs; the two reader sites are already fixed and are the worked example for the rest.
close_reason:
Closed by orchestrator TanElk at 714625a, work landed in 9a12d56.

AC1 stable-attribute scoping: data-notebook-dialog added in src/reader/notebook/panel.ts, data-search-dialog in src/search/CommandPalette.ts and CommandPalette.tsx; all nine sites across scripts/test-equation-browser.mjs, scripts/test-notebook-browser.mjs and scripts/e2e/searchPalette.mjs now select by attribute rather than element name or DOM order.

AC3 was the risk I named when filing this bead: that a count() === 0 assertion would be relaxed to 1 to accommodate an extra mounted dialog. I diffed every changed assertion. All seven searchPalette sites remain strictly 'assert.equal(..., 0)', only the selector changed from 'dialog' to '[data-search-dialog]'. Nothing was relaxed.

AC4 negative: scripts/test-notebook-browser.mjs now mounts a foreign open <dialog data-clarification-dialog>, closes the notebook, and asserts nb && !nb.open && foreign.open - so a coexisting dialog cannot spoof notebook closure.

Re-executed by me against the build at 46aec48: bun scripts/test-notebook-browser.mjs -> '25 notebook browser checks passed.'

AC2 partial, stated rather than glossed: SwiftForge reported searchPalette check 10 (corrupt shard retry) timing out under Chromium force-cache, and test-equation-browser previously failing early at line 18. The line-18 failure is resolved (am-w7rx, closed). The searchPalette cache-retry timeout is unrelated to dialog scoping and is not evidence about this bead's change; it is not carried as met.

  'Revisit trigger: A FIFTH technical compound of points is needed... At that point reconsider whether the discriminator should move from the modifier noun to the scoring construction (earn/award/collect/score N points), which is a larger change to matchWordListRule and NEEDS ITS OWN BEAD.'
'distributed points' is that fifth compound. So the documented next step is this bead, not a sixth line in the allowlist.
The same record also says: 'Status: NOT OWNER-RATIFIED. am-a33s carries the human-gate and decision labels, so editorial-voice ownership has the final word and this entry is not binding until a named editorial owner or the project owner ratifies it.' And it records that an agent-made version of this very change, ba91f675, was REVERTED IN FULL by 36371082 with no stated reason, leaving only the narrowest exception standing. An agent quietly editing this rule a third time is the wrong move.

THE TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, for the owner to choose between:
  A. Add 'distributed points' to the allowlist. One line, consistent with the chosen option B, and it makes the enumeration five entries - which is the trigger saying the enumeration is the wrong shape.
  B. Move the discriminator to the scoring construction: flag 'points' when preceded by a scoring verb or a bare count (earn/award/collect/score/N points) and let the noun sense through. Larger, changes matchWordListRule, and needs the negatives the original decision proved: 'bonus points', 'reward points', 'experience points', 'extra points', bare 'points', 'earn points for each passage' must all still fire, plus the four existing compounds and 'distributed points' must pass.
  C. Reword the recap. I am not proposing it: the prose is correct physics and rewording it to satisfy a misfiring rule is the inversion this project's doctrine forbids.

BLOCKING: CI step 10 cannot go green until one of A or B lands. It is one of the three remaining real CI failures. am-a33s (P3, in_progress, pane30) is the sibling; this should probably be dispatched to whoever holds that, not opened as a second front.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PREPARED, NOT LANDED. pane30 (BrightIsland). The patch lives at
scratchpad/am-xsue-scoring-construction.patch, developed and proved in an isolated
git worktree (scratchpad/wt-xsue) so nothing sits dirty in the shared tree. Four
files, 125 insertions, 0 deletions, no commit, no push, nothing closed.

=====================================================================
1. A CORRECTION TO THE DISPATCH'S PREMISE, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE
=====================================================================
The dispatch says the scoring-construction change is the one that "was reverted in
full at ba91f675 to 36371082, so do not re-attempt the reverted approach." That is
not what those commits contain. I read them rather than trusting the summary:

  ba91f675  content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml  +9
            adds allowlist: data points / data point / plot points / plot point /
            sample points / sample point / grid points / grid point
  36371082  the same 9 lines removed, a lone targeted revert

The reverted approach is the COMPOUND ALLOWLIST - option A's shape - not the
scoring construction. The scoring construction has never been attempted in this
repository: `grep -rn "scoringVerb|scoring construction|scoringConstruction"
docs src content` returns exactly one hit, the revisit-trigger sentence in
DECISIONS.md itself (control grep for matchWordListRule returns 2 files, so the
search works).

That inverts the constraint. "Do not re-attempt the reverted approach" rules out
option A - adding a sixth line to the allowlist. It does not touch option B.
Option A's shape is also the one already re-landed and standing today, as a3892d4.

=====================================================================
2. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES BETWEEN A AND B
=====================================================================
I did not want to choose on taste, so I counted. Census over every string the voice
scanner actually sees (content records via the real record walk, .tsx via the real
extractStringsFromTsx), not a raw grep:

  occurrences of the word "points" in scanner-visible text   47
  distinct tokens immediately before it                      24
  of those 47: mathematical noun or verb                     36
               inside identifiers (argument ids, tape ids)   10
               a fragment the extractor split mid-sentence    1
               GAMIFICATION                                   0

The attested preceding tokens are independent (9), movable (4), distributed (2),
the, locked, recorded, labeled, material, data, plot, sample, grid, between,
adding, unites, bibliography ("the bibliography points to the digitized table" -
the VERB, which no enumeration of modifier compounds can ever reach).

Two numbers follow from this and they are the whole argument:

  a. The allowlist covers 4 of the 47. The other 43 pass the gate only because
     theater is a flag rather than an error in PROSE. The enumeration is not
     holding the line; the prose severity is.
  b. Every commit in this repository's history that has ever introduced a
     gamification "points" phrase - "earn points", "bonus points", "reward
     points", "experience points", "Total points", "points!" - is a test fixture
     in this rule's own suite. Not one is reader-facing copy. In two years of
     this word being on the list it has fired on: one aria-label, reworded at
     ef5e69a, and one argument recap, which is this bead.

I want to state the fair counter-argument rather than let it go unsaid: a voice
rule is partly preventive, and zero hits can mean deterrence rather than
uselessness. That is real. It is also why option B is the right answer instead of
deletion - B keeps "earn 5 points" an error and only stops the noun firing.

So the revisit trigger fired for the right reason. Option A would take the
enumeration to 5 of 47.

=====================================================================
3. THE PATCH
=====================================================================
content/editorial/voice-rules.yaml   +7   scoringConstruction: [points]
src/content/checks/voice/rules.ts    +6   the optional field on WordListRule
src/content/checks/voice/matchers.ts +62  isScoringConstruction + one guard line
src/content/checks/voice/voice.test.ts +50  two tests

The validator needed no change: validateVoiceRules spreads rulesRaw through, so a
new key on the theater rule is carried without touching the loader.

An occurrence of a scoring-construction word is a finding only when a scoring verb
governs it, a scoring modifier precedes it, a scoring participle follows it, or
the whole scanned string is a bare score readout. The verb, modifier and
participle lists are closed.

A BARE COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SUFFICIENT, and this is the one design decision
worth flagging. "When the 10 points are rigidly locked" is ordinary prose about
dots, and the committed suite ALREADY requires "12 sample points recorded" to
pass, so a numeral before the word cannot decide anything. A numeral is admitted
only between a scoring verb and the word: "earned 10 points".

DELIBERATELY ABSENT: no DECISIONS.md entry. Recording the decision as settled is
my best reading of why ba91f675 was reverted, and this one is even less mine to
settle - it edits matchWordListRule. The record is the owner's to write.

=====================================================================
4. THE PROOFS, WITH DENOMINATORS
=====================================================================
Baseline in the worktree at HEAD b5d2b968: 71 pass, 0 fail.
With the patch:                            73 pass, 0 fail.
All seven voice test files with the patch: 102 pass, 0 fail.

Every one of the 17 cases the existing suite pins - the four "<any word> points"
negatives, bare "points", "earn points for each passage", the two per-occurrence
mixed sentences including the index-8 assertion, "12 sample points recorded",
"Perrin plotted 50 data points" - survives unchanged.

RED PROOF A, the ordinary-sense test is load-bearing. Delete the two
scoringConstruction lines from the YAML and nothing else: 72 pass, 1 fail, the
failure being exactly the new test. Restored byte-identical (cmp).

RED PROOF B, the scoring test is load-bearing. Neuter isScoringConstruction to
return false for everything - the naive way to make the sentences pass: 67 pass,
6 fail. The six are my new negative plus FIVE PRE-EXISTING ones, including both
am-a33s per-occurrence tests. Restored byte-identical (cmp).

Neither plant is vacuous: each was driven to red against the real mechanism, and
each red state is a different edit, so neither test can pass for the other's
reason.

The nine phrases in the new positive test are real corpus text and NONE is in the
compound allowlist, so each can only pass through the construction predicate. That
is deliberate: a test using "data points" would have proved the old mechanism.

=====================================================================
5. WHAT IT CLEARS - AND A SECOND CORRECTION
=====================================================================
"One fix clears two required steps" is half right, and I would rather say so now
than have it discovered in CI.

  STEP 10 verify-content  CLEARED OUTRIGHT, measured both ways in the worktree
    with the patch:     exit 0, {"ok":true,"flags":394,"skipped":[]}
    key removed only:   exit 1, stderr carries the bead's line verbatim -
                        theater: recap: Voice violation [theater]: Remove or
                        rephrase "points"
    Two YAML lines are the entire difference. The control also shows 7 further
    theater "points" FLAG lines in content records, all legitimate technical
    prose, all cleared by the same patch.

  STEP 13 voice-lint  NOT CLEARED. 6 errors to 5, still exit 1.
    The five left are not mine and not this rule:
      2x em-dash          BrownianFirstEncounter.tsx, DataPanel.tsx
      3x status-enum-leak modern-codata-2022.yaml, einstein-1905-mass-energy-
                          printed.yaml (both gasConstantProvenance),
                          MassEnergyFirstEncounter.tsx
    Flags drop 84 to 37, which is exactly the 47 occurrences the census counted -
    an independent cross-check that the census and the live scanner agree.
    DataPanel.tsx is the em-dash placeholder glyph TanElk already recorded on
    am-a33s comment 586; it is the same class of defect as this one.

  bunx tsc --noEmit: zero errors in the four changed files. (The worktree reports
  90 errors, all downstream of gitignored src/generated being absent there; I am
  reporting the filtered count and will re-run in the real tree before any land.)
  biome check on the four files: clean, no fixes applied.

comments.text:
THREE SEPARATE DEFECTS FOUND WHILE DIAGNOSING. Reported, not fixed, and not
folded into the patch. Folding any of them in would have been the cheaper route
to green and would have left the real defect standing.

=====================================================================
A. ARGUMENT RECAPS ARE LINTED AS READER-PROGRESS COPY  (the near miss)
=====================================================================
This one nearly changed my answer, so it gets the detail.

resolveVoiceContext maps any field path CONTAINING "recap" to reader-progress:

  src/content/checks/voice/contexts.ts:41   normField.includes("recap")

reader-progress is the context for progress copy - "Your streak: 3 days", "75%
complete". It is also the ONLY context besides task-feedback and ui-label where
theater is an error rather than a flag. Grep for reader-progress in
voice-rules.yaml returns exactly two lines: the context declaration, and
theater's `reader-progress: error`. So that classification has one practical
effect in the entire rule set.

An ArgumentNode's recap is not progress copy. It sits beside question,
conclusion, premises and limitations, and it reads like this:

  "Independent centred steps add mean squares; the root therefore grows as the
   square root of time."
  "For an unbounded point source, the Gaussian has mean square 2Dt and
   coordinate RMS sqrt(2Dt)."

42 of the 46 argument records carry one. Measured, not assumed:

  record kinds in all of content/ with a recap field:  Counter({'argument': 42})
  `grep -rn "^\s*recap:" content/`                      0 matches in YAML

There is not one reader-progress record with a recap field anywhere. The line was
written speculatively and, today, its only effect is to put 42 physics summaries
under the strictest severity in the rule set. resolveVoiceContext has no test file
at all - nothing anywhere asserts reader-progress for "recap", or for any other
field.

WHY I AM NOT FIXING IT HERE, even though it clears the same CI step. I checked
the blast radius across all 42 recaps under both contexts:

  recaps producing any finding                 5
  errors when linted as reader-progress        1   (this bead's)
  errors when linted as prose                  0

So one line in contexts.ts would turn step 10 green too, and it would be tempting
to call it the clean fix. It is not the right fix for this bead:

  1. It does not stop the rule misfiring. It downgrades the misfire to a flag for
     42 fields and leaves the other 43 corpus occurrences exactly where they are.
  2. It BUYS green by making 42 fields less strict. The classification is wrong on
     its own terms, which is why I am reporting it as a defect rather than a
     workaround - but the strictness loss is real and belongs in the owner's view,
     not buried inside a fix for something else.
  3. The two defects are independent. The word list over-fires; the context
     resolver mislabels. Fixing either hides the other.

This is a candidate bead, not a follow-up laundering of am-xsue's scope: am-xsue
is "theater fires on 'distributed points'", and the misclassification is a
distinct defect that happens to touch the same failing line. Filing is yours.

=====================================================================
B. THE COMPONENT EXTRACTOR SPLITS A SENTENCE AT AN INTERPOLATION
=====================================================================
One "points" flag survives the patch, and I chased it rather than reporting a
round number. src/components/lab/PredictPanel.tsx:543:

  Recorded prediction: Sketch with {record.choice.points.length} points

extractStringsFromTsx splits the JSX at the expression, so the trailing text node
reaches the linter as the standalone string "points". My bare-score-readout branch
fires on it, correctly by its own terms - a lone "points" IS how a score label is
written, and the committed suite requires bare "points" in ui-label to stay an
error.

It is a false positive, it was ALREADY a false positive before my patch (one of
the 48 baseline flags), and it is a flag rather than an error, so it blocks
nothing. I could have made it pass by restricting the bare-readout branch to the
strict contexts. I did not, because that would be tuning a voice rule to an
extractor artifact, and the artifact affects every rule, not this one. Saying so
is better than a quiet special case.

=====================================================================
C. THE LINTER SCANS IDENTIFIER FIELDS AS PROSE
=====================================================================
10 of the 47 "points" occurrences are inside ids, not prose: lq-05-predict-ten-
points (6), lq05-ten-points-half- (2), arg-lq-independent-points,
lq05-sixty-points-logarithmic - reached through fields like
content/experiments/lq-05.yaml :: argumentIds[1]. Each was a flag. Smallest of the
three and purely noise-in-the-denominator; recording it because it inflated my
first census and would inflate anyone else's.

=====================================================================
WHAT I DID NOT DO
=====================================================================
No commit, no push, nothing closed, no DECISIONS.md entry, no bead filed for A.
Did not touch content/arguments/light-quanta/arg-lq-independent-configurations.json:
option C, rewording correct physics to satisfy a misfiring rule, stays rejected
for pane28's reason. Did not add a voice-overrides.yaml entry either - that
mechanism exists and would work per-occurrence with a reason and a dated reviewer,
but it needs a named reviewer from docs/OWNERS.md, which is a human gate I cannot
self-certify. Noting it as an option D the bead did not list.

The shared tree is untouched: everything above ran in scratchpad/wt-xsue, a
detached worktree at b5d2b968 with node_modules symlinked. git status in the real
repo shows the same single dirty file it showed when I started.

title: Five runtime-conformance readers are unit-tested and composed by nothing the gate invokes
description:
Five reader modules in scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/ each have a passing unit test in the node
lane, and the runner that the registered browser-acceptance gate actually invokes imports none of
them. The measuring half exists and is tested; the failing half exists and is required in CI; they
are not connected to each other.

FOUND while sweeping band A of am-o44v. networkLogClassifier turned up there for a loose predicate,
and the loose predicate turned out to be the smaller problem.

=== THE FIVE ===

    scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/identityReader.ts
    scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/networkLogClassifier.ts
    scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/performanceMarkReader.ts
    scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/rafSampler.ts
    scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/tapeUrlBuilder.ts

Measured from the TypeScript program's import graph (every ImportDeclaration, ExportDeclaration and
dynamic import() in the repository, built from tsconfig.json), then cross-checked with a grep for
each path as a command string outside test files: the only importer of each is its own test.

=== THE RUNNER DOES NOT USE THEM ===

scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts:163, which the registry lists as the browser-acceptance gate
with requiredInCi: true, dynamically imports ./e2e/runtime-conformance/run.ts. That composer
imports exactly two local modules:

    import { ... } from "./checks.ts";
    import { assertRuntimeRegistration } from "./fixtureRegistration.ts";

and checks.ts imports no local module at all. So none of the five is reachable from the gate.

=== THE TESTS DO RUN, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS INVISIBLE ===

All five test files are in the node lane. Derived by calling nodeOnlyTestArgs on bunfig.toml rather
than by reading the lane's output:

    node lane file count: 45
    runtime-conformance files in the node lane: 8, including all five reader tests

So the suite is green, every reader is "tested", and nothing that reads a browser ever consults
them. A green lane is evidence that the readers parse their own fixtures, not that any conformance
property is checked.

=== WHAT THE PREDICATES LOOK LIKE, since nothing exercises them ===

networkLogClassifier.ts:6

    if (lower.includes("worker") || lower.startsWith("blob:")) return "worker";

A substring decides a NetworkKind, ahead of the .js arm, so any URL whose path contains the word
worker is classified as a worker request rather than a script. Its test's only worker assertion,
classifyNetworkRequest("blob:http://127.0.0.1/worker"), satisfies BOTH arms of that condition, so
the test cannot tell which one is load-bearing and would stay green if either were deleted.

That is what an unconsumed measurement decays into: nobody notices the predicate because nothing
depends on the answer.

=== DISPOSITION ===

Not fixed, and deliberately not fixed by the sweep. Either the readers belong in the conformance
run and run.ts should compose them, or they are dead and should be retired - and retiring files
needs the owner's permission. Tightening networkLogClassifier's predicate first would be the worst
of the three: it would make an unconsumed module look cared-for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the five is either composed into runtime-conformance/run.ts with an assertion that
  consumes its output, or recorded as retired with the owner's written permission.
- If composed, each carries one negative a naive wrong implementation would fail. For
  networkLogClassifier specifically: a URL containing "worker" that is NOT a worker request must
  not classify as one, and the blob: and includes("worker") arms must be separable by a test.
- The reachability question is checked rather than remembered: something fails when a module under
  scripts/e2e/runtime-conformance/ has no importer but its own test.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS BEFORE WIRING, 2026-09-21, pane31 / AmberFalcon. Nothing wired. Three of the bead's
claims confirmed, one corrected, and two larger disconnections found above it.

CONFIRMED - the five are orphaned. Census by import specifier over every .ts/.mjs/.js/.json in
the repo, classified by whether the importing file is a test:

  identityReader.ts         1 ref   its own test            0 production
  networkLogClassifier.ts   1 ref   its own test            0 production
  performanceMarkReader.ts  1 ref   its own test (+1 ratchet baseline KEY, not an import)
  rafSampler.ts             1 ref   its own test            0 production
  tapeUrlBuilder.ts         1 ref   its own test            0 production

Controls behave differently, which is what makes the census trustworthy: checks.ts and
fixtureRegistration.ts are each imported by run.ts.

CORRECTED - they were not written against a runner that no longer exists. All eight files in
the directory, run.ts included, arrived in ONE commit, 9c38a5f7 (2026-09-17T03:13:49-04:00).
The five were born orphaned. That commit's own message enumerates exactly the nine assertions
run.ts makes and never mentions identity attributes, network classification, performance marks,
paint labelling or tape seeds. So connecting them is not restoring a lost wire; it is writing
five checks that were never written, using helper halves that were.

THE FIVE ARE NOT ONE KIND OF THING. identityReader is not a missing check, it is a REDUNDANT
WRAPPER: checks.ts:2 imports parseInstrumentRoot from ../domContract.ts and calls it directly at
:38, :39, :67 and :80, and identityReader.readInstrumentIdentity is a pass-through to that same
function. Only its second export is unique - missingIdentityAttribute, which turns a
DomContractError into the name of the attribute that was missing. checks.ts contains ZERO
try/catch, so today a DomContractError crashes the conformance run instead of failing a named
check, which is the exact thing that helper was written to prevent. The other four
(networkLogClassifier, performanceMarkReader, rafSampler, tapeUrlBuilder) are helper halves for
properties checks.ts does not test at all: grep of checks.ts gives 0 hits for performance, mark,
network, paint and seed.

WHAT THE REGISTERED GATE MEASURES - this is the part that is bigger than the bead.

The registry entry "browser-acceptance" (family browser, requiredInCi true, requiredInProfiles
preview+launch) has command ["bun", "scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts"] with NO selection
flag, and quality-gates.ts:357-363 spawns step.command verbatim, appending nothing. Run through
the real gate runner:

  bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --only browser-acceptance --family browser
  -> FAILED (exit code: 1), Steps Passed 0, Steps Failed 1, Duration 141ms

141 ms because the harness exits 2 on a usage error: parsePaperE2EArgs requires exactly one of
--paper / --changed / --all / --self-test-failure / --fixtures / --smoke. It never reaches the
preflight, a lane, a browser, or run.ts. So the answer to "connected to nothing" versus
"measuring a subset" is neither: as registered, it measures nothing and says so with exit 2.

AND THE WORKFLOW NAMED AFTER IT RUNS SOMETHING ELSE. .github/workflows/browser-acceptance.yml
does not invoke the registered command. It runs

  node --experimental-strip-types --test scripts/e2e/checks/*.test.ts scripts/e2e/*.test.ts
                                         scripts/e2e/fixtures/*.test.ts

which matches 20 files, NONE of which references runtime-conformance. `--fixtures` appears
nowhere in package.json, any workflow, or any script - only in the harness's own usage string
and docs/PAPER_E2E_HARNESS.md.

THE GOOD NEWS, AND IT MATTERS FOR SEVERITY. run.ts's nine assertions - six behavioural and three
planted negatives against real Chromium with real Workers - ARE enforced in CI, by a route
nobody documented: live.test.ts calls runRuntimeConformance() unconditionally, bunfig's
pathIgnorePatterns puts all of scripts/e2e in the NODE lane, and .github/workflows/
quality-gates.yml:60 runs `bun run test:node` as a required step with chromium and webkit
installed. Derived from nodeOnlyTestArgs rather than from reading output: 50 files in the node
lane, 8 of them under runtime-conformance, live.test.ts among them.

So the conformance properties are real and enforced. What is broken is the gate that claims
them and the workflow named after it, and neither failure is visible because a third route
happens to carry the work.

THE PREDICATE, with observed examples rather than argued ones:

  classifyNetworkRequest("http://127.0.0.1/apps/runtime/worker-protocol.js") -> "worker"
  classifyNetworkRequest("http://127.0.0.1/docs/workers-guide.html")         -> "worker"

A script and a page. Its test has four assertions and its only worker case,
"blob:http://127.0.0.1/worker", satisfies BOTH arms of `includes("worker") || startsWith("blob:")`,
so either arm can be deleted and the test stays green.

NOT DONE, deliberately: nothing wired, no predicate tightened, no file retired, no registry entry
edited. Tightening networkLogClassifier first would make an unconsumed module look cared-for, as
the bead says. The orchestrator has the shape and rules on sequence.

title: The pinned-facsimile gate cannot run in either lane, so its red is partly an artifact and not a verdict about the pins
description:
scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts is authored for one lane and requires the other, so it has never produced a complete measurement on this host.

  - It imports from `bun:test`, so under node it dies at import:
    ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME, "Received protocol 'bun:'" - 1 test, 0 pass, 1 fail,
    before any assertion runs.
  - It spawns pdftoppm and pdftotext, and bunfig.toml's own header records that this
    cannot work: "Subprocess-spawning tests cannot run under bun test on this host:
    bun's test runner posix_spawn of node fails with EBADF (measured: the same files
    pass under node --test)." The file is NOT in pathIgnorePatterns, so it runs under
    bun and every spawn fails.

## The failures split in two and only one half is real

Verified by TanElk. pdftoppm 26.06.0 IS installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/pdftoppm, all six
parent PDFs ARE on disk (ap-17-132.pdf is 2,737,365 bytes), and calling the gate's own
renderPageHash() directly at its own RENDER_DPI of 40 returns a hash successfully. The
same call inside the test file fails with 'exit undefined'.

REAL, and computed with no subprocess - keep these:
  ap-17-549  anchor/FACSIMILE_PAGE_OFFSET_MISMATCH: parentPageIndices[0] is 132 but the
             verified anchor implies 173 (parent 173 -> printed 549, offset -376)
  ap-19-289  anchor/MALFORMED_VERIFIED_ANCHOR: anchor fields written directly under
             articlePages instead of inside a verifiedAnchor object
  ap-34-591  anchor/MISSING_VERIFIED_ANCHOR

ARTIFACT of the broken lane - these are NOT findings about the pins:
  all six      artifact/RENDER_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE
  the three 'Measurement primitives against real pinned bytes' tests
  'Summary: 6 pins checked, 0 verified, 6 refused'

The gate's own report says which is which and I missed it for several ticks: the
declared and anchor columns carry numbers because they are config arithmetic, while
folio, extract-is and content are '?' for every row because nothing ever measured them.

## Why this is P0 rather than a tidy-up

am-cf6m asks the owner to authorize re-extracting and re-pinning ap-17-549 from parent
pages 173-184. That decision has been presented against a gate output that is partly a
measurement failure. The anchor half of the evidence stands, so the request is not
withdrawn - but nobody should be told '0 of 6 pins verified' as though it described the
pins. It describes the lane.

## A second defect, which is what cost the investigation

requireTool() treats ANY spawnSync error as a missing binary:

    const probe = spawnSync(tool, ["-v"], { encoding: "utf8" });
    if (probe.error) throw new PinMeasurementError("RENDER_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE",
      `'${tool}' is not available on PATH. ...`)

An EBADF from the test runner becomes the confident, false sentence "'pdftoppm' is not
available on PATH", which is checkable and wrong. A refusal message must not assert a
cause it did not establish.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The file runs in a lane that can spawn. Either port it off bun:test to node:test and
   add it to bunfig.toml pathIgnorePatterns beside the other subprocess-spawning tests,
   or split the config-arithmetic assertions (which need no subprocess) from the
   measurement ones.
2. requireTool distinguishes ENOENT from every other spawn error and reports the error
   code it actually saw. A spawn failure that is not ENOENT must not say 'not available
   on PATH'.
3. Planted negative that goes RED: with the tool genuinely absent from PATH, the refusal
   says ENOENT/not-found; with a spawn failure that is not ENOENT, it says something
   else. Confirm both states are reachable before trusting either.
4. Once it runs, re-run it and report the TRUE pin verdict on am-cf6m, stating how many
   of the six were actually measured.
5. scripts/download-facsimiles.test.ts fails in the same run ('validates all real
   production facsimile source configs cleanly'); check whether it is the same cause
   before treating it as separate.
close_reason:
Fixed at d771b9e6 by pane28; closed by orchestrator TanElk on re-executed evidence. Closing this against my own corrected premise, not the one I filed.

1. THE LANE. bunfig.toml now lists scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts in pathIgnorePatterns, which moves it to the node lane (run-node-only-tests.ts derives its list from that field rather than hardcoding one). Verified by running the lane, not by reading the config: bun run test:node now reports 293 tests, 292 pass, 1 fail. Before this, the lane REFUSED TO START at all and the file could not execute in either lane. The sub-assertions that never previously ran now run and pass, including "ap-19-289's stale extract refuses on content identity and names where it was cut from", "ap-34-591's stale extract refuses on content identity", and the control "repairing a stale extract clears the content-identity refusal" - which is the right shape: it proves the gate goes GREEN when the defect is repaired, not only red when it is present.

2. THE MESSAGE THAT ASSERTED A CAUSE IT NEVER SAW. requireTool now branches on the error code. Exercised all three states directly: present -> no throw; absent -> "'am-no-such-tool-xyz' is not available on PATH (ENOENT from spawnSync am-no-such-tool-xyz)"; found-but-unlaunchable (/etc) -> "'/etc' was found but could not be started: EACCES from spawnSync /etc". Both failure branches are reachable and distinct, which is what the criterion asked for. The new RENDER_TOOL_SPAWN_FAILED text goes further than I required and says what the result does NOT mean: "This is a failure of this process to launch the tool, NOT evidence that the tool is missing and NOT a finding about the pins. Nothing was measured, so no pin is verified or refused on this run." That sentence is the direct antidote to the error I made reading the old message.

3. CRITERION 4, REWRITTEN MID-BEAD AND SATISFIED. The true verdict is recorded on am-cf6m: 6 pins checked, 3 verified (ap-17-132, ap-17-891, ap-18-639), 3 refused, with ap-17-549's offset carried by 144 folio votes against 4.

MY OWN ERROR, RECORDED SO THE BEAD READS HONESTLY. I filed this P0 claiming the gate had "never completed a measurement on this host". False: the gate SCRIPT worked the whole time (bun scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.ts, exit 3). I inferred the gate's capability from its test file's failure - the same class of mistake this sweep exists to find. The real defect was narrower and still worth fixing: the measurement happened and the assertion enforcing it could not run. Severity was also overstated - registry.ts sets requiredInCi false, so this never blocked CI.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CORRECTION FROM TanElk, WHO FILED THIS BEAD AND OVERSTATED IT. I wrote that the gate 'has never completed a measurement on this host'. That is false and I am withdrawing it.

THE GATE SCRIPT WORKS. `bun scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.ts` exits 3 and reports 'Summary: 6 pins checked, 3 verified, 3 refused'. ap-17-132, ap-17-891 and ap-18-639 each report 'anchor, content identity and folio coverage all agree'. It renders pages with pdftoppm, hashes them, and counts folio votes out of the parent text layer - every capability I said it lacked. The registry invokes it as command ["bun","scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.ts"], a SCRIPT; bun spawns subprocesses fine outside its test runner, and the EBADF defect is specific to `bun test`. My error was inferring the gate's capability from the test file's failure - the same mistake in kind as the ones this sweep exists to find.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS STILL WORTH DOING:

1. scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts cannot run in either lane - bun:test import kills it under node (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME), and it spawns, so bun test cannot run it. The measurement therefore happens but THE ASSERTIONS THAT ENFORCE IT NEVER EXECUTE. That is the accurate form of the finding and it is still a real hole: a gate whose enforcement lives only in a test that cannot run.

2. requireTool still converts ANY spawnSync error into the confident false sentence "'pdftoppm' is not available on PATH". Unchanged.

CRITERION 4 IS REWRITTEN. The true verdict is already in hand, so the deliverable is making the ENFORCEMENT executable, not recovering the measurement.

SEVERITY IS LOWER THAN P0 AS FILED. registry.ts sets requiredInCi: false with requiredInProfiles [preview, launch], because /sources is git-ignored so CI has nothing to compare against. This never blocked CI. Leaving the priority for the next owner to set rather than quietly re-grading my own bead.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacValley (pane %29) - answered by running the gate's own detector on those exact two
files. THE GATE IS NOT FAILING OPEN, and pane30's detector is the loose one. Both files
are correctly not ignored.

WHAT THE GATE'S OWN DETECTOR SAYS, classifyTestFileContent from
scripts/quality-gates/bunfigNodeOnlyTests.ts, run directly on each file:

  src/content/manifest/report.test.ts
    gate verdict         null            <- not a violation
    static child_process import   true
    dynamic child_process import  false
    spawn-call shape              true   (execSync()
    mentions EBADF                true
  src/content/coverage/coverageLedger.test.ts
    gate verdict         null            <- not a violation
    static child_process import   false
    dynamic child_process import  true
    spawn-call shape              true   (execSync()
    mentions EBADF                true

So the gate SEES both files as spawning - imports and call shape are both true, which is
exactly what pane30 detected - and then exempts them on the third condition,
`!code.includes("EBADF")`. Neither half of pane30's finding is wrong; the finding just
stops one clause short of the gate's rule.

AND THE EXEMPTION IS SUBSTANTIVE, NOT A WORD IN A COMMENT. classifyTestFileContent runs
stripComments BEFORE that check, so a mention in a comment cannot buy it. Both files use
it in live code:

  report.test.ts:251   } catch (err: any) {
                 252     if (err?.code === "EBADF") {
                 253       // Fallback directly via module functions when subprocess
                 254       const report = generateManifestReport(fixtureManifest);
  coverageLedger.test.ts:452  } catch (err: unknown) {
                        453    if ((err as { code?: string })?.code === "EBADF") {

They try the subprocess and fall back to calling the module functions when it is refused.
That is precisely the case the exemption exists for: a test that spawns OPTIONALLY does
not need to leave the bun lane.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by reading the rule: both pass under bun.
  bun test src/content/manifest/report.test.ts          5 pass 0 fail
  bun test src/content/coverage/coverageLedger.test.ts  11 pass 0 fail
  bun test src/content/manifest src/content/coverage    114 pass 0 fail across 6 files

So: pane30's detector is looser than the gate's, the gate would not have prevented
am-yf6h by catching these two because these two are not that defect, and the correction
is yours to carry. A confirmed finding here would have cost someone a pointless lane move.

NOW THE PART I DID NOT EXPECT, AND I AM REPORTING IT WITH ITS LIMITS RATHER THAN AS A
CONCLUSION. bunfig.toml's premise does not reproduce on this host today. Its header says
"bun's test runner posix_spawn of node fails with EBADF (measured: the same files pass
under node --test)". Under bun 1.4.0, from inside a bun test file, I spawned:

    echo hello                                  -> OK
    node --version                              -> OK
    bun --version                               -> OK
    bun --version + node --experimental-strip-types --version, with cwd set  -> OK

Every one succeeded. Not one EBADF.

THE LIMITS, because this is exactly where I would fool myself: my probe ran a single test
file, then a six-file directory. It did not run the full `bun test src scripts` sweep,
1113 files, which is the condition the premise was measured under, and a posix_spawn
failure that depends on file-descriptor pressure would not show up in either of my runs.
So what I have measured is that spawning is NOT universally broken here, which is weaker
than "the premise is dead" and I am not claiming the stronger thing.

But if it IS stale, the consequences are wide: the whole pathIgnorePatterns list exists to
route spawning tests out of the bun lane for that reason, and I moved two files - including
my own formatterExclusions guard - into the node lane on that premise earlier tonight. It
is worth someone running the real sweep condition before more files are moved. I have not
filed a bead because the measurement that would justify one is the one I have not done.

Report, not a closure. No files changed; the probe files are in my scratchpad, outside the
repository.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
pane28: DONE in d771b9e6 - bunfig.toml, scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.ts, scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts. Reporting, not closing.

YOUR DIAGNOSIS HELD, AND ONE PART OF IT DID NOT, so take the second part before the rest. The lane is the cause, but NOT because bun cannot spawn on this host. I probed it directly: spawnSync of pdftoppm, pdftotext and pdfinfo all return status 0 under bun test, 40 consecutive spawns without error, and the gate's own renderPageHash imported into a scratch bun test returns 5855e61943eb3a4a - the right hash. What actually decides the outcome is WHERE THE TEST FILE LIVES. The same file copied to a scratch directory, with only its relative imports rewritten, runs under bun and reports 19 pass 1 fail and "6 pins checked, 3 verified, 3 refused". In scripts/ it reports 16 pass 4 fail and "0 verified, 6 refused". I have not established the mechanism and I am not going to guess at one; I am recording it because the bunfig header's sentence, read as "bun cannot spawn here", is not what I measured.

THE REAL ERROR, instrumented rather than inferred. I patched renderPageHash temporarily to print out.error and restored it from a copy: EBADF, syscall "spawnSync pdftoppm", message "posix_spawn '/opt/homebrew/bin/pdftoppm'". An ABSOLUTE PATH. PATH resolution had already succeeded, so "not available on PATH" was false in a way anyone could have checked, and that is why criterion 2 mattered as much as criterion 1.

CRITERION 1. Ported to node:test with node:assert/strict and added to bunfig pathIgnorePatterns, which is the single list nodeOnlyTestArgs reads, so the node lane picks it up (verified: it appears in the 45 inputs) and bun no longer discovers it (verified: bun test names it as an unmatched filter). The 56 assertions were converted by a paren-matching pass, not a regex sweep, then read; biome flagged 16 sites where the conversion had wrapped an optional chain, and those are fixed.

CRITERION 2. requireTool distinguishes ENOENT from everything else and prints the code and syscall it saw. A non-ENOENT failure is a new RENDER_TOOL_SPAWN_FAILED that says in words that nothing was measured and that this is not a finding about the pins. renderPageHash and pdfPageTexts had the same defect in a quieter form - "exit undefined" implies a tool that ran and failed - and now report the spawn error when there is one.

CRITERION 3, two permanent tests instead of a one-off plant, both states produced for real. Absent tool: ENOENT, says "not available on PATH". A file that exists and is not executable: EACCES, refused as RENDER_TOOL_SPAWN_FAILED, and it asserts it did NOT get ENOENT before asserting anything else, so it cannot pass by reaching the wrong branch. It also asserts the sentence that caused this bead is absent. Planted negative: requireTool collapsed back to one branch turns the EACCES test RED. EACCES stands in for EBADF, which cannot be summoned on demand; what the test is about is the only thing they share, that the error is not ENOENT, and the test says so.

CRITERION 4 IS BELOW, AS A SEPARATE COMMENT ON am-cf6m TOO.

CRITERION 5: NOT THE SAME CAUSE. scripts/download-facsimiles.test.ts fails at "validates all real production facsimile source configs cleanly" because checkAllConfigs() returns valid false. No subprocess is involved: bun scripts/download-facsimiles.ts --check-config prints ap-19-289 INVALID (MISSING_VERIFIED_ANCHOR) and ap-17-549 INVALID (FACSIMILE_PAGE_OFFSET_MISMATCH). It is the same two config defects the pin gate finds, surfacing in a second gate. It is a real red about the configs and it is not a lane artifact.

AND ONE DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN THE TWO GATES, which I am reporting and not resolving: --check-config prints "ap-34-591.yaml: valid" while the pin gate refuses ap-34-591 with MISSING_VERIFIED_ANCHOR. The yaml genuinely has no verifiedAnchor - articlePages goes straight to printedFirst/printedLast/parentPageIndices. So two gates apply the same named rule to the same file and disagree. Either one of them is wrong or the rule is scoped differently on purpose, and I do not know which.

THE ROOT CAUSE OF CRITERION 1, which is a live hole and not a historical note. assertNoUnignoredSubprocessTests could never have caught this file. classifyTestFileContent reads ONLY the test file's own text and requires BOTH a direct child_process import AND a spawn call in that same file. verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts has neither: it spawns transitively through verify-facsimile-pins.ts. The guard is one hop deep, and its own test "passes on the live repository tree" was green the whole time this file was in the wrong lane. Second defect in the same function: the exemption is `!code.includes("EBADF")`, so any file that mentions the string EBADF anywhere, in a comment, exempts itself. That is a substring test standing in for a category test, in the guard that assigns lanes. am-zm52's src/testing/trackedImports.ts already has the transitive resolver this needs.

EVIDENCE. node --experimental-strip-types --test scripts/verify-facsimile-pins.test.ts: 27 passing, 1 failing - section 6, the deliverable red, which stays red until the owner authorizes re-pinning. bunx tsc --noEmit exit 0. biome clean on all three files. scripts/quality-gates/bunfigNodeOnlyTests.test.ts: 10 pass 0 fail after the bunfig change.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacValley (pane %29) - it does not reproduce under load either. Your hypothesis is dead
and the premise is unexplained. Taking you at your word that this answer is worth having.

WHAT I RAN. A probe test file joined to the real sweep as an extra argument, so it
executed inside the same bun process as everything else rather than beside it. Twenty
iterations, each doing execSync("node --version") and spawnSync("node", ["--version"]),
with a two-second wait between them so the attempts STRADDLE the run instead of landing in
whatever moment the file happened to be scheduled - a burst at second one would have said
nothing about pressure that builds.

    bun test src scripts <probe>
    [loadprobe] attempts=40 failures=0 spanMs=40882
    Ran 9894 tests across 1113 files. [112.15s]

Forty spawn attempts spread over 40.9 seconds of a 112-second sweep across 1113 files.
Zero failures. The string EBADF appears zero times in the whole output.

I also ran the node lane's OWN spawn shape from inside a bun test, since a large argv was
the one plausible difference left:

    spawnSync("node", ["--experimental-strip-types", "--test", ...45 files])
    [bigargv] files=45 error=none status=0

So it does not reproduce quiet, it does not reproduce under load, and it does not
reproduce in the exact shape run-node-only-tests uses.

WHY THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATIONS DO NOT HOLD EITHER. It is not a bun version drift: the
bunfig header itself says "bun 1.4.0 honours camelCase pathIgnorePatterns", and we are
ON 1.4.0. It is not file-descriptor pressure in any ordinary sense: the soft limit here
is 1048576. node is v25.9.0.

WHAT I AM NOT SAYING. That the original measurement was wrong. Someone wrote "measured"
in that header and I have no reason to doubt they saw it; a failure that will not
reproduce is not a failure that never happened, and the difference is machine state,
session, or a shape I have not thought of. I am also not recommending that the ignore
list be dismantled on this evidence. Most of that list is playwright and browser tests
which genuinely cannot run under bun for reasons that have nothing to do with EBADF, and
the two subprocess entries I added tonight - formatterExclusions and inventoryVersions -
pass in the node lane either way.

WHAT IT DOES CHANGE. The gate's third clause, `!code.includes("EBADF")`, exempts a file
for handling an error I cannot make happen. If the premise really is stale, that clause
is exempting files from a lane requirement that no longer has a reason, and the two files
pane30 flagged are exempt for a condition that may never fire. That does not make
pane30's finding right - those files pass under bun, measured, 5 and 11 tests - but it
does mean they pass because spawning WORKS, not because their fallback catches anything.

You said you would file it only in the other branch, so I have not. If you want the
premise chased rather than left unexplained, the next step I would take is to ask whoever
wrote that header what they ran, because the cheapest explanation left is that the
failing shape is one none of us has reproduced yet.

One incidental, since it affects anyone reading sweep numbers tonight: the failure count
moved from 25 to 5 between my two runs, eighty seconds apart, entirely from peers landing
work mid-sweep. A sweep failure count is not a stable quantity right now.

Report, not a closure. No repository files changed; every probe lives in my scratchpad.

THE FULL LIST, 15 files with absolute paths outside the repository:

  /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space   - structural.e2e.test.ts, editions.refusals.test.ts,
                                            reconciliation.refusals.test.ts, kernelRefusals.test.ts,

In reopening this bead I wrote requirement 2 as: "the gate is re-shaped from a denylist to an allowlist: no test file may contain ANY absolute path except ones derived at runtime from os.tmpdir() or the repo root."

THAT IS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A GATE NOBODY KEEPS. I swept the tree afterwards. Most absolute-looking literals in test files are URL ROUTES, not filesystem paths:

    83  "/papers/...
    61  "/lab/...

A gate written to my requirement flags all of those. It would be red on its first run for 180-plus legitimate strings, and it would be disabled or allowlisted into uselessness within a day - which is precisely the failure mode I warned about when specifying the tracked-imports gate, and I walked into it one bead later.

THE CORRECT DISCRIMINATOR is not absolute-versus-relative. It is whether the path reaches a FILESYSTEM CALL. Measured on the eight /home/ literals now in the tree, exactly ONE is a defect:

    writeGeneratedSection.test.ts:103   feeds mkdirSync            DEFECT
    shareForms.media.test.ts:12         a filePath field in test data   fine
    loader.test.ts:19                   a string in a fixture           fine
    probeLld.test.mjs (several)         /home/runner/work/... is GitHub Actions' own home, and belongs there

So the gate should catch absolute paths that flow into mkdir, writeFile, readFile, existsSync, stat or rm, and permit anything derived from os.tmpdir() or the repo root. Requirement 2 is replaced by that.

A SEPARATE THING THE SWEEP EXPOSED. The am-yhus fix was in part a blanket substitution of /Users/jemanuel for /home/agent across several files. That is why it passed the old gate while fixing nothing: the new root was neither /Volumes nor /Users. Worth checking for other instances of the same non-fix.

Requirement 3 stands and is now sharper: the proving plant must be an absolute path under a third root FEEDING AN FS CALL. A plant that merely mentions such a path in test data should stay green, and demonstrating that it does is part of the proof.
